name: CG Power and Industrial Solutions Ltd

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to remain in 17-18% band
items.quote: So margin will remain between 17% to 18%, somewhere in that band. That should happen.

items.statement: No volume guidance provided for FY27
items.quote: No guidance as such. We just want to do our job and we'll work for the best.

items.statement: January volumes encouraging; positive growth expected from Q4
items.quote: January is looking positive and encouraging and we are seeing a positive growth going forward from quarter 4 onwards.

items.statement: Sanitaryware targeting double-digit volume growth
items.quote: Even though that will have a much -- in sanitaryware, we're definitely looking at a double-digit volume growth from here.

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA margin 17.2%, up 442 bps YoY but down 74 bps QoQ due to lower realization from SKU liquidation
items.quote: EBITDA margin in quarter 3 FY '26 is 17.2%, plus 4 42 basis points against 12.8% in corresponding quarter last year. However, EBITDA dropped by 74 basis points sequentially as compared to quarter 2 F Y '26, mainly because of lower sales realization as we gave some discount in order to reduce our SKUs.

items.statement: Cost optimization continues; gross margin stable at 36-37% including power and fuel
items.quote: To be very precise, it was 37% in Q2 FY '26 and in this quarter, it is 36%. For that, you have to take raw material, trading purchase and power and fuel in source and spare.

items.statement: Tiles revenue flat YoY at INR1,030 cr; Bathware up 9% to INR103 cr; Adhesives up to INR35 cr from INR20 cr
items.quote: Tiles segment remained flattish year-on-year at INR1,030 crores in quarter 3 F Y '26 compared to INR1,040 crores in quarter 3 F Y FY '25. Bathware segment registered a 9% growth in revenue, reaching INR103 crores in quarter 3 FY '26 compared to INR95 crores in quarter 3 FY '25. Revenue from adhesive grew to INR35 crores in quarter 3 FY '26 as compared to INR20 crores in quarter 3 FY '25.

items.statement: Converted 9.1 msqm ceramic line to GVT at Gailpur plant for value-added products
items.quote: In Gailpur plant, we have converted 1 unit with a capacity of 9.1 million square meters from ceramic floor tiles to glazed vitrified tiles , to move towards value -added products as per prevailing market demand scenario.

items.statement: Total capacity 82.5 msqm including JVs; outsourcing available from Morbi if needed
items.quote: We have a capacity, 82.5 million. The rest of the players are still in a much lower capacity than us.

items.statement: Faucet prices hiked 8-12% from Jan 19; sanitaryware hike planned from Mar 1
items.quote: So from 19th of January, we have taken a price hike in the faucet products in the -- to the tune of about 8% to 12%. And sanitaryware, we plan to take a price hike probably from 1st of March.

items.statement: Gas price averaged INR37-38/MMBTU in Q3; expected stable with INR1 increase in Q4
items.quote: Sonali, in quarter 3, the gas pricing has been average of INR37, North was INR38, South INR38 and West was INR37. And going forward also, we expect it to remain stable.

items.statement: SKU rationalization 70-75% complete; rest to finish in Q4; plants more efficient
items.quote: So I would say about 70% to 75% is already done. Rest will all happen in this quarter.

items.statement: Dealer unification progressing; pricing aligned across ceramic, GVT, PVT from Jan 1
items.quote: With effect from 1st of Jan, we have aligned the pricing in ceramic, GVT and PVT, made the discount structure very similar.

items.statement: Retail 70%, projects 30% of sales mix
items.quote: So roughly, our share is 70% in retail and 30% in projects.

items.statement: Organized players' share ~40%, Morbi ~60%; expects 50-50 in 2-3 years
items.quote: I would say about 2 years' time or 3 years' time, it will be 50-50.

items.statement: India tile exports fell 20% to INR16,000 cr in FY25; Q3 exports ~INR4,000 cr; 9M FY26 ~INR12,000 cr
items.quote: Indian tile exports have experienced a 20% fall in value in FY '25 to INR16,000 crores due to increased freight rates due to Red Sea crisis and the ongoing geopolitical disturbances. In quarter 3, we exported around INR4,000 crores from the country approximately.

items.statement: Working capital days increased to 64 from 56 due to higher receivables and lower current liabilities
items.quote: As of December '25, the working capital days increased by 8 days to 64 days compared to 56 days on 30th of September '25, mainly due to increase in receivables and decrease of other current liabilities.

items.statement: No major borrowings planned; balance sheet strong
items.quote: We are -- the balance sheet -- driving the balance sheet in a -- and we don't see major capex in next 1 or 2 years.

items.statement: Approved acquisition of 10% in one JV to make it wholly owned subsidiary; aim to merge all JVs
items.quote: one of the subsidiary, we have in the Board meeting, we have taken approval to acquire 10%. Rishi Kajaria: One of the joint ventures to make it a wholly owned subsidiary

items.statement: Hiring 3-4 C-level executives within 1-2 months
items.quote: We are hiring at least 3 to 4 C-level people, which we will disclose when they join within next 1 or 2 months.

items.statement: Forensic audit by EY underway for fraud; amount not beyond prior disclosure; strengthening controls
items.quote: We have appointed a forensic auditor also. Ernst & Young, we have appointed. They have yet to give the report but prima facie the fraud amount because I know this question will come again, so I'm answering. So the fraud amount is not beyond what we have st ated earlier

items.statement: Ad spend INR24 cr in Q3; FY26 total lower than FY25 due to no dealer meet and vendor renegotiation
items.quote: We spent roughly INR24 crores in quarter 3. This is what... Sanjeev Agarwal: We spent around INR24 crores in Q3. Keshav Lahoti: Got it. Sanjeev Agarwal: Little lower than the Q3 of the previous year. But in the fourth quarter, we intend to increase it much higher than

items.statement: TMD order book is Rs 2,600 crore, of which actual orders are Rs 1,500 crore
items.quote: With respect to the order book, we currently hold an order book of 2600 crores of which the actual orders are around 1500 crores.

items.statement: Textile demand recovery delayed by tariff uncertainty; order flow better than last 12 months but confidence low
items.quote: However, the factors which are affecting, especially in terms of tariff which has come in, these are the things which have, were not factors which we know in the past.

items.statement: TMD continues five-day working week due to low capacity utilization; MTD at 75% utilization with room to grow
items.quote: As we have mentioned earlier, we continue a five-day working week for Textile Machinery Division on account of lower capacity utilization.

items.statement: MTD and ATC margins improved; composite billing at 20% of ATC turnover aided margins; Foundry has cost pass-through
items.quote: The composite as a percentage of turnover stands at 20%. Right and yes, there was billing on composite for few items and that is where the margins have become better for the current quarter.

items.statement: Commodity cost increases being absorbed via value engineering; no price hikes possible in muted demand; Foundry and ATC have pass-through clauses
items.quote: We are, we have our own process through which either we look at alternates, there's a value engineering work which we do. But as of now considering the market as it is, there is no way we feel that i t is something which can be observed by the market

items.statement: MTD mix is 75% turning centers, 25% machining centers; focus on expanding machining center footprint
items.quote: with respect to MTD, the machining center, turning center, you can take a percentage of 75% turning centers and 25% m achining centers

items.statement: ATC order book grew 20% to ~Rs 360 crore deliverable over 1.5 years; 90% export, tariff discussions ongoing
items.quote: It is around 360 odd crores which is deliverable over one and a half years. That's what it is.

items.statement: TMD export share 9% of sales; LMW Global turnover Rs 128 crore (9M), loss Rs 25 crore; China turnover Rs 52 crore, loss Rs 11 crore
items.quote: the ratio of domestic to export to spares stands at 65% domestic, 9% exports and 26% spares.

items.statement: India spindle age 40-44 million, ~40% older than 15-20 years; running spindles at 90-95%+ utilization
items.quote: we would put the current spindle age between 40 to 42 million or 40 to 44 million, give or take, you know, few million. So out of this we would say almost 40% would be older spindles

items.statement: Continuing investment in shop floor, IoT, new product development during downturn; ATC capex for new orders
items.quote: We continue to invest in our shop floor and today the technology has changed. We continue to invest in IoT. We continue to make our process efficient and costs efficient and these are the time we also invest in our new product development.

items.statement: Tariff uncertainty postponing investment decisions; EU FTA limited direct benefit; Bangladesh, Turkey challenges persist
items.quote: Because of the external factors there is post ponement of decision. But we look out for, you know, whatever is the order flow and how we can get more orders into the system.

items.statement: Sold 10% stake in Super Sales; not a core investment, no restructuring indicated
items.quote: With respect to super sales, it is an. It was not a poor investment which we wanted to hold and that is the reason we have sold the sales of the shares of super sales.

items.statement: Small VRS scheme (Rs 1.29 crore) to cut fixed costs during lean period
items.quote: for the period ended Q3 there is a 1.29 crore which was incurred towards VRS.

items.statement: No specific revenue or margin guidance given; MTD outlook strong, TMD recovery timing uncertain
items.quote: Yes, we are quite optimistic about Machine Tool Division. Especially the fact that we are seeing more numbers on the machining centers, VMCs. So, the demand outlook is quite strong.

items.statement: Textile machinery competition already consolidated in India/China; Machine Tool competition increasing as India becomes manufacturing hub
items.quote: the entire the machine ry manufacturing to a large extent in fact to a probably 95% and above extent has moved to of course in India and also to China.

items.statement: EU FTA supports ATC/Foundry exports to Europe; no direct TMD/MTD export benefit; one-time Rs 11.5 crore Labour Code impact
items.quote: For the previous year there is an exceptional item of around rupees 11.5 crores during the quarter and period ending December 25 which is a one-time impact on account of the new Labour Code regulations.

items.statement: Seamless pipe margins improved slightly as expected; ERW margins improved due to product mix; overall EBITDA higher; margin increase driven by reversal of prior inventory markdown
items.quote: This was a fairly regular quarter with a slight increase in margin on the seamless pipes front, which was expected because we had communicated the same i n the previous quarter. On the ERW front also, margins improved because of improvement in product mix

items.statement: Order book at INR1,302 crores as of 20th January; 33% from ONGC and Oil India; proportion of oil sector orders increased vs previous quarter
items.quote: The current order book is at INR1,302 crores, of which 33% comprises ONGC and Oil India orders. This order book is broadly similar to the order book which was present in the previous quarter. The only difference between these two order books is that the proportion of oil sector orders have increased in the most recent order book.

items.statement: Value-added products defined as cold drawn, cylinder, drill, sour service subsea pipes and premium connections; company makes 4 of 5; no drill pipe orders currently; good order book for cylinder, sour service subsea and cold drawn pipes
items.quote: Value -added products are col d drawn pipes, cylinder pipes, drill pipes, sour service subsea seamless pipes and premium connections. I think these are the 5 key categories of value- added products, out of which we manufacture 4 of these. So in the previous quarter, there were no orders for drill pipes. Even now we don't have orders for drill pipes. Cylinder pipes we had a good order book in the p

items.statement: Two projects started: cold drawn pipes project completed; Telangana finishing line with INR90 crores purchase orders issued, portion to start this quarter; premium connections production expected in ~6 months
items.quote: The capacity expansion plan that we have detailed in one of the slides in the presentation, out of that, we have started two projects, the cold drawn pipes project, which has been completed. And the other one is the finishing line at Telangana, in which we have issued purchase orders of INR90 crores, and we'll be able to start some portion of it in the current quarter.

items.statement: Telangana finishing line adds 1 lakh ton finishing capacity (not production capacity); resolves bottleneck for existing 2 lakh ton unutilized production capacity; active utilizable capacity 5.5 lakh tons vs 6 lakh total
items.quote: It will not increase the production capacity. It will increase the finishing capacity. So we already have production capacity of 2 lakh tons, which is curr ently unutilized because commensurate finishing facility is not in place. That bottleneck is being resolved by the finishing line which is currently being implemented

items.statement: Demand dependent on government oil & gas expenditure; dispatches maintained at ~1.01-1.03 lakh tons/quarter despite muted government spending; order book replenished without compromising tonnage
items.quote: In the second quarter, we dispatched 1,03,000 tons of pipe. In the third quarter, we dispatched 1,01,000 tons of pipe. And in spite of a challenging economic environment in which government expenditure was also muted, we have managed to replenish the order book.

items.statement: Imports remain 20-25% of domestic industry (9 lakh tons); Chinese dumping continues unabated; margins maintained and improved despite dumping
items.quote: No. No. And it has not reduced. And despite the unabated dumping from China, we have managed to maintain and improve upon our margins, and Maharashtra Seamless Limited 29 January 2026 the tonnage that we have dispatched has not declined despite the challenging economic

items.statement: Order book backed by back-to-back raw material booking; raw material price increases passed to customers; pre-safeguard duty orders already covered with raw material
items.quote: Our order book is supported by back -to-back booking of raw materials. So if raw material prices will increase, then the same will be passed on to the customer. And for orders which were in place prior to the implementation of safeguard duty, we had already covered those orders with raw material.

items.statement: No specific guidance given; margins not expected to decline materially; EBITDA per ton seen in INR10,000-15,000 range
items.quote: We do not give out guidance specifically, but the only thing that I can tell you from some experience is that we don't see margins to de cline materially from here. I think it will remain in the range of INR10,000 to INR15,000 per ton

items.statement: Conserving cash for inorganic opportunities; only distressed assets at comfortable cost; United Seamless Tubulaar acquired for INR477 crores + INR73 crores reactivation; generates INR100-200 crores EBITDA/year; tax savings ~INR375 crores fr
items.quote: We acquired it for INR477 crores, and we invested an additional INR73 crores to reactivate the mill. So against a total capital expenditure of INR550 crores, that mill generates between INR100 crores to INR200 crores of EBITDA every year depending on the margin profile. In addition to that, there were accumulated losses and unabsorbed depreciation in excess of INR1,500 crores in United Seamless Tu

items.statement: Dividend quadrupled from FY22 to FY24; maintained quadrupled level in FY25 despite lower profit; management focused on long-term value creation over short-term distribution
items.quote: We have quadrupled the dividend which is being paid out to the shareholders in the period from FY '22 to FY '24. And in FY '25, even with a lower profit, we maintained the quadrupled level of dividend which was paid out.

items.statement: CFO changes due to unique factors per individual; current CFO Arup Mandal in place ~1.5 years; IR/Finance head with company 14 years
items.quote: The changes in the CFO was on account of various factors which were unique to each CFO. So right now, Mr. Arup Mandal is the CFO, and he's been with us for about a year and half. But in addition to the CFO point, I would also like to mention that I have been with the organization for 14 years.

items.statement: Exports improved previous quarter; reviewing India-EU FTA impact; premium connections market 50,000-1 lakh tons/year currently supplied by Jindal Saw and imports; company will need to take share
items.quote: Exports have seen some improvement in the previous quarter. Maybe in the next quarter's call, we'll be able to update you better on this FTA point.

items.statement: Growth dependent on government oil & gas capex; if budget doesn't increase expenditure, market won't grow; company remains only survivor in cyclical seamless pipe industry where all peers bankrupted
items.quote: Since the Union Budget is only a few days away, maybe I'll be able to address your query better after the budget because we are dependent on government expenditure for expansion and growth. So if government expenditure does not improve, then the market will not grow, which will directly impact us.

items.statement: Aerospace EBITDA margin target 23-25% long term; Auto EBITDA margin target above 15% yearly
items.quote: I think in the Aero, we could look at 23% to 25% in the long run. And in Auto, we would definitely break the 15% barrier and aim towards a higher rate on a yearly basis.

items.statement: Andhra Pradesh capex ~INR 500 cr Aero and ~INR 430 cr Auto over 5 years
items.value: INR 500 cr Aero; INR 430 cr Auto
items.quote: Over the next 5 years, basically, we are looking at about INR 500 crores in Aero and about INR 430 crores in Auto.

items.statement: Annual capex ~INR 100 cr each for Aerospace and Auto & Precision Technologies
items.quote: I think we are talking about INR 100 crore annual capex for Aerospace as well as INR100 crore annual capex for Auto & Precision Technologies.

items.statement: New Sinnar plant commissioned January 2025; Andhra facility to be ready as existing capacity fills up
items.quote: We built a new plant in Sinnar in January. We have space there. So that will be filled up. We have some capacity available in different plants. So we are optimizing capacity and building capacity as we speak.

items.statement: Aerospace order book ~2.5-3 years of revenue; growing with >1 new part developed daily
items.quote: Typically, like I explained last time, you have 5-year contracts and 10-year contracts. And, it depends on which portion of the contract you are. Normally, the contracts are just renewed on expiry because -- or it grows in market share. But in general, you're averaging a 2.5 -year window in most cases, and you can round it off to three sometimes depending on your 10 -year contracts, right, because

items.statement: Q3 FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin 14.3% vs 13.3% YoY; 9M FY26 14.7% vs 15.8% YoY
items.quote: Raymond Limited continued its growth momentum, delivering -- and delivered a robust quarterly performance, reporting a total income of INR 580 crores, reflecting an 18% increase compared to the same quarter of the previo us year, while EBITDA stood at INR 83 crores and an EBITDA margin of 14.3% in Q3 FY '26 versus a total income of INR 493 crores in Q3 FY '25, delivering an EBITDA of INR 65 crores

items.statement: Aerospace Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin 18.6% vs 19.8% YoY; 9M FY26 20.9% vs 20.8% YoY
items.quote: At the segment level, the Aerospace & Defense business reported robust performance with a revenue of INR 105 crores, indicating a 4 9% year-on-year growth and an EBITDA of INR 19 crores, indicating a 39% year-on-year growth and an EBITDA margin of 18.6% in Q3 of FY '26 versus revenue of INR 70 crores and an EBITDA of INR 14 crores with an EBITDA margin of 19.8% in Q3 FY '25.

items.statement: Auto & Precision Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin 13.7% vs 10.4% YoY; 9M FY26 12.7% vs 10.4% YoY
items.quote: At the segment level here, the Precision Technology & Automotive Components reported a revenue of INR 417 crores, which is up 15% year-on-year growth, with an EBITDA of INR 57 crores with a growth of 51% year-on-year growth and an EBITDA margin of 13.7% in Q3 FY '26 versus revenue of INR 363 crores with an EBITDA of INR 38 crores and an EBITDA margin of 10.4% in Q3 FY '25.

items.statement: Aerospace demand strong: Boeing back at high production, inventories depleting, schedule increases; LEAP-1A growing 10-15%, LEAP-1B 15-20%
items.quote: is back, and they are producing at very high levels. So, I think the trend is very good, although we've still not reached pre-COVID levels, so which means the potential is even higher. Clearly, the supply chains are getting better. And therefore, the opportunities are improving because as the inventory is being eaten up, the opportunities are opening up

items.statement: Auto & Precision demand supported by China Plus One, integration synergies, operational efficiencies
items.quote: We continue with our strategy to expand into new international geographies and industrial sectors. We are observing business momentum across domestic and international markets supported by China Plus One strategy, integration synergies and focused operational efficiencies across all segments.

items.statement: Aerospace material costs (Inconel, aluminum) fully passed through in contracts; localization pressure may lower costs in 2 years
items.quote: Well, there is first of all, in all of our contracts, the materials are written by the customer contracts, so which means if Inconel goes up, the prices go up, if Inconel goes down, the prices will go down. Having said that, there is a pressur e to localize materials, which will then ultimately come to a lower level in the long run.

items.statement: Receivable days not crossing 100 days; revenue and profit growth expected to outpace working capital increase
items.quote: Receivable days are also not very different than the average industry receivable days that you see. And, there is nothing which is actually crossing 100 days or so. In fact, our revenue and profitability growth is expected to outpace any increase in the working capital. That's how we see it

items.statement: Debt-free with net cash surplus INR 214 cr as of December 2025
items.quote: We continue to remain a debt -free business with a net cash surplus of INR 214 crores in December 2025.

items.statement: Aerospace: ~21% US, ~60% Europe; Auto & Precision: ~10% US, ~30% Europe
items.quote: Our 60 percentage of Aerospace business comes from Europe and 30 percentage of Auto & Precision Technologies business comes from Europe. I think currently, Europe and India, some of the deals are in advanced stages.

items.statement: LEAP engine parts: 300-350 part numbers across 1A/1B/1C models; market share progression from 35% to 65% on >50% of parts
items.quote: So basically, we supply around between 300-and 350-part numbers depending on which model of 1A, 1B and even 1C is being introduced now. So roughly, that is the mix. There are many common products that go to 1A and 1B, but some products are also specific.

items.statement: Aerospace kit value per aircraft ~0.2-0.3% or ~$35,000 on one platform; low volume high mix business
items.quote: So, at the moment, it's -- you can say that on an estimate, it's about 0.2% to 0.3%, right, but closer to maybe $35,000, if you look at. But that's in one case, right? We have so many customers in so many places and so many part numbers.

items.statement: One-time INR 14 cr labor code implementation impact in exceptional items
items.quote: Yes. That INR14 crores, yes, that's on account of labor code-related onetime impact that we had.

items.statement: US tariffs creating logistical complexities and temporary scheduling delays in Aerospace
items.quote: While internal growth indicators remain strong, the near-term outlook is currently influenced by external macroeconomic factors, specifically global trade pressures spreading from U.S. tariffs. These have introduced some logistical complexities and results in some temporary scheduling delays across the industry.

items.statement: 5-6 strategic engine partners with approvals; multiyear agreements evolving to co-design and value engineering
items.quote: The business is witnessing a surge in RFQ activity, particularly in aero engines, landing gears and structural component segments. This is co mplemented by growing interest from global OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers who are increasingly looking to India for supply chain diversification. Raymond is capitalizing on this trend by entering multiyear strategic supplier agreements that go beyond build -to-pr

items.statement: Aerospace: >1 new part developed daily; expanding on 15+ engine programs including LEAP and GTF
items.quote: We are still averaging more than one new part every day. So that will keep growing as well. So yes, the order book keeps improving and keeps increasing as we increase our sales.

items.statement: Value unlocking (separate listings) premature; need tariff uncertainty to settle, Andhra benefits realization, critical EBITDA scale
items.quote: think the first thing to my mind is that this whole tariff thing, uncertainty, etcetera, which has -- all of this has to settle down. Businesses have to stabilize because at this stage, business performance tends to be volatile in this ever -changing environment. I gue ss that's sort of one, to my mind, which is very critical. The second milestone to my mind which is critical is that we have to re

items.statement: SAP HANA implementation and team integration over last 1-1.5 years driving efficiency gains
items.quote: The teams have been formed and therefore -- and we've adopted like SAP HANA is coming into play. So all the systems and the hard work that we did over the last 1, 1.5 years are slowly playing out and helping us to increase these margins.

items.statement: Q3 decorative volume grew 7.9% despite shorter festive season and prolonged monsoon; rural markets outperformed urban
items.quote: When we look at, from a point of view of the overall volume and value of the decorative business, we had a little bit of a compressed festive season. All of you know, we had earlier Diwali, and 14 | therefore we got only about 15 odd days in October which was festive. We also had a prolonged monsoon which stepped into October as well. So, it was not great. So, overall, November and December, were

items.statement: Rural demand stronger than urban in November-December due to good rainfall
items.quote: One of the things which we saw was, that the rural parts batted better than the urban centres, possibly a good rainfall which has augured well. I think the mood has been good. So, November and December that is a clear trend in terms of what we see, that rural markets were slightly ahead of the urban centres.

items.statement: Overall coatings volume growth 8.3% and value growth 4.4% in Q3, driven by industrial segment
items.quote: When we see this the volume growth jumps to about 8.3% from the 7.9% in decorative and the value growth for all coatings jumps to 4.4%. So, I think it literally is closer to the mid-digit level in terms of what we spoke about last time.

items.statement: Standalone gross margin 44.9% (+200bps YoY), PBDIT margin 21.4% (+100bps YoY) in Q3
items.quote: At the same time, when we look at the gross margin, one of the highest Gross Margins I would say over the quarters in terms of what we have registered, about 44.9%, 200 bps points higher, and I think other than the deflation, we have also seen a lot of efficiencies in terms of the cost which we have brought in giving us a boost in terms of overall gross margins. The PBDIT growth is almost closer t

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin 44.3% (+200bps YoY), PBDIT margin 20.1% (+90bps YoY) in Q3
items.quote: At a consolidated level, when we see again, from a top line perspective we are at about 4% yoy growth, a part of the industrial sale is not here. The Gross Margin is 44.3% which is higher by about 200 bps points. Again, in terms of the PBDIT growth, almost 9% growth here, with PBDIT margin of 20.1%, which is also higher about by 90 bps points.

items.statement: Raw material deflation of ~1.1% in Q3, driven by lower monomer and TiO2 prices
items.quote: I think the paint market has gone through a certain bit of deflation, given the fact that today consumption worldwide is something which is down. And we see larger raw materials, whether it is monomers, whether it is TiO 2 - the prices have been low. And we have seen a material deflation of about 1.1% as well, which is also really helping us in the gross margins we are deriving in this quarter.

items.statement: Distribution expanded by 3,500-4,000 retailers this year; reach now 1.6+ lakh outlets
items.quote: We also continue to expand our distribution footprint . W e have added about 3,500 to 4,000 retailers this year overall, and our reach is now in more than 1.6 lakh retail outlets.

items.statement: White cement plant started; next phase of backward integration beginning next year
items.quote: As you know that this is a journey, which we are on to, we have started our white cement plant, and we are now really looking at the next level in terms of what basically starts in the coming year in terms of the whole area of backward integration, which will give us a lot of advantages as we go ahead.

items.statement: Beautiful Home stores network expanded to 74 stores across India
items.quote: Our Beautiful Home stores network, which is doing quite well overall, expands to about 74 stores across the country.

items.statement: January demand trajectory continuing December momentum; Q4 volume growth expected in 8-10% band
items.quote: I think we are seeing some of the trajectory of December into January as well, for sure. And as we look at it, given the fact that the second quarter for us was at about 10.9%, this quarter is about a high -single-digit. I think as we go ahead, this band would remain, in terms of what we would be able to target for the Q4 as well.

items.statement: International business grew 6.3% value (4.2% constant currency) in Q3; strong growth in Sri Lanka, UAE, Ethiopia; PBT up 26%
items.quote: what we have done. We see there is a 6.3% value growth, in constant currency terms i t boils down to about 4.2%, given the fact that INR has depreciated. Very strong growth which has been coming in units of Sri Lanka, UAE, Ethiopia, and that is something which has given us a larger growth. If you can see largely, all the units have grown, except for the Pacific units. Even PBT has been very strong

items.statement: Labour code impact: Rs 63.74 cr consolidated, Rs 60.56 cr standalone exceptional charge in Q3
items.quote: There are two exceptional items in the quarter which are there, one is all of you are aware , the impact of the labour code , which basically has a component in terms of gratuity and leave accumulation. And that is something which is Rs. 63.74 crores.

items.statement: White Teak impairment: Rs 94 cr consolidated, Rs 106 cr standalone for Obgenix Software
items.value: Rs 94 cr consolidated, Rs 106 cr standalone
items.quote: As I mentioned that while we got the top line in White Teak the month of October was not good. I think the whole bottom line was affected here. So, we have to take another impairment here, and that has been something which is close to about Rs. 94 crores which has been taken in White Teak which is the Obgenix Software Private Limited. Similarly, on a standalone basis, the two exceptional items, on

items.statement: Trained 6.7 lakh people under skilling program; targeting 10 lakh this year; employee engagement scores healthy

items.quote: We've been consistently saying, I think you can look at expense growth of about 15%, plus, minus 1-2. That's what we've always said.

items.statement: Yields: Equity ~53 bps, Debt ~25 bps, ETF ~20 bps, Overall ~37 bps; Gold ETF ~60 bps, Silver ETF ~30 bps

items.quote: Coming to specifics, the removal of the 5 basis points exit load will surely have some impact on the overall industry equity-oriented AUM and even the revision in TER slab will have some impact on the bigger scheme but on the smaller scheme it will see some benefit. Lastly, the brokerage on the cash transaction was reduced to 6 basis against 12 basis but the average brokerage used to be in the ran

items.statement: Yields may come down 1-2 bps year after year; focus on building efficiency to absorb
items.quote: Over the last 2 -3 years, as I have always mentioned, irrespective if it is not the regulator, whether it is the regulatory push, whether it is the investor demand, one needs to be mentally prepared that the yields can come down by 1 or 2 basis points year after year and that is the direction we will keep moving.

items.statement: SIF strategy: 6-member team, focus on profitability over AUM, higher yields, not running like liquid or passive fund
items.quote: We are very clear. We would like to add value to the investors and do it at higher yields. So, we do not want to run it like a liquid fund. We do not want to run it like a passive fund. This is a specialized product. We clearly see if you can add value to the investor, the investor will be willing to pay. So, our strategy for SIF will be not AUM but more profitability.

items.statement: Small-cap fund: stopped lump sum investments ~2 years ago, continue SIP only, no negative net flows yet
items.quote: We have stopped taking lump sum investments. We were very clear that at that point in time, the market was getting more heated, and I think we were right to have arrested more flows in this fund. As we speak, we continue to be in that camp.

items.statement: Flexi Cap fund: late starter in 2021, mid/small-cap correction impacted near-term performance, focusing on stability to gain market share
items.quote: We were late starters in 2021 with this fund. And it's a five -year product at this point in time. The mid and small -cap correction which has happened has impacted, does impact the fund performance in the near term. And what we are looking at is that how do we bring in more stability into this performance.

items.statement: ESOP expense for Q3 FY26 ~Rs. 11 crore; expected ~Rs. 26 crore for next financial year
items.quote: ESOP expense for this quarter was around Rs. 11 crores. And for next year, of the current ESOP scheme, we are expecting ESOP expense rate of around Rs. 26 crores for the next financial year.

items.statement: Labour Code one-time gratuity impact taken in Q3; no further material incremental impact expected
items.quote: So, the Labour Code impact is the one -time changes to the gratuity. There are still some clarifications still awaited. So, we will do a needful, if anything, in the March quarter. But the one-time impact is on the gratuity changes on the basic and definition of wages, which has been notified, which has been taken in the financials.

items.statement: Q3 TCV hit record INR 662 crores, up 20% sequentially

items.statement: Added 34 new logos in Q3

items.quote: DSO days improved by another 3 days to 79 days as we had guided. We also reported strong operating cash flow during this quarter at INR92 crores which translates to 105% of my EBITDA.

items.quote: Our balance sheet remains strong, with a healthy liquidity and net cash position improving from INR113 crores in quarter 2 FY '26 to INR125 crores in quarter 3.

items.statement: Management reaffirmed 40% year-on-year revenue growth guidance for FY26

items.statement: Asphalt segment projected to generate INR80-100 crores revenue in next 12-18 months

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin improved to 11.75% from 9.38% in Q3 FY25

items.quote: The contract manufacturing portion which is a highly profitable venture increased from a 35% of turnover to a 48%. From a numbers perspective, it increased from INR65 crores to INR130 crores almost two times.

items.quote: Our current borrowings are in the range of around INR40 crores. And this is only the working capital facilities and a small long-term debt of about INR6 crores.

items.quote: So these deposits are refundable in nature. These are multi -year deposits, as in when the concerned plant utilization increases and improves to about 80% plus. items.statement: All B2B transactions conducted with proper GST compliance; suppliers also charge GST
items.quote: Sir, we are in the B2B segment. We do not do retail business. So all the B2B business that we do, the proper GST is applied on it. And all the business that we do, all the INR350 -INR400 crores or INR500 crores business that we do, it is done on paper only after applying proper GST.

items.statement: Targets revenue of INR1,050-1,100 crores by FY28 with EBITDA margin of 16-18%

items.statement: Cooling agents (WS23, WS03), clove/eugenol, citral derivatives, phenol derivatives (Anisole, MEHQ, Guaiacol, 4-MAP, BHA) at Dahej; menthofuran pricing $80-200/kg depending on purity
items.quote: Pricing could start from $80 a kg, going up to $200, depending on the level of purity and the type of product it is. So, it is on the isomer ratios.

items.statement: Top 5 customer profile stable for ~decade; ingredients approved in compositions create high switching costs; initial Dahej sales via distributors/traders, majors approval by year 2-3
items.quote: So, a large portion of our business is with sticky customers. And the numbers of the top five customers pretty much have not changed in the last decade or so because once your ingredients are approved in their composition, it becomes very difficult for them to onboard someone else and bring them on.

items.statement: ~60% of exports to US in FY25; actively diversifying to Europe and other territories; EU trade deal expected to benefit flavors & fragrances
items.quote: So far in terms of FY 25 a large portion of our exports, almost 60% of our total exports was to the US market. And majority of it, as you rightly mentioned is under tariffs.

items.statement: Krystal inventory days expected to fall vs current 45% of earnings as working capital; evaluating factoring (implemented for 2 customers last quarter) to reduce debtor days
items.quote: But given the nature of products like, for example, phenol derivatives, citral derivatives, for that matter, even clove and eugenol and f urther derivatives would not require us to carry so much inventory because they're easily available. items.quote: On reported pr ofitability, profitability was impacted by higher depreciation of INR8.7 crores, which is a non-cash charge, following capitalization of a large portion of approximately INR250 crores incurred capex out of the total planned capex of around INR270 crores at the Dahej facility

items.statement: US tariff uncertainty persists; US+1 strategy underway but long due-diligence cycle; geopolitical shifts add challenge; GST issue expected to stay for some time
items.quote: We've done a lot of work to do this, but clearly the headwinds from a standpoint of changing global scenarios by the current geopolitics that we see also makes it very challenging. But we are working on a dual one US plus one strategy from a standpoint of getting that approved.

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance of INR1,500 crores expected to be significantly exceeded
items.quote: INR1,500 crores revenue guidance for FY26. It's still intact. Kartik Teltia: I hope we exceed that significantly

items.statement: Executed order book of INR2,600 crores as of Dec 31, 2025 with 7 EPC projects and 2 BESS orders
items.quote: As on 31st December 2025, we have an executed order book aggregating to almost INR2,600 crores, comprising 7 EPC projects and 2 BESS orders.

items.statement: Expect to execute ~20% of order book in Q4 FY26, balance in FY27
items.quote: So out of this order book, maybe we will execute maybe about 20% this year or round about that. And the balance will be executed in the next year.

items.statement: Solar module manufacturing line (1.552 GW) commissioned in Roorkee with ALMM approval received Dec 23, 2025
items.quote: On the manufacturing front, we successfully commenced operations of our solar module manufacturing line in Roorkee during the quarter, and also received the ALMM approval for 1.552 gigawatts of annual capacity.

items.statement: 1.2 GW solar cell manufacturing facility under construction, commercial operations targeted for June 2027
items.quote: In parallel, construction of our 1.2 gigawatt solar cell manufacturing facility is progressing as planned, with commercial operations targeted for June '27.

items.statement: 3.4 GW BESS manufacturing facility to be operational by end of March 2026
items.quote: BESS will get commissioned in the next couple of months, maybe end of March. So BESS capacity of 3.4 gigawatt will also be available for us to sell in the market.

items.statement: Junction box manufacturing line expected operational by end of March 2026 for backward integration
items.quote: We are also strengthening backward integration through the establishment of a junction box manufacturing line, which will support our solar module operations and improve cost efficiencies. The facility is expected to be operational by end of March 2026.

items.statement: Silver prices quadrupled from INR500 to INR2,000 per panel, constituting ~25% of panel cost; market adjusting with PPA price increases
items.quote: Currently, module manufacturers are kind of suffering because the silver prices have kind of quadrupled. So cost of silver in a single solar panel has gone up from about INR500 to about INR2,000. So that's a challenge. But the market does tend to adjust to higher prices and the PPA tend to adjust.

items.statement: BESS cell prices risen 20-25% to $65/kWh from expected $40; recent tenders show 30% price correction
items.quote: On the flip side, the supply side, most of the BESS cells are coming from China. The prices have shot up by almost 20%-25%. So you will see that initially the tender, there was a euphoria in the market and people were bidding, assuming prices of BESS coming down to maybe $40 which are hovering around $65.

items.statement: Module line running at full capacity; monthly output ramping: 50 MW Jan, 70 MW Feb, 80-90 MW from March
items.quote: So we are expecting -- in January, we are expecting about 50 megawatt. In Feb, it should go up to about 70. And from March onwards, you should see maybe somewhere between 80 to 90 megawatt.

items.statement: Module line expected to add INR70-80 crores PAT per GW at full utilization
items.quote: Typical line, if you just do tooling, should give you a profit of somewhere about INR70 crores to INR80 crores PAT on a gigawatt scale.

items.statement: DCR mandate from June 2026; cell line commercialization targeted Dec 2026-Mar 2027 to capture DCR margin upside (cell cost INR7-8/W vs market INR14-15/W)
items.quote: We believe that the cost of manufacturing a DCR cell is somewhere between INR7 to INR8 per watt. Whereas in the market, we are currently able to procure them somewhere between INR14 to INR15.

items.statement: Active discussions with ~14 C&I factories in North India for BESS as UPS/genset backup replacement
items.quote: Sir, we are already discussing with about 14 factories not to replace the generator but to add our BESS product as a UPS for them and a backup for about one hour and after which the generators can kick in.

items.statement: Competitive advantage in BESS from integrated EPC+manufacturing model vs pure manufacturers (Pace Digitek) or traders (Micromax, Patanjali) paying higher duties
items.quote: The advantage we have is that we are also an EPC company. So we can engage with developers and do an end-to-end project where we do the EPC and supply both. That definitely gives us an advantage over that kind of competition.

items.statement: Net worth INR7,991 million, total debt INR2,553 million, debt-to-equity 0.32x as of Dec 31, 2025
items.quote: On the balance sheet side, as of December 31, 2025, our net worth stands at approximately INR7,991 million, while total debt is around INR2,553 million, resulting in debt-to-equity ratio of 0.32 times.

items.statement: Government seeking industry input on Make in India timelines for BESS; DISCOMs now requiring solar+BESS or RTC projects instead of pure solar
items.quote: In terms of BESS, government has now asked our suggestions on how quickly we can do it under Make in India. So they have given a timeline that has been shared with many manufacturers on which comments have now been sought.

items.statement: SJVN projects (2x Bhuj) delayed 24 months due to land non-allocation; arbitration initiated to recover retention money and storage costs; no negative P&L impact expected
items.quote: And today in January 2026, we are yet to receive that land. So we have gone to the court to request the court or to request SJVN to start arbitration proceedings in this so that we can close out the contract because it has already been 2 years. We, in terms of negative financial implications, there will be no negative financial implication.

items.quote: Rishabh is stepping down as executive role and will be a Non-Executive Director on the company. Rishabh -- so one of our shareholders is Pioneer Facor IT, which is one of the main line of business for Rishabh as well. One of the subsidiaries is going for listing there. He's going to be the Executive Director there.

items.statement: US exports down due to 50% duty; Chinese panels stopped; actual Indian module capacity ~80-90 GW vs 140 GW claimed
items.quote: If you see exports to US, I think are down because of 50% duty and US is not pushing for a lot of solar, which was a big market for Indian exporters. Chinese solar panels have stopped coming in, but India, it's not 144 gigawatts, to be honest. Currently, the capacity, actual capacity should be close to 80-90 gigawatts.

items.statement: FY27 expected to be strong with revenue growth driven by BESS, module manufacturing (INR1,000+ crores incremental), and 25-30% EPC growth
items.quote: If we are able to keep our module line running for the whole year, and if we sell that capacity into the market, it should add about INR1000 to crores to the top line. EPC, I believe, will see a 25% to 30% if the market sustains, should see a very good growth of about 25% to 30% next year as well. Third is BESS. BESS is something that should add a lot to our top line.
