items.quote: So, essentially, the thing is that the table change impact on the pricing is a little different for the 3-Star and a little different for the 5-Star. 3-Star is a little lesser, but 5-Star is a very, very significant increase. So, the increase will impact the 5-Star more.

items.statement: Chennai plant capacity 1 million units, expanding to 1.5 million in 1-2 months; utilization expected 85-90% this summer; Pantnagar at 100%
items.quote: And the Chennai plant, we have built a capacity of 1 million units, which we are in the process of expanding to 1.5 million capacity in another 1-2 months. Our sense is that this summer season, we would have maximized the capacity utilization to almost between 85% to 90% or so, Mr. Jain.

items.statement: EMPS consolidated order book around Rs. 6,100 crores with healthy pipeline; domestic projects booking and executing across verticals
items.quote: With a robust, consolidated order book of around Rs. 6,100 crores and a healthy order pipeline, the segment is well-positioned to drive steady growth and deliver consistent performance over the medium term.

items.statement: Working capital tightly managed with improved inventory and receivables ahead of season; balanced profile at quarter exit
items.quote: Working capital was tightly managed in Q3, with improved inventory and receivables ahead of upcoming season, supported by availability of priority SKUs and steady project buildings and collections.

items.statement: Channel inventory at 5-6 weeks, expected to deplete by mid-March; structured network expansion tracking 29,000 counters across 19,000 pin codes
items.quote: Inventory of Voltas, my sense is that we are talking about a few weeks, 5 to 6 weeks of inventory is there in the channel. And it's just a matter of time. By March middle, I suppose, the entire inventory will get finished.

items.statement: Added decent number of channel partners directly and through distribution; focus on higher wallet share in modern trade (Reliance, Croma, Vijay Sales) and entering 85 regional retailers in South and West
items.quote: We have added a decent number of channel partners either directly through as a direct billing point. We have also added a fair amount of counters through our distribution network. That's as far as the General Trade is concerned. terms of modern trade, we have a fair presence across all the three Modern Trade

items.statement: Focus on manufacturing and data center MEP projects (fast track, 9-12 months); selective in commercial buildings; cherry-picking Electrical and Water projects
items.quote: The focus currently is that we want to have a larger pie of the manufacturing and the data center market. We are also looking at the steady flow. These are generally fast track projects which will quickly give, are turned around within less than 9 months to 12 months.

items.statement: Data center chiller bidding with new technology partner alliance offering most energy efficient Screw and Centrifugal chillers; competing with York, Trane, Johnson Controls in district cooling
items.quote: So, we probably offer the best energy efficient products in the Screw category. And we also offer the best energy efficient products in the Centrifugal category. Centrifugal has two variants. One is the regular Centrifugal Chillers and the second Oil-free Chillers. Across these three segments, we have probably the most energy efficient products.

items.statement: BEE new efficiency table effective Jan 1 2026 prohibits manufacturing old products; old stock can be sold till June end; company fully ready with refreshed lineups and calibrated pricing
items.quote: The Company is fully ready and realigned for the new BEE efficiency table with refreshed lineups and calibrated pricing architecture in place and is geared to meet seasonal demand with aligned production plans across Pantnagar and the new Chennai factory.

items.statement: Copper is the big BOM item; aluminum impact not heavy; commodity inflation and rupee depreciation being monitored closely
items.quote: The commodity and dollar, actually both of them are on an upward trend as you can imagine, essentially copper. The impact of aluminum is not like on the overall BOM is not that heavy. But copper is the big sort of item on the BOM.

items.statement: Committed to cost optimization through value engineering, better inventory planning; cautious on commodity and currency impact
items.quote: In terms of margin, we are committed to further optimize costs through value engineering, better inventory planning, while being cautious about the impact of commodity and currency fluctuations.

items.statement: Textile Machinery Division adversely impacted by 50% US tariff on textile products weighing on MSMEs and domestic demand
items.quote: The Textile Machinery Division (TMD) business was adversely impacted by macro backdrop, notably the 50% U.S. tariff imposition on certain textile products, which weighed on MSMEs and led to production cuts and softer domestic demand for yarns and fabrics.

items.statement: Chennai plant backward integration includes sheet metal, powder coating, indoor plastic injection, oil and fin shop; CAPEX details to be discussed offline
items.quote: One is the entire Sheet Metal work, which is the outdoor body. Second is the Powder Coating and the Painting of that outdoor unit, which is, again, a high-value addition sort of process. The third is the entire Indoor Unit Plastic Injection, Moulding of that internal plastic part and a fully backward integrated Oil and Fin Shop.

items.statement: Multiple moving parts: commodity inflation, currency depreciation, BEE table change impact, old vs new inventory mix making margin trajectory uncertain
items.quote: So, the recovery would be sequential as we sort of discussed. Right? And also there are too many moving parts, unfortunately, in this piece. I think the commodity inflation, the currency depreciation. So, there are multiple moving parts and also the table change impact also.

items.statement: Expect sequential margin improvement but too many moving parts to quantify timeline to reach 8-10% normative margins
items.quote: Intent is to sort of definitely get better and come closer to the expectations that we have. Akshen sir, does that answer your question?

items.statement: Price increase is reality; quantum and timing depend on commodity, currency, BEE table impact; cost-down projects underway
items.quote: So, price increase is the reality. The quantum amount and when the exact time when the new products will come into the market are the moving pieces in this entire thing. We also have some cost-down projects which we are doing.

items.statement: Pre-buying in December positive; no decline seen in January numbers; laying runway for good February and March
items.quote: Actually the pre-buying in December actually was in a way a very positive thing for us. We were very pleasantly happy with the result that we have done. And a little bit of this might be the January thing, but as of now, we are not seeing any decline in our numbers.

items.statement: Voltbek progressing from seasonal cooling to year-round full-stacked consumer durable enterprise with premiumization strategy and expanded energy-efficient portfolio
items.quote: Together, these developments reinforce Voltas' progression from a predominantly seasonal cooling business to a year-round, full-stacked consumer durable enterprise supported by a broader innovation-led portfolio and disciplined operational execution.

items.statement: Voltbek focus on market share gains; scale building towards break-even in near future
items.quote: And the profitability in a way, the scale is slowly getting us to a place where in the very near future, we will see this get into at least a break-even kind of situation.

items.statement: EMPS domestic projects prudent selection across MEP, Water, Electrical & Solar verticals; focus on manufacturing, data center, metro/airport projects with price variation clauses
items.quote: We have been very prudent in picking up jobs in this category and we have been very selective about it. However, in the MEP vertical , we have been picking up fairly good, healthy jobs. In the manufacturing segment, we are also focusing on the data center segment.

items.statement: International project environment competitive; sequential exposure reduction reflecting tighter commercial controls and collection
items.quote: The international environment remains competitive for fresh wins, but delivery momentum supported by a mix of ongoing projects and disciplined project engagement. During the CY'25 year-to-date, Voltas secured new orders and lifted the order pack, and the International Project business reported sequential exposure reduction, reflecting tighter commercial controls and collection.

items.statement: Total income Rs. 3,130 crores vs Rs. 3,164 crores YoY; PBT Rs. 116 crores vs Rs. 191 crores; Net profit Rs. 84 crores vs Rs. 131 crores
items.quote: At an overall level for the quarter, Total income was Rs. 3,130 crores against Rs 3,164 crores last year. Profit before tax was Rs. 116 crores after factoring in the labor code impact versus Rs. 191 crores in Q3 2025. Net profit was at Rs. 84 crores against Rs 131 crores last year.

items.statement: Revenue expected flat until new furnace starts in Q4 FY27, then up 60% with capacity increase
items.quote: Generally, up to December, it will be similar kind of revenue. And once we start the production from the new furnace, which are under construction right now, in the Q4 FY '27, we might see some revenue coming from them. And then thereafter, the revenue will increase by 60% as the capacity is going up by 60%.

items.statement: Target ROCE upwards of 25% after 4,600 TPD expansion
items.quote: ROCE will be upwards of 25%.

items.statement: New 600 TPD furnace expansion on track for December 2026 commissioning with 3-month stabilization period
items.quote: We expect to fire the furnace in December '26. And thereafter, we generally plan for 3 months trial period to stabilize the production.

items.statement: Current 2,600 TPD capacity (18 GW); new expansion adds 60% capacity; land and utilities ready for another furnace if needed
items.quote: We can easily go for another furnace. It's all there. We have to decide to do it and it can get done. In fact, we have all the utilities batch house, everything is ready in case we want to go ahead.

items.statement: Domestic demand steady at ~55 GW module glass consumption for FY26; imports cover 70% of consumption
items.quote: Considering the expected current demand of about 55 gigawatts on DC basis for domestic installations, imports occupy about 70% share of the consumption, leaving huge scope for capacity addition for import substitution.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin 33.4% in Q3 FY26 vs 7.6% YoY; consolidated EBITDA INR130.94 cr
items.quote: The company's EBITDA at INR129.04 crores, which is 33.4% of sales, was a quantum jump of 518% from INR20.89 crores, which is 7.6% of sales in the corresponding quarter last year.

items.statement: Average ex-factory selling price INR149.97/mm in Q3 FY26 vs INR104.54 YoY; prices stable at current levels
items.quote: We don't foresee a significant change going forward. The prices are quite stable at these prices at these levels, and they are fairly competitive in that sense.

items.statement: Power and fuel ~32% of production cost; renewable energy to save ~1.5 bps incremental margin (~INR1.25 cr/month) from Feb 2026; gas prices up slightly
items.quote: Natural gas price recently has gone up to some extent because of the increase in the prices of the U.S.A gas, the Henry Hub Gas.

items.statement: CVD on Malaysia imports extended to 8 June 2026; ALMM-II for cells from June 2026; ALMM-III for ingot/wafer from June 2028
items.quote: The next step will be to introduce ALMM-III from June 2028, under which ingot and wafer will also be mandated to be locally produced.

items.statement: Exports INR20.74 cr (5.4% of turnover) in Q3 FY26; EU, Turkey, US face low demand; rupee depreciation gives marginal price benefit
items.quote: So you can see in the last quarter, our average realization was INR147.50 and this quarter, it is nearly INR150. So some advantage we are gaining out of this depreciation. But it's only marginal increase and not a significant one.

items.statement: India solar installations ~30 GW in 9M FY26, targeting 40 GW full year; module capacity 145 GW rising to 200 GW by 2027
items.quote: With 145 gigawatts of module manufacturing capacity, India is now an international manufacturing hub. This is expected to rise further to 200 gigawatts by 2027.

items.statement: Malaysian imports now 25% of total imports (up from nil pre-ADD); Vietnamese 10%; Chinese 65%; Malaysian capacity expanding
items.quote: Yes, they have commissioned more capacity in Malaysia. So the capacity is available for export to India or to any other part of the world.

items.statement: German subsidiary Geosphere filed for insolvency; balance sheet deconsolidated; no further losses expected; recovery unlikely
items.quote: Frankly, I think that is unlikely.

items.statement: No further equity dilution planned; expansion fully funded; cash accruals to support future growth
items.quote: No, there will be no further equity dilution. We are completely funded from the perspective of these expansions. And in case we ne ed to expand further, the cash accruals will support us

items.statement: Volume growth ~6% in 9M FY26 YoY; expect similar in Q4; further 2-3% efficiency gains possible
items.quote: It would be marginal in my view at least 2, 3 percentage is what we can expect.

items.statement: Caution on rapid expansion due to talent poaching by new entrants; monsoon may delay project; CVD sunset review outcome uncertain
items.quote: We expect the authority to issue the final findings in the next couple of months.

items.statement: Overall sales volume increased ~15% QoQ in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Despite these headwinds, we delivered a strong sequential improvement during the quarter. Our overall sales volume increased by around 15% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Europe demand rebound attributed to better season anticipation and destocking levelling out
items.quote: So I think overall, there anticipating better season to begin from this year. So that could have been the course. And as I mentioned in my earlier comments during the last quarter that a lot of the destocking had levelled out.

items.statement: US volumes down YoY but regained some momentum QoQ by sharing tariff impact with channel partners
items.quote: In the U.S. market, despite the ongoing tariff situation, our strong product quality, brand positioning and by sharing the tariff impact with our channel partners, this has enabled us to regain some of the sales momentum.

items.statement: Southern America and Asia markets facing decline
items.quote: So I think Southern part of America would be there. And Asia also a little bit.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin 22.5% in Q3 FY26 and 22.7% for 9M FY26
items.quote: The standalone EBITDA for the quarter was at INR605 crores, a margin of 22.5%. For 9 months, the standalone EBITDA was at INR1,760 crores, registering a de-growth of 11% year-on-year. However, the margins for 9M stood at 22.7%.

items.statement: India share has slightly lower ASP but EBITDA levels maintained at par with past
items.quote: Yes, it does have a slightly lower ASP. But if you see after all that also with the enhanced level of India, the EBITDA levels are at par with what they've been in the past. So it is nullifying the overall effect.

items.statement: Freight cost around 5% of revenue in Q3, expected to remain stable in this range
items.quote: I think it's around 5%, and we look at it to be stable at the moment.

items.statement: Capex spend ~INR2,200 crores in 9M FY26; additional INR300-400 crores in Q4 FY26, balance in FY27
items.quote: Our capex spend for the 9 months of this financial year was approximately INR2,200 crores.

items.statement: FY26 capex expected ~INR2,500-2,600 crores; FY27 capex not similar range, balance of committed budget
items.quote: No, as we mentioned, we are not seeing an overrun. So out of the total amount that we had committed from the budget, about INR2,500 crores, INR2,600 crores would be done in this financial year and the balance would be done in that financial year.

items.statement: New carbon black line commissioned, total capacity now 265,000 metric tons per annum
items.quote: During the quarter, we have commissioned a new line of carbon black, taking the total capacity to 265,000 metric tons per annum.

items.statement: CV and PV foray projects on schedule; CV pilot to start this quarter, rubber tracks under OE validation
items.quote: So as we have mentioned in my opening comments, all the projects are going as per schedule. So the CV will also come up in this quarter.

items.statement: Volumes 80,620 MT in Q3 FY26 (+6% YoY); 231,536 MT in 9M FY26 (-1% YoY)
items.quote: For the quarter, our volumes stood at 80,620 metric tons, a growth of 6% year-on-year. For 9 months, volumes stood at 231,536 metric tons, a minor de-growth of 1% year-on-year.

items.statement: Oil and natural rubber prices moving up; impact too early to quantify
items.quote: So oil is going up, and natural rubber is also moving up, but it is too early to say what will be the impact.

items.statement: Euro-INR rate ~INR97 in Q3; expected to marginally improve; forward hedge policy continues
items.quote: So the euro rate for Q3 was at approximately INR97.

items.statement: European realizations stable; no significant movement despite Euro appreciation
items.quote: Yes, realizations are same. There has not been a significant movement on that.

items.statement: India market split ~60% industrial construction, 40% agriculture
items.quote: It's roughly about 60%-40% between industrial construction and agri, very rough approximation.

items.statement: EUDR implementation deferred by 1 year to 1 Jan 2027
items.quote: For Europe, it is important to note that the EUDR norms, which were to get implemented from 1st January '26, the same has now been deferred by 1 year and is now likely to be implemented from 1st Jan '27.

items.statement: India-EU FTA signed; current EU duty 4%, post-FTA duty unclear
items.quote: Current duty is 4%, and it is not very clear what will be the duty after this treaty.

items.statement: Gross debt INR3,649 crores, cash INR3,012 crores, net debt ~INR637 crores as of 31 Dec 2025
items.quote: As on 31st December ' 25, the gross debt and cash and cash equivalents were INR3,649 crores and INR3,012 crores, respectively. Accordingly, we have a net debt of about INR637 crores.

items.statement: Third interim dividend of INR4 per equity share declared (INR8 already paid in first two quarters)
items.quote: The Board of Directors has declared a third interim dividend of INR4 per equity share in addition to the INR8 already paid in the previous two quarters.

items.statement: US tariff situation unchanged; strategy to regain lost momentum by sharing tariff impact with channel partners
items.quote: the situatio n with U.S. tariffs remain unchanged. Despite these headwinds, we delivered a strong sequential improvement during the quarter

items.statement: Geopolitical volatility makes Q4 outlook difficult to comment on for US and Europe
items.quote: going forward, it is difficult to comment becau se of the volatility across the worl d with the geopolitical scenarios, how it plays out. So it will be very difficult to make a comment on how we see it

items.statement: ESG: S&P Global Corporate Sustainability Assessment score of 58, among leading tire manufacturers
items.quote: we have established an S&P Global Corporate Sustainability Assessment score of 58. This placed us amongst the leading tire manufacturers in terms of sustainability performance.

items.statement: Sports partnership: Official partner with all five Women's IPL teams for 2026 season
items.quote: BKT Tires is the offici al partner with all the five women's IPL teams, franchises in a landmark multi-team deal for '26 season

items.statement: Expects double-digit growth across retail portfolio in FY26
items.quote: Looking ahead, we continue to see good visibility for double -digit growth across our retail portfolio in FY26, supported by strong consumer demand trends, healthy retailer performance and ongoing portfolio enhancement.

items.statement: Retail consumption grew 25% YoY in Q3 FY26 to Rs 4,992 crore
items.quote: In Q3 FY26, consumption grew by 25% at Rs. 4,992 crores, with strong momentum across all categories.

items.statement: Retail EBITDA grew 16% YoY to Rs 585 crore in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Rental income grew by 13% year-on-year to Rs. 573 crores, while EBITDA increased 16% to Rs. 585 crores, underscoring the opera ting leverage in our portfolio.

items.statement: Retail trading density at PMC Bangalore reached Rs 3,011 psf for 9M FY26, up 23% YoY
items.quote: At Phoenix Market City Bangalore, trading density grew to Rs. 3,011 pspm for 9MFY26 by 23% year-on-year.

items.statement: Retail trading density at PMC Pune reached Rs 2,214 psf for 9M FY26, up 14% YoY
items.quote: Similarly, PMC Pune recorded a 14% increase to Rs. 2,214 pspm (trading density) , with 19% of its GLA under transformation and over a third of new brands already operational.

items.statement: Capex for construction and ongoing projects was Rs 722 crore in 9M FY26
items.quote: Capital expenditure towards construction and ongoing projects during the first nine months amounted to Rs. 722 crores.

items.statement: Office portfolio scaled from 2 msf in 2023 to nearly 5 msf across four cities
items.quote: From a base of around 2 million square feet across two cities in 2023, we have scaled now to nearly 5 million square feet of completed office spaces across four cities today.

items.statement: Achieved 1.2 msf gross leasing in offices YTD December 2025
items.quote: By December 2025, we have achieved nearly 1.2 million square feet of gross leasing across our office assets in Mumbai, Pune, Bengaluru, and Chennai.

items.statement: Office occupancy at stabilized assets rose to 76% from 67% at March 2025
items.quote: Occupancy at our stabilized assets in Mumbai and Pune increased to 76% from 67% at the e nd of March 2025.

items.statement: Recently completed office assets at 41% lease occupancy with advanced discussions for ramp-up
items.quote: And in our recently completed developments across Pune, Bangalore, and Chennai, lease occupancy now stands at about 41%, with advanced-stage discussions providing good visibility for continued ramp-up across this portfolio.

items.statement: Newer office assets expected to contribute meaningfully to earnings from FY27
items.quote: With the leasing progress achieved during the year, the office portfolio is now entering the transition from a build and lease phase into a rental monetization phase, with newer assets expected to begin contributing meaningfully to earnings and cash flows from FY27 onwards.

items.statement: Hotel EBITDA margin at 45% for 9M FY26, up 300 bps YoY
items.quote: Our EBITDA margins for the two hotels were very healthy at 45%, with an improvement of 300 basis points over the same period last year.

items.statement: St. Regis Mumbai occupancy at 85% with ARR above Rs 20,000, up 8% YoY for 9M FY26
items.quote: The St. Regis Mumbai, drove this EBITDA improvement, operating at a healthy 85% occupancy for nine months of FY26, with average room rates crossing Rs. 20,000, up 8% year-on-year.

items.statement: Residential gross bookings Rs 412 crore in 9M FY26; Rs 180 crore likely in Q4
items.quote: Gross booking for the first nine months was around Rs. 412 crores. Revenue recognized for the first nine months is only Rs. 273 crores. So, essentially Rs. 180 crores is likely to be booked in Q4, subject to registration and other documentation completion.

items.statement: Residential pricing in excess of Rs 29,000 per sq ft
items.quote: Pricing was in excess of around Rs. 29,000 per square feet, led by the strong demand in the market.

items.statement: Gross debt Rs 5,200 crore; net debt Rs 3,344 crore; net debt/EBITDA 1.3x at Dec 2025
items.quote: Gross debt at 31st December stood at ~Rs. 5,200 crores, with overall liquidity improving to Rs. 1 ,858 crores. The net debt as on 31st December was Rs. 3,344 crores. Net debt to annualized EBITDA remained at a healthy 1.3x.

items.statement: Average cost of debt reduced from 7.68% to 7.62% in Dec 2025
items.quote: During the period, we also reduced our average cost of debt from 7.68% to 7.62% in December 2025.

items.statement: Completed first tranche of ISML buyout for Rs 1,257 crore; stake up to 58.33%
items.quote: First tranche payment has been made for Rs. 1,257 crores in November 2025. With this, PML stake in ISML stands at 58.33%, up from 51% earlier.

items.statement: Operating cash flow after working capital, taxes and interest Rs 1,508 crore in 9M FY26, up 24% YoY
items.quote: Operating cash flow after working capital and taxes and interest stood at Rs. 1,508 crores for the nine months, an increase of 24% year -on-year basis.

items.statement: Renewable energy now 30% of retail energy needs, up from 20% in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Renewable energy now accounts for 30% of our retail energy requirements for common area and HVAC, up from 20% during Q3 last year.

items.statement: Phoenix Mall of Asia occupancy at 88%, targeting 94-95% in next two quarters
items.quote: In fact, occupancy right now is at 88%. And typically, you would see for the rest of our portfolio, all new malls are at 95% or thereabout in those trading levels. And even in the Phoenix Mall of Asia, in the coming next two quarters, we are going to see occupancy stabilize at the 94 %-95% level going forward.

items.statement: PMC Bangalore and Pune trading occupancy to cross 90% by March 2026, reach 94-95% by mid-FY27
items.quote: I think we are on track to cross 90% trading occupancy in both Bangalore and Pune by March 2026 in line with our original timelines. And we have a lineup of some great first-time brands that are entering the city such as IKEA, Uniqlo, etc that are opening their first stores in the city of Pune and Bangalore will also have a similar trajectory. I think you should expect to see the 95% level by the

items.statement: Thane mixed-use development: demolition started, excavation and construction tenders out, work to commence in 2-3 months
items.quote: We are awaiting the environmental clearance and we at the m oment have commenced demolition activities of the old existing structures on the Thane site. And in the next two or three months, we also expect to commence excavation and the subsequent construction activities. Tenders are already out for excavation and we are also, you know, very soon going to be launching the tenders for the ci vil con

items.statement: Kolkata residential launch timeline update expected in next two quarters
items.quote: Kolkata residential, I think we are in the final stages of approvals as well as design fine-tuning. I think in the coming two quarters we will come back and update you on the launch timeline of Kolkata.

items.statement: GST rate cuts had only sentimental impact, not material needle mover for consumption
items.quote: I think on the GST cut, we have evaluated our brand portfolio. And the impact that we have is, I would say, it is a sentimentally positive impact. But otherwise, it is not that material a needle mover in our perspective.

items.statement: Blended tax rate expected to sustain at 22-23% range going forward
items.quote: So, my suggestion would be that for the modeling purpose, I think 22 % to 23% range will sustain in future. 25% could be in one of the quarter, but that is not something w hich will happen for the entire year.

items.statement: Phoenix Mall of Asia consumption Rs 732 crore in Q3, up 112% YoY; rental up 58% to Rs 62 crore
items.quote: Consumption at Mall of Asia reached Rs. 732 crores for the third quarter. And it is up 112% year-on-year. While rental also has grown by 58%. And quarterly rental for this asset reached Rs. 62 crores.

items.statement: Repricing achieved 35-40% fixed rent increase on optimized area at PMC Bangalore, 25% at PMC Pune
items.quote: And if I just compare the increase in the fixed rent compared to the total rent that we were seeing previously, we expect to see a 35% to 40% increase in the area that we have optimized in Phoenix MarketCity Bangalore. Similarly, in (Phoenix MarketCity) Pune as well, we have optimized and refreshed almost 40% of the area. And there, the overall impact that we are seeing is about a 25%.

items.statement: Full impact of PMC Bangalore and Pune repricing visible in FY27 numbers
items.quote: Yes. I think you will see the full impact of it in the numbers during FY27.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth guidance upgraded to 12-15% from 10-12%
items.quote: In any way, we have increased the overall guidance for this year, which is as an exception. From 10% to 12% as an overall growth of the company to between 12% to 15% growth.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin guidance ~14% with 100-150 bps drag from retail
items.quote: We have given an FY '26 guidance, and we've upgraded that guidance from 10% to 12% to 12% to 15% revenue guidance, and we maintain a 14% approximate EBITDA level with a 100, 150 basis points drop in retail.

items.statement: FY26 retail revenue target INR70-80 crore
items.quote: So our original target for the whole year was around INR70 crores to INR80 crores, and we will I think be able to achieve, we'll be in line with that guidance.

items.statement: Maintenance capex INR50-70 crore annually for legacy business
items.quote: Legacy business is more of an asset -light model and doesn't need regular capital investments. It's more of maintenance Capex, which we have indicated in the line of INR50 crores, INR60 crores, maybe INR50 crores, INR70 crores in every year.

items.statement: Retail capex INR35-40 crore for FY26
items.quote: Even the retail business is a more calculated approach where we have indicated, I think, about INR35 crores to INR40 crores that we will spend this year.

items.statement: Added 2 ZECODE and 5 DEVO stores in Q3 FY26; total 25 ZECODE and 17 DEVO stores
items.quote: In Q3 of FY '26, we continued expanding our store network by adding two ZECODE and five DEVO outlets, taking the total number of stores f or ZECODE and DEVO to 25 and 17, respectively.

items.statement: Target ~35 store openings in FY26 for ZECODE and DEVO combined
items.quote: We remain focused on achieving our plan of opening about 35 stores during the year.

items.statement: Q3 demand occasion-driven with moderate footfall; cautious consumer spending
items.quote: In the third quarter of FY '26, we saw demand pick up at the start of the festive season. However, as the quarter went on, customers stayed cautious with their spending and footfall remained moderate.

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA margin 13.2% vs 14.1% YoY; decline due to labour code cost, ad spend, retail losses
items.quote: I think I've already mentioned earlier that there are two or three main reasons. One is the employee cost because of the new labour code, that was a hit we had to take, as well as some increase in advertising, and this retail business that we have earlier indicated to drop our EBITDA.

items.statement: Marketing spend guided at 4-5% of revenue including new brands
items.quote: The spends as a percentage of turnover, we have indicated between 4% to 5% of revenue. And this is the kind of nu mber that we are comfortable with and will continue this year as well as in the ongoing years

items.statement: Fabric share declined from 80%+ to 75-78% as garment, yarn and retail grow
items.quote: So fabric traditionally has been a much larger percentage, north of 80% since, for a few years ago. It has gone down to 75% to 78% now as other businesses are growing.

items.statement: Exports ~10% of revenue, mainly fabrics to converters; EU FTA seen as positive
items.quote: We are already exporting about, as you mentioned, 10% of our turnover. This is largely fabrics. So it's not direct export to these countries, but it is export to converters. So these new treaties and India positioned as a manufacturing hub will definitely help us.

items.statement: Second interim dividend INR3 per share (face value INR2) declared
items.quote: We are pleased to share that the Board of Directo rs has declared a second interim dividend of INR3 per share with a face value of INR2 each.

items.statement: One-time employee cost hit from new labour code implementation
items.quote: One is there is a onetime cost of this employee expense because of the new labour code, and there is some increase in advertising and sales promotion. So this is, both these put together is roughly INR10 crores, INR12 crores extra.

items.statement: Retail business still nascent; store economics not yet disclosed; gross margin challenges in sourcing

items.quote: Two-wheeler domestic ICE sales grew by 21% compared to Q3 of last year as against an industry growth of 16%. International market, company sales grew by 35% over last year as against an industry growth of 23%.

items.statement: Rural grew ~19% and urban ~21% in Q3; expects Q4 to do extremely well supported by good rainfall, reservoir levels, RBI rate cuts and GST reduction
items.quote: Rural grew by almost 19% and urban by about 21%. The GDP growth for this financial year is also estimated about 7%. This robust performance not only reinforces the underlying strength derived from the domestic market, but also positions India as world's fastest -growing major economy against many challenges in the global landscape.

items.statement: EV 2-wheeler sales grew 40% to 1,06,000 units in Q3; 3-wheeler EV volumes ~8,500-9,000 units in Q3
items.quote: EV 2-wheeler sales grew by 40%, and it has crossed 1 lakh this year, 1,06,000 units as against 76,000 units during Q3 of last year.

items.statement: 3-wheeler total sales more than doubled to 60,000 units in Q3 vs 29,000 last year
items.quote: Total sales of 3-wheeler is more than doubled to 60,000 units as against 29,000 units during last year third quarter.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin improved 120 bps YoY to 13.1% in Q3; normalized margin improvement 70 bps YoY and 40 bps QoQ
items.quote: The company's operating EBITDA margin improved by 120 basis points at 13.1% as against 11.9% during Q3 of last year.

items.statement: Confident EBITDA will continue to grow going forward leveraging scale benefits, premiumization, better product mix and cost reduction
items.quote: With top line growth, we will leverage the scale benefits. We will look at more premiumization and better product mix. Our sustained effort on cost reduction will also enable us to continue, and we are confident that EBITDA will continue to grow going forward.

items.statement: Revised FY26 capex to ~INR 1,700 crores (from INR 1,600 crores) and total investments to ~INR 2,900 crores (from INR 2,000 crores)
items.quote: The capex will be around INR 1700 crores or slightly around that because we are also now looking at increasing some of the areas capacity given the kind of growth what we have seen, okay? And investments around INR2,900 crores overall.

items.statement: EV production ~30,000-32,000 iQube/month and ~10,000 Orbiter/month; reviewing capacity expansion for next year
items.quote: EV, we are producing about average 30,000 to 32,000 of iQube. And as of now, we are producing about -- they are coming closer to 10,000 of Orbiter.

items.statement: TVS Credit disbursed loans to 41 lakh new customers in 9M FY26; book size INR 29,678 crores, up 9% YoY; PBT INR 390 crores in Q3, up 21% YoY
items.quote: First 9 months, TVS Credit disbursed loans of over 41 lakh new customers, bringi ng its total customer base to nearly 2.3 crores. The book size is INR29,678 crores, grew by 9% over last year Q3.

items.statement: International revenue INR 2,909 crores in Q3; exports from India grew 23% in Q3; Africa and LatAm growing, Europe challenged; FX realization ~INR 88 with 12-week hedging policy
items.quote: IB overall revenue for this quarter is about INR2,909 crores and spare parts all put together about INR1,183 crores.

items.statement: Mexico exposure very small; building localization to mitigate duty impact
items.quote: So we see, first of all, we are now building Mexico, okay? As of now, while there are some impact on the duty, we are also looking at localization. So we are not seeing a serious impact at this point of time because the volumes are low, and we are also trying to like increase our local content.

items.statement: Scooters near 40% category share of 2-wheeler industry; premium and super-premium growing faster; entry-level not growing as much
items.quote: Scooters have really done well. While the industry has done well, I think one category which has done extremely well is scooter. You remember, I always believe that scooters with ICE Plus, we should always add the EV. We are close to a 40% category share of overall 2 -wheeler industry.

items.statement: PLI benefit ~0.7% of revenue in Q3 (up from ~0.5%); not all EV models eligible due to price thresholds
items.quote: It has a little bit gone up. It is about 0.7%.

items.statement: Norton investment INR 240 crores last quarter, INR 290 crores this quarter; TVS Credit invested INR 200 crores this quarter; ION PT TVS project ~INR 100 crores; Dubai investment for international focus
items.quote: I think last quarter, it's about INR240 crores and this quarter, about INR290 crores, Norton.

items.statement: Norton products to hit market in 2026; will invest in technology and marketing to build brand; no timeline given for breakeven
items.quote: And these products are going to hit the market in 2026 this year. You will see the growth coming, and they are super premium, and it is going to definitely delight the customers globally.

items.statement: EV penetration in 3-wheeler L5 category ~32% in Q3; expects penetration to rise in both 2W and 3W
items.quote: And you have seen the highest EBITDA for the company. With top line growth, we will leverage the scale benefits. We will look at more premiumization and better product mix. Our sustained effort on cost reduction will also enable us to continue, and we are confident that EBITDA will continue to grow going forward.

items.statement: Dealer stock target 21-30 days; some dealers need better planning but supplies being managed
items.quote: And we always believe that the dealer should keep only 21 to 30-day stock because we want products to be fresh to the customer.

items.statement: EV magnet availability was a setback but now recovering; expects full EV supplies within a month
items.quote: Of course, in the EV side, we had a setup setback because of the magnet availability. We t ried our level best. Now it is recovering. I can tell you that it is recovering. And hopefully, by another month, you will see full supplies of EV also into the market.

items.statement: Exceptional item INR 41 crores for past service cost from new labor codes
items.quote: During this quarter, company recognized TVS ~ INR41 crores as an exceptional item towards the past service cost arising from the new labor codes.

items.statement: Preference share listing delayed; closely following up with SEBI but no date given
items.quote: No, no, the listing is still taking time. We are closely following up with SEBI. We will continue to follow up more closely. That's the status now. It's not in my control. We are not able to give a date.

items.statement: Sustainable gross margin range guided at 58% to 60%
items.quote: we believe that it can be between a 58% to 60% range. Don't hold us on for each an d every quarter. Our endeavor is to reach the higher end of the range always

items.statement: US revenue target of $400 million by FY28 reiterated
items.quote: Our endeavor is to reach about $400 million in U.S. And we also said that the Ex-U.S., we want to mirror the U.S. markets in the two years' time.

items.statement: Ex-US markets to mirror US markets within two years
items.quote: And in the next two years' time, we should be able to mirror those markets completely.

items.statement: Cash-to-cash cycle expected in 120-125 days range
items.quote: we expect it to be in the range of 120 to 125 days, depending upon how the market conditions are.

items.statement: Effective tax rate expected at 15% to 18% for the year
items.quote: Effective tax rate for the quarter is at 15% and we expect it to be in the range of 15% to 18% for the year.

items.statement: Maintenance capex guided at Rs 100-125 crore range
items.quote: from a maintenance CAPEX standpoint, we are on track in the 100 crore to 125 crore kind of a range.

items.statement: US flu season delayed, seasonal sales did not pick up in Q3
items.quote: The seasonal sales on account of the flu, unlike the last year, did not pick up in Q3. Usually the Q3 and Q4, the seasonal sales will be very good.

items.statement: Ex-US markets grew 20% YoY to $64 million in Q3
items.quote: And in this quarter, we delivered $64 million of revenue, representing almost 20% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: Other regulated markets broke $40-43M range, reached ~$48M with 21% YoY growth
items.quote: They broke the trend of $40 million to $43 million. We recorded almost about $48 million, 21% YoY growth.

items.statement: Growth markets revenue at $16.6M with 19% YoY growth
items.quote: And our growth markets, revenue has been about $16.6 million, delivering almost about 19% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: Gross margins touched 60%+ in Q3, overall at 59.8%
items.quote: Our gross margins have touched 60% plus in this quarter. Overall gross margins have reached about 59.8%

items.statement: EBITDA grew 12% YoY to Rs 236 crore, highest ever quarterly EBITDA
items.quote: For the quarter, our EBITDA grew 12% year-on-year to Rs. 236 crores, which is also our highest ever quarterly EBITDA.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 160 bps YoY to 19.8%
items.quote: Our EBITDA margins are at 19.8% for the qu arter, which is an expansion of 160 basis points year-on-year

items.statement: 9M EBITDA at Rs 686 crore, up 17% with 19.4% margin
items.quote: For the 9-month period, our EBITDA is at Rs. 686 crores, which is a healthy growth of 17% with an EBITDA margin of 19.4%.

items.statement: Discontinued 8 products not meeting profitability threshold over last 9 months
items.quote: We also discontinued 8 products that did not meet our profitability threshold for the last 9 months, and this shows our discipline towards profitability

items.statement: Invested Rs 284 crore in capex including targeted global product rights acquisitions

items.quote: one is already filed. So, it's undergoing a review with US FDA. There are two more products which are looking at in the next wave of filing. It is expected to get filed in the next 2 quarters, maybe by May, June.

items.statement: Price erosions part of generics business, compensated by COGS improvement reflected in gross margins
items.quote: the price erosions are part of the generics business. So, some prices will go up, some prices will come down. But overall, it's a portfolio. I think the price erosions will always be compensated by the better COGS improvement.

items.statement: Ex-US markets driven by B2B partnerships in Australia and Europe with high entry barriers and stickiness
items.quote: we have onboarded many partners. And the lead time to onboard a partner is also quite high in that business. Plus, once you onboard, the stickiness is going to be there in that market for a long time to come.

items.statement: Competition exists across select molecules, portfolio balanced by launches to cover erosions
items.quote: It is not across the board . It can be in select molecules. And we are working towards how to launch many products as we go along. And the US portfolio has to always be balanced by the launches, as well as which will cover up for all the erosions from the competition.

items.statement: New labor code implemented, no financial impact due to simplified compensation structure alignment
items.quote: we have evaluated the impact of this code on our financials. And we are very pleased to report that we have not had a financial impact on our financial statements on account of the new labor code.

items.statement: Peter Hardwick appointed CEO of North American Business with 30 years experience including leading Apotex
items.quote: we are also excited to h ave Peter Hardwick joining us as the CEO of North American Business. Peter brings in about 30 years of global pharmaceutical experience, including leading Apotex Corporation

items.statement: Nandini Matiyani appointed Executive VP of HR with over two decades experience
items.quote: We appointed Nandini Matiyani as the Executive VP of HR. She brings over two decades of experience in driving people's strategy, leadership development and cultural

items.statement: Operational PAT grew 38% YoY to Rs 128 crore, operational EPS at Rs 13.9
items.quote: We are reporting an operational PAT of Rs. 128 crores with an operational PAT ma rgin of 10.7%. It's a 39% growth year-on-year. With this growth, our operational EPS is at Rs. 13.9 per share for the quarter

items.statement: Access market subdued due to reduced donor funding from countries like US to Global Fund
items.quote: Several countries have reduced their funding to large donor in stitutions like the Global Fund, w hich has caused a significant reduction in the amount of orders from these institutions to not only us but all the other manufacturers

items.statement: India-EU FTA not expected to benefit generics business
items.quote: As far as this current thing, while it is early days, our initial view is that, generics will not get any benefit from this deal.

items.quote: Our objective is to get to 2%. And then only after we hit that milestone will we share our plans to go up. But clearly, is 2% the gold standard? No. We do understand that any formidable NBFC from the stable of, let's say, the M&M Group should deliver a 15% ROE and our goal is to get to that 15% ROE.

items.statement: Credit cost target range maintained at 1.5%-1.7%; 9-month FY26 at 1.8% with confidence to reach target zone
items.quote: You would all recollect that for the business model that we said, which requires us to get back to a 2% ROA, credit costs should be in the range of 1.5% to 1.7%. YTD, we are at 1.8%. We do see capability for us to live up to that commitment of being within that Zip code of 1.5% to 1.7%.

items.statement: 9-month FY26 NIM at 7.1% vs 6.6% YoY; Q3 NIM 7.5% includes one-time benefits from trade advance runoff and GS2/GS3 write-backs
items.quote: I would request you to read the 9 -month FY'26 NIM, which has come up to 7.1%. All of you would be aware that this is one of the metrics we've been talking about that the NIMs which had bottomed out at 6.5%, we clearly said that we are looking at getting back to 7% and then from there on, inching up.

items.statement: Fee income rose to 1.4% of avg assets (9M FY26) from 1.1% YoY, driven by insurance corporate agency and MIBL dividends; structural and sustainable
items.quote: Overall, what is structurally also improving is our fee income. Fee and other income has expanded Q -on-Q by 10 bps and 9 months for the financial year to 1.4% versus 1.1% for 9 months of last fiscal.

items.quote: GS3 numbers for quarter 3 are at 3.8%. This is sequentially down 14 bps and Y -o-Y down 13 bps. As I mentioned in the opening comments, GS3 plus GS2 together is 101 Mahindra & bps lower than last year, same time at 9.2%.

items.quote: So in our mind, we have adjusting for this provision movement, the real credit costs, which one would read, which was INR623 crores for quarter 2 of FY '26 has reduc ed to INR482 crores for quarter 3.

Of course, most of these benefits for us has been, I would say, enjoye d with tractor disbursement growth, which is up 65%.

items.statement: Tractor demand strong on favourable monsoon and MSP price discovery; PV entry-level bounce-back seen; CV demand rationalized post-GST with ticket size reduction; momentum waned post-festive season

items.quote: As I mentioned, we believe that the business transformation now is complete. It is evidenced clearly that 95% of our channels have adopted the new stack. This is resulting in both acquisition and collections now at a very strong pace on the new stack.

items.quote: OpenX has been largely range bound. We are investing, as I said, in new businesses and growth. So we do believe our business franchise can absorb between 2.5% - 2.8% open to average assets.

items.statement: Focus on rural/semi-urban self-employed segments; tracking incremental market share by product; CV participation limited to retail borrowers, avoiding stressed fleet segment
items.quote: Our business teams track incremental market shares for every vehicle product. We are keen that whatever commerce is happening and where our business model is highly indexed on, whether it is EV, CV, tractor, 3-wheeler, in the rural, semi -urban, self -employed segments, we look at getting a hig her clip of the incremental market share.

items.statement: Intense competition in declining rate environment; balancing growth and margins in Wheels business; not chasing prime PV growth at expense of margins
items.quote: Fair to say in a declining interest environment, we are going to see intensified competition, which will mean as cost of funds go down, we'll have to pass on some benefits. The competition intensity is quite acute, so we will have to be competitive.

items.quote: We have taken to both the boards today , a plan to look at what's the best way to do mortgages going ahead, which includes an evaluation of merging the 2 entities. We are going to do a full evaluation and take the final suggestion to the Boards in due course of time.

items.quote: To grow, of course capital is important, and we are extremely well capitalized. Our Tier 1 still at 17.4% , so all the growth plans that we have are supported by a very strong capital adequacy.

items.statement: ROA 2.5% in Q3 (with one-time benefits); 9M FY26 ROA 1.9% vs target of 2%+; PAT up 59% QoQ, 76% 9M YoY
items.quote: If you look at the quarter 3 ROA, we have climbed to 2.5%. Now there have been onetime benefits in this quarter. If you look at 9 months of FY '26, our ROA is moved up to 1.9%. items.quote: We have set up just for everyone to know, we have a fee and we have a setup an organization structure, which basically supports this from a medium to long term. We are not looking at this being one -off.

items.quote: I'm happy to share that for last 2 quarters, that business is now shaping up well. We are holding the asset quality well. We did, of course, bring the GS3 below 3%. items.statement: Double-digit revenue growth guidance intact; margin outlook to be clarified next quarter
items.quote: So the guidance we have given is the double -digit growth on th e revenue side, that looks intact. On the margin side, as I said we will come to know in the next quarter.

items.statement: 9M EBITDA margin 11.6%, down 30 bps YoY due to brand investment and digitalization
items.quote: On the profitability front, the company reported an EBITDA margin of 11.6% in 9 months, down 30 basis points from 11.9% in 9MFY25, primarily due to increased brand investment, certain strategic initiatives, including digitalization initiatives.

items.statement: January shows slight slowdown in US mainstream consumption; Q4 will clarify trend

items.quote: I can give you a ballpark number is $20 million revenue will be more, yes.

items.quote: On the market share, we are growing at a premi um end of the market, losing on the lower price point, the market share. But overall, on the premium end of the market, we are growing.

items.quote: The final determination was earlier expected by November 17, 2025. However, due to U.S. government shutdown, the time lines have been further extended and is now expected by February 17, 2026.

items.statement: Hungary Ministry rejected Global Green Group acquisition on national/economic/sectoral risk grounds
items.quote: Ministry of National Economy Hungary has not approved the proposed acquisition on grounds of identified national, economical and sectoral risks.

items.statement: RTH/RTC segment EBITDA breakeven at INR 400 cr revenue; target in next 3 years

items.statement: Board declared interim dividend of ₹6/share, up 20% vs ₹5/share previous year
items.quote: Based on the strong performance, board has declared an interim dividend of ₹6/share, up by 20% vs ₹5/share declared in the previous year.

items.statement: AMC net flows robust at ₹11,600 crores in Q3FY26; AUM at ₹1.89 lakh crores, up 33% YoY
items.quote: Net flows in Q3FY26 were robust at ₹ 11,600 crores. Our AUM stood at ₹ 1.89 lakh crores as of 31st December 2025, up 33% YoY.

items.quote: Our Private Wealth business is on a strong growth path. Our AUM grew 31% YoY to ₹ 1.95 lakh crores. We have 8,200+ families, grew by 41% YoY, served by a high-quality RM team of 410+.

items.quote: Our distribution book grew 34% YoY to ₹ 42,775 crores. NII income recorded 21% growth YoY, supported by robust book expansion . Our total loan book AUM grew 25% YoY to ₹ 6,630 crores.

items.quote: PAT at ₹ 280 crores for 9MFY26, up 14% YoY. Cost-to-income ratio improved to 53% in 9MFY26.

items.quote: Our consolidated annual recurring revenue now stands at 65% of the total net revenue for Q3FY26. We believe, the share of ARR revenues will continue to rise in the years ahead.

items.quote: The AMC business continues to gain market share with mutual fund AUM market share at 2.7%, highest ever. There is still headroom to increase further given that our net flow market share is much higher than 2.7% and stands at 7.6%.

items.quote: It is Important to note that our share of broking revenue in the Wealth Management segment has declined from 60% in FY21 to 37% in Q3FY26, led by sharp focus on growing our distribution income & NII.

items.quote: It is very small; the Asset Management firm has grown very strongly over a period of time. It has come down to just over 10%.

items.quote: On the market share - our F&O premium ADTO market share has actually grew up by 20 bps on YoY basis to 8.4%. Cash market shares have been lower YoY as our Cash ADTO has been lower by almost 20%.

items.statement: PAT includes ₹14.4 crores impact from employee benefits under new labour code
items.quote: Q3FY26 PAT includes the impact of ₹ 14.4 crores towards employee benefits under the new labour code.
