items.quote: It is important to note that during the quarter, there was a onetime impact of Rs. 18.1 million under employee benefit expenses due to the implementation of the new labor codes announced by the Government of India in November 2025.

items.statement: Automotive business grew 46% YoY vs industry 15.7%, ~3x outperformance
items.quote: Our automotive business grew by 46% Y-o-Y compared to a 15.7% Y-o-Y growth in the automotive industry volumes, that is 2-wheeler and passenger vehicles put together. So, resulting in approximately a 3x outperformance of the industry growth.

items.statement: Highest ever quarterly revenue of Rs 2,435.3M, up 36.4% YoY
items.quote: Q3 FY 26 marked an important milestone for SJS with the company reporting its highest ever quarterly revenue of Rs. 2,435.3 million, representing a Y-o-Y growth of 36.4%.

items.statement: Exports revenue Rs 283.1M, up 146.2% YoY and 22.1% QoQ, 11.6% of consolidated revenue
items.quote: During Q3 FY26, exports recorded their highest ever quarterly revenue of Rs. 283.1 million, growing 146.2% Y-o-Y and 22.1% Q-o-Q. This reflects increasing traction with global customers and strengthening acceptance of our decorative aesthetic products.

items.statement: 9M FY26 export revenue Rs 655.9M already surpasses full FY25 export revenue of Rs 567.9M
items.quote: For 9M FY26, export revenue stood at Rs. 655.9 million, already surpassing the full year FY 25 export revenue of Rs. 567.9 million, reflecting strong traction with the global OEMs.

items.statement: New generation products contributed over 23% of consolidated revenue
items.quote: During the quarter, new generation products contributed over 23% of consolidated revenue, reflecting increasing adoption of advanced aesthetic solutions.

items.statement: Revenue mix: 38.8% 2-wheelers, 42.3% passenger vehicles, ~19% consumer and others
items.quote: Segment-wise, revenue contribution was 38.8% from 2-wheelers, 42.3% from passenger vehicles and approximately 19% from consumer and other segments, providing healthy diversification.

items.statement: Added new EV-focused 2-wheeler customer Raptee and Urban Company for water purifiers; expanding with Mahindra, Hero MotoCorp, Whirlpool, Samsung, Hyundai, Spark Minda, Mabe, John Deere
items.quote: During the quarter, we added new EV-focused 2-wheeler customer, Raptee and Urban Company that is launching its own range of water purifiers. We continue to expand businesses with key customers like Mahindra, Hero MotoCorp, Whirlpool, Samsung, Hyundai, Spark Minda, Mabe, John Deere, amongst others.

items.statement: Stellantis business ramping across North America, Latin America, Europe; Whirlpool global plant win; targeting Western European OEMs including Germany
items.quote: So largely, the Stellantis business that we won, which we said is a large business, we will supply across North America, Latin America, Europe. So a few plants have started. This will gain momentum as we go along in this current year.

items.statement: Evaluating inorganic targets, accumulated sufficient cash, aim to conclude transaction within next year
items.quote: We have targets in mind. We are reviewing their financials. And as I stated many times earlier, we focus on inorganic targets, which we can add great value to as we've done in the past 2 acquisitions we've done. So, we are in the evaluation phase at the moment, and we will make our bids as we go along. So, the target was to have a cash surplus. So, we've accumulated sufficient cash and hope to hea

items.statement: M&A focused on faster market access via acquired channels, not filling product gaps; portfolio has 14 technologies
items.quote: Currently, we don't see any gap. So we are an end-to-end design to delivery solution provider. So for the aesthetic and the human machine interface parts that we have, we are fairly comfortable with the product portfolio we have. So the inorganic opportunity is not for filling any gap. It's primarily for faster accessing markets.

items.statement: Display market TAM estimated at Rs 3,000-4,000 cr by FY30; display penetration in PVs expected to reach ~100% by FY30 from ~30% now
items.quote: Our initial estimate is that the size of this market by FY 30 could be close to about Rs. 3,000 crores to Rs.4,000 crores. So that's the huge potential that exists in the market when you have penetration across the board.

items.statement: Display business asset turns expected >5x vs current 2-2.5x; ROCE to be very good
items.quote: Yes. So these kind of businesses have a higher asset turn. It should be more than 5x. Currently, we are operating around 2x - 2.5x, but this business will have more than 5x.

items.statement: Free cash flow for 9M FY26 was Rs 975.9M, driven by robust operating performance and disciplined working capital management
items.quote: Free cash flow for the 9 MFY26 was Rs. 975.9 million, driven by robust operating performance and disciplined working capital management.

items.statement: Net cash position of Rs 2,030.1M as of Dec 31, 2025; cash and equivalents Rs 2,098.8M
items.quote: As of December 31, 2025, cash and cash equivalents stood at Rs. 2,098.8 million, resulting in a net cash position of Rs. 2,030.1 million.

items.statement: Free cash flow conversion ~76% of EBITDA
items.quote: So we generate free cash is close to about 76% of EBITDA.

items.statement: Launched Pink Line initiative for women empowerment, inclusion, workplace safety; increasing women employment in quality inspection roles
items.quote: During the quarter, we launched the Pink Line initiative, a dedicated production line aimed at promoting women empowerment, inclusion and workplace safety. This initiative will help increase women employment across our operations, particularly for quality inspection roles.

items.statement: Securing 2MW wind power from DB Renews; 80% of group energy needs to be met from renewable sources
items.quote: We are also in the process of securing a 2-megawatt wind power from DB Renews Private Limited. With this, 80% of the SJS Group's energy needs will be met from renewable sources.

items.statement: FY26 net store additions target of 60-70 stores
items.quote: As of nine months of FY '26, the company has added 49 stores and we expect to close FY '26 with a net addition of 60 to 70 stores.

items.statement: FY26 inventory days target of 100 days
items.quote: For the full-year FY '26, we anticipate inventory levels to stabilize in the range of 100 days, ensuring operational efficiency and healthy working capital management.

items.statement: Target to convert more than 50% of EBITDA into Pre-IndAS operating cash flows for FY26
items.quote: Our strong focus on inventory and working capital efficiency will help us achieve the target of converting more than 50% of our EBITDA into Pre-IndAS operating cash flows.

items.statement: Daily Wear concept to scale to about 10 stores by March 2026
items.quote: As of now, we have opened six stores for our Daily Wear concept, and we look to scale it to about 10 stores by March 2026.

items.statement: SSSG recovery target from negative to mid-single-digit positive over next year
items.quote: Today, we are at minus 5%. Our aim is to get to mid-single-digit to 5%, right? So from minus 5% we have to take it to plus 5%.

items.statement: No specific store opening guidance for next year; expansion will be muted and selective
items.quote: See, honestly, Gaurav, we are not guiding, unlike like earlier times, right, earlier times we used to be very clear with our guidance on how many store openings. This time we have seen that because of negative SSSG, margins have taken a hit. So under the management, we have taken a conscious call to slow down the store expansion and do it selectively.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 impacted by lower footfalls and subdued retail environment across industry
items.quote: The overall retail environment remained subdued with discretionary consumption, witnessing moderation across categories. Factors such as uneven festive demand, selective consumer spending and lower footfalls resulted in a slower same-store sales growth during the quarter.

items.statement: LFS channel sales dropped 30% due to key partner pausing inventory intake for 45 days
items.quote: Q3 FY '26 was deeply impacted by a slowdown in our LFS channel. One of our key LFS partners had a pause of fresh inventory intake across brands, which affected our LFS sales by 30%.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 gross margin stable at 64.3% despite revenue decline
items.quote: During Q3 FY '26, revenues stood at Rs. 194 crores, with gross margins of 64.3%.

items.statement: Full-price sales ratio maintained above 95% supporting gross margin stability
items.quote: The company continued to prioritize full-price sales ratio by maintaining a full-price sales ratio more than 95%. This disciplined approach helped us maintain healthy gross margins at a stable 64.3% in Q3 FY '26.

items.statement: Early EOSS start by 10 days impacted EBO gross margin offsetting mix benefit
items.quote: Last year we had started EOSS as a little late at the EBO level. This time we had started a little earlier, where usually we start. Last year, our EOSS start date itself was late. So, because the quarter three had a weak 10 days of more EOSS weeks, that could have had an impact on the EBO gross margin.

items.statement: Revenue mix shifted to 80% EBO from 74% last year; EBO gross margin 35-40% better than LFS
items.quote: Our revenue mix has improved towards EBO, right, so it is 80% EBU this time around versus 74% last year? Gautam Saraogi: Correct. Devanshu Bansal: The gross margin for this channel is about, in my understanding, 35%, 40% better versus the LFS channel, right

items.statement: Buyback announced of 14,13,000 shares at Rs. 460 per share totalling Rs. 65 crores
items.quote: In line of our commitment to shareholders, we have announced a buyback this quarter of 14,13,000 shares at a price of Rs. 460 per share, with a total size of Rs. 65 crores.

items.statement: Non-legging bottom wear category now contributes 65% of sales, up from less than 50% earlier
items.quote: Over the time, we have strengthened our position in the non-leggings category and it has further strengthened. Today, our non-legging bottom wear category gives us a 65% contribution in our sales, which in earlier times used to be less than 50%.

items.statement: Inventory at 114 days as of Dec 31, 2025; increase due to Daily Wear concept
items.quote: We continue to keep a close watch on inventory levels, with inventory levels being at 114 days as of December 31, 2025. On the inventory front, we have seen an increase in our inventory due to our new Daily Wear concept, which had increased our inventory marginally from the earlier times.

items.statement: GST reduction benefit passed to consumers; no MRP change; may remove discount instead of price hike later
items.quote: we are giving the benefit to the consumer. We have not changed our MRP for such products. So we are continuing to give the benefit to the consumer. There might be a time where we feel instead of taking a price hike for those products, we will just remove the discount what Go Fashion ( we were giving for the GST benefit

items.statement: No price increases planned for sub-Rs.1,000 products; only minor corrections on underpriced items
items.quote: No, not right now. See, Ankit, we are in a volume-led business, right, so our entire company focuses to drive volumes. I have reviewed the products under Rs. 1,000. We have made very small correction in certain products where we have increased the pricing because it was underpriced to begin with, but those are very, very few products.

items.statement: Online and quick commerce channels (Blinkit, Zepto) showing good traction; share to grow organically
items.quote: Our online channel has seen decent traction. Our quick commerce also we have been live on Blinkit and Zepto and we have seen very good traction there. So I think as that channel picks up speed for the apparel category, our share also in the e-com space will organically grow.

items.statement: LFS partner rebranded stores leading to exit of 137 stores; future LFS expansion dependent on partner proposals
items.quote: These stores are largely one of our key LFS partners. They have changed the format of that store and they have rebranded and changed the format of the store. So when that happened, all the external brands had to move out of those particular stores, including us.

items.statement: LFS partner format changes may continue; visibility limited; seeking clarity from partner
items.quote: Can it happen next year? Maybe yes. So we are also speaking to our partner and trying to get that clarity so that we are also prepared, or if there are going to be such format changes at their end we will know about it.

items.statement: 9M FY26 ROCE (ex-IndAS) at 13.1% and ROE at 10.3%
items.quote: ROCE and ROE, excluding IndAS impact, as on nine months FY '26, stood at 13.1% and 10.3%, respectively.

items.statement: 9M FY26 EBITDA margin at 29.2%; PAT margin at 8%
items.quote: EBITDA is at Rs. 187 crores, with EBITDA margin at 29.2%. PAT stood at Rs. 51 crores, with a PAT margin of 8%.

items.statement: International store in Dubai and Daily Wear concept showing healthy unit economics in early stages
items.quote: On our new initiatives, including our international store in Dubai, and our Daily Wear concept are demonstrating healthy unit economics in early stages, and we remain excited about their performance in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Smaller stores seeing SSSG decline of 9-10% vs company average of -5%; relocations planned
items.quote: Ankit, no, I will tell you, like for example where our company average level is minus 5%, the smaller stores we have seen a slightly higher degrowth of more than 9%, 10% SSSG.

items.statement: Unit economics similar for stores up to 1,000 sq ft; changes dramatically beyond 1,000 sq ft
items.quote: Even a 600 square feet store from a unit economic perspective comes under the same category as well. So it's not that my EBO unit economics will go down because I am opening a 500 square feet, 600 square feet store. See, if today I would have gone and opened, say, 2,000 square feet, 3,000 square feet store, that's a completely different unit economics.

items.statement: New bottom-wear stores will be 500-1,000 sq ft; unlikely to exceed 1,000 sq ft unless rental deal is very good.
items.quote: So for the new stores what we are opening for the bottom wear will be below 1,000, largely. So it will be in that range between 500 sqft. and 1,000 sqft.

items.statement: Stores below 300-350 sq ft are classified as small; management is calibrating data on these stores and will guide on closures once lease renewal clarity emerges.
items.quote: When I talk about a small store, yes, any store which is effectively lower than a 300 square feet or 350 square feet store comes down to being a small store.

items.statement: Negative SSSG is driven by footfall decline, not product mix; footfalls down ~5% when SSSG is -5%.
items.quote: The main reason of SSSG decline is because of the decline in footfalls. So suppose if you are having minus 5% SSSG today, our footfalls are down by minus 5%.

items.statement: Channel checks show broad-based slowness across women's apparel categories (ethnic, western, fusion, top and bottom wear).
items.quote: we have seen a decline everywhere, but in the women's category we have seen a bigger decline, and this I am talking about in general overall women's apparel.

items.statement: Non-leggings share at ~65% of sales; mix evolution is structural and unrelated to negative SSSG.
items.quote: for this quarter you have given bifurcation wherein from non-leggings, sales is around 65%.

items.statement: Value-added bottom wear (trousers, palazzos) have shorter lifecycle (1-2 years) vs leggings (3-4 years) but not fast-fashion risk.
items.quote: If a legging churidar stayed in season for three years, four years, maybe other value-added products will be for more than a year and closer to two years.

items.statement: Pricing benchmarked to like-to-like competition; aim for parity or lower; occasional single-product overpricing corrected quickly.
items.quote: In general when we are releasing products, we benchmark to see that we are not very expensive compared to competition. We should be either on par or maybe lesser and that's how our pricing strategy is.

items.statement: Leggings priced at Rs 599 vs market range of Rs 549-649; management believes pricing is sharp and price cuts would not boost footfalls.
items.quote: If you take a product of similar spec, you will see brands selling between Rs. 549 and Rs. 649. So we are somewhere in between, we are at Rs. 599.

items.statement: Gross margin steady at 62-64%; no expansion expected; EBITDA margin improvement depends on sales recovery and operating leverage.
items.quote: currently at a company, we are between around 62% to 64% of gross margin we are delivering right now. See, from a gross margin delivery perspective, we are very happy, and I do not see any expansion there.

items.statement: High gross margin reflects 95% full-price sales ratio and negligible discounting.
items.quote: We are in a very full-price sales category. So, because we are able to achieve and keep that 95% of the full price sales ratio going, that is very clearly indicative in our gross margins.

items.statement: New customer acquisition volume up but percentage down due to larger base; focus on younger age groups.
items.quote: our new customer acquisitions have been slightly on the lower side. The actual quantum of new customer acquisitions have increased, but because the base has increased, the percentage has fallen slightly.

items.statement: Digital marketing shifted to personalized, product-led communication via WhatsApp/Instagram and influencers to drive repeat visits.
items.quote: our entire digital marketing has become more personalized around the products with our existing customers and new customers. So, we are leading our digital marketing more transitioning into product-led communication than just brand communication.

items.statement: Market share stable at 8% of Rs 10,000 cr branded bottom-wear market (FY24 Technopak report).
items.quote: the report says that we are having the same 8% market share in FY '24 what we had earlier. And it shows that the branded market for bottom wear is a Rs. 10,000 crores branded bottom wear market as on 2024, in which we have a 8% market share.

items.statement: Acknowledges rise of unlisted agile brands (Snitch, Souled Store, etc.) adding supply; believes Go Colors pricing remains sharp vs them.
items.quote: the number of brands in the retail industry whether unlisted, whether listed, whether Go Fashion ( digital, whether offline has significantly increased

items.statement: Inventory days at 114 currently (up due to muted sales); target steady-state 85-90 days given size/color SKU complexity.
items.quote: Currently we have about 114 days and the reason why inventory has slightly gone up, your inventory days has increased because of muted sales.

items.statement: Payable days kept low to secure better pricing, which supports gross margin.
items.quote: We get a better pricing, that's why we keep our payable days low, and that reflects in the gross margin.

items.statement: Online channel remains small; category is touch-and-feel driven; large store network makes offline faster than delivery.
items.quote: our category is a very offline category because of the colors, the touch and feel, the fitting. I think women in general prefer and find the product out in a physical store.

items.statement: Lease terms standardized at 9-12 years with standard lock-ins; rent-to-revenue ratio used for site economics, not rent per sq ft.
items.quote: Our agreements are very standardized. We do the lease from anywhere from nine years to 12 years, and our lock-in periods are very standardized what the industry follows.

items.statement: COCO model preferred for hygiene, SOPs, customer experience; franchisee only selectively in markets without operational control.
items.quote: We have realized that COCO stores deliver a much better customer experience because we have SOPs in place. So for us, we are largely going to go to the COCO route.

items.statement: LFS channel volatility in Q3 due to partner withholding POs post-festive without notice; issue resolved post-Dec 15.
items.quote: we were obviously not informed once festive got over, POs were on hold, we could not sell stock. It was something we did not know about it, we obviously could not foresee it.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth (SSSG) negative for 11 quarters; footfalls directly correlate with SSSG.
items.quote: what directly correlates with negative SSSG is the footfalls and not the product mix. Because what we have seen in the past, even in the good times when we had double-digit SSSG during pre-COVID, our legging, churidar contribution was falling at that point of time and our other product sales was improving.

items.statement: Management will guide on small-store closure count once lease renewal data is calibrated; no timeline given.
items.quote: as we get more clarity on that, we will definitely guide the market on how many such stores in the smaller bucket is there and how many of the smaller stores will be shutting in the short-term

name: Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Ltd

items.statement: Regulator guided 10% price hike for senior citizen products; similar range expected across portfolio
items.quote: So, Dipanjan, the guidance says that 10% senior citizen is the number that has been guided by the regulator. So, you can assume that that will be the number for almost all the products in that range, maybe slightly higher or lower depending on the product portfolio.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 combined ratio improved 320 bps YoY to 98.9%; loss ratio down 301 bps to 68.8%
items.quote: We reported IND AS underwriting profit of Rs. 46 crore in Q3 FY2026 as compared to an underwriting loss of Rs. 79 crore in Q3 FY2025. This was driven by improvement in combined ratio by almost 320 basis points from 102.1 % in Q3 FY2025 to 98.9% in Q3 FY2026.

items.statement: 9M FY26 combined ratio improved 222 bps YoY to 99.8%; loss ratio 70%, expense ratio 29.8%
items.quote: We reported IND AS underwriting profit of Rs. 20 crore in 9MFY2026 as compared to a loss of Rs. 227 crore in 9M FY2025. This was driven by significant improvement in combined ratio by 2 22 basis points from 102.1 % in 9MFY2025 to 99.8% in our current 9M FY2026.

items.statement: Retail health insurance grew 33.6% YoY in Q3 FY26 vs 11.5% for non-life; GST exemption driving category growth
items.quote: While overall non-life insurance grew at 11.5% in Q3 FY2026, retail health insurance grew 33.6%, that is 3x more over the same period.

items.statement: GWP grew 23% YoY to Rs 5,047 crore in Q3 FY26; 9M FY26 GWP up 16% to Rs 13,856 crore
items.quote: In Q3 FY2026, our top-line i.e. the GWP on N basis increased by 23% year-on-year to Rs. 5,047 crore.

items.statement: Fresh premium grew 45% YoY in Q3; renewal premium grew 17% YoY in Q3
items.quote: Continuing with N basis on the business metrics during the quarter, our gross premium increased 23% year-on-year by fresh business growth of 45% and the renewal premium growth of 17%.

items.statement: Long-term policies 51% of fresh GWP in 9M FY26 vs 34% YoY; 23% of fresh NOP vs 14%
items.quote: On GWP basis, it is 51% versus 34% on nine months last year.

items.statement: Retail to group mix 95:5 in 9M FY26 vs 91:9 in 9M FY25
items.quote: On a YTD basis, our reta il to group business mix was 95:5 as against 91:9 for 9M FY2025.

items.statement: Agency channel 83% of business; agent count exceeds 8 lakh; 60% fresh business from semi-urban/rural
items.quote: Our granular market reach continues to convert consumer demand into growth with 60% fresh business emerging f rom semi-urban and rural markets. So, Star Health is as we know very strong in the semi -urban and rural markets as well and we continue to invest in the agency channel with overall agent count exceeding 8 lakh by December 31, 2025.

items.statement: Digital channel 9% of GWP, 20% of fresh business; 77% from in-house D2C; GWP up 35% YoY in 9M
items.quote: Digital channel contributed 9% of our overall business and 20% of the fresh business for 9M FY2026. Our GWP from digital channels grew 35% year-on-year basis for nine months driven by a strong fresh premium growth of more than 46%.

items.statement: Bancassurance 7% of GWP; 94% fresh premium from preferred products vs 76% YoY; added 6 new partners
items.quote: We have deliberately upgraded the mix of our bank assurance products towards certain preferred products which is now making almost 94% of our fresh premium contribution in 9M FY2026, which used to be 76% in last year nine months. We continu e to expand our base of Banca partnerships. We have added six new Banca partners during the current fiscal.

items.statement: Corporate channel 1% of GWP; 73% from SME segment vs 44% YoY; group loss ratio improved to 83.5% from 94.6%
items.quote: Corporate contributed 1% of our overall GWP owing to our recalibrated channel strategy as we have articulated earlier. In this phase, we are focusing on the higher quality SME segment with 73% of the corporate business coming fro m the SME segment during these nine month compared to 44% in the previous year. Our corporate group loss ratios have significantly improved from 94.6% in 9M FY2025 to 83.

items.statement: Medical inflation expected 12-13% in 2026; price increases essential for sustainability
items.quote: Medical inflation in India continues to be at a very elevated level. Various studies conducted by leading firms like Aon and Willis Towers Watson expect medical inflation in India to be higher than 12% to 13% in 2026. Unless there is a structural cost moderation through government interventions, price increases by insurance companies would be essential to preserve sustainability.

items.statement: FHO cohort-based pricing showing good results; better retention for non-claimants; will continue approach
items.quote: As far as the cohort -based pricing approach that we took for FHO, that has given us very good results. We are clearly seeing a good lift in terms of the no n-claimants and the risks that are giving us better retentions. So, that is clearly playing out and we will follow this approach going forward as well.

items.statement: Regulator may review expense of management limits; company prepared for strict implementation
items.quote: I think there is, we expect that the regulator may be reviewing this. This is what we have been also hearing. We await for some final clarity on that. But at a macro level, I think in the larger interest of the consumers, expenses of management have to be adhered to and we believe that it has to be implemented very, very strictly.

items.statement: Hospital negotiations ongoing with AHPI and GI council; common empanelment work progressing
items.quote: We are seeing good interaction with hospitals with multiple partners like AHPI and all of that. We are talking to all of them. We are meeting them. We are also able to see some acceptance of, you know, from their side to find a solution which is a win-win for all of us. There is a lot of work going on at the GI council level, as you know, in terms of common empanelment of hospitals and so on.

items.statement: Largest tech investor in health insurance; 94% new policies digital; 76% premiums digital; ATOM app 85% fresh acquisitions
items.quote: Probably, we are the largest investor in technology in the health insurance business. So, we are able to deliver tangible progress on both productivity and service outcomes. Digital is now embedded across the value chain through our modernization of legacy platforms, our workflow automation and enablement of multiple straight-through journeys at scale.

items.statement: AI claims platform handles 57% claims traffic; home healthcare expanded to 300+ locations; telemedicine up 73%
items.quote: On the claims and wellness side, our AI -powered claims platform continues to scale and has now enabled migration of around 57% of our claims traffic, translating to better productivity outcomes and also reduction in FWA. We expanded our home healthcare services to more than 300 locations from around 250 at the close of last quarter. Expansion of doctors and specialties has driven 73% growth in ou

items.statement: Retail loss ratio 68.4% in Q3 FY26, down 103 bps YoY; 9M retail claims ratio 69.4%
items.quote: The retail loss ratios also have decreased by 103 basis points year-on-year to 68.4% in this quarter.

items.statement: Claims settlement ratio 90% in 9M FY26; grievance ratio 20 per 10k policies vs 22 YoY
items.quote: Our claims settlement ratio consolidated at 90% for 9M FY2026. Our grievance ratios for 10,000 policies reduced from 22 in 9M FY2025 to 20 for 9M FY2026.

items.statement: Renewal persistency 99.2% value-wise in 9M FY26; cashless claims NPS 72 (industry leading); overall NPS 64
items.quote: Our renewal retention trends which is also indicator of the consumer satisfaction were robust during 9M FY2026 with 99.2% persistency value-wise. Our claims NPS improved to 63 in December 2024. More importantly, our cas hless claims NPS improved to 72 from 63 during the same period last year. So, our cashless claims NPS probably is the industry leading right now with 72 points. Our overall company

items.statement: Outstanding claims 8.5-10% of NEP; IBNR strengthened quarterly; cashless claims 85% of book
items.quote: But we believe it should be in that range of 8.5% to 9.5%, 10%. It should operate in that range. So, we tried it on a trailing 12 -month basis also which is the right metric.

items.statement: Investment yield 9.6% in 9M FY26; 18.7% in high-yield assets (equities, ETFs, REITs, InvITs)
items.quote: We registered an investment yield of 9.6% for 9M FY2026, supported by a diversified profile of assets. As on 31st December 2025, 18.7% of our book was in high-yielding assets such as equities, ETFs, REITs and InvITs.

items.statement: Equity cap at 15%; REITs/InvITs at regulatory 3% cap; AIF drawdowns small but scaling; core fixed income yield 7.71%
items.quote: For equities, currently, we have kept this cap of 15%. And obviously, it would be a function of opportunities. So, that is one. As far as REITs and InvITs are concerned, there is a regulatory cap of 3%. We are currently operating close to 3. On AIFs, we have started investing. Drawdowns are small, but we do have intent to scale up the book slowly.

items.statement: Sombit Bhattacharyya joined as Head of Investor Relations; Aditya Biyani moving to business role
items.quote: I would also like to take this opportunity to introduce Sombit, who has joined us as the Head of Investor Relations, and he will be interacting with all of you. I would like to also take this opportunity to thank Aditya, who has been your face of the company, meeting all of you. He will continue to be with Star Health to play a very important role on the business side of things.

items.statement: IFRS P&L volatility from equity MTM; equity returns correlated to nominal GDP growth long-term
items.quote: But yes, quarter-to-quarter, there would be volatility. That is the problem of IFRS, you know, that P&L accounts would become volatile. But that does not mean that we should stay a way from high yielding assets, especially when we are long term investors in the market.

items.statement: Labour code one-time impact Rs 16.5 crore in Q3 opex; ESOP cost only under IFRS, not IGAAP
items.quote: In terms of labor code, the one-time impact for the quarter is Rs. 16.5 crore, which is reported in Opex, and that is again, which is the point for impact on the expense ratio for the quarter.

items.statement: Targets 55-60% occupancy for next year
items.quote: Our objective is to improve occupancy to around 55%–60%, which is the range where we deliver strong operational and financial outcomes.

items.statement: Targets 17-18% revenue CAGR over four-year period
items.quote: Over a four-year period, we believe we should be able to achieve around 17-18% CAGR.

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA margin aspiration 24-25%
items.quote: From a consolidated perspective, our long-term margin aspiration remains around 24% to 25% EBITDA.

items.statement: Expects ARPP to grow at 5-7% CAGR long term
items.quote: We expect ARPP to grow at around 5%–7% CAGR over the long term.

items.statement: Invested INR 57 crores in capex during Q3 FY26
items.quote: During the quarter, company has invested INR57 crores in capital expenditures towards expanding and enhancing our services at existing and upcoming hospitals.

items.statement: Commissioned 100-bed hospital at Rajahmundry
items.quote: During the quarter, we commissioned a 100-bed hospital at Rajahmundry, strengthening our presence in Coastal Andhra Pradesh.

items.statement: 90-bed spoke hospital in Electronic City Bangalore commenced operations
items.quote: The 90-bed spoke hospital in Electronic City, Bangalore, it just commenced the operations, reinforcing our footprint and advancing the hub-and-spoke model in Bengaluru.

items.statement: 60-bed Hennur Bangalore hospital awaiting final approvals, expects to commence in few weeks
items.quote: The 60-bed spoke hospital in Hennur in Bengaluru city is in concluding stages, and we're awaiting for the final governmental approvals. We expect to commence operations in a few weeks' time.

items.statement: 130-bed Coimbatore hub hospital construction started, targeting operations by end of 2027
items.quote: The construction has started at the regional hub hospital at Coimbatore of 130 beds. We are targeting to commence operations by end of the '27.

items.statement: Gurgaon expansion at basement stage, expects to complete basement slabs in 3 months
items.quote: Our upcoming Gurgaon hospital's expansion in Sector 44 and Sector 56 NCR, right now we are at the basement stage slab, and we are hoping to complete the basement slabs in 3 months' time.

items.statement: 150-bed Pune greenfield hub received plan approvals, excavation started
items.quote: The greenfield regional hub hospital in Pune of 150 beds has received project plan approvals from government and excavation work has just started.

items.statement: Added close to 780 beds over last two years, next phase over 18-24 months
items.quote: Over the last two years, we have added close to 780 beds, which is a significant capacity expansion. Our pipeline remains strong, with the next phase of bed additions expected over the next 18 to 24 months.

items.statement: Plans to operationalize additional beds at Guwahati hospital in next 3-4 months
items.quote: Over the next three to four months— likely in the early part of the next financial year— we plan to operationalize additional beds at the Guwahati hospital.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 saw muted seasonality impacting occupancy, especially in mature hospitals
items.quote: Currently, our overall occupancy stands at around 47.2%. This year, we have seen some muted seasonality across the group, more pronounced in mature hospitals such as Hyderabad, Andhra Pradesh, and Bangalore.

items.statement: Inpatient discharges grew 9%, outpatient volumes 18%, deliveries 16% YoY in Q3 FY26
items.quote: In terms of the operational performance, inpatient discharges, outpatient volume witnessed a growth of 9% and 18%, respectively, when compared to the corresponding period of the last financial year. Deliveries grew by an impressive 16% when compared to the corresponding period of last year.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin at 33%, 9M FY26 at 32.1%
items.quote: The EBITDA margin for the current quarter is at around 33%, while for the first 9 months, our EBITDA margin is 32.1%.

items.statement: Guwahati margins broadly in line with company level, Warangal EBITDA positive and improving
items.quote: Margins at Guwahati are broadly in line with company-level margins. Warangal is EBITDA positive and continues to improve, though it is still on a ramp-up trajectory.

items.statement: Rajahmundry close to breakeven in last month of quarter
items.quote: Yes, Rajahmundry is close to breakeven—specifically in the last month of the quarter.

items.statement: Expects most units launched over last two years to be EBITDA positive by next year
items.quote: Overall, by next year, most units launched over the last two years should be EBITDA positive.

items.statement: Bangalore units Electronic City and Hennur expected full-year EBITDA loss of INR 12-15 crores for FY26-27
items.quote: Yes, INR 12–15 crores would be a prudent assumption.

items.statement: Guwahati revenue INR 26-27 crores, Warangal INR 7 crores in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Guwahati contributed approximately INR 26–27 crores, and Warangal contributed around INR 7 crores during the quarter.

items.statement: Payor mix 51% insurance, 49% cash in Q3 FY26; 9M FY26 52% insurance, 48% cash
items.quote: Our payor mix continued to remain robust and the balance with 51% of the revenue coming from the insurance, and the balance 49% coming from the cash patients.

items.statement: Competition increasing in Hyderabad from multi-specialty hospitals re-entering mother-child care and standalone clinics
items.quote: Competition in Hyderabad has existed for the last 10–12 years, but it is certainly increasing. Multi-specialty hospitals that earlier lost pediatric and obstetric volumes are now attempting to re-enter mother-and-child care within their broader hospital frameworks.

items.statement: Evaluating selective CGHS empanelment at revised rates, no decision taken yet
items.quote: We are also evaluating selective CGHS empanelment at revised rates, though no decision has been taken yet.

items.statement: International revenue at 2% currently, targeting 4-5% over time by diversifying source markets
items.quote: We have gradually come back to around 2% of revenue from international business. While we had originally budgeted for about 4%, geopolitical situations significantly impacted some of our key source markets.

items.statement: Cash position INR 579 crores as of Dec 31 2025, sufficient for planned capex and M&A
items.quote: I'm pleased to inform that our company continued to maintain a robust balance sheet with a cash position of INR579 crores as of December 31, 2025. These funds will support our ongoing capital expenditure, merger and acquisitions plans.

items.statement: Appointed Abrarali Dalal as Group CEO with 25 years experience across healthcare, telecom, FMCG
items.quote: I'm pleased to welcome Mr. Abrarali Dalal as a Chief Executive Officer. I'm sure his leadership and experience will be a strong addition to the organization.

items.statement: Occupancy for Q3 FY26 stood at 47.2%
items.quote: Occupancy for the quarter stood at 47.2%.

items.statement: ALOS typically fluctuates between 2.6-2.8 days with average around 2.7 days
items.quote: ALOS typically fluctuates between 2.6 and 2.8 days, with an average of around 2.7. This is appropriate for our business model.

items.statement: IVF contributes ~4% of revenue (INR 17-18 crores), Butterfly Essentials ~1% (INR 4 crores quarterly)
items.quote: IVF business currently contributes around 4% of overall revenue, translating to approximately INR 17–18 crores. We believe this represents a good scale-up so far. As for Butterfly Essentials, it continues to grow. On a quarterly basis, it contributes roughly INR 4 crores, which is about 1% of total

items.statement: Daily average AUM for first 9 months FY26 was INR119,000 crores; opening AUM for Q3 FY26 was INR130,000 crores, up 9.2%
items.quote: During the first 9 months, we earned revenue on a daily average AUM of INR119,000 crores. Our opening AUM for the current quarter stands at around INR130,000 crores. That's an increase of about 9.2%.

items.statement: Current AUM stands at approximately INR126,000 crores after Nifty500 correction of around 5%
items.quote: In the current month, the broader Nifty500 Index has corrected by around 5%. And consequently, our current AUM stands at approximately INR126,000 crores.

items.statement: Equity net sales for January crossed INR1,200 crores as of yesterday
items.quote: Our equity net sales for the January have crossed INR1,200 crores as of yesterday, which has helped cushion the impact of market volatility.

items.statement: SIP book increased from INR1,130 crores in December 2025 to INR1,170 crores
items.quote: SIP addition has also remained robust during the month, with our SIP book increased from INR1,170 crores compared to INR1,130 crores in December 2025.

items.statement: Quarterly average AUM for Q3 FY26 was INR127,600 crores, up 21% YoY and 7.2% QoQ
items.quote: The average AUM for the quarter was INR127,600 crores. Our quarterly average AUM grew by 21% year-on-year and 7.2% quarter-on-quarter, reflecting steady and sustained business momentum.

items.statement: Equity AUM grew 22.4% YoY from INR102,700 crores to INR125,700 crores in December 2025
items.quote: Starting with year-on-year view on left, our equity AUM grew by 22.4% during Q3 of FY '26. It moved from INR102,700 crores in December '24 to INR125,700 crores in December '25.

items.statement: Equity AUM grew 6.9% QoQ driven by mark-to-market gain and net sales of INR3,444 crores
items.quote: Coming to quarter-on-quarter view on the right, equity AUM grew by 6.9% during the quarter. This was driven by mark-to-market gain and a strong net sales of INR3,444 crores.

items.statement: Aim to cross INR1,200 crores in monthly SIP flows by March 2026
items.quote: We aim to cross INR1,200 crores in monthly SIP flows by March 2026.

items.statement: Mutual fund revenue grew 8.2% QoQ vs 7.2% AUM growth; yield stable excluding one-off INR1.4 crore brokerage release
items.quote: On the mutual fund side, our quarterly average AUM grew by 7.2% sequentially, while the mutual fund revenue has increased by 8.2%. The mutual funds revenue grew at a faster pace, led by an extra income to the tune of INR1.4 crores due to release of individual brokerage following some relaxation in KYC norms. Excluding this one-off income, our yield were stable on a sequential basis.

items.statement: Insurance premium grew 13% QoQ but revenue grew only 3.6% due to rate rationalization post GST changes in retail health
items.quote: On the insurance front, our premium grew by 13% sequentially, led by a good uptick in our LI vertical. However, revenue grew at a slower pace of 3.6%, primarily driven by the rationalization of rate post GST changes in the retail health vertical.

items.statement: Operating expenses grew 7.2% QoQ including one-off INR1.49 crore labor code provision and INR1.61 crore ESOP charge
items.quote: During the quarter, employee costs included one-off provision of INR1.49 crores related to implementation of new labor code. In addition, there was an ESOP charge of INR1.61 crores for this quarter, and it will remain the same for next 3 quarters as an annualized cost for ESOP would be in the range of INR7.2 crores.

items.statement: Finance cost increased by INR92.32 lakh per quarter due to deferred consideration for Indus Capital; will continue for next 11 quarters
items.quote: Increase in finance cost of INR92.32 lakh is attributable to accounting treatment of deferred consideration payable to Indus capital. Deferred payout is recognized at its discounted present value and periodically recognized as the finance expense. Accordingly, interest accretion of INR92.3 lakh has been charged to P&L. Please keep a note that these costs will continue to be recognized over the nex

items.statement: Depreciation policy changed for Karvy assets from 10 to 15 years, reducing quarterly amortization by INR1.7 crores; Indus assets to be amortized over 15 years
items.quote: Karvy in November 2021, we have been depreciating the acquired assets over a 10-year period. Accordingly, in consultation with our auditors, we have revised the useful life of these assets to 15 years, extending the depreciation period up to Novemb

items.statement: Net profit grew 7.6% QoQ and 19.6% YoY to INR57.6 crores; 9M net profit up 13.2% to INR162.9 crores
items.quote: A stable operating performance has led to a net profit growth of 7.6% sequentially and 19.6% on a year-on-year basis to INR57.6 crores. On a 9-month basis, net profit grew by 13.2% to INR162.9 crores.

items.statement: Indus integration working well; completed two meetings with big clients; looking for similar acquisition opportunities with treasury corpus of INR537 crores
items.quote: Given the successful integration and experience, we are in a lookout for similar opportunity in this space, wherein distributors are seeking alignment with scale, technology-driven platform to ensure business and service continuity for their clients. items.statement: SEBI TER changes: expense ratio now exclusive of GST (revenue neutral for GST-registered); 5bp exit load benefit removed; level playing field helps attract smaller players
items.quote: Under the new structure, my rate will be 85 basis points, exclusive of GST, so I'll invoice GST on top of that and still effectively earn 1%. So, more or less, we believe it's revenue neutral for those who are registered under the GST. items.statement: No AMC has initiated discussion on passing TER cut; discussions expected mid-February; clarity by mid-March
items.quote: As of now, no AMC has started the discussion about passing on the TER cut. My guess is that, by mid of March, probably we will have a better clarity. We definitely will start discussion with the AMCs mid-February.

items.statement: Life insurance GST impact reduced from 30% to less than 10% of business by December through renegotiation; arrangement only till March
items.quote: In the month of December, we could renegotiate that cut with the same manufacturer. So as of now, I think at least till March, the cut in the GST component from the life insurance business is not even 30%. I think it will be less than 10% now.

items.statement: Non-GST distributors will get commission net of GST from April, improving Prudent's competitiveness and margins on those partners
items.quote: From April, on the same business, he will get x minus 18%. So, by default, the competitiveness or the margins of Prudent on that particular partner or that particular MFD will increase. So yes, I think that is a very, very positive point.

Here, I would say that, yes, I think, our PMS book is increasing steadily. So that also contr

items.quote: If you look at last year, we added close to around 4,700, 4,800 distributors in Prudent kitty. And this year, we will be able to add these many numbers in the Prudent platform. So, we don't see that, I think the number of distributors joining Prudent has come down. It's the same. So there is no change.

items.statement: Top 5 AMCs contribute ~50% of AUM; expected to pass on TER cut to all channels including Prudent
items.quote: So, top 5 AMCs contribute around 50% of our AUM. Whether they will pass it on that cut to the distribution community? The answer is definitely yes. They would pass on some cut or the entire cut to the distribution community.

items.statement: More than 50% of AUM from non-GST distributors; savings from GST change will compensate yield loss
items.quote: Today, I would say that almost -- more than 50% of our AUM is contributed by those guys who are non-GST. Whatever we will be able to save, that will definitely compensate the loss in the yield.

items.quote: That is what I say one-third of that is INR10,000 crores, so it's roughly about one-third, 35% is from direct. I can say the number, 35% comes from the direct.

items.statement: January saw highest ever new SIP registration, net SIP addition, net sales, health insurance; second highest life insurance despite market correction
items.quote: As I said, our numbers in January is the highest ever in new SIP registration. The highest ever in net SIP addition, the highest ever in net sales, the highest ever in health insurance. The second highest in life insurance.

items.statement: SIP terminations higher than last year but not alarming; no increased termination seen in January despite market correction
items.quote: I think, yes, if you are comparing the termination ratio versus the last year, definitely, it is higher than the last year. items.statement: No lump-sum pickup seen in current correction unlike past cycles; negative news deterring side-line investors
items.quote: Right now, the market in a correction zone for almost last 12 months, so expecting that another new additional flow comes when -- in the month of January, I think what the February market correction comes. items.quote: Third is, number of employees are 1,539, 1-5-3-9 as on 31st December -- number of employees.

items.statement: SIP market share improved 20bps from 3.3% to 3.5% in December 2025
items.quote: Our market share has improved by 20 basis points from 3.3% in December 2024 to 3.5% in December 2025.

items.quote: Q4 going forward, we are confident that we should be able to grow sequential or sequential target, which we did about INR1,264 crores, we should be able to grow this figure by about INR1,600 crores plus such that we should be sitting at anything between INR4,850 crores, INR4,900 crores to INR5,000 crores. That's the range. But to me, the revenue figures are very important, but more important is th

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth target of 30% and EBITDA growth of 30% to INR650 crores
items.quote: So, if we are able to do about INR5,000 crores, INR4,900 crores of revenue this year, a 30% growth will be what would result in to. And more importantly, if we deliver INR500 crores EBITDA, which I'm very confident, it's not. If it will deliver INR500 crores EBITDA this year, next year, a 30% growth rate is INR650 crores of EBITDA.

items.statement: Order book visibility INR6,400 crores as of December end with auto 31%, consumer 25%, industrial 27%
items.quote: Our order book visibility as of December end is approximately INR6,400 crores, which includes auto sector related approximately 31%; consumer business, about 25%; industrial business, 27%; and balance in healthcare, IT/railways.

items.value: INR529 crores gross debt; INR404 crores net cash

items.statement: EU-India FTA signed; long-term positive for electronics exports, especially auto electronics
items.quote: One very positive thing which has happened a couple of days back is the signing of the EU -- FTA with the EU Union. Some of the end equipment's, which were attracting duties, have been rationalized or brought down to zero or very low dutie

items.quote: Coming to ROCE performance, ROCE for the quarter is approximately 16% on an adjusted basis when we adjusted for the goodwill and unutilized IPO money. items.quote: Gross margin for the quarter is 27.4% as against 26% for Q3 of last year. items.quote: Yes, this closing debt was not exactly available for the entire period. So, this is something -- during the quarter, the debt number was actually lower. items.statement: Tax rate ~23-24% for Q4 FY26, ~26% for FY27
items.quote: Tax rate for the fourth quarter would be somewhere around 23% -- 23%, 24%. And next year, we can assume over 26%.

items.value: INR80-100 crores organic; INR300-350 crores PCB

items.statement: Current portfolio proportion improved 10 bps to 81.77% in December from 81.67% in September
items.quote: We have seen the first reflection of this in Q3, where the current proposition of our portfolio has gone up from 81.67% in September to 81.77% in December.

items.statement: Unique customer collection efficiency stable at 95.1% and overall at 96.6% vs last quarter
items.quote: Our focus on collections is also reflected in our collection metrics, with both unique customer collection efficiency and overall collection efficiency remain stable at 95.1% and 96.6%, respectively, compared with last quarter.

items.statement: Unique customer collection efficiency excluding NPA loans rose to 97.26% from 96.5% in Q2
items.quote: If the NPA loans are excluded, the unique customer collection efficiency goes up from 96.5% in Q2 to 97.26% in Q3.

items.statement: Unique customer collections on current book improved to 99.01% from 98.5% in Q2
items.quote: Additionally, the unique customer collections on the current book, which is the most important bucket for any lender, have gone up from 98.5% in Q2 to 99.01% in Q3.

items.statement: Stage-3 slippages remain slightly elevated but credit cost only up marginally to 1.44% from 1.34%
items.quote: Despite the slight elevated slippages, the credit cost has only gone up marginally from 1.34% in Q2 to 1.44% in Q3, reflecting adequate provision coverage on our loans.

items.statement: Recoveries from NPA and technical write-offs were INR 23 crores in Q3
items.quote: During Q3, our recoveries from NPA or technical write-offs amounted to about INR 23 crores in a quarter, and given this trajectory, we are confident of maintaining a healthy recovery trend in quarters to come.

items.statement: Stage-2 assets flat at INR 1,249 crores vs Q2, indicating controlled fresh slippages from Stage-1
items.quote: In fact, one of the data points that we would like to give you is that during the current quarter, our Stage-2 assets stood at INR 1,249 crores, almost the same as what was there in Q2.

items.statement: Addition to Stage-2 assets lowest in 4-5 quarters at INR 70-80 crores vs INR 130-140 crores earlier
items.quote: This quarter has probably seen the lowest addition to Stage-2 assets in the last maybe 4 to 5 quarters. What used to be about INR 130 crores, INR 140 crores, this quarter I think it's almost like INR 70 crores, INR 80 crores.

items.statement: Write-offs in Q3 were INR 63 crores
items.quote: So, about INR 63 crores.

items.statement: Overall provision coverage at 1.7-1.8% of AUM, expected to hover in this range
items.quote: For the foreseeable future, you will see this number hovering maybe around 1.7% to 1.8%.

items.quote: On the yields, the yields are moving in the same trajectory that we have guided in the past, about 20 basis points of drop every quarter, primarily on account of lower yields on incremental disbursements, but we have managed to counter this well with similar drop in our cost of funds, so the spread remains almost stable at about 13.9%.

items.statement: NIMs compressed ~50 bps YoY and ROA fell from 8% to 7% due to lower disbursements and credit costs
items.quote: There has been a marginal increase in Opex due to lower disbursements and lower growth, and coupled with credit costs, we have seen our NIMs compress by about 50 basis points on a year-on-year basis, and our ROA has come down by about 1% from 8% to 7%.

items.statement: Cost of incremental debt at 8.19%, slightly lower than previous quarter
items.quote: On the borrowings, during the quarter, we availed incremental debt of INR 460 crores, and the cost of incremental debt came at 8.19%, which is slightly lower than the cost of incremental debt borrowed during the previous quarter.

items.statement: Cost of funds on book dropped >50 bps YoY from 9.63% to 9.12%
items.quote: Over the past 1 year, the cost of funds on the book has dropped by over 50 bps, from 9.63% to 9.12% from Q3 last year to Q3 this year.

items.statement: Further 10-15 bps cost of funds benefit expected in next 3-6 months from RBI repo transmission
items.quote: So, I think if I have to put a number, maybe another 10 to 15 basis points benefit should certainly be there, purely on account of actions taken by RBI. But the good part is also that we are borrowing at rates which are much lower than what is the cost of funds on the book, which should also give us a kicker in terms of benefit and cost of funds.

items.statement: Liquidity buffer INR 2,276 crores and unavailed sanction lines ~INR 1,500 crores
items.quote: Liquidity buffer was at INR 2,276 crores and unavailed sanction lines were little less than INR 1,500 crores.

items.quote: we continue to invest in people and in physical infrastructure, reflected in the additions of 35 branches and 678 business and collection office rs during Q3, in line with our collections focus. items.quote: There is no significant impact to us because we don't have the vintage as a company and as a business. It is just a 5 year, 5.6 years old business. So, we are not crossing the threshold.

items.statement: Demand visibility healthy for FY26 supported by strong corporate activity and sustained MICE momentum; Q4 typically a strong quarter.
items.quote: Looking ahead, our outlook for FY '26 remains strong. The demand visibility continues to be healthy, supported by strong corporate activity and sustained mice momentum. We are also expecting improved traction from our F&B offerings. We expect this momentum to continue into the coming quarters.

items.quote: The demand and supply dynamics for the next 5 years are very healthy in all the markets we're operating, be it Bangalore, Chennai, Hyderabad. So, for Bangalore as well, the supply is growing only at 7.3% for the next 5 years, whereas demand is growing at 10.1%.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 ARR INR7,852 (+17% YoY), occupancy 76.1%, RevPAR INR5,973 (+17% YoY); 9M ARR INR7,246 (+12%), occupancy 75.4%, RevPAR INR5,465 (+12%).
items.quote: From an operational standpoint, during Q3 FY '26 ARR stood at INR7,852 compared to INR6,708 in Q3 FY '25, with occupancy at 76.1%. This translated into a RevPAR of INR5,973 reflecting a year-on-year growth of 17%.

items.statement: Net cash position INR132 crores as of 31 Dec 2025; adjusted ROCE 13.1%, ROCE (operating) 18.8% for 9M FY26.
items.quote: As on 31st December 2025, our net cash position stood at INR132 crores. Our adjusted ROCE for 9 months FY '26 is 13.1% and return on operating capital employed for 9 months FY '26 stands at 18.8%.

items.statement: Current debt minimal: INR148 crores loan from parent (to be repaid); net debt negative (net cash INR132 crores); plan to raise fresh debt for construction capex starting next fiscal year.

The only amount we have is about INR148 crores, which is a loan from the parent company, which we plan to repay as well. And our net debt is, in fact, negative because we have a cash surplus at the moment about INR132 crores of net cash.

But we've already have the banks, everything sorted out for our deadline.

items.statement: No asset recycling planned; will fund expansion via fresh debt, not asset sales.
items.quote: No, we plan to go for fresh debt because we've repaid all the debt through the IPO proceeds. So, it will all be fresh. No, and we are not planning to sell any of our existing portfolio assets.

items.quote: So, yes, we're discussing with Marriott already and we're just seeing what is the best outcome for the hotel and just trying to see which is the best outcome for the overall property in the long term. So, it's still under negotiation and we're still discussing to see what to do. Either we renew with the current one, or we up brand it.

items.quote: In buses, I think we have seen a strong momentum now with multiple tender wins, accounting to total of almost 6,000 units, which we will now deliver over period of next 10 to 12 months.

items.quote: As the consumption continues to be at a higher level post GST 2.0 leading to expansion in some of the end-use sectors and infrastructure activity by government, we are looking at improved levels of demand in Q4 as well across all the segments.

items.quote: I think our guidance, we continue to remain within the guidance that we had given. And we have been pretty disciplined in terms of our CapEx spend and without compromising on the need for new tech.

items.quote: In terms of bus bodybuilding capacity, yes, I did mention about increasing the capacity by debottlenecking, so it is roughly around 15% increase that we have done in anticipation of higher demand in Q4 and Q1.

items.quote: Strong FCF that you see in this quarter is a clear result of strong operating profit, efficient working capital management, and disciplined spending.

items.quote: In this quarter, the replacement demand for trucks is most likely gaining momentum post GST 2.0 because it has prompted the fleet operators to initiate vehicle replacement that were previously delayed.

items.statement: Competitive intensity exists in every segment, varying by segment but no segment with very low intensity
items.quote: I think i n every segment, we'll see competitive intensity, yes the intensity may vary a bit from segment to segment, but I can't see of any segment which will have very low intensity or competitive intensity

items.quote: Recently signed EU FTA, we could benefit to this particular lever, not only on the products, but it will also see good benefit on the components or aggregate that we are sourcing from Europe.
