So on Slide #38 of the IR deck -- see, again, I'm sure like you would appreciate, our IR decks are very transparent and very full of information. So on 38 page number, you will see the mothballing of these 2 capacities, Jamul and Sindri very old mills.

items.statement: Power consumption reduction of 10 units/ton targeted with high visibility via existing plant debottlenecking, utilization improvement, and new efficient clinker lines.
items.quote: Both, Ashish. I mentioned to you in terms of the stability, reliability and therefore, the utilization factor of the existing plant, and that will be a key for every kind of KPIs. And on top of it, the blend of the new assets. So it will be a benefit of both coming together. On an overall basis, the reduction of 10 units.

items.statement: Blended cement rollout accelerating in South (Penna started) and premium cement launched in Bombay (OPC market) with strong response; blended share to improve rapidly.
items.quote: I'm also happy to share with you that in Bombay, the blended cement in form of premium cement. Otherwise, Bombay is more of an OPC market. But Bombay also, for example, we have launched our premium cement and it has got a huge response for the tube.

items.statement: Railways bulk movement discount policy and CONCOR tie-up enabling BCT/container model, reducing capex vs grinding units; fly ash advantage from group.
items.quote: Good thing is railways have also come out with the bulk movement discount policies, our tie-up with CONCOR. So in fact, my capex actually will be a tad lower because now instead of GU, you can also very well plan BCT and the advantage of fly ash which the group has.

items.statement: Sanghi turnaround progressing: colony revamp, infrastructure upgrade, talent attraction improving after initial remote location challenges; site visit planned for February.
items.quote: Earlier, you would see that the colony was also, the plant life was very badly managed. But it takes time for us to also revamp the whole quality of life over there, the infrastructure, the facilities. And therefore, I'm very eager to take you all now to

items.statement: Sanghi ramp-up delayed by extreme weather (floods, storms), low-voltage transmission line (being upgraded for 20-25 MW green power), and dredging needs; now resolved with December clinker at 80% utilization.
items.quote: So last year, for example, you have seen flooding and all and huge storms. Some of the plants were affected and Sanghi was also -- some equipments were damaged. Second is in terms of some improvements, for example, the transmission line was a little low - voltage transmission line and which is -- if you would just track it, therefore, already now the transmission line from government is getting re

items.statement: Organic assets delivered INR1,045/ton EBITDA in Q3; blended average INR715/ton; North/West stronger, South modest, Center/East subdued; competition aggressive in Center.
items.quote: Well, generally, it's like you all know the answer. It's like South will generally be modest compared to the other markets. West, for example, is generally better. And in this case, markets like Bombay are always far, far better. In terms of East was also subdued, although it picked up in the last month of the December.

items.statement: Capex model shifting from pure grinding units to blend of BCTs, container terminals, and grinding units leveraging railway discounts, CONCOR tie-up, and group fly ash; detailed footprint updates quarterly.
items.quote: I will rather put a blend of BCTs and grindings and container movement and so on and so forth. Therefore -- the models are reemerging. And therefore, I will keep updating you all in terms of the footprints with every passing quarter.

items.statement: Coal sales gross-up (INR315 crore in Q3 at ACC level) is accounting reclassification only; no impact on consolidated EBITDA, realizations, or NSP; eliminated at consolidation.
items.quote: So Rohit will answer you on this. Rohit? Rohit Soni: No, no. So that's not the reason. It's just a gross up and gross down from accounting perspective. So all the numbers, what we report, they don't consider that. We report it from the management this thing. That is just a gross up, gross down. Nothing to do with any of the numbers what we report.

items.statement: Penna utilization ~52-55% in December (clinker); Tandur kiln restarting in 1-2 weeks; Krishnapatnam grinding expansion (2 to 4 mtpa) ramping up, will sharply lift utilization.
items.quote: Penna ballpark is -- for the month of December is ballpark 52% to 55%. And as I mentioned, like this asset of Tandur of Penna was down, but now it is going to be up and running in the next week or 10 days. And therefore, like you will see a good level of utilization, sharp improvement in Penna assets.

items.statement: Outsourcing/contracting initiative progressing well with good momentum; positive updates expected soon.
items.quote: Of course, yes, whatever we are discussing with you on every investor call, we are moving our journey on that. So in terms of the outsourcing also, I must compliment my team and the efforts which has been coming out that we are in a good momentum on that, and you will hear positive things on that part as well.

items.statement: Dividend payout ratio increased to 20-25% for FY26 from 17-18% previously
items.quote: Between last year and this year, we were at about 17%-18%. We are now little about 20%, probably closer to 25% for this year.

items.statement: Deploying cash for fleet modernization by selling older vessels and buying modern ones, not capacity expansion
items.quote: We have been modernizing our fleet while we have not done capacity expansion. We have been selling our older vessels and buying some more modern vessels.

items.statement: No plans to invest in LNG fleet due to high capital requirement and sub-optimal returns vs tanker/bulker/LPG
items.quote: So, at the moment at least we are not going to even consider that business.

items.statement: Crude tanker markets strong due to OPEC+ supply and South America production; product tankers recovered; dry bulk Capesize strong
items.quote: Crude tanker markets were strong. Product tanker markets also recovered in the quarter from where they were the previous couple of quarters.

items.statement: Offshore vessel utilization at 65-66% marketed utilization, near historical peak of 70-72%
items.quote: The utilization of the ships currently are at about 65%-66%. It is called marketed utilization. Now, while that, in an absolute terms, may seem a bit low, for our industry, that is actually quite good.

items.statement: Jack-up rig utilization at 84-85%, near historical peak of 90%; Saudi Aramco recalling 9 rigs in 2026
items.quote: Again, on the market and without using the cold layup jack-up rigs, right? The utilization is about 85%, 84%, something like that, right? And the peak that we have seen historically is about 90%.

items.statement: Current yield on ships at today's freight rates ~10% return on $1 invested; not investing due to asset price risk
items.quote: So, if we buy a ship today and earn today's earning at today's freight rates, you would probably make a 10% return on that $1 invested.

items.statement: Offshore charter rates have held up at elevated levels for last 1-1.5 years with no dip
items.quote: All I can tell you is that over the last calendar year, about a year, year-and-a-half at least, since the rates have gone up a lot, they have broadly held up at these levels, and we have seen no dip.

items.statement: LR2 tankers switching from product to crude trade has tightened LR2 market and pushed up rates
items.quote: We have already seen switching in LR2s, which are the most common vessels to move between crude and product trade. So, there has been a significant amount of switching from LR2s to Aframax trade, which has now pushed up the LR2 rates as well.

items.statement: Shipping segments: 15-20% capacity on time charter (products, dry bulk); crude and LPG 100% spot
items.quote: Typically on the shipping segments, we have about between 15% and 20% of the capacity on time charter. This is a normal situation in each of the sectors, which is products and dry bulk. In crude, we are 100% on spot currently. In LPG, we are 100%.

items.statement: Offshore: 80% coverage for FY27 at current rates; rigs mostly covered for FY28
items.quote: I can tell you in FY '27, we are largely fixed out at these rates, at about 80% is our coverage. And most of our rigs also are covered for FY '28.

items.statement: Net cash position >$500 million since mid-FY23; was net levered $360M in FY17-19
items.quote: And we have been net cash ever since middle of FY '23, and now we are more than $500 million+ net cash.

items.statement: 16th consecutive quarterly dividend declared; NAV grew 20%+ CAGR over 5 years
items.quote: And we have yet again declared a dividend. This is the 16th consecutive quarterly dividend that we are declaring.

items.statement: Prefers dividends over buybacks; buybacks tax-inefficient and only benefit tendering shareholders
items.quote: We have chosen dividends because this is something that goes to every shareholder. Buybacks go to the shareholders who tender in the buyback. We have also had this issue in the last few years, where the tax treatment of the buyback has made it somewhat unviable as an option.

items.statement: Sanctions on Russian oil tightened last 6 months; 500-750k bpd Russian crude unable to find destination, boosting Middle East/South America trade
items.quote: However, in the last six months, we have seen that maybe 500,000-750,000 barrels per day of Russian crude is not being able to find a destination, largely because India is not taking that much crude.

items.statement: Not investing at current high asset prices due to risk of 40-50% price drop from peak; prefers buying in downturns
items.quote: Now, the question is whether you risk that drop in the asset price in the hope of making this 10% in current yield. That is the approach. That is the thing that we have decided that we will not do.

items.statement: Time charter equivalent (TCE) earnings in line with international peers across segments
items.quote: The segment-wise TC compares well with the benchmarks. We are in line with what most of our peers in international markets are earning, because these are pretty transparent markets.

items.statement: Offshore vessel fleet aging industry-wide; scrapping minimal (8-12% of fleet over 10 years) creating overhang
items.quote: Scrapping has been very minimal for the last 10 years. So, we are talking of only about between 8% and 12% of the fleet getting scrapped in an entire 10-year period, which is very low.

items.statement: Greatdrill Chetna rig contract ends end-February; in discussions for next contract but nothing tied up yet
items.quote: And yes, the short-term contract of the Greatdrill Chetna is scheduled to get over in end February. We are in discussions with customers and potential customers on the next contract, but we have not yet tied up anything yet.

items.statement: No plans to enter container segment; tonnage provider rates strong but box rates weak, fleet supply strong ahead
items.quote: On the container space, so as of now, we have no plans.

items.statement: Gopalpur TAN and Dahej-II nitric acid projects expected to commission in Q1 FY27 and contribute to bottom line for at least half the year
items.quote: Both key projects are progressing well and expected for commissioning in Q1 FY '27. They will materially enhance competitiveness and margin resilience once operational.

items.statement: YTD capex of INR 1,495 crores directed towards Gopalpur TAN and Dahej-II nitric acid projects
items.quote: On the investment front, YTD capex is around INR 1,495 crores, largely directed towards Gopalpur TAN and Dahej -II nitric acid project.

items.statement: Gopalpur TAN project at 91% completion, Dahej acid project at 79% completion
items.quote: we are forging ahead with now almost 91% completion of our Gopalpur technical ammonium nitrate project and around 79% completion of our Dahej acid project.

items.statement: 70% of Dahej-II nitric acid capacity tied up with long-term contracts
items.quote: we have -- almost 70% of the capacity is already tied up with long-term CNA capacities tied up.

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA declined 27% YoY to INR 353 crores due to higher raw material costs, inadequate subsidy support, weaker IPA and nitric acid realizations
items.quote: Q3 EBITDA came in at INR 353 crores, a 27% Y -o-Y decline, driven by higher raw material costs, inadequate subsidy support in fertilizers, a weaker realization in IPA and nitric acid.

items.statement: Ammonia breakeven EBITDA currently around USD 430 FOBME; Equinor LNG contract from Q1 FY27 expected to reduce breakeven by double-digit percentage
items.quote: currently, with the revised GST reduction, which has happened in October towards the end of -- towards September end, our breakeven EBITDA is almost around USD430 FOBME, at this point of time at the current gas prices, which will come down substantially in the coming quarter once we have an Equinor contract getting in.

items.statement: TAN demand growth expected at 6% CAGR over next 5-6 years; 4 lakh tons of imports substitutable; 2.5 lakh tons additional demand every 2-3 years
items.quote: the demand growth in India, which is driven by mining and infrastructure largely for our products, for TAN products, is likely to be in the range of 6% compounded average growth rate over the course of next 5 to 6 years at least that we can see.

items.statement: Specialty fertilizers and Croptek contributed 33% of CNB revenue; B2C mining chemicals at 16% of segment revenue
items.quote: Specialty product contributed 33% of CNB revenue and B2C accounted for 16% of mining chemical revenue.

items.statement: Ammonia prices increased globally, raising raw material costs for TAN and nitric acid; IPA impacted by lower propylene prices globally but not available in India at those prices
items.quote: we also saw an increase in the ammonia prices globally. And that brought in the raw material price increase for both technical ammonium nitrate and nitric acid.

items.statement: Net debt at INR 4,021 crores with net debt/EBITDA at 2.27x, aligned with capex cycle
items.quote: Net debt stands at INR 4,021 crores with a net debt EBITDA of 2.27x, in line with our planned capex cycle.

items.statement: Discussions with ministries to review 50,000 tons/year ammonium nitrate export quota; quota may be removed eventually
items.quote: there is a very strong case for reviewing this 50,000 tons per year of export quota. And if things goes as per the plan based on the way the discussions have gone by, this quota may also get removed eventually.

items.statement: Market share in TAN business around 40%; supplying to almost every customer in the segment
items.quote: our market share is almost around 40% what we hold in this business. And any customer you talk about in TAN business, we are supplying to them.

items.statement: Signed agreement to acquire an India-based explosives manufacturer subject to due diligence; aimed at differentiated products and export bundling
items.quote: What we have done is we have signed an agreement to acquire. So that's the first clarification. And the acquisition will be subject to certain due diligence and conditions, precedents, as we say, being fulfilled, after which if everything goes to our satisfaction, then the transaction will go through.

items.statement: IPA prices corrected 22-23% this year due to softer acetone prices and imports; volumes held but pricing pressure to continue near term
items.quote: the price correction or rather the price reduction in this year is almost around 20 -- roughly around 22%, 23%. That's the kind of a price correction which IPA business has seen this year.

items.statement: Chinese ammonium nitrate exports increased from 7% to 30% market share, pressuring global spreads; domestic coal demand declined 1% YTD and 5% in Q3
items.quote: in January, the share of ammonium nitrate exports from China used to be 7%. It has increased to about 30% between January and December. And it is playing its role perfectly well in terms of decreasing the ammonium nitrate spreads also.

items.statement: Equinor 15-year LNG contract starting Q1 FY27 to support gas pricing and reduce ammonia breakeven substantially
items.quote: The year is also going to see a partial advantage emerging out of our 15-year long-term LNG contract with the Norwegian giant, which will be somewhere supporting the good, I would say, gas pricing.

items.statement: B2C mining chemicals grew 26% YoY in Q3; direct sales, regional warehousing, exports and TCO-based engagement model being strengthened
items.quote: The bright spot was our B2C segment, which continued its strong momentum with 26% Y-o-Y growth.

items.statement: DMSL demerger completed; subsidiary listing timing not yet decided; each business to draw own growth charter
items.quote: Demerger per se in a separate entity happened last year. We have created a separate entity, which is DMSL, and the business of mining chemical moved out of MAL and gone to DMSL.

items.statement: Nitric acid demand remains strong long-term; Q3 softness due to TAN demand impact from extended monsoon; excess imports a one-quarter phenomenon
items.quote: Normally, nitric acid, otherwise, is short in demand. We don't have the issue of demand side of nitric acid. If you see nitric acid remains stable for a long, long time, even it's just 1 quarter when we have seen softness in nitric acid prices.

items.statement: Export development focused on selective profitable markets; not targeting every country; export quota review may open opportunities
items.quote: We are not saying we'll export nitrate -- TAN to every place, every country, every market. No, that's not our goal. We are looking at focused market, and that's where the export development is going on.

items.statement: PICKBRITE steel pickling solution in early ramp-up stage with a couple of manufacturers; not yet meaningful contribution
items.quote: That is still in ramp -up stage, I call it. It's an early stage where we are working with a couple of manufacturers, and then, I'll say, take it up from -- you call it from a ramp-up stage to commercialization.

items.statement: Target 5,000 crore turnover for copper business by FY28-29, preponed from earlier FY30 target
items.quote: Earlier, we were looking at reaching a turnover of 5,000 crores by the year 2030, but seeing the demand, we have preponed it to 28 -29 now, so our target is to reach a 5,000-crore turnover by 28 -29, looking at the demand and the growth which is happening in the market.

items.statement: Expect at least 25% growth in FY27 across top line, EBITDA and PAT after 35-40% growth in FY26
items.quote: We are looking at at least a 25% growth. This year, we are looking at roughly 35-40%, and next year, at least 25% growth for the next year. In all the three.

items.statement: Target EBITDA margin of 5% and PAT margin inching toward 3%+ at 5,000 crore scale
items.quote: Yes, that's right. We are targeting 5% EBITDA margin, and P AT, hopefully, will keep going up, inching slowly up. Towards 3, and maybe slightly beyond

items.statement: Installed heat recovery systems on furnaces to reduce fuel cost and cycle time
items.quote: So, one thing that we've achieved is we've installed state-of-the-art heat recovery s ystems on our furnaces. So, what this does is it not only reduces the cycle time of all the furnaces, but it also reduces the amount of fuel required to make a certain batch

items.statement: Total installed capacity to reach 35,000 metric tons per annum by end of February 2026
items.quote: During this year, we are under further additional of capacity. By, end of February, we should reach 35,000 metric tons per annum as our total installed capacity, by February end.

items.statement: 60-acre Toopran plant can support 3-4x current capacity expansion without land constraint
items.quote: For any future expansion, which we can envisage, probably even up to 3 to 4 times the existing capacity, this land parcel will be enough, so we'll never have a shortage of land for any expansion and future.

items.statement: 9-month turnover of 1,643 crore exceeds full FY25 turnover of 1,625 crore, up 40% YoY
items.quote: The turnover, which, total turnover of, 1643 cores, which is higher than the entire turnover of the FY25. From 1625 for the whole year last year, we have already reached 1643, and we hope to have the best quarter ahead of us.

items.statement: EBITDA per kg doubled from Rs 19 to Rs 37 driven by value-added mix shift, not inventory gains
items.quote: So, most of this is, only, the value -added portion increase in, T he EBITDA margin has gone up, or margin per ton has gone up, mainly because of moving towards value -added products

items.statement: Added tin/silver-plated copper bus bars for AI data centers (export to US) and scaled solar interconnect wires
items.quote: The main highlights of these are the tin and silver -plated copper bus bars that go into AI data centers. We focus this to be a very big demand sector in the future, upcoming years, and we've already entered this market.

items.statement: Commodity margins 1-3%, value-added margins 5-10%; value-added defined as multi-process products with enamel, silver, tin
items.quote: So, in commodity, our margins can be anywhere between 1% to 3%, and in value-added, our margins can be anywhere between 5-10%, if that answers your question.

items.statement: Copper demand to boom 10-15 years driven by AI, EV, green energy requiring 3.5-4x more copper
items.quote: So, with this 3, we expect the, demand for copper to boom continuously for the next 10 to 15 years, and we as a company hope to be part of that story.

items.statement: No significant competition in silver/tin plated bus bars due to 20-year expertise, in-house systems, and China-avoidance by buyers
items.quote: So, in the short term, we don't see a lot of competition, and price-wise, I think India is very competitive with most of the… in comparison to other countries. And a lot of these countries that we are selling to, they don't prefer to take material from China, due to their policies, so we're looking at this to be a very big market for us, and not something that anyone else can easily enter.

items.statement: Working capital value will rise with copper prices though cycle days unchanged; short-term debt will increase
items.quote: So, you're absolutely right, as the copper prices go up, while it doesn't have any impact on other issues, the working capital will definitely go up. The number of days in the cycle doesn't change, but the value goes up because everyt hing is much more expensive

items.statement: Cost of debt ~8.5-9%; BBB+ upgrade saves ~25 bps; A- target could save 50-100 bps further
items.quote: Probably about, 8.5 to 9%.And going forward, I guess we may save about 0.25 or so. Post our, upgrade in rating from BBB to BBB+. And we are hoping that after the announceme nt of our yearly results , we'll try for A -, and that will give us a space of 0.5 to 1% in further reduction of… borrowing cost.

items.statement: Demerger into Tieramet Ltd (copper business) and Bhagyanagar India (land parcels + windmills, ~30 cr book value, zero debt); mirror shareholding
items.quote: So, the company will be moved into two parts. To keep it very simple, everything which is there in Bhag yanagar India today, in the consolidated balance sheet, will move to the, Tieramet, the new company. What will be left out in, the old company, that is Date-31st January, 2026 Time-12:00pm (IST) Bhagyanagar India, will be the land parcels and the windmills. And, the book value of the land passes

items.statement: Inventory hedged regularly; profits from operations not inventory gains; dynamic hedging being added
items.quote: Our, mostly our inventory is hedged on a regular basis, while we are doing some dynamic hedging in the… going forward, but most… the profits are mainly from operations and not from inventory gains.

items.statement: Pricing formula: copper (LME) plus fabrication; minimal long-term contracts; realization per ton to rise sharply in Q4 due to higher copper prices
items.quote: Just to clarify to you once again, our pricing is based on the current market value of the copper. We have very little long-term contracts, and every order is basically copper plus fabrication. So this… this quarter, the realization per ton will be much higher than the last quarter.

items.statement: Realization range Rs 1,280-1,350 per kg recently; commodity price driven
items.quote: So, on any given day, our realization… for example, yesterday's sale could be from 1280 to 1350 rupees.

items.statement: Company secretary role sees frequent resignations due to better offers from larger companies; overall employee turnover negligible
items.quote: A lot of people look at the tag of a 2,000 crore or a 1500 crore listed company. And, get better offers. I think that is the only thing which I can think of, because people are getting a lot of better prospects, having seen that somebody is a company secretary of a thousand crore -plus company.

items.statement: Aluminum substitution largely played out over 15 years; copper irreplaceable in high-reliability and space-constrained applications
items.quote: the major areas of replacement from copper to aluminum are already over. Having said that, I won't say that there are not many more areas where Copper can be replaced by aluminum. There are two areas which are critical where copper only can be used. One is the reliability of copper is much higher than aluminum, because aluminum tends to oxidize, and all the connections a nd other things tend to we

items.statement: Maintains consolidated sales growth guidance of 5.5%-6.5% for FY26
items.quote: During the last call, I said, growth in consolidated sales could be 5.5% to 6.5%. I maintain the same guidance.

items.statement: Revises consolidated Ceramics sales growth guidance down to 13%-14% from 16%-18% for FY26
items.quote: Consolidated Ceramics, we communicated a sales growth of 16% to 18% in the beginning of the year. We marginally bring this down from 13% to 14%.

items.statement: Maintains Abrasives sales growth guidance of 4%-5% for FY26
items.quote: Abrasives sales in our last call, we communicated to 4% to 5% for the year. I maintain the same.

items.statement: Maintains consolidated EMD sales growth guidance of 1%-2% for FY26
items.quote: Consolidated EMD, we gave a guidance of 1% to 2% sales growth. I maintain the same.

items.statement: Revises Ceramics PBIT margin guidance down to 21%-22% from 23.5%-23.7% for FY26
items.quote: In the Ceramic segment, we communicated PBIT margin of 23.5% to 23.7% on a full-year basis. We are likely to be at 21% to 22%.

items.statement: Maintains EMD PBIT margin guidance of 4.5%-5.5% for FY26
items.quote: EMD in the last call, we said 4.5% to 5.5% is the PBIT margin. We maintain the same guidance.

items.statement: Revises Abrasives PBIT margin guidance down to 4%-4.5% from 6%-6.5% for FY26
items.quote: Abrasives, last time, we said PBIT margin would be 6% to 6.5% on a full year basis. We now revised that to 4% to 4.5%.

items.statement: Revises consolidated PBIT margin guidance down to 7%-8% from 8.2%-8.5% for FY26
items.quote: We said the last time, the overall consolidated PBIT margin could be 8.2% to 8.5%. This could be 7% to 8%.

items.statement: Maintains full-year capex guidance of INR350 crores; spent INR248 crores in 9 months
items.quote: On the capex side, we said we will spend INR350 crores on a full year basis. We spent so far INR248 crores on a 9-month basis. We maintain the full-year guidance of INR350 crores of capex.

items.statement: Ceramics has strong order backlog; bagged highest-ever order in Q3 from SOFC/high-end customers
items.quote: In fact, we bagged the highest-ever order in the last quarter from them.

items.statement: Ceramics Q4 expected to be strong based on order backlog; project delays in Q3 caused guidance cut
items.quote: we feel that Ceramics on a full year basis, the projects are getting delayed, and that is what is causing us this challenge of Q3. But I think if you look at se quentially, they have done well on a standalone basis and we feel that Q4 will be a very strong quarter based on the order backlog that what we have

items.statement: Wear ceramics continues to face challenges; US project deferrals due to tariff uncertainty impacted last 2 quarters
items.quote: Wear ceramics continues to have this challenge. Largely, we feel that one, the ceramic business in U.S., particularly in the last 2 quarters, were sluggish. The end customers on many projects have delayed and deferred because of the uncertainty in the tariff.

items.statement: Standalone Ceramics full-year growth expected at 9%-11% despite 1.7% YTD growth
items.quote: We expect that overall growth rate, we know that the current rate is 1.7%, but we expect this to be in the range of about 9% to 11% at the full year level.

items.statement: Standalone PBIT margin increased sequentially from 12.2% in Q2 to 15% in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Standalone PBIT margin increased sequentially from 12.2% in Q2 FY26 to 15% in Q3 FY26.

items.statement: Consolidated EMD margins declined from 14% in 9M FY25 to 6% in 9M FY26
items.quote: At the 9 months level, margins have declined from 14% in FY25, to 6.0% in FY26.

items.statement: Foskor realisation fell 13% due to Chinese competition price pressure; rand appreciated 6%
items.quote: Sales volume went up substantially, 28% growth. At the same time, the realis ation fell by 13% because of the price pressure from Chinese competition

items.statement: EU FTA expected to lower tariffs by 4%-5% vs MFN rates, improving competitiveness
items.quote: So hence, definitely compared to that rate, MFN FTA rate will be definitely lower, at least to the extent of about 4% to 5% lower which definitely increases our competitiveness.

items.statement: China removed export rebate on abrasives from 9% to 0% effective April, seen as positive for domestic market share
items.quote: China has recently removed the export rebate on abrasives products including grinding wheels from 9% to 0%. This will be in effect from April onwards.

items.statement: Consolidated debt increased to INR290 crores in Q3 FY26 from INR210 crores in Q2 FY26; debt-equity ratio 0.07
items.quote: The total consolidated debt was about INR290 crores in Q3 FY26, compared to INR210 crores in Q2 FY26 and, INR108 crores in the same period last year. The debt-equity ratio is 0.07 at the consolidated level.

items.statement: Foskor Zirconia: tapering ZC business, focusing on Z450; will take firm call in 1-2 quarters if no improvement
items.quote: So, we have tapered down the ZC business. we are only focusing on Z450. So, the Q4 will have only Z450 operation, and we want to see how that performance is. If it is going to improve, that is fine. If not, we need to take a firm call.

items.statement: Awuko: will take firm call in a year's time; incurred ~EUR30 million losses over 4 years
items.quote: And Awuko, we think that we should take a firm call in a year's time.

items.statement: Capacities being created; investment progress in line with plan; technology tie-ups and people additions progressing
items.quote: Capacities are being created and our investment progress is pretty much in line. That's why we are also maintaining the guidance of INR350 crores. All the programs in terms of technology tie -ups, working with partners in two b road areas are all progressing well

items.statement: Standalone Electrominerals export mix improving, close to 30% long-term target
items.quote: I think our aim is to have a 30% mix, that is 30% export mix on a long-term basis, but the current trend shows that even now, we are very close to that.

items.statement: Consolidated Ceramics export contribution 50%-55% blended; industrial ceramics up to 75%
items.quote: If you see a blended rate, it could be in the range of around 50% to 55%. and industrial ceramics, it could be as high as 75% because it's a combination of two businesses.

items.statement: Rhodius full-year sales revised down to ~EUR60 million from EUR62.6 million; full-year loss expected EUR4.5 million after EUR2.8 million PPA write-off

items.statement: Consolidated net cash position of $3.2 billion

items.quote: Physicians are reporting early signs of hair regrowth in patients, which mirrors our clinical data, including in some patients who have previously failed other JAK inhibitors.
