items.statement: US tariff uncertainty: 50% currently, may reduce to 25%; EU trade deal benefits not before early 2027
items.quote: They are indicating in every newspaper day before yesterday also, it can reduce any time.

items.statement: Domestic turnaround may take 1-2 quarters to rectify 30 years of mismanagement
items.quote: it might take one to two quarters minimum to get it rectified. Yes, initially since last one month, we have already started controlling everything, reducing the manpower, u nwanted manpower

items.statement: Q3 FY26: Laminate sheets sold 32.67 lakh (domestic 12.31 lakh, export 21.35 lakh)
items.quote: Domestic is 12.31% and export is 21.35%, so total is 32.67% for Q3.

items.statement: Further expansion plans (2-3 new plants) under study; announcement expected in 2-3 months
items.quote: There are two or three multiple plants which we have already studied and discussed. So, hopefully, we might be able to give some news in the next two, three months about our expansion plans.

items.statement: Management expects full-year conductor volume growth of 8-9% and cable revenue growth of 20%+ for FY26
items.quote: overall if you see last year, Q3, Q4 was heavy and we expect that full year should be around the YTD range that we have been getting till now on the volume growth front. That's what we expect as of now to end the year

items.statement: Management maintains conductor EBITDA per ton guidance at INR30,000+ despite strong Q3 performance
items.quote: We'll continue with the same guidance that we have been giving in the past. Of course we have been saying the tailwinds are always not so easy to predict given the various macro challenges and domestic competition that comes.

items.statement: Management expects cable EBITDA margin around 9.5-10% for FY26 despite U.S. margin pressure
items.quote: We've been guiding about 9.5%, 10% margin and we expect it should be around this level. YTD already we are at 10%. We expect that our margin profile should be in similar range more or less.

items.statement: Conductor order book at INR7,396 crores with 32% export share; 9-month new orders at INR8,052 crores
items.quote: Our order book is reasonably strong at INR7,396 crores, of which exports is contributing approximately 32%. The total new orders received in the 9-month period is at about INR8,052 crores.

items.statement: Domestic revenue grew 30% YoY in Q3 and 26.9% in 9M; export revenue down 11.2% in Q3 due to U.S. tariffs
items.quote: If you look at the domestic revenues, it grew by 30% in Q3 FY '26 versus the previous year and 26.9% if you look at it in the 9-month period. Exports for the quarter were down 11.2%.

items.statement: Conductor domestic revenue up 37% YoY in Q3; export revenue down 11%; premium product mix at 44.2% vs 37.4% prior year
items.quote: grew by 37% versus Q3 of FY '25. The export revenue for the Conductor division de-grew by about 11%. The export mix is about 18% compared to 25% in the previous year. The premium product mix remains healthy at 44.2% and this has grown compared to 37.4% in the previous period

items.statement: Cable domestic revenue up 34.6% YoY in Q3; export revenue down 44.3% with U.S. revenue down 65%
items.quote: The domestic business had a strong performance and it grew by 34.6%. Overall, exports de-grew by 44.3%, which was basically because the U.S. revenues were down 65% in the third quarter over the previous year.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA up 20.4% YoY to INR483 crores at 8.8% margin; exceptional loss of INR25 crores for gratuity provision
items.quote: If you look at EBITDA, the EBITDA is up 20.4% year-on-year to INR483 crores. The EBITDA margin stands at 8.8%. Due to the enactment of this new labour code, we have had to recognize a provision towards past service cost of gratuity and we had to increase the provision amounting to approximately INR25 crores.

items.statement: Conductor EBITDA post forex per metric ton at INR44,195 in Q3 vs INR29,593 prior year; 9M at INR42,311 vs INR34,949
items.quote: If you look at EBITDA post open forex, it has grown to INR251 crores for the Conductor division. The EBITDA post forex per metric ton stands at INR44,195 as opposed to INR29,593 per metric ton in the same period previous year.

items.statement: Oil division EBITDA per KL at INR5,331 vs INR6,364 prior year; impacted by forex depreciation
items.quote: EBITDA per KL came in at INR5,331 per KL against INR6,364 a year ago. Foreign exchange depreciation did affect the profitability for this quarter.

items.statement: Cable EBITDA post forex at 8.7% margin (INR132 crores) in Q3; 9M EBITDA margin at 10% (INR431 crores)
items.quote: The EBITDA post forex came in at 8.7% to reach INR132 crores. And the EBITDA margin is at 9.7% due to a favourable product mix as well as there were some gains on the cable side with respect to foreign exchange.

items.statement: Completed INR500+ crores capex out of INR1,400 crores plan; remaining to be spent in Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27, facilities operational by mid-FY27
items.quote: We've already completed about INR500-plus crores worth of capex as of Q3 out of a total plan of about INR1,400 crores. We expect that in Q4 and Q1 of FY '27, a large portion of that remaining capex will actually take place. And by September, I mean by the mid of FY '27, we'll pretty much have all the facilities up and running.

items.statement: Government allowing bushing imports to resolve transformer delivery delays; domestic bushing capacity expanding in 6 months
items.quote: The government is actually making a concession for import of bushings, which will kick in very shortly within the next week or so. In the meantime, the bushings capacity in India is also getting increased. Several new plants and brownfield expansions in place. So in about 6 months' time, we expect that the domestic side will also increase.

items.statement: Full pass-through of copper/aluminium price increases and exchange rate impact; B2B orders hedged back-to-back above 25 metric tons
items.quote: So we've actually increased prices to cover the delta in copper. So the entire copper pricing has been passed through. All the B2B orders that we take, we'll take it only on a back-to-back basis. So any order which is 25 metric tons or higher of copper that's involved or aluminium, we would take a specific hedge.

items.statement: Cable U.S. prices reduced to maintain market access under 54% tariff; aluminium products still viable with price adjustment, copper products face significant tariff disadvantage
items.quote: So whatever order inflow we have got in Q3, which is approximately INR500 crores for the cable business, where we have had to adjust the prices down to some extent to keep the order flow going. So mind you, there's also been some increase that has happened across the board because other countries also have had some increase in tariffs.

items.statement: U.S. Section 232 tariffs at 54% covering most cable/conductor products; EU FTA signed but fine print and BTN classifications awaited
items.quote: The current tariff situation remains the same at 54%. So whatever order inflow we have got in Q3, which is approximately INR500 crores for the cable business, where we have had to adjust the prices down to some extent to keep the order flow going.

items.statement: New Cable Solutions CEO Chandrashekhar Shrotri joined Dec 4; 30 years at Siemens leading low voltage business across 27-28 countries
items.quote: Mr. Chandrashekhar Shrotri has joined the Cable business. He joined on the 4th of December so he's been in the role for almost a little over 1.5 months. Previous to this, he worked for Siemens for 30 years and was in charge of the low voltage business across 27 or 28 different countries.

items.statement: Steady-state EBITDA margin expected at 15% going forward after investments
items.quote: On a steady-state basis, and taking into account some accelerated investments we will be making going forward, EBITDA margin will be about 15%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 212 bps QoQ to 18.2% in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Consequently, EBITDA margin expanded 212 basis points quarter-on-quarter from 16% in Q2 to 18.2% in Q3.

items.statement: Steady-state EBITDA margin estimated at 16.5% excluding forex and one-offs
items.quote: If I were to remove those, my steady state EBITDA margin from 18.2% is down to 16.5%.

items.statement: TCV for Q3 FY26 stands at $202 million, up 89% QoQ with 46% net new
items.quote: As a result, our TCV for the third quarter stands at $202 million, which is up 89% quarter-on-quarter. Out of the $202 million, nearly half of it is new engagements.

items.statement: Q4 signings expected to be better than Q3 signings
items.quote: What we are confident of, Priyank, is our Q4 signings will be better than Q3 signings.

items.statement: No material change in demand environment; discretionary spending remains constrained
items.quote: As all of you know, from our perspective we have not seen any material change in the demand environment, and we have discussed this even in the past. Customers continue to focus on optimizing their spends, and discretionary spending therefore remains constrained.

items.statement: Manufacturing and Life Sciences to face headwinds in Q4; turnaround expected Q1/Q2 FY27
items.quote: Sustainably, I think Manufacturing will continue to face headwind, at least for one more quarter. And I expect the Manufacturing business to turn around sometime Q1 or Q2 onwards for the next financial year.

items.statement: BFSI and Energy & Utilities expected to be steady in Q4 and grow in FY27
items.quote: We strongly believe that E&U and Financial Services will continue the growth momentum. As you know, this was a furlough quarter, so optically you are seeing a degrowth in Financial Services. But I believe Financial Services will be steady in 4Q, and next year definitely we will see growth. Similar goes for E&U.

items.statement: Renewals coming at lower margins due to pricing pressure; steady-state margin at 15%
items.quote: What we can say is that all the bad news is behind us. I don't think we will lose any existing business, but they will get renewed at a lower margin because we see pricing pressures, which is why Chandru talked about a steady-state margin of about 15%.

items.statement: Shift to fixed-price and offshore work improving revenue quality and margins
items.quote: We have also benefited from favorable shifts in our revenue mix, with a rise in fixed price business and offshore work.

items.statement: Client count rationalized to focus on profitable accounts; million-plus clients grew from 78 to 85
items.quote: However, if you look at our million-plus clients, that has expanded from 78 to 85, which also should tell you that our focus on growing clients which have the potential is very, very sharp.

items.statement: DSO improved to 54 days; highest quarterly collection this fiscal year
items.quote: As a result, our DSO has improved quarter-on-quarter and now stands at 54 days, which you would agree is amongst the best in our industry.

items.statement: Cash and cash equivalents increased to Rs. 2,491 crore, up 6% QoQ and 21% YoY
items.quote: Cash and cash equivalents at the end of Q3 increased to R s. 2,491 crore, up 6% quarter -on- quarter and 21% year -on

items.statement: Wage hike decided for next financial year between Q1 and Q2; promotions done this quarter
items.quote: We have already taken a decision that we will do a wage hike next financial year. We are doing promotions this year, this quarter, and we will affect a wage hike between Q1 and Q2, depending upon what level of employees there are in the organization.

items.statement: Komal hired to drive Americas business; will speak on strategy after settling in
items.quote: Manish, as you know, the Americas contribute almost about 85% of our business and Komal has been hired to drive our Americas business. Manish, he's just joined the company. He's just four months in the company. He is meeting clients, meeting people. He is getting the right leadership hired. So, he is doing a lot of good things. And we are very pleased and we are privileged to welcome Komal to the

items.statement: Investments planned in people, leadership, training and capabilities for future growth
items.quote: Point number two, the investment that we are talking about for the most part will be in people and in capabilities. So, these are specific capabilities that we will continue to acquire as we go forward based on where we see our business going and where we see our business coming from some of our existing and new customers. And the investments will be made in people, leadership, and in training of

items.statement: One-time provision of $4.6 million taken for Labor Code changes on gratuity and leave encashment
items.quote: Our EBIT performance for the quarter under review reflects the impact of a one-time provision that we have taken to conform to the changes in the Labor Code with regard to gratuity and leave encashment. That provision, which we have called out as an exceptional item, amounts to $4.6 million or Rs. 40.7 crore.

items.statement: Revenue grew 0.3% QoQ in constant currency to $150.8 million in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Our revenue for the quarter grew 0.3% in constant currency and 0.1% in dollar terms to $150.8 million.

items.statement: Healthcare vertical faces pricing pressure in Q4 and Q1 due to tariff uncertainties
items.quote: What will happen, though, is we will see immense pricing pressure in the healthcare business because of the uncertainties that my clients face, thanks to the tariff situation. So, I see that pressure continuing in 4Q and I see that pressure partly continuing in 1Q.

items.statement: Subcontractor ratio at 8%; endeavor to reduce further
items.quote: Yes, I think what you are talking about is subcontracting. I didn't quite hear the question properly, but if subcontracting is the question, yes, our endeavor is to continue to reduce subcontractors. As a business today, about 8%, right Chandru? 8% of our population is subcontractors.

items.statement: Pass-through revenue to be zero going forward except one-off infrastructure deals
items.quote: We want to deliver more outcome -based work for our clients . And to deliver that outcome we may work with technologies, or we may work with tech stacks, etc., but we will have zero pass- through revenues going forward, outside of a one -off infrastructure deal, if it necessitates us to Classification: Public do something

items.statement: Q4 has three fewer working days vs Q3; impact mitigated by shift to outcome-based deals
items.quote: There are, I think, three working days lower in Q4 versus Q3, Manik. Yes, that will have an impact. But as we move more towards outcomes-based deals, and that is exactly why we are doubling our focus on fixed price, outcome-based deals where the working days should not necessarily have a direct impact.

items.statement: No new one-time provisions expected in Q4 unless accounting changes arise
items.quote: So, on that again, I am not aware of any one-timers in the next quarter unless there is something new that comes up based on any accounting practice changes or accounting requirement changes. But right now, I am not aware of any new one-timers, Vibhor.

items.statement: Board seized of capital allocation including buyback; will decide at appropriate time
items.quote: This is a topic that is for the Board of Directors to look at. And I can assure you that this is a topic that the Board is fully seized of, and we will continue to look for opportunistic capabilities, investments, and anything that fits into our strategies as we go forward, Manish. And capital allocation, which is the point that you are making, is certainly part of the entire exercise for us to en

items.statement: ROW region delivering strong growth and improved margin profile
items.quote: Also, Manish, you must have seen and Chandru also commented on, all our investment in the ROW region is playing out. ROW region has delivered amazing growth for us this quarter. And I think, they will continue to show great growth even next year. And the margin profile has also significantly improved because of the revenue uptick.

items.statement: Furloughs in Q3 were in line with last year at 0.5-1% impact
items.quote: Now, it is hard for me to predict Q4 from a revenue standpoint, but our focus will be on generating pipeline and signings. What we are confident of is we will deliver better signings in Q3 and Q4. Now, how much out of that will be playing out on the revenue? We will have to wait and watch. But like I have always said, our problem, or rather, the focus of the management team has to be on revenue gr

items.statement: Management guided for high single-digit revenue growth in FY27, excluding M&A.
items.quote: we are looking at high single -digit growth. And then, of course, occasionally, we do look at M&A. So I'm not factoring M&A into this, but the high single digit is something that would be a decent number to look at.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 18.9% in Q3 FY26, up 604 bps YoY and 75 bps QoQ.
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at 18.9%, reflecting an improvement of 604 basis points on a year-on-year basis and an improvement of 75 basis points on a quarter -on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Management expects to sustain and improve EBITDA margins going forward.
items.quote: Yes, we will be sustaining the EBITDA margins. We continue to look at in terms of how we can keep our cost in control and keep growing. That's basically the key thing that we are looking at. So EBITDA will maintain the EBITDA margin and keep improving.

items.statement: Digital Experiences segment will remain soft in Q4 FY26 due to client transition to captives, with upswing expected from Q1 FY27.
items.quote: Quarter 4 of this year, we will expect the full impact of that transition. From quarter 1 of next year, we'll see an upswing because we signed several new logos and they are much healthier margins as well.

items.statement: Digital Technologies and Digital Operations segments showing robust growth and healthy pipeline.
items.quote: On digital operations and digital technologies, as you see, the numbers in digital technologies have been quite robust, and I see that contin uing for the next few quarters. I don't see a major challenge there. We have a healthy pipeline.

items.statement: Pipeline seeing slight uptick; deal velocity still slow but mood improving.
items.quote: right now, it's still fairly strong. In fact, we are seeing a little uptick on the pipeline. So that's good. I think the current uncertainties in the U.S. have become a state of normal in a way. Everybody knows, and everybody remains uncertain. So they've to take it in this ride. Generally, the mood is improving. The velocity is still slow, but we see a slight upward trend.

items.statement: Annual spend on transformation/AI technologies maintained at Rs. 40-50 crores, expensed not capitalized.
items.value: Rs. 40 crores to Rs. 50 crores a year
items.quote: our spend on these transformation technologies is roughly Rs. 40 crores to Rs. 50 crores a year. Earlier, it was more in the product space where we are pivoting away from product investments and more into the AI investment. So basically, it's all in the investment space, right? So a little more on investment. So we've reallocated our plans internally. So that investment continues.

items.statement: AI/tech investment of Rs. 40-50 crores per year to be maintained for some time, reviewed quarterly.
items.quote: Right now, we will maintain that between Rs. 40 crores and Rs. 50 crores because this whole area of technology is changing so fast, and we need to keep abreast with that area. So we will maintain it for some time. But we keep reviewing every quarter just to see where we're going. So as of now, it's there.

items.statement: Rolling out Google Gemini Enterprise across organization; 200 employees certified in past month as Phase 1.
items.quote: I'm excited that we are rolling out Google Gemini Enterprise across the organization, empowering our teams to build intelligent agents, improve productivity and drive innovation at scale. In partnership with Google, we have certified 200 employees on Gemini Enterprise in the past 1 month as Phase 1 of this exercise.

items.statement: Built industry-specific AI solutions for insurance, banking, logistics enabling autonomous workflow orchestration.
items.quote: Additionally, we have built industry-specific AI solutions for insurance, banking and logistics, enablin g autonomous workflow orchestration, smarter decision -making and enterprise -wide productivity at scale.

items.statement: Top 5, 10, 20 clients contribute 29%, 42%, 55% of revenue respectively; concentration healthy.
items.quote: Our client concentration remains very healthy with top 5, 10 and 20 clients contributing to 29%, 42% and 55%, respectively.

items.statement: Dextara cross-sell into Datamatics customer base yielding strong pipeline and larger deal sizes.
items.quote: Yes. Dextara is doing very well, and we've been able to very successfully cross -sell into the Datamatics customer base. We've got a very strong pipeline right now , and not only a strong pipeline, but also much larger deals compared to what Dextara had.

items.statement: Billed DSO at 55 days as of December 2025.
items.quote: Our billed DSO was at 55 days as of December 2025.

items.statement: Net cash and investments net of debt stood at INR 540.2 crores as of December 2025.
items.quote: As of December 2025, our net cash and investment net of debt stood at INR540.2 crores.

items.statement: One-time Rs. 40.3 crores gratuity/leave encashment liability hit from new labour codes in Q3 FY26; minimal ongoing impact expected.
items.quote: Changes in the new labour codes resulted in a one-time increase of Rs. 40.3 crores in gratuity and leave encashment liability. This one-time increase was shown as an impact on labour codes under the exceptional item.

items.statement: Labour code impact is one-time legacy hit; from next quarter only marginal routine increase of ~0.5% expected.
items.quote: It is just for this quarter i n the sense that there is a backlog because of the one-time hit with a retrospective effect. Therefore, this quarter has taken a big hit. From the next quarter onwards, it has become a routine marginal increase in gratuity. So we expect something in the range of maybe 0.5.

items.statement: Headcount not significantly increased; focusing on AI augmentation and productivity; next wage hike cycle in April-May next financial year.
items.quote: we've not added too much more. It's more about augmenting it with AI and improving productivity and not really increasing headcount now. In terms of the wage hike for this year, there's nothing happening this year. We already did a midyear increment cycle. The next cycle will probably be next financial year, April-May time frame.

items.statement: TNQ Tech integration successful; organic sequential growth of 4% for last two quarters excluding acquisition bump.
items.quote: Overall, we've had a sequential quarter-on-quarter growth of 4% as you see. So that, of course, includes TNQ as well as the rest of Datamatics. So , the growth is not coming from the acquisition. Of course, we got a bump up because of 19% because of the acquisitions for Q1, Q3. But if you see for the last 2 quarters, our sequential quarter growth has been 4% number for this quarter as well as the

items.statement: Revenue grew 19.9% YoY and 4.1% QoQ to Rs. 510.1 crores in Q3 FY26.
items.quote: Our total revenue for Q3 stood at Rs. 510.1 crores, giving us a revenue growth of 19.9% on a year-on-year basis and 4.1% on a quarter -on-quarter basis.

items.statement: EBITDA grew 76.4% YoY and 8.3% QoQ to Rs. 96.2 crores in Q3 FY26.
items.quote: Our EBITDA for Q3 stood at Rs. 96.2 crores, giving us an EBITDA growth of 76.4% on a year -on-year basis and 8.3% on a quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: US remains largest geography at 52% of revenue, followed by UK/Europe 22%, India 17%, ROW 9%.
items.quote: In terms of geographical footprint, the U.S. remains our largest geography with 52% of our business coming from here, followed by the U.K. and Europe at 22%, India at 17% and ROW at 9%.

items.statement: US market still has political overhang creating uncertainty; mood improving but velocity slow.
items.quote: They are still a little lukewarm more because of, I think, political reasons and political pressures more than business. And I think that overhang of the politics is still there. It's beginning to look up right now. So , it is improving because I think everyone is now very comfortable with the uncertainty. Everybody is in the same board, and they've been in this board for quite a while. So I think

items.statement: Guidance conservative due to political uncertainty and AI disruption greyness.
items.quote: We rather be conservative because there's still a lot of uncertainty , partly thanks to the political situation, partly thanks to the disruption that AI can have. And therefore, there's some degree of greyness there. Therefore, this is the current outlook.

items.statement: Not diversifying away from US/UK markets as they cover 80% of global outsourcing; focusing on wallet share expansion in existing large enterprise accounts.
items.quote: We've got good contracts in business. We're not looking at diversifying because between the U.S. and the U.K., it pretty much covers 80% of the global outsourcing market. So if you're looking out elsewhere, you're looking at as best traction. Now 20% is the rest of the world.

items.statement: AI adoption accelerating: customers moving from testing to production; Datamatics solutions receiving strong response in pilots/POCs.
items.quote: the customers are testing these things right now, they started going into production. Also, we see some customers going into mainstream production. And not only that, we find some customers very open to adopting technology as the main platform on which they want to operate.

items.statement: NTPC Group added 1,744 MW in Q3 FY26 including 800 MW Patratu thermal, 694 MW renewables, 250 MW THDC pumped storage
items.quote: NTPC Group added 1,744 MW in Q3 FY '26, comprising of 800 MW from Patratu thermal power station, 694 MW from renewables and 250 MW from THDC pumped storage project.

items.statement: Total capacity addition in FY26 reached 6,615 MW by January 2026, highest in 10 months
items.quote: Further, during January 2026, 468 MW renewables has been added, taking total capacity addition in FY '26 to 6,615 MW, the highest achieved in the 10 months period.

items.statement: NGEL targets 5 GW capacity addition in FY26, 8 GW in FY27 and 8 GW in FY28
items.quote: Our plan as of now for FY '27 is 8 GW. And we have already commenced work on the various plants which have to give the capacities next year. And likewise, for FY '28 also, we are targeting 8 GW of capacity addition.

items.statement: NGEL total contracted and awarded capacity increased 11.54% to 15,527 MW as of Dec 2025
items.quote: Total contracted and awarded capacity increased by 11.54% to 15,527 MW as on 31st December 2025.

items.statement: NGEL PPA tied capacity: 82% for FY26, 83% for FY27, 60% for FY28, 74% consolidated
items.quote: In FY '26, the capacities that we will now be adding will be -- is almost 82% PPA tied. FY '27, it moves to 83% FY '28 capacity as on date is 60% is tied up. And if you pick up total of all on a consolidated basis, we are 74% PPA tied.

items.statement: NGEL EBITDA margin improved to 87% in 9M FY26 with operating EBITDA up 25% to INR 1,701 crores
items.quote: Consolidated revenue from operations increased by 23% to INR1,946 crores in 9 months FY '26, while operating EBITDA grew by 25% to INR1,701 crores. EBITDA margin improved to 87%, underscoring the robust profitability of the renewable portfolio.

items.statement: Group capex INR 33,466 crores in 9M FY26 vs INR 30,779 crores in 9M FY25; standalone capex INR 19,439 crores vs INR 17,853 crores
items.value: INR 33,466 crores group, INR 19,439 crores standalone
items.quote: As regards capex in the 9 months FY '26, we have incurred a group capex of INR33,466 crores as compared to INR30,779 crores in the corresponding previous period. While on a standalone basis, NTPC has incurred a capex of INR19,439 crores in 9 months FY '26 as compared to INR17,853 crores in the corresponding previous year period.

items.statement: NGEL consolidated capex INR 11,653 crores in 9M FY26 vs INR 7,261 crores in 9M FY25
items.quote: Consolidated capex during 9 months FY '26 stood at INR11,653 crores compared to INR7,261 crores in the corresponding period last year.

items.statement: NTPC executed unsecured term loans of INR 5,000 crores (INR 3,500 crores SBI, INR 1,500 crores J&K Bank) at 15-year tenure linked to 3M T-bill and repo rate
items.quote: NTPC has executed unsecured term loan agreement aggregating to INR5,000 crores comprising of INR3,500 crores with State Bank of India and INR1,500 crores with Jammu & Kashmir Bank. These loans carry a door-to-door tenure of 15 years with interest rate linked to the 3 months treasury bill rate in the case of SBI and repo rate in case of J&K Bank.

items.statement: Weighted average interest rate on borrowings improved to 6.05% in 9M FY26 from 6.64% in 9M FY25
items.quote: The weighted average interest rate on borrowings during the 9M FY '26 stood at 6.05% compared to 6.64% in 9 MFY '25, reflecting the benefits of proactive refinancing and strategic restructuring of the company's loan portfolio.

items.statement: NGEL issued INR 1,500 crores unsecured NCDs at 7.01% via private placement, oversubscribed 8x
items.quote: In the quarter 3, NGEL successfully issued INR1,500 crores of unsecured nonconvertible debentures through private placement at a competitive interest rate of 7.01%. The issue was oversubscribed by around 8X, which shows the investors' confidence and favorable market perception.

items.statement: Outstanding receivable days improved to 26 days as of Dec 2025 from 34 days as of Dec 2024
items.quote: Outstanding receivable days improved to 26 days as on 31st December 2025 compared to 34 days as of 31st December 2024.

items.statement: NTPC coal stations PLF 70.69% in 9M FY26 vs 60.79% for rest of India
items.quote: The PLF of NTPC coal stations during 9 months FY '26 stood at 70.69% compared to 60.79% for the rest of India.

items.statement: NGEL capacity utilization factor 21.8% in 9M FY26 despite weather challenges
items.quote: Despite weather-related challenges, NGEL achieved a healthy capacity utilization factor of 21.8%.

items.statement: Coal stock at NTPC stations 15 MT sufficient for 18 days at 85% PLF; captive mines dispatch grew 4.34% YoY
items.quote: Coal stock at NTPC stations stood at 15 million tonnes, sufficient for about 18 days of generation at 85% PLF. Captive mines recorded dispatch growth of 4.34% year-on-year.

items.statement: Cumulative capex in coal mining INR 14,136 crores as of Dec 2025 under cost-plus framework
items.quote: The cumulative capital expenditure in coal mining stood at INR14,136 crores as on 31st December 2025, providing a long-term equity deployment under the cost-plus framework and supporting a stable return on equity.

items.statement: NTPC commissioned 3 MWh vanadium redox flow battery pilot (India's first MWh scale long-duration storage) and 3.7 MW solar at Chushul Ladakh for 24x7 carbon-free power to Army
items.quote: NTPC commissioned 3-MWh vanadium redox flow battery pilot project, which is India's first MWh scale long-duration energy storage system. We have also commissioned 3.7 MW solar project at Chushul, which is in Ladakh, which is designed for providing 24X7 carbon-free electricity to the Indian Army.

items.statement: Biomass co-firing 9.68 lakh MT in 9M FY26, more than double 4.29 lakh MT in 9M FY25
items.quote: In the first 9 months of FY '26, our station co-fired 9.68 lakh metric tonnes of biomass, more than double the 4.29 lakhs metric tonnes used in the same period last year, supporting sustainability objectives.

items.statement: CERC issued draft regulation allowing BESS at thermal stations enabling coal plants to support peak demand under cost-plus framework
items.quote: CERC has issued draft regulation allowing the installation of battery energy storage system at thermal generation stations. This is a positive development as it enables coal-based plants to remain online and support peak demand by supplying additional power through BESS during peak hours.

items.statement: SHANTI Nuclear Act enacted positioning nuclear as key baseload pillar for Viksit Bharat 2047 and Net Zero 2070
items.quote: The government has recently legislated Sustainable Harnessing and Advancement of Nuclear energy for Transforming India, SHANTI Nuclear Act, which positions nuclear power as a key pillar of India's long-term baseload energy strategy in support of Viksit Bharat @2047.

items.statement: Sinnar thermal plant (1,350 MW) shareholders agreement signed Jan 9 2026 after NCLT approval; transfer expected shortly with 1,600 acres for expansion
items.quote: The shareholders' agreement for Sinnar thermal power plant was signed on 9th January 2026, following approval of the resolution plan submitted by NTPC and MAHAGENCO by the National Company Law Tribunal. The transfer process is expected to be completed shortly. This would add 1,350 MW of capacity with approximately 1,600 acres of vacant land available for future expansion.

items.statement: Ayana Renewable Power acquisition added 2,624 MW to NGEL commercial capacity
items.quote: On a year-on-year basis, commercial capacity increased by 4,535 MW, including 2,624 MW from the acquisition of Ayana Renewable Power Private Limited.

items.statement: NTPC declared second interim dividend of INR 2.75 per equity share for FY26
items.quote: NTPC has declared a second interim dividend of INR2.75 per equity share for the financial year '25-26.

items.statement: Over 33 GW under construction: 16.5 GW coal, 1.9 GW hydro, 15 GW renewables
items.quote: We have over 33 GW of capacity under construction comprising 16.5 GW of coal-based capacity, about 1.9 GW of hydro and around 15 GW of renewable energy, and this is providing a solid foundation for near- to medium-term growth.

items.statement: Thermal capacity addition: 2,780 MW in FY26; 1,600 MW (Patratu U2&3) in FY27; 2,120 MW (TTPS Stage 3 1320 MW + Lara Stage 2 800 MW) in FY28
items.quote: Over the next 3-year period, 6,500 MW would be added, 2,780 during the current year; next year, it is 2 units of 800, 1,600; and the year next, it would be 2,120 MW, this is coming from TTPS Stage 3 1320 MW and Lara -Stage 2, this is 800 MW.

items.statement: NTPC plans 4 GW thermal awards in FY27: Lara-2 1,600 MW, Jhabua 800 MW, BRBCL 800 MW, Bhilai 800 MW; Talcher 800 MW extension in FY28
items.quote: Next year, we are looking at an award of 4 gigawatt that will be Lara-2 1,600 MW. Jhabua, BRBCL, Bhilai 800 MW each. The next financial year, we are planning Talcher thermal-based extension of another 800 MW at this instance.

items.statement: NGEL lost 420 MU to curtailment in 9M FY26; NREL lost 212 MU; NGEL curtailment now zero after Narela K3 line commissioning
items.quote: a total in this -- for the 9 months that have gone by, we lost around 420 million units on account of curtailment in NGEL alone. And in NREL also, we had lost around 212 million units of generation. So I think this answers you that curtailment has been a significant issue in the past that we had faced. But I'm happy to inform you that as regards NGEL, now the curtailment will be zero because the l

items.statement: Tehri pumped storage 3rd unit commissioned; 4th unit (250 MW) by end FY26; 160 MWh CO2 storage at Kudgi; 13 GW pumped storage studies; Tato-II 700 MW hydro started
items.quote: The third unit of Tehri pumped storage project has been commissioned and the final unit of 250 MW is scheduled to be commissioned before the end of the current financial year. Work is also in progress on the 160-MWh CO2-based energy storage system at Kudgi. Further preliminary studies are underway for pumped storage projects aggregating to around 13 GW allocated by state governments, which will be

items.statement: DISCOMs reported INR 2,700 crores profit in FY25 vs INR 25,553 crores loss in FY24 due to lower AT&C losses and better payment discipline
items.quote: A key positive indicator is that the distribution companies reported an overall profit of over INR2,700 crores in FY '25 compared to a loss of INR25,553 crores in FY '24, driven by lower AT&C losses and improved payment discipline.

items.statement: MSCI ESG rating upgraded to B from CCC after nearly 10 years due to sustained initiatives
items.quote: MSCI ESG ratings upgraded NTPC to a B rating from CCC, marking a significant improvement in its ESG assessment after nearly 10 years due to our sustained initiatives.

items.statement: Print advertising revenue grew 8% sequentially and was marginally down year-on-year due to festive shift; English ad revenue grew 16% sequentially.
items.quote: Ad revenue came in at INR 301 cr which is an 8% growth versus last quarter and a marginal decline versus the previous year, basically because of the festive shift; otherwise, it's been a healthy revenue number for the quarter.

items.statement: Print operating EBITDA margin expanded to 15% from 11% year-on-year driven by pricing growth, lower newsprint costs, and tight discretionary spends.
items.quote: Operating EBITDA for the Print business came in at INR 60 cr which is a 15% margin versus a 11% margin the previous year.

items.statement: Advertising pricing is seeing an uptick both year-on-year and sequentially.
items.quote: Yes, both yoy and sequentially, we are seeing an uptick.

items.statement: Newsprint costs remain below last year for the quarter and YTD; no major shift expected next quarter with reasonable cover till Q1 next year, thereafter potential gradual increase.
items.quote: Currently, we are still below last year for the quarter as well as on a YTD basis. And I think pretty much next quarter also, we are not expecting any major shift. And we have reasonable cover till the first quarter of next year. Thereafter, we might see some upward move.

items.statement: Digital operating revenue grew 30% year-on-year and 9% sequentially to INR 67 cr; losses narrowed with significant margin improvement.
items.quote: In Digital, there is significant growth on a yoy basis with operating revenue coming at INR 67 cr at a 30% growth. Sequentially also, there is a 9% growth. The segment is reporting losses at INR 23 cr but margins have significantly improved, both on a sequential and on an annual basis

items.statement: Radio revenue dropped to INR 34 cr year-on-year due to high base from prior year event; sequentially revenue grew 5% with operating EBITDA loss stable at INR 5 cr.
items.quote: Coming to Radio. It is seeing a big drop in revenue to INR 34 cr which is primarily driven by the high base effect from a big event that we had in the base last year. Sequentially, you can see there is positive 5% revenue movement; with operating EBITDA holding at about INR 5 cr loss.

items.statement: Exceptional item of INR 41.4 cr booked due to new labour code true-up of carrying liability; not indicative of future annual cost increase.
items.quote: There's an exceptional item of about INR 41.4 cr which has been booked, and there is a note given in the results also to that extent, which is an impact of the new labour code.

items.statement: Government has proposed regulatory framework requiring AI platforms to compensate original content providers, viewed positively.
items.quote: There's also a certain regulatory framework that's been proposed by the government, which suggests that partners using AI will have to remunerate the original content providers in some manner, which also seems to be on the positive side.

items.statement: AI is being used as a tool for editorial setup and seen as enabler for better offerings; focus on revenue opportunity over cost efficiency.
items.quote: While on the content side, it can be a tool for our editorial setup, which we are utilizing very strongly . From an impact perspective, we've seen there's a lot of AI being used and one view is that could also put a high importance on credibility and trustworthiness of the content, which puts us in a good position .

items.statement: Net cash remains robust at INR 945 cr, similar to last quarter.
items.quote: PAT before exceptional is at INR 17 cr with a margin of 3% and net cash remains robust at INR 945 cr - a similar number as was reported last quarter.

items.statement: Management does not provide specific guidance on projections.
items.quote: Before we start, just a quick reminder that we do not give or provide specific guidance on projections, and there is a disclaimer on any forward-looking statements.

items.statement: Conversations ongoing with AI platforms but not at liberty to share details.
items.quote: So, we have conversations, but currently not at a privy to really to share anything on this call.

items.statement: Targeting 8-10% sustainable growth over next 2-3 years
items.quote: Clear growth revival road map is there, targeting a return of 8% to 10% sustainable growth over the next two to three years.

items.statement: Full year EBITDA margin target remains double-digit despite current 11.8%
items.quote: The full year is going to show a double -digit margin. So the target for this year was to have a double-digit margin. We crossed 12%. Now we are at 11.8%. So there will be some decline for sure. How much it is difficult to say now. But of course, we'll be landing with double -digit margins.

items.statement: Q3 demand subdued with weak farmer activities, cautious channel behavior, weather issues and low pest incidence
items.quote: Q3 played out in challenging operating environment. The quarter was marked by weak farmer ac tivities, cautious channel behavior and weather issues, along with low incidence of

items.statement: Demand recovery gradually emerging with stabilizing raw material prices and inventory levels improving visibility
items.quote: Demand recovery is gradually emerging, while near -term demand remains selective, stabilizing raw material prices and inventory levels improve visibility for a gradual recovery.

items.statement: Gross margins moderated in Q3 due to higher B2B share and limited pricing power vs 36% gross profit base last year
items.quote: From a profitability standpoint, gross margins moderated due to: number one, higher B2B share; number two, pricing power remains limited in comparison with the higher base of last year, having 36% gross profit.

items.statement: Q4 gross margins expected to remain under pressure; maintaining 35% level in H2 will be difficult
items.quote: Given these conditions, gross margins are expected to remain under pressure and maintaining 35% level in H2 will be difficult.

items.statement: SPARCLE, Centran, Million showing strong traction; Torry, Torry Super, Xplode entering next phase of volume expansion
items.quote: A key positive in this quarter was the strong traction from new project launches, SPARCLE, a broad -spectrum insecticide for brown planthopper control in rice was successfully launched, developed using advanced chemistry from Corteva, strong farmer acceptance supported by IIL distribution strength and brand credibility. Other recent launches like Centran, Mill ion, also witnessed encouraging farme

items.statement: Technical plant at Sotanala expected to increase power and oil consumption by INR30-40 crores per annum
items.value: INR30 crores to INR40 crores per annum
items.quote: But when it comes to technicals, technicals of course, will come with the cost . So when I do technical synthesis, then yes, my power bill and both my oil bill, they are going to increase. So the consumption, I can assume will be in the range of INR30 crores to INR40 crores per annum on these two accounts.

items.statement: Dahej new formulation and technical plant in full action, will help improve performance in FY27
items.quote: The new formulation and technical plant is in full action at Dahej site. Its going to help us to improve our performance in FY '27.

items.statement: Q4 expected to see 5-6% preseason discounts; raw material costs up 2-3%
items.quote: And since the cost of currency is going up and some expectation in the price rise and some other things, so I would say generally 5% to 6% is the type of discount, which is considered during this quarter. So let's see where the market went as the demand starts. So I believe that somewhere about 5% to 6% discount only will come, not more than that because at the other point, the cost has also gone

items.statement: Consciously cutting tail of low-margin generics (25 products contributing 2-3% sales) while growing specialty Maharatna/Focus Maharatna products
items.quote: In my list, you wi ll find 25 more products, but they are ineffective. The total contribution is about 2% to 3% from this sale of '25 products and we are continuously cutting down this.

items.statement: B2B grew ~15% in Q3, B2C grew 3-4%; B2B share higher in Q3 driving volume-led growth
items.quote: So in the B2B segment in particular, it will be about 15% roughly, B2B. And in the B2C segment, it might be about 3% to 4% growth. So yes, it is more volume led in this quarter.

items.statement: Tightening credit limits and credit periods to prevent repeat of high sales returns
items.quote: We are wor king out our strategy. That's how we have to go more stronger in the markets with the tighter credit limits at one place and also the tighter credit periods. So we'll try to get the investment from the network and we will be very particular that this situation don't get repeated.

items.statement: Monocil (to be banned) final year sales ~INR75 cr; previous bans (Nuvan, Thimet ~INR200 cr) offset by new launches
items.quote: The new product, which is going to get banned is Monocil, This is the final year for that product. And that will also go, and that -- when it will go, the gross sales of the product will be around INR75 crores. So you can say about INR 75 crore from that product. So that will be the additional loss, which is going to hit the company. But as you know, that Nuvan and Thimet when they went in the fin

items.statement: ICS Plots (Integrated Crop Solutions) demonstrating ROI to farmers; plan to double investment in this brand-building initiative
items.quote: The plan is to at least double whatever investment we are making in the ICS Plot and we are going to do it in a big way in the future, and I believe this is going to help us in brand building in various crops and providing the complete solution for various crops across the country.

items.statement: Management reiterated medium-term guidance: top-quartile revenue growth vs peers, EBITDA margin 24-28%, and sequential EBITDA and EPS growth.
items.quote: And we'll continue to deliver on those in terms of growth in the top quartile of the peer segment that we operate. EBITDA margin between 24% to 28% and EPS and EBITDA growth sequentially.

items.statement: Underlying demand remains healthy with robust pipeline; Q4 may be softer due to near-term volatility but medium-to-long-term outlook is positive.
items.quote: While near-term volatility is inherent in our business and may result in Q4 being softer than the first 3 quarters, underlying demand remains healthy. Our pipeline continues to be robust, supported by sustained and meaningful engagement with clients.

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA margin 27.9%, down 90 bps QoQ due to higher variable payouts, travel and marketing; delivery cost improved 30 bps from higher utilization.
items.quote: On a Q-o-Q basis, EBITDA margin is down 90 bps, while it is up 190 bps compared to the same quarter of last fiscal. Increase in sales and distribution variable payouts and higher travel and marketing costs are the major contributers to the Q-o-Q margin decline.

items.statement: Q3 deal wins were $45 million; Analytics and Automation up 10%; average deal size (ACV) has increased versus 12 months ago.
items.quote: Deal wins for Q3 were $45 million. Analytics and Automation is up 10%, which is healthy.

items.statement: Added 400 new seats in Chandigarh; Egypt (Cairo) center will start servicing multiple clients in near term.
items.quote: And we've added 400 new seats in Chandigarh.

items.statement: DSO increased by about 2 days to 78 days.
items.quote: DSO has moved up by about 2 days to 78.

items.statement: Buyback completed in January with 625,000 shares extinguished; Board approved 1:1 bonus issue for shareholder approval.
items.quote: On an administrative note, we eClerx Services Limited January 29, 2026 4 completed the buyback process in January, and 625,000 shares were extinguished as a result. And the Board has approved 1:1 bonus, which will be put up for shareholders' approval in the coming

items.statement: New labor code impact low because basic pay already at 50% threshold; no significant cost increase expected.
items.quote: I think the impact for us is low because for most designations, our basic was already at that 50% mark, which is what is required by the new definition of wages. So, we did not have to do a lot of [changes] and the revised impact was not significant.

items.statement: Potential capex in Peru and Mohali in Q4 or Q1; continued investment in tech, AI, and sales.
items.quote: There is some CapEx that may happen in Peru. There is something that we are working on Mohali, which may be Q4 or Q1. So, there is some investment, but there may be investments on the people front as well.

items.statement: Hedging strategy is programmatic; no near-term plans to change despite potential elevated losses from spot/forward rates.
items.quote: So yes, we don't plan to look at it at least in the near term. I think that the strategy is programmatic for a reason and relooking at it may just lead to move away from hedging into speculation.

items.statement: Winning market share through supplier consolidation; tech-first IP-owned BPO/KPO model differentiates in Agentic AI deals.
items.quote: So, a, we are winning if there is a consolidation opportunity. I think on the back of strong delivery tech-first IPO, we are absolutely gaining market share whenever there's a consolidation opportunity.

items.statement: Confident that FY25-26 ACV of deal closures will be higher than prior year.
items.quote: I had said in Q2 that overall ACV of the deal closures that we will do in FY25 - 26 will be higher than what we did last year, and I continue to maintain I'm confident of delivering on the same.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 10.6% YoY to INR 1,404 crore, driven by Electricals segment
items.quote: Consolidated net revenue from operations for Q3 FY26 stood at INR 1,404 crore, reflecting a YoY growth of 10.6%.

items.statement: Electricals segment revenue grew 26% YoY led by volume expansion and higher copper prices
items.quote: The Electricals segment – our largest revenue contributor, comprising of Wires, Pumps, Switchgears, and Modular Switches – reported robust YoY revenue growth of 26% which was led by volume expansion and also supported by higher copper prices.

items.statement: Electronics segment revenue flat at INR 286 crore; summer categories muted but offset by growth in other categories
items.quote: The Electronics segment, which includes Stabilizers, UPS systems, and Inverters, reported largely flat revenues of INR 286 crore in Q3 FY26.

items.statement: Consumer Durables revenue grew 4.6% YoY; water heaters performed well, fans and cooling products subdued
items.quote: In the Consumer Durables segment – comprising of Fans, Water Heaters, Kitchen Appliances, and Air Coolers – revenues grew by 4.6% YoY.

items.statement: Sunflame revenue declined 9.9% YoY due to softness in kitchen appliances and weak CSD channel demand
items.quote: Sunflame reported a YoY revenue decline of 9.9% in Q3 FY26, reflecting continued softness in the kitchen appliances category.

items.statement: Gross margin contracted 100 bps YoY to 35.7% due to mix impact; margins remain resilient
items.quote: Gross margin for the quarter stood at 35.7%, compared to 36.7% in Q3 FY25, reflecting a contraction of 100 basis points, largely arising from the mix impact.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 60 bps YoY to 8.8%; EBITDA grew 18.3% YoY to INR 123 crore
items.quote: EBITDA (excluding other income) for Q3 FY26 stood at INR 123 crore, representing a YoY increase of 18.3%. EBITDA margin improved to 8.8% from 8.2% in Q3 FY25, an expansion of 60 basis points.

items.statement: Company plans calibrated pricing actions across portfolio in coming quarter due to input cost increases
items.quote: We foresee some input cost increases coming up and the Company plans to undertake calibrated pricing actions across the product portfolio in the coming quarter.

items.statement: Fans category needs significant price hikes due to commodity inflation and new energy rating norms from Jan 1; another 2-3% increase required before March
items.quote: We see some risk in the F ans’ category where this impact is very severe, coupled with new energy rating norms kicking in on 1st of Jan. So, there has to be significant price hikes in the Fans’ category. We have already taken some increases and I think another 2- or 3-odd percent of increase is required before

items.statement: Wires have dynamic pricing with short lag pass-through; Consumer Durables segment faces margin challenge; other categories need 2-3% price increases
items.quote: In Wires, as we have mentioned before, there is dynamic pricing. So, all the price increases and decreases are passed on to the market with a short lag. So really, I think the Consumer Durables' segment is where we feel there could be some challenge. Other categories, we don't; at this point, we don't feel it so much. Yes, there is a price increase that is required but the quantum is not that high

items.statement: Stabilizers require 1.5-2% price increase; copper-based fan models need higher increases than BLDC/aluminium models
items.quote: Yes, for Stabilizers it will be about maybe 1.5% to 2%. So generally, in most ; I think even in Fans, the problem is for the copper models . For BLDC, or alumin ium-based model s, the increases are lower

items.statement: Price increases initiated in Fans, Pumps in Jan, some categories in Feb, more by end of March; typically 2-3% except copper-based fans
items.quote: We have started to initiate price increases. I think we have passed on some price increase in Fans. We have passed on ; we have taken some price increase in P umps in Jan and in some categories we are doing in Feb and some we will be doing towards the end of March. A nd we will be landing all of these things. Typically, in some of the categories, it's about 2% - 3% and Fans is one that is fairly s

items.statement: Copper-based fans constitute 25-30% of fan mix; rest are aluminium or BLDC models
items.quote: Yes. About 25% - 30% would be copper i.e., copper-based. Others are all either aluminium or BLDC and aluminium models.

items.statement: Wires Q3 FY26: volume growth 10%, price growth 20%; January volume muted but value growth strong due to 30% price increase
items.quote: For December quarter on your question, the price growth was about 20%, volume growth was 10%.

items.statement: January Wires offtake decent but volume growth muted due to 30% price increase; some softening from project customers
items.quote: January also, we have seen continued increases in copper prices, and we are also in the process of revising prices. So Jan also, there has been decent offtake. Volume growth is muted, but value growth will be there because it's almost, I think, now 30. If you look at Jan over Jan, it's almost 30% increase in prices

items.statement: BLDC fans currently ~25% of V-Guard fan sales; expected to grow 5-10% share annually; induction fans will not disappear due to voltage fluctuation issues in upcountry markets
items.quote: So definitely, like today, for V-Guard, maybe the BLDC sales may be 25-odd-percent of total sales. We will see that steadily increasing, but I don't think 100% will move to BLDC because BDLC still has some challenges or some acceptances' issues.

items.statement: Fan manufacturing facility and second battery facility in Hyderabad are key pipeline projects to increase in-house manufacturing share
items.quote: In terms of capex, the fan manufacturing facility and the second battery facility, both in Hyderabad, are the two key projects in the pipeline. These will further increase the share of in-house manufacturing.

items.statement: Sunflame operational integration completed; sales integration underway since November; product refresh roadmap over next 12 months; customer service integration done; supply side integration ongoing
items.quote: We are right now in the process of Sunflame 's sales integration, which started actually about 2 months back. When I'm talking about sales integration, we are talking about integrating the sales force and the go -to-market system between Sunflame and V-Guard.

items.statement: Sunflame gross margins held; pricing transmission not a challenge; stress from delayed product refresh cycle (18 months)
items.quote: Landing pricing has not been a challenge as far as Sunflame is concerned, I think we have been able to hold our gross margins. We have been able to transmit pricing. So that has not been a challenge at all at any point in time.

items.statement: Stabilizers market share estimated at 40-45%; main national competitor Microtech at INR 150-180 crore; AC brands launch intermittently
items.quote: We estimate that we have a market share of about 40% - 45%. This category is fairly niche in that sense. The only serious competitor we have today is a company called Microtech, which is into Inverters and Batteries, based in Delhi. They are probably our closest peer and maybe doing about INR150 crores - INR180-odd crores.

items.statement: Inbuilt AC stabilizers debated for 15 years; Stabilizers volume CAGR 7-8% over 7-8 years, 10% over 5 years; category now <15% of sales vs much higher 10-20 years ago
items.quote: So this is a debate that's been going on for 15 years. This is not a new thing. And to put it in perspective, last 7- 8 years, we have had a volume CAGR of 7%- 8%. So even last 5 years, we've had a volume CAGR of 10%.

items.statement: Stabilizers inventory largely normalized; working capital management good in Q3; Kerala seeing warm temperatures (32-33°C) in January
items.quote: Stabilizers' inventory is largely normalized, you would have seen that our working capital management in Q3 has been fairly good. So a lot of the inventory that we had produced last summer, a lot of them have started to get liquidated.

items.statement: Electronics segment: AC Stabilizers and Air Coolers sharply degrown in FY26; expecting strong rebound in FY27 on low base; Solar Rooftops growing fast
items.quote: So in the Electronics' segment within that, the Air Conditioner Stabilizer s category has sharply degrown this year, the same as for Air Coolers. For both these products we are expecting a very strong rebound in the current year. The base is already low.

items.statement: Expect better profitability in FY27 vs FY26 due to better summer contribution and operating leverage, unless commodity prices violently spike further
items.quote: So, but I think in my sense is we should do better in FY '27, better than FY '26 is what we feel because of the better summer categories' contribution and operating leverage.

items.statement: Target double-digit EBITDA margins by FY27 if raw material inflation normalizes and growth returns
items.quote: I think so. I think if our growth does come back, we should be expecting double-digit EBITDA margins, yes.

items.statement: Wires volume growth could be challenged by 30% price increase; other 75% of categories have manageable inflation; summer onset key trigger
items.quote: So definitely, in the case of W ires, there has been a significant increase in prices to the tune of close to 30-odd percent. So definitely, there this argument that volumes for the product demand could take a hit, is true. But for the other 75% of categories, the price inflation is not that high.

items.statement: Six categories can exceed INR 1,000 crore: Stabilizers, Fans, Inverters & Batteries, Solar Rooftops, Kitchen Appliances (V-Guard + Sunflame), Modular Switches
items.quote: So there are a lot of categories that are more than INR 500 crores, INR600 odd crores for us - there is the Stabilizers category, Fans, Inverters and Batteries and S olar Rooftops, on its own. So these are all , these 4 categories are very much , and Kitchen Appliances is almost INR500 crores, if you put V-Guard plus Sunflame. So, we have at least six categories that can do more than INR1,000 cror

items.statement: Solar Pumps business started with first order of INR 4-5 crore from Maharashtra government; targeting meaningful scale-up in 12-18 months
items.quote: So we have started to participate in the tenders for S olar Pumps. And I think we have got our first order, and we are in the process of completing it. It is not a very large order, but we tend to, in the next 12 -18 months, scale it up meaningfully.

items.statement: Focus on profitable segments not volume chase; aim for top-3 in Decorative/BLDC Fans and Premium TPW Fans; not mass economy segment
items.quote: I think we do not chase volumes. We are more chasing profitability. So if you look at the F ans segment, we do not play in the mass segment, the econom y segment. And that segment is a segment that's going to get hit the hardest when inflation like this happens. So I think our focus is on building a profitable business rather than claiming a certain market share position.

items.statement: Expect strong power demand next year as base effect wears out; already seeing good bilateral PPA demand with high tariffs
items.quote: We expect to return the strong power demand in the ensuring year as the base effect wears out. We are already witnessing good bilateral PPA demand with high tariff being tied up.

items.statement: Target to reduce open merchant capacity from 10% to 3-4% over 6-7 years
items.quote: It is our strategy also, we are also trying to reduce this capacity, so maybe by 3% to 4% over the period of time. So, over the period of 6, 7 years, it will further reduce from 10% to 3% to 4%.

items.statement: Incurred INR 15,000 crores capex in 9M FY26 including advance payments to BTG suppliers
items.quote: On expansion side, this year, we have incurred capex of near about, , the INR 15,000 crores, including advance payments we have given to our BTG suppliers.

items.statement: Total capex program of INR 2 lakh crores (USD 22 billion) over 5-6 years to add 24 GW
items.quote: So, INR 2 lakh crores capex program we have in Adani Power that we are going to incur over the period of 5, 6 years.

items.statement: Mahan Phase-II 80% complete, Raipur Phase-II 44%, Raigarh Phase-II 38%; Korba Phase-II construction resumed
items.quote: Mahan Phase-II is about 80% complete. Raipur Phase-II is around 44% complete. Raigarh Phase-II is close to 38% complete. Construction at Korba Phase 2 project has also resumed.

items.statement: Korba Phase-II first unit by mid-FY27, second unit by end-FY27; Mahan Phase-II also targeted for FY27; all three projects by mid-FY29
items.quote: Next year, we are going to add Korba Phase-II, 2 x 660 MW, this year. Next year, we are also putting all the best possible efforts also to complete Mahan Phase 2 as well.

items.statement: Commissioning schedule: ~2.9 GW in FY27, 2.4 GW in FY28, 2.4 GW in FY29, 8 GW in FY30, 5.6 GW in FY31, 2.4 GW in FY32
items.quote: Broadly speaking, next year, around 2.9 gigawatts will get commissioned; in fiscal '28, another 2.4 gigawatts; in fiscal '29, 2.4 gigawatts; in fiscal '30, we have 8 gigawatts being commissioned altogether. In fiscal '31, we will have 5.6 gigawatts and then 2.4 gigawatts.

items.statement: Received Letter of Award for 3,200 MW greenfield project in Assam under DBFOO model with SHAKTI fuel linkage
items.quote: During the quarter, we received a Letter of Award for a 3,200-megawatt project in Assam. This project will be developed on a greenfield basis under the DBFOO model, on land to be provided by the state. Fuel linkage will be arranged under SHAKTI Policy.

items.statement: Over 90% of 18.15 GW operating capacity tied up under long/medium-term PPAs; targeting 93% as more PPAs operationalize
