items.quote: In my thesis, I would say, with also the restructuring that is happening broadly now in the European chemical industry, I would see more opportunities of Indian companies actually exporting into Europe.

items.statement: US exposure only 10% of revenue (INR 300 crores), of which only 10% directly impacted by tariffs; no material impact in Q3.
items.quote: Laxmi's exposure to the U.S. market is only 10% of our top line revenue. That is INR 300 crores. Of that INR 300 crores, only about 10% of that was truly impacted by the tariff topics.

items.statement: Employee cost rose to INR 46 crores from INR 34 crores YoY due to Lote/Dahej headcount additions (INR 4 crores), annual increments, and prior year ESOP reversal (INR 4 crores).
items.quote: Our employee cost is at INR 46 crores versus previous year of INR 34 crores. In previous year of INR 34 crores, mainly there was a reversal of ESOP of nearly INR 4 crores. And also it has an impact of additional headcounts at Lote and Dahej of INR 4 crores.

items.statement: One-time gain of INR 407 million from Supreme Court order on wheeling/transmission charges; offset by INR 38 million labor code provision and INR 9 million supply chain redesign cost.
items.quote: These results also include a one -time gain, which we have called it out specifically from our notes i n the published accounts for favorable litigation settlement for wheeling and transmission charges of INR 407 million.

items.statement: Lote facility operating in compliance with all Indian regulations; no hazardous discharge; reaffirmed commitment to transparency and stakeholder engagement.
items.quote: We also affirmed that our Lote facility operates in compliance with all applicable Indian requirements, and there has been no discharge of hazardous affluence into the environment where we operate.

items.statement: Acetic acid expected to trade between $340-370 in near term; not returning to $320-330 lows; ethyl acetate spreads improving toward $130 range.
items.quote: From today's perspective, that is where we expect somewhere between upward of $340 to that $360, $370 level is where it might float.

items.statement: Challenging business environment with muted customer offtake, pricing pressure, tariff uncertainties, and incremental Chinese capacities
items.quote: The current quarter was marked by challenging and uncertain business environment, driven by muted customer offtake, pricing pressure and tariff-related uncertainties, along with incremental capacities of some of the products, especially in China.

items.statement: HALS business delivered 55% YoY growth driven by favorable product mix and higher derivatized HALS polymers
items.quote: On a positive note, the HALS business delivered robust Y -o-Y growth of 55%, driven by a favorable product mix and higher contribution from cost -efficient higher derivatized HALS polymers.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin 40% and PAT margin 29% in Q3 FY26
items.quote: The EBITDA and PAT margins are at 40% and 29%, translating into an EBITDA of INR72 crores and a PAT of INR52 crores.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 33% and PAT margin 21% in Q3 FY26
items.quote: the consol EBITDA and PAT margins are at 33% and 21%, respectively, which stood at INR72 crores a nd INR46 crores

items.statement: Top 4 products contribution to standalone revenue declined to 75% from 80% in previous quarter
items.quote: Consequently, top 4 products contribution to stand -alone revenue declined to 75% as against 80% in the last quarter.

items.statement: 9-month revenue declined 10% YoY due to loss of key cosmetic customer, pricing pressure, and lower Agchem offtake
items.quote: On 9-month Y-o-Y basis, the revenue declined by 10%, that is from INR668 crores to INR602 crores. It was -- the reduction in revenue was attributed to a loss of a key customer in one of our Clean Science and products in cosmetic section, also pricing pressure and lower offtake in Agchem segment.

items.statement: Hydroquinone and catechol plant commercialized in December; customer trials ongoing
items.quote: The hydroquinone and catechol was commercialized in the mon th of December and customer trials are ongoing.

items.statement: Performance Chemical 2 capex on track, expected commercialization in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Further capex time line of Performance Chemical 2 is as per plan, and we expect to commercialize in Q1 FY '27.

items.statement: Capital infusion in subsidiary INR150 crores in last 9 months, total investment around INR700 crores
items.quote: During the last 9 months, the capital infusion in subsidiary has been INR150 crores with now the total investment in subsidiary around INR700 crores.

items.statement: Interim dividend of INR2 per share approved
items.quote: the company has approved an interim dividend of INR2 per share.

items.statement: Two new Board members appointed: Mr. Raj Kamal and Mrs. Pallavi Gokhale
items.quote: We are also very happy to announce and welcome two new Board members, Mr. Raj Kamal and Mrs. Pallavi Gokhale as successors to our earlier retiring independent directors.

items.statement: Performance Chemical 1 at 80% utilization expected to generate INR260 crores revenue (down from earlier INR320 crores)
items.quote: But to just pinpoint with the Performance Chemical 1 because of the prices reduction overall, the -- around 80% capacity utilization, we are looking at a revenue of INR260 crores, which was earlier INR320-odd crores.

items.statement: Performance Chemical 2 facility to begin by May-June, staggered revenues expected from Q4 FY27
items.quote: And Performance Chemical 2, the capex is under -- I mean, we are still under capex phase and the facility will only begin by May, June. And we expect after teething issues, customer approvals, we should only see revenues in Q4.

items.statement: HALS volume at 2,000 tons for 9 months; target 50% utilization over 2-year period
items.quote: So I mean, for this year, we are already at 2,000 tons of volume for 9 months. And I mean, we'd be happy to note that year -on-year, we have reported a 55% growth in HALS sales for this particular quarter, right? And our target remains like that's typically with any new product which we are commercializing at least around 50% of utilization over a 2-year period.

items.statement: Blended HALS portfolio realization at INR425 per kg for Q3 FY26
items.quote: Our blended portfolio realization for this quarter has been INR425 a kg.

items.statement: Lost key customer in China for 4-MAP in FMCG segment; customer backward integrated
items.quote: FMCG segment, where a product called 4-MAP, where we've lost a customer in China. And due to secondary impact of tariff of our end customers in India, they have l ost their business in the United States, and hence, we are impacted by them as well.

items.statement: Chinese competitors lowered hydroquinone prices to all-time lows, forcing MEHQ price cuts to maintain volumes
items.quote: Now because the Chinese have lowered the prices of hydroquinone all-time low price and hence, the conventional process of hydroquinone to MEHQ makes MEHQ also at a lower cost point. To attribute to this, we have no choice but to lower our prices of MEHQ to compete with these emerging players of hydroquinone-derived MEHQ in China.

items.statement: BHA volume decline due to North American tariff concerns and year-end destocking
items.quote: The BHA, we've reduced -- it went lower mostly in quarter 3. It is a very typical standard because the drop has happened in North America. There was some tariff-related concern and also because Clean Science and a lot of customers prefer to have lower stocks at the end of December

items.statement: Indian 4-MAP customers slowed purchases due to 55% US tariff on avobenzone
items.quote: Now avobenzone from India has a tariff of 55% in the United States. So all the Indian customers who are buying have s lowed down dramatically because of this severe impact of tariffs from the U.S.

items.statement: Hydroquinone plant: 15% captive consumption, 85% for domestic and international sales
items.quote: No, no. We will have a lot of HQ to sell. Probably, we will be only using about 15 -odd percent for our own captive and the balance will be sold in the market. That is both international and local.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin guidance deferred; will reassess after next quarter
items.quote: it would be Clean Science and appropriate to wait for at least for a quarter to really understand where we stand. So probably in the next quarter or the end of the next quarter, we can have this discussion, please

items.statement: International sales declined 15-16% in Europe and US due to tariffs and low acrylic acid prices
items.quote: International, yes, definitely, both in Europe and U.S., we have seen a decent decline closer to 15%, 16% in these markets. As I Clean Science and mentioned right now, it is because of two factors: one is tariff; and other is whether they're being impacted by the global acrylic acid prices, which have come down and they are at its all -time low

items.statement: Domestic Agchem volumes postponed not lost; expected to return when cycles resume
items.quote: In terms of India, these were just campaign -related cycles, I think, which have moved or postponed, and it is a very customer -centric thing. So when these agchem cycles come back, probably these volumes will again come back. But we have not lost the volumes. I just want to repeat this. The volume is not lost, it is postponed.

items.statement: Performance Chemical 1 plant started; imports of hydroquinone and catechol stopped; sales from February
items.quote: We will start seeing -- so the plant started. Currently, we are using -- because there are teething issues, the product is slight off spec, but we are currently consuming all the products in -house. So where I was importing, say, probably around 70, 80 tons of hydroquinone per m onth, you would have seen that those imports have stopped completely. Same is the case with catechol, which we were impo

items.statement: Performance Chemical 2 delayed by 2 months; production start expected by May with 60-day delay
items.quote: Yes. I think we had anticipated that we will start the production in March. But now we feel with the current scenario, we'll start by May. So there has been a 2 month -- a 60-day delay, probably another 15-odd days for water trials and commissioning. So yes, there has been a quarter delay; yes, you're right.

items.statement: HALS sequential volume growth 6% (760 to 810 tons); revenue growth 5-6%
items.quote: Abhijit, on a sequential basis, we have witnessed 6% growth in volume. So this quarter, we have almost crossed 800 tons in volumes, almost 810 tons is the sales volume. And just to add over that, the product mix has also improved meaning 944 is now almost contributing 20% to the HALS portfolio.

items.statement: Tariff uncertainty and Chinese pricing pressure expected to continue for at least next 2 quarters
items.quote: Whether this will improve? I think, with tariffs not going Clean Science and anywhere, so that impact of tariffs still remains. And the prices, which currently we are seeing in the chemical market segment, primarily led by the Chinese also, I think, might remain for the quarter or 2. So the impact would be at least continue for the next 2 quarters, if not more

items.statement: HALS domestic 70%, international 30%; export mix expected to improve in Q4 and FY27
items.quote: 70% is domestic currently, Ankur. 70% is domestic, 30% is international, but you will start seeing as we mo ve in quarter 4 and then subsequently in '27, this mix will start changing, and we expect the exports to quickly start ramping up.

items.statement: India-EU FTA benefits (5.5-12% tariff advantage) expected to start in FY27 after paperwork
items.quote: this will only start in '27. I think there's still a l ot of paperwork has to be done between the two countries. So it is not going to -- I mean you will not see anything on an immediate basis. This will, I think, only start in '27. And the trade impact would have a 5.5% to 12% is the tariffs, which we pay an d also the Chinese. So if those will come out then, of course, it will help the Indian ch

items.statement: Hydroquinone/catechol EBITDA margins expected between HALS and parent business; current pricing fluid
items.quote: No. I don't think that -- no, that EBITDA margins will not be at those extent. They would be -- they will be lower. I think they will be better than HALS', lower than the parent business. Again, they will be like midpoint. And with these current prices of hydroquinone, which we are currently seeing and because they have declined quite a bit, so I think it is, again, a very fluid condition to menti

items.statement: Company sitting on INR450 crores cash; capex completed within anticipated costs despite volatility
items.quote: I mean, we are healthy in terms of cash flow, company is still sitting on INR450 crores of cash. The projects, which we had mentioned, have all happened beyond -- I mean, within probably a less than a quarter delay, but all the capexes have happened at the project costs, which we had anticipated despite of all these volatile times.

items.statement: Expect to offset 30-40% of PIDF impact this quarter and more over time
items.quote: Our expectation is at least 30 - 40 percent of this will be offset this quarter and more over time.

items.statement: Contribution margin may decline to mid-50s due to PIDF impact
items.quote: you also talk about contribution margin going from 57 percent now to mid 50s as a result of the PIDF impact.

items.statement: Payment processing margin expected to stay above 4 basis points for next few quarters
items.quote: We feel pretty confident that it will stay above four basis points for the next few quarters.

items.statement: EBITDA impact expected in Q4 from remaining 60% of PIDF impact not offset this quarter
items.quote: So yes, in the very short term, we will take an EBITDA impact in Q4.

items.statement: Buy Now Pay Later crossed 1 lakh customers in 3 months since launch
items.quote: We have crossed one lakh customers. And within six months of launch, we expect to cross hundred crores of disbursal.

items.statement: Expect to cross 100 crores monthly disbursal on Buy Now Pay Later within 6 months of launch
items.quote: And within six months of launch, we expect to cross hundred crores of disbursal.

items.statement: Wallet relaunch planned for consumer completeness, not expected to be as large as previously thought
items.quote: We do think that just to manage expectations, because in conference meetings and so on, we get a lot of questions on this. We had talked about wallet profitability being Rs 500 crores in January 2024. We don't think the product is that big in the industry going forward.

items.statement: Paytm Money target to become top 5 player in less than 3 years
items.quote: We want to make Paytm Money a top five player in less than next three years.

items.statement: Online payment business restarted after being paused since 2021, now recruiting for enterprise sales
items.quote: I think we have literally added a new line of business, which will be materially sizable because that business since 2021 was paused practically.

items.statement: Subscription merchants (deployed device base) at 1.44 crores, used as top-of-funnel proxy
items.quote: We do talk about subscription merchants. These are merchants that actually have a device from us. That is 1.44 crores. We see that as the proxy for our top of the funnel.

items.statement: Registered merchants at 4.8 crores but not used for operations, only SEBI obligation
items.quote: We have a number of registered merchants, which is disclosed in the back of the document, which is 4.8 crores. Ignore that completely.

items.statement: Not in device deployment or rental device as business model; focus on payment and financial services
items.quote: We are not in device deployment, rental device as a business model, capex as a revenue model. We are strictly about payment and financial services and that is sacrosanct.

items.statement: Cost optimization continuous; sales employee cost at all-time high, marketing paused for product-led approach
items.quote: Our sales employee cost this quarter is actually all time high. So we're not under investing. We do think in parallel, we're constantly working like Vijay is saying on productivity. So, for example, we reduced our marketing expenses somewhat because Vijay was not convinced that it is as productive as it can be.

items.statement: AI-based sales planning enables disciplined recalibration and payback measurement
items.quote: A huge amount of our sales planning now is AI based and it is extremely intelligent. So for us to recalibrate certain efforts and measure payback periods is much more advanced than it was maybe a year and a half or two years ago.

items.statement: PIDF not required for business model; industry welcomes government initiatives but model not based on grants
items.quote: Does the industry need PIDF? Well, as an industry, we are welcoming every initiative that the government or any other entities look to give us. But at the same time, our business model is not based on this. That's the key word. We are not sitting here to take grants as our profit and revenue.

items.statement: Merchant loan business grew 25% like-for-like (reported 20%)
items.quote: We have also mentioned that we did 25% growth on a like-for-like basis, which you can take it for what it's worth. Obviously, the reported number is 20%.

items.statement: Marketing services revenue flattish over last 3-4 quarters
items.quote: We have been quite transparent about the fact that the marketing services, it's been flattish over the last three, four quarters.

items.statement: Consumer credit cycle longer than expected, affecting personal loans and credit cards
items.quote: The consumer credit cycle continued for a bit longer than we thought, which affected personal loans and credit cards.

items.statement: Outlook intact: positive on device growth, merchant loans, payments processing margin; expect growth acceleration and EBITDA margin improvement
items.quote: I think the outlook is more or less intact. I think we are as excited about the opportunity in India today as we were two or three years ago. The more we do, the more opportunities we find. So we think on device growth, with or without PIDF, that business is robust.

items.statement: Adopted conservative revenue recognition: stop recognizing revenue from merchants inactive >30 days, increases PDD but EBITDA neutral
items.quote: We have tightened that. As a result of that policy, we would get some provision for doubtful debt. Because some of that revenue you're not able to collect. So what we did was we said, we're going to be much tighter about merchants if they've been inactive for more than 30 days, we'll stop recognizing revenue from them.

items.statement: Continuous removal of deadwood and relocation within cost base; investing in future while pruning non-core
items.quote: And the good thing is that I'm removing the deadwood continuously. That project will continue. So there you see relocation happening within the cost. It is not that we are not investing in the future. We are rather investing in the future and removing what we don't want to carry forward.

items.statement: Device-led offline merchant business phenomenally better than anyone else; every replica is proof of model
items.quote: Now that everybody's numbers are out in the market, I can flawlessly say that every replica of our business model is a proof of our business model and acknowledgement and we've done better than anybody else that is shown there.

items.statement: Promotional expense at calibrated level; focus on product-led, technology-led growth not marketing spend-led
items.quote: I'd rather build a product-led, technology-led product instead of marketing or marketing spend-led product. So we were bare minimum and we had told about it in a previous quarter, if you remember that, that we would do it calibrated. So I think this could be more or less the normal trend.

items.statement: Promotional spend driven by market share gain via high-quality users and engagement, not dilution
items.quote: It is not about let's go in and double down. That is not the focus. The focus, because you could dilute quality on the platform dramatically and that affects your RoI and retention rates and so on. So, yes, like Vijay just said, it's market share gain, but it's driven by making sure we have high quality users, high quality of engagement and that being the path to market share gains.

items.statement: Not guiding to higher payment margin numbers right now; want to see market discipline continue
items.quote: We're not guiding to higher numbers right now. We want to see just market discipline continue and the trend of things like RuPay on UPI, et cetera, continue and positive mix.

items.statement: Marketing services business bottomed out last quarter and should continue to grow
items.quote: We did see bottoming out last quarter and we could see that it had bottomed out, which is why we called it out in the last quarter. And we do think that this business should continue to grow.

items.statement: Awaiting budget announcement on potential MDR for organized merchants; two days away
items.quote: It's two days away. So let's just wait now.

items.statement: Subscription revenue on blended basis will offset some PIDF impact; not simply raising subscription fees
items.quote: My sense is in certain places, we are going to see that years of investment have changed behavior to a point that merchants are actually okay to pay a little bit more, right? Whereas in other areas, we're going to find that a merchant is quite engaged, and as a result, there's more lending propensity in that area. So it's not a combination of these things. But I think it's fair to say the subscrip

items.statement: RuPay credit card on UPI and EMI merchants contributing to higher payment margin; growing EMI market share
items.quote: Yes, there is a contribution from RuPay and UPI. Better credit card and EMI merchants, and just growth in our EMI market share overall. We're doing extremely well.

items.statement: Consumer UPI GMV of 5.1 trillion includes both P2P and P2M transactions
items.quote: It is what NPCI gives the GMV value.

items.statement: Net payment margin as percentage has not gone up; GMV up 24%, revenue up 22% year-on-year
items.quote: My understanding is GMV is up 24%, revenue is up 22%.

items.statement: Soundbox rental pricing varies by merchant engagement, device type, cost reductions, and lending propensity; no blanket increase
items.quote: There are two, three factors. One is a merchant who is highly engaged, is willing to pay more for the soundbox and it may even be a higher-end soundbox, right? So they might want to take a tap soundbox or they might want to take even a swipe soundbox, AI soundbox, etc. So they are willing to pay more. The second is our cost per soundbox has come down dramatically if you're talking about over a thr

items.statement: Online strategy focuses on commerce-led business for D2C merchants, combining online and offline with consumer reach
items.quote: We are not looking at it as purely payment processing, which is a very thin margin business rather. We are looking at it, how can we increase the business of this person? So it's a commerce led business plan that we have on online and that inherently inherits that only large enterprise processors are not useful because they have their own businesses of acquiring customers.

items.statement: Ambition to solve market share concentration risk via organic technology plans; less than one year since regulator permission
items.quote: We want to solve for the market share concentration risk by our organic technology plans. That's it. That's our ambition. That's our mission and we will keep at it. And I am very happy to tell you that we earned the right to be that once the regulator permitted us last October. So let's remember, we are less than one year old company, man.

items.statement: Digital gold is a customer retention product, not a margin or classic revenue product; over 5 million customers purchase gold
items.quote: We don't look at it as our winning bet or losing bet. We look at it as a very consistent customer retention bet. I believe if a customer has a lock-in on us with this, he will stay longer term. So we don't look at it as a margin or classic revenue product, but we look at it as let's retain the customer by committing something on our platform.

items.statement: Will take down industry take rate on digital gold with volume; prefer selling at least margin leftover to drive payment processing volume
items.quote: I would take down the take rate of the industry with our volume. You've seen that we did it in many categories and we will do it. I would prefer to sell it on the least margin leftover so that we can take care of the payment processing.

items.statement: International expansion focused on replicable merchant stack; foundational work done, announcements expected in 3-6 months
items.quote: Over the next three to six months, there might be a couple of announcements with respect to what specifically we are doing and what partnerships we have entered into.

items.statement: Merchant lending driven by device additions (~27 lakh YoY), penetration rising ~1% YoY, average ticket size compounding ~15% annually
items.quote: The three main drivers of our merchant loan business, in a sense, are a number of devices, which is growing at about 27 lakhs year on year, percentage penetration, which is broadly going at about 1% a year, give or take, and then average ticket size, which has been growing, if you look at last four or five years, compounded about 15% a year and slightly higher than that.

items.statement: Consumer credit shifting to BNPL as foundational layer; less interested in pure personal loan distribution
items.quote: In the consumer side credit, we are adding BNPL as a foundational way to expand on it. So a little bit of growth on that. Then secondly, which also means that we are less interested in distributing just a personal loan, which we believe everybody who has an app can do.

items.statement: Paytm Money showing green shoots; equity broking market share and monetization up, driven by MTF products
items.quote: Market share went up a bit and monetization went up a bit more than that because of MTF products and so on.

items.statement: Other direct expenses up 16% QoQ driven by FLDG for scaling merchant loans and higher collection costs
items.quote: We have other direct expenses, a combination of FLDG, which, which goes there as our merchant loan business is scaling and also a little bit higher collection costs. Those are the primary drivers.

items.statement: Paytm Check-in AI product shows 30%+ conversion funnel; AI-first product with technology differentiation
items.quote: We have a funnel that converts 30 plus percent. I mean, it is shocking that you talk to AI and say that I want to book the cheapest ticket between Delhi, Bombay next week. And it has seven days and it has any hour of the day. And people find something so phenomenally good that they're converting 30 percent. One third conversion of an AI query.

items.statement: Key consumer monetization use-cases: credit, wealth, and commerce (travel/deals)
items.quote: I think credit, wealth, and commerce equivalent , which are called travel or deals, et cetera.

items.statement: Payment margin guidance may be revisited in next two quarters; currently on solid positive trajectory
items.quote: We'll probably look at that in the next two quarters. But currently we are seeing quite a solid. Actually. Positive trajectory.

items.statement: MDR changes could dramatically alter payment margins; acquiring side has huge upside if MDR implemented
items.quote: MDR will dramatically change it because there's an acquiring side. There is a huge amount of upside on MDR may not be on the consumer app. Actually, I just want to be reminded that all the money goes to the bank.

items.statement: Subscription per device should decline low to mid single digits annually; efficiency gains on capex/opex must exceed that
items.quote: You should also know that we do factor that like for like subscription per device, even besides the subvention that Vijay mentioned should go down some low to mid single digits every year. And our efficiency on capex and opex should be higher than that.

items.statement: Big decline in other indirect expenses due to PDD; provisioning policy tight, collecting receivables well including past provisions
items.quote: The big decline is because of PDD. There are things that we continue to do on making sure overall we are efficient. So a big decline is because of PDD. And also we are doing a pretty good job of collecting receivables, including provision receivables in the past. So our provisioning policy is also pretty tight.

items.statement: Depreciation not expected to rise next year due to low capex last year; may increase year after as capex ramps for deployment
items.quote: I think because our capex was quite low last year and much higher the year before, and we have probably a two to three year depreciation policy. So next year you should not see an impact, but as we increase capex for deployment, then yes, the year after that there might be an increase.

items.statement: Targeting 250 million monetizable customers in India over next 3-4 years; current monetization machinery can handle that scale
items.quote: I'm going to say about 250 million customers is a good number for us to aim for. I mean, what percentage of the market would it be? That's for the market to discover. But at the same point of time, I fundamentally believe we today's monetization machinery have the ability to monetize 250 million customers.

items.statement: AI agent development leading in real-world enterprise benchmarks; topped rankings ahead of ByteDance, Alibaba, AT&T, Snowflake
items.quote: We are much ahead of ByteDance, Alibaba, and even AT&T, Snowflake, everybody. And it is not just number one for one use-case. We are also on the number six on use-case that we are showing up here.

items.statement: Medium-to-long-term guidance: revenue CAGR ~15%, gross margin 55-58%, EBITDA ~30%, PAT ~15%
items.quote: Our ASP growth, Saurabh has been in that range, pretty much, 2% to 3%. So for example, in Q2, our growth -- overall growth rate was around 12%. So take out 3% from there, and that's how you get the percentage. In this quarter, our overall growth is 15%. So if you take out 3%, 12% will be volume growth. So broadly in that range. Our ASPs growth has been largely consistent in that 2% to 3% range.

items.statement: Pre-IndAS PAT margin drag expected at 1.2-1.3% run-rate, higher when large stores open
items.quote: On an ongoing basis, I think it should be around at 1.2%, 1.3%. YTD, that percentage is higher because, as you remember in Q2, we opened 4 Foot Locker stores. So whenever we open the big size stores where the entry periods are slightly higher, because the stores are higher and -- are bigger and it takes more time for -- in the fit out of the store. That's why you get that higher hit.

items.statement: Q3 consolidated revenue grew 15% YoY, crossing INR 800 cr for first time; double-digit growth for third straight quarter
items.quote: As you are aware, we posted a 15% growth in our stand -alone business and our consolidated business. It was good to have a quarter without any unusual even ts or any offset from the year before. The key Diwali and Wedding season performed well and we are pleased to see that the traffic stays steady, both in our online and offline channels.

items.statement: Digital commerce grew 24% YoY, now 12% of total revenue
items.quote: I'm also pleased to see the consistent growth from our multiple e-com channels with our digital commerce business as it grew 24% and now reached a 12% share of our total revenues.

items.statement: EBITDA grew 16% standalone and 18% consolidated; EBITDA margin 33% for both
items.quote: On the EBITDA side, we grew by 16% for the standalone and 18% for the consolidated business, and we delivered a 33% EBITDA for both.

items.statement: PAT grew 33% to 16% margin for both standalone and consolidated, despite INR 3.3 cr Labour Code accrual
items.quote: Nonetheless, our PAT grew by 33%, and we achieved 16% for the quarter for both the standalone and consolidated business.

items.statement: Opened 35 new stores, closed 11 in Q3; 100+ net new stores YTD; launched 3 MetroActiv stores
items.quote: We opened 35 new stores this quarter and closed 11, bringing our total new stores this fiscal year to over 100. Additionally, we are excited to announce the launch of 3 new MetroActiv stores.

items.statement: Clarks stores planned around Q3 FY27; Foot Locker expansion measured due to BIS uncertainty
items.quote: As I mentioned on our previous call, our new partnership is off to a great start, and we plan on opening Clarks stores around Q3 of this coming fiscal year.

items.statement: Total store count ~1,000; 13.9 lakh sq ft used for sales per sq ft calculation
items.quote: It is 13,90,000-odd square feet. And sales per square feet, we only take store revenue.

items.statement: Premium (>INR 3,000) share at 55% of business; GST rate cut benefits 40% of Metro Mochi and 90% of Walkway portfolio
items.quote: The GST benefits continue to help specific parts of our business and our ongoing focus on premium products kept our sales of over INR3,000 at a 55% share of business.

items.statement: GST reduction passed to consumers via discounts; net sales unaffected; consumer pays ~3% less overall, 6-11% less on specific price bands
items.quote: So around 3% to 4% less is what the customer is paying on our entire portfolio. On specific sales, if it is below 2,000 -- if the item was -- with MRP was below INR1,000, the overall differential would be around 6%, 7% from a customer point of view. And if it was between INR2,500 to INR1,000, the differential would be somewhere in the range of 11%.

items.statement: New products being re-priced with revised MRPs reflecting lower GST; existing inventory continues to get discount at invoice
items.quote: For all the new products that are getting added, we are evaluating what is the final GST that we had to pay to the government and accordingly, realigning our MRPs. We believe in maintaining our markup and passing on benefits to the customer wherever we get, just to make sure that customer continues to see value at the price point at which the product is offered.

items.statement: BIS certification delays affecting Foot Locker and FILA high-heat (>INR 10-15k) imported products; resolution now expected Q2 FY27

items.statement: Inventory slightly built up in Q3 in line with season and store openings; nothing abnormal vs prior years

So broadly in line, nothing much. We don't see anything abnormal there, broadly in line with what we saw -- what we see year -on-year.

items.statement: Finance cost lower YoY; IndAS notional lease cost ~INR 39-40 cr for 9M vs INR 28-29 cr last year

items.statement: Volume growth ~9% in Q2 and ~12% in Q3 (derived from 12-15% revenue growth minus 2-3% ASP growth)

items.statement: E-commerce mix target sub-20%; focus on profitability and brand value over growth chasing

But we don't want to do that. We will not do that. We want to create a busi ness that's accretive, both to our sales, but also to our brand value.

items.statement: Online channel uses exclusive product lines (not low quality) to serve zip codes without physical stores; not a discount-driven channel

items.statement: Industry closing stock estimated ~6 million tonnes vs earlier 8 million tonnes estimate, supportive of sugar prices
items.quote: And this will reduce the closing stock. In the last few weeks, we believe that there is further impetus. And we can see that signs from the budget, the Union budget that was announced yesterday, the focus on energy , etc and clean energy is something that is definitely being driven home by North block

And we find that we are very much on track, as I have previously said, for this to happen during under this quarter, this calendar quarter.

items.statement: Cycle 2 ethanol tender focused on rice-based ethanol, may limit molasses allocation for Q3-Q4
items.quote: Unfortunately, we understand that the focus of the Cycle 2 tender, which is primarily for Q3 and Q4 supplies, it will be focused primarily on rice-based ethanol, which is FCI rice-based ethanol, followed them by B -heavy and C molasses. So not sure how much B -heavy and C molasses will make its way through to Q3, Q4.

items.statement: ₹22.4 crore provision for new labour codes impact on employee benefits
items.quote: There has been a provision of ₹22.4 crore, which has been estimated because of the changes brought about by the new labour codes in respect to the employee benefit expenses, as disclosed in our exceptional items.

items.quote: As such, we now expect our constant currency revenue growth for FY26 to be in 13% to 14% range. This does not include the recent Pastdue Credit Solutions and TeleMedik acquisitions. Including these two acquisitions, we expect our FY26 constant currency revenue growth to be in 14.5% to 15.5% range.

items.statement: FY26 EBIT margin guidance raised to 11.5-12% range
items.quote: We also raise our EBIT margin guidance for FY26 to 11.5% to 12% range.

items.statement: Q3 EBIT margin 11.9%, up 80bps YoY and 40bps QoQ, fifth straight quarter of expansion
items.quote: EBIT margin for the quarter was 11.9%, up 80 basis points and 40 basis points on a YoY and QoQ basis, respectively. It is also the fifth straight quarter of margin expansion

items.statement: Deal pipeline remains above $1 billion, won 13 large deals in 9M FY26 vs 14 in full FY25
items.quote: Importantly, despite the strong closure, our deal pipeline has stayed above US$1bn. Let me give you some additional insights. We have won 13 large deals in the f irst nine months of FY26, versus 14 wins in the entire

items.statement: Broad-based demand across verticals, pipeline evenly distributed +/-3-5% across segments, UnBPO creating traction
items.quote: When I look at our pipeline and the composition of the pipeline, I think we see almost even distribution +/-3% to 5% points in terms of the distribution across different vertical segments itself.

items.statement: DSO 67 days vs 69 in Q2; OCF/EBITDA 93% for quarter, 86% for 9M; FCF/adjusted PAT 164% for quarter, 159% for 9M
items.quote: DSO was 67 days for the quarter versus 69 days in Q2. Tighter working capital days helped on improved cash conversion. Our OCF to EBITDA was 93% and FCF to adjusted PAT was 164% for the quarter.

items.statement: Net debt Rs 11.7bn at Dec 2025 vs Rs 10.8bn at Sep 2025 and Rs 13.2bn at Mar 2025; cash balance Rs 4bn
items.quote: Our net debt stands at Rs 11.7 billion as of 31 st December 2025 versus Rs 10.8 billion as of 30 th September 2025 and Rs 13.2 billion as of 31st March 2025

items.statement: Hedge book: GBP 95.3M at avg Rs 113.9/GBP, USD 178.2M at avg Rs 88.6/USD for next 12 months
items.quote: Our hedge book as of 31st December was as follows: we had coverage of GBP 95.3 million for the next 12 months with an average rate of Rs 113.9 per Pound and coverage of USD 178.2 million with an average rate of Rs 88.6 per US$.

items.statement: Board declared interim dividend of Rs 5.5 per share
items.quote: I am pleased to share that the Board has declared an interim dividend of Rs 5.5 per share.

items.statement: Over 50% of business now non-linear in construct (outcome-based, not T&M or fixed price)
items.quote: what I will state is upwards of 50% of our business today is non-linear in construct.

items.statement: Offshore/nearshore revenue mix 43.4%, up ~13-14pp over 9-10 quarters; 80% gross hiring offshore/nearshore
items.quote: Our offshoring has increased very smartly to around 43.4% in this quarter, up by almost 13%, 14% points over the last 9 to 10 quarters.

items.statement: One-time Rs 914M charge for gratuity/leave encashment provisioning per new Labour Code; Rs 88M exceptional item for legacy investment diminution
items.quote: As I mentioned, there is a one -time charge of Rs 914 million on account of increased provisioning for gratuity and leave encashment in accordance with the new Labour Code announced by the Government of India. items.quote: So, it is a little too early to react to it because, as I understand, as I am sure you are also seeing this, this is still a proposal at this point in time. Details on the implementation and compliance requirements associated with this are still awaited.

items.statement: UK onshore headcount down ~40% over 4 quarters, South Africa headcount up ~50%; 80% gross hiring offshore/nearshore to continue
items.quote: our UK onshore headcount has come down by about 40% over the last four quarters, while the corresponding headcount in South Africa during the same period is up by about 50%.

items.quote: The impact in Q3 was about a couple of million dollars. We think it will be a little higher in Q4, so roughly about 50 basis points on our FY26 revenue growth itself.

items.statement: Pastdue Credit acquired for GBP 22M (incl GBP 4.4M earnouts), paid Rs 2.2B in Q3; TeleMedik announced, integrates Q4 FY26

items.statement: Effective tax rate 21% in Q3, 20% for 9M, within guided 19-21% for FY26; steady state ~1% +/- from current 21% post new tax regime
items.quote: Effective tax rate in Q3 was 21% and for nine months it was 20%, which is within the guided 19-21% range for FY26.

items.statement: UnBPO model creating differentiation, winning against traditional linear contracts; ISG Booming 15 for 5th consecutive quarter

items.quote: Revenue for Q3FY26 came in at Rs 24.4 billion or US$274 million. This implies a YoY growth of 16.2% in the rupee term and 10.2% in US$ terms. In constant currency, this translates to a YoY growth of 10.6%.

items.quote: Over the last 8 quarters, the revenue share of Top5 and Top10 clients has come down by 8% and 11% respectively. items.quote: During the quarter, we laid the foundation for a fundamental shift from a role -based to a skills-first organization with the launch of unBound, our skills and talent platform, enabling every Firstsource employee to build a unique skill profile to support internal mobility, targeted development, and future work post -planning. items.statement: Completed rights issue raising INR 49.42 crores

items.quote: Approval for an overseas fundraiser of up to 70 million for bond issue, including exchanging some of the current pending resolution bonds and an increase in borrowing to INR 1,500 crores to provide additional financial headroom for growth.

items.quote: To invest up to 20% equity in EverOn Power, which has about 19 megawatt operating renewable energy assets and project EPC capabilities amounting up to INR57 crores, to make it an associate company which will help us to capture their turnover as well as the profits for the consolidation -- in the consolidated results for the future growth.

items.quote: A proposal to invest up to 10 lakhs in Nova Power Private Limited to make it a subsidiary through which we plan to implement the 4-megawatt solar project by involving the customer for a long-term PPA tie-up.

items.quote: So, that our first goal is how soon we reach the EPS beyond one. So, we are at 0.5, 0.6 level EPS now. So, we want to shareholder to really see that full value.

items.statement: Long-term demand for clean and reliable power remains supportive
items.quote: The operating environment for renewable energy continues to remain supportive, and we are encouraged by the long-term demand for clean and reliable power.

items.quote: For Q3 of 2026, our consolidated revenue stood at INR6.19 crores compared to INR5.89 crores in Q3 of 2025, reflecting growth of about 5%. The company has returned to profit by reporting a PAT of INR0.35 crores during the quarter under review as compared to a loss in Q3 of 2025

items.quote: The Tamil Nadu government has now announced repowering, refurbishing and solar hybrid policy rules guideline.

items.quote: And we are also planning something more new area like a capacitor, the battery storage, which will help us to store some energy and then keep doing it.
