items.quote: Overall, gross profit margin improved by 20 basis points quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Repeat visit gap reduced by ~10% (e.g., 100 to 90 days); new customers repeating well
items.quote: The time gap between repeat visits has improved by around 10%. If it was, say, 100 days earlier, now it's 90 days.

items.statement: 53% of overall dine-in transactions now through own digital channels (app/web)
items.quote: Overall, pre-Ind AS restaurant operating margin stood at 14.6%, while the matured portfolio delivered higher margins of 16%, reflecting the aligned strength of our core business.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR80 crores from INR90 crores; INR10 crores cash generation in Q3 net of capex
items.quote: Our net debt, if you remember, last quarter was around INR90 crores. This has actually come down this quarter. We are around INR80 crores.

items.statement: Barbeque India mature restaurant operating margin target raised from 16% to 18% then 21%
items.quote: We have delivered around 16% matured restaurant op erating margin. I'm talking about Barbeque India. At a group level, we have done around 17%. The endeavor is to increase it by 2 percentage points

items.statement: Q3 FY26 Service EBITDA reached Rs 421 crore at 15.1% margin; Express margin at 18.1%, PTL at 11%, SCS improved to 13% from 2.1% YoY.
items.quote: Total service EBITDA is at about 421 crores, which translates to about 15.1%. In transportation, we've maintained that we want to get to a 16% to 18% goal. You'll see that in Express, we've gotten to 18.1%. And in PTL, we've expanded our margins to about 11%.

items.statement: 9M FY26 Service EBITDA crossed Rs 1,000 crore milestone for the first time.
items.quote: And the highest ever Service EBITDA we've seen of 1,053 crores and a PAT of about 260 crores.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA for Q3 FY26 was Rs 147 crore, nearly matching full FY25 Adjusted EBITDA.
items.quote: The Adjusted EBITDA came in at about 147 crores. It's been a very efficient quarter. We've clogged in this much EBITDA all of last year. And in this quarter alone, we've gotten about 147 crores.

items.statement: PAT before Ecom integration costs was Rs 110 crore (3.8%); after integration costs Rs 40 crore.
items.quote: PAT profitability is at 110 crores before Ecom integration costs. And even after the integration costs, it's about 40 crores.

items.statement: Express parcel volumes hit record 295 million shipments in Q3 FY26, up 43% YoY; PTL volumes crossed 500k metric tons, up 23% YoY.
items.quote: If you look at the business highlights, it's been a record festive season with about 295 million express parcel shipments. Driven by strong share -of-wallet gains across clients. PTL has also crossed 500k metric tons, another record.

items.statement: 9M FY26 volumes reached 748 million express parcels and 1.44 million metric tons PTL freight.
items.quote: If you look to the right side, as we add all of these numbers and the first half results, it comes to 748 million express parcel shipments in 9 months to date. And about 1,442,000 metric tons of PTL freight.

items.statement: Express network has stably operated at 22-23% margins historically; management sees no reason margins cannot rise if pricing holds, but cautions service quality may suffer beyond that range.
items.quote: The network has stably operated up to, you know, 22-23% margins as well in the past. Beyond that, of course, we can expand margins, but that usually comes at the cost of some service quality in some locations.

items.statement: Capex expected to decline to 4-4.4% of revenue over medium term (7-10 quarters); near-term phasing may shift between quarters but trajectory unchanged.
items.quote: We continue to expect that Capex will decline down to the sort of, you k now, 4% to 4.3%, 4.4% of revenue over the not so medium term. Perhaps maybe even seven, eight quarters out, ten quarters out, we should be starting to hit those kinds of

items.statement: New business investments (Delhivery Direct, rapid commerce) estimated at Rs 60-80 crore for next fiscal year; Delhivery International profitable from launch.
items.quote: So net net in terms of new businesses, I think it's safe to assume somewhere in our sort of 60 to 80 crore kind of range that we will invest next fiscal.

items.statement: Delhivery maintains pricing pressure on competitors; competitors lack incremental margins at current yields; dynamic/utilization-based pricing being developed to offer lane-specific discounts while improving profitability.
items.quote: We are the pricing pressure in this market and we will continue to maintain pricing pressure on competition in this market, as we've said in the past. You know, we will retain yields where they are.

items.statement: PTL revenue growth (25% YoY) exceeded volume growth (23% YoY), indicating continued yield improvement.
items.quote: Revenue growth is at 25% YoY. Volume growth is at 23% YoY. So revenue growth surpasses volume growth, which is indicative of the continued yield improvement efforts of the team.

items.statement: SCS won key contracts: pan-India redesign for a large engineering company and supply chain redesign for a flagship luxury home and lifestyle brand.
items.quote: We are starting off with one of India's largest engineering companies and a flagship luxury home and lifestyle brand in SCS.

items.statement: Express client concentration remains very low; volumes spread across D2C, SME, and channel partners; not dependent on any single customer strategy.
items.quote: And within our Express business, actually, we have a very sort of spread out set of volumes. And so our ability to grow, our ability to perform as a business is not dependent on any customer's individual strategy.

items.statement: SCS has a healthy pipeline and clear plan to accelerate top-line growth after margin-focused restructuring; new mandates starting implementation this quarter.
items.quote: But as we enter this quarter, the good news is that with all the profit actions in place, we now have new mandates as well that we are st arting to implement this quarter. And we have a very healthy pipeline to convert

items.statement: Mid-mile capex driven by PTL, not e-commerce; vehicle-related capex (LNG trucks, tractor-trailers) and potential sixth mega gateway in Noida (not imminent); sorter capex minimal as equipment acquired via Ecom Express.
items.quote: Really, the mid-mile Capex gets determined by PTL as opposed to, you know, anything to do with e-commerce. There'll be some minor sortation Capex here and there, but nothing very much large overall.

items.statement: PTL salesforce expanded to ~60 locations from 6 major ones two quarters ago; new teams fully trained and on ground, expected to accelerate new client acquisition in Q4 FY26 and FY27.
items.quote: We are now in, I think, whatever, about 60 odd locations compared to, you know, maybe six big locations that we were in two quarters ago.

items.statement: Network utilization higher across facilities and haulage; technology-driven productivity gains (e.g., auto-docking saving 20-30 mins per truck) contributing to margin expansion.
items.quote: It's a complex mathematical problem, but the impact it has is, you know, something like 20 minutes to 30 minutes per truck that shows up. But when you're transacting, you know, thousands of trucks across the entire network, you're saving several man hours of time.

items.statement: Launched Delhivery Direct (intra-city on-demand) in Mumbai and Hyderabad; launched Delhivery International (air economy for SMEs) via FedEx/Aramex partnerships.
items.quote: Delhivery Direct, we've extended our on -demand intra-city service to two new cities, Mumbai and Hyderabad. And we've launched an air economy product, which our SME customers can benefit from, which is Delhivery International.

items.statement: Scaled SaaS footprint with TransportOne; launched Freight Index One; completed first autonomous VTOL drone field mission (12 km medical delivery in UP in 12 minutes).
items.quote: We've scaled our SaaS footprint with TransportOne. We've launched Freight Index One, which is an industry first for us. And we've successfully completed our first field mission with autonomous VTOL drones.

items.statement: Ecom Express integration costs tracking at ~Rs 150 crore vs initial Rs 300 crore estimate; facilities shut earlier than planned and some integrated into network faster due to sustained volumes.
items.quote: We have been able to shut down facilities earlier than originally thought. We have been able to also because we've sustained volumes, be able to integrate some facilities into our network, you know, more quickly than we'd originally anticipated.

items.statement: Board reconstitution: Deepak Kapoor (Chairman since 2018) and Saugata Gupta stepping down after 8 years; management thanked them for governance, controls, and public listing contributions.
items.quote: I would like to place on record on behalf of Delhivery's Management Team, Board and shareholders, our deepest gratitude to Mr. Dee pak Kapoor and Mr. Saugata Gupta, who will be stepping away from their roles on the Board of Delhivery.

items.statement: Management not concerned about sustainability of margins or volumes despite large e-commerce customer captive logistics recovery talk; asserts cost structure advantage is structural and client concentration is low.
items.quote: Our margins are sustainable. They do not depend on variations in volume. You can go back from the day that we went public to today. We have maintained that express margins will remain in the 16 -18% range.

items.statement: Express parcel volume growth 43% YoY vs estimated market growth of 15-18%, implying significant share-of-wallet gains.
items.quote: Best estimates are that e-commerce volume growth, you know, GMV growth obviously may have been slightly higher if Fl ipkart sold more mobile phones. But other than that, you know, broadly speaking, volume growth would have been in that 15-18% kind of range.

items.statement: PTL margin target 16%+; current 11% with clear path via network utilization, service center fill-up, truck fill-up, and contract repricing cadence.
items.quote: PTL is in good double digits and diligently marching to the 16+% goal that we spoke about.

items.statement: Management states comfortable on working capital and cash reserves; disciplined investment in new businesses.
items.quote: We've been disciplined in investments in new businesses and comfortable on working capital and cash reserves.

items.statement: Free cash flow breakeven expected at ~6% Adjusted EBITDA margin; CapEx steady state ~4.5% of revenue; working capital at 15 days
items.quote: at about 6% we will be free cash flow breakeven. The math is simple. The CapEx will be in the 5% zip code area. So maybe 4.5% is what we have said in the steady state. Our working capital is already down to 15 days.

items.statement: PTL volume growth guidance of 15-20% long-term average; near-term quarters may vary 17-23%
items.quote: we'll continue to stick to our guidance wherein in a longer run, you can expect a ballpark 20% growth to play out. Now, for a few quarters, it might go down to 17%, 18%, 19%. For a few quarters, you'll see 21%, 22%, 23%.

items.statement: Corporate overheads expected to settle in 6-7% of revenue range from current 9.1%
items.quote: We have said we expect this to settle in the 6, 6.5%, you know, maybe up to in the sort of more short term, 6-7% kind of range.

items.statement: Service EBITDA margin target 16-18% over next three years; corporate costs to ~7%; overall Adjusted EBITDA 10-11%
items.quote: We have always maintained that our business can generate about 16 to 18% kind of service EBITDA margin over the next three years. Alongside that, our corporate costs are expected to also come down to about 7% kind of levels. So that gives us about 10 to 11% types of overall Adjusted EBITDA margins.

items.statement: ROIC target 25-30% on tangible assets (ex-cash, ex-ROU) at steady state
items.quote: the short answer, we think our business can generate 25 to 30% kind of ROICs. First, one important clarification. When I talk about ROICs, I talk about ROICs on our tangible assets. This does not include cash or ROU assets.

items.statement: CapEx as % of revenue not increasing; decline may be slower due to earlier vehicular capex (LNG trucks/tractor trains) for anticipated volumes
items.quote: We continue to believe that capex will get down to the levels that we'd spoken about. We're not saying that we're going to go from, you know, 5% of revenue to 6% of revenue next year. That's not going to happen.

items.statement: Express CapEx not significant; Ecom Express sorters being deployed; PTL facility relocations only
items.quote: Express capex will not be significant. In fact, even for PTL, we don't really anticipate a very large amount of facility capex. There are some facilities that we need to relocate. Those will happen.

items.statement: PTL margins to continue improving with volume; Q3 margin ~11% suppressed by excess infrastructure built early for e-commerce peak
items.quote: PTL margins normatively actually would have been a little higher than the 11% that you're seeing over here. So there's no particular reason that I can see for us to worry about whether PTL margins can expand past 11%.

items.statement: Supply Chain Services margins at 13% with no cap; accounts delivering 30%+ EBITDA; potential to improve via inventory reduction for clients
items.quote: We're already at 13%. We are nowhere near the full potential margins of this business. What will they be exactly? I'm not really sure. It depends on how much inefficiency we can strip out of various people's supply chains.

items.statement: Express parcel margin levers: DC utilization (800 to 1,100 pkgs/day), infrastructure consolidation (Pune, Delhi NCR), claim rate reduction (30-40 bps), D2C heavy volume growth, dynamic pricing
items.quote: There are these maybe three, four different steps that inch the margin up from wherever with 18.2, 18.3% that we're at towards the 20%.

items.statement: Express parcel volume growth 15-20% long-term; insourcing by e-commerce players viewed as unprofitable and unlikely to sustain
items.quote: If insourcing goes up, you know, as you've seen insourcing went down in the last two quarters. Now, as we have been saying, that makes sense. You know, networks are becoming more complex. They're becoming more difficult to run. They do not have cost advantages.

items.statement: DC capacity utilization rising: currently ~800 pkgs/day per DC vs theoretical ~1,100; sorters and infrastructure consolidation to add margin
items.quote: Now, our DCs theoretically have a capacity to go a little beyond that. They can probably get to about 1,100 or so. We used to be in sort of the 550-600 kind of range. Now we're at about 800. We can get to about 1,100.

items.statement: Dynamic pricing systems in development (lane, time, destination, weight indexed); not yet live due to real-time complexity
items.quote: We are starting to develop those systems. Why they are not live as yet is because these systems are fairly complicated to run in almost real time, and if you don't do it in real time, then it has no meaning.

items.statement: Working capital at 15 days; ~1% of revenue increase needed for 15-20% revenue growth
items.quote: Our working capital is already down to 15 days. So that would roughly mean that about 1% of working capital increase for the 15 to 20% kind of revenue growth rate.

items.statement: ROU assets excluded from ROIC calculation as no capital tied up; leases exitable anytime
items.quote: ROU assets is an accounting entry or our long-term leases, we actually do not have any capital tied up on our ROU assets. We can exit any of those leases anytime.

items.statement: Ecom Express integration costs tracking below forecast: Q2 ₹90 Cr, Q3 ₹35 Cr, Q4 ~₹25-30 Cr; total ~₹150-160 Cr vs original ₹300 Cr
items.quote: I think we had 90 crores in integration costs last quarter. We are at 35 in this quarter. And I think the guidance that Vivek has put out for the next quarter, maybe about 25 to 30 crores of residual costs. So net net looks like it'll end up at that sort of 150, 160 kind of range.

items.statement: Competitive intensity reducing; rivals with high client concentration, asset-light models, or no network advantages face capital and operational challenges
items.quote: I think the space for error has shrunk dramatically. I think the private equity strategy of sort of saying we don't mind funding the number four player in this space because somebody has got to be number four is also going to eventually die.

items.statement: Express parcel mix shifted to smaller parcels post Ecom Express acquisition, optically lowering yield but margin per shipment maintained
items.quote: since our acquisition of Ecom Express, our relative share of small parcels as opposed to heavy parcels has gone up, which is why optically it looks like the yield has come down . But again, as I had mentioned, the margin % that we expect

items.statement: D2C heavy volumes growing 40-50% YoY; step-change in yield and profitability for network
items.quote: When I look at our D2C business and the heavy volumes, we've grown, I think, something like 40, 50% a year, which is much faster than anywhere else. It's not a pricing change, but it's a step change in terms of yield for the network.

items.statement: Asset turns target 3x at steady state; capital employed ~40% of revenue (33% gross block + 6-7% working capital)
items.quote: We think we can generate about 3x asset turns in the steady state. This coupled with further tightening of our working capital, it's already down to 15 days, will likely give us about 33% of revenue as our gross block and about 6-7% as our working capital. So about 40% of revenue as capital employed in our business.

items.statement: New labor code for gig workforce implemented; recurring cost impact absorbed; levels playing field as Delhivery already bore compliance burden
items.quote: We're very glad to hear that the Indian government has decided to have a labor code for gig workforce, which places certain compliance burdens on everybody in this industry that for the longest time, Delhivery was one of the few players bearing it.

items.statement: International cross-border shipping launched; profitable from day one; no capex; leverages FedEx/Aramex partnerships and Air India for economy product
items.quote: This is profitable from day one. We've already been carrying packages in December. All of the packages that we've carried are profitable. So this, as I'd mentioned earlier, there's no, you know, capital earmarked towards investing in this business.

items.statement: No plans to enter cold chain; storage-dominated market with limited value add for Delhivery's transport-optimization model
items.quote: Cold chain is a step perhaps too far for us, and the second problem, of course, in cold chain is my understanding could be dated, but from what I remember, the storage market in cold chain is significantly larger than the transportation market.

items.statement: Technology costs up due to server capacity for volume growth and agentic AI deployment across network
items.quote: Given the sharp increase in the network volumes, we have added server capacity. So that's playing a role. But the point to note is that from second quarter to third quarter, despite the 20% increase in volumes, the cost has actually not gone up. The rest of the cost has moved up because we have actually meaningfully stepped up our investments related to AI in our network.

items.statement: Management does not provide revenue guidance for future periods
items.quote: We unfortunately, do not provide any guidance for future numbers

items.statement: Steady-state EBITDA margin target is 24 percent; recent quarters at 18% and 29% are outliers
items.quote: One important point that I keep mentioning in calls you know when steady state margins are 24 percent in the EBITDA level. And if you look at the two numbers in December 24, which is 18 percent and September 25, which is 29 percent. Both are outliers and both are not sustainable. Our target is always about 24 percent of EBITDA.

items.statement: Bonus equity issue announced at 3:1 ratio (three shares for each share held)
items.quote: Bonus ratio is 3 to 1. So every share that you hold, you will get three InfoBeans shares for each.

items.statement: New labour code has no material impact as basic pay already at 50%; gratuity and leave encashment unaffected
items.quote: Thankfully, you know, our basic was already 50%. So, when we did a lot of analysis and calculations and consulted our experts in the industry, we realized that there is no material impact in the company due to this new labour code. Our gratuity liability, leave encashment might stay un-affected our pay structure also needs to be revised to ensure compliance of new labour code.

items.statement: Launched Insane SDV spec-driven development accelerator delivering ~50% speed gain, 50% defect reduction, up to 50% dev day savings
items.quote: Last week, we launched what we call Insane SDV, it's a spec-driven development accelerator, essentially inspired from Tesla's Insane mode, if any of you have experienced Tesla's Insane mode drive, it goes from 0 to 60 in about 1.9 seconds. That's the kind of inspiration that we have taken and essentially enabling our customers to now achieve that kind of development with roughly 50% gain in speed,

items.statement: Expona 2.0 with Graph RAG and live RAG launching next week for rapid deployment on public or private cloud
items.quote: Next week, you will see unveiling of Expona 2.0, which will enable anybody out there in the world to deploy Expona in their own environment.

items.statement: BeanTrail enhanced with AI agent, pending Salesforce approval for deployment on Agent Exchange
items.quote: BeanTrail has been an existing product of ours on the Salesforce side with roughly 40,000 licenses that are already sold. We have enhanced BeanTrail with the AI agent and pending Salesforce approval, it will be deployed on Salesforce's agent exchange.

items.statement: Revenue grew 38% YoY and 6% QoQ in Q3 FY26; USD revenue grew 30% YoY
items.quote: Coming on to the snapshot of October to December quarter, December 25 to December 24, it was a signiﬁcant jump in revenue of 38 percent, EBITDA shoot up by 89 and PAT by 173 percent. And quarter on quarter we still had good growth in terms of revenue, 6 percent growth

items.statement: EBITDA dropped 6% QoQ and PAT dropped 15% QoQ due to October appraisals, 77 net hires, and continued investment in sales and AI
items.quote: Here we look at the expenses side, we have increased the expenses, you know publicly I mentioned in the last quarter as well. We had appraisals sitting in October, so that impact is showing a plus, you know if you notice we hired net addition in the company was more than 77 people in the last quarter, which also added to the cost. Then we are investing in sales continuously and in the AI efforts.

items.statement: Net headcount addition of 77 employees in Q3 FY26; total headcount 1,600
items.quote: if you notice we hired net addition in the company was more than 77 people in the last quarter, which also added to the cost.

items.statement: Continued investment in sales teams (6+ hires in US) and AI efforts including accelerators
items.quote: we have been investing more often here now in that geography to ensure that we rebuild the momentum that we lost because of, you know, all the, you know, all the situation in the region. So, yes, that's an investment that's going on.

items.statement: Revenue mix: 55% US, 33% Europe, 7% Middle East, 5% India and others
items.quote: A quick revenue breakup by geography, which means 50 percent, 55 percent market share of US geography 33 percent from the European market, 7 percent from the Middle East, and 5 percent from India and other

items.statement: Nine-month revenue Rs 392 crore, EBITDA Rs 104 crore, PAT Rs 65 crore, cash and equivalents Rs 319 crore including Rs 108 crore receivables
items.value: 392 cr revenue, 104 cr EBITDA, 65 cr PAT, 319 cr cash
items.quote: Nine months' ﬁnancials on a middle row, as you see. We have 392 crores of revenue, EBITDA has touched 104 crore, PAT 65 crore, and 319 crores of cash and cash equivalent that includes account receivables, which is mostly good, of about 108 crores

items.statement: InfoBeans Cloudtech merger in process; standalone only covers India business
items.quote: From a business point of view, I think this is pretty irrelevant by the way, because InfoBeans Cloudtech is already in the process of merging with InfoBeans. So, it is not a big question of the total revenue of ICL

items.statement: Client concentration risk acknowledged; target to keep single client below 25% of revenue
items.quote: We deﬁnitely want to not have more than 25% from one single client. So I think we're still well diversiﬁed and not put all our eggs into one basket

items.statement: Sustainable gross margin expected between 40% to 45% going forward
items.quote: So looking at our current business mix and the plan that we have in the coming quarters, what we believe that our sustainable gross margin should anywhere be between 40% to 45%.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin expanded to 15%, up 280 bps YoY and 383 bps QoQ
items.quote: In quarter 3 FY '26, EBITDA increased by 47% year-on-year and 19% quarter-on-quarter to INR22 crores with EBITDA margin expanding to 15%, an improvement of 280 basis points year-on-year and 383 basis points quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 PAT margin expanded to 7.4%, up 98 bps YoY and 76 bps QoQ
items.quote: In quarter 3 FY '26, Profit after tax grew 38% year-on-year to INR11 crores with PAT margin expanding to 7.4%, up 98 basis points year-on-year and 76 basis points Q-on-Q.

items.statement: Other businesses segment grew 33% YoY in Q3 FY26 and 46% YoY in 9M FY26 driven by hearables, wearables and new client wins
items.quote: Building on this momentum, the other businesses segment maintained a robust growth trajectory, increasing 33% year-on-year to INR101 crores in Q3 FY '26 and 46% year-on-year to INR298 crores in 9 months FY '26.

items.statement: Revenue from outside India rose 57% YoY to INR90 crores in 9M FY26, now 21% of total revenue, led by Middle East
items.quote: Revenue from outside India increased to INR90 crores in 9 months FY '26, up 57% year-on-year and now accounts for roughly 21% of the total revenue achieved despite a slowdown in the U.S. amid tariff uncertainty.

items.statement: Block II civil construction complete, assembly lines arriving, awaiting government approvals; commercial production expected from Q1 FY27
items.quote: It is already -- the construction is finished and the assembly lines are coming in, and we are waiting for some government approvals. I think by end of this coming quarter, it will be finished from Q1 '27, it will be done.

items.statement: Automotive lighting production started this month for 4-5 major customers; volumes initially small but strong pipeline
items.quote: Yes. Yes. We already started -- this month, we have already started delivering the products to all the four, five big customers. So it is taking a very big momentum.

items.statement: Honeywell products approved and order booking started; brands work on planning basis with 3-6 month visibility
items.quote: Yes. We -- they already approved all the products and because there are a lot of certifications and approvals were there. So we got already, and we have started getting the orders also. Orders, order booking, everything is started now.

items.statement: Added 4-5 new brands in ODM lighting; supplying to 150+ brands in India in-store lighting and 50-70 brands in Middle East
items.quote: In fact, we have onboarded 4 to 5 new brands. Again, it's a tedious process, but a lot of hard work has already been done and we have started manufacturing for two or three of them already.

items.statement: Working with 4-5 major brands in hearables/wearables under NDAs; participating in Automechanika for automotive electronics
items.quote: We are working with all. Again, we have signed up NDAs. So we are working -- there are 4 or five major brands in India. We are working all of them -- for all of them.

items.statement: Acquired 88% stake in Gravus Tech to leverage premium lighting distribution expertise via consultants, architects, lighting designers
items.quote: So that is just to leverage the experience and the expertise that they already have in the distribution of high-end lighting products. So very premium lighting products. And this is in line with what we were planning and what we are already doing with some of our new product categories where we are -- again, in the B2B segment, we are working with consultants, architects and that particular segmen

items.statement: Applied for PLI scheme; expect benefit of 4-4.5% (~INR5-6 crores) from next financial year
items.quote: So around 4%, 4.5% amounting to a value of somewhere around INR5 crores to INR6 crores. So that is going to be for the next year.

items.statement: IPO proceeds used for debt repayment completed immediately post-IPO; 83% of IPO funds deployed, on track for full utilization
items.quote: Debt repayment was completed immediately post IPO. Block I is now operational and civil construction for Block II is ready to start operational activities. We have deployed approximately 83% of the IPO funds and remain on track to fully utilize the balance within the committed timeline.

items.statement: Revenue contribution from other businesses segment increased to 70% in Q3 FY26 from 63% in Q3 FY25, and 69% in 9M FY26 from 55% in 9M FY25
items.quote: As a result of these initiatives, revenue contribution from the other businesses segment increased from 70% in Q3 FY '26 from 63% in Q3 FY '25 and to 69% in 9-month FY '26 from 55% in 9-month FY '25, reflecting successful diversification beyond home lighting ODM.

items.statement: Front-loaded strategic expenses currently elevated; expect normalization as scale and economies of scale achieved
items.quote: As we scale up for the next phase of growth, we have front-loaded certain strategic expenses, which are currently elevated. We expect these costs to normalize as we achieve greater scale and realize economies of scale.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 revenue grew 20% YoY to INR146 crores; 9M FY26 revenue grew 15% YoY to INR430 crores
items.quote: Our presentation has been uploaded on the stock exchange, and I hope you have had a chance to look at it. I would like to highlight a few key developments before handing over the call to Mr. Sanjeet Singh for further details. First of all, to begin with business performances in Q3 FY '26, the company continues to diversify its business mix while sustaining strong revenue momentum, delivering 20% y

items.statement: U.S. exports minimal due to tariff uncertainty; existing U.S. inventory being liquidated; hope for improvement via India-Europe FTA
items.quote: So as you know, currently, the tariff situation in the U.S., so our exports from India are very, very minimal as of now to the U.S. market. So whatever contribution has happened to -- from the export unit in India is mainly to the Gulf market.

items.statement: No major new capex planned; focus on reaping benefits from existing investments in automotive, hearables, wearables
items.quote: Right now, we have already done a lot of -- we have to see the fruit what we have invested first. Sanjeet Singh: So now it is time to reap our benefits of what we've been investing

items.statement: Hearables/wearables target 80-85% optimal utilization; automotive target 80-85% optimal utilization at maturity
items.quote: So hearable, wearable should that somewhere around 80% because it's a volume-driven business, 80% to 85%. And again, likewise, for the automotive, it's again volume driven, it's going to be volume driven. And that also, I think it should touch somewhere close to around 80%, 85%.

items.statement: Automotive EBITDA margins expected similar to current consolidated level; will add to overall EBITDA
items.quote: automotive, what I can say is that it's definitely going to be similar to what we are achieving right now on the consolidated level. So it's only going to add up to the EBITDA

items.statement: Standalone company rejig plans to be shared by end of FY26; will not affect consolidated performance
items.quote: But yes, definitely, we are just discussing internally how to rejig and what we are doing, the verticals that we are currently handling. So we'll sort of bring in some new verticals in the standalone companies. And you'll get to know that in -- by the end of the year.

items.statement: Middle East subsidiary expanding from retail in-store lighting to home lighting; Europe entry planned in baby steps over next couple of quarters
items.quote: We are working very strong on that. We are expanding there with the teams and we started with the home lighting in the retail in-store lighting, but now we are expanding to the home lighting it as well there.

items.statement: Gravus Tech acquisition brings experienced team for premium lighting distribution
items.quote: No, it is not that because this is actually a new company with the experienced team. So they are into high-end lighting, indoor and outdoor. So that is how we acquired that company.

items.statement: Cash PAT increased 27% YoY and 3% QoQ to INR19 crores in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Cash PAT increased 27% year-on-year and 3% quarter-on-quarter to INR19 crores.

items.statement: Dombivli hospital to be inaugurated Feb 15, start with 200 beds, expect EBITDA breakeven by end of year 2
items.quote: The hospital is slated to be inaugurated on February 15 and will commence full clinical operations thereafter. In the interest of operational efficiency, we will only begin operating 200 beds in Phase 1 and then ramp up capacity in a phased manner as the occupancy increases.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA drag on consolidated numbers for around next 2 years before Dombivli contributes financially
items.quote: beginning next quarter, you will see a much higher depreciation load than you have seen so far and should also expect an EBITDA drag on the consolidated numbers for around the next 2 years before the new h ospital can start contributing financially

items.statement: Dombivli project completed at capex of roughly INR425 crores for 500-bed structure with 300+ bed fit-outs
items.quote: we were able to complete the entire construction for the 500-bed, fit-outs for over 300 beds and all biomedical equipment installation in just over 24 months and at a capex of roughly INR425 crores.

items.statement: Pune Bibvewadi project in early construction stage, capex incurred so far less than INR50 crores
items.quote: Capex so far, as you can imagine, because it's only excavation and a little bit of basement, which is not very high, but maybe less than INR50 crores so far.

items.statement: Total capex incurred in 9M FY26: Dombivli INR425 crores, Pune INR45 crores, Mira Road not started
items.quote: Dombivli, as I said, INR425 crores is the total that we have spent for the project. Pune, I can see a number of around INR45 crores so far. Mira Road, we have not started.

items.statement: Dombivli 500-bed hospital ready, Phase 1 launch with 200 beds, phased ramp-up as occupancy increases
items.quote: In the interest of operational efficiency, we will only begin operating 200 beds in Phase 1 and then ramp up capacity in a phased manner as the occupancy increases.

items.statement: Pune Bibvewadi construction started, targeting calendar year 2028 launch; Mira Road under regulatory approval
items.quote: The Pune South project construction has kicked off and is progressing well, and the Mira Road project is under regulatory approval process.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin 22.8%, 9M FY26 EBITDA margin 22.8%; PAT impacted by INR6.4 cr one-time Labor Code provision
items.quote: The EBITDA margin is 22.8% in this quarter. The PAT stood at INR42.5 crores, representing a decrease of 18.7% year-on-year and the margin for the quarter is 11.6%.

items.statement: Dombivli to lose money for first 1-2 years, Indore to deliver incremental margins, mature hospitals stable margins
items.quote: Indore is in its growth phase. We should expect slightly incremental margins from Indore over the next couple of years. And Dombivli, as I just said a short while back, should lose money for the first year or 2.

items.statement: Demand remains very high in Thane, Pune, Indore due to population growth and insurance penetration; high-quality supply easily absorbed
items.quote: The population keeps increasing. The insurance penetration keeps increasing in large Indian cities. So on account of both those factors, the demand is still very high. I don't think the supply situation is enough in either of the 3 markets at a high quality.

items.statement: 9M FY26 payer mix: insurance 55.7%, self-pay 43.2%, government schemes 1.1%
items.quote: The payer mix, insurance represents 55.7%; self-payers 43.2% and government schemes at just around 1.1%.

items.statement: Indore ARPOB grew ~15% in past year due to inflation and maturity; mature hospitals ARPOB grows with inflation
items.quote: The ARPOB side, we should have had a growth of, let me see, maybe 15-odd percent, I think, on account of both inflation and this maturity phase.

items.statement: Doctor cost typically 20-25% of revenue, stable in that range over past years
items.quote: typically, the doctor cost varies between 20% and 25% of the top line and we have generally been in that range.

items.statement: Zero doctor attrition; one full-time doctor moved; nurse availability remains national challenge
items.quote: No impact on doctor attrition. We have had one full-time doctor move, so I would call it zero attrition.

items.statement: EU-India trade deal impact uncertain; implementation details and China manufacturing base may limit medical equipment duty savings
items.quote: One is that headlines are different and fine prints and implementation is different. So I would wait to see how it gets implemented and what is in the fine print.

items.statement: No CGHS exposure on P&L; government scheme revenue only 1% from radiation oncology and pediatric cardiac
items.quote: we have just 1% of the revenue coming in from the government scheme. So in our view, that is our social contribution.

items.statement: Dombivli EBITDA drag estimated INR2-3 crores per month average for first year based on past experience
items.quote: our previous hospital experience is first year, something between INR 2 crores to INR 3 crores a month should be the average for the first year.

items.statement: Nurse shortage is national challenge with no magic answer; doctor availability good in large cities but costly in smaller towns
items.quote: nurses is a national challenge, and there is nothing new. It has been a challenge for a long time, not specific to one hospital or one location.

items.statement: Keen to add seventh hospital in Western India; in discussions on opportunities but no announcement yet due to land uncertainties
items.quote: we are keen to do the seventh hospital as well. We remain committed to Western India for now. We are in discussions with a few opportunities currently, but I don't have any announcement to make.

items.statement: No ARPOB target; ARPOB is byproduct of case mix; mature hospitals grow with inflation, new hospitals grow faster initially
items.quote: We do not have any ARPOB target either now or for the future. We think that this ARPOB number is more of a byproduct of what you do.

items.statement: No plans to join common empanelment program; currently nothing under discussion
items.quote: Currently, there is nothing under discussion with Jupiter on common empanelment.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 revenue growth driven almost entirely by ARPOB increase (from ~INR59k to INR66k); ALOS stable at 3.85 vs 3.88
items.quote: ALOS, I don't have -- what I have is last year, ALOS was for 9 months, 3.88. This point in time, it is 3.85. So largely similar. ARPOB was 59,000 plus something, and this time, it is 66,000.

items.statement: Management confident of surpassing 15% revenue CAGR guidance for FY26 and expects to outperform it for the next two years.
items.quote: revenue growth has consistently surpassed our stated guidance of delivering a 15% CAGR, reflecting a sustained momentum across our business and the strength of our underlying growth drivers. Hence, we are confident in surpassing our guidance of 15% for FY '26

items.statement: Pens segment targeting high single-digit growth in FY27.
items.quote: And we have always maintained that going forward also in FY27, we would be targeting high single-digit number in that, because still we feel there is a lot of scope in this category going forward.

items.statement: Creative segment volume growth of 141% in Q3 FY26, similar to previous quarter.
items.quote: But yes, just to answer that question in terms of volume in Creative, the volume growth is as big as 141% if you take volume.

items.statement: Pens own brand volume grew 18% in Q3 and 11% in 9M FY26.
items.quote: And to give you some more insight, if we talk a bout our own brands, the volume has increased by 18% of in 3 months. And when we talk about 9 months, the volume of our own brand sales has gone up by 11

items.statement: Gross margin declined 95 bps YoY to 50.9% in Q3 FY26 due to product mix change.
items.quote: Gross profit margin came in at 50.9%, a decrease of 95 bps year -on-year. While it is closer to the historical range, it decreased mainly due to a change of product mix.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved 80 bps YoY to 17.9% in Q3 FY26 on operating leverage.
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 17.9%, an increase of 80 bps year -on-year. As we see the operating leverage kicking in, the incremental growth in translating more directly into EBITDA.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to gradually improve as economies of scale kick in and new units operationalize.
items.quote: the EBITDA margin will gradually g o up as economies of scale s kick in and once new units are fully operationalized

items.statement: Creative revenue grew 71.8% YoY to INR 211 cr in 9M FY26; Steel Bottles & Houseware grew 102.2% to INR 64 cr.
items.quote: The Creative division grew 71.8% year-on-year to INR 211 crores in 9-month FY '26, while the Steel Bottles and Houseware segment rose to 102.2% year-on-year to INR 64 crores.

items.statement: Valsad facility partially operational in Q4 FY26, fully by Q1 FY27; Flomaxe Surat CAPEX INR 9.6 cr in 9M FY26 plus INR 8.28 cr for new building completing Q1 FY27.
items.quote: On CAPEX and expansion initiatives, the new Valsad facility is slated to become partially operational in Q4, which will further strengthen our manufacturing capacity in writing instruments and stationery. At our Flomaxe Surat facility, the total CAPEX as of 9-month FY '26 stands at INR 9.6 crores, primarily directed t owards plant and machinery, and the subsidiary continues to contribute positivel

items.statement: FY26 CAPEX around INR 80-90 cr, ~INR 60-65 cr spent; post Valsad commissioning, only maintenance CAPEX and mould investments planned.
items.quote: So, with the commissioning of the Valsad unit, our IPO proceeds commitment would be over by then. And then we will look towards only the maintenance CAPEX and the investment in the moulds for launching new products. So, there won't be any major manufacturing facility being added, until these are fully utilized.

items.statement: Launched 28 new products in Q3 FY26; Creative portfolio at 240 SKUs as of Dec 31, 2025.
items.quote: During the quarter, we expanded our portfolio by introducing 28 new produ cts across all range and categories. As on December 31, 2025, we have a total of 240 product offerings in Creatives.

items.statement: Steel Bottles portfolio expanded to 50+ SKUs with continuous new launches.
items.quote: In Steel Bottles & Houseware segment, we are driving growth through design innovations with in-house lacquering and coloring, strong general trade distribution network, supported by modern retail, quick commerce and e -commerce with a dedicated distribution team and expanding our portfolio to 50 -plus SKUs with continuous new launches to meet all seas on demands.

items.statement: Domestic OEM relationships reduced to zero; new Flomaxe subsidiary added INR 6 cr domestic OEM revenue.
items.quote: With respect to the domestic OEM business, our earlier OEM relationships have reduced to zero, as indicated in the previous calls. Despite this, we have exceeded our stated growth targets, even though performance was moderated by the domestic OEM segment, as highlighted earlier. We are also pleased to report that new customer engagements through our Flomaxe subsidiary have added a fresh revenue st

items.statement: Export own brand grew 29.9% YoY in Q3, 28.8% in 9M FY26; OEM exports up 22.4% in Q3, 22.6% in 9M.
items.quote: Overall for the quarter, our total own brand sales grew by 23.3% year-on-year to INR 286 crores, of which the domestic own brand sales grew by 22.5% and export own brand s grew by 29.9%. This quarter's strong performance in the export sales was also supported by growth in OEM exports by 22.4%, bringing the overall export growth to a healthy 26.5%.

items.statement: US tariffs no impact (only 3% of topline); EU FTA expected to boost exports to Europe.
items.quote: And to answer your question on the U.S. tariff . U.S. tariffs, see, we were never dependent on U.S. as an export. Overall, if you look at it, it was only 3% of our total top line, but it has not impacted us in any way, U.S. tariffs. And when we talk about EU tariff declaration, see, we are already exporting to European countries. And with the new trade deal, we will definitely gain more momentum i

items.statement: Board approved interim dividend of INR 0.50 per share (10% of face value).
items.quote: In line with our strong performance and positive outlook, the Board of Directors has approved an interim dividend of INR 0.50 per share, representing 10% of face value of our equity shares.

items.statement: Exploring inorganic acquisition opportunities in fast-growing segments.
items.quote: Having operationalized the Flomaxe JV in this year and Maped partnership starting to contribute to revenue, we are also exploring opportunities for inorganic acquisition in the fast -growing segments of our business.

items.statement: Promoter stake to be pared to 75% by November 2025 calendar year end.
items.quote: Well, by the guidelines, we have time till November end of this calendar year.

items.statement: Pen realization stable at INR 5.4 per piece.
items.quote: It's stable. It's stable at INR 5.4 per piece.

That is of Creative, which is 72% up than last year. And when we talk about the H ousehold category and Steel Bottle category, primary number is at INR 25 crores in Q3, and 9-months number is at INR 64 crores, which is 102% up than what we did last

items.statement: Mass category volume growth offsetting premiumization, keeping overall pen realization flat.
items.quote: So, more or less, if you look at the numbers, see, when we talk about premiumization, of course, we have a big share of premium product range and mid -premium product range. But yes, the volumes in mass category is increasing at a rapid speed, which when we look at the overall numbers, it looks at the overall realization is same.

items.statement: Secondary sales at par with primary as distributors hold 45-60 days stock.
items.quote: So, more or less, if you say, when we talk about the secondary sales is at par with the primary sales, because the distributors or the super stockers would keep stock of maximum 45 days to 60 days. They will not invest in a company more than that. So, the secondary sales is also at par with the primary numbers.

items.statement: Flomaxe JV to commence wooden pencil manufacturing and boost polymer pencil, eraser, sharpener capacity.
items.quote: In addition, the Flomaxe Stationery JV is expected to c ommence manufacturing of wooden pencils and also significantly boost capacity and sharpen our focus on polymer pencils, erasers, sharpeners and allied categories.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth guided at 18-20%, expects to close at upper end
items.quote: Our 9-month consolidated growth of 22.7% positions us to close the fiscal year at the upper end of a guided range of 18% to 20%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guided at 16.5-17.5%, Q3 at upper end 17.5%
items.quote: The EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at 17.5% at the upper end of our guided range of 16.5% to 17.5%.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth target 18-20%, similar to FY26
items.quote: we'll continue the current growth momentum and target to achieve a sales growth of 18% to 20%.

items.statement: FY26 capex expected to cross INR250 cr, FY27 target INR225-250 cr
items.quote: We believe a similar sort of investment will be done in the next financial year with that capex investment target between INR225 crores to INR250 crores.

items.statement: Wooden pencil capacity to increase from 5.53M to 8M over next couple of years
items.quote: Our target to increase the capacity of our wooden pencil is from about 5.8 million that we have -- sorry, 5.53 million that we have currently to about 8 million going in the next couple of years.

items.statement: Export growth >15% over 9 months despite US tariffs, driven by Nepal, Sri Lanka, Middle East, Africa and FILA distribution to Chile, Mexico, Canada, Europe, Turkey, South Africa, Australia
items.quote: On the export front, despite headwinds in the U.S. market due to higher tariffs, we are pleased to report a double-digit growth of more than 15% over the 9-month period.

items.statement: Q3 consolidated EBITDA INR103.4 cr, up 17.7% YoY, margin 17.5%
items.quote: The consolidated EBITDA for Q3 FY'26 grew by 17.7% surpassing the INR100 crores mark and stood at INR103.4 crores as compared to INR87.9 crores in Q3 FY'25.

items.statement: Uniclan Q3 EBITDA margin 12% due to seasonality, full-year expected 8-9%
items.quote: at a same level, we think this business will do about 8% to 9% annual margin.

items.statement: Input costs flat/lower in Q3 but trending up; expect neutral full-year impact; will decide on price hikes after 1.5 months if sustained
items.quote: During the quarter under consideration, input costs for most goods had remained constant or were lower, especially for key raw materials like polymers, waxes, etc., providing a positive impact to our margins. However, with prices now trending upwards, we expect a neutral impact on our full year results.

items.statement: Office supplies growth driven by pen capacity ramp-up; focus on INR5 pen segment, expanding INR10 portfolio; no move beyond INR10 yet
items.quote: In terms of focus, we still continue to focus primarily on the INR5 pen segment and with expanding our portfolio in the INR10 segment also. So mix-wise we are still similar to what we were earlier.

items.statement: Uniclan: >90% sales from diapers, wipes building up (launched 72-count and 30-count packs); diaper remains core focus
items.quote: So more than 90% of the sales is still diapers. Wipes is something which is still building up.

items.statement: Domestic demand >85% of sales; export growth via FILA distribution to new geographies
items.quote: Geographically, our revenue growth continues to be anchored by strong domestic demand, which has grown to represent more than 85% of overall sales.

items.statement: Pencil market share ~35% currently, targeting ~45% with new capacities
items.quote: it would be fair to assume that we'll be especially in the pencil segment upwards of about 35%. And with the new capacities coming in, we'll be close to about 45% of the market share.

items.statement: SKIDO: invested INR1.02 cr (DOMS share), 9M sales INR9.5 cr; total investment ~INR2 cr; mass market focus via DOMS distribution
items.quote: Till now, we've invested about INR1.02 crores in SKIDO. And for the 9 months ended 31st December, we generated a sale of about INR9.5 crores in this business.

items.statement: Uniclan (Wowper): FY25 sales ~INR160 cr, FY26 target ~INR200 cr; launched flat diapers via OEM
items.quote: When we invested in this company last year, they closed last full financial year at INR160-odd crores. This year, we are targeting to close -- at close to INR200 crores.

items.statement: STPL (paper stationery): acquired recently; first back-to-school season with DOMS; backward integration (printing line) near completion
items.quote: STPL, Super Treads is something which we have invested very recently and this is now the first back-to-school season where we'll participate through them also.

items.statement: Granted 137,690 ESOPs to 1,000+ employees in Oct 2024 (ESOP 2023 scheme); in addition to CTC; same vesting as prior grants
items.quote: This year from the same pool, we granted about 137,000 plus of ESOPs to 1,000-plus employees. So basically, the vesting period and time frame remains the same. This is in addition to their current CTCs.

items.statement: Commodity price volatility (polymers, waxes) rising; waiting 1.5 months to assess sustainability before price hikes; may impact margins in current quarter
items.quote: There has -- the volatility has also increased. But as a company right now, we are just waiting and watching whether these are sustainable or if these are something which are like a temporary phenomenon.

items.statement: Scholastic stationery, art & kits/combos combined grew 11.5% YoY in Q3; wooden pencil capacity expansion key driver for FY28
items.quote: overall, when we see all these 3 categories put together, we've grown by about 11.5%.

items.statement: Jammu land acquired for INR16 cr (2.5+ acres, 50k sq ft built-up) for wooden slat processing and fine art products
items.quote: So Mosam, we paid about INR16 crores for acquisition of land, building and certain electrical fittings, which will be of the use to the company.

items.statement: Capex projected to reach $1.2 billion by next year with a $5 billion roadmap by 2030, financed via internal accruals and disciplined debt, maintaining 0.6x debt gearing and max 3.5x EBITDA leverage
items.quote: Now, by next year, our aggregate capital expenditure is projected to reach $1.2 billion. And in line with our long-term vision, we have charted a capex roadmap of approximately $5 billion to be achieved by 2030.

items.quote: Work is underway to add an additional 318,100 cubic meters of liquid capacity and 77,236 metric tons of LPG capacity, marking a significant expansion. Alongside this, construction of an -- there is construction of an LPG bottling plant with an annual capacity of 35,000 metric tons, so that's also in progress. The overall project, which involves a capital expenditure of INR1,675 crores, is advancin

items.quote: We intend to spend around another INR500 crores on the liquid assets at Kandla, Mangalore, Kochi, in fact more. So you see, we are well geared to reach a capex of INR10,000 crores by the time we end FY27. We'll double the capex.

items.statement: Liquid capacity expected to reach 2.5 million cubic meters plus by FY27 end from current 1.7 million via expansions at JNPA, Kandla, Mangalore, Kochi, Haldia
items.quote: So, you know that we are expanding at Kandla around 100,000, and then we are also expanding at Mangalore, as well as Kochi, as well as Haldia, which is 60-60-50, that is around 200,000 further. And we are also doing 318,000 at JNPA. We are at 1.7 million. So, I think we should be around 2.5 million plus by FY27 end.

items.statement: Pricing based on industry benchmarks; no trading margins; revenue purely from tolling/throughput fees; infrastructure cost advantage from in-house development drives high ROCE
items.quote: These are industry benchmark. So we follow the industry benchmark and charge the same. Because as my parent is the infrastructure developer, we have a unique advantage of getting the infrastructure in quickest time and cheapest. So being an infrastructure business, we are much more at an advantage than anyone else because it is our in-house infrastructure development, which gives us this benefit.

items.statement: EU-India trade agreement may boost specialty chemical exports over 6-9 months, benefiting terminal demand indirectly
items.quote: I think specialty chemicals export now being the duty being reduced probably to zero. As and when it is implemented, it's still some time away. The agreements are not yet in operation. They may take 6, 9 months. But I think it will help because there will be more exports of specialty chemicals to Europe. And port terminals would definitely be required for that rush.

items.quote: We have signed an 8 lakh square feet of single managed office space contract in Ahmedabad, which is on Ambli - Bopal Road. That's the same micro market, wherein we have a current standing of three and a half lakh square feet.

items.quote: We are committing an investment of INR 100 crores across four years and an occupancy of 85%. It will start generating a revenue of INR120 crores.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin reached 61% in 9M FY26, up from 57.5% YoY; consolidated EBITDA margin 46.1%
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin increased to the highest level in the industry, which is 61 percentage, up from 57.5 percentage in the same period last year.

items.statement: New 3.15 lakh sq ft Capital One center expected to operate at 60-65% margin initially due to rent-free period, stabilizing at 30-35% center-level margin
items.quote: At the center level, typically we operate at 30%-35% margin. For the first few months, this center would be operating at 60%-65% margin because of the rent fee availability there.

items.statement: 95% pre-leasing achieved at 3.15 lakh sq ft Capital One center before operations; 50% pre-leasing at Pune center before fit-out start
items.quote: We have already achieved 95% pre-leasing even before going operational. This is technically not heard of because this size typically takes anywhere between 9 to 12 months to reach a 95% occupancy.

items.statement: One-time other expenses increased >100% in standalone due to post-IPO processing costs
items.quote: No, these are one-off expenses, one-time expenditures that were incurred post the IPO processing.

items.statement: Development management model: charge INR 400-600/sq ft for project monitoring expertise; landowner bears capex; DevX takes operational lease
items.quote: For doing this, the revenue that we will charge them is anywhere between INR400 to INR600 per square feet.

items.statement: Design & Build subsidiary on track for ~INR 50 crore revenue in FY26 (100% YoY growth for 3 years); 9M FY26 revenue INR 38.8 crore at 16.8% EBITDA margin

items.statement: GCCs drive 60-65% of flexible office demand; Tier 2 cities growing 16% CAGR faster than national average; hiring in Tier 2 growing 21% YoY; GCC share in Tier 2 rose from 5% (FY19) to 20% (FY25)
items.quote: GCCs, as I touched upon earlier, are the single biggest demand driver for flexible office space providers. They contribute anywhere between 60% to 65% of the seat observation annually.

items.statement: Top 10 clients contribute ~40% of revenue; 1/3 clients multi-city; 13,500 seats across 28 centers in 12 cities at 88.4% occupancy
items.quote: The top 10 clients, the question that you asked, the second one, contributes today roughly 40% of our entire revenue.

items.statement: Expect Q4 FY26 to be stronger across verticals, consistent with historical second-half strength
items.quote: Historically, the second half of the year, especially Q4 has tended to be stronger across verticals, and we expect this trend to play out in Q4 FY26.

items.statement: Confident to maintain gross margins in 43% to 45% range, monitoring dollar impact
items.quote: On the overall outlook, we are confident to maintain on a similar range from 43% to 45% gross margins. However, we are also keeping a close eye on the dollar increase and we would see how things move on from here.

items.statement: Gross margin expansion driven by favorable product mix, operational efficiencies, procurement gains, lower import costs, and in-house inlay manufacturing
items.quote: Primarily, we have benefited from the favorable product mix similar to what we had in the last quarter as well. Operational efficiencies have kicked in as volume and scale has grown in this quarter. Another part is where on the procurement initiatives, we were able to source from vendors with favorable payment terms and our overall import costs reduced.

items.statement: Secured multi-year payment solutions contracts with 4 PSU banks and 3 PSU banks for chequebooks/QR kits, total budgeted tender value ~INR 489 crores
items.quote: These multi -year contracts based on volume allocation represent a business potential of approximately INR489 crores for Seshaasai as per the budgeted tender value over the tender period.

items.quote: These multi -year contracts based on the value allocation represent the business potential of approximate ly INR210 crores for Seshaasai as per the budgeted tender value over the contract period.

items.statement: Onboarded 8 new payment card customers across banking, fintechs, forex issuers; strong traction in metal/premium cards
items.quote: In addition to this, we also onboarded eight of the customers for payment cards across banking, fintechs and forex card issuers. We are seeing strong traction in the metal card and premium card segment.

items.statement: Shortlisted by large European fintech for global metal/PVC card supply; submitted bids for domestic payment scheme metal card RFP
items.quote: We have been shortlisted by a large European fintech to supply metal and PVC cards globally. This is a very prestigious account and holds good potential. items.statement: IoT: 6 new wins including largest Indian retail giant (19,000+ stores) for two fashion sub-brands, shortlisted for major RFID rollout
items.quote: Notable among them is a special win for us which is the largest Indian retail giant having more than 19,000 stores for whom we have begun our supplies for two of their fashion sub-brands and shortlisted for their major RFID rollout shortly.

items.statement: Over 200,000 sq ft under construction across 4 locations (Bengaluru, Nagpur, Navi Mumbai, Kundli) for future growth
items.quote: Currently, we have over 200,000 square feet under construction across four locations for our new facilities at Bengaluru, Nagpur, Navi Mumbai and Kundli for our future business growth.
