items.quote: We had successfully doubled our paint protection film capacity to 600 LS F in September '25. The capacity is ramping-up as per the plan. The expansion has enhanced manufacturing efficiencies and unlocked additional capacity headroom for our future growth.

items.statement: New PPF line at 65% utilization; old PPF line running full; sun control lines running at optimal levels
items.quote: New line, I'm talking, it is running at 65% capacity. Old line is running full. But the thing is that is, again, if you really see, we are growing very strong in certain regions, that is Middle East, North Africa, India.

items.statement: Order book remains robust; orders for U.S. market held in bonded warehouses awaiting favorable tariff outcome
items.quote: Our order book continues to remain robust. Despite a 50% tariff, the EBITDA decline has been contained at 7.4% on Y-o-Y basis in Q3 FY '26.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin 18.9%, down 118 bps YoY; contained decline via cost optimization and product mix
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 18.9%, down only 118 bps year -on-year, maintaining a healthy level despite tariff headwinds, which have primarily been driven by cost optimization initiatives.

items.statement: Mitigated ~INR40 cr of ~INR50 cr potential tariff impact in Q3 via efficiency, product mix, and re-export strategies
items.quote: So there has to be a INR50 crores impact on PBT, right, which we did not see. We saw only INR7 crore s to INR8 crore s impact. So we have successfully navigated by our efficient manufacturing process and efficient product mix strategy. And some of the products which we diverted to the territory where it was going to U.S.A. then being diverted to other territories. We have really managed that well

items.statement: Tariff impact split: portion passed to distributors/dealers, portion absorbed via efficiencies and product mix
items.quote: It's a mix of both. I mean we are passing some of it to our distributors, dealers, so which ultimately goes to pass on to consumer, but a very small fraction to end consumer. But some of it is passed on to our distributors and customers. The rest we are observing with our efficiencies, operational efficiencies and product mixes.

items.statement: Q3 product mix: 44% Sun Control, 26% PPF, 30% IPD; high-margin IR films increase in Q4/Q1
items.quote: Yes. So it's 44% Sun Control, 26% PPF and 30% of IPD.

items.statement: Architectural films grew from 10% to 22-23% of consumer product sales; targeting 30% share
items.quote: Yes. So if you see, I mean, we started this architectural journey at around 10% of our total CPD sale, right, which was roughly INR1,500 crores last year, right? So now currently, we are at around 22%, 23% of architectural sales. But with ultimate aim is to reach around 30% of that.

items.statement: UAE subsidiary established to manage MENA trading/exports; two global application studios opened in UAE; targeting 300+ Garware Application Studios in India by end FY26 (250+ already)
items.quote: Recognizing the growth potential in the Middle East market, the company has announced to establish a wholly owned subsidiary in UAE. The new entity will manage trading and exports of films, ceramic coatings and paint protection films across the MENA region and other international markets. We also set up two of its kind global application studio in UAE, and we are in process of onboarding more part

items.statement: Garware Home Solutions launched as D2C e-commerce model for architectural films; first studio in Chembur, Mumbai; plans to expand to all towns
items.quote: In addition, we launched Garware Home Solutions, a new D2C business vertical aimed at expanding our domestic footprint and cater to unmet consumer demand in the architectural film space. We opened our first GHS studio in Chembur in Mumbai. It is in collaboration with a local interior design firm, and we plan to follow the same approach to increase our presence to all towns in India.

items.statement: Exports 74.3% of Q3 revenue; U.S. share ~40% (down from 43-44%); Middle East doubled to 8% of 9M sales; EU stable 10-11%; India ~25%
items.quote: Export continued to form a significant part of our business, contributing 74.3% of total revenues for this quarter.

items.statement: Rupee depreciation benefits exports but ~40% of raw materials are import-parity priced, offsetting part of gain
items.quote: But there is like 40% of that is taken away with our raw materials. So that is the net impact on that.

items.statement: U.S. inventory increased from normal 60-75 days to ~100 days (30-40 extra days in bonded warehouses); production unchanged, only release controlled
items.quote: Right now, if you add everything, so this goes almost, I can say, around 100 days. I mean it's like you can just see 60 days versus 100 days. So there is like 30, 40 days more inventory is lying with us in the warehouse. I mea n, transit remains the same, only in the warehouse inventory has been increased. And that has been done purposefully.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free with INR669 cr cash and liquid investments as of Dec 31, 2025
items.quote: On the balance sheet front, GHFL continues to remain debt -free with a robust cash and liquid investment balance of INR669 crores as on 31st December 2025.

items.statement: 50% U.S. tariff fully impacted Q3; hoping for reduction to 25% via trade deal or Supreme Court action
items.quote: During the quarter, we experienced the full impact of 50% tariff structure. The offtake was calibrated to maintain undisrupted supply chain. Even in this challenging environment, GHFL largely maintained its offtake.

items.statement: High entry barriers: fully backward integrated, 10+ patents, proprietary base film, metallizing, nano dispersion, adhesive and top coat processes developed over 30 years
items.quote: The product which we make, it is made out of very high base films, which is normally available with only few people in the world. And the reason of that is this we are fully backward integrated. That means we make our own base film. We do like metallizing, we do the nano dispersion facility and some preparation on the base films, adhesives and our top coats like surface resistant coa ting and ever

items.statement: Architectural film certifications: GreenPro (only Indian company), GRIHA, American Cancer Foundation, UK/TUV/EN safety standards
items.quote: We are the only company in India to be certified by GreenPro which is government has given that guideline that if you have any building as per the government guidelines, so it is recommended to have a company associated with the GreenPro certification. So we are the only one in India, then we are GRIHA certified. We are certified by American Cancer Foundation to avoid cancer. And we have certified

items.statement: Prepared for long-term 50% tariff scenario; strategies to mitigate impact to be announced shortly
items.quote: Though everyone of us, including our exporters thought it's a short-term phenomenon, but we are prepared for a long-term as well, like that remains, that became stable at 50%. That too will maintain 20-plus margin and with the sales growth of 15% bare minimum at CAGR level.

items.statement: Separate architectural teams built globally; hired top talent from peers in U.S. and Middle East
items.quote: And the last and not the least is the team, which was like earlier, there used to be only one team. Now we have like a separate architectural teams all around the world. That includes in U.S.A., we have a top person from a peer group. He has really done we ll and got some big distributors converted to our brand. Same in Middle East, we are growing and one of the major growth area is architectural

items.statement: Q3 FY26 revenue INR459 cr (-1.6% YoY); 9M FY26 revenue INR1,523 cr (-2.4% YoY); EBITDA INR86.7 cr (-7.4% YoY); PAT INR55.8 cr
items.quote: For Q3 FY '26, our consolidated revenue stood at INR459 crores compared to INR466 crores in Q3 of FY '25, reflecting a 1.6% year-on-year decline, primarily due to the tariff -related disruptions in the key export market. Despite this, exports remained stable at 74%.

items.statement: Near-term soda ash demand is tepid and flat, constrained by weak macroeconomics in Southeast Asia and parts of Asia, with export restrictions impacting the U.S. market.
items.quote: In terms of the demand scenario across geographies, especially for soda ash, demand growth is fairly tepid and flat in the near term, constrained by weak macroeconomic s in a couple of geographies, especially in Southeast Asia and some parts of Asia.

items.statement: Medium-term soda ash demand expected to grow modestly, supported by structural growth in solar glass and stable consumption from other applications.
items.quote: While this is so in the short term, the medium -term soda ash demand is expected to grow modestly, supported by structural growth of solar glass and a stable consumption from other applications.

items.statement: India shows relatively robust demand growth; China and U.S. witness marginal declines and flat demand; other regions in Asia, Americas (ex-U.S.), and Africa see broadly resilient demand.
items.quote: India continues to exhibit relatively robust demand growth, while China and U.S. are witnessing marginal demand declines in some sectors and overall, very flat demand.

items.statement: Soda ash prices remain challenging across most geographies, approaching record lows due to persistent oversupply and muted demand; Indian domestic list prices declined marginally in Q3.
items.quote: In terms of pricing, the soda ash prices remain challenging across most geographies, with prices in certain markets approaching record low levels on persistent oversupply and muted demand.

items.statement: Chinese soda ash prices declined approximately 54% between Q3FY23 and Q3FY26 due to low-cost natural soda ash; current domestic prices around CNY 1,200.
items.quote: Chinese soda ash prices have declined by approximately 54% between Q3FY23 and Q3FY26, primarily due to the low -cost natural soda ash which has come on stream.

items.statement: U.S. domestic soda ash realizations negotiated at par or $5-$10 variation, with about a $5 drop overall.
items.quote: Yes, the US domestic prices which have been negotiated are at par or about $5 to $10 variation, the bulk of them. Overall, I would say that there's been about $5 drop in realizations on the domestic market.

items.statement: U.S. fixed costs increased ~$15 million over 5 years; variable costs up ~$5/tonne; gas settled at much higher price post-COVID; coal cost up ~$5/tonne to ~$55/tonne due to annual escalation and longer haul distances.
items.quote: On a fixed cost basis, which is in dollar terms, if you spread it between 2 elements, the increase in fixed cost over the last 5 years has been broadly about $15 million. On the variable cost, this would vary from the various pricing of coal and gas contracts. But a $5 movement has happened broadly per tonne basis.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue down 1% YoY to INR 3,550 crore; EBITDA INR 345 crore vs INR 434 crore, sharp fall mainly in U.S. due to subdued pricing; PAT before exceptional items negative INR 15 crore vs INR 49 crore.
items.quote: The revenue was about 1% down compared to the previous year, at INR 3,550 crores, despite the fall in prices in the market supported by higher volumes. EBITDA at INR 345 crore s compared to INR 434 crores, mainly on account of subdued pricing across all geographies.

items.statement: Standalone revenue up 3% to INR 1,204 crore; EBITDA up 9% to INR 228 crore on higher volumes and lower fixed cost; PAT before exceptional items INR 87 crore, up 21%.
items.quote: The revenue from operations stood at INR 1,204 crores, up 3% compared to Q3 FY25 due to higher volumes. EBITDA at INR 228 crores in standalone was 9% up from Q3 FY25, effect of also higher volume and lower fixed cost.

items.statement: Board approved INR 515 crore for 210 ktpa iodized salt greenfield facility at Valinokkam, Tamil Nadu, to be commissioned over 36 months.
items.quote: The Board also approved an investment of INR 515 crore for setting up a greenfield facility in this Board meeting with a capacity of 210 kilo tonne per annum capacity of iodized salt in Valinokkam in Tamil Nadu. This facility is expected to be commissioned over the next 36 months.

items.statement: Board approved 50 ktpa precipitated silica expansion at Cuddalore for INR 775 crore and 350 ktpa dense ash plant at Mithapur for INR 135 crore.
items.quote: Board in its meeting on November 21st, 2025, also approved 50 kilo tonne per annum precipitated silica expansion at Cuddalore at an investment of INR 775 crore, and a 350-kilo tonne dense ash plant in Mithapur with an investment of INR 135 crores.

items.statement: Commissioned new L55 line at Mambattu in October 2025 and Pearl grade Silica 3,000 tpa at Cuddalore in December 2025.
items.quote: We also commissioned a new L55 line in Mamba ttu in October 2025. Pearl grade Silica of 3,000 metric tonnes per annum in Cuddalore was commissioned in December 2025.

items.statement: 50 kt electric calciner soda ash plant in Kenya operationalized, to be fully stabilized by March 2026; it is additional capacity with superior low-carbon product.
items.quote: 50 KT electric calciner soda ash plant in Kenya was operationalized and will be fully stabilized by March 2026.

items.statement: Entered share purchase agreement to acquire Novabay Singapore on Dec 19, strengthening position in premium value-added Bi-carb market across UK, Europe, India, ASEAN and Far East.
items.quote: We also announced the acquisition of Novabay Singapore on December 19th, where we entered into a share purchase agreement . This acquisition strengthen s Tata Chemical's position in premium grade value-added Bi-carb market by expanding the geographic footprint, which now extends from UK which serve the European market , India, as well as now the Asian markets, including ASEAN and Far East.

items.statement: U.S. consciously reducing export volumes to Southeast Asia where contracts are below acceptable contribution; may lead to volume decline in coming quarters.
items.quote: While we continue to serve all markets which have held more or less pricing steady . Especially in the Southeast Asian market, we are stopping to take orders which are below our expected number. So, you would see in the coming quarter, us not delivering the volume, sort of going down on the volume because it doesn't make any sense to be selling in those markets at negative contribution.

items.statement: UK turnaround delayed by ~6 months due to snowstorm; fixed cost savings on track, aiming for break-even in Q4 and profitability next year; guided FY26 EBITDA ~INR 250 crore.
items.quote: Yes, as I mentioned, this quarter while we were aiming to get pretty close to that number, we were impacted by a one -off event which led to certain production issues because of the snowstorm they had, which really was not an insurable event in many ways. So, we have had an issue with that piece. But clearly, we are making progress, and the fixed cost savings have come through and part of that jou

items.statement: Capex focused only on India in non-commoditized spaces (salt, bicarbonate, silica, FOS); dense ash expansion at Mithapur is low-cost reconfiguration (INR 135 crore for 350 kt); all projects target returns >16%, aiming ~18%.
items.quote: And even in the commoditized space, if you look at the CAPEX, which are highlighted for dense ash, for 3 50,000 tonnes of dense ash, spending 1 35 crore is a very, very competitive number. It is not an easy number anybody can get to. We have the flexibility to get there because of the resources we have access to. It's also reconfiguration of one of the existing units within Mithapur, which already

items.statement: Operating cash flow negative INR 700 crore for 9MFY26, including INR 350 crore forex impact on debt; sharp reduction in capex spend vs last year, further reduction expected next year.
items.quote: So, this year, for example, if you look at the cash flow for three quarters, it's about INR 700 crores negative at the operating level, of which 350 is forex movement on the debt taken, debt we already have. So, the real number hasn't moved up. But 350, which is additional, is fundamentally a sharp reduction and that has bee n achieved because of sharp reduction in CAPEX expenditure from last year

items.statement: Net debt stands at INR 5,596 crore, excluding lease liability of INR 772 crore.
items.quote: Net debt stands at INR 5,596 crores, excluding a lease of INR 772 crores.

items.statement: Geopolitical risk and tariff uncertainties persist, clouding global demand visibility; economic recovery expected to remain slow, limiting industrial demand resurgence.
items.quote: Geopolitical risk and ongoing tariff uncertainties persist, continuing to cloud global demand visibility. The pace of economic recovery is expected to remain fairly slow in the year ahead, limiting any sharp resurgence in industrial demand.

items.statement: U.S. serving domestic and nearby markets (South America, parts of Far East) for higher realizations; UK internal soda ash demand now met by U.S. operation; India remains net importer needing more capacity.
items.quote: So, for US, the nearby markets tend to be Southern American markets and parts of the Far East, and they would focus on those markets rather than extend themselves beyond that and do as much of a volume in those markets as possible. At the same time, the U.K. has completely withdrawn. So, part of the U.K. demand for internal consumption of soda ash is being met by our U.S. operation.

items.statement: Chinese natural soda ash capacity additions (target 50% natural/50% synthetic) driving oversupply; synthetic plants unprofitable, leading to maintenance shutdowns but new capacity offsets curtailment.
items.quote: And this, in our view, is in line with the target, China has set a target of having 50% synthetic and 50% natural. But the way we see it is that while the new natural capacities have come, the synthetic capacities have to go. So, overall, there will be capacity rationalization which has to happen in China. With the current pricing, most synthetic plants are actually losing , and are not making mon

items.statement: Publication segment revenue expected to grow ~15% in FY27 due to curriculum changes in Maharashtra (4 grades) and Gujarat (2 grades)
items.quote: Overall, with these grades changing, we feel around 15 -odd percentage revenue growth we will achieve in publication segment for FY '27.

items.statement: Domestic stationery business targeting 15-20% growth in FY27 driven by non-paper stationery expansion and new marketing team
items.quote: And with that, overall, both put toge ther, we will see at least 15% to 20% growth in stationery business. That is domestic, I'm only talking about.

items.statement: UAE manufacturing facility capex of ~INR30 crores for machinery, no land/building investment, operational by Q2 FY27
items.quote: So around INR30-odd crores, we are investing ther e. Balance, as I said, partly we are shifting -- additionally, partly we are shifting from India.

items.statement: UAE facility to start with paper and plastic-blended products, settled categories only for first 1.5 years, new categories later
items.quote: paper. Paper and of course, plastic also, not only paper, but plastic. So these are blended products, plastic and paper mix. So these kind of products would be manufactured in UAE, but not the newer categories that we are planning or developing right now to offer to our

items.statement: UAE facility expected revenue INR50-55 crores with 8% EBITDA in FY28, scaling to INR90+ crores with 12% EBITDA in FY29
items.quote: So basis of our calculation today, it would be between INR50 crores to INR55 crores of revenue with around 8% of EBITDA next year. And in the subsequent year, that may figure -- FY '29, I'm saying, it will reach around INR90 -odd crores with the same facilities and EBITDA would be around 12%.

items.statement: Export EBITDA margin dropped from 15-16% to 4-5% due to 10% discount offered to US customers to absorb tariff impact
items.quote: So at present, in exports, we would hav e done around 4% to 5% EBITDA margin versus 15% that we normally generate in exports. So that is the margin difference between the 2 periods.

items.statement: Domestic stationery EBITDA margin compressed to 5-6% from ~10% due to initial costs of non-paper stationery expansion and manpower
items.quote: Domestic also, it has come down to 5%, 6%. And reason I did mention that since we are growing our non -paper stationery business, and we have -- there are initial expenses that we are incurring, including the manpower cost for which -- against which we have not yet received the good revenue.

items.statement: Targeting 20% of domestic stationery revenue from non-paper categories by FY28
items.quote: Yes. FY '28, if you're asking, then we would like to 20% of our revenue -- domestic revenue to come from non-paper stationery.

items.statement: Export realization dropped from INR100 to INR90 per unit due to tariff-related discount, pricing set by international buyers not country-specific
items.quote: At present, we are realizin g INR90 instead of INR100. And this INR90 automatically, whatever our EBITDA was around 15%, 16% in exports, that has come down to 5%.

items.statement: US consumption down 10-15% due to inflation, reducing export volumes; new categories (files, metal, canvas) being added to offset
items.quote: And because of that, the consumption at the U.S. also has gone down by 10% to 15%. Now that is likely to impact our volumes for sure. And therefore, as a strategy, we are developing newer and newer categor ies so that value-wise, at least we match up to what we have been doing so far.

items.statement: US customers assured continued buying but requested 10% discount; new product RFQs on hold due to tariff confusion
items.quote: Immediately, in the week when the new tariffs were announced, proactively, my team sat in front of them physically and did say that we want to continue thi s business with you for very, very long. And for that, we did offer them 10% discount.

items.statement: UAE facility driven by customer demand for country risk diversification, not just tariff resolution; tariff timeline uncertain
items.quote: So it is a country risk mitigation policy that we have adopted. Going forward, the way world is behaving, when what will happen, no one knows. And therefore, in the interest of company, we decided to have operations there.

items.statement: Navneet AI platform built on 110,000+ digital resources for teachers; no separate revenue, aims to drive book/digital sales via teacher adoption
items.quote: India's first custom -made education AI model purely from Indian context has been built by Navneet, which is built on 110,000 -plus trusted digital resources, specifically designed to empower teachers rather than replace them.

items.statement: UAE operations staffed by deputed senior Indian team, local hiring for junior roles; no additional manpower for AI platform
items.quote: So the present senior team of Stationery division, manufacturing division, we have deputed a couple of them from India. So most of the senior staff will be going from India who are quite experienced enough with Navneet itself and the lower level staff, we will appoint there.

items.statement: K12 Techno stake revalued at INR6,550 crore valuation; stake to dilute to ~13% after March funding round; open to partial sale
items.quote: So finally, there is going to be a second round also in March. And post that round -- and of course, it will be valued a little higher than what the figure that I mentioned. But post that, our shareholding will be around 13-odd percentage.

items.statement: Company maintains debt-free balance sheet with significant liquidity
items.quote: On the balance sheet now, we maintain a strong debt -free position with significant liquidity, providing a crucial buffer against current operational challenges and strategic flexibility for future growth initiatives.

items.statement: Tariff resolution timeline unclear; US volume decline 10-15%; EU FDA changes no benefit for paper/plastic-blended products at 0% duty
items.quote: Somehow none of them are able to give us a clear indication as to when this issue of tariff will get resolved. But we believe this issue of tariff cannot go long for very , very long. It has to settle.

items.statement: AUM target INR33,000-34,000 crores for FY26
items.quote: So I think we have said that this year, we will continue to deliver a growth AUM to be in the range of about INR33,000 crores to INR34,000 crores, and we are on that track.

items.statement: AUM target INR43,000-44,000 crores for FY27
items.quote: Next year, we have revised our guidance to deliver anything between about INR43,000 crores to INR44,000 crores.

items.statement: AUM target INR55,000 crores by FY28
items.quote: Earlier, we said that we'll achieve INR50,000 crores AUM by FY '28. Now that guidance we revised to reach to INR55,000 crores by FY '28.

items.statement: ROE target 16%+ and ROA 4-4.25% by FY28
items.quote: Our aim will be to deliver ROE in the range of about 16% plus and ROA anything between 4% to 4.25%.

items.statement: Spread target 7.2% for Q4 FY26
items.quote: I think we've given a guidance of 7.2%, which we hope to deliver that.

items.statement: Gold Loan yield expected to improve 20-25 bps next year
items.quote: Overall, Gold yield is likely to be 18% and our overall yield of the company, which is 16.4% should improve slightly. It should improve by 20 to 25 basis in next year.

items.statement: Plan to add 100-125 branches across Micro LAP, MSME and Home Loan in FY27
items.quote: So next year, we can assume that between 100 and 125 branches across Micro LAP, MSME and Home Loan, we will add.

items.statement: Gold Loan branches at 999 by end of Q3 FY26, added 68 in Q3
items.quote: As far as expansion is concerned, by current quarter, we will be ending up 999 branches of the Gold Loan. And last quarter, you have seen we have added about 68 branches in gold alone.

items.statement: Gold Loan branch expansion in H2 FY27 subject to RBI approval
items.quote: We'll approach the RBI at appropriate time and RBI give their approval and decision within 45 days. So in the second half of FY '27, we'll announce the expansion of our Gold Loan branches based on what time we approach and subject to our approval and program.

items.statement: Consolidated AUM INR30,406 crores, up 47% YoY and 12% QoQ
items.quote: As of December 31, 2025, our consolidated AUM stood at INR30,406 crores, reflecting a robust 47% year-on-year growth and 12% quarter-on-quarter growth.

items.statement: Gold Loan AUM INR12,799 crores, up 26% QoQ and 80% YoY
items.quote: Gold Loan AUM saw robust growth, increasing from INR10,170 crores at the end of September to INR12,799 crores by December, a sequential increase of 26%, led by healthy customer demand and improving branch productivity.

items.statement: Co-lending AUM INR7,138 crores, up 93% YoY, 23.5% of total AUM
items.quote: Our co-lending AUM surged 93% year-on-year to INR7,138 crores, now accounting for almost 23.5% of total AUM, up from 21% in Q2 FY '26, highlighting our strategic focus on capital-efficient growth.

items.statement: MSME AUM INR5,886 crores, up 19% YoY
items.quote: Our MSME AUM grew to INR5,886 crores, up by 19% year-on-year, supported by steady execution and network expansion.

items.statement: Housing AUM INR6,490 crores, up 40% YoY
items.quote: Housing AUM stood at INR6,490 crores, delivering a year-on-year growth of 40%.

items.statement: Construction Finance AUM INR5,109 crores, up 37% YoY
items.quote: Our construction finance AUM saw steady growth of 37% year-on-year to INR5,109 crores, now funding over 279 active residential projects with an average ticket size of INR37 crores sanction-wise and outstanding portfolio ticket size of INR18 crores.

items.statement: Micro LAP AUM INR650 crores, target INR3,000 crores in 2.5-3 years
items.quote: In Micro LAP, we added 14 branches during Q3, taking the total branch network to 151 branches as of December end. Our immediate focus now in this segment will be on improving sales productivity and operating efficiency across the expanded network before undertaking the next phase of branch expansion.

items.statement: Yield on advances 16.4%, spread 7%, NIM 9.1% in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Our yields and spread on net advances remained healthy in the quarter at the 16.4% and 7%, respectively, driven by continued loan book expansion, decline in cost of funds and enhanced margin.

items.statement: Cost of funds reduced 24 bps QoQ, target further 20-25 bps reduction in 3-6 months
items.quote: As a result of MCLR reduction and our effective effort on repricing existing liabilities, we are happy to share that we saw quarter-on-quarter reduction of 24 basis in our cost of funds.

items.statement: Consolidated GNPA 1.2%, NNPA 0.7%, both improved QoQ
items.quote: At consolidated level, our Stage 3 assets remained flat at INR275 crores quarter-on-quarter, resulting in our gross Stage 3 ratio at 1.2%, down sequentially by 10 basis, while net Stage 3 ratio stood at 0.7%, down 7 bps sequentially.

items.statement: Gold Loan GNPA 0.39%, portfolio LTV 60%, fresh disbursement LTV 64-70%
items.quote: Our Gold Loan gross NPA stood at 0.39% as of December, underscoring our focus on risk management and portfolio quality even amid rapid growth.

items.statement: Micro LAP GNPA 0.9%, collection efficiency 99%

And we -- not like other Micro LAP, we are using here technology and other tools to see that we are able to -- at the time of sourcing the customer, bad customers are rejected there itself. So GNPA at Micro LAP, GNPA at the end of third quarter is about 0.9%, which is very, very good.

items.statement: Impairment cost INR23 crores (0.4% of gross loan book), PCR on Stage 3 improved to 43.6%
items.quote: Our impairment cost for the quarter stood at INR23 crores in Q3 FY '26, down from INR31 crores in Q2 FY '26 or 0.4% of the gross loan book and our provision coverage ratio on Stage 3 loans improved to 43.6%, demonstrating our prudent provisioning and conservative approach to risk management.

items.statement: Gold Loan fresh disbursement LTV reduced to 64-70% vs regulatory 75%
items.quote: In the rising trend of the gold, we reduced our LTV. So during the January, whatever we disbursed, our loan disbursement was happening at the LTV about 64% against the 75% permitted. And the portfolio level, our LTV is 60% overall.

items.statement: Borrowings up 38% YoY, INR6,860 crores incremental sanctions YTD, 11 new lenders added
items.quote: Our borrowing increased by 38% year-on-year and incremental borrowing sanction limit year-to-date this fiscal was around INR6,860 crores. We added 11 new lender relationships year-to-date, taking the active relationship now to 30-plus.

items.statement: Raised INR635 crores via NCDs and commercial paper in Q3
items.quote: We also continue to diversify our borrowing mix by raising funds through other instruments such as NCDs and commercial paper. During the quarter, we raised INR635 crores from NCDs and commercial paper.

items.statement: Leverage 2.8x, capital adequacy 30.3% (CGCL) and 24.8% (CGHFL), liquidity INR4,274 crores
items.quote: Following equity capital infusion of INR2,000 crores in Q1 FY '26, our balance sheet is now significantly stronger with a low leverage ratio of 2.8x, providing ample headroom to support accelerated growth across business segments. Our stand-alone capital adequacy ratio of CGCL is at 30.3% and 24.8% for Capri Global Housing Finance Limited. Our liquidity remains comfortable with INR4,274 crores in

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio improved to 51.6% from 58.2% YoY
items.quote: Our continued focus on operating efficiency is visible with the cost-to-income ratio improving 51.6% in Q3 FY '26 compared with 58.2% in Q3 FY '25. items.statement: Q3 EBITDA margin compressed to 16% due to incremental investments of ₹10-15 Crs in Purple Fabric, distribution, and delivery capacity
items.quote: EBITDA for Q3 was ₹122 Crs. translating to a margin of 16%.

items.statement: Gross margin dipped to ~54% in Q3 from ~57% LTM trend due to capacity building costs; expected to revert to 57%
items.quote: If you if you look at our trend maybe again in the last 12 months and then even in the previous last 12 months it was hovering around 57%.

items.statement: Incremental investment of ₹10-15 Crs in Q3 FY26 for Purple Fabric, distribution expansion, and delivery capacity building
items.quote: Just to add last quarter we said we made an incremental investment of ₹15 Crs. and similarly this quarter also we have made similar investments between ₹10 to ₹15 Crs. That's an incremental investment this quarter.

items.statement: LTM total income crossed ₹3,000 Crs (₹3,025 Crs), up 23% YoY; license-linked revenue grew 37% YoY to ₹1,595 Crs; platform revenue grew 128% YoY to ₹497 Crs; ARR grew 60% YoY to ₹1,118 Crs
items.quote: I'm pleased to share that for the first time in our history, Intellect's LTM total income has crossed ₹3,000 Crs., reaching ₹3,025 Crs. and representing a 23% year -on-year growth.

items.statement: 53 new customers added and 82 digital transformations went live in LTM period
items.quote: Over the last 12 months, 53 new customers have chosen Intellect's digital stack for their transformation journeys. In parallel, we have successfully enabled 82 digital transformations, wherein global financial institutions went live on our products and platforms.

items.statement: 62% of revenue from advanced markets (Americas, Europe, Middle East, APAC, India); no geographic concentration
items.quote: Revenue is better tested in the world's most demanding financial hubs with 62% of our revenue coming from advanced markets and is also well distributed across the Americas, Europe, Middle East, APAC, and India; avoiding any geographic concentration in any place.

items.statement: North America revenue approaching ₹1,000 Crs run-rate; investing in Toronto and New York hubs; Purple Fabric, Payments, Corporate Core driving growth
items.quote: I think I want to maybe just quantitatively share one more forward thing I think across North America I'm not far from start touching ₹1,000 Crs. revenue.

items.statement: Purple Fabric embedded across businesses; 14 value discovery partners and 1 large global SI signed in Q3; advanced talks with mainframe infrastructure leader for mainframe-to-cloud migration
items.quote: During the quarter, 14 new value discovery partners joined the Purple Fabric ecosystem, expanding our reach across AI-led risk underwriting, claims collections and payments use cases.

items.statement: eMACH.ai Core Banking named Visionary in Gartner Magic Quadrant for Retail Core Banking Systems Europe; IDC MarketScape leader for Corporate Loan Lifecycle Management; Euromoney World's Best Transaction Banking Software Provider 2025
items.quote: Gartner acknowledged eMACH.ai Core Banking as a Visionary in the Magic Quadrant for Retail Core Banking Sy stems, Europe. IDC MarketScape identified Intellect's Corporate Loan Lifecycle Management System as a leader in its worldwide vendor assessment for 2025

items.statement: 27 senior leaders joined in LTM; Manish Maakan elevated to Executive President & Group CRO; D. Shivakumar appointed as Independent Director (5-year term, subject to shareholder approval)
items.quote: 27 senior leaders have joined Intellect during the last 12 months. These additions strengthen our global consulting de livery product and go -to-market

items.statement: Q3 collections ₹913 Crs vs ₹553 Crs YoY (+65%); cash position ₹1,198 Crs vs ₹804 Crs YoY (+49%)
items.quote: Collections for Q3 stood at ₹913 Crs. compared to ₹553 Crs. in Q3 as of full year '25; up by 65% year -on-year.

items.statement: Cash balance ₹1,198 Crs as of Dec 2025; strong cash generation supports balance sheet strength
items.quote: Our cash position as of December '25 was ₹1,198 Crs. compared to ₹804 Crs. as of December '24, delivering a 49% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: One-time gratuity provision of ₹30.84 Crs and deferred tax of ₹7.8 Crs due to new labour code impacted Q3 PAT
items.quote: Profit after tax stood at ₹28 Crs., impacted by a one -time gratuity provision of ₹30.84 Crs. on account of the new labour code and the resultant deferred tax of ₹7.8 Crs.

items.statement: Purple Fabric competes primarily with Palantir and C3.ai for end-to-end enterprise AI orchestration; Indian SI players (TCS, etc.) lack full stack and governance layer
items.quote: I think Palantir and C3.ai are the fundamental main competitors the way we see it. There will be lots of noise with small players coming and doing cases in different areas. But when you actually look at end to end orchestration and enterprise level AI deployment, I think those two would be our primary sort of competitors.

items.statement: No material headwinds or tailwinds; balanced portfolio across products, geographies, and customers provides downside protection; designed for 20% LTM growth
items.quote: There are always headwinds of you hear the noise of politics and different things we got to deal with that. That's what we design business for. So, there's nothing right now material of headwinds or material tailwinds. I think a balanced growth is I'm feeling good and confident.

items.statement: LTM EBITDA grew 33% YoY to ₹709 Crs; PBT grew 34% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA for the last 12 months stood at ₹709 Crs. compared to ₹534 Crs. in LTM as of Q3 '25, showcasing a 33% year-on-year growth. PBT for the last 12 months grew 34% over the previous period.

items.statement: Q3 total income ₹753 Crs (+21% YoY); license-linked revenue ₹391 Crs (+34% YoY)
items.quote: Total income for the quarter stood at ₹753 Crs. reflecting a 21% year-on-year growth. License-linked revenue, which is the platform plus license plus AMC for the quarter stood at ₹391 Crs. growing 34% y ear-on-year. On

items.statement: Management acknowledged shareholder suggestion for buyback given ₹1,200 Crs cash and 5% dilution over 5 years from ESOPs; no commitment made
items.quote: We'll record your comment.

items.statement: CentralOne Forge acquisition already profitable at single-digit margins (better than initial margin-neutral expectation); cloud infrastructure support still provided by CentralOne
items.quote: We are already making profit on CentralOne, the single digit profit that we are making. In fact, initially we said it's going to be margin neutral, but we are making some profits out of it.

items.statement: SG&A step-up calibrated to revenue milestones: current investment level supports ₹800 Crs run-rate; further increments planned at ₹900 Crs and ₹1,000 Crs milestones
items.quote: No see if you as soon right now like we said beginning of year ₹700 Crs., ₹800 Crs. as we stabilize at ₹800 Crs. when we say ₹900 Crs. or ₹1,000 Crs. we will have to add more so it's a cycle.

items.statement: Purple Fabric consumption-based model starts small but scales significantly in Years 2-3; large deal mix increasing alongside smaller discovery engagements
items.quote: See with Purple Fabric what will happen is they will start small. But suddenly they will start showing big results in Year 2, Year3, three as the consumption grows. So, that's a consumption-based business.

items.statement: Sales cycles remain long but pipeline converting; multiple levers firing in North America (Purple Fabric, Payments, Corporate Core); credit union growth in Canada
items.quote: Payments has our Liquidity and CTX platform was a growth platform. Payments is where we are now making multiple breakt hroughs so we investing over there. Corporate Core is something which we have been winning over

items.statement: Alu-Zinc upgrade and solar plant to drive strong margin expansion in FY27, quarter-over-quarter
items.quote: We should be able to see the benefits of both Alu-Zinc and solar power kicking in effectively and in a large manner in the coming fiscal for sure, quarter-over-quarter.

items.statement: Second color coating line expected to commission in early FY27, expanding overall coating capacity by 174% to 236,000 tons per annum
items.quote: The second color coating line is expected to be commissioned in early FY '27, and it will expand overall coating capacity by a staggering 174%, touching 2,36,000 tons per annum.

items.statement: 7 MWp captive solar power plant targeted for Q1 FY27, expected to offset 50-55% of grid power consumption
items.quote: In addition to this, the 7 -megawatt peak captive solar power plant is targeted for Q1 of FY '27 and is expected to offset approximately 50% to 55% of the grid power consumption.

items.statement: Alu-Zinc coating technology upgrade successfully commissioned in Q3 FY26, increasing capacity by 36% to 180,000 tons per annum
items.quote: During the current quarter, the Aluminium-Zinc coating technology upgrade was successfully commissioned, resulting in a 36% increase in capacity, touching 1,80,000 tons per annum.

items.statement: Robust export order book of approximately INR350 crores supports strong visibility for coming quarters
items.quote: Further reinforcing our outlook, the company is supported by a robust export order book of approximately INR350 crores.

items.quote: Alu-Zinc as a product and pre-painted Alu-Zinc as a product sells at a premium and costs us lesser to produce in terms of raw material cost.

items.quote: Zinc and aluminium typically have been operating at levels of between $2,700 to $2,800 per ton over the last 6 to 9 months, whereas currently, we are seeing a situation where both zinc and aluminium have touched levels of between $3,200 to $3,500 per ton.

items.quote: The realization per ton that we achieved in pre-painted Alu-Zinc, well, if you both -- if you consider both blended of domestic and export, should be in the range of about INR83,000 to INR85,000 a ton.

items.statement: Strong liquidity with working capital facilities largely unutilized on fund-based side

items.statement: Financial tie-ups for second color coating line and solar power plant already achieved; no capital raise needed for these projects
items.quote: The financial tie-ups for both the second color coating line and the solar power plant have been already achieved. So, there is no problem in both.

items.statement: 9M FY26 margin expansion driven by higher export realization, healthier capacity utilization (color coating >95%, galvanizing >80% in H1), and better product mix
items.quote: Better product mix, better selling strategy in terms of geographies and healthier capacity utilization, all 3 have contributed to the margin expansion.

items.statement: 9M FY26 total income rose 15% YoY to INR580 crores; EBITDA up 67% to INR77 crores; net profit up 241% to INR35 crores

items.statement: Margin expansion from Alu-Zinc and solar not immediate; requires full cycle of trials, commercial orders, and larger orders
items.quote: The margin expansion will not happen immediately or instantly. It is a process of us being able to sell our new Alu-Zinc product to our customers effectively and successfully.

items.quote: As far as the margins are concerned, as specified earlier, we would be reaching around 14-15% in FY28, but somewhere in between the current margins and 15% in the next year.

items.quote: Post Kurlon acquisition, we had talked to the investors, and we set ourselves a target of 15% growth with a 15% EBITDA margin, on which we have been speaking very strongly. That journey is currently underway. We are halfway towards it.

items.statement: Consolidated core EBITDA margin at 10.9% in Q3 FY26, up 220 bps YoY; 9-month margin at 10.6%, up 213 bps YoY
items.quote: Our consolidated core EBITDA continues to be in double digit at 10.9% for Q3, expanding by 220 basis points YoY, growing from 84 crores to 117 crores. For the 9 months ending December '25, core EBITDA stood at 10.6%.

items.statement: U2O segment grew nearly 100% over 9 months reaching 75 crores turnover by Dec'25 and 120 crores run rate
items.quote: The segment grew by nearly 100% over the last 9 months, reaching a turnover of 75 crores by December '25, and reaching a run rate of 120 crores supported by continued product innovation across mass, value and economy segments.

items.statement: Expects JLG portfolio to be around 30% of total portfolio going forward

items.statement: MBBL portfolio grew 80% YoY and 38% QoQ, now 19% of Micro Banking Loan Book
items.quote: We are encouraged by strong performance of our Micro Banking Business Loan, MBBL portfolio, which grew by 80% YoY and 38% QoQ, now represents 19% of our Micro Banking Loan Book.

items.statement: Non-JLG lending grew 28% YoY and 8% QoQ; MSME loans up 24% YoY to INR 4,275 crores
items.quote: Beyond microfinance, our non-JLG lending business have maintained healthy momentum, growing by 28% YoY and 8% QoQ. MSME loans expanded by 24% YoY to INR 4,275 crores.

items.statement: Housing loans grew 13% YoY to INR 965 crores; Business Banking Group portfolio up 22% YoY
items.quote: Housing loans grew by 13% YoY to INR 965 crores, while our business banking group portfolio fully secured against immovable collateral grew by 22% YoY.

items.statement: Secured lending now 50% of overall loan book, up from 41% a year ago; JLG exposure moderated to ~33%
items.quote: Secured lending now comprises 50% of our overall loan book, up from 41% a year ago. This structural shift will eventually lead to a fundamentally stronger bank with less cyclicality in credit cost.

items.statement: Cost of funds reduced ~20 bps QoQ from 8.3% to 8.1%; expected to reduce further as repricing takes effect
items.quote: These calibrated actions have driven a gradual reduction in our overall cost of funds by around 20 bps QoQ from 8.3% in Q2FY26 to 8.1% in Q3FY26 and it is expected to reduce further as repricing takes effect.

items.statement: CASA + RTD ratio improved to 82% from 70% YoY; CASA ratio ~22%
items.quote: Our CASA deposits increased by 16% YoY and 3% QoQ, resulting in an improved CASA + RTD ratio of 82% as on Dec-25 from 70% as of Dec-24, reflecting our conscious effort to reduce reliance on bulk deposits and build a granular, low-cost deposit franchise. CASA rate has improved to around 22% as on Dec

items.statement: X-bucket collection efficiency for JLG improved to 99.5% in Dec-25, up from 98.7% in Sep-25; fresh NPA slippages reduced significantly vs Q3FY25
items.quote: X-bucket collection efficiency in the JLG segment improved to 99.5% in the month of Dec-25, up from 98.7% in the month of Sep-25, the highest in 3 quarters of FY26. Fresh NPA slippages has reduced significantly during Q3FY26 as compared to Q3FY25.

items.statement: Microfinance slippages in Q3FY26: JLG ~INR 272 crores out of total INR 426 crores
items.quote: So, in JLG it was close to INR272 crores out of INR426 crores.

items.statement: Not taking provisioning benefit from CGFMU coverage; provisioning as if no coverage exists
items.quote: Currently, we don't take any benefit of in terms of from the provision angle. We will provision as if there is no coverage at all, and we are not taking any benefit of that.

items.statement: Capital Adequacy 20.1%, Tier 1 17.1% as of Dec-25; Rights issue of INR 950 crores in Nov-25 strengthened Tier 1
items.quote: Despite the losses, our Capital Adequacy ratio remains strong at 20.1% as on December 31, 2025, comfortably above the regulatory threshold. The successful rights issue of INR 950 crores in Nov-25 has further strengthened our Tier 1 capital base.

items.statement: No capital raise needed for next 12 months; Tier 1 target floor ~15%, overall CRAR floor ~17.5%
items.quote: Typically, overall, we will be in the range of 17% to 17.5% from this 20%, we don't want to go below that. And though we don't have any specific number for Tier 1, but around 15% of Tier 1, around 17.5% of overall capital, that is what we intend to not go below that level.

items.statement: CD ratio declined to 79% from 92% YoY; surplus liquidity ~INR 4,700 crores; LCR 207%
items.quote: Our CD ratio declined to 79% as on Dec-25, which is against 92% as on Dec-24. We ended the quarter with surplus liquidity of approximately INR 4,700 crores, which is higher than our usual liquidity requirement and LCR ratio of 207%.

items.statement: Repaid >INR 2,000 crores institutional term deposits; retail term deposits and CASA grew by similar amount
items.quote: We have restructured the whole liability business. In sense, there are more than INR 2,000 crores of institutional term deposits which we have repaid and we have not renewed those cases, whereas our retail term deposit in CASA has gone up by almost same amount.

items.statement: One-time employee cost impact of INR 9 crores from new Labour Law Codes, LTIPs and ESOP grants
items.quote: During the quarter, we incurred a one-time impact of INR 9 crores due to new Labour Law Codes, LTIPs and ESOP grant, etc, pertaining to employee benefits obligations.

items.statement: JLG collection workforce expanded to nearly 1,300; centralized call center operationalized; branches split for better oversight
items.quote: We have expanded our collection workforce for JLG and MBBL business to nearly 1,300 as on Dec-25, operationalized a centralized call center for overdue accounts and split larger micro banking branches to improve oversight.

items.statement: Reverse merger of holding company into bank: NCLT petition filed Dec 26, 2025; first hearing Jan 15, 2026; order awaited
items.quote: During the quarter, the filing of petition with NCLT is completed on December 26, 2025, for approval of scheme of amalgamation of holding company into the bank, that is reverse merger. The first hearing has happened on January 15, 2026, and the order is awaited.

items.statement: Disbursement momentum improving: Oct ~INR 800 cr, Nov ~INR 1,000 cr, Dec ~INR 1,100 cr, Jan >INR 1,200 cr
items.quote: When we talk of October last year, we have around INR 800 crores disbursement. But in November we have around INR 1,000 crores. It's a mix of all these things, INR 1,100 crores in the month of December and January had been more than INR 1,200 crores.

items.statement: AUM growth expected in Q4 FY26 (~INR 250-300 crores in Jan pre-write-off); JLG portfolio growing again after 12-13 months
items.quote: In fact, in January also, we have seen, I mean, good growth, maybe around close to INR 250 crores – INR 300 crores of AUM growth. I mean, at least on pre-write-off basis, we should see a good growth in the Q4 because now our JLG is also growing.

items.statement: Raipur hospital on track to achieve EBITDA breakeven in next 6 to 8 months
items.quote: we are pleased to share that the facility is on track to ach ieve EBITDA breakeven in the next 6 to 8 months, well within the targeted time frame

items.quote: So the Jamshedpur facility is expected to be commissioned around Q4 of FY '27 we expect losses of around INR3 crores to INR4 crores for that during the period.

items.statement: Raipur 9-month EBITDA loss INR10 crores; expect additional INR1.5-2 crores loss in Q4; full year FY26 just about EBITDA positive
items.quote: So 9 months EBITDA loss is around INR10 crores for Raipur. Yes, we do expect another INR1.5 crores to INR2 crores of EBITDA loss in Q4.

items.statement: Raipur EBITDA loss INR2.5 crores this quarter, considerably reduced from previous quarter
items.quote: So the Raipur EBITDA loss is around INR 2.5 crores in this quarter. And this has considerably reduced from the previous quarter.

items.quote: We expect that in the next 6 months to 8 months, the ratio should significantly come down.

items.quote: We are actively pursuing and evaluating opportunities which come to us. It is about a matter of time as to what ends up being the right fit for the expansion process.

items.quote: It was at around the 40% mark. It has already moved to the 51%, 52% mark, and we are seeing significant traction for it go further up.

items.statement: 9M FY26 ARPOB INR38,797; network ARPOB ~INR39,600; Dum Dum ARPOB INR42,396 (up from INR40,880); Agartala ARPOB ~INR37,000 (9% YoY growth)
