items.quote: Rossell was never impacted by the duties and the tariffs. Rossell has always been getting exemptions, so that really has not impacted us at all.

items.statement: Enhanced working capital limits backed by increased banking partner commitments; no external equity infusion to date
items.quote: We enhanced our working capital limits backed by increased commitments from our banking partners. To enable our next phase of expansion, we are planning a Qualified Institutional Placement, a QIP.

items.statement: Europe partnerships and tie-ups announcements expected soon; RFPs received from European customers
items.quote: I am happy to say that we will be releasing some very positive announcements soon of some tie -ups and some partnerships that we are planning in Europe.

items.statement: ROE currently 12-15%; targeting steady improvement over next 2-3 financial years
items.quote: ROE we are between 12% to 15% as of now currently and we are looking at consistent steady improveme nt in the next two, three financial years without giving any particular guidance as such.

items.statement: Delivered EBITDA and PAT profitability in Q3 FY26 as committed for H2 FY26
items.quote: we had given a commitment that we would turn profitable in the second half of FY '26. And I am delighted to report that we have delivered both EBITDA and PAT profitability in Q3 FY '26.

items.statement: Payments GMV hit all-time high of Rs 481 billion, up 63% YoY and 11% QoQ for 12th consecutive quarter
items.quote: On the Payment side, GMV - which is basically the total value of payments processed - rose to an all-time high in this quarter for Rs. 481 billion, which is a consistent record high for the 12th quarter in a row.

items.statement: UPI transactions grew 220% YoY to 3.2x, UPI share increased from 32% to 41% YoY
items.quote: UPI transactions for MobiKwik, which are visible also on the NPCI website, have actually grown 220% to 3.2 times in the last one year, and despite the UPI share growing from 32% in the same quarter last financial year to 41% this financial year

items.statement: Payments net margin at 17 bps, up from previous levels, driven by wallet and bill payments revenue
items.quote: we have expanded both payments revenue, which in this quarter is Rs. 223.7 crores, and payments net margin, which is around 17 basis points.

items.statement: Financial services gross profit at Rs 37 crore, up 405% YoY and 45% QoQ; lending expenses down 57% YoY
items.quote: gross profit for financial services at INR 372 million or Rs. 37 crores, which is up 405% year-on-year and 45% quarter-on-quarter. So, it is not just the growth in disbursal and the growth in revenue. It is the margin which has expanded in lending, resulting in better profitability. Lending related expenses came down 57% year-on-year

items.statement: Personal loan disbursals reached ~Rs 900 crore, up 126% YoY for ZIP EMI product; consistent growth over 4-5 quarters
items.quote: we have reached a disbursal of personal loans to a high of ~9000 million, which is Rs. 900 crores for this quarter, which is consistent growth over previous quarter, as well as I would say it is a fourth or fifth quarter consistent growth, with actually a 126% year-on-year growth in terms of our ZIP EMI product.

items.statement: FLDG/DLG business is 80% of disbursals, 20% is distribution-led risk-free business
items.quote: the FLDG or DLG led business is 80% of the current quarter's disbursal and 20% is the distribution led risk-free business.

items.statement: Long-term sustainable payments net margin guided at 12-15 bps; current 17 bps not seen as sustainable
items.quote: we believe that on a long-term basis, a more sustainable margin in payments is between 12-15 basis points for us, given the contribution of UPI is going up and looking at the wallet and the bill payments business. So, 17 bps is not what we also see as a long-term sustainable margin

items.statement: Offline merchant footprint expanded from 366 to 1,118 cities; focusing on Tier 2/3 markets
items.quote: we have improved our footprint from 366 cities to 1118 cities, because we believe that underpenetrated markets will offer us good upside from a long-term potential perspective

items.statement: PIDF and UPI incentives only 0.4% of revenue; not material to business strategy
items.quote: PIDF as well as consumer side UPI incentives put together are only 0.4% of our revenue this quarter, and for other quarters. So these incentives are very small compared to our overall revenue and are therefore not material to us.

items.statement: Rentpay category shut down across all players; revenue negligible to zero this quarter
items.quote: Rentpay as a category has been shut down across all the players in the market. And so yes, it has been shut down on our platform as well and yes, the revenue coming from Rentpay would have been there in the bill payments category in the previous quarters but in this quarter, it is negligible, if not zero.

items.statement: Wallet has 18% market share by value per industry data; wallet over UPI (pocket UPI) drives stickiness and cross-sell
items.quote: we are the largest wallet, and as per industry data, we have 18% share by value. The wallet business is also growing overall for industry.

items.statement: Bond product experiment with expected revenue realization of 0.5-1.5%
items.quote: the bond product that we have put on our website, it is an experiment. It is too early to say what the realization is, but we do see the revenue realization will be between 0.5% to 1.5%.

items.statement: Sticky wallet customers drive higher transaction frequency, ticket size, bill payment propensity and cross-sell to loans
items.quote: the frequency of transactions, average ticket size of the transactions, the propensity of the transactions on bill payments, generating convenience fees, via different mechanisms in the wallet, even the amount of money that they keep in the wallet, all of this results in higher revenue

items.statement: Merchant acquiring market large and doubling in 5 years; focusing on underpenetrated Tier 2/3 markets rather than competing head-on with large players
items.quote: this market is extremely large from total addressable market perspective and despite the fact that there are 2-3 large players, the market is not fully penetrated. Also as per various industry reports, the market itself is going to double in the next 5 years.

items.statement: No specific quarterly profitability improvement guidance; focus on sustainable operating model with revenue growth and stable margins
items.quote: I wish there were a formula that you could improve Rs. 15-20 crores profitability every quarter, it would then become infinite. But unfortunately, that is not the case. Like I said earlier, we can say that we are reaching a more stable operating model.

items.statement: Credit quality and collection efficiency significantly improved; static pool risk performance cohorts stable over many quarters
items.quote: We have seen the cohorts of static pool risk performance continue to improve and maintain over the past many quarters. So therefore, we do believe that we can continue to maintain this margin.

items.statement: Target to open 700 stores by end of FY26
items.quote: We closed Q3 with 600 stores open pan India and we are very much in line for opening 700 stores by the end of this fiscal.

items.statement: Units sold 68,000 in Q3 FY26, up 50% year-on-year
items.quote: Units sold were 68,000, which was up 50% year -on-year.

items.statement: Adjusted gross margin improved to 25% in Q3 FY26, up 700 bps year-on-year and 19% quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: Adjusted gross margin was up 111% year-on-year and 19% quarter-on-quarter to INR251 crores, which is only about 25%, which at 25% itself is a 700 bps improvement year-on-year.

items.statement: EBITDA improved 1,600 bps year-on-year and 700 bps quarter-on-quarter to negative 3% in Q3 FY26
items.quote: EBITDA improved by 1,600 bps year-on-year and 700 bps quarter-on-quarter to land up at negative 3 overall.

items.statement: Target of a couple thousand stores in next few years with expanding portfolio including EL
items.quote: I do believe that a couple thousand stores in the next few years is a pretty healthy ask and practically possible with the expanding portfolio.

items.statement: Announced INR 3,000 price hike at start of Q4 FY26, using base vehicle price and ProPack levers
items.quote: In fact, even in the start of this quarter, Q4, we have announced a INR3,000 price hike. And we are managing that well.

items.statement: Not having PLI is a strength for resilient P&L; competitors' PLI benefits create future pricing risk
items.quote: us not having PLI is actually one of the strongest and one of the biggest reasons to be optimistic about us in the mid -term, because we are already operating on the most cleanest pricing principle.

items.statement: Retail registrations ~72,000 vs wholesale 67,800 in Q3 FY26; channel inventory reduced efficiently towards end of calendar year
items.quote: In fact, our actual registration count and actual units sold were materially higher at almost 72,000 units and it was very efficient management of our channel inventory with our partners, which allowed us to reduce the channel inventory towards the end of the calendar year.

items.statement: Charging network reached 5,000 points as of Dec 31, 2025; operating on LECCS protocol and monetized
items.quote: Ather runs the largest fast charging network for electric two wheelers in the country, with our total network size reaching 5,000 charging points as of 31st December.

items.statement: All hands on deck occupied with scooter segment and EL launch; motorcycle work ongoing but no announcement
items.quote: We are still at an early stage. We are still evaluating it. Honestly, all hands on deck, completely occupied with the scooter segment right now, particularly with EL and its associated products.

items.statement: Entered auto insurance as corporate agent to control end-to-end consumer experience; expected to be margin accretive
items.quote: The primary reason for us to enter there was to take better control of the end -to-end consumer experience and deliver a delight feature there. But we also expect the entire play to be margin accretive for the company.

items.statement: Management expects steady double-digit revenue growth and pre-Ind AS EBITDA margins of 11%-12% going forward.
items.quote: We want to be a steady double-digit growth and EBITDA 11%-12% steady, sorry, the pre Ind AS margins.

items.statement: Capex for FY26 expected to be north of INR300 crores, perhaps INR320-330 crores.
items.quote: This year, our capex will be north of INR300 crores, perhaps INR320 crores, INR330 crores.

items.statement: Net debt reduction target of INR75-100 crores from current INR800 crores; aim for net debt closer to zero over next three years.
items.quote: The plan is to reduce it, bring it to by another INR75 to INR100 crores. But you know, Vishak and Ashish can talk on the growth capex after demerger which was the rationale which we conveyed that the company will have the growth capital available to them.

items.statement: Emerging brands portfolio expected to become one-fourth of overall ABLBL business in next 4-5 years.
items.quote: This portfolio is expected to be one-fourth of overall ABLBL business in next 4-5 years.

items.statement: Innerwear business expected to turn profitable in FY28; hopeful for at least one profitable quarter in FY27.
items.quote: I'm hopeful that FY '28 will be a profitable year. I think that's the kind of trajectory that we've built for ourselves right now.

items.statement: Management targets steady state growth of 12% overall, with Lifestyle Brands like-for-like of 6%-7% and rest from expansion.
items.quote: Personally, between you and me, and I've said this earlier as well, I'm hoping more for a 12% kind of a steady state growth.

items.statement: Q3 demand strong in Oct-Nov, moderated in Dec due to wedding calendar shift; festive season partially in Q2 this year.
items.quote: As we reflect on demand during the quarter, it began on a strong note with healthy momentum through October and November before moderating in December, partially due to a shift in wedding dates.

items.statement: January second half encouraging post-Makar Sankranti; momentum expected to continue through next couple of months.
items.quote: The calendar is such that most of the wedding season began post-Makar Sankranti. So we've had an encouraging second half of January. And my sense is that momentum should continue through the next couple of months.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded 180 bps YoY to 18.4% in Q3 FY26; Lifestyle Brands EBITDA margin at 20.6%, highest in four years.
items.quote: EBITDA margin expanded by 180 bps from 16.6% in Q3 FY25 to 18.4% in Q3 FY '26.

items.statement: YTD EBITDA margin improved 100 bps to 16.9% despite higher advertisement spend.
items.quote: EBITDA grew at 12% in absolute terms to INR1,054 crores versus INR940 crores in previous year, with margin improving by 100 bps to 16.9% despite higher advertisement spend versus last year.

items.statement: Added 90+ stores in Q3; expect another 90+ net stores in Q4, totaling ~150 stores for FY26; pipeline of 120+ stores for FY27 and 300 identified locations.
items.quote: We've added about 50 plus stores in this quarter. Our sense is that we should add another 90 plus net stores in the next quarter. So that would make the overall addition to about INR150 stores this year.

items.statement: Emerging brands network spans 375+ stores with 20+ added in Q3; Reebok network expanded to 200+ stores, targeting 230+ by year-end.
items.quote: Overall, Reebok's network expanded to 200-plus stores, doubling from 100 stores at the time of acquisition.

items.statement: Capex split: ~80%+ for Lifestyle Brands (renovations, expansions, larger stores), remainder for emerging brands.
items.quote: The lion's share would be for the Lifestyle Brands. Probably 80% of that spend would be Lifestyle Brands, maybe a little more than 80%.

items.statement: GST rate changes: net small negative impact on blended basis; benefit on products below INR2,500 (t-shirts), negative on wedding wear (suits/blazers moving 12% to 18%).
items.quote: Overall, it's a small net negative, but not a significant one.

items.statement: Innerwear: passed on GST benefit (12% to 5%) to consumers; no price hike taken.
items.quote: No, actually we passed down the GST benefits to consumers. So you would have seen that a lot of segments which had a 12% which moved to 5%. So we passed that on to consumers.

items.statement: Lifestyle Brands growth driven by product upgrades in wedding categories and enhanced in-store experience; 6th consecutive quarter of like-to-like growth.
items.quote: Growth during the quarter was driven by a combination of targeted product portfolio upgrades, particularly in wedding-like categories, and continued enhancement to the in-store experience.

items.statement: Reebok apparel contribution increased from 25% to 36%+; added strong performance footwear and carbon-plated running shoes.
items.quote: When we took on the brand, the apparel contribution was about 25%. Today, it's a little more than 36% already.

items.statement: Small town India (ITG) same-store growth at 13-14% YTD; urban IT-heavy markets not specifically weaker but small towns outperforming.
items.quote: You know that small town India went through a few tough quarters. This year, our own same store growth pages in small town ITG would be about 13%-14%.

items.statement: Innerwear: consumer stickiness high; distribution network well-oiled; confident despite D2C competition and market leader slowdown.
items.quote: I think the first thing is the biggest thing which gives me confidence personally is the consumer acceptance of this brand and this category. I think the consumer stickiness on those who ever tried the product, is very high.

items.statement: Rent expense (franchisee commission + variable mall rent) declining 100-150 bps due to operating leverage from 10% like-for-like growth vs 5-6% store cost growth.
items.quote: Is that question answered now? I think it's the operating leverage of having a higher like-to-like sale which is what is bringing that down.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR800 crores at Dec-end from INR1,000 crores at Sep-end; INR500 crore NCD issuance approved for refinancing repaid debentures, no fresh borrowing.
items.quote: Our net debt reduced to INR800 crores as of December end from INR1000 crores in September end.

items.statement: Board approved INR500 crore NCD issuance to refinance debentures repaid in January; no fresh borrowing.
items.quote: The INR500 crores debentures which we repaid recently in the month of January, we intend to raise it and to refinance the existing, the debentures repaid. There is no fresh borrowing.

items.statement: Lifestyle Brands retail like-for-like growth at 5% in Q3 (10% YTD); Emerging Brands retail like-for-like at 16% in Q3 (25%+ YTD for Innerwear).
items.quote: The business delivered growth of 9% during the quarter, supported by healthy like-to-like growth of 5%.

items.statement: Wholesale channel grew 21% in Q3; e-commerce and trade channels grew double-digit; secondary sales robust across department stores.
items.quote: Performance across other channels also improved meaningfully during the quarter, while secondary sales continued to remain strong in line with past quarters.

items.statement: Wedding calendar shifts cause quarterly demand volatility; December weddings ended 5th Dec impacting Q3, Q4 weddings in Feb-Mar.
items.quote: December, the wedding calendar was such that the last of weddings was on, I think, 5th December. So the calendar was not t he same after 5th December

items.statement: Revenue recognition unchanged: wholesale recognizes on sell-to-partner; retail consignment recognizes on sell-to-consumer; conservative accounting maintained.
items.quote: of trade are built around that, that we recognize revenue when we sell to the partner. Sell to the partner, not the end consumer? In retail consignment, retail sales, we recognize that when we sell to end consumer

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margin guided at 22%-23% for next several years
items.quote: we are confident of keeping the operating EBITDA in the range of 22% to 23%.

items.statement: R&D spend guided at 10%-11% of revenue for next several years
items.quote: And the R&D spends, again, to be around 10% to 11% of revenue for the next several years.

items.statement: R&D spend expected above INR 500 crores over FY26, FY27, Q1 FY28
items.quote: we are expecting confidently to keep R&D spend above INR500 crores, if we look at fiscals '26, '27, and Q1 of '28 taken together.

items.statement: Pithampur facility acquisition INR 149 crores and additional capex INR 70 crores in YTD
items.quote: This INR340 crores comprises INR149 crores investment behind Pithampur plant acquisition, capex of INR70 crores, bank deposits of INR87 crores and our investment in Gen1E Lifescience of INR18 crores.

items.statement: Pithampur facility validations by mid CY2026, commercialization in Q1 CY27
items.quote: At Pithampur, we are on track to operationalizing, kind of doing all the validations by mid of 2026 calendar year, we should be able to complete that and we expect commercialization in quarter one of CY '27.

items.statement: Gross margin pressured by higher outsourcing due to stronger-than-expected demand
items.quote: This has put pressure on the GM but the root problem is, it is a good problem to have because we are having more than anticipated demand and we had to actually do more outsourcing than what we had actually envisaged at the start.

items.statement: Gross margin expected to return to 67%-68% range as Pithampur ramps up and outsourcing reduces
items.quote: we are confident of going back to our earlier gross margin range of 67%-68%.

items.statement: Demand stronger than anticipated, sales ramp-up above expectations
items.quote: what has happened in the market right now, for the demand which we had anticipated, actually our demand has even been more than what we have envisaged.

items.statement: Specialty share of gross profit increased to 31%-32% in Q2/Q3 from 26.9% in FY25
items.quote: if you see, the specialty share of gross profit has remained in Q2 and Q3 at 31% to 32%. This is higher than 26.9%, which was there in the full year of FY '25.

items.statement: R&D productivity multiple improved from 3.3x to 4.1x to 5.7x over rolling three-year periods
items.quote: if you compare that to the R&D spend that was made in fiscals '22, '23, and Q1 of '24, that is INR226 crores, and that is 5.7x.

items.statement: R&D productivity expected to sustain upward of 5x going forward
items.quote: we are confident that the R&D productivity will be upward of 5x.

items.statement: Net working capital at 132 days as of Dec 31, broadly in line with March at 137 days
items.quote: our working capital, net working capital as on 31st of December was INR 607 crores translating into 132 days of net working capital which was broadly in line with the March number which was at 137.

items.statement: Borrowings reduced to INR 285 crores from INR 393 crores at March 2025 due to repayment
items.quote: Our borrowings were at INR285 crores versus INR393 crores as on 31st of March and reduction was primarily driven by repayment in debt.

items.statement: IPO proceeds of INR 478 crores received in YTD FY26
items.quote: Our cash flow from financing activities of INR326 crores on a YTD level was primarily driven by IPO proceeds of INR478 crores and net debt repayment of INR116 crores.

items.statement: Dr. Pradnya Saravade appointed as Independent Director; General Atlantic nominee Anand Agarwal stepped down
items.quote: we have appointed Dr. Pradnya Saravade as an Independent Director. And one nominee, General Atlantic, Director, Mr. Anand Agarwal, has stepped down.

items.statement: Regulatory approval timelines factored with conservatism in business plans
items.quote: when we look at our modelling or our long range plans, we factor in conservatism from all the external variability factors, regulatory being one, but it could be competition, it could be change in the FDA guidelines.

items.statement: 98% of revenues from US dollars, healthy dollar-to-dollar growth year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: Also, if you look at the performance because 98% of our revenues come from US dollars, even a dollar to dollar comparison, there is a healthy growth year on year and quarter on quarter.

items.statement: No significant product concentration, top 5 and top 10 products not dependent on single hero product
items.quote: if you saw the numbers on our top five, top 10, I think there's no concentration there that we are dependent on one product.

items.statement: Specialty defined as max one competitor; even if competition increases, margin profile remains healthy
items.quote: the way we define speciality wherein apart from Rubicon, there is at the max one more competition. But even if, let us say, there is more than one competition and the product does not continue to be a speciality, even then the margin profile of that product is fairly healthy.

items.statement: Pricing remains stable with focus on specialty products
items.quote: If you look at the pricing, with our focus on specialty products, the pricing remains to be stable

items.statement: Cash reserve of INR 334 crores provides dry powder for inorganic growth
items.quote: Our cash reserve was at INR 334 crores which gives us dry powder for our inorganic growth aspiration.

items.statement: ROCE at 34% despite higher inventory, improved vs March 2025 and previous quarter
items.quote: if you look at our ROCE, despite this higher inventory level, our ROCE is at 34% which demonstrates our laser sharp focus on capital efficiency as an organization and this ROCE has also improved versus March '25 as well as the previous quarter.

items.statement: Inventory at INR 685 crores, 25%-30% for recent and upcoming launches
items.quote: if I look at the inventory which is for recent launches and the upcoming launches, so 25% to 30% of the inventory will be towards the recent or the expected launches.

items.statement: Net cash from operations INR 35 crores in Q3 after INR 46 crores tax payment; pre-tax cash generation INR 81 crores
items.quote: our net cash flow from operating activities for the quarter was INR35 crores. This INR35 crores cash from operation was after payment of INR46 crores of income tax in the previous quarter versus INR 12 crores in the H1. So if you look at the cash from operation before tax, it was at INR 81 crores for the quarter which was a healthy cash generation.

items.statement: YTD net cash from operations INR 140 crores
items.quote: And if you look at our net cash flow on a YTD level, it was INR 140 crores.

items.statement: Management targets minimum 1 GW each of solar panel, inverter, and battery sales in FY27
items.quote: We will do minimum 1 gigawatt each solar panel, inverter, and battery.

items.statement: Ratlam expansion capex is Rs 272 crore excluding land, with Rs 159 crore for machinery split across module, inverter, and battery lines
items.quote: The overall size excluding land, it is around Rs. 272 crores. Specifically if we ask, out of these Rs. 272 crores, Rs. 159 is for machine. And if we further segregate this machine, so Rs. 106 crores will be for solar module, Rs. 28 crores for the solar inverter, and Rs. 25 crores for lithium ion battery.

items.statement: Dadri 1 GW solar cell plant commissioned in 6 months with Rs 300 crore investment; total panel capacity now 1.6 GW
items.quote: We are excited to announce the successful commissioning of our 1 gigawatt solar cell manufacturing plant at Dadri, Uttar Pradesh. With this facility, Fujiyama has taken a meaningful step towards backward integration with an investment of approximately Rs. 300 crores. With this new capacity, the company now operates a total 1.6 gigawatt of solar panel manufacturing capacity.

items.statement: Dadri cell line at 40% utilization currently, targeting 80% by end of Q4 FY26
items.quote: We are now about around 40% at this time. And at the end of this quarter, we are expecting up to 80% basically.

items.statement: Ratlam facility utilization target: at least 50% in FY27, 100% in FY28, with possibility of full utilization in FY27
items.quote: I think what I can say, definitely, at least 50% we would utilize in next year and 100% in second next year. Or maybe if you have, with good wishes of yours, maybe we could use it fully maybe in next year, but we cannot commit basically on that part.

items.statement: Sequential EBITDA margin improvement of 0.9% in Q3 vs Q2 FY26 from scaling benefits and backward integration
items.quote: On a quarter-on-quarter basis, revenue from operations increased by 3.6% compared to Q2 FY26, whereas EBITDA and PAT increased by 6.7% and 7.0%, respectively, compared to previous quarters. The sequential improvement as a percentage of revenue in margins was supported by a 0.9% extension in gross margins, driven by continued backward integration and scale efficiencies.

items.statement: Rooftop solar market projected at 40-45% CAGR; government budget shows continued support for rooftop solar
items.quote: Actually, there is a historical CAGR of 45% and the upcoming industry expectation is also 40% to 43% CAGR. And in the last budget, we have also seen that there is a continued support for the rooftop solar. So we expect that the CAGR is possible and it will happen.

items.statement: Budget exempted basic customs duty on solar glass raw materials from 7.5% to 0%; company uses mostly India-made glass and expects better pricing
items.quote: Like raw material for glass is exempted, like custom duty is reduced from 7.5% to 0%. Then domestic glass, we expect domestic glass we will get at a better price, basically. Aniket Madhwani: So can we expect improved operational benefit? Pawan Kumar Garg: And we are using mostly India-made glass. Major raw material, we are using India-made. So definitely, we are expecting better prices in the

items.statement: Q3 FY26 revenue split: Rs 2,980M solar panels, Rs 1,000M batteries, Rs 1,600M electronics, rest others
items.quote: So, out of Rs. 5,884 million, around Rs. 2,980 million was for solar panel, Rs. 1,000 million for battery, and around Rs. 1,600 million for electronics, and rest in others category.

items.statement: Solar panels contribute 45-47% of total revenue by value due to higher per-watt cost vs inverters and batteries
items.quote: So in terms of value, out of our total revenue, generally it amounts to 45% to 47% out of Rs. 100. Pawan Kumar Garg: Actually, sir, per watt cost of solar panel is higher than per watt cost of inverter or per watt cost of battery basically. So that's why total revenue from the solar panel side is higher

items.statement: Distribution network expanded by 60+ distributors, 400+ dealers, 20 Shoppes outlets in Q3; total channel partners now over 8,200
items.quote: During the quarter, we added over 60 distributors, more than 400 dealers, and 20 exclusive Shoppes outlets, taking our total channel partners base to over 8,200.

items.statement: Distributor onboarding process: evaluate market standing, business size, financials, bankability, dealer relationships; require investment from distributor
items.quote: We first check their current market standing, their current business size, their statement we check, and their bankability we check. And then we make them our distributors after they invest in our company.

items.statement: Total debt at Rs 470+ crore including term loan, working capital, and vendor finance
items.quote: s around Rs. 470-plus crores. Anuj Upadhyay: 470? Prashant Gupta: Yes. It is including term loan, working capital, vendor finance, all collective streams

items.statement: Silver paste substitution R&D underway but will take minimum 6-12 months if successful; long experimentation required
items.quote: It will take time, sir. Years of time. Basically, this process is not easy just to replace basically silver paste. Yes, R&D is started basically. But it can take one year or six months minimum if it is successful, because there is a long experiment for that.

items.statement: Operational efficiency program CAPA (Corrective and Preventive Action) implemented; AI being introduced across operations
items.quote: There is one trend in our company that is called CAPA, C-A-P-A, Corrective and Preventive Action. Any problem comes, we generate CAPA, and we work on that, what is corrective action and what is preventive action. So it improves operational efficiency every time. So we hope and we are keen for making more and more. We are introducing AI in every operations.

items.statement: Targets >15% revenue growth and >15% EBITDA growth for FY26; aims for 18-20% revenue and earnings growth in FY27
items.quote: But I think for the whole year we should maintain 15% plus revenue growth, 15% plus EBITDA growth compared to the same period last year. And '27, I think, and we will talk more about '27 when we talk about the March results. But internally, we are working to be more ambitiou s and while current year our targets have been around 15% plus, next year, the idea would be closer to 18% to 20% rather tha

items.statement: Retail sales grew 24% in Q3 across piping, irrigation and tissue culture; volume growth 8-9%
items.quote: So, overall growth might seem lower at 17%, but ret ail sales grew very well at 24%. And that is what our focus is going forward as well, that as we bring down the project sales, as we complete the projects etc., next 12 months, it would almost be negligible, the retail sale is what is going to fuel the growth for the company and tha t already automatically means better balance sheet because retai

items.statement: Plastic division Q3 EBITDA fell from Rs 42 cr to Rs 33 cr (margin 10.8% to 7.2%); half due to inventory loss, half due to lower volumes from extended rains
items.quote: So, I think when you look at EBITDA terms, and abs olute amount, right, the EBITDA last year in 3rd Quarter was Rs. 42 crores. This year it came down to at Rs. 33 crore. So, loss of about 20% in absolute amounts and percentage-wise it came down from 10.8% to 7.2% in this particular quarter. And about half of that I will a ttribute towards loss of inventory and half of that with less volume growth

items.statement: Government project receivables: expect Rs 125 cr net reduction in Q4, Rs 350-400 cr reduction in FY27

items.statement: EBITDA per kg improved to INR135-140 levels with guidance to maintain these levels long-term
items.quote: We have now improved our EBITDA per kilo. It's now at INR135, INR140 levels, and we'll continue to maintain -- try and continue to maintain at these levels.

items.statement: India branded business operating margins in 5-8% range with continued investment for growth
items.quote: I think this number because we don't kind of granularly kind of publish numbers. So let us stay with that. And it's not a very broad margin, 5% to 8% to my mind is quite a decent spectrum that we are giving.

items.statement: Long-term contracts increasing as green coffee prices stabilize, driving volume growth from 10-15% to 15-20%

items.statement: Blended utilization at 65-70% in Q3, targeting 85-90% in 2 years with capacity expansion decisions after 1.5 years
items.quote: So let's say, at an annual level, next -- by the end of 2 years from now, let's say, we are looking at an 85%, 90% kind of a capacity utilization.

items.statement: Green coffee prices stable at INR3,600-4,000 range, outlook better than year ago but post-Tet volatility possible
items.quote: the green coffee prices, as far as they are concerned, they remain in the range of INR3,600 to INR4,000 levels. We'll have to wait and watch, post I told this before as well, post pet holidays, how things pan

items.statement: Cost-plus model ensures EBITDA per kg unaffected by green coffee price declines
items.quote: Absolutely, there will be no impact on EBITDA because a lot of people ask these questions. We don't speculate on coffee prices. It's a cost-plus model, very sound in terms of how we build prices.

items.statement: Branded retail sales growing 40-50% YoY, targeting INR430-440 crores for FY26 with INR330 crores in 9M
items.quote: We are growing at almost 40%, 50% this year. And this year, we are likely to close at around INR430 crores, INR440 crores of only branded sales.

items.statement: Direct distribution expanded to 140,000 outlets, strong e-commerce presence with double-digit market share on platforms
items.quote: We are now distributed -- directly distributed in 140,000 outlets. We are also expanding our networks beyond South, which is North, East and West markets.

items.statement: Plant-based snacks category exited due to poor market outlook, experimenting with traditional snacks under Malgudi brand
items.quote: That category itself, if you see around you, has kind of -- has not done well. In fact, the whole category is almost on a shutdown basis. And we quickly took a call because we didn't want to further our losses in that category.

items.statement: Client base well-diversified with top 20% clients contributing only 40-50% of revenue
items.quote: Our top 20% of the clients contribute only 40% to 50%, which means that the diversification of CCL Products ( our clients is also very good

items.statement: Growth across all geographies - Africa, Americas, Europe, Asia with brand growth in India
items.quote: We are getting very good growth from Africa. We're getting good growth from the American markets as well as the European markets. Asia is growing for us. Our brand is growing for us very handsomely.

items.statement: Gross debt reduced from INR2,000 crores to INR1,448 crores YoY through DSO reduction and inventory management
items.quote: The gross debt, which used to be around INR2,000 crores a year ago, has come down to INR1,448 crores as at 31st December '25.

items.statement: Renegotiated customer contracts to reduce credit periods, lowering DSO days and freeing working capital
items.quote: We have approached the customers and then renegotiated the contracts saying that we'll reduce the credit period. And that has helped us in terms of reducing the DSO days, which in turn helped us reduce the debt.

items.statement: Average interest rate ~7% across group, net debt ~INR1,248 crores as of Dec 2025
items.quote: Interest rate would be around 7% on an average across the group. And our guidance was INR1,250 crores at the end of -- as at 31st March '26.

items.statement: Natural FX hedge through import-export matching, rupee depreciation creates minor exchange gains but not material
items.quote: We have a natural hedge sort of thing. Most of our imports -- most of our raw material procurement happens only from -- most of our imports -- most of our procurement is only through imports.

items.statement: Target 12-13% global outsourced instant coffee market share at peak capacity utilization of 77,000-78,000 tons
items.quote: When we are at peak capacity utilization, which is some time away from now, we probably will hit at 12%, 13% global market share of the outsourced market.

items.statement: Declared interim dividend of INR2.75 per equity share for FY25-26
items.quote: Additionally, the company CCL Products has declared an interim dividend of INR2.75 per equity share for FY25-26

items.statement: Post-Tet holiday green coffee price volatility risk if farmers hold stocks, Brazil crop outlook currently positive
items.quote: But the real test would be after pet holidays, if the farmers decide to hold on to the stocks, then we could see some more volatility coming in, some more price increases coming in.

items.statement: TTM free cash flow ~INR700 crores, expect slightly higher FCF in FY27 with improved operating profit and working capital
items.quote: For the current year, we have generated close to -- on a TTM basis, we would have generated close to INR700 crores of free cash flows, right? So we continue the same momentum and probably now that we have higher operating profit and working capital efficiencies, both will lead to higher free cash flow.

items.statement: Expects double-digit top-line growth in Q4 FY26, though summer brands have high base from last year
items.quote: That is what we expect that hopefully, we should get to double-digit growth. The only caveat is winter is extended, and we have to get to the summer.

items.statement: Standalone tax rate to reduce to 25% from FY27 due to budget amendments, consolidated rate around 20%
items.quote: But with this recent announcement, now it is going to be 25% tax rate. So in fact, it has come down with th e recent proposed amendments in the union budget

items.statement: Gross margin expanded to 70.6% (+30 bps), EBITDA margin improved to 33.4% (+110 bps) in Q3 FY26
items.quote: On the financial front, gross margin expanded to 70.6%, an improvement of 30 basis points, underscoring our rigorous cost discipline, judicious price hikes and benefits of input price stability. EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR384 crores, growing by 13%, while EBITDA margins improved to 33.4%, an expansion of 110 basis points.

items.statement: Winter season extended with erratic patterns; November strong, December mixed, January second half good
items.quote: October, November were damn good. The winter set in very early. November was superb. December, first half got warm. December, second half was again very good. January, first half, especially in the hindi Heartland got warm. January, second fortnight was very good.

items.statement: Digital brands (The Man Company, Brillare) grew 31% in Q3; expect sustained robust growth
items.quote: Quarter-on-quarter, we've seen growth strengthen in the digital brands. And this quarter, we've seen a very robust 31% growth over last year. And this growth in the coming quarters, we expect to sustain this robust growth.

items.statement: Quick commerce doubled sales, now 20% of e-comm; organized channels 32% of YTD sales (+280 bps)
items.quote: Our omnichannel strategy continues to perform well with quick commerce doubling its sales and now contributing 20% to our e -comm business. Overall, organized channels contributed around 32% year -to-date, increasing their contribution by 280 basis points ov er the previous year

items.statement: Trade inventories normalised, no excess stock; dealers holding very low inventory
items.quote: Absolutely. I think we have great -- we have no excess inventories as far as the trade is concerned. Naveen Trivedi: Sure, sure. Mohan Goenka: And they're very well, I think. We have migrated very well

items.statement: Amortisation of INR23 cr/quarter to continue 3-4 years, declining to INR80/70/60 cr annually
items.quote: So that will continue for another 3, 4 years, and the rate would come down gradually to INR80 crores, INR70 crores and INR60 crores kind of. So gradually, it will come down. In the next 4 years, it will completely be done.

items.statement: Second interim dividend of 600% (INR6/share) declared; total 9M FY26 dividend INR10/share
items.quote: I'm also delighted to announce that our Board of Directors have declared a second interim dividend of 600%, amounting to INR6 per share for FY '26. The total dividend declared in 9 months FY '26 amount to INR10 per share

items.statement: International sales grew 9% with double-digit growth in 7 Oils, BoroPlus, Creme 21, pain management; SAARC and CIS strong
items.quote: On the international front, our sales grew by 9% with double-digit growth in 7 Oils in One, BoroPlus, Creme 21 and our pain management range. We saw steady growth led by SAARC and CIS regions.

items.statement: Bangladesh market sales double-digit but primary sales low single-digit due to pipeline correction; elections Feb 12, Ramadan holidays March
items.quote: Bangladesh per se, in market sales, we have registered a good double-digit growth, but somehow we were correcting certain pipeline. But in the primary sales, you will reflect a very low single digit growth.

items.statement: Iraq and North Africa weak; Southeast Asia, SAARC, Russia, CIS, parts of Africa strong double-digit
items.quote: So we have faced certain pressures in what we call as other MENA like Iraq and some lukewarm response in certain North African markets. So that is where we have with a lukewarm. But most of the other markets, even our business spans in Southeast Asia, SAAR C, Russia, CIS, parts of Africa have all shown very good double -digit growth

items.statement: Engaged KPMG for future-ready supply chain transformation across omnichannel operations
items.quote: We have engaged KPMG to drive a future-ready supply chain transforming across omnichannel operations.

items.statement: Digital spends now ~50% of total media spends, targeting youth/new consumers
items.quote: Our digital spends now account for almost 50% of our overall media spends in line with evolving consumer media consumption trends, enabling sharper targeting and higher engagement.

items.statement: Summer season loading starts Feb-Mar; last year high base for summer brands (Navratna, Dermicool); winter extended may delay summer
items.quote: Navratna Oil and Navratna talc and Dermicool are big summer brands. And we have to load these 3 products now in the month of February and March. Yes. And last year basis were very, very high as far as the summer brands are concerned.

items.statement: No plans to enter coconut oil category despite competitors doing so
items.quote: Prashant, right now, we don't have plans.

items.statement: Input price stability contributed to gross margin expansion
items.quote: gross margin expanded to 70.6%, an improvement of 30 basis points, underscoring our rigorous cost discipline, judicious price hikes and benefits of input price stability.

items.statement: Value-added hair oil segment growing across industry; Kesh King and 7 Oils relaunches driving organic growth beyond low base
items.quote: The organic part is about relaunching it, redeploying it, putting the new plans, new communication, addressing the consumer concerns which came out, that's the hope for the future. So far, it looks good.

items.statement: Rural demand recovery outpaced gradual urban improvement in Q3 FY26
items.quote: During the quarter, consumption trends remained steady, led by sustained recovery in rural demand, which continued to outpace the gradual improvement in urban markets.

items.statement: Nutralite Professional launched Cheesy Delight and Slim Mayonnaise variants for food service channels

items.quote: On the Comfort Click business, it deepened its portfolio with the launch of 4 adult gummies variants, 1 probiotic gummies variant for kids and Pure Himalayan Shilajit Resin, reinforcing its position in high-growth Wellness categories.

items.quote: Additionally, the WeightWorld brand advanced its European expansion by entering Poland, Finland, and Portugal, strengthening Comfort Click's regional footprint and unlocking access to fast-growing Wellness markets in Europe.

items.statement: RiteBite Max Protein expanded to 2 additional international markets reaching 9 countries in first year

items.quote: Zydus Wellness initiated marketing and distribution for the Cuticolor brand in the organized channel.

items.quote: Net sales for quarter 3 financial year 2026 registered growth of 113.7%. Within this, Food & Nutrition segment delivered growth of 134%, while Personal Care segment declined by 1.4% during the quarter.

items.statement: Volumes excluding Comfort Click delivered double-digit growth in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Volumes for quarter 3 financial year 2026, excluding the newly acquired Comfort Click business, delivered double-digit growth, reflecting underlying demand momentum.

items.quote: On a year-to-date basis, financial year '26, excluding Comfort Click and seasonal brands, recorded strong growth of double-digit, in the high teens range, supported by mid-teen volume growth.

items.quote: On the raw material front, except for milk, other key inputs remained largely under control ahead of the upcoming season.

items.quote: On a consolidated basis, the company recorded EBITDA of INR610 million, representing a quarter year-on-year growth of 312.2%. EBITDA margin expanded to 6.3%, up from 3.2% in the previous year.

items.statement: Company certified as Great Place to Work for fourth consecutive year

items.quote: Everyuth continued to lead in the niche subsegments delivering double-digit growth in Y-T-D FY '26. The Tan Removal segment sustained strong growth, further enhancing brand saliency.

items.quote: Within the sweetener portfolio, market share expanded by 80 basis points as per MAT December 2025 report of Nielsen and IQVIA while Sugar Free Green delivered 19th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth.

items.statement: Nutralite delivered double-digit growth with 6-year CAGR driven by consistent portfolio performance
items.quote: Nutralite continued to broaden the portfolio through focused innovation supported by strong execution from dedicated B2B and B2C teams. The brand delivered double-digit growth with a 6-year CAGR, driven by consistent performance across the portfolio.

items.statement: RiteBite Max Protein EBITDA improved from breakeven at acquisition to approaching double-digit margins
items.quote: One year post acquisition, the RiteBite Max Protein business continues to significantly outperform its internal expectations across both value and volume metrics. items.quote: I think Comfort Click, we are looking at continued growth of top line in good double-digits, as we have mentioned. items.statement: RiteBite repeat purchase rates improving both online and in-store; positive spiral of distribution, investment, innovation driving throughput

items.statement: Improved segmental disclosures targeted by end of year
items.quote: So over the next few months, by end of the year, we'll come back and work on some of these things so that we can give you a better visibility.

items.quote: One of the points I also made in my speech was also there's almost INR90 million GST, which was budgeting support, which was in the last quarter, and some of the additional expenses in terms of investing in the additional people field that we have created. items.statement: Everyuth Q3 growth below expectation but YTD double-digit; offtakes building up; consistent 5-6 year performance with occasional quarterly volatility

items.quote: Anything is possible because the market is large enough. So if you're saying, is it possible? Yes. Will it be? Hard to say. items.quote: I think from a Comfort Click U.K.-based entity, they would first want to, where should I be? India is clearly one of the priorities, but we'll evaluate maybe in some time as things go along.

items.quote: Overall, I mean, early days to say, everything is in line. This I mean, 30 days, the real season starts from March-April. So these 30 days, yes, we are it's in line with our expectation, but that's it. Nothing beyond that.

items.quote: Yes. items.statement: Full-year FY26 revenue growth expected at 7-8%

items.statement: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin expected back to 13-14%

items.statement: EBITDA margin of 15-17% likely in H2 FY27

items.statement: Q3 FY26 revenue grew 11.1% YoY, sequential recovery from 5-6% in Q2
items.quote: During the quarter, the company delivered a healthy top line growth of 11.1%. This follows the sequential recovery witnessed in the previous quarter where revenues grew in the range of 5% to 6%.

items.statement: Actual demand improvement drove Q3 growth, not pre-buying ahead of price hike
items.quote: So, there is an actual improvement in demand. If you look at our growth even in Q2, we have grown by 5% to 6%. In fact, the price increase has happened only yesterday.

items.statement: Project share steady at 38-39% of sales; retail ~60-63%; project share stable for several quarters

items.statement: Geographic shift: UP now leading zone; Bihar, Jharkhand showing reversal; previously South/Kerala led

items.statement: FY26 capex INR 13.2 cr by Dec 25; measured outlay for maintenance, brand/retail initiatives
