items.quote: Obviously, if it keeps on increasing at the current trend, then again, we will have to revisit the position.

items.statement: Europe revenue expected to grow 20%+ annually over next few years with margin improvement
items.quote: I'm not just looking at top line growth, but we should look at Europe over the next few years as growing at 20% plus in revenues. But more importantly, we should be watching the margins to improve on that business.

items.statement: Europe revenue could reach INR400-500 crores by FY28-29
items.quote: Yes, yes. We can expect that. We can.

items.statement: FPP US portfolio expects at least 5 new product launches in FY27
items.quote: We have right now visibility for '26-'27, where there is expectation that at least five new products should be launched out of our own portfolio.

items.statement: Warren Remedies OTC business expected to grow at least 30% next year
items.quote: this number should go up safely by at least 30%.

items.statement: Consolidated other expenses targeted at INR150 crores per quarter
items.quote: we are confident to keep it at INR150 crores on a consolidated basis.

items.statement: Long-term debt to reduce to ~INR550-555 crores by March 2026
items.quote: So with that, we'll have at the year-end about close to about 550 or 555, that is the number for long-term.

items.statement: Maintenance capex of INR35-40 crores per annum for next 2-3 years
items.quote: Around 35, 40 max per annum would be the maintenance capex required.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin at 7.3% in Q3 FY26 vs 3% YoY
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA to sales for the quarter is 7.3% at INR315 million compared to 3% at INR120 million same quarter last year.

items.statement: Gross margin improved ~300 bps sequentially due to better subsidiary performance and portfolio mix
items.quote: These were both fledgling businesses earlier and were giving a drain on the business. So that has improved. In addition to which COGS at even IRL lev el have improved

items.statement: Target to stabilize at 13-14% EBITDA margin in next couple of years
items.quote: I feel in the next couple of years, we would be stabilizing at around 13, 14.

items.statement: International formulation revenue grew 26.2% YoY to INR1,356 million
items.quote: Revenues from International Formulation business grew by 26.2% at INR1,356 million compared to INR1,074 million same quarter last year.

items.statement: US formulation revenue grew 21.6% YoY to INR341 million
items.quote: Revenues from U.S. business for the quarter grew by 21.6% at INR341 million as compared to INR280 million same quarter last year.

items.statement: Europe formulation revenue grew 36.9% YoY to INR485 million
items.quote: Revenues from Europe for the quarter grew by 36.9% at INR485 million as against INR354 million same quarter last year.

items.statement: Emerging markets formulation revenue grew 26.8% YoY to INR495 million
items.quote: Revenues from emerging markets for the quarter grew by 26.8% at INR495 million as against INR390 million same quarter last year.

items.statement: API revenue grew 24% YoY to INR344 million
items.quote: Revenues from API business for the quarter grew by 24% at INR344 million as compared to INR278 million same quarter last year.

items.statement: Warren Remedies revenue grew >43% YoY in Q3 and ~38% YTD
items.quote: Warren Remedies have grown by more than 43% this quarter. And I think for YTD basis, it is in 38%.

items.statement: Europe YTD revenue INR167 crores; Q4 expected to be much better due to MMP Phase II approvals
items.quote: have done on YTD basis. Ankit Gupta: How much was it last year? Aditi Panandikar: Equivalent it was. And however, last year, if you remember well, we had major challenges due to the MMP execution because of which the fourth quarter for Europe was extremely poor. This year, in fact, like I mentioned earlier, many of the issues with Phas e II of MMP which allowed our -- wherein we have got approval

items.statement: Patalganga API site received EIR with zero 483s from USFDA
items.quote: Patalganga site of APIs has also received the EIR for USFDA audit where we had Zero 483s.

items.statement: Auric API block ready for validation batches; commercial supply pending USFDA/EU qualification
items.quote: the finished API block at Auric site in Aurangabad, which is part of the Warren Remedies Group, which is now ready and is taking validation batches of products. As soon as US FDA comes down and qualifies it or EU comes down and qualifies it, we will be able to sell in those markets

items.statement: Goa Plant II sterile lines restarted but meaningful contribution pending USFDA audit
items.quote: Well, nothing meaningful yet. I'll be very honest. In fact, we have started getting small amounts of sales from sterile, but it's still largely from outsourced, but we have begun.

items.statement: One-time remediation and penalty costs of INR8-9 crores in Q3; INR20 crores annual tech transfer costs
items.quote: Around INR8 crores to INR9 crores.

items.statement: New product introductions contribute 6.5% of India revenues
items.quote: the total new introductions to sales is now at 6.5% of India revenues.

items.statement: Launched 2 new OTC products: Sensodent DSP and Sensodent DPC
items.quote: launched 2 products, Sensodent DSP and Sensodent DPC. One is a daily sensitivity protection toothpaste and is an addition to our sensitivity product basket. And the o ther is a daily Procare toothpaste, which is actually our entry into clean toothpaste segment in the OTC area

items.statement: Ranked 21st in IQVIA prescription audit with 10.86 crore prescriptions, jumped over Pfizer
items.quote: we have jumped 1 rank and are now ranked 21st in the prescription audit with a total of 10.86 crores prescriptions, and we have jumped over Pfizer, and that is a matter of great pride for us.

items.statement: Goa Plant II under USFDA warning letter; Goa Plant I unaffected and supplying US solid orals
items.quote: The site which is under US FDA cloud for warning letter is only Goa Plant II. Goa Plant 1 in fact, is solid oral site and many of the new launches are from the solid oral sites as well.

items.statement: Total debt ~INR900 crores (INR700 cr main business, INR220 cr WRPL); long-term debt INR590 cr
items.quote: So our total debt right now sits at around INR900 crore s. INR700 crores in the main business and INR220 crores in

items.statement: Scheduled long-term repayment of INR135-140 crores per annum for next 2 years
items.quote: And then next 2 years, we have a significant amount of repayment at around about 135 to 140 per annum.

items.statement: Acute therapy demand unpredictable due to weather and post-COVID patterns; primary sales volatile but prescriptions growing
items.quote: Post-COVID, somehow the acute has not settled. We don't know what is happening. But of late, there is indication that things are back on a very kind of a path where you can ignore the COVID -- pre-COVID, post-COVID years. And now again, things are beginning to continue.

items.statement: Management expects Africa EBITDA margin to reach 7-8% in H1 FY27 and cross 10% in H2 FY27 driven by order book recovery.
items.quote: I am expecting Africa's EBITDA margin for next financial year, that is FY '27, by the second half of that year, cross 10% easily, maybe even stay at an average of about 10% in '27 based on the order volumes that we anticipate.

items.statement: India EBITDA margins will remain at current levels until US reciprocal tariff is corrected.
items.quote: India, until the U.S. tariff corrects, the macroeconomics will remain what they are. In the longer run, EU FTA will kick in and so will U.K. FTA. But un til that happens, we may see some degree of status quo with improvements only coming in from internal improvements that we will usher in

items.statement: Consolidated performance has bottomed out in Q3; improvement expected from Q4 led by Africa recovery.
items.quote: So on a consol basis, I think we can say it firmly that this is a bottomed out performance. And going forward, things should better from here on, primarily led by international operations.

items.statement: Q3 consolidated EBITDA declined 18% YoY to INR96 cr due to sharing US tariff burden; adjusting for tariff share, EBITDA would have grown 17%.
items.quote: We reported an EBITDA of INR96 crores, a decline of 18% year -on-year. This was primarily due to sharing a considerable portion of the U.S. tariff burden with our key customers. Adjusting for the burden share, our EBITDA should have grown by 17%.

items.statement: Net US tariff impact after supply chain offsets was INR40.2 cr in Q3; gross penal tariff impact was ~INR60 cr offset by INR20 cr from suppliers.
items.quote: The total impact of the penal tariff was closer to INR60 crores, and we set off about INR20 crores of it from our supply chain.

items.statement: Africa EBITDA margin was 1.5% in Q3 due to low volumes from AGOA expiry; expected to recover from Q4 as volumes return.
items.quote: EBITDA margin from Atraco is 1.5%. While the EBITDA margin for the India operations remains at the same level, at the average of around 11%

items.statement: Gross margin improvement in Q3 driven by productivity gains, product mix favouring India fabric, and strong fabric supplier negotiations linked to tariff pressure.
items.quote: The gross margin improvement happened because of more productivity gains and also product mix changes. Usually in spring, summer, we do have a lot of India-based fabric that we use. And we also did a strong negotiation with fabric suppliers given the tariff-related challenges that we had.

items.statement: Gross margin benefits from supplier negotiations will persist as long as US tariff remains high; product mix shifts in Q1/Q2 may lower gross margin but EBITDA margin protected.
items.quote: The only onetime benefit we got was our negotiations with supply chain as far as raw material is concerned, which is linked to US tariffs staying high. So as long as that re mains, that benefit will continue as

items.statement: US apparel exports declining since July 2025 despite strong retail sales; US retailers not yet passing cost to consumers but likely to in 2026.
items.quote: On the demand front, apparel exports into the U.S. witnessed a continuous decline since July 2025, despite retail sales posting a stronger growth during that period. Most U.S. retailers have so far not increased the prices for their customers. This is like ly to change in 2026 as retailers are seeking to pass on some of the cost increases to their customers

items.statement: EU and UK imports showed higher growth Jan-Nov 2025 vs prior year; company growing European revenue quarter-on-quarter from ~13% to 16-17% of mix.
items.quote: Our European revenue is constantly increasing quarter -on-quarter. We were at about 13%. Now we are further increasing it going forward, about -- we'll be about 16%, 17%. We are constantly increasing our European business going forward.

items.statement: Decent robust order book for Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 for both India and Africa; Africa order book rebuilt after August tariff changes gave Africa 10% advantage vs Asia 20%.
items.quote: I look at our order book for Q4 and Q1 of next financial year, we have a decent robust order book for both the quarters.

items.statement: Africa order book rebuilding due to 10% reciprocal tariff vs 20% for Asia; AGOA restoration possible with retrospective effect.
items.quote: In the month of August, we saw Asian countries see their reciprocal tariffs go up to 20%, while Africa remained at 10%. So even without AGOA, Africa enjoying a superior tariff regime as far as U.S. is concerned. So that has also helped us to build the business in Africa.

items.statement: Two India units (Bhopal phase 2, Karnataka) and Kenya expansion nearing completion; commercial production expected Q1 FY27; INR105 cr planned for FY26.
items.quote: These 2 units are in advanced stages of execution completion, and we expect the commercial production to happen in the next financial year. Apart from that, we have expanded the capacity in Kenya. That's a substantial portion. We are installing new machineries and expanding the capacity, bringing up another unit additionally in the existing premises itself. That will also come on stream in the nex

items.statement: Ramp-up margin impact minimal as expansions are within existing operational units.
items.quote: Most of the ramp-up related challenges have already been absorbed as currently expansions are all happening in the units, which -- where we have operations. So we don't anticipate a significant margin setback on account of this.

items.statement: US penal tariff burden sharing (discounts) to continue until tariff corrected; no ability to raise prices in current environment.
items.quote: I don't see any ability for us to increase prices in the interim, with high tariffs as well as the expectation of inflation in U.S., et c., our ability to increase prices is next to zero. So we will have to continue to seek ways to improve margins by operational improvements, supply chain - related cost savings as well as continue to book business by giving tariff-related burden share or tariff-re

items.statement: Tariff burden sharing reverses immediately when penal tariff removed; discounts adjust from next shipment clearing customs at lower rate.
items.quote: If our customer is able to take the goods at less than 50% tariff, let's say, the penal tariff of 25% goes away on a certain date, 1st of May, then any goods which they are able to clear customs in US at 25%, not 50%, our burden share stops from those shipments onwards.

items.statement: Using US cotton for ~25% of FOB value in cotton garments to offset reciprocal tariff; benefit may reduce in Q1 as mix shifts to synthetics from Far East.
items.quote: Yes. So I think we should have about 20, a little above closer to 25% of the FOB in cotton-based garments as US cotton. Bhavin Chheda: Yes. And sir, my last question, sorry, the third one... S. Ganapathi: And what will happen in the first quarter is that we will be switching more to synthetics. So that is when some of these benefits may come down because then we will be using

items.statement: Business predominantly seasonal fashion orders; no large program-based orders yet; European customers smaller but growing.
items.quote: So almost all our business comes from fashion orders. We don't do large program -based orders as yet. In the future, we may be doing it, but most of the orders are sought and won on a seasonal basis.

items.statement: Onboarding one new EU customer in next 1-2 months; three UK customers showing growth without tariff benefit yet.
items.quote: We have also, as I said in my opening remarks, we have added one more customer whom we will onboard in the next 1 or 2 months. So that will also give a further incremental growth from European business side.

items.statement: Bangladesh production volumes stable despite internal challenges; geopolitical issues and visa restrictions may impact ease of doing business going forward.
items.quote: While there are issues in Bangladesh, the production volumes from Bangladesh has not really fallen. So factories are working and factories are continuing to export from Bangladesh. So while there are some challenges brewing in that country on account of factor costs going up, on account of geopolitical situation, we have not yet seen an impact on Bangladesh till date.

items.statement: UK FTA signed July 2025 awaiting parliamentary ratification and implementation; zero-duty benefit not yet flowing.
items.quote: UK FTA was signed in July 2025. However, we have not seen the benefit of FTA flow through. It is awaiting implementation. So at the moment, the exports to UK are still tariff rated, and we have not seen zero tariff benefit flow through as yet.

items.statement: India-EU FTA recently announced; expected implementation ~1.5 years (2027); will give 12% duty advantage vs China and parity with Bangladesh/Vietnam.
items.quote: In the long-term, the recently announced India-EU FTA will open access to a significant market, placing Indian exporters at par with key competing countries like Bangladesh, Vietnam and a 12% duty advantage with China. This, along with India -U.K. FTA would accelerate sourcing from India.

items.statement: One-time gratuity provision of INR3.4-3.5 cr taken in Q3 due to New Labour Wage Code; no other one-offs.
items.quote: Apart from the tariff effect, whatever we have disclosed, we have also incurred -- taken a hit of INR3.4 crores on account of our gratuity restatement because of the New Labour Wage Code. So other than that, there is no one-off items.

items.statement: Africa EBITDA margin expected 7-8% in H1 and at least 10% in H2 of next financial year
items.quote: Africa for next financial year, we are anticipating at least in the second half going to 10% in the first half, staying at between 7% and 8% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: India margins to stay at current levels until U.S. tariff remains
items.quote: India margins will stay where they are until the U.S. tariff remains.

items.statement: Target to push African revenues to $120-125 million next financial year
items.quote: Our endeavour for next financial year is to try to push African revenues to 120 US$ million, 125 US$ million or thereabouts next financial year.

items.statement: European revenue share target 20-25% from current 14-16%
items.quote: Intention is to take it up to 20%, 25%. But these things do take time. These things take several quarters before the percentage of the revenue for Europe gets built up.

items.statement: Long-term India EBITDA margin target 12-13% and Africa 10-11% if U.S. tariff drops to 25% and EU FTA kicks in
items.quote: should be able to operat e at 12% to 13% EBITDA margin in India and about 10% to 11% in Africa

items.statement: India operating margin around 10% currently
items.quote: We are around 10% level in India at the operating margin level.

items.statement: U.S. EBITDA margin low single digits post tariff discounts; Europe margins 11-12.5%
items.quote: US margins will be in the low single digits post tariff discounts. Whereas European margins are in the region of about 11%, 12.5% or thereabouts.

items.statement: U.S. EBITDA margin 6-7% after tariff burden sharing; non-U.S. margins ~13.5% due to cost efficiencies
items.quote: when I look at EBITDA margin for US, it is in the order of 6%, 7% for US. And European margin or non -US margins have actually kicked up because of the cost efficiencies that we drove. So that is at a blend ed region of about 13.5% or thereabouts

items.statement: Africa operation EBITDA margin only 1.5% currently
items.quote: Africa operation is only 1.5%. The remaining amount, you can arrive at it. That is for India operation...

items.statement: GSP withdrawal impact minimal at 2.4% on margins
items.quote: That's 20% GSP discount on 12%. That's 2.4%. That is operating in the margins that it doesn't make an impact at the moment.

items.statement: Order book expected to swell driving better capacity utilization in Africa
items.quote: That improvement will happen primarily because the order book is going to swell and that itself results in better capacity utilization.

items.statement: Currency depreciation benefits may be retained while steep U.S. tariff remains; eventually shared with customers
items.quote: As long as the steep U.S. tariff remains, since we are bearing a significant burden, we may tend to hold on to some of those currency -related benefits for now. But eventually, in the longer run, those do get shared.

items.statement: Higher India-based raw material proportion helped negotiate with vendors; U.S. cotton content may decrease next season
items.quote: we may not have as much of US cotton in Q1, we may see some amount of tariff burden slightly increasing on that count. It may not impact margins much. It may affect us at about 1%, 1.5%.

items.statement: Sportswear dominant in European customer base; expanding sportswear business to offset margin challenges
items.quote: our European customer is sportswear dominant. And in fact, that is one of the reasons why we were able to expand our margins also. So we are continuing to push most sportswear-related business to offset some of the margin challenges that we have.

items.statement: Atraco growth faster than India would lower average selling price (ASP)
items.quote: If Atraco's growth happens at a faster rate than India, definitely, ASP -- average selling price will come down.

items.statement: European retailers actively onboarding Indian suppliers due to Bangladesh geopolitical concerns and prospective FTA
items.quote: many of them are actively present in India trying to onboard suppliers in India, looking at options to buy from India, even for retailers who are either to not buying from India, buy only from Bangladesh and other duty -free regions.

items.statement: U.S. retailers destocking inventory; imports down 1% while retail sales up 4%+
items.quote: U.S. imports are down by 1%. So there is a delta there, rig ht? U.S. retailers are importing less even though the retail sales are going up, which clearly indicates that they are not allowing their inventory to build up.

items.statement: Cautious on U.S. demand outlook for 2026 due to inflation, interest rates, geopolitics; demand growth may stay muted
items.quote: I wouldn't say there is going to be a demand upswing. On the contrary, demand growth will stay muted till this geopolitics plays out in 2026.

items.statement: Supreme Court tariff ruling unlikely to benefit supply chain; retailers would get windfall gain
items.quote: It's highly unlikely that, that benefit will accrue down to the supply chain. So it will be unfortunate, but our retailers will get a windfall gain if that happens.

items.statement: AGOA restoration would be prospective only; no duty refunds for past periods
items.quote: AGOA, no, no, no. So all that will be prospect. I don't think we'll get a duty refund for past, yes.

items.statement: Maintains FY26 defence revenue guidance of Rs 3000 crore; Pinaka dispatches to start in Q4
items.quote: We are expecting that from Q4, it will be quite (Inaudible) 12.15 moving towards our annual guidance number.

items.statement: Expects FY27 defence performance to be very good with gradual quarterly improvements; full guidance to be shared at start of FY27
items.quote: We have been improving our defence revenue and as we move forward in next quarter or next year, we will see gradual improvements on every quarter basis. So, in FY27, we are likely to perform very good.

items.statement: Total consolidated order book at Rs 21,000 crore including defence order book of Rs 18,000 crore
items.quote: Solar's defence business showed a splendid growth of 72% by hitting a revenue of Rs. (+700) crore in this quarter, evidenced by a record-breaking defence order book of Rs. 18,000 crores which takes us to the highest ever total order book of Rs. 21,000 crores.

items.statement: Defence order book split: Rs 6,500-7,000 crore domestic, Rs 11,000 crore international
items.quote: If you look at our total order book from defence, it's around 18,000 crores. And out of that, around Rs. 6,500 crores to Rs. 7,000 crores is from Indian market. And balance which is around, say, Rs. 11,000 crores is from the international market.

items.statement: Expects to maintain EBITDA margins around 27%-28% going forward
items.quote: So, we are confident that we should be able to maintain the EBITDA margins around 27%-28 % as we move forward also.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margins around 27% sustainable for next 3-5 years
items.quote: And based on those things, I expect that getting 27% on next 3-5 years should not be a big problem for us.

items.statement: International business crossed Rs 1000 crore revenue in Q3, up 35% YoY driven by commodity demand
items.quote: Our international business has crossed 1000 crore revenue in this quarter which is a significant increase of 35% year-on-year.

items.statement: African market demand strong; good traction in South East Asia, Turkey and nearby markets
items.quote: Specifically on your question on which geography. So definitely demand in African market is quite good. We are getting good traction in some of the South East Asian market also. We are doing quite good in Turkey and nearby market also.

items.statement: Domestic mining demand impacted by heavy monsoon and economic slowdown; expects 6-7% annualized growth long-term
items.quote: If you look at India business definitely in the first 9 months, the demand was greatly impacted due to heavy monsoon and some slowdown in the economy.

items.statement: Defence revenue hit quarterly high of Rs 702 crore, up 72% YoY; Pinaka rockets to start contributing from Q4
items.quote: Defence revenue was quarterly highest till date at Rs. 702 crores versus Rs. 409 crores up by 72% showing a wonderful fix in the defence business.

items.statement: Commercial production of 155 mm calibre ammunition to start in Q4; participating in long-term RFPs for 23 mm and 30 mm programs
items.quote: Like I said in the previous quarterly call that we are planning to start manufacturing of 155 mm calibre ammunition. So, we're still working on that. And commercial production definitely should start in the Q4.

items.statement: New facilities at Dhule, Maharashtra and Dholpur, Rajasthan optimize domestic manufacturing footprint
items.quote: Our new facility at Dhule, Maharashtra and Dholpur, Rajasthan optimizes and reinforces Solar's position as a dependable long-term partner to the mining and infrastructure sectors within the country.

items.statement: Total CAPEX update to be shared with Q4 numbers; guided ~Rs 2500 crore for the year
items.quote: We can share the total CAPEX update on the Q4 numbers, please.

items.statement: Customer mix: CIL 10% (down from 13%), non-CIL institutional 11% (down from 14%), housing/infra 10% (down from 13%), international 40% (up from 38%)
items.quote: CIL in the basket stands at 10% compared to 13%. Revenue from non-CIL and institutional stands at 11% compared to 14%. Revenue from housing and infrastructure stands at 10% compared to 13%. International revenue stands at 40% compared to 38% up by 35% year-on-year.

items.statement: Raw material consumption decreased from 53.5% to 48.71% of revenue; absolute cost Rs 1241 crore vs Rs 1056 crore YoY
items.quote: The percent of raw material consumption has decreased from 53.5% to 48.71%. In absolute terms, the cost is around Rs. 1241 crores versus Rs. 1056 crores in the same quarter previous year.

items.statement: Forex exposure approximately Rs 20 crore, normal routine cost of operating in multiple currencies
items.quote: So, this is one which is a very normal cost of the business and approximately it is in the range which we expect. So, it's approximately around Rs. 20 crores odd which is very, very normal cost.

items.statement: Expects overall business growth of 15% annually; 20% CAGR possible over 3-5 years combining mining and defence
items.quote: If you combine the mining and defence together, definitely growing at (+20%) is not at all difficult for solar at this stage for next 3-5 years down the line.

items.statement: Key challenge: maintaining stakeholder relationships while expanding defence across zones; priority: adopting new technologies and developing products
items.quote: As we are expanding in defence in various zones or areas, it will be a challenge for us to maintain the relationship and strong connect with all our stakeholders. So that is, I believe, is a key priority or challenge as well.

items.statement: Working on MALE drones, loitering munitions, humanoid robots; will share details once programs fructify
items.quote: We have been sharing that we are working a lot on announcing our product especially loitering munitions and then we have started work on the MALE category of drones also and it is going to take some time before we really comment on the total targeted market and what we can get out of that.

items.statement: FY26 revenue expected flat in value terms; volume decline but will recover next year
items.quote: Current year, I think we will be flat, flat to positive, but yes, flat. That is what I can tell you. It is in value terms. In volume terms, definitely some decline, but I'm sure we'll more than make up for it in the next year.

items.statement: Land acquired in Indore and Palwal for future expansion; tower crane plant planned on 22-acre Palwal site
items.quote: Currently, first of all, we will be developing our tower crane plant on our -- this new piece of land, which we have bought in Palwal. We have bought 2 pieces. One is about 22 acres. The other which we are about to get possession is about 86 acres.

items.statement: Current capacity INR 5,000-5,500 crores, can reach INR 6,000 crores with tweaks; tower crane capacity 800-900 units, expanding to 1,100 units
items.quote: See, our current capacity is upwards of INR5,000 crores. I think a little tweak here and there, it can go to INR5,500 crores to INR6,000 crores.

items.statement: Defense orders of ~INR 500 crores in hand; expect INR 150-200 crores execution next year
items.quote: Currently, we have orders of approximately INR500 crores in hand, which have to be executed. Because of certain procedural delays, they did not go into execution and we start to go into execution now very soon.

items.statement: Construction equipment EBIT margin at ~20%, near peak; agri equipment EBIT margin target 12-15% from current ~4-5%
items.quote: Construction equipment, this quarter, we are already at close to about 20% EBIT level, which I think is one of the best in the country and maybe in the world as well. I think we are touching our peak.

items.statement: Gross margin improvement driven by cost efficiencies, automation, pricing power, and product mix shift to higher-value cranes
items.quote: With our cost efficiencies, which we are building in and automation and productivity improvement and our continuous focus on maintaining, ensuring and increasing our sales price and our input cost in terms of raw material. It is a combination of that.

items.statement: Price increases post-CEV norms now fully accepted by market after 8-10 months; input cost pass-through with 3-4 month lag
items.quote: Now that acceptability is very much in place. We struggled in quarter 1 and to some extent in quarter 2 on account of price acceptability. Now I think it is 9 months down the line, 10 months down the line. Now it has totally flown into customers.

items.statement: Shift to new-generation cranes (AI features, clutchless transmission, rigid chassis) and higher-tonnage models driving margin improvement
items.quote: The current quarter, I think it's more to do with the product mix, because what is happening, new generation cranes are becoming more popular than the traditional hydra cranes. In that, again, the higher tonnage cranes are becoming more popular.

items.statement: Demand stabilized in Q2, returned to normalcy in Q3 after BS III/IV to CEV transition; sequential revenue growth of 15% in Q3
items.quote: Our quarter 3 performance, along with the sequential improvement in demand as the year progressed, has reinforced our assessment that the initial softness following the transition from BS III and BS IV to CE V V was temporary. Demand stabilized in quarter 2 and returne d to normalcy in quarter 3

items.statement: Ground-level traction improved from December onwards; EPC order books strong, payments improving, steel prices rising indicating manufacturing pickup
items.quote: We are definitely improving. There's been a lot of traction December onwards. It took us by surprise. I think now, especially with the European FTA deal, just the sentiment obviously how much it will take shape, when it will take shape, but sentiment matters more than anything else.

items.statement: Export contribution 6-7% in FY26, targeting 10%+ in FY27; defense 2% in FY26, targeting 4-5% in FY27
items.quote: Last year, we did 4% contribution from exports. This year, we are looking at somewhere around 6% to 7%, more towards 7%. In the current year, 7% exports and 2% defense will make it about 9% contribution to our business. Currently, 9%, so next year, we can be pretty confident it will be somewhere upwards of 10%.

items.statement: Chinese competition aggressive in excavators (20-25% share) and heavy cranes (>30-40 tons) via predatory pricing and credit terms; antidumping duty recommended but not notified
items.quote: In the last 5 years, they've taken up 20%, 25% market in India on account of their predictive pricing and the credit terms and all they offer. So yes, they are reasonably aggressive in terms of their pricing and their positioning strategy with respect to credit.

items.statement: Antidumping duty on Chinese crawler/truck cranes recommended by DGTR in September but not notified by Finance Ministry; CIE PLI scheme expected in 2-4 months for import substitution
items.quote: Finally, duty was recommended on the Chinese cranes in the month of September. Unfortunately, for some good -bad reason, it has not been notified by the Finance Ministry.

items.statement: CIE PLI scheme to focus on crawler cranes, truck cranes, piling rigs, reach stackers, aerial platforms; FY25 revenue/investment as benchmark
