items.quote: Q3 onwards, October onwards, we started seeing some uptick in consumption, both rural and urban. Now OND normally is a good consumption month because all festivals, Dussehra, Diwali and then marriage season and then overall up to Christmas and New Year, the market is always good.

items.statement: Management expects at least single-digit growth in Edible Oils and double-digit growth in Food going forward, driven by stable commodity prices and improving consumption sentiment.
items.quote: We are looking at least single-d igit growth in Edible Oils and double-digit in Food going forward. That is what indicates -- gives -- indications are like that from the

items.statement: Last 12-month EBITDA close to INR2,200 crores; Q3 EBITDA stood at INR637 crores, consistently delivering over INR600 crores quarterly.
items.quote: Our last 12-month EBITDA now is close to INR2,200 crores and the Q3 EBITDA stood at INR637 crores. Consistently, we are delivering EBITDA of plus of INR600 crores quarter after quarter.

items.statement: Alternate channel last 12-month revenue close to INR4,800 crores, growing rapidly with quick commerce at 30% of alternate channel volumes.
items.quote: Alternate channels for us continued to scale very rapidly with last 12-month revenue from this only channel close to INR4,800 crores now.

items.statement: No specific capex guidance provided; focus on distribution expansion, leveraging oil distribution for food, and scaling alternate channels.
items.quote: the big initiative that we would be taking is on the distribution side, number one. And number two, given the encouraging results on the quick com and alternate channel, we would be spending quite a big focus and big efforts on this particular channel

items.statement: Distribution reaches close to 950,000 outlets directly; rural distribution scaled to over 60,000 towns, focus on improving throughput and efficiency.
items.quote: As far as the distribution is concerned, now we reach close to 9,50,000 outlets across the country directly. Rural distribution has scaled up to over 60,000 towns now, and we are now focused on improving throughput and distribution efficiency.

items.statement: Edible oil prices ~20% higher YoY drove grammage reductions to 750g for affordability; grammage now stable at 750g for palm/soya/sunflower, not mustard.
items.quote: Now at 750, it is almost stable at 750, and all the competitors are at 750 levels. This is only to reduce the price and create affordability. And I'm sure if the Edible Oil prices remain stable or calm, the grammage might go up, and it is possible.

items.statement: Non-rice/wheat food products (sugar, nuggets, poha, suji, rawa, maida, besan) now 30% of Food & FMCG volume, growing double-digit.
items.quote: Products other than rice and wheat continued to grow in a strong double digit and now contribute to the 30% of the Food & FMCG volume. And these products are basically sugar, nuggets, poha, suji, rawa, maida and other products, which constitute now 30% and growing in a double digit.

items.statement: Launched Fortune Multi Grain Atta; expanding health and convenience portfolio with cold-pressed oils, high-protein atta, Xpert functional oils.
items.quote: in that direction, in the health and convenience portfolio. We launched Fortune Multi Grain Atta during this quarter. And the initial feedback is quite positive on the product. Our value-added and convenience offering across oils and food are also steadily scaling as we plan to expand this portfolio further in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Food & FMCG: 25% revenue from alternate channels (75% general trade); in top metros, alternate channel share reaches 50% for staples.
items.quote: Food & FMCG staples business, 25% business comes from alternate channels. 75% comes from your general trade. This is at all India level. Now when you go to different towns, say, rural, there isn't any alternate channel, everything is general trade. But rest in towns when you go, you have different alternate channels doing well.

items.statement: Fortune brand growing faster than second brand King's; all-India Fortune market share increased, consumers returning to preferred brands after price corrections.
items.quote: In fact, we are finding -- people are coming back to Fortune. Growth of Fortune is higher than our second brand. And that can be very clearly seen because Nielsen is also catching the same thing. And we have seen our brand Fortune doing better.

items.statement: Nepal soybean oil imports under SAFTA reduced 30-40% from peak of 200,000 tons/quarter to ~125,000 tons/quarter; AWL market share recovering in affected regions.
items.quote: Nepal in flux has reduced by almost 30%, 40%. At its high, it was almost 200,000 tons per quarter. Now it has come down to roughly around 125,000 tons per quarter. So it has reduced, not that it has become 0, but the impact has surely come down.

items.statement: US tariff deal announced (details pending); branded exports tariff reduced from >50% to 18%, potential benefit for oleochemical exports once details clear.
items.quote: the branded exports were attracting more than 50% of tariffs, which now come down to 18%.

items.statement: Basmati rice market share on MAT basis crossed 11.9%; wheat flour market share maintained; non-Basmati rice and Chakki Atta volumes impacted by pricing and local competition.
items.quote: Now Basmati rice market share is now on a MAT basis has actually crossed 11.9%.

items.statement: Edible oil volumes grew 8% YoY with broad-based growth across categories and double-digit growth in mustard oil.
items.quote: Edible Oil volumes grew by 8% with broad-based growth across categories and double-digit growth in mustard.

items.statement: Kohinoor brand (acquired May 2022) registered 32% YoY growth; King's brand (2nd largest in India) oil and food together grew ~7% YoY.
items.quote: Kohinoor, which we acquired in May 2022, registered a strong growth of 32%, while King's, which is now second largest brand in India. Oil and food together grew by close to 7% year-on-year.

items.statement: G.D. Foods (acquired April 2025) delivered 15% revenue growth with 18% underlying volume growth; material margins at 54%, distribution expenses key focus.
items.quote: On G.D. Foods, which we acquired this year in April 2025, the business delivered a growth of -- revenue growth of 15% with underlying volume growth of 18%. Material margins stood at healthy 54% and distribution expenses remained the key focus.

items.statement: Oleochemicals: specialty chemicals now 7-8% of oleo volumes, offering higher margin potential; oleo volumes flat, contributing ~30% of segment with high single-digit margins.
items.quote: We are steadily diversifying into specialty chemicals, which now contributes close to 7%, 8% of our oleo volumes and offer higher margin potentials.

items.statement: Continuously evaluating inorganic opportunities for Foods; acquired Kohinoor, G.D. Foods, Omkar Chemicals previously; will pursue if valuation fits.
items.quote: as a company, we keep evaluating a lot of proposals, which comes on our table, and that's a continuous process that keeps going on. I would not comment anything whether the opportunity is there today, yes or no. But I think, yes, as a process, we continue to look out for such kind of any opportunity that comes in and it fits into our valuation and if it's into our bill, we certainly do it as we di

items.statement: Wheat prices rangebound INR27.5-29/kg disadvantages large procurers vs small repackers; carrying cost not recovered due to flat prices, impacting Chakki Atta growth.
items.quote: On wheat side, this year, the wheat prices more or less remained rangebound between the range of INR27, INR27.5 to INR28.5 or INR29 per kg, flattish kind of price trend that we have observed. This essentially puts players like us into a disadvantageous position who procure a significant amount of wheat during the harvest.

items.statement: Food business FY27 revenue target of INR10,000 crores may slip to FY28; striking distance expected in FY27 with G.D. Foods contribution and new interventions.
items.quote: I think we -- if not INR10,000 crores, I think we would be in a striking distance that we are trying to work out. Yes. But FY '27, INR10,000 crores seems to be now kind of number, which we may not be able to achieve,maybe it may go to FY '28, but we would suddenly be into a striking distance of this number.

items.statement: FY27 guidance: revenue INR850-900 cr, EBITDA INR280-300 cr, PAT INR180 cr
items.quote: we are expecting the numbers to reach INR850 crores to INR900 crores and EBITDA of almost INR280 crores to INR300 crores bottom line.

items.statement: SNVA Veranda FY27 target: revenue INR250 cr, EBITDA >INR60 cr
items.quote: For FY '27, we expect to be able to reach a top line business of about INR250 crores in SNVA Veranda, and we are targeting an EBITDA in excess of INR60 crores for FY '27.

items.statement: Commerce vertical EBITDA expected to grow 60-65% in FY27
items.quote: we expect these measures to potentially drive up our EBITDA in the commerce vertical by about 60% to 65% in FY '27.

items.statement: K-12 managed schools EBITDA expected to grow 60-65% in FY27
items.quote: we expect our EBITDA from the schools -- K-12 managed schools business to significantly move up probably by another 60%, 65% in that segment, too.

items.statement: Demerger of commerce vertical filed with NCLT; targeting NCLT approval by end-April and listing by June 2025
items.quote: the attempt would be to get the approval from NCLT if we can before end of April, and possibly start work on the listing and trading permissions and the hope will be to get this listed and traded sometime in June of this year.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin expanded to 45% from 328% YoY EBITDA growth
items.quote: Operating expenses were streamlined and reduced over the past year. This cost discipline has translated into a 328% of surge in EBITDA compared to year -on-year to INR53 crores, with EBITDA margins expanding to 45%.

items.statement: Gross margin improved to 65% in Q3 FY26 from 62% a year ago
items.quote: Gross profit is up 47% year -on-year to INR76 crores, driving gross margin of 65% in earlier quarter from 62%.

items.statement: Enrolments up 55% YoY to 111,363; collections up 46% YoY to INR144 cr in Q3
items.quote: Enrolments increased to 111,363, up 55% year -on-year driving collections growth of 46% to over INR144 crores for the quarter.

items.statement: Government test prep expansion via franchising in South India; online programs launching in Telugu and Hindi next year
items.quote: there is a plan to expand the network of our centers through franchising. You will see that happening, especially in the southern markets of Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Kerala. Next year, we also plan to launch our online programs in both Telugu and Hindi.

items.statement: Three colleges being added, operational by June; another 10-15 planned for coming academic year
items.quote: currently have 15. Three are being added as we speak. They will go operational by June. We'll start taking students from this academic year. For the coming academic year, there is a plan to add another 10 to 15 more, which will literally double our size in FY '27

items.statement: Refinancing INR140 cr of high-cost debt at 17.23% to sub-10% rate (9.9%)
items.quote: We have mentioned in the disclosure, it's only to refinance the existing debt with the effective credit high -cost debt at a rate of 17.23%. The entire proceeds are being used to refinance. As you have seen in earlier calls, we are sub two-digit, we got at 9.9%.

items.statement: Existing debt INR222 cr at average 17% interest; refinancing underway to reduce interest cost
items.quote: Our balance sheet remains strong with existing debt of INR222 crores at an average interest rate of 17% as on date. And there have been steps in refinancing being taken, which will be seen in the ongoing quarters.

items.statement: SNVA Veranda formed via strategic disinvestment of vocational assets; combines domestic brands with SNVA's international university network
items.quote: We have also successfully created SNVA Veranda through the strategic disinvestment of our vocational education assets. This transaction combines Veranda's strong domestic scaling brands with SNVA's international university network across the U.S., U.K., Europe and Singapore.

items.statement: SNVA Veranda targets listing when EBITDA crosses INR100 cr as debt-free business; potential FY28 listing
items.value: INR100 cr EBITDA target for listing
items.quote: internally, our target is to take it for a listing only when it crosses about, at least, INR100 crores of EBITDA as a debt-free business. So we think those days are not too far away.

items.statement: AI courses contribute 35-40% of Edureka revenue and growing monthly
items.quote: almost about 35% to 40% of our revenue comes through AI courses as of now, which is increasing by every month.

items.statement: AI being piloted across telecalling, assessments, content generation, customer support, multilingual delivery, and mentor tools
items.quote: across functions, across verticals, it's currently being tested. And as Aditya mentioned, early days for us to put a number on efficiency. But across all functions, it is being used, and we have significant incentive programs for all our employees based on the percentage of AI adoption that they are able to showcase.

items.statement: Budget 2026 initiative for professional bodies (ICAI, ICSI, ICMAI) to offer modular courses for MSMEs; Veranda uniquely positioned to leverage
items.quote: this was one of the most beneficial thing that was announced in the budget, that they will have professionals with specific defined certification who can help MSMEs do their compliance but at a more affordable cost. So given our strong presenc e in this vertical across online, offline and the academic segment, we expect to play a significant part

items.statement: Demerger timeline dependent on NCLT approval and lender NOCs; targeting acceleration but regulatory process remains key risk
items.quote: we are in the process of submitting no objection certificates from both our secured and unsecured lenders, which we hope to get during the month. Subsequently, we plan to be able to get it to NCLT so that we can proceed possibly directly to a meeting of the shareholders in a court convening here.

items.statement: Succession planning in commerce vertical: Professor J.K. Shah (64) as Chairman; his children and next-gen leaders groomed for 2-3 years; Bhanwar Borana heads online; regional brands have successors
items.quote: Already, there are multiple people in the organization, which is, when I say organization, the commerce vertical, who are being groomed as successors. The professor's son and daughter themselves have been with the organization for the last 7, 8 years, and they are being mentored to take on a significant role over the next 3, 4 years.

items.statement: Cash deployment priority: deleverage to debt-free, fund academic expansion (10-15 colleges), buy residual stakes via internal accruals, grow commerce vertical
items.quote: currently we want to sort of deploy it quite significantly to as quickly as possible deleverage the organization so that at some point we make it debt-free. Having said that, there is a plan to expand our academic footprint. So we are currently working on a plan to add possibly about 10 to 15 managed colleges going into the next year.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 focus: enhance faculty, digital admissions, university/corporate partnerships, high-value courses, marketing efficiency
items.quote: Looking ahead to Q4, our efforts remain focused on enhancing faculty capabilities, driving digital-led admissions, strengthening university and corporate partnerships, introducing high -value courses and optimizing marketing efficiency across all our functions.

items.statement: 9M FY26 revenue INR350 cr (+29% YoY), EBITDA INR150 cr (+409% YoY), PAT INR114 cr
items.value: 350 cr revenue; 150 cr EBITDA; 114 cr PAT
items.quote: consistent strong quarterly execution since the start of FY '26 has translated into a robust 9 -month performance with revenue reaching INR350 crores, up 29% year -on-year. Expenses remained broadly stable, enabling operating leverage and EBITDA has been reaching INR150 crores for 9 months number with a substantial 409% year-on-year increase. This execution-led performance over the 9 -month period

items.statement: Commerce demerged entity (J.K. Shah Commerce Education) projected FY27 revenue >INR250 cr, EBITDA >INR60 cr, 25% CAGR, targeting 200k+ learners annually
items.quote: The entity is projected to generate over INR250 crores in revenue by FY '27, growing at a 25% CAGR with EBITDA exceeding INR60 crores, and it will pursue a separate public listing over time.

items.statement: Management denies 3i Infotech's allegations of undervaluation and conflict of interest in the 2010 divestment, citing Deloitte valuation and board composition.
items.quote: So, this allegation is being made after almost 16 years. So, the divestment was made in 2010. And now in 2026, they are making this allegation.

items.statement: Management states the 2010 divestment to Indus Innovest was at INR 55 crores, above the Deloitte valuation of INR 30-35 crores.
items.quote: Deloitte valuation report valued the company around INR 30 crores, INR 35 crores, but actually, we divested at a value of INR 55 crores.

items.statement: Management explains preference share redemption terms agreed with 3i Infotech in 2015, including staggered payments and event-based triggers.
items.quote: So based on that, there was a detailed term sheet and a detailed agreement between me and the 3i Infotech regarding this redemption of preference shares.

items.statement: Management confirms INR 5 crore preference shares were redeemed in 2017 per agreement terms after a trigger event, with shares returned and forms filed.
items.quote: So, then what they did was they said, okay, you redeem this INR 5 crores. We have a letter from them also. We redeemed, then they returned the preference shares.

items.statement: Management attributes current allegations to new 3i Infotech management unaware of prior settlements, noting a year of inactivity before the EOW complaint.
items.quote: So, this new management is only raising whatever was done by the old management. This new management put some committee to examine all these things and raising all these matters after 15 to 17 years.

items.statement: Management expresses confidence in legal victory but acknowledges the process may be prolonged.
items.quote: With all those details, we feel we are very confident that we can come victorious in the process of law and court, but it may take some time and prolong.

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance maintained at INR800-900 crore with 2.5-3% net margins
items.quote: So we are holding on to the guidance, yes. For this year, there's no change in that.

items.statement: FY27 guidance to be shared by end of March or April call
items.quote: For the next year, we'll give you more accurate numbers probably by end of March or in the April call, rather than giving it now.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 9-10%
items.quote: So guidance of margin, we are still maintaining 9% to 10%.

items.statement: Strong demand across product segments; peak season Q4 and Q1 expected to be strong with decent summer
items.quote: I see a good demand coming from various customers across product segments. Of course, this month -- this quarter and next quarter are our peak seasons. And we hope that with a decent summer, the number should be at their peak.

items.statement: Quarter-on-quarter demand improvement visible; demand expected to continue in Q4 and Q1 FY27
items.quote: Yes, quarter-on-quarter, of course, numbers are also depicting it. So the demand has gone up. And fourth quarter and Q1 next year, I see, I mean, I see the demand to continue.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 standalone EBITDA margin in excess of 11% at INR23 crore; 9M FY26 EBITDA margin shade under 11% at INR55 crore
items.quote: What is important to note here is that the EBITDA margins have been very healthy for Q3. Standalone basis if you see, it's in excess of 11%. The absolute number is roughly INR23 crores for Q3 alone.

items.statement: Non-AC products contributing to healthy EBITDA and PAT margins; compressor business at 5% EBITDA margin currently
items.quote: EBITDA margins with China competition being there and without backward integration are about 5%.

items.statement: AC division running at full capacity for next few months; refrigeration capacity completely booked for season; compressor 60%+ capacity booked for calendar year targeting 70-80%
items.quote: Over the next three, four months for the current season, we are running on full capacity, or we have an order book which expected to run on full capacity for the next few months.

items.statement: Chennai AC plant (300k units) operational by Q1 FY27; EMS capacity to double by Q1 FY27; compressor at 50%+ utilization, 2.8M capacity targeting 7.5M if QCO decision favorable; washing machine pilot done, ramp up from April-May
items.quote: Chennai capacity, we have taken charge in January. We hope that by Q1, the plant will become operational. And the real benefit from that plant will only come for the next financial year.

items.statement: FY26 capex ~INR120 crore spent so far, targeting INR130-150 crore by March end; FY27 capex dynamic, to be finalized by April
items.quote: So we have, I think, done almost close to INR120 crores so far. And we are looking at a INR130 crores to INR150 number by March end in CapEx.

items.statement: AC share to reduce to 60-65% in FY27 from current ~60-64%; other products (EMS, refrigeration, compressor, components) to contribute 30-35%
items.quote: We believe AC in the overall revenue will go down, will be about 60% to 65%. And 30%, 35% will come from the other products that we have invested in in the last couple of years.

items.statement: Added 3 new AC customers, onboarding 4th this season; Voltas share stable or growing; AC moving from OEM to ODM with multiple customers
items.quote: But the other customers, we've added three customers currently, onboarding maybe another one customer this season. So four additional customers this year in AC apart from Voltas.

items.statement: Most customers on conversion pricing model (cost pass-through); some on quarterly price reset; no massive copper price impact expected on margins in next 2-3 months
items.quote: So maximum customers, we are on a conversion pricing model. So there, the cost is transferred and the impact to us is minimal.

items.statement: Compressor backward integration and capacity expansion to 7.5M dependent on government QCO decision in March; lateral capacity expansion based on customer bookings
items.quote: We also want to see how the government decision on QCO comes in March. Based on that, we will decide on a quick ramp up to add another five-odd million capacity.

items.statement: Debt may increase slightly in FY26 but no major addition unless major compressor expansion; targeting debt-equity <1x; will balance debt and equity
items.quote: As far as debt is concerned, debt from the current level of this financial year, debt might go up slightly, but I don't see major debt getting added to the books because of capacity expansion.

items.statement: Evaluating fund requirements; will raise equity/debt based on segment progress and government decisions; equity raise decision after commitments
items.quote: So we are, of course, evaluating fund requirement and we will raise wherever there is necessary. But we are still evaluating based on what segments and how they are panning out.

items.statement: 9M FY26 revenue INR505 crore (AC INR300-320 cr, EMS INR70-80 cr, Refrigeration INR60-70 cr, Compressor INR15 cr, Components balance)
items.quote: Out of the total INR500 crore revenue that we have done, roughly INR300 crores to INR320 crores would come from air conditioning business. About INR70 crores to INR80 crores is coming from EMS business and INR60 crore to INR70 crore is coming from refrigeration and the remaining is coming from compressor.

items.statement: Compressor 2.8M capacity can generate INR400 crore revenue; at 60%+ utilization ~INR240 crore
items.quote: the 2.8 million capacity that we have can achieve a top line of aboutINR400 crores based on the product mix and the size of compressors that we make

items.statement: Washing machine peak revenue potential INR100 crore with current capacity; FY27 utilization target 50-70%
items.quote: Peak revenue we can currently achieve is about INR100 crores. And capacity expansion, what I mentioned was '28, we will decide based on how '27 goes.

items.statement: EMS current setup capable of INR150-180 crore top line at 4 lakh CPH
items.quote: The current EMS setup, we are capable of doing about INR150 crores, INR180 crore top line.

items.statement: Refrigeration premium multi-door market ~0.5M units in India; current monthly revenue INR1.5-2 crore
items.quote: My estimate for the frost-free and multi-door segment is between -- should roughly be about 0.5 million in the country.

items.statement: Channel inventory high per peers but reduced by Oct-Nov; primary sales strong in Dec-Jan; risk if secondary sales muted
items.quote: I think dried up by the end of, I mean, or dried up in the sense it significantly reduced by October, November, from whatever discussions we've had. December onwards, of course, the channel has again started buying material

items.statement: Compressor order booking and backward integration dependent on government QCO decision; indecisive decision could slow order booking
items.quote: But if there is no finite timeline, and it is an indecisive decision, then yes, order booking will also get slower.

items.statement: Mainboard migration process ongoing; awaiting BSE clarification on traded volumes; targeting H1 FY27 for migration
items.quote: We are in process of that. There is one technicality in terms of the traded volumes that we are discussing with BSE, which is a criteria of BSE, but not with NSE, but the documentation is in process, and we are hoping to file soon.

items.statement: Cross-flow fan capacity matched to IDU capacity; not sold standalone; PCB manufacturing maybe for captive in future
items.quote: So cross-flow fan capacity, we are increasing to match with effectively our capital requirement. We are not selling cross-flow fan as a standalone product.

items.statement: FY27 capex estimated below Rs.500 crores, down from ~Rs.1,000 crores in FY26
items.quote: Next year CAPEX is probably, below Rs.500 crores would be our estimate.

items.statement: FY26 capex ~Rs.1,000 crores, with Rs.600-700 crores for Noida; Rs.3,000 crores planned over next five years
items.quote: We have been somewhere in the Rs.1,000 crores range, I think, on next year CAPEX. So, this is Rs.3,000 crores over the next five years.

items.statement: Added 537 beds in 9M FY26 (99 Patna, 110 Ranchi, 328 Noida); 496 beds brownfield headroom (193 Lucknow, 81 Patna, 222 Noida)
items.quote: During the first nine months of FY26, bed capacity increased by 18% year-on-year with addition of 537 beds, comprising 99 beds at Patna, 110 beds at Ranchi and 328 beds at Medanta Noida.

items.statement: Noida added 102 beds in Q3 FY26 to reach 328 beds and 14 OTs; 222 more beds planned
items.quote: At Noida, we accelerated the ramp-up with the addition of 102 beds, taking the total bed count to 328 beds, with 9 new operation theatres added this quarter, taking the total count to 14 operation theatres.

items.statement: Inpatient volumes up 14% YoY, outpatient volumes up 20% YoY in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Inpatient volumes grew by 14%, while outpatient volumes increased by 20% year-on-year.

items.statement: Occupancy ~59% on expanded bed days; occupied bed days up 7% YoY
items.quote: Occupied bed days increased by 7%, translating into an occupancy of approximately 59% on expanded bed days.

items.statement: ARPOB up 10% YoY to Rs.67,361; developing hospitals ARPOB up 8% to Rs.56,853
items.quote: ARPOB increased by 10% to Rs.67,361, supported by improvements in ALOS and case mix.

items.statement: ALOS reduced 7% YoY to 3.02 days
items.quote: Our average length of stay reduced to 3.02 days, a 7% year-on-year improvement.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 21.8% (incl. Noida loss); ex-Noida 25.4%; mature 23.9%; developing ex-Noida 31.7%
items.quote: EBITDA, including Noida, stood at Rs.2,494 million, with margins of 21.8%, reflecting the expected impact of early-stage operating losses from our newest hospital.

items.statement: Mature hospital margins impacted by higher employee costs and R&M; expects 200-300 bps efficiency gains over time
items.quote: I do believe there are efficiencies, especially in some of the older units that we can eke out, and we will work towards that. You will see some of those efficiencies are already playing out on some cost items.

items.statement: International patient revenue up 30% YoY to Rs.703 million; OPD pharmacy up 30% to Rs.465 million
items.quote: We also saw encouraging momentum in international business; international patient revenue grew by 30% year-on-year to Rs.703 million, driven by higher volumes, while our OPD pharmacy business grew 30% to Rs.465 million.

items.statement: CGHS rate revision positive, ~Rs.7-10 crores impact in 9M FY26; insurance contract renewals at 2025 tariffs to benefit FY27
items.quote: CGHS rate revision has of course been beneficial for the industry. It has been a long demand after many, many years. There has been positive movement across the group o n that in terms of tariff increases. We have captured some of that in the nine month numbers that you see. I think, high single digit in terms of gross is the impact on

items.statement: ARPOB growth guidance 5-7% annually; realization growth 3-5%
items.quote: We have always maintained that ARPOB's growth is 5% - 7% a year as opposed to what we have seen maybe in the last three, four years where we have seen much higher growth.

items.statement: Noida hired ~220 doctors; majority of hiring done, some niche departments (Pediatrics, Obstetrics, Liver Transplant, Vascular Surgery) still pending
items.quote: We have now signed up about four or five major insurance contracts, other insurance contracts are coming onboard. We have not yet taken any of the panels in Noida that may come on as we move forward in line with our broader philosophy of serving every strata of society and every category of patients.

items.statement: Lucknow received JCI accreditation in January 2026, first in region
items.quote: I am also pleased to share that Medanta, Lucknow has received the Prestigious Joint Commission International (JCI) quality accreditation in January 2026. Medanta, Lucknow is the first hospital in the region to be accredited by JCI.

items.statement: Net cash ~Rs.600 crores as of Dec 2025 (loan Rs.600 crores, cash >Rs.1,200 crores)
items.quote: We have a loan of about Rs.600 crores and a cash position of over Rs.1200 crores, so, net cash is about Rs.600 crores.

items.statement: Noida EBITDA loss Rs.320 million in Q3 FY26; peak losses hoped to be behind but no breakeven guidance given
items.quote: Medanta, Noida, which commenced operations in September 2025, completed its first full quarter of operations during Q3. The hospital g enerated Rs.343 million in revenue and reported an EBITDA loss of Rs.320 million in line with the investment required to operationali ze a facility of this scale and high standard

items.statement: War for clinical talent across North India; retention strong but hiring costs rising
items.quote: I think this is a phenomenon the industry is facing, to the best of my knowledge across the board. I can tell you in the regions where we operate, which is more on the northern side.

items.statement: One-time statutory impact of Rs.366 million from new labor codes classified as exceptional item
items.quote: Consolidated profit after tax stood at Rs.950 million, impacted by higher depreciation and finance costs related to Noida, initial operating losses and a one -time statutory impa ct of Rs.366 million, arising from the implementation of new labor codes classified as an exceptional item

items.statement: FY26 presales guidance of INR 4,000 crores will be very well achieved; projects 25% presales growth YoY for FY27
items.quote: And on our FY '26, our presales guidance of INR4,000 crores is going to be very well achieved. As I have mentioned, because of sales of one of our projects that we are taking up in this quarter, and you'll be very happy to hear our results in April.

items.statement: Projects 25% presales growth year-on-year going forward for FY27
items.quote: While I don't want to give any guidance for FY '27, I can tell you our growth trajectory will continue. And we will see a 25%. And as usual, we will stay cautious in our forecast, but we'll project a 25% growth year-on-year going forward.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 presales INR 837 crores; YTD FY26 presales INR 2,676 crores, up 23% YoY
items.quote: For the Q3 FY '26, our presales performance has been encouraging, and we have achieved INR837 crores of presales taking the total of presales for the year -to-date FY '26 to INR 2,676 crores. That's INR 2,676 crores. That's a 23% year-on-year growth on a year-to-date basis.

items.statement: Launched 5 projects YTD FY26 with total GDV INR 5,835 crores, achieving 83% of full-year launch target
items.quote: On our project launches, we've launched one more project in the Q3 with an estimated GDV of INR 919 crores. This takes our total to 5 launches this year with a total GDV of INR 5,835 crores for year-to-date FY '26. With this, we've achieved 83% of our full year launch target.

items.statement: Added 4 projects in 9M FY26 with estimated GDV INR 8,650 crores, 1.44x annual guidance
items.quote: To summarize, we've added 4 projects totally in the 3 quarters of FY '26, having an estimated GDV of INR 8,650 crores. Notably, that's about 1.44x our annual guidance. We've already crossed our annual guidance by about 1.44x.

items.statement: Lokhandwala Cluster total estimated GDV approximately INR 3,900 crores
items.quote: In Q3 FY '26, we have added another project, which is part of our Lokhandwala Cluster. With this, the total estimated GDV of our Lokhandwala Cluster would be approx imately INR 3,900 crores

items.statement: Total estimated GDV across 4 cluster developments about INR 12,500 crores
items.quote: And you asked a question about the total GDV across these 4 clusters. We are looking at sorry, across 3 clusters, I have the number, but just give me a second. It's about INR 12,500 crores across all our 4 cluster developments.

items.statement: Commercial project 33 Fifteen at Bandra West launched with estimated GDV INR 950 crores, 18% sold
items.quote: The journey has commenced with the successful launch of 33 fifteen at Bandra West. This is a marquee commercial project development with an estimated GDV of about INR 950 crores, of which 18% have already been sold off the launched inventory.

items.statement: Planning commercial launch at Prabhadevi in H1 FY27 with estimated GDV INR 1,150 crores
items.quote: Building on the momentum, we are actively working towards another commercial launch in the first half of FY '27. This will be at Prabhadevi with an estimated GDV of about INR 1,150 crores.

items.statement: Thane commercial project construction to commence in FY27 alongside commercial acquisition opportunities
items.quote: Additionally, construction activity at our Thane commercial project is expected to commence again in FY '27, alongside the several commercial acquisition opportunities that we are actively evaluating.

items.statement: YTD FY26 gross margin 35% vs 32% YTD FY25
items.quote: Our gross margin for year-to-date FY '26 is 35% vis-a-vis 32% for year-to-date FY '25.

items.statement: Underwrites projects with gross margin of 35% driven by location and value transformation
items.quote: Financially, we continue to maintain strict thresholds with upfront equity capital limited to 10% of total project GDV up to launch. And this allows us a margin expansion by underwriting projects with a gross margin of 35%, driven, of course, by the locati on and led by value transformation post development of these projects.

items.statement: Construction spend YTD FY26 INR 718 crores, up 18% YoY from INR 609 crores
items.quote: Our construction spend has risen from INR 609 crores year-to-date FY '25 to INR 718 crores in the year-to-date FY '26, reflecting an 18% year-on-year growth so far.

items.statement: YTD FY26 OCF INR 229 crores; Q3 OCF low at INR 2-3 crores due to higher construction spend on new launches
items.quote: YTD FY '26, our OCF stands at INR 229 crores. This again reflects our continued focus on disciplined execution and prudent cash management.

items.statement: Expects OCF to pick up significantly from H2 FY27 as new launches mature
items.quote: The OCF has been low for this quarter, particularly, but I expect it to go up, particularly from the second half of the next financial year. Not that it will be at that level, what has been in the quarter 3, but then there should be a significant upwards movem ent of the OCF in the second half of the next financial year.

items.statement: Collections YTD FY26 INR 1,770 crores, up 12% YoY; targets 75-80% collection efficiency vs presales
items.quote: We have grown in collection by 12% the same time last year, we did INR 1,580 crores. And this year, we have done INR 1,770 crores in the 9 months. Collection, as I said, since there are large amount of new projects, the construction pace is picking up. Collections are construction linked. We should be seeing this efficiency achieved definitely, for sure, in the next year.

items.statement: Gross and net collections are same; difference in reporting due to JV/DM project cash flows not consolidated in OCF
items.quote: In our case, the gross and net collections is the same. While when we say the net collections, some of the JV projects and some of the DM projects, while on the operating number, we report their collection. But in the OCF, we only report to the extent it is consolidated into our financials.

items.statement: Gross debt INR 625 crores as of Dec 31, 2025; gross debt-to-equity 0.22:1; free cash INR 717 crores; net cash positive
items.quote: As of 31st December '25, our gross debt is at INR 625 crores, translating to a gross debt-to-equity ratio of 0.22:1. This is very well within our guidance range. We've ended the quarter with free cash of about INR 717 crores. again underscores our healthy liquidity position. We remain net cash positive status

items.statement: India Ratings assigned A+ with Positive Outlook; ICRA has A+ with Stable Outlook
items.quote: As you are aware, in addition to ICRA's existing rate of A+ with a Stable Outlook, India Ratings has also assigned to us a credit rating of A+ with a Positive Outlook.

items.statement: DA to launch timeline improved to ~12 months; examples: Stella 8 months, Panorama 11 months, Crescent 10 months, Privé 12 months
items.quote: Further, we are improving continuously our go -to-market timelines. Once the development agreement is signed, a project typically moves to launch within almost 12 months. This year, we have launched multiple projects within these 12 months from the date of DA.

items.statement: Completed 3 projects YTD FY26 covering ~1.98 million sq ft: Belle Vue, Paramount F Wing, Crown Tower C
items.quote: I am pleased to announce that y ear-to-date FY '26, we have completed 3 projects covering approximately 1.98 million square feet. These include Rustomjee Belle Vue, which is a plotted development, Paramount F Wing, which is an SRA redevelopment and Rustomjee Crown, which is at Prabhadevi, w here we've completed Tower C.

items.statement: New launches contributed 32% of 9M presales and 37% of Q3 presales
items.quote: So in 9 months, our 37% of the total sales have been contributed -- 32% for the 9 months and 37% in the quarter 3 is contributed by the new launches. 1/3 of the presales basically is contributed by the new launches.

items.statement: Balmoral project in Chembur seeing slower sales due to price points; sample home ready this month; deferred payment schemes offered
items.quote: Of course, the price points that we have started out there are something that market is just not able to or has still not been able to digest. And what we've understood is that, we'll have to first bring it to some form of creation where people will be able to see what's really happening. And our sample home is about to get ready later this month.

items.statement: Cluster redevelopment under Regulation 33(9) provides higher incentives for developers and larger area for societies vs 33(7)(B)
items.quote: Larger the development gives an opportunity to give some area or some landmarks to the community in terms of development of amenities, social in frastructure. And that is why additional incentive is given to the developer and the housing societies.

items.statement: Finished inventory GDV approximately INR 220 crores
items.quote: No, I'll tell you the total value of the finished inventory is about INR 220-odd crores.

items.statement: Crown project inventory INR 276 crores; Towers A&B largely sold, Tower C part OC received, full OC expected this quarter
items.quote: So inventory at Crown is in 2 buckets. One is we are all aware that our landowner also has his stock to sell. I don't have a ready answer for you as to his inventory. But our inventory is about INR 276 crores, not about pretty precisely about INR 276 crores.

items.statement: BD deployments ~INR 650 crores in FY26; expects ~25% growth to INR 850-1,000 crores in FY27, ~40% debt funded
items.quote: So, this again depends largely on what kinds of developments come our way in '27. But this year, we've done about INR 650 crores in terms of BD deployments or whatever. So you can say that maybe a 25% growth thereof would be about INR 1,000 crores or something INR 850 crores to INR 1,000 crores, let's see.

items.statement: Has huge debt headroom at current 0.22:1 D/E; FY27 BD funding ~40% debt, rest internal accruals/OCF
items.quote: So, Ritwik, as you know, we are at a very reasonable debt -equity ratio. So , we have a huge amount of headroom to go as far as debt is concerned. So yes, obviously, a part of the capital will come from debt. And also internal accruals, so -- going forward, our OCF will also support this kind of development activities that we need to undertake.

items.statement: MMR demand continues; Western suburbs strong; data-driven location selection near infrastructure drives traction
items.quote: And also the Western suburbs continue to be strong. And if you've seen our BD, all the cluster developments that I have maintained, 3 of them are in the Western suburbs, where there's a great amount of demand that we see even today. And all the data, again , points towards a strong growing population in these areas.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin for 9 months FY26 at 24.9%, closer to lower end of guidance
items.quote: Accordingly, the adjusted EBITDA margin for 9 months '26 is 24.9%, which is closer to the lower end of our EBITDA guidance.

items.statement: R&D expense for Q3 FY26 at 2.9% of sales, within full year guidance range of 2.5% to 3%
items.quote: The R&D expense for Q3 '26 remains within the range of 2.5% to 3% of our guidance for the full year FY26.

items.statement: Capex spend for 9 months FY26 at INR473 crores, 4.4% of revenue, in line with guidance of 4% to 5% of revenue
items.quote: Our capex spend for 9 months FY'26 was INR473 crores, which is 4.4% of total revenue and the same is in line with our guidance of 4% to 5% of revenue.

items.statement: Domestic revenue grew 11.1% YoY in Q3 FY26 to INR3,046 crores, organic growth 9.1% excluding OTC
items.quote: In quarter 3 financial year '26, our domestic revenue grew 11.1% year -on-year to INR3,046 crores, supported by strong organic growth of 9.1%, excluding OTC.

items.statement: Chronic therapies grew 16.7% in cardio and 14.4% in antidiabetes in Q3 FY26
items.quote: We continue to do well in our focus area of chronic therapies as we witnessed strong growth of 16.7% in cardio and 14.4% in antidiabetes in quarter 3.

items.statement: Inhaler portfolio including Symbicort and Combihale growing at 30%, delivering 1.3x IPM growth
items.quote: Our inhaler portfolio, including Symbicort and Combihale continue to grow at 30%, deliver ing 1.3 times the growth of the IPM.

items.statement: Vonalong in gastro grew 86% YoY, significantly outperforming IPM growth of 54%, achieved Number 1 rank in 9M FY26
items.quote: In gastro, Vonalong recorded an impressive 86% year -on-year growth s ignificantly outperforming the IPM growth of 54% and achieved the Number 1 rank in 9 -month financial year '26.

items.statement: Crenzlo in cardio emerged as Number 1 brand in branded generics with 92% YoY growth
items.quote: In cardio, Crenzlo has emerged as the Number 1 brand in the branded generics category with strong 92% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: OTC revenue grew 5.2% YoY in Q3 FY26 vs decline in Q2, 9M FY26 OTC revenues increased 5.6%
items.quote: OTC revenue grew 5.2% year-on-year in quarter 3 compared to the decline in quarter 2. For 9 months financial year '26, OTC revenues increased 5.6% de spite some softness in the general trade channel

items.statement: Secondary sales of Gas-O-Fast, Manforce and Ova News grew 33%, 8% and 36% respectively in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Secondary sales of Gas-O-Fast, Manforce and Ova News grew 33%, 8% and 36%, re spectively, during quarter 3.

items.statement: Modern trade and e-commerce channels registered over 40% growth, contribution increased to 13% of OTC sales from 10% last year
items.quote: Modern trade and e -commerce channel s registered over 40% growth, increasing their contribution to 13% of OTC sales, up from 10% last year.

items.statement: Export revenues grew 14% YoY to INR521 crores in Q3 FY26, 9M FY26 exports increased 51% to INR1,503 crores
items.quote: Export revenues grew 14% year-on-year to INR521 crores in quarter 3 this year. For 9 months financial year '26, exports increased 51% to INR1,503 crores.

items.statement: BSV portfolio delivered double-digit growth in Q3 FY26, BSV prescription business surpassed FY25 sales in 9M FY26
items.quote: The portfolio delivered double -digit growth in quarter 3, driven by strong performance across both domestic specialty and exports. The restructured prescription portfolio which transitioned t o Mankind effective 1st of November 2025 has performed really well. And for the 9 -month financial year '26, the BSV prescription business has already surpassed financial year '25 sales.

items.statement: Gross margin increased 170 bps YoY to 72.6% in Q3 FY26 from 70.9% in Q3 FY25, driven by price increase, favorable mix, inventory accrual release
items.quote: Our gross margins for the quarter has increased by 170 basis point year-on-year basis to 72.6% from 70.9% in Q3 '25. This increase is a combination of sal es price increase effect, favorable sales mix and release of certain inventory-related accruals.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin declined 170 bps YoY to 25.9% in Q3 FY26 from 27.6% in Q3 FY25, due to higher R&D and employee costs
items.quote: Our adjusted EBITDA margin for the quarter is 25.9% as compared to 27.6% in Q3 '25. This decline of 170 basis points is largely attributable to increase in R&D cost by 70 basis points, and the balance is due to higher employee costs.

items.statement: Reported EBITDA margin 22.9% in Q3 FY26, lower by 300 bps vs adjusted EBITDA due to exceptional items
items.quote: Our reported EBITDA margin for the quarter is 22.9% which is lower by 300 basis points as compared to the adjusted EBITDA margin of 25.9% in Q3 '26. This decrease is attributable to exceptional items comprising of New Labour Code adoption, stamp duty on slump sale of BSV branded generic business within the group, and impairment of some noncurrent surplus assets.

items.statement: Net operating working capital days at 51 days on trailing 12 months basis vs 52 days in corresponding period, working capital value decreased INR110 crores QoQ
items.quote: The net operating working capital days for the quarter on a trailing 12 months basis is at 51 days as compared to 52 days in the corresponding period. The working capital in value terms has decreased by INR110 crores between the current quarter and the previous quarter.

items.statement: CFO to EBITDA ratio increased to 93% in 9M FY26 from 68% in 9M FY25, driven by working capital optimization and government receivables realization
items.quote: During the 9 months FY '26, our CFO to EBITDA ratio has increased to 93% as compared to 68% in 9 months FY'25. This is primarily on account of improvement in the working capital as well as realization of certain government receivables.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR4,294 crores as of Dec 31, 2025, net debt to adjusted EBITDA ratio improved to 1.3x from 1.4x as of Sep 30, 2025
items.quote: In line with our prudent financial strategy, we continue to strengthen our balance sheet and have reduced our net debt to INR4,294 crores as of 31st December 2025, resulting in the net debt to adjusted EBITDA ratio of 1.3x in Q3 '26 on a trailing 12 months basis, which has improved as compared to net debt to adjusted EBITDA ratio of 1.4x as on 30th September 2025.

items.statement: Finance cost decreased to INR157 crores in Q3 FY26 from INR170 crores in Q2 FY26, driven by repayment of INR1,500 crores commercial papers in Oct 2025
items.quote: The finance cost for Q3 FY'26 has decreased to INR157 crores from INR170 crores in Q2 FY'26. This reduction is primarily driven by repayment of last tranche of commercial papers worth INR1,500 crores in October 2025.

items.statement: Chronic contribution increased 200 bps YoY to 36.7% in 9M FY26 from 34.7% last year, led by outperformance of 1.2x vs IPM ex GLP-1
items.quote: In 9 months financial year '26, our chronic contribution increased by 200 bps year -on-year to 36.7% versus 34.7% last year, primary led by continued outperformance of 1.2x vs IPM ex GLP-1.

items.statement: In-licensed portfolio less than 2% of overall sales mix as of Q3 FY26
items.quote: Tushar, as of now, the portion of specialty portfolio or the in-licensed portfolio, in particular, is quite negligible. It is less than 2% or so in the overall sales mix.

items.statement: GLP-1 launch on track for day 1 launch around March end FY26
items.quote: So it's a currently innovator market, and we are on track for a day 1 launch. It would be around March, somewhere around March end. So we are on track, and we expect to be a participant in the launch in day 1.

items.statement: Udaipur facility received EU GMP certification, strengthening international capabilities
items.quote: As part of our ongoing commitment to global quality standards our Udaipur facility has received EU GMP certification, further strengthening our international capabilities.

items.statement: Approximately 20-25% of field force including managers is new, hired in phases over last 15-18 months
items.quote: Approximately 20% - 25% is new. Sudipta Roy: 20% including all new managers and field force, it is overall around 20%. This 20% also it's not at one go. So it's happened in phases

items.statement: Attrition in field force has gone down drastically, teams becoming more stable quarter on quarter
items.quote: And obviously, in the last couple of quarters, that attrition, which was happening has gone down drastically. Initially, we asked people to leave. And during this process, even good people left. Then we saw a huge attrition because that meant insecurity creeped in people's mind.

items.statement: Anti-infective segment growth muted due to relationship-driven nature and team transition, gradual recovery expected as relationships mature
items.quote: However, very rightly said, performance in the anti -infectives segment for Mankind has been relatively muted. Why? Because this category is people and relationship driven where prescriptions are typically ranging from 3 to 5 days. So as our teams get settled and doctor relationship will mature, we expect consistent growth over the coming quarters.

items.statement: OTC primary sales growth muted due to stockist reduction, cash-and-carry business stopped, and accounting policy differences in modern trade/e-commerce
items.quote: See, last 3 quarters or 4 quarters what we have done, we have taken plenty of transformation. I mean maybe we mentioned in the past that from a few thousand stockists, we reduced down number of stockists, those who would be responsible for doing o ur OTC business. That's also one of the major reason that this kind of reflection is coming

items.statement: PCPM improved to INR7.2 lakhs as of Dec 31, 2025 from INR6.5 lakhs as of Mar 31, 2025 on trailing 12-month basis
items.quote: Mankind's overall PCPM has also improved to INR7.2 lakhs as on December 31, '25 from INR6.5 lakh as of March 31, 2025 on a trailing 12-month basis.

items.statement: Secondary sales grew 8.5% YoY in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Further, our secondary sales during the quarter grew by 8.5% year -on-year.

items.statement: Management expects unit volumes to be flattish in FY27 with revenue growth driven by higher ASPs
items.quote: So demand from -- as I said earlier, demand unit-wise, in my view, would be flattish. It may not degrow because India digitization, PC penetration is still very, very low. And the higher selling price will help us to get the revenue.

items.statement: Management expects continued positive revenue trend in coming quarters due to further price hikes and preponed demand
items.quote: We are not seeing any softness in pricing. There is no indication so far of any softness in the pricing.

items.statement: Q3 saw sustained sales momentum with channel partners stocking inventory ahead of expected price increases and component shortages
items.quote: During the quarter under review, demand conditions remained strong. This was probably one of the best performing third quarter as usually, this quarter is followed by a high Q2 seasonal and there is a major dip.

items.statement: India PC market delivered one of its strongest quarters ever with shipments growing upwards of 10% year-over-year
items.quote: The domestic PC market delivered one of its strongest quarter ever in this quarter with shipments growing upwards of 10% year-over-year.

items.statement: Q3 consolidated PAT margin was 1.85% with PAT of INR75 crores, up 132% YoY
items.quote: Revenue from operations increased by 43% to INR 4,030 crores and PAT for the same period was INR75 crores, registering a growth of 132% year-on-year with PAT margins at 1.85%.

items.statement: Management expects margin trend to continue similar to Q3 with business market size, ASP and product mix all in similar mode
items.quote: Yes. So currently, business market size trend, average selling price, all 3 are in the similar mode. So our expectation is that it will be the similar trend only. We are not seeing any major variation.

items.statement: Component price increases vary: motherboards no increase, some products 20-30%, RAM 2x-3x, laptops/desktops up 20-30% with further hikes expected
items.quote: There are some products, where there is no price increase at all, especially in products like motherboard. There are some products, where the price increase is between 20% to 30%. And there are some p roducts like the RAM, where the price increase is 2x or even 3x

items.statement: 43% YoY revenue growth driven ~50% by volume and ~50% by ASP increase (including dollar appreciation)
items.quote: Yes. So more than -- I would say 50% is volume growth and 50% is because of the ASP, which is also supported by the dollar appreciation.

items.statement: PES (branded desktops, notebooks, workstations) share increased to 56% from 51% YoY, LIT share decreased to 44% from 49%
items.quote: However, in the current Q3 of 2025, the PES business has gone up and now it is at 56%. So there is a 5 percentage basis point increase in the PES business in terms of ratio.

items.statement: Dell business started in previous quarter, expected to be decent in Q4 and substantial in FY27
items.quote: Absolutely. In fact, in Q4 also, it will be decent. And next year, it will be substantial.

items.statement: Inventory days 56, debtor days improved to 47 from 61 YoY, creditor days 43, working capital days stable at 60
items.quote: Inventory days increased marginally to 56 days, primarily to support strong demand and ensure product availability. While remaining well within a well-controlled range, debtor days improved to 47 days from 61 days a year ago.

items.statement: Positive operating cash flow of INR34 crores for 9M FY26 after periods of outflow in earlier years
items.quote: On cash flows, after periods of outflow in the earlier years, we generated a positive operating cash flow of INR34 crores for year-to-date.

items.statement: Current debt-equity ratio 0.5, expected to maintain around that level; blended cost of borrowing 7.5-8%
items.quote: 0.5 is the debt equity, which currently is there. And we expect looking at the business growth and all, we expect to maintain around that only.

items.statement: Credit rating upgraded to AA category; primary objective to reduce borrowing cost while maintaining working capital cycle for increased revenue
items.quote: So let me add to what Himanshu mentioned is that with rating increase, we -- our primary objective was to reduce our cost of borrowing.

items.statement: Opened new branch in Solapur, now 55 branches across 55 towns in India
items.quote: In addition, we also launched a new branch in Solapur, which is now our 55th branch in India, an unprecedented network of branches, service center and warehouses spread across 55 towns of India.

items.statement: Pan-India network serves 10,000+ distribution partners across 700+ locations nationwide
items.quote: Today, our pan-India network of distribution serves over 10,000-plus distribution partners across 700-plus locations nationwide, providing unmatched reach, faster fulfilment and localized service capabilities.

items.statement: New Labour Code notified Nov 21, 2025 led to incremental INR4+ crores impact from higher gratuity, leave liabilities and enhanced employee benefits
items.quote: Further, following the notifications of the new L abour Code by the Government of India on 21st November 2025, the company has prudently recognized an incremental impact of over INR4 crores, primarily on account of increased gratuity obligations related to past service costs, higher leave liabilities arising from the revised definition of wages and enhanced employee

items.statement: INR14 crores ESOP cost provisioned year-to-date for attracting, retaining and incentivizing key talent
items.quote: On the people front, we incurred INR 14 crores of ESOP cost year-to-date provisioning, reinforcing our commitment to attracting, retaining and incentivizing key talent, while aligning employee interest with long-term value creation.

items.statement: Micron declared Crucial consumer brand end-of-life; will impact next financial year but Micron enterprise business continues with backup plans ready
items.quote: Yes. So very valid. That's the only little bit concern point that we have since they have declared crucial business as end of life, but they will continue to do Micron business. So yes, we will have a hit in the next financial year.

items.statement: Supply constraints expected to continue with prices rising periodically; main concern is unaffordability on B2C side rather than supply shortage
items.quote: My bigger worry is the price increases and hence, the unaffordability, especially on the B2C consumer side, more than the supply.

items.statement: Base business (ex-large deals) grew ~24% for 9M FY26 vs guidance of 15-20%; growth without INR2,000 crores project orders from last year
items.quote: Yes, Bhavin, ji, so that -- I think that's a very pertinent point. I'm happy to share that on a 9 months to 9-month basis, our revenue growth is 5%, but all this growth, even bigger 5% growth is without any project order.

items.statement: Management focuses on own planning and execution capabilities (55 branches, 700 towns, CRM, AI) rather than competing on pricing, credit or service
items.quote: I think we focus more on ourselves. And as I have started saying that one is a very strong business planning, which is done months in advance. And second, because of our geographical reach in 55 towns of India and 700 towns, where we have our customers, our execution, we continue to strengthen those capabilities.

items.statement: UAE subsidiary set up for execution in SAARC countries where material pickup preferred from Dubai/Hong Kong; business expansion to follow
items.quote: So as a part of -- one is the need for execution because in SAARC countries, material pickup is normally preferred from either Hong Kong or Dubai. So at this moment, it is more for execution purpose. Once we set up the operations and start expanding, then we'll look at the business angle.

items.statement: Large deal pipeline decent but execution slower due to supply extensions and price volatility; conversions expected in FY27
items.quote: The pipeline is decent, but the execution because from the supply side and because of the price increasing, the execution is far slower. So for example, you pick up a project today and if it is scheduled to be executed after 3 months, generally, what is happening is, one is the supply gets extended beyond 3 months.

items.statement: Dollar appreciation contributing to ASP increases and revenue growth
items.quote: While the industry is witnessing an uptrend in the IT product prices due to global supply constraints, and dollar appreciation.

items.statement: Revenue target for FY26 revised upward to INR1,900 crores from earlier INR1,710-1,720 crores
items.quote: So instead of INR1,710 crores, INR1,720 crores, I think we will touch probably INR1,900 crores this year.

items.statement: Revenue target for FY27 projected at INR2,060 crores with potential to cross INR2,100 crores
items.quote: Next year, we are projecting that we will do 20% on INR1,720 crores, which comes to about INR2,060 crores, if I'm not mistaken, right? So I think we should cross that. We are building up enough capacity that we should cross that figure next year from INR1,900 crores to go up, maybe we'll cross INR2,100

items.statement: Capex of INR120 crores spent in 9MFY26, total INR150 crores projected by June-July 2026 for two new plants
items.quote: INR120 crores would be the outgo by the end of March because all the machinery and all will be in. Then another, I think, INR30 crores or INR40 crores will be left for first quarter of the nextyear. So that is the INRL50 crores we had projected that we will spend on these 2 existing plants

items.statement: Current capacity utilization high with ~10% headroom before new Gujarat plant commissions by June-July 2026
items.quote: think our utilization is pretty high now. So we are doing - let's say, if we have done INR522 crores, that means we are already doing about INR156 crores, INR157 crores a month. Probably we still have scope for another 10% increase before the next capacity will come into play

items.statement: AP Plant 2 (heavy structures) and Gujarat Plant (PEB) to commission in phases between June and December 2026
items.quote: these have started, and both these will be in play in different phases between June and December. Now, while we were looking at the market in the last 6 to 8 months, we found that, as you have seen from our results, the demand is there in the market

items.statement: Heavy structures capacity target raised to 40,000-45,000 tons/year from 20,000-24,000 tons to be a serious market player
items.quote: So we felt that to be a serious player in the market, we need to have a capacity of about 40,000 to 45,000 tons, and we need to start it today so that we can be a serious player in the market.
