items.statement: Laminates double-digit EBITDA margins expected next year
items.quote: Double-digit margins next year for sure.

items.statement: MDF margin recovery expected over next 1-1.5 years as capacity additions slow and demand grows 20%+ CAGR
items.quote: The equilibrium should be at least maybe over the course of the next year, 1.5 year. So, during this time period, you should se e margin recovery

items.statement: MDF: Badvel line extension +70k CBM in Q1 FY27 (total ~625k CBM); UP MDF 300k+ CBM in ~2.5 years from land possession
items.quote: On the MDF side, I think we'll be able to unlock 70,000 cubic meters additional once we are able to extend the line. I think that will be within Q1 of the next financial year itself. And post that, we will be limited where total capacity, which should be around 625,000 cubic meters per annum. And as far as the Uttar Pradesh project is concerned, that will have a MDF capacity of -- in excess of 3 l

items.statement: UP project INR 1,100 cr total (MDF ~INR 800 cr, plywood ~INR 330 cr); funding from internal accruals, final plan later
items.quote: Funding out, I think it is a dynamic scenario. Currently, we have very strong internal accruals. So going forward, as and when we finalize the funding plan, we shall get back to you.

items.statement: Plywood Q4 FY26 capacity ~430k CBM after internal expansions at Kandla, Guwahati, Joka
items.quote: in Q4, we will be at almost 430,000 CBM in this quarter. Because we've b een doing expansion in Kandla, we've been doing expansion in Guwahati, we've been doing expansion in Joka

items.statement: MDF Andhra plant currently 247k CBM, ramping to 315k CBM post expansion
items.quote: The current capacity for Andhra is 247,000 cubic meters. It will be ramped up to 315,000 post the expansion.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA ex-forex INR 170.5 cr, margin 12.6% vs 10.7% YoY; driven by volumes, operating leverage, cost optimization
items.quote: On the profitability front, we achieved our consolidated EBITDA, excluding forex of INR170.5 crores. The EBITDA margin ex-forex improved to 12.6%, compared to 10.7% in the corresponding quarter last year. This improvement was driven by higher volumes, operating leverage and the benefits of our ongoing cost optimization initiatives.

items.statement: MDF Q3 margin 12.1% ex-forex vs 10.7% YoY; Q4 expected higher due to Punjab flood easing, better utilization, chemical price stabilization
items.quote: Firstly, like I mentioned, there was a flooding situation in Punjab in last quarter that led to slightly higher prices for North plant, which is now eased out. Secondly, we will be looking at higher capacity utilization in the current quarter. Q4 is traditionally always better than Q3 as far as demand is concerned. So, I think that these are going to help us look at slightly higher margins for the

items.statement: MDF prices bottomed out; expect slight increase; raw material (timber) prices to decline due to plantations
items.quote: Nobody is talking. There is nothing happening in the market. And still we are selling and there is an EBITDA. So, that itself is a proo f that the prices have bottomed. Capacities are still unutilized in certain -- with some -- many manufacturers. So, that means prices have bottomed. They will not go down further. And we really expect the prices to go up actually a little bit. And the raw material

items.statement: Chemical prices stabilized, aiding MDF margins
items.quote: Chemical prices have also stabilized, and this is also likely to aid margins.

items.statement: Q3 consolidated revenue INR 1,350 cr, +18.4% YoY; 9M FY26 +17.3% YoY; broad-based growth across segments
items.quote: At a consolidated level, the company recorded its quarterly revenue of INR 1,350 crores, representing a year-on-year growth of 18.4%. This growth was driven by sustained demand across product categories and robust performance from our newly commissioned units. On a 9-month basis, FY '26 revenue grew 17.3% year-on-year, demonstrating our ability to sustain momentum despite a challenging macroeconom

items.statement: Laminates ASP jump due to larger-size exports; domestic demand to recover from Q4/early next year
items.quote: As far as the export market is concerned, it is larger sizes. And because it is larger sizes, the per unit realization will always be higher. So, that could be the reason for the ASP jump. Having said that, domestic is also likely to start firing again from Q4 itself or from early next year.

items.statement: UP largest perennial raw material source for MDF (except Andhra); no MDF plants currently in UP
items.quote: Uttar Pradesh is the largest and most perennial source of raw material as far as most of India is concerned, with the exception of maybe Andhra Pradesh. And currently, there are no MDF plants that are located within Uttar Pradesh.

items.statement: Strong internal accruals; UP project funding plan to be finalized after land acquisition
items.quote: Currently, we have very strong internal accruals. So going forward, as and when we finalize the funding plan, we shall get back to you.

items.statement: Expect R&D spending to remain 9-10% of revenues
items.quote: With R&D spending, we expect that to remain in the range of 9% to 10% of revenues.

items.statement: Will continue significant AI investments over next 3-4 quarters
items.quote: We are determined to be one of the leading players when it come s to becoming a full -stack AI shop that can partner with banks and financial institutions worldwide, and we will kind of make significant investments in this over the next three, four quarters

items.statement: Intend to decouple headcount growth from revenue growth using AI tools
items.quote: Because of the architectural leverage that w e have built into our tools, into our platforms, we intend to largely decouple the headcount growth from revenue growth

items.statement: Order book around Rs.1,650 crore, pipeline 65-66% larger than last year
items.quote: Present order book, so, we will publish a number. I think it is something of the range of Rs.1,650 crore probably or maybe slightly more than that.

items.statement: Pipeline significantly larger with deal sizes much bigger than last year
items.quote: Second, the scale of deals that we are talking about now is significantly larger than th e scale of deals we were talking about same time last year

items.statement: Transit margins to at least match banking software margins long-term
items.quote: I feel Transit would at least match banking software margins over the long run.

items.statement: DSOs around 100-110 days, expect positive operating cash flow for full year
items.quote: I would say DSOs, what I have said in the past, something between 100 and 110, it is more or less what it has, it is at this time of the year, and I think it will probably be around that number.

items.statement: Target converting 60% of EBITDA to cash, subject to Q4 execution
items.quote: typically, one would expect, we would be able to convert in the range of 60% of EBITDA to cash, but it can go up and down depending on execution, right?

items.statement: Recurring plus near-recurring revenue around 55% of business
items.quote: So, look, I think typi cally recurring plus near recurring would be in the range of 55% odd in the business

items.statement: Acquired InfraRisk to fill lending gaps in commercial and auto, at good value
items.quote: We said, we want to be a full-spectrum lending play and we would kind of build in various areas where we still have gaps. We wanted to build a little bit around commercial, around auto especially. And InfraRisk is a very high-quality team.

items.statement: Invested ~Rs.1,000 crore in R&D and acquisitions (half-half), will continue acquisitions
items.quote: We have invested Rs.1,000 crore between R&D and acquisitions, right , I think roughly half-and-half, I think Rs.600 crore on acquisitions, Rs.400 crore on R&D, but the R&D number, obviously, is climbing up now.

items.statement: 9M FY26 revenue Rs.1,066 crore (up 26%), EBITDA Rs.216 crore (up 23%), PAT Rs.150 crore (up 9%)
items.quote: We delivered a strong performance in the first nine months of FY26, with revenue from operations growing 26% to Rs.1,066 crore compared to Rs.846 crore in the same period last year.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 revenue Rs.371 crore (up 21%), EBITDA Rs.75 crore (up 18%), PAT Rs.44 crore
items.quote: In Q3, revenue came in at Rs.371 crore, which is a 21% year-on-year increase, EBITDA for the quarter grew 18% to Rs.75 crore, and margins remain steady at 20% plus.

items.statement: Added 23 new logos in Q3, one of fastest rates of customer additions
items.quote: During the quarter, as I mentioned, a very strong sales quarter. We added 23 new logos across our business segments, one of the fastest rates of customer additions in our journey so far.

items.statement: Aim to be top-3 global player in each segment, not even 2% there yet
items.quote: We said, we want to be a top three global player in each of the spaces, right. You are not even close. Each of our businesses is probably a $20, $25, $30 million business.

items.statement: Near-term capacity constraints from not growing headcount while resetting to AI tools
items.quote: This can cause some near-term capacity challenges as you would expect, but that is necessary to be able to reallocate the capital and talent towards our long-term objectives.

items.statement: Expect cost of production to drop significantly on software build side from AI tools
items.quote: we expect the productivity to really enhance significantly and result in the cost of production actually coming down, right?

items.statement: AuroPay secured offline and online payment licenses in India, progressing in other geographies
items.quote: We have done that anticipating a number of regulatory licenses, which we continue to get. I mean, as you say, in India, now we also got the offline as well as the online licenses, and we continue to make progress in other geographies as well.

items.statement: Won landmark lending mandate from Singapore-headquartered bank for international subsidiaries
items.quote: Aurionpro won a landmark lending transformation mandate from a leading Singapore-headquartered bank with selected Integro to modernize its lending operations across its international subsidiaries.

items.statement: Not increasing headcount on core development side, productivity gains expected from AI tools
items.quote: we have not really increased our headcount. If you peel under the layer, on the software side, the headcounts have actually come down.

items.statement: Cash balance approximately Rs.250-300 crore
items.quote: So, cash balance, I would not know the exact number, but I think something of the range of, I do not know, Rs.250-300 crore should be the number.

items.statement: Management maintains EBITDA margin target range of 19% to 21% for FY26 and FY27
items.quote: We continue to maintain this expansion between 19% to 21%. We have seen some gains in the form of EBITDA this particul ar quarter, but of course that is not translated to PAT because of the one-time exception. But in terms of a long -term range, even for the coming year, we ar e maintaining a similar range of 19% to 21% as the EBITDA that we look to deliver

items.statement: Q3 demand improved versus Q2; expects better performance to flow into Q4
items.quote: Quarter 3 has largely been, barring the impact of Diwali, which a portion of that was actually absorbed in Quarter 2 this year because of the advancement. Other than that, the market has relatively been better when compare d to Quarter 2. We expect that to flow into Quarter 4 as well

items.statement: Entry-level innerwear demand remains slower than mid-premium and premium segments
items.quote: Yes, in relative terms Avi, it is slower than the mid-premium and premium segments. We are seeing better growth rates in the higher-priced products when compared to the entry-level products.

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA margin at 22.9%; 9M EBITDA margin at 22.3%
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was Rs. 3,181 million, which is again a growth of 5.2% year-on-year. EBITDA margin was 22.9%.

items.statement: Gross margin declined sequentially from ~60% to ~58% due to product cost variation and higher marketing spend
items.quote: There has been slight variation in the product cost, which is sequential and which is normal. So, that is what reflects in the gross margin overall.

items.statement: No price hikes taken in Q3; ASP increase driven by product and channel mix shifts
items.quote: So, there has not been any price increase in the current quarter while we have been discussing that. But as such, there has not been any price increase. And the increase in ASP is a reflection of both category and within category changes of product mix as well as shift in channel mix.

items.statement: GST rate cut from 12% to 5% on products above Rs 1,000 passed on to consumers; impact negligible as most products under Rs 1,000
items.quote: Wherever there has been a reduction in rates from the earlier 12% to 5%, we have done the necessary changes. So, if the selling price itself was higher due to 12% GST, then that had been reduced. And wherever the selling price was still attracting 5% that has remained the same.

items.statement: Price hike under consideration if input costs rise substantially; closely monitoring cotton prices and FTA impacts
items.quote: Nothing yet, but it is expected considering the recent news about exports, specifically how it impacts textile garments. It i s quite volatile. There could be an increase in input costs. There may not be, but we do not know. So we are waiting and watching, keeping a very, very close eye on how the input costs are moving

items.statement: Distribution network: 113,600 MBOs, 1,556 EBOs, 1,778 LFS; strong e-commerce growth
items.quote: We have been maintaining a momentum on our distributio n expansion, our network stood at 1,13,600 multi-brand outlets. We now have 1,556 exclusive brand stores and 1,778 large format stores. We continue to lead across e-commerce platforms, recording strong growth in that channel as

items.statement: Insourcing at 64% vs 70% last quarter; outsourcing increased to 36% per plan, providing cost benefits
items.quote: Yes, there have been some increase in our outsourcing procurement. So, currently or in the current quarter, outsourcing is around 36%. So, there has been some increase which is well in line with our plan.

items.statement: Premium products (bonded collection, athleisure, women's innerwear) driving growth; entry-level innerwear weaker
items.quote: Our growth in women's innerwear as well as outerwear have been relatively better in terms of both volume and value growth. Wi thin price points itself, I do not think we wil l attribute that to competition at this point. But yes, the more premium offering seems to have had better acceptance

items.statement: JKY Groove expanded to 150 EBOs in Q3; next launch in April 2026 targeting 500 EBOs; phased rollout to MBOs/LFS
items.quote: In Q3, that has expanded to 150 EBOs. The next version is expected to be launched in the month of April, which is again the summer 2026 version. It is expected to expand to about 500 EBOs.

items.statement: General trade throughput per store softened; EBO and e-commerce like-for-like flat but softer than target
items.quote: In the general trade channel, yes. While we do not have tertiary data, but yes, I would expect that the throughput per store would have softened when compared to last year. But in the other channels, we do have that data at a consumer level. We have not de-grown like-to-like, but it has been a lot softer than what we targeted.

items.statement: Inventory days 67 at end of Q3 vs 64 at start of year; net working capital 52 days vs 54 days at start of year
items.quote: Inventory days was 67 in the end of Q3, as against 64 days in the beginning of the year. Net working capital was 52 days, as against 54 days in the beginning of the year.

items.statement: Headcount reduced by 2,500-3,000 due to recruitment freeze, automation, lean initiatives and productivity gains; new Odisha facility added workforce as planned
items.quote: We had a recruitment freeze for most part of the year. And given the fact that our efficiency has been improving and maintained over a l arge part of the year, we did not see any requirement of major recruitment this year. Of course, there has been workforce addition in our new facility in Orissa, which was as per

items.statement: New labour codes notified November 2025; Rs 350 million one-time provision for gratuity and earned leave made in Q3
items.quote: The ne w labour codes were introduced in November 2025. The amendment stipulated changes in the definition of wages, including enhanced basic wages for calculation of retirement benefits. Accordingly, additional provision of Rs. 350 million for gratuity and earned leave has been made in the current quarter

items.statement: International expansion focus on GCC: licenses secured for Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain; groundwork done, launch expected soon
items.quote: We have gained the license for, we ha ve always been in the Middle East but only in select markets like UAE, Oman and Qatar. We now have the license for Saudi. We have the license for Kuwait and Bahrain. So the whole of GCC now is a license page for Jockey which we see as a large market

items.statement: Revenue grew 5.6% YoY in Q3; volume grew 1.4% YoY; 9M revenue up 4.1%, volume up 1.9%
items.quote: In Q3, revenue was Rs. 13,868 million, which was a growth of around 5.6% year-on-year. Sales volume in the quarter was for 58.6 million pieces, which has grown by 1.4% year-on-year.

items.statement: Double-digit volume growth target timing uncertain due to multiple variables; depends on demand recovery and execution of initiatives
items.quote: Again, it will be difficult for me to put a timeline to this because like I said, there are too many variables at play for us to get to that goal. We have seen consistent improvement even within this financial year. And that kind of a number is what we will be running for even for quarter 4.

items.statement: Input cost volatility from cotton prices, FTAs, and export policy changes could pressure margins if not passed on
items.quote: We are keeping a close watch on the cotton prices also with FTAs and all that. There can be pressures on the input costs. So, it is very volatile out there. So, our pricing strategy will be based on those developments in the market.

items.statement: No evidence of market share loss; shelf share and partner channel data show gains in innerwear and athleisure
items.quote: Well, Gaurav, it is hard to tell. Because there is actually no syndicated study of market share in this particular industry. But from physical evidence and our understanding of the market and what is happening on the ground, we do not believe there is any erosion in market share.

items.statement: Odisha manufacturing facility operational; workforce added as planned; automation and value stream mapping ongoing
items.quote: Of course, there has been workforce addition in our new facility in Orissa, which was as per plan. But otherwise, our wages cost and staff cost has been well within our target ranges.

items.statement: FY29 revenue aspiration of Rs 8,000 crore includes organic and inorganic avenues: quick commerce, international, new product spaces; open to acquisitions but no visibility yet
items.quote: Well, the projection that has been given is for overall. It will be all the opportunities that comes our way and that we see meaning in investing in. We see inorganic opportunities within the existing business itself. These could be new channels that are coming up, quick commerce, the way it is growing and how much we can bring back to the business is a very inorganic avenue for us.

items.statement: Target Rs 250 crore quarterly run rate and Rs 1,000 crore annual revenue in near future
items.value: Rs 250 crore quarterly, Rs 1,000 crore annual
items.quote: Our idea of Rs. 1,000 crore is to achieve Rs. 250 crore quarterly and I feel run rate should be Rs. 250 crore. So, we are at Rs. 247 crore, we should be able to do Rs. 250 crore from next quarter onwards and then keep on improving.

items.statement: Revenue growth target mid-teens for FY27
items.quote: So yes, we are looking at mid-teens to be a little conservative.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target 11-12% in next 3-4 quarters, mid-teens in 2-3 years
items.quote: We would want that to continue. And that is possible since as soon as our larger Smart City implementation projects move into O&M, we will see better and improved margins coming in.

items.statement: Order flows healthy with over Rs 250 crore in Q3 FY26 from new wins, renewals and follow-on orders
items.quote: Order flows during the quarter remained healthy with over Rs. 250 crores, supported by a mix of new wins, renewals and follow -on orders from existing customers.

items.statement: International operations grew 26% YoY in Q3 FY26; US enterprise clients moving to decisive activity in network modernization, digital workplace, cybersecurity, managed services
items.quote: From a geographic standpoint, our international operations continue to demonstrate improving momentum as the rest of the world operations reported a year-on-year growth of about 26% in quarter 3 FY '26.

items.statement: India standalone revenues declined 5% YoY in Q3 FY26 due to no significant project milestones; renewed billing expected next quarter as milestones complete
items.quote: India operations de-grew, as reported a decline to stand-alone revenues by 5% year-on-year in quarter 3 FY '26 as there were no significant project milestones which were to be achieved during quarter 3.

items.statement: EBITDA grew 11% YoY to Rs 26 crore in Q3 FY26; margin improved over Q2 but pricing environment challenging
items.quote: In Q3 FY '26, EBITDA grew by 4% year -on-year basis to INR26 Rs. 26 crore. As our top line continued to expand, we are seeing a parallel increase in profitability as we reported an improved margin in Q3 over Q2.

items.statement: Smart City implementation phase margins low; O&M phase margins improve to double digits upwards of 20% gross margin overall
items.quote: So, once you move out from a solutions space to a S ervices revenue, your margins keep on improving. So yes, if somebody is a player who is only doing the hardware business, they will have single -digit margins, but a solution provider like us who does end -to-end from building a Smart City to managing it for a perio d of 5 years, will have improved margins overall in the tune of double digits upw

items.statement: Services revenue grew 16% YoY, Solutions revenue flat in Q3 FY26; Services provide stability, Solutions act as entry point for annuity-led engagements
items.quote: From a segment perspective, our Services business grew 16% year -on year, while Solutions revenue remained flat.

items.statement: Non-Government revenue grew 13% YoY, Government revenue grew 12% YoY in Q3 FY26; enterprise clients showing stronger engagement
items.quote: Reflecting the renewed E nterprise sentiments, revenue from Non - Government customers increased 13% year -on-year, outpacing growth from the G overnment segments, which reported 12% year -on-year growth.

items.statement: European pharma contract: ~$1 million/month (~$12 million/year) for 4 years, ~$50 million total, margins in teens
items.quote: So, we are looking at a revenue top line of about $1 million a month, about $12 million a year for 4 years. That is close to about $50 -odd million. Margins would be in the teens.

items.statement: Investing in team capability and compliance for large multi-country contracts; hiring Chief Growth Officer and salespeople in US for direct mid-sized customers
items.quote: With 700 crore, 800 crore revenue top line, we announced 2 large deals worth 500 crore each last year. So, when we acquire such kind of large customers, there is a lot of investments that also go in to make sure that we are having the right kind of team ability.

items.statement: Union Budget emphasizes digital infrastructure, data centres, AI, data security; cloud services tax holidays for international entities managing US customer cloud services from India-based data centres
items.quote: The Union Budget has reiterated the government's continued emphasis on strengthening India's digital infrastructure. incentivization of key areas such as data centres, artificial intelligence and data security has emerged as a central theme this year.

items.statement: New Labour Codes: only Rs 1.3 crore one-time provision for limited adjustments; salary structures already compliant
items.quote: We are pleased to note that no material provisions were required in relation to the New Labour Codes during the quarter. Our salary structures, which were designed to be employee -friendly while remaining fully compliant with applicable regulatory requireme nts are well aligned with the new framework.

items.statement: DSO improved to 75 days; no uneasiness in collecting from Government; some debtors >3 years old under consideration with ECL provisions
items.quote: With respect to future projects, I think the mid -teens will be a conservative growth target that I would want to give out. The reason is beyond the macroeconomic conditions that we also have to keep in mind. But having said that, the pipeline looks strong.

items.statement: US subsidiary loan (quasi-equity) to be converted to equity by March 31, 2026 to resolve audit qualification; no interest charged previously
items.quote: So, we are planning, we are working on it so that this loan amount can be converted into equity finally by 31st March. So that this qualification will also be removed permanently.

items.statement: Audit qualifications on physical verification of fixed assets/inventory, old debtors >3 years, unbilled revenue; targeting resolution by March 31, 2026; impact not expected at last year's scale
items.quote: fact, these notes, the points are not new. In fact, last March onwards, these similar points are coming continuing. These are a few things which we have realized, we have accepted their points, and we are seriously wo rking on that to rectify Q3 & 9M FY2026 Earnings Call Transcript those points

items.statement: Prior year tax provision of Rs 4.8 crore increased tax expense in Q3 FY26; adjusted PAT ~Rs 20 crore excluding this and Rs 1.3 crore exceptional item
items.quote: During the quarter, we have made a provision of Rs. 4.8 crore pertaining to prior year taxation. This has served to increase the tax expense for the quarter.

items.statement: Hired Chief Growth Officer in US; hiring more salespeople for direct mid-sized customer acquisition
items.quote: In the U.S., we have also hired a Chief Growth Officer. We are also hiring more salespeople to put more f eet on the ground to acquire more direct midsized customers.

items.statement: AI-first strategy: AI embedded in all services; Agentic AI platform deployed in NOC for 50+ customers; 3 deals this quarter leveraging AI; AI improves productivity and automation leading to margin improvement
items.quote: Today, our NOC drives AI Ops as part of building complex solutions and resolving critical issues using our own AI engine. So, we see tremendous traction in terms of usage of AI over time.

items.statement: Government pipeline strong in Western Railways, metros, Maharashtra; bids submitted, financial opening stage; expect announcements in next 2 months
items.quote: our focus typically for the current quarter and the next quarter is going to be for the Western Railways, metros and Maharashtra as a state. So, we see a very healthy pipeline coming in there, and we will see some Q3 & 9M FY2026 Earnings Call Transcript kind of announcements coming in of order wins if we win some of them in the next 2 months

items.statement: Railway projects similar construct to Smart City: solution implementation + 5-year O&M; margins slightly lower than Safe City due to standardization
items.quote: Absolutely. Yes, yes. Correct. Absolutely. See, only this time, the Services could be a little lower than the ones in the safe cities margin because railways is pretty straightforward and standard.

items.statement: US-India trade agreement framework announced; removes overhang, reinforces long-term opportunity for Allied Digital with established US presence
items.quote: The other exciting development this week is the announcement of framework for U.S. India trade agreement. This removes the overhang for Q3 & 9M FY2026 Earnings Call Transcript the last few months and will draw out a clear path towards incentivizing greater economic cooperation between the 2

items.statement: Customers seeking outcome-linked commercial models, tighter SLAs, faster implementation; award cycles competitive with sharper negotiations
items.quote: Customers are increasingly seeking outcome -linked commercial models, tighter SLAs and faster implementation timelines. Our Award cycles remain competitive with sharper negotiations, but there is also a clear preference for partners who can assume end -to-end responsibility.

items.statement: FY26 booking value guidance INR32,500 crores; 74% achieved in 9M FY26, on track to beat guidance
items.quote: GPL has, as a result, achieved 74% of its annual guidance for booking value and remains on track to beat its guidance of INR32,500 crores for the financial year.

items.statement: FY26 collections guidance INR21,000 crores; 57% achieved in 9M FY26, on track to meet guidance with Q4 skew
items.quote: We believe we remain on track to achieve our full year guidance of INR21,000 crores for the full year as deliveries and collections this year are significantly skewed towards Q4.

items.statement: FY26 deliveries guidance 10 million sq ft; expect to exceed guidance due to construction spend ramp-up
items.quote: our guidance for the full year for deliveries is 10 million square feet. We've only done about half of that in the first 9 months and we actually expect to do because of these construction spends more than the 10 million square feet guided.

items.statement: FY27 operational guidance to be provided with Q4 results; expect healthy growth to sustain across key metrics
items.quote: A detailed operational guidance for financial year '27 will be provided with our Q4 results, but we can expect healthy growth to sustain across key metrics.

items.statement: Confident of beating FY26 booking value guidance; 73-74% achieved in 9M FY26
items.quote: I think very confident on the guidance. So I would maintain what we said in the previous calls as well. In fact if you see purely from a 9-month perspective, it's about 73%, 74% of an annual guidance already.

items.statement: Added 3 new projects in Q3 FY26 with 7.3 msf salable area and INR8,400 crores booking value; 12 projects in 9M FY26 with 22 msf and INR25,000 crores, achieving 123% of annual BD guidance
items.quote: For the 9 months, GPL has added 12 new projects with an estimated salable area of 22 million square feet and expected booking value of nearly INR25,000 crores thereby achieving 123% of our annual guidance within the first 9 months.

items.statement: Total inventory pipeline INR135,000 crores; fresh inventory from last year acquisitions ~INR65,000 crores
items.quote: We currently hold about INR135,000 crores worth of inventory. And within that, if I talk about inventory that is very recent, which is very fresh inventory which is from the acquisitions of last year, that itself give or take is about INR65,000 crores.

items.statement: Market maturing from euphoric speculative phase to end-user/seasoned investor driven; froth fading in Gurgaon but market extremely strong across geographies
items.quote: So the froth of the market, which is mostly say speculative investors, especially I'm talking about Gurgaon, that I see is kind of fading out and rightly so. But that aside, I would say market is extremely strong.

items.statement: Strong demand across all segments (premium, luxury, mid); value-conscious end-users driving product-focused purchases
items.quote: I have seen in our portfolio strong demand across segments. And look at last quarter itself, on one hand, we had Panipat launch, right? It's been our best ever plotted launch in a small city with a INR1,000-plus crores of sales.

items.statement: Demand strong across segments; customers value-conscious and product-focused regardless of price tier
items.quote: So it's a very end user thought process, but nothing really that we would say that only mid-segment or a premium segment or luxury is doing this. I have seen in our portfolio strong demand across segments.

items.statement: Target net profit margin 10-15% and EBITDA margin ~25% through cycles; last year slightly above net margin range
items.quote: I think the margins we've guided to are that we'd like to deliver anywhere between 10% and 15% net profit margin. Last year, at an imputed level, we were slightly above that ratio. But I expect over time through cycles to be operating within that range.

items.statement: Construction spend up 66% in 9M FY26 to improve execution speed; near-term OCF impact but strengthens long-term collections and ROE target for FY28
items.quote: we've seen and I think we talked about in our earnings call a couple of quarters back as well that for this year, we would be focusing a lot on improving our execution speed and muscle and there's been lot of work that has gone in building that muscle.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 OC pipeline includes 2-2.5 msf in Pune (Mahalunge/Mamurdi), projects in Meridian, Khalapur, RGA; expect to exceed 10 msf annual delivery guidance
items.quote: We have a series of OCs planned in the Pune market and this is specifically on the Mahalunge and the Mamurdi cluster. This itself is close to 2 million, 2.5 million square feet of a portfolio and most of these will come largely in quarter 4 and some in quarter 1.

items.statement: Geographically diversified sales: no market >30% of bookings; 5 markets >INR3,000 crores each in CY25; top 2 rank in Mumbai, NCR, Bangalore, Pune, Hyderabad
items.quote: The company's sales were also well diversified geographically with no individual market contributing more than 30% to booking value and with five individual markets contributing more than INR3,000 crores each.

items.statement: Net debt/equity at 0.37x; governance ceiling 0.5x; comfortable headroom for growth opportunities
items.quote: from a leverage point of view, I think we probably even captured, I think in our investor presentation, we are at 0.37 and we endeavor not to cross 0.5 from a governance perspective.

items.statement: Price hikes seen across most portfolios except Pune; degree of hikes moderating; future hikes calibrated based on qualified supply and project-specific
items.quote: we've seen price hikes more or less in most of our portfolios. So yes, there is available. But yes, the degree of current price hikes are more subdued, but they are available.

items.statement: Land acquisition disciplined; walking away from overpriced auctions; seeing attractive valuations in Gurgaon after 18-month peak; 30-35 live term sheets at any time
items.quote: sometimes there are auctions, right, where we have consciously not gone beyond a particular price threshold on buying the land because we didn't feel that there was a fair market valuation for that.

items.statement: CY25 bookings INR34,171 crores (+19% YoY); collections INR18,979 crores (+28% YoY); operating cash flow INR7,246 crores (+20% YoY); earnings INR1,582 crores (+6% YoY)
items.quote: GPL delivered its best ever year in calendar year 2025 and achieved bookings of INR34,171 crores, a year-on-year growth of 19%. Collections of INR18,979 crores, a year-on-year growth of 28%. Operating cash flow of INR7,246 crores, year-on-year growth of 20%. And earnings of INR1,582 crores, which is a year-on-year growth of 6%.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 collections INR4,282 crores (+40% YoY, +5% QoQ); 9M FY26 collections INR12,000+ crores (+19% YoY)
items.quote: Collections in the third quarter grew 40% year-on-year and 5% quarter-on-quarter to INR4,282 crores. Collections in 9 months FY '26 grew 19% to just over INR12,000 crores.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 net profit INR195 crores (+20% YoY); 9M FY26 net profit INR1,200 crores (+18% YoY); highest ever Q3 and 9M net profit
items.quote: We delivered our highest third quarter and 9-month net profit of INR195 crores and INR1,200 crores, respectively, a growth of 20% and 18% year-on-year for the quarter and the 9 months.

items.statement: 9M FY26 EBITDA INR1,867 crores (+40% YoY); Q3 FY26 EBITDA INR338 crores (+21% YoY)
items.quote: EBITDA grew by 40% for the 9 months to INR1,867 crores and net profit grew by 18% to INR1,200 crores.

items.statement: AI impact on IT job creation uncertain; could affect commercial/residential demand in Bangalore/Hyderabad but currently seeing exceptional outcomes in both markets
items.quote: Of course hard to know exactly what the impact of AI on job creation is going to be over the medium term and I think we're all going to have to wait and watch.

items.statement: Ranked #1 globally in real estate on S&P Dow Jones Best in Class Indices 2025; CDP Leadership Index A rating 2025; CDP Supplier Engagement Leader; CDP A List 2024
items.quote: Godrej Properties has ranked number one globally in the real estate and management sector on the S&P Global Dow Jones Best in class Indices for 2025 as of the 31st December cutoff.

items.statement: Expect double-digit top-line growth in FY26 and commensurate or slightly higher growth in FY27; normalised growth rates expected from FY28 onwards
items.quote: in terms of execution. For FY 2027, as we come into that year with a strong order book, we should look at, commensurate if not slightly higher growth than we had in FY 2026. But our order booking projections for FY 2027, lead us to believe that we should be reverting to a normalised growth rates of what we spoke about, starting FY 2028 onwards

items.statement: Q3 FY26 order booking was ₹391 crore, about ₹200 crore below recent quarterly average due to deferred advances; expect Q4 to make up the shortfall and revert to normal average
items.quote: So, we had an order booking in Q3 of ₹391 billion, which I want to say is about ₹200 plus crores short of what our average has been in the previous quarters. And that is exactly the quantum of orders that were sort of deferred because of non-receipt of advance.

items.statement: Expect FY26 order booking growth over FY25 base of ₹2,300+ crore despite lumpiness; NTPC order not treated as one-off
items.quote: So, despite that, we look at the order booking in FY '25 of ₹2,300 plus crores as being the base for us to grow off in FY '26.

items.statement: Domestic market showing double-digit growth in Q4 FY26; export enquiry pipeline strong but conversion delayed by tariff and geopolitical uncertainties
items.quote: Based on the current enquiry pipeline what we feel is our domestic market going to grow further in Q4. So, with a year-on-year growth of something like a double-digit growth, what we are expecting.

items.statement: Heat pump enquiry book exceeds 100; first order received for execution in FY27; MVR has 7-8 orders under execution for FY27 commissioning
items.quote: Our heat pumps now have an enquiry book well in excess of 100, and we're quite confident of hitting that market in a manner with great focus. We've already received our first order for this, and we'll be happy to share some more details about that.

items.statement: MVR initial orders sizable at 7-8 under execution; expect commissioning in FY27; strong customer interest due to adjacency to core product line
items.quote: Coming to MVR, initial orders we picked up, are sizable around seven, eight orders, which are under execution. That also we expect to commission those things in FY 2027.

items.statement: Net Promoter Score study indicates customer satisfaction at all-time high; HR performing well with strong retention of high-calibre workforce
items.quote: The quality system that we have in place are well regarded by our customer, and we feel that the recently concluded Net Promoter Score study seems to indicate that our customer satisfaction is at an all-time high.

items.statement: US tariff reduction to 18% expected to accelerate order finalisations; US enquiry book multi-hundred million dollars; target US to contribute meaningfully to top and bottom line in 2-3 years
items.quote: With the tariffs now coming down, we should be well placed to convert these enquiries. While they were there, because of the tariffs, there has been a delay in the decision-making, but with the now tariffs coming down, things could be materialising in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Export-domestic order booking mix expected to remain around 55%-45%; both markets expanding in parallel with lumpiness quarter-to-quarter
items.quote: I agree. More or less, both the domestic and export market also expanding. I agree, more or less we'll be at around that, 55%-45% level.

items.statement: No new plant expansion planned in Asia or Europe until US subsidiary stabilises; focus on bandwidth and track record validation
items.quote: So, until the U.S. stabilises, I don't think we would look at expansion both from a perspective of bandwidth, as well as validating our track record.

items.statement: South Africa subsidiary: 100% control of TSE Engineering achieved; unifying operations to expand from SADC to Sub-Saharan Africa; bullish on utility refurbishment in FY27
items.quote: We've taken complete 100% control of TSE Engineering, which has been reported to the exchanges. And we would look at unifying our operations in the South African market. Of course, with this unified approach, we would be expanding the scope from the SADC region to Sub-Saharan Africa.

items.statement: US market has no local turbine producers; competition similar to Europe; brand building and local references needed for faster conversion
items.quote: It's similar to our competition in Europe. But there are no local turbine producers in the United States.

items.statement: Municipal waste-to-energy potential in India enormous but constrained by urban local body creditworthiness and governance; needs central backing for viable concession agreements
items.quote: Urban local bodies are not creditworthy on a counterparty risk assessment basis, and so there's no concession agreement that can be signed, which is credible, unless it's backed by the centre.

items.statement: Shreya Sharma joined as Head of Investor Relations and Value Creation; over 7% workforce in R&D and 8% in engineering
items.quote: We have over 7% of our workforce is on, is in R&D only. We have another 8% part in engineering. So, it gives you an indication as to where the manpower strength of Triveni is.

items.statement: Energy storage (CO2 and non-CO2 thermal) a key medium-term focus; combining multiple products for applications; expect traction in FY27
items.quote: One of the applications that we're very bullish about in the medium term is energy storage. We think that that presents a unique market for us, and we will be combining a lot of products together to come up with correct applications there.

items.statement: Geothermal and boiler feed water pump drives identified as growth markets for next 3-5 years; refurbishment success in geothermal now translating to product orders
items.quote: Geothermal is really about getting – we've had great successes in the Refurbishment side in this space, and the product orders have also now picked up, and so therefore this will represent a good growth opportunity for clean, renewable firm power that is required by customers.

items.statement: Tariff reductions in US will be passed on to customers; enables quicker finalisations and better returns for both parties
items.quote: Obviously, the tariff reductions will have to be passed on to customers.

items.statement: Pressures to not compromise balance sheet and payment terms for dispatches; raw material availability and customer inspections affecting Q4 dispatch catch-up
items.quote: There are pressures in terms of ensuring that we don't compromise our balance sheet and payment terms just to dispatch orders, as well as the availability of raw materials, which is required for final assembly, and the availability of customers for inspections.

items.statement: Targets Rs.4,000 Cr disbursement and Rs.16,200 Cr AUM for FY2026; Rs.5,000 Cr disbursement for FY2027
items.quote: We are targeting Rs.1200 Crores to Rs.1400 Crores kind of disbursement in the current quarter and we are targeting Rs.16200 Crores AUM. Coming to the disbursement in next financial year, yes, we are setting a target of close to about Rs.5000 Crores disbursement in the next financial these are from disbursements side.

items.statement: Targets GNPA 2.5% and Stage 2 assets 7.5% by end of FY2026
items.quote: in first conc all of this financial year we have given guidance of about dis bursing Rs.4000 Crores disbursement and we have given guidance to take our AUM to Rs.16,200 Crores and we said we want to bring down our NPA to 2.5% and Stage 2 assets to 7

items.statement: Expects credit cost to remain negative for FY2026 and Q4 FY2026
items.quote: I am not expecting any credit cost for the current financial year, the credit cost will be negative.

items.statement: Expects cost of funds to reduce by another 10 bps in Q4 FY2026
items.quote: Keeping all those things in mind I am expecting that my overall cost of fund s may be reduced by another 10 basis points. We can see reduction in cost of funds to the extent of 10 basis points in the current quarter, that is what I would say.

items.statement: Q3 FY2026 disbursements Rs.1,064 Cr, up 40% YoY; Maharashtra, MP, Rajasthan improved QoQ
items.quote: During the quarter end of December, we disbursed close to Rs.1069 Crores, which is almost in line with our disbursement of September 2025. Again, this current financial year, our disbursement has crossed second time Rs.1000 Crores mark. If you compare our disbursement of December 2025 versus December 2024, we have seen 40% year-on-year growth in the disbursements.

items.statement: AUM Rs.15,394 Cr at Dec 2025, up 8.8% YoY; net addition Rs.360 Cr in Q3
items.quote: Coming to the A UM, our AUM at the end of December 2025 stood at Rs.15,394 Crores as compared to last year December of Rs.14,155 Crores. Yes, we have seen growth rate of 8.8%. During the quarter I said Rs.1064 Crores we have disbursed of which around Rs.360 Crores added to my loan book remaining going for principal return -off.

items.statement: Yield on assets flat at 12%; spread 3.3%; NIM 5.41% at Dec 2025; targets spread 3.2-3.3%
items.quote: Our spread at end of December stood at 3.3%, our yield on assets is almost flat compared with September , our yield on assets in September 2025 was 12% and December2025 also it was also 12%. We are maintaining a spread of 3.3% and our NIM was close to about 5.41 % at end of December 2025.

items.statement: Cost of funds down 30 bps YTD to 8.45%; passed on 20 bps to borrowers (10 bps July, 10 bps Feb)
items.value: 8.45% cost of funds; 20 bps passed on
items.quote: Cost of fund s at the beginning of the year was close to about 8.75%, a t e nd of December 2025 it was close to about 8.45%. We have experienced 30 basis points reduction in cost of fund s. We have passed on 20 basis points to our borrowers in the manner of 10 basis points effective from July 1, 2025, and another 10 basis points effective from February 1, 2025.

items.statement: GNPA Rs.449.5 Cr (down from Rs.475 Cr QoQ, Rs.545 Cr YoY); Stage 2 Rs.1,235 Cr (down Rs.88 Cr QoQ, Rs.260 Cr YoY); recovered Rs.25 Cr NPA in Q3
items.quote: Coming to the recovery side, our gross NPA at the end of December stood at Rs.449.53 Crores as against Rs.545 Crores in the last year of the same period. During the quarter ended December 2025 we recovered NPA to the extent of Rs.25 Crores. A t the end of September 2025, our gross NPA in absolute term s was Rs.475 Crores. In the last concall I have given you a promise that our NPA numbers will com

items.statement: Targets Stage 2 below 2% in 1-2 years; reducing 2-2.5% per year; 225 staff on recoveries
items.quote: So, going forward, every year we are planning to reduce by at least 2 to 2.5% in Stage 2 accounts, in another one or two years we will bring it down to less than 2% or 1.5%.

items.statement: Borrowings Rs.11,769 Cr at Dec 2025; NHB refinance Rs.829 Cr; bank borrowings Rs.9,893 Cr; Repco Bank Rs.810 Cr; CP Rs.145 Cr; PTC Rs.93 Cr at 7.75%; NCD Rs.100-125 Cr planned
items.quote: Coming to the borrowing side, our borrowings stood at Rs.11,769 Crores at the end of December 2025. items.quote: the competitive environment in Tamil Nadu has grown up. So yes, we do have competition but not to the extent of it impacting my disbursement or my disbursement plans and of course we are also concentrating on our growth in non -TN states like most of the br

items.quote: Well, the labour code has been enacted effectively since November 2025. Based on that we have made provisions for leave encashment and gratuity to the extent of close to 5 crores for

items.quote: September employee cost was about Rs.34 Crores at the end of December it was Rs.42 Crores. Well, the labour code has been enacted effectively since November 2025. As per the labour code, we must make adequate provision for leave and benefits, funds like leave encashment, gra tuity, etc ., etc. We have given the data to our actual valuer, they have valued and we got the numbers. items.quote: We are discussing with few companies, bank s and NBFCs. Now the matter is asset mix, what kind of assets can we take 80, 20, 80 is a home loan, 20 is a home equity loan, what price and all. For the sake of growth, for the sake of disbursement growth, for the sake of AUM growth, we will not land into trouble in the form of taking a bad loan from other companies, we will be very cautious. items.statement: Karnataka growth constrained by e-Khata issue; expects resolution by March 2026
items.quote: Karnataka, we wanted to grow faster, but we could not do so because Ekata is yet to be resolved in full. Though we can maintain our books there and maintain our disbursement levels there, growing a bit faster is now becoming a problem there because of e-Khata. I think by March, the e-Khata issue should get sorted out.

items.statement: Introduced new credit assessment schemes (gross profit, banking balance, average income methods) over last 2-3 years; will not compromise asset quality for growth
items.quote: Two years, three years back, we followed unaltered profit and loss accounts. Nowadays we introduce so many schemes based on gross profit methods, banking balance method, average income method we introduced so many methods , so we have improved our credit policies and will continue to improve in coming days also. T. Karunakaran: We have reviewed our entire credit policy in line with the present req

items.statement: ALM comfortable with no bucket gaps; Rs.1,000 Cr unutilized sanctions from 6-7 banks; Rs.150 Cr investments on balance sheet
items.quote: First thing our ALM position was very, very comfortable, we are not having a gap in any ALM buckets I want to confirm you. On the balance sheet we are having adequate liquidity. name: Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Ltd

items.statement: Overall demand environment remained mixed with consumption centered around festive and wedding-related shopping
items.quote: Looking back at the quarter, the overall demand environment remained mixed with consumption largely centered around festive and wedding-related shopping.

items.statement: Pantaloons targeting mid- to high single-digit LTL growth and double-digit overall growth over next 2 years
items.quote: So we are looking for mid- to high single-digit growth in Pantaloons for LTL and double-digit growth at an overall level, yes.

items.statement: TCNS targeting 50-60 store additions in FY27 and double-digit growth with double-digit pre-Ind AS margin over medium term
items.quote: I expect that we'll add between 50 to 60 stores next year in TCNS, something that we had held back so far.

items.statement: TMRW expected to breakeven around FY29 on pre-Ind AS basis
items.quote: We expect TMRW, as we have mentioned in our various sort of presentations, including investor presentation, to be somewhere between FY '29 is when TMRW should breakeven.

items.statement: ABFRL excluding TMRW already breakeven on pre-Ind AS basis for 9 months, expects pre-Ind AS profit from FY27 full year
items.quote: For the entire business, without TMRW, we are 9-month EBITDA positive or breakeven. And this is pre-Ind AS, yes. And therefore, the losses Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited (ABFRL) February 06, 2026 even at consolidated today, this includes all the losses that we talked about currently in TCNS, Tasva, Galeries Lafayette, etcetera. With all that included, we are breakeven today ex TMRW. And w

items.statement: Overall EBITDA margin expanded to 15.6% in Q3 FY26 from 14.9% in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Overall EBITDA grew by 13%, with margins at 15.6% for the quarter compared to 14.9% in the same period last year.

items.statement: Ethnic business margin expanded 350 bps YoY to 22.7% in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Within segments, our ethnic business continued its consistent margin expansion for the eighth consecutive quarter with Q3 margin reaching 22.7%, up 350 basis points versus last year.

items.statement: ABFRL excluding TMRW margin at 20% in Q3 FY26, up 70 bps YoY
items.quote: If we see ABFRL, excluding TMRW, overall margin stood at 20% in this quarter, up 70 basis points versus last year.

items.statement: YTD EBITDA margin improved 70 bps to 10.6% despite 100 bps higher ad spend
items.quote: EBITDA grew 17% in absolute terms to INR655 crores versus INR559 crores in YTD last year, with margins improving by 70 basis points to 10.6% despite 100 basis point higher advertisement spend versus last year.

items.statement: TCNS margin improved ~500 bps on improved product performance and retail execution
items.quote: On this more focused and profitable base, we delivered strong LTL growth of 8% for the quarter with YTD LTL growth at 10%, reflecting improving underlying performance. Margin was up by approximately 500 basis points, driven by improved product performance and retail execution.

items.statement: Ethnic portfolio at INR2,200 crores annual sales with 650+ stores
items.quote: Our ethnic portfolio is now at INR2,200 crores annual sales with 650-plus stores across the country.

items.statement: TMRW at INR1,100 crores annual revenue run rate including Wrogn
items.quote: The business is now operating at an annual revenue run rate of INR1,100 crores, including Wrogn with improving profitability trends.

items.statement: Added net 5.5 lakh sq ft over last 12 months; 50 new stores and 2.5 lakh sq ft added in Q3
items.quote: We have also continued to invest in network expansion through growth capex, adding a net 5.5 lakh square feet of area over the last 12 months. This positions us well for future growth and operating leverage as these stores mature.

items.statement: 9-month capex ~INR300 crores including security deposits
items.quote: Capex across business for 9 months is roughly INR300 crores, including security deposits.

items.statement: Overall retail network at 1,226 stores spanning 7.7 million sq ft as of Q3 end
items.quote: Our overall retail network stood at 1,226 stores, spanning over 7.7 million square feet as of Q3 end with 50 new additions during the quarter with area up by 2.5 lakh square feet sequentially.

items.statement: Pantaloons new stores targeting 18,000-30,000 sq ft in Tier 1/metro cities
items.quote: So we are largely looking at stores in the range of 18,000 plus, going up to 25,000, 30,000 depending on the potential of the market.

items.statement: OWND! plans 40-50 store openings in coming year
items.quote: So from a store opening standpoint, we would be looking at opening about 40 to 50 stores in the coming year.

items.statement: Pantaloons plans ~20 store additions per year going forward
items.quote: I think about 20 stores is what we would say we need to build in because Gaurav, as Sangeeta had explained, a lot of our premiumization strategy was building around aspirational and experience premiumization, not necessarily significant shift in pricing.

items.statement: Pantaloons average selling price increased 2-3% due to premiumization shift
items.quote: Also with non-apparel being integrated into our apparel strategy, we hope to see an ongoing improvement in our basket sizes as well. So not a very significant impact in terms of the basket size. But in terms of our average selling price, we've seen about a 2% to 3% increase because of the shift and because of our premiumization.

items.statement: Pantaloons private label mix shifted 1-1.5% higher over last 2-3 years
items.quote: As far as the mix is concerned, I think because of the nature of changes that we've made in the format, opening larger stores, our mix over the last 2, 3 years has shifted by 1% to 1.5% in favor of private label.

items.statement: Pantaloons Greencard loyalty contributes 70%+ of revenue; Insignia paid tier on top
items.quote: Our overall Greencard contributes to about 70% plus of our revenues and Insignia sits on top of that.

items.statement: Standalone net cash ~INR800 crores (INR1,600 crores cash vs INR750 crores long-term debt); consolidated net cash ~INR600 crores
items.quote: With me is around INR800 crores. So consolidated -- sorry, stand-alone entity has INR750 crores of long-term debt. So from INR1,600 crores, you can take that down. That's why he's talking about INR800 crores. There is a further -- TMRW, because of the fundraise is sitting on a net cash of about INR400 crores, INR500 crores.

items.statement: Galeries Lafayette launched Nov 2025 with INR125-130 crores store investment, INR60-70 crores inventory, total capital employed INR180-200 crores
items.quote: Overall, as I mentioned, the gross investment in fixed assets is about INR125 crores, INR130 crores or in that range. The inventory would be about INR60 crores, INR70 crores with -- and therefore, the total capital employed will remain in the range of INR150 crores to INR200 crores, INR180 crores to INR200 crores in that.

items.statement: Pantaloons EOSS deferral to Q4 carries risk of market share loss to competitors who ran sales in December
items.quote: Any strategy can backfire, but I think this should give you a sense of confidence that we have got to in our merchandising cycle in this business. It's taken us some time and a fair bit of understanding of business. You can be sure we have sort of thought deeply about it. It's a very difficult -- as you're rightly alluding, it's a different call -- difficult call.

items.statement: TCNS leadership transition: Anant transitioning out, Sooraj (Tasva head) taking over with 3-4 month handover
items.quote: As Anant transitions out of it, first of all, he's spending next 3, 4 months with our next leader who is Sooraj, who has been in this ethnic business for the last 2, 3 years, was responsible for growing and building Tasva business, looking after Jaipur.

items.statement: Proposed merger of subsidiary Sammaan Finserve into Sammaan Capital announced to consolidate lending business and distribution
items.quote: one of the major developments was the announced proposed merger of our subsidiary, Sammaan Finserve into Sammaan Capital.

items.statement: Preferential allotment to IHC received shareholder and CCI approval; awaiting RBI and SEBI approvals
items.quote: post the approval from the stock exchanges, we have also received shareholder approval and CCI approval. We await RBI approval for the preferential allotment and SEBI approval for the open offer.

items.statement: Long-term leverage target of 4x to 4.5x by around 2030 as cost of funds reduces and ratings improve
items.quote: As our cost of funds reduce, as the ratings probably improve, the leverage, which is about 2.2x, should settle in the range of 4x to 4.5x. That is the go -to long-term for the company, which I believe we should be hitting sometime around 2030.

items.statement: Expect to start paying dividends within a year of investment; long-term payout ratio target 30% to 40%
items.quote: And in a year or so of the investment, I believe we will be ready to start paying dividends. There is a dividend payout policy of the Reserve Bank of India. Conservatively, we believe that we should be in the 30% to 40% sort of dividend payout ratio over a longer-term, basis all the calculations of RoA and capital that we have simulated.

items.statement: Annualized credit cost guidance of 100 basis points for core mortgage product suite
items.quote: So what we've guided on the cost of credit is on a longer -term basis, an annualized credit cost of 100 basis points.

items.statement: Current incremental borrowing cost around 9%; target to reduce overall cost of funds by 270 bps by end of FY27
items.quote: Right now, we are borrowing at, give or take 9%. And we expect, as I said, a movement down to below 8% quickly right after this investment is to come through. On an overall stock basis, we would expect that in about 9 months to 12 months, the cost of funds should go down by about 270 basis points.

items.statement: Gross NPA improved to 1.2% from 1.3% at end FY25; Net NPA improved to 0.7% from 0.8%
items.quote: At the end of financial year '25, our gross NPA was at 1.3%, which is now at 1.2%. Net NPA was at 0.8%, which stands at 0.7%.

That INR1.03 lakh crores now stands at about INR17,000 crores. So about INR85,000 crores of loans have come back to our partner banks and financial institutions. And th

items.statement: Net collections of INR5,000 crores from legacy book this year; expect bumper Q4 collections and recoveries via IBC
items.quote: This year, we've already done net collections of about INR5,000 crores while maintaining the overall asset quality. And I'm quite optimistic as it was last year, the fourth quarter would be a bumper quarter in cash collections and recoveries. Just earlier this week, we've had major progress in a couple of large recoveries on the IBC front.

items.statement: Branch expansion calibrated at ~10 branches per quarter; blueprint to reach 400-500 cities over next 2 financial years post-investment
items.quote: And as of right now, our pace is calibrated, so we will look at only adding about 10 branches a quarter. We've made a blueprint as to how do we get to about 400 to 500 citie s very, very quickly over the course of the next 2 financial years. The pace of the rollout will increase very rapidly post the investment coming through.
