items.statement: India net debt-free with free cash ~Rs. 12,250 million; consolidated net debt negligible at Rs. 256 million as of Dec 31, 2025
items.quote: As on 31st December 2025, the India business continued to remain net debt-free with free cash of ~Rs. 12,250 million. At the consolidated level, net debt stood at a very negligible level of Rs. 256 million at the year-end.

items.statement: CRISIL upgraded long-term credit rating to AAA/stable in CY2025
items.quote: During the year, CRISIL upgraded the company's long-term credit rating to AAA/stable, reflecting the strength of our balance sheet and cash flow profile.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of Rs. 0.50 per equity share for CY2025
items.quote: In line with our commitment to d elivering value to our shareholders, the Board has recommended a final dividend of Rs. 0.50 per equity share, subject to shareholders

items.statement: Government notified 4 labour codes in Q4 CY2025, incremental cost impact ~Rs. 14 crore absorbed in employee benefits expense
items.quote: During the quarter, the Government of India notified the 4 labo ur codes consolidating the existing labo ur laws, resulting in an incremental cost impact of Rs. 14 crore roughly, which has been recognized under employee benefits expense

items.statement: Currency benefits in Africa operational from CY2026 as 3-4 month inventory carried; real cost benefits to show from this year
items.quote: First of all, the main currency advantages would come starting from this year because in Africa, we normally carry 3 - 4 months of inventory or even higher than that. The real currency benefits is operational, and cost of operations will start showing from this year onwards.

items.statement: No specific working capital metrics discussed; cash flows healthy supporting balance sheet strength
items.quote: Our balance sheet remains strong, supported by healthy cash flows, providing flexibility to support organic expansion, invest in cold-chain and distribution infrastructure and pursue value-accretive strategic opportunities.

items.statement: Weather remains key risk; CY2025 was worst season in years due to unprecedented heavy rainfall
items.quote: Unfortunately, we have never had rains like we have had in the last year. If weather conditions are reasonable, there is no reason why we should not have the double-digit growth, which we are anticipating.

items.statement: Net realization per case improved 3.4% in Q4 CY2025 to Rs. 177.3; full year up 0.5% to Rs. 178.8
items.quote: Net realization per case improved by 3.4% in Q4 CY 2025 to Rs. 177.3 driven by improved realization in international territories. For CY 2025, net realization per case increased marginally by 0.5% to Rs. 178.8.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 revenue INR 720 crore, up 5.5% YoY; expected INR 20 crore higher but delayed to January
items.quote: For the quarter ending December 31, 2025, we did a revenue of about INR 720 crores as compared to INR 682 crores in the comparable quarter of last year, which is a growth of about 5.5%.

items.statement: FY26 full-year revenue growth expected to be much higher than 9M 4.3%, in line with previous guidance
items.quote: What we expect and we are very much on target to achieve that, is that by the end of the financial year, this growth rate should be much higher than what it is reported for the first nine months, more or less in line with what we had stated in the previous calls.

items.statement: Bavla site FY26 revenue expected ~INR 250 crore; bigger growth in FY27
items.quote: But yeah, it should be closer to about INR 250 crores by the by the end of the financial year.

items.statement: India business target INR 500 crore revenue in next 12-18 months, then INR 800 crore over 3-5 years
items.quote: So overall, our first target is to get to INR 500 crores of revenue, which should happen in the next 12 to 18 months is what our expectation is. And then the next target is to get to INR 800 crores of revenue coming out of India's side.

items.statement: French subsidiary expected breakeven next FY with both manufacturing lines
items.quote: So, what we are expecting is that in the next financial year, we should be breakeven in that particular facility with both the manufacturing lines.

items.statement: ADC co-investment second round (CHF 25M) to add ~CHF 30M incremental revenue; completion in ~1.5 years
items.quote: Again, I can repeat that we are on track, and this should be finished in about one and a half years.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA INR 113 crore (15.7% margin); 9M FY26 EBITDA INR 403 crore (19.4% margin) vs 15.9% YoY
items.quote: Overall, all of this translated into a reported EBITDA of about INR 113 crores, which is a margin of about 15.7% on the top line.

items.statement: CDMO margin 17% in Q3 (vs 22% YoY); 9M 19.7% (vs 17.2% YoY, +250bps)
items.quote: From a margin perspective, we did close to about 17% margin on the CDMO side of the business, which also includes our French facility, as compared to 22% in the previous financial year.

items.statement: Marketable Molecules margin 7.2% in Q3; 9M 17.5% (vs 8.3% YoY, +920bps); target 20% then 25%
items.quote: The Marketable Molecules segment did a 7.2% margin, largely because there was more of the cholesterol sales that happened in this quarter as compared to the previous quarter.

items.statement: Phase III margins 30%+; early phase 12-15%; commercial Switzerland ~25%; commercial India 35-40%
items.quote: Well, a broad range would be, in phase III is where we make our highest margins. So you know we're talking about upwards of 30%. The early phase would be close to 12% to 15%.

items.statement: ~INR 1,200 crore RFPs submitted from India site; expect 30-35% conversion
items.quote: And in terms of value, this would be close to about 1,200 crores worth of RFP's that have been given out. We expect that at least 30%, 35% of this should get converted into orders.

items.statement: ADC linker-payload: FY25 CHF 22M, FY26E CHF 30M, FY27E CHF 40M; volume ramp over 3-5 years
items.quote: For the last financial year, we supplied roughly about CHF 22 million worth of material to the customer. This year we expect it will be about CHF 30 million, and for the next year it could be closer to about CHF 40 million.

items.statement: Co-investment expansion with Japanese customer at Aarau/Neuland (Switzerland) in detailed engineering; construction starting soon
items.quote: The project is on track. We are now at the detailed engineering activities and planning, so that we can start soon with the construction, the preliminary work has already started.

items.statement: French facility manufacturing lines operationalized; D&A run rate ~INR 84 crore/quarter to continue
items.quote: The depreciation and amortization for the first nine months stood at about 250 crores, which is an increase as compared to the last year, largely on account of the operationalization of the manufacturing lines at our French facility, and more or less, it will remain at the same run rate as we look into the future.

items.statement: ADC capacity limited; second co-investment round to expand capacity for additional indications
items.quote: The current capacity we have is based on the first forecast the client came to us with, and as soon as the customer realized that he got more indications which were successfully tackled, he also came to us and asked for bigger capacities.

items.statement: French drug product site: increased RFPs, projects secured, interest in late-phase (Phase II+) projects
items.quote: The market shows increased interest in the product capabilities. We got more RFP's, more projects secured over the past quarter, and we also got interest in late phase projects, phase II and so on.

items.statement: Drug substance: passed mock FDA audit at Vionnaz (Switzerland); ADC molecules with priority status in oncology pipeline
items.quote: In drug substance, we passed successfully a mock FDA audit at the Vionnaz's site. This is one of the four swiss sites. That's a preparation inspection or a PAI inspection, which will be executed sooner or later by the FDA.

items.statement: Specialty: strong vitamin D analogue (VDA) sales, high-margin; cholesterol cost reduction ongoing; new wool grease sources at Veenendaal
items.quote: There we see a strong VDA, vitamin D and analogue sales. This is the branch and part of the portfolio with high margin. So, this is very satisfying, and we are happy about this.

items.statement: Added sales people in China and US; SPRINT initiative for early-phase projects; targeting big pharma expansion
items.quote: We have hired additional sales people in China and also in the U.S. So, the focus is on attraction of new development projects. This means early phase, but also late phase projects.

items.statement: Unified sales leadership under Francois Baduel (CBO) across all global sites since Sept 1
items.quote: Mr. Francois Baduel, Chief Business Officer is now leading the Dishman Group sales teams across all their sites globally: India, China, Switzerland, France, UK and Netherlands.

items.statement: 9M FY26 revenue mix: CDMO INR 1,750 crore (+6.7% YoY Q3), Marketable Molecules INR 330 crore (+21.5% YoY 9M)
items.quote: For the first nine months the revenue stood at about INR 1,750 crores as compared to INR 1,723 crores in the first nine months of the previous financial year.

items.statement: Q3 COGS ~20% (vs 15% YoY) due to higher commercial vs development mix; early-phase development margins lower
items.quote: The cost for the quarter ending December 31, '25 stood at close to about 20% as compared to about 15% in the comparable quarter of last year. The increase in the COGS specifically in this quarter was largely on account of higher commercial supply.

items.statement: Q3 finance cost INR 45.7 crore includes INR 11 crore one-time for Swiss syndicated facility refinancing/enhancement
items.quote: In this finance cost of INR 45.7 crores, there was a one-time expense of about INR 11 crores that was booked in this quarter. This was on account of the new syndicated facilities that we entered into with the consortium banks in Switzerland.

items.statement: 9M finance cost INR 130 crore (vs INR 170 crore YoY); Swiss SARON near 0%, effective rate 3-3.5%; expect lower coming quarters
items.quote: The finance cost stood at about INR 130 crores as compared to INR 170 crores. We are seeing the borrowing cost for us going down, especially at the Swiss entity, where now the SARON, which is the Swiss equivalent LIBOR has gone down to 0% and our effective interest cost is now between 3%, 3.5%.

items.statement: Q3 revenue delayed ~INR 20 crore due to key intermediate supply delay and Europe holidays; shipped in January
items.quote: We actually expected the revenue to be higher by about INR 20 odd crores in this particular quarter. However, there was a delay in the shipment of certain product, which has now gone out in January, and the delay was largely on account of delay in supply of key intermediate, as well as because of the holiday season in Europe because of Christmas.

items.statement: French facility ANSM approval received; driving inquiries and order conversions
items.quote: But overall, from a business perspective, after receipt of the ANSM approval, we are seeing a huge amount of inquiries, a lot of inquiries getting converted into orders.

items.statement: Japanese customer final API quote decision expected April/May; KSM already supplied
items.quote: And we expect -- so, the preliminary feedback was that they were okay with the, with the price that we had given, but the final confirmation that we should receive should be most likely in April or in

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin target of 19.5-20% reaffirmed; first nine months at 19.4%
items.quote: So, we could be ending the year with anywhere between 19.5% to 20%. So if you take the first nine months, we are already at about 19.4%.

items.statement: Target 25-26% consolidated EBITDA margin in next two years and 30% by end of 2030
items.quote: And that is the reason our target is to get as quickly as possible to the 25%, 26% consolidated margin that we were doing prior to March of 2020. So that's the first target to be achieved over the next two years and then get to the 30% EBITDA margin mark by the end of 2030.

items.statement: French subsidiary booked orders and strong pipeline after ANSM approval; 9M revenue EUR 7M, full year expected EUR 9.5-10M
items.quote: For the current financial year in the first nine months, we did a revenue of about EUR 7 million and we should end the year with close to about EUR 9.5 million to EUR 10 million of revenue.

items.statement: Japanese customer: fair visibility for next three years; co-investment underway; primary supplier for payload and linker across 5-7 ADC molecules
items.quote: We have a fair visibility on the revenues coming from this particular customer over the next -- at least for the next three years, and that is the reason why we are doing the co-investment along with the customer.

items.statement: Site utilizations: Swiss 75%, French ~20%, Netherlands 60%, Manchester 75%, Shanghai 50%, India 20-25%; no commercial capacity constraints
items.quote: So, for example, the Swiss site is operating at roughly about 75% capacity. The French site has just started operations last year, so that's at roughly about 20%. The Netherlands facility is at about 60%, Manchester at about 75%, Shanghai at about 50%, apart from that, India, which is at about 20% to 25%.

items.statement: India site targets 2.5x production utilization in 3 years; French facility similar ramp; Shanghai targets 75% utilization; Swiss aims to double development revenue in 5 years
items.quote: So India should be able to easily make a 2.5x of what it is doing today as far as the production capacity utilization is concerned. And as far as the French facility is concerned, it should be a similar kind of number that we will be targeting in the next three years' time.

items.statement: ADC linker+payload ~1.5% of end-product price; antibody ~20-25M of 60M addressable; Dishman supplies ~60% of linker/payload
items.quote: So, we being the primary supplier, I mean, if you talk about the ADC, that would be close to about, say, maybe 1.5% at max of the final product price that the customer is realizing.

items.statement: Partnership with Celonic (antibodies) enables end-to-end ADC offering (antibody, linker, payload, conjugation, form/fill/finish); RFPs issued; small biotech interest rising
items.quote: So, with this partnership with Celonic, we are able to offer the end-to-end solution to the customer, including the antibodies, the conjugation, the payload, and the linker.

items.statement: All regulatory hurdles behind: EDQM, US FDA, Japanese PMDA inspections successful; India site upgraded for long-term compliance
items.quote: All of the regulatory hurdles are behind us, not just from the EDQM, but we also had successful FDA inspection, even from the Japanese PMDA, all of the regulatory issues are now behind us.

items.statement: Net debt ~CHF 150 million, mostly Swiss franc denominated; priority to pay down higher-cost India rupee debt using free cash flows
items.quote: So basically, our net debt or a large portion of our debt is denominated in Swiss francs, and that will be the right way to look at our debt number. So, we are at close to about CHF 150 odd million of net debt.

items.statement: Development revenue composition higher than commercial in FY26 driving margin improvement from 17.3% to ~20%
items.quote: And that is one of the key reasons why from the last year's 17.3%, we should be ending the year with closer to 20% margin, and I think we stick to that even today as we see the full FY26.

items.statement: Quarterly margins volatile due to revenue mix (development vs commercial) and customer shipment timing; yearly view more appropriate
items.quote: Well, I would say the nature of our business is such that it is very difficult to have a linearity in the margins every quarter, because it all depends upon whether -- I mean, what is the composition of revenue that is driving the margins in that particular quarter.

items.statement: Asset base inflated by ~1,000 crore due to rupee depreciation vs foreign currencies; goodwill also significant non-cash item
items.quote: So right now, there is almost an effect of almost 1,000 crores plus sitting as part of the gross plot, just on account of the foreign exchange fluctuation.

items.statement: India-EU FTA benefits fine chemicals (tariff reduction) not pharmaceuticals (already exempt); BioSecure Act driving some pharma demand from China to India
items.quote: On the fine chemical part, personally I see a big chance because there they are falling on the tariff regimes, but if we have now a free trades agreement between Europe and India, there's absolutely the chance that we can produce more in India and export it to Europe.

items.statement: Customer geographic preference diverging: some avoid China, some avoid India; Dishman's multi-site footprint (India, China, Europe) captures both
items.quote: One part of the customer, they say, we want to go to Asia. It doesn't matter if it's China or India. Some people say everything, but China, and some people say everything, but India. So this is where our strength is, that we can offer whatever the customer expects.

items.statement: No guidance given for FY27 growth API business; will provide with ibuprofen decision in Q4
items.quote: So we don't give -- we are not yet ready to give a guidance for the growth business. We will do it along with our decision on ibuprofen.

items.statement: Non-ibuprofen growth API business at 56% gross margin and 25% EBITDA margin
items.quote: Adjusted for the ibuprofen losses, you will notice that the non-ibuprofen business now trades at a significant gross margin of 56% and EBITDA of 25%, which is above industry or in the higher end of the industry range for API businesses.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin 47% in Q3 FY26, down 386 bps QoQ due to ibuprofen headwinds
items.quote: Our gross margins are at 47% for the quarter. It's marginally down by 386 basis points on a Q-o-Q basis, primarily driven by the headwinds in the ibuprofen base business.

items.statement: Non-ibuprofen growth API business gross margins in 51-55% range continuously
items.quote: And we have clocked in close to 51% to 55% kind of a range of gross margins in that business continuously.

items.statement: Investing to convert Vizag plant to multipurpose and high potent API facility; targeting commercial production in 5-6 months
items.quote: Our intention is to get Vizag back, although it is FDA approved and live, to get it back into commercial production by -- in the next 5 to 6 months. And that would come with us making one of the blocks converting to a multipurpose plant, one of the blocks being converted to a high potent API plant. And we are making the necessary investments as we speak.

items.statement: Growth API business capacity utilization a little over 70%
items.quote: I was saying a little over 70%.

items.statement: Ibuprofen capacity 10,000-12,000 tons with only 3,000 tons utilization; Pondicherry 6,000 tons single-product facility; Vizag mothballed
items.quote: Having built both Vizag and Pondicherry with almost 12,000 tons of ibuprofen -- 10,000 to 12,000 tons of ibuprofen with our current capacity utilization of only about 3,000 tons, we are finding significant headwinds in this

items.statement: Debt reduced by INR146 crores (19%) adjusted for FX; INR113 crores from rights issue first call money by May 2026, INR33 crores from operational cash flows
items.quote: In our continuous journey towards a healthier balance sheet, we have been able to reduce our debt by close to INR146 crores adjusted for the foreign exchange impact as well what we have on the closing debt. And hence, we have reduced our debt by close to 19%, INR 113 crores of that coming from the rights issue money, w hat we had called in the first call, money of rights, by May '26 and balance IN

items.statement: Line of sight to reduce debt to sub-INR500 crores by May 2026 post final rights issue call money
items.quote: Further, we have a line of sight to reduce the debt to sub INR500 crores levels by May '26 post receipt of our final call money.

items.statement: Ibuprofen sold at 15-17% premium to competition due to big pharma customers; gross margin only 21% despite premium pricing
items.quote: Clearly, for the generic market, we're not competitive. We sell , our gross margin at 21% is in spite of us selling the product at least 15% to 17% greater than our competition because we sell to big pharma.

items.statement: New labour code effective 21st November 2025 caused one-time INR6.7 crores adverse impact from gratuity and leave encashment liability increase
items.quote: Further, the change in the labor wage code, which was effective on 21st November, has resulted in a onetime adverse impact of around INR6.7 crores, driven by the impact of increase in liability towards gratuity and leave encashment.

items.statement: Corporate actions (including Vizag carve-out) delayed pending ibuprofen strategic review; decision expected with Q4 results by end of April
items.quote: We expect to have this -- the results of an analysis to be part of our Q4 results. That will give a clear direction to the company. Our thinking today is that we would put more capital and growth around our growth API business and would take certain actions in terms of cost reduction or strategic resets on our ibuprofen business.

items.statement: Integrated CRAMS and chemistry structure retained; carve-out decision delayed as rest of business generates enough free cash to pay down debt
items.quote: Although at that time when we announced it, we thought it was the right thing to do, on further reflection, we think there's more value to retain everything in one house. And that is why we kind of delayed that decision until such time we have a clearer view on ibuprofen.

items.statement: Developed markets contribute 75% of overall sales
items.quote: Business contribution from our developed markets continues to be strong at 75% of overall sales.

items.statement: Ibuprofen derivatives part of growth business and growing; plain ibuprofen raw material is the loss-making segment
items.quote: The ibuprofen derivatives is not part of the numbers. The ibuprofen derivatives is a very significant business for us, and it is a growing business. It's part of the growth business. The derivatives are an important part of our business. So what we talk about ibuprofen is the ibuprofen plain raw material.

items.statement: Ibuprofen demand not catching up to new capacities built in India; excess capacity causing pricing pressure
items.quote: Given that with the advent of significant new capacities out of India and the demand for ibuprofen not catching up to the capacities that has been built, we have been facing significant headwinds on the ibuprofen business.

items.statement: Strategic review of ibuprofen business underway with external advisors; options include technical, commercial, or corporate actions; results expected by Q4
items.quote: In consultation with the Board, we have today decided to seek external advice in terms of what we should be doing with our ibuprofen business in the near term, while we continue to invest in the Solara growth API business and with more fil ings and approvals and customer acquisition, we expect that business to be a significant part of our future growth story.

items.statement: R&D revived with new investments and talent to support Vizag conversion and growth API pipeline
items.quote: And we were also balancing our equipment's, I mean, our capacities to meet that demand. And we also see the base business growing quite healthy. But to feed Vizag, we need to revive R&D to a much higher level, and we've done that with investments and new talent that has come in to lead those initiatives.

items.statement: OneSource CDMO product approval expected in FY27; specific revenue and margins not disclosed
items.quote: I think there is just a couple of products that we do with OneSource. I think your question was about , there's one specific product that we do with our CDMO OneSource. And that approval should come in the FY '27, our financial year time frame. I think that's when the product launch will happen.

items.statement: Target to grow 4-5% ahead of market (15-20% overall)
items.quote: our target is to grow between 15% to 20% ahead of the market, at least 4% to 5% ahead of the market. So that the direction still remains.

items.statement: 9M FY26 new order wins annualized peak revenue INR 20,636 million, 74% EV motors
items.quote: In 9 months of Financial Year '26, we achieved net new business wins with annualized peak revenues of INR 20,636 million.

items.statement: INR 982 crore of new orders to move to SOP in FY26
items.quote: nearly about INR 982 crores will move to SOP this year.

items.statement: India EBITDA 11.9% and PBT 7.6% in Q3 FY26, grew YoY and QoQ
items.quote: the India EBITDA and PBT were strong at 11.9% and 7.6%, respectively, and grew both on a year-on-year basis as well as sequentially.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA 9.3% in Q3 FY26 vs 9.2% YoY; PBT before JV 4.4% vs 3.2% YoY
items.quote: Our EBITDA for the quarter was around 9.3% as compared to 9.2% on a year-on-year basis. Our PBT before JV profits was 4.4% of revenue in Quarter 3 of FY '26 as against 3.2% in Quarter 3 of FY '25.

items.statement: India margin improvement driven by fixed cost control and operating leverage
items.quote: It's a combination of both, but mainly, if you really see the fixed cost part of it, I think there was a good amount of cost control, which we did there.

items.statement: Land purchase INR 150 crore near Pune, part in Q4 FY26, part spills to Q1 FY27
items.quote: we plan to invest close to about INR 150 crores in land, yes, of course, greenfield facility near Pune, in Pune. Entire thing may not come and hit us in Q4 this year. Part of it may come this year and part of it may spill over to Q1 of next year.

items.statement: FY27 capex INR 300-350 crore on new greenfield; outer years INR 250-300 crore
items.quote: Next year, let's talk about could be in the range of maybe INR 300 crores to INR 350 crores. Then in the outer years, it should moderate to maybe INR 250 to INR 300.

items.statement: Romania electronics capacity utilization very low; significant revenue growth from H2 FY27
items.quote: Romania at present, the utilization is very low of the capacity. And you will see that with a lot of new orders kicking in from the second half, the revenue growth will be significant from the second half.

items.statement: India auto production Q3 FY26: 2W +15%, 3W +34.7%, PV +19.1%, CV +17.5% YoY
items.quote: On a year-on-year basis, 2-wheelers grew by 15%, 3-wheelers grew by 34.7%, passenger vehicles grew by 19.1%, and commercial vehicles grew by 17.5%.

items.statement: EV revenue share 14.3% in Q3 FY26, up 50% YoY; 9M FY26 at 12.1%, up 38% YoY
items.quote: The revenue from supplying to EV vehicles in this quarter was at 14.3% of the revenues and which grew by 50% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: EV models revenue grew 53% YoY in Q3; 75% of new order wins are EV
items.quote: EV orders also add up to 75%, which actually indicates the strength of our EV product portfolio.

items.statement: Bajaj 46% of revenue; India 89% vs 11% overseas; non-Bajaj EV traction building
items.quote: customer segmentation, if you really see Bajaj adds up to 46%. And within India, 89% versus 11% outside.

items.statement: Non-Bajaj e-powertrain SOP from early FY27; one incumbent, one top 7-8 new player
items.quote: We are already starting an SOP with one of the customers for these e-Powertrain from early next year, and also in discussions with others, and we are very close to winning an e-powertrain business also with one more premier customer going forward.

items.statement: Net debt INR 4,405 million (9M FY26), up due to VRS INR 799M; net debt/equity 0.26
items.quote: The net debt of the company in the 9 months of Financial Year '26 is INR 4,405 million. This has increased for the first time after many quarters to the one-time cash outflow pertaining to our VSS. The net debt to equity is very comfortable at 0.26.

items.statement: Interest cost ~INR 100 crore for 9M FY26; no significant reduction till FY27
items.quote: In terms of the interest cost, yes, like what I mentioned, there won't be a significant reduction between now and end of the year. It will more or less be in this range.

items.statement: VRS: 400+ employees opted, INR 799M cost, 95% from ICE powertrain; payback ~4 years
items.quote: The first one is the launch of a voluntary separation scheme in which more than 400 employees opted for the benefits of the scheme, and this resulted in a separation cost of INR 799 million.

items.statement: VRS annual savings ~INR 20 crore+; no revenue impact seen in 1.5 months
items.quote: Yes, yes, that's right. It could be a little more than that. But yes, that's a safe number to go with.

items.statement: New labour code impact INR 225M incremental expense for gratuity/leave encashment
items.quote: The second exceptional item pertains to change in the definition of the wage as per the new labo ur code as a result of which we had to recognize an estimated incremental expense of INR 225 million towards reassessment of gratuity and leave encashment costs

items.statement: EU retail agreement and US tariff cuts positive for auto component exports; targeting US market entry
items.quote: The recent retail agreement with the European Union and reductions in reciprocal tariffs with the U.S. shows that the world is recognizing the importance of India, both as a market and as a reliable supply chain partner also.

items.statement: Metallic products (engine valves, forged parts) seen as key US export opportunity
items.quote: See, largely, I think a lot of these products are the metallic products, including engine valves, which is a very big product for us, a lot of the forged machine products, which we do already.

items.statement: OPmobility arbitration EUR 66M; no provision made; claims disputed as unreasonable/frivolous
items.quote: We feel that these claims are very unreasonable. Yes, some of them are frivolous. So we cannot provide for that.

items.statement: R&D spend ~INR 25-28 crore quarterly for 4W lighting/electronics; steady state near current levels
items.quote: the overseas R&D investment will more or less be around these levels for the near future. So there should not be a significant increase in the overseas R&D spending.

items.statement: Store addition target for FY27 is 80-90 showrooms for Kalyan Jewellers India
items.quote: Yes. So, the store count for the next couple of years may will be in this range of 80 to 90, KJ India.

items.statement: Overseas store expansion target is 6-7 showrooms per year for the next couple of years
items.quote: So, that is why we maintain overseas expansions in the range of about six to seven showrooms a year. That should be the target for the next couple of years.

items.statement: FY26 maintenance capex for India is Rs 175 crore; regional brand 5 showrooms may come partly this year or next; Candere 30-40 showrooms at Rs 2-2.5 crore each
items.quote: So, this year should be in the range of what Rs. 175 crore for maintenance CAPEX India and the regional five showrooms might not come this year, it can come in the next financial year maybe, partly this year. And Candere around what 30 - 40 showrooms with around Rs. 2 crore - Rs. 2.5 crore of CAPEX.

items.statement: Regional brand showrooms capex estimated at Rs 4-5 crore per store for 5 stores in next 12 months
items.quote: So, regional we will open only five showrooms in the next 12 months and the CAPEX should be in the range of what Rs. 4 crores to Rs. 5 crore per store.

items.statement: Q4 started well with strong customer traction, walk-ins and momentum despite volatile gold prices
items.quote: Yes. Q4 so far has been good. Customer traction has been strong. Even with this volatile gold prices, the customer walk-ins, footfalls, the momentum at the store are running strong.

items.statement: Upbeat about ongoing wedding season across the country and expect to end FY26 on a very strong note
items.quote: We are upbeat about the ongoing wedding season across the country and expect to end the financial year on a very strong note.

items.statement: Gross margin improved due to higher studded share, procurement changes, higher franchisee revenue share, new FOCO store operating leverage, and silver/platinum price surge
items.quote: Multiple factors have contributed. First being the encouraging improvement in our studded share across most of our markets, including South markets, during the last quarter. items.quote: Honestly, I don't know, I mean why would it affect us. I mean trade is more for goods, right. Services were not under tariffs anyway.

items.statement: 9M FY26 revenue INR 758 crores (+18% YoY), EBITDA INR 142 crores (+29% YoY), PAT INR 97 crores (+24% YoY)
items.quote: For the 9 months ended of the Financial Year 26, the operating revenues were reported at around INR 758 crores, representing a growth of nearly 18% year-on-year. The EBITDA stood at INR 142 crores, which grew by nearly 29% year-on-year, with the EBITDA margins being at 18.7%.

items.statement: NTCF demand improved post GST cut on tyres and automobiles leading to higher volumes in Q3; further improvement expected in Q4
items.quote: In the tyre cord segment, demand for NTCF improved post GST cut on tyres and automobiles leading to higher volumes in Q3. We expect demand to improve further in Q4 due to these lower GST rates.

items.statement: Filament yarn demand weak post festive season in Q3 but expected to improve in Q4 with marriage and summer season
items.quote: In the filament yarn segment, after festive season, fabric and yarn demand remained weak in Q3, but is expected to improve in Q4 with marriage and summer season.

items.statement: Margins under pressure from low Chinese prices and duty-free imports from FTA countries; US tariff changes and EU trade deal positive for future demand
items.quote: However, margins continued to remain under pressure due to low prices from China and duty-free imports from free trade agreement countries. Recent changes in the tariff situation with US and trade deal with EU are positive for future demand of tyres and yarns.

items.statement: PTCF approval process moving ahead smoothly with regular commercial sales expected to begin in FY27
items.quote: In addition, PTCF approval process is moving ahead smoothly with regular commercial sales expected to begin in FY27.

items.statement: Caprolactam prices increased after continuous decline since September 2024, supported by industry-wide production cuts in China
items.quote: On the raw materials side, caprolactam prices increased after a continuous decline since September 24, supported by industry-wide production cuts in China.

items.statement: Renewable energy at Bharuch plant helped control power costs; additional renewable capacity expected to be commissioned in FY27 to further reduce power expenses
items.quote: The use of renewable energy at Bharuch plant helped control power costs, with additional renewable capacity expected to be commissioned in FY27, which should further reduce power expenses.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA at INR 41 crores, up 50% YoY and 29% QoQ; EBITDA margin expanded to 9.93%, up 442 bps YoY and 220 bps QoQ
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 41 crores, which increased by 50 % YoY and increased by 29% QoQ. EBITDA margin expanded to 9.93%, up by 442 basis points YoY and 220 basis points QoQ.

items.statement: 9M FY26 EBITDA at INR 92 crores, down 13% YoY; EBITDA margin 7.56%, up 75 bps YoY
items.quote: EBITDA stood at INR 92 crores, which declined by 13% YoY. EBITDA margins for the period are 7.56%, an improvement of 75 basis points YoY.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty application for nylon filament yarn at final stage of notification; DGTR ruling expected by March 25th, likely in February or March
items.quote: The association has moved the anti-dumping duty application and which is at the final stage of notification. In fact, it was to be completed by December, but because of some changes in the DGTR, the date was extended up to March 25th. So, most likely, somewhere in February or March, we are expecting the final ruling from DGTR to be get notified.

items.statement: Rising caprolactam prices not expected to impact margins as pricing accounts for RM cost; only timing of pass-through could be an issue
items.quote: No. Actually, our pricing is normally taking into account the RM cost. In the past, we used to have stock losses when the prices are falling. Actually, a rising market normally should not give any issues on the margins.

items.statement: Renewable energy capacity at 15% currently, expected to increase to 30-35% post second phase commissioning in later half of FY27
items.quote: So, on a company basis, it is about 15% currently. Vipulkumar Shah 15? Suresh Sodani 15 of both the sites combined together. And it should increase to about 30 -35% post commissioning of second phase, which is expected in later half of FY27

items.statement: Additional renewable power expected to yield annualized savings of INR 10-12 crores versus grid rates; full benefit to flow in FY28
items.quote: So, assuming that the grid rates remain the same, we should have in excess of about 10 to 12 crore rupees gain on account of the additional power which would come on an annualized basis. So, it will depend on when actually we start getting it. But as I said, it should be most likely in the later half; second half of FY27. Vipulkumar Shah So that full 10 to 12 crore benefit will flow

items.statement: PTCF capacity expansion under evaluation after first phase commercialization; exploring other product opportunities using nylon and polyester yarns
items.quote: So, we could look at opportunities to increase our PTCF capacities in future, which is still under discussion because the first phase still needs to get commercialized on a regular basis. But that we are also evaluating other opportunities to get into other pr oducts where we could use our nylon and polyester yarns

items.statement: Future investments focused on value-added products in nylon filament yarn (not significantly adding to top line but supporting bottom line) and technical textiles/reinforcements; no further investment in nylon tyre cord
items.quote: So, what I'm saying is in the nylon filament yarn, our investments are towards improving the value addition to our current portfolio, so which will not significantly add to the top line, but it should be sufficiently supporting our bottom line on this product segments. As far as the expansions in future are concerned, that will be more towards technical textiles, which basically covers our reinfor

items.statement: Post-GST improvement in reinforcement demand continued in early Q4; tyre companies seeing replacement market pickup supporting tyre demand
items.quote: So, as I mentioned, post GST , we have definitely seen an improvement in reinforcement demand, which has continued in the early part of Q4 as well. As mentioned, we are hopeful of this demand to continue because the t yre companies are also seeing the replacement market now picking up.

items.statement: PTCF expected to deliver similar margins to existing nylon tyre cord business; projects have minimum 12% IRR threshold
items.quote: We expect similar margins . Since we report our results in single segment , I will not be able to give you breakups of that. But normally, our projects have a minimum threshold of 12% IRR. So , you can expect that kind of margins to add to the bottom line once the commercial supply start.

items.statement: Exports mainly yarns and depolymerized chips; no tyre cord fabric exports currently; polyester tyre cord fabric could open export opportunities long-term after domestic approvals
items.quote: Our exports are mainly just yarns basically and some depolymerized chips that we sell. We don't sell any tyre cord fabric mainly because the nylon tyre cord fabric demand in US and Europe and other markets is very low because the tyres are made in India and exported like farm tyres or OTR tyres. However, in future, once we have domestic approvals for our polyester tyre cord fabric, that could open

items.statement: Buyback referred to board and senior management; promoters aware of investor views; management focus on deploying cash for growth projects
items.quote: Actually, this has been referred to our board as well as senior management. Promoters are aware of this, and we continue to inform them the views of the investors and the shareholders. But our aim as management is to deploy and utilize the cash on balance sheet for projects, which will give good growth and sustainable profitability to the business, and that focus would continue.

items.statement: Company is debt-free with positive cash on balance sheet; working capital limits not significantly utilized; finance cost very low
items.quote: Actually, we are debt free. In fact, we have positive cash on balance sheet. So, our limits are only limited to some working capital that also is not significantly utilized. So, our ratings are good and we get good return and good interest rate, but if you can see, our finance cost is very low, which is coming in the profit loss.

items.statement: PTCF raw material is PET/polyester chips sourced mainly domestically from Reliance; import trials started for multiple sources
items.quote: We buy the PET chips, polyester chips, mainly domestic is from Reliance. We have started some trials with imports as well. So, we are looking at all opportunities since it is still at a phase where we are starting and we are more in terms of stabilizing and getting regular , but we're evaluating and we're keeping multiple sources.

items.statement: Caprolactam prices rising after Chinese production cuts (~10%) due to unsustainable margins; prices expected to stabilize at sustainable levels for producers
items.quote: We have seen that prices increasing somewhere from October almost after a year . And one of the reasons is that the caprolactam producers even in China were struggling because of the low margin over their base raw materials. So, there was a cut, possibly an industry level cut, that's what we hear from the reports that close to 10% production cuts were taken by caprolactam producers in China, which

items.statement: Mother yarn and VAP investments of over INR 30 crores completed in previous year; small capacities added in current year; supporting nylon filament yarn margin improvements
items.quote: We had in total invested over 30 crores on these two, three projects, which have given good returns and continue to support our nylon filament yarn business.

items.statement: Nylon filament yarn imports from China up 50-70% QoQ and YoY due to weak Chinese domestic demand and US tariffs diverting Chinese exports to India
items.quote: But in terms of volume, on a QoQ basis and on a YoY basis, the imports have gone up by -- particularly in the nylon filament yarn are higher by between 50% to 70%.

items.statement: PTCF approval process rigorous with extensive testing by tyre companies for passenger car tyres; single ply reinforcement makes it more critical than nylon tyre cord
items.quote: Actually, whenever we give a new product, especially in a completely new segment, the t yre companies go through a very rigorous approval process because it's not a regular product and they do multiple audits. They do extensive testing both at the lab scale, but also by making t yres and running them on the roads because, one, it is going to passenger car t yres; second, this product in a passenge

items.statement: Total volume for 9M FY26 declined 12% YoY to 52,981 metric tons; tyre cord fabric sales down 24% YoY to INR 571 crores; filament yarn sales down 19% YoY to INR 599 crores
items.quote: Total volume for the period declined by 12% YoY to 52,981 metric tons. Tyre cord fabric sales for the period declined by 24% YoY to INR 571 crores, while filament yarn sales declined by 19% YoY to INR 599 crores.

items.statement: Company exited and decommissioned old inefficient capacities over last 2-3 years; now evaluating new investments to significantly improve return metrics
items.quote: And third is that we have actually exited and decommissioned a lot of our old capacities which were either very inefficient or already done that, I'm just giving in terms of last two, three years. So that process to a large extent come to a level where now we have started looking at the new investments in a perspective where that should give a significant uptick to the return number and that shoul

items.statement: Domestic underlying volume growth was 11% in Q3 FY26, with Consumer & Bazaar at 9.7% and B2B at 7.4%; domestic UVG has been inching up over the last 8 quarters.
items.quote: If you look at our total domestic business, which is made up of both Consumer, Bazaar as well as the B2B business, that reported underlying volume growth of 11%. And I think the challenge that we faced in this quarter was on account of exports, probably the harshest quarter in terms of whatever is happening in the geopolitics world.

items.statement: Exports declined 13.5% in Q3 FY26 due to geopolitical challenges, but management expects the impact to be largely behind them by the turn of the quarter.
items.quote: And therefore, our exports in totality declined by 13.5%, which resulted in an overall underlying volume growth of 9%.

items.statement: Standalone gross margins improved ~200 bps YoY due to benign input prices; VAM consumption cost was $830/tonne vs $884 last year.
items.quote: Our gross margins at a stand-alone level improved by about 200 basis points as input prices remained benign. Just for information, VAM consumption in the quarter was at about $830 as compared to $884 in the same period last year.

items.statement: A one-time provision of INR47 cr (standalone) and INR52 cr (consolidated) was taken for the new Wage Code impacting gratuity and leave encashment.
items.quote: Basically, for two elements, gratuity and leave encashment, we have recognized the impact because of the new Wage Code that resulted in a onetime charge of INR47 crores in stand-alone and about INR52 crores in consolidated.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin improved 24 bps to 24.5% despite the one-time wage provision and higher A&SP spend.
items.quote: And despite all that one-offs and increased A&SP spending, our stand-alone EBITDA margins improved by about 24 basis points and stand at 24.5%.

items.statement: Management aims to sustain EBITDA margin at the upper end of the 20-24% range for the full year, reinvesting margin gains into growth.
items.quote: Look at a slightly longer term, look at a full year as a basis. In this one quarter, yes, it may appear to be ahead of or above the comfort corridor. But if you look at full year, we are confident that we will be at the upper end of this 20%, 24% range.

items.statement: Pricing growth of 100-150 bps over volume is expected to be maintained through tactical pricing and price laddering, though not guaranteed every quarter.
items.quote: I think my view is that in the zone of about 100 to 150 bps, in and around there, I think you should continue to expect, I think it would be our endeavor, but will it flow through as a formulate number quarter- on-quarter, year-over-year, perhaps

items.statement: Dr. Fixit growth is distinctly better than the last 2-3 years; Roff growth is very robust; FeviSeal sealants, UnoFin, Fevicol Shoefix, Fevicryl Yudu, Fevicol Nail-free Ultra, and Roff Starlike epoxy grout are gaining traction.
items.quote: If you look at Dr. Fixit's growth this year is better than the growth has been in the last 2 to 3 years. I can tell you that. I think it is distinctly better. So we pushed this up a little bit. Roff's growth at this moment is very robust, very good.

items.statement: Core adhesive portfolio (Fevicol) growing at 1.2-1.4x GDP with robust single-digit growth; innovation and premiumization pilots underway to inch up growth further.
items.quote: I think in all these spaces, we are seeing robust single-digit growth. I think more like 1.2 to 1.4x of the GDP. So in the zone. Could it be a bit better? Yes, I think that is an area we would like to continue to strive for.

items.statement: No slowdown seen in residential construction; portfolio spans repair/renovation (70-75%) and new construction (25%); ultra-high-end and second-home segments are not slowing.
items.quote: Our portfolio has new construction, renovation and repair. And renovation and repair account for maybe 70% plus, I would say, 70% to 75%, and new construction is more like 25%, maybe a little higher, so depending on the cycle.

items.statement: Construction business spans residential, commercial, government, infra and industrial segments; no slowdown seen in any segment; budget focus on Tier 2/3 cities and infrastructure supports 3-7 year outlook.
items.quote: As of now, I can confirm to you that we haven't seen any slowdown whatsoever even in residential. And by the way, within the industry, we keep talking to each other who are in the allied businesses. And as of now, we do not see any slowdown in any part of the construction segment.

items.statement: Management believes market share is being gained in waterproofing (Dr. Fixit) and tile adhesives (Roff) through retail and projects push; category creation and penetration drive growth.
items.quote: I think with the growth which we are seeing, I think that definitely would be the case is my sense. And I can tell you now for both Kavinder and me, I think that is why our focus is a lot on growth. We want to have growth, which is very clear, which is a standout growth if I can use the word meaning which is not like in the zone of the market.

items.statement: Tile adhesive category growing at 18-20% (vs tile market at 8-10%) driven by penetration; Roff aims to grow well ahead of category with premium NioPro range.
items.quote: What is happening is the penetration of tile adhesive and tile laying is growing pretty fast, at least we believe in high double digits in terms of about 18%, 20%, roughly to that effect. So it is a game of penetration.

items.statement: VAM prices have stabilized in a narrower range due to significant capacity expansion in China not consumed locally, stable acetic acid and oil feedstocks; VAM now <10% of raw material basket.
items.quote: Historically, the range has been much narrower than what you saw during that disruption. And one of the reasons that you could ascribe to it is that there has been significant capacity expansion in China, and that capacity is not getting consumed locally.

items.statement: Distribution expansion continues via Pidilite Ki Duniya (PKD) and pilot of 'super PKD' for deeper reach, phygital demonstration, and user education; bulk of growth from existing outlets via premiumization and range expansion.
items.quote: Basically, when we go deep down, we have been looking at what we have been talking about Pidilite Ki Duniya( PKD). I think there is continuous work happening on basically making sure that we go deeper in PKD and there is also pilot happening on what we call super

items.statement: Haisha Paints expanding to Eastern states but right-to-win model still being polished before all-India rollout; Electronic adhesives expanding TAM to automotive and consumer electronics, undergoing rigorous 12-18 month specification and tes
items.quote: We continue to progress well but we are still not and I keep saying this, sorry, for it may seem like a repetition of what I said, but then that is the case. I think we are making steady progress, but we are not being able to ascertain for ourselves as to what our right-to-win model is.

items.statement: EU trade deal benefits will accrue but ratification by European Parliament is 6-9 months away; impact likely in second half of next fiscal; business development for EU geographies underway.
items.quote: EU trade deal till the time it is ratified by the European Parliament and all that, is at the very least, 6 months away, maybe 9 months away. So therefore, anything in that in terms of when the rubber hits the road on the ground will happen only towards the end of this year.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty persists (Russia-Ukraine, Middle East, Iran) with potential commercial ramifications; company is learning to live with it.
items.quote: Even now, it is on, and to be fair, I think some of the wars are far from over. Russia-Ukraine is not over as yet. There is also the conflict in the Middle East. There is also the overall Iran question.

items.statement: India automotive production robust in Q3 FY26 across PV, 2W, CV, tractor, 3W segments driven by festive demand, rural recovery, policy tailwinds
items.quote: India's automotive production remained robust in the October -December quarter, driven by broad-based strength across Passenger Vehicles, 2-wheelers and Commercial segments as OEMs ramped up output to meet domestic and export demand.

items.statement: Expects PV, Tractors, 2W to hit all-time high production in FY26; LCV sub-segment also to reach all-time high
items.quote: Looking ahead to fiscal year 2026, we anticipate a period of steady and robust growth for Indian automotive industry. The outlook is very positive as we expect 3 of the core segments, the Passenger Cars, Tractors and 2 -Wheelers to achieve all -time high production levels.

items.statement: Mobility business grew 18.5% YoY in Q3 FY26 driven by Power Solutions (+19.5%) and 2W Powersports (+58.3%)
items.quote: Quarter-on- quarter, the Mobility business has shown 18.5% in October, December 2025 as compared to October, December 2024, driven mainly from the Power Solutions business, w hich grew by 19

items.statement: Revenue from operations grew 9.4% YoY to INR48,856 million in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Quarter-on-quarter, revenue from operations in October, December '25 stood at INR48,856 million, which grew by 9.4% over October, December 2024.

items.statement: EBITDA grew 5.1% YoY to INR6,124 million in Q3 FY26; margin improvement driven by favorable product mix and expense optimization
items.quote: The EBITDA for October, December '25 was INR 6,124 million, which grew by 5.1% over the same quarter of the previous year. The improvement in EBITDA margin was primarily driven on account of favorable product mix and optimization of expenses.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBIT margin at 10.5% after first provision for New Labour Code
items.quote: we had already, again, a very strong quarter with a very good 10.5% EBIT. And we also did already the first provision for the New Labou r Code

items.statement: Product mix impact on margins: new products start as finished goods import, then assembly, then localization; tractor stable but common rail and exhaust gas components in early localization phase
items.quote: if new products are coming in, we are usually starting this -- we first bring the finished goods into the market, then we start the assembly and testing. Then if this is stabilized, we start with the localization.

items.statement: Capex for FY27-28 under consideration; no guidance given; investments adjusted based on customer volume forecasts and capacity utilization buffers
items.quote: We are currently under -- or in consideration, and we do not want to give a guidance.

items.statement: Exports growing steadily in spark plugs, sensors, pumps to Japan/Korea; main focus remains Indian market
items.quote: We have increased already our export volume for the spark plugs in 2025, and we expect also further good development of volumes in the spark plugs and in components for the common rail products.

items.statement: OBD-II norms implementation from April 1, 2025 driving 58.3% growth in 2W Powersports exhaust gas sensors
items.quote: The 2-Wheeler business grew by 58.3%, mainly on account of higher sale of exhaust gas sensors due to ramp-up for OBD-II norms implementation from 1st April 2025.

items.statement: No visibility on precise TREM V implementation date; discussions with OEMs indicate timeline still open
items.quote: At least at this point of time, there is no visibility of a precise date of TREM V implementation. So things are still quite open as far as we know with our discussions with the OEMs.

items.statement: Targeting e-axles as largest value component for EV 4-wheelers in India; in advanced discussions with several OEMs; currently supplying chargers and DC/DC converters
items.quote: From the portfolio of Bosch Limited, we will strongly aim to begin in e-axles and that would be the biggest component that comes into an electric vehicle. So we are in advanced discussions with several OEMs.

items.statement: Hydrogen fuel engine development: working with virtually every CV/bus OEM; vehicle testing ongoing; no known rollout plans yet; infrastructure readiness key; expect significant activity by 2030
items.quote: We are working very closely with virtually every commercial vehicle and bus OEM in India. And as you've probably seen in the press or in media, there's a lot of vehicle testing activity that's currently ongoing.

items.statement: India-EU FTA signed; impact under study; localization strategy (local-for-local) unchanged regardless of duty changes; logistics costs favor localization at volume
items.quote: The Bosch approach with or without FTA has always been to have localized production wherever the demand is and our international production network always operates on that theme of producing in the region where it's relevant and where it's consumed.

items.statement: Dividend policy clarified to 55-80% of profit payout range; previous policy was open-ended; final decision remains with Board
items.quote: we've just brought a lot more clarity into our dividend policy right now. If you looked at our previous one, it was an open policy. There were no limits or ranges set and it was completely left open.

items.statement: Power Solutions division strong growth across all segments with exceptional performance in Tractor and HCV segments boosted by GST 2.0 rollout
items.quote: The Power Solutions division delivered strong growth this quarter on the back of broad-based growth across all segments with exceptional performance in Tractor and Heavy Commercial Vehicle segments, boosted by successful rollout of GST 2.0.

items.statement: 2W Powersports: key technology partner for new launches including TVS Apache RTX 300 and Harley X440 T with integrated Bosch powertrain and safety systems
items.quote: The launch of new TVS Apache RTX 300 powered by advanced Bosch systems marked a significant new chapter for the iconic Apache brand. In addition, we further demonstrated our role as a key technology partner with the launch of the Harley X440 T.

items.statement: Bidadi plant awarded CII SCALE Awards 2025 for digital excellence and innovation in logistics; integrated autonomous digital ecosystem automates entire logistics value stream
items.quote: our Bidadi plant was recently awarded at the prestigious National CII SCALE Awards 2025 for digital excellence and innovation in logistics for developing an integra ted autonomous digital ecosystem that automates our entire logistics value stream

items.statement: CV demand robust for HCV and LCV driven by GST 2.0, government fleet orders, construction/mining activity, and last-mile delivery; trend expected to continue
items.quote: the Commercial Vehicle demand both for HCV and LCVs has been very robust in the last quarters. And it's connected to, in our view, a good demand following the GST 2.0 changes and of course, increased offtake on government fleet orders and ongoing activities around construction and mining.

items.statement: Localization ongoing: NOx sensor for common rails localized in 2025; further localization planned for common rail products and NOx sensors; pumps relocated from Japan to India in last 1.5 years
items.quote: this year, we have -- in '25, we have localized NOx sensor component for the common rails. We are going ahead with more localization for the common rail products. We will go ahead in the perspective of also local the NOx sensor.

items.statement: Power Tools division facing intense price pressure from Chinese competitors; Cordless segment achieved double-digit growth for fourth successive year; dealer network expanded to 1,800 partners, 25,000 retail points across 1,600+ cities
items.quote: the last -- past year was one of navigating a challenging market characterized by intense price pressure, particularly from competitors in China. This resulted in moderate growth for the division in both our quarterly and year-to-date results.

items.statement: Power Tools: Standard line launched for artisans at accessible price point with new 100+ distributor network; Hand Tools launched as new segment achieving INR100 million revenue in first year
items.quote: we successfully launched the Hand Tools as a new business segment. This initiative demonstrates strong market acceptance, achieving INR100 million in revenues within the first year.

items.statement: Margin improvement trajectory: last 3 years show PAT growth from cost improvement and localization; product mix and new product localization cycles temper near-term margin expansion; no 3-4 year guidance given
items.quote: if you look at the overall result for the last 3 years, then of course, we had a tailwind with the growth, which helped us. But we also did a lot of cost improvement and localization. So you see the EBIT is -- or profit after tax is going up.

items.statement: Mobility Aftermarket rebounded after temporary GST 2.0 impact in October; growth driven by OE/OES block and core product groups (diesel, wipers, braking systems)
items.quote: The Mobility Aftermarket began with a temporary sales impact from the GST 2.0 implementation in October, but we saw a strong rebound shortly thereafter. This recovery was supported by a synchronized upturn in the automotive sector.

items.statement: Expect market momentum to continue in coming quarter and better performance going forward
items.quote: we are happy that the market momentum has been positive and we expect this to continue in the coming quarter, and we are looking forward to much better performance as we go forward.

items.statement: JLR reconfirms FY26 EBIT >0% and free cash flow negative GBP 2.2-2.5 billion
items.value: negative GBP 2.2 billion to negative GBP 2.5 billion
items.quote: we are reconﬁrming our guidance of greater than 0% EBIT and free cash ﬂow in the range of negative GBP 2.2 billion to negative GBP 2.5 billion

items.statement: JLR FY26 capex guidance GBP 3.6-3.7 billion
items.quote: Capex guidance, I think, will be GBP 3.6 billion, GBP 3.7 billion from what I can see today.

items.statement: India business FY26 capex expected Rs 4,200-4,300 Cr
items.quote: We expect to end the year somewhere around Rs. 4,200 Cr to Rs. 4,300 Cr for the full year.

items.statement: India PV Q3 EBITDA margin 7%, EBIT margin 1.2%, up ~1% QoQ
items.quote: EBITDA margin and EBIT margin for the quarter stood at 7% and 1.2%, respectively, about a 1% gain on a quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: JLR Q3 EBIT margin -6.8%, better than Q2 due to inventory restocking reversal
items.quote: EBIT was minus 6.8%, better than Q2, though this is largely the eﬀect of inventory build -down in Q2, relieving the balance sheet of som e manufacturing costs, and that eﬀect reversing in

items.statement: India PV industry Q4 growth expected 13-14%, Tata Motors ~40% YoY; FY26 industry ~8-9%, Tata Motors mid-teens
items.quote: We clearly see that the growth of industry in Q4 will be around 13% to 14% kind of a zone. We should be 40%, roughly that kind of a growth rate. So, we expect that for FY26, therefore, the industry would grow by about 8% to 9%, rough estimate, I would say. Whereas for us, we should be somewhere in mid-teens.

items.statement: JLR order bank end Q3 higher than end September; Defender order intake ~10,000 units/month post Dakar win
items.value: higher than end September; ~10,000 units/month Defender
items.quote: decent place at the end of Q3 and is higher than it was at the end of September, so we are building order intake relatively strongly. And I think the power of our brands is our biggest advantage, and I did mention the Dakar win early on, we are already seeing a direct inﬂuence of that on the order intake on Defender. So, Defender order intake is now around 10,000 units a month from the global pres

items.statement: Sierra capacity ramp-up in two phases over next 5-6 months; Sanand 2 dedicated capacity being increased; supplier constraints at Tier 1-3 (castings)
items.quote: In-house capacity ramp up is happening to the extent of capacity, which has been dedicated to Sierra in our Sanand 2 factory. But we are also increasing the capacity further in two phases in the next ﬁve to six months. And therefore, the waiting period, which today would be, say, around six to seven months, should progressively come down as we ramp up and further ramp up with the enhanced capacity

items.statement: India PV commodity impact ~1.7-2% of revenue recent quarters; Q4 impact still being assessed
items.quote: Generally we have been seeing even in the last few quarters it has been about 1.7% to 2% of our revenue. We are still assessing what is going to be the impact in Q4.

items.statement: India PV Q3 FCF ~Rs 300 Cr; positive working capital changes on high demand; cash profit after tax less capex adverse ~Rs 200 Cr
items.quote: we have seen it about Rs. 300 Cr. The cash proﬁt after tax less investment spend was adverse by about Rs.200 Cr, but there were positive working capital changes in the quarter on the back of high demand , resulting in FCF of ~Rs. 300 Cr

items.statement: JLR Q3 working capital significantly negative from inventory build-up and lower volume; YTD working capital c. GBP 1.25 billion negative, portion to reverse in Q4
items.quote: Working capital was signiﬁcantly negative from the inventory build-up and the lower volume quarter. Cumulative year-to-date working capital is c. GBP 1.25 billion negative, although a proportion of that will reverse in Q4

items.statement: Consolidated net debt ~Rs 39,000 Cr; India business cash positive ~Rs 5,000 Cr; JLR net debt ~Rs 39,000 Cr (GBP ~3.9bn)
items.value: ~Rs. 39,000 Cr consolidated; India +Rs. 5,000 Cr; JLR ~Rs. 39,000 Cr
items.quote: Consolidated net debt for the group stands at ~Rs.39,000 Cr. The India business is cash positive at ~Rs.5,000 Cr, while JLR is at net debt of ~Rs.39,000 Cr.

items.statement: JLR started FY26 with ~GBP 250m net cash; FY26 FCF guidance negative GBP 2.2-2.5bn + GBP 450m dividend paid; net cash not returning in 2-3 quarters
