items.statement: JM Financial Credit Solutions now 100% subsidiary after minority buyout
items.quote: And Credit Solutions now has become a 100% subsidiary of JM Financial Limited, and we also get the benefit of consolidating that business 100%.

items.statement: Wealth Management recurring AUM up 33% YoY to INR33,100 crores; recurring proportion 29%
items.quote: The recurring AUM of all our wealth businesses grew by 33% year-on-year to INR33,100 crores. The proportion of recurring to total AUM has increased to 29%.

items.statement: Mutual Fund non-liquid average AUM up 15% YoY to ~INR12,000 crores
items.quote: On the mutual fund space, the average AUM from non-liquid funds has increased by 15% year-on-year to approximately INR12,000 crores.

items.statement: Affordable Home Loans AUM up 23% YoY to ~INR3,200 crores
items.quote: AUM has increased by 23% year-on-year to approximately INR3,200 crores.

items.statement: Private Markets focus loan book yield ~13.5%; book stable at ~INR4,000 crores in Q2/Q3
items.quote: So, I think we have a yield of approximately 13.5%. And if you look at the quarter 3 and the quarter 2, loan book has been pretty stable, around INR4,000 crores.

items.statement: IPO execution delayed due to market volatility (US trade deal, gold/silver prices, FPI selling)
items.quote: When you have a lot of volatility, because of the pending U.S. trade deal, the sudden increase in prices of gold and silver and some FPI selling, then it's hard in volatility to get transactions done.

items.statement: H2 FY26 revenue expected ~20% higher than H1; Q4 revenue guided 9-10% above Q3
items.quote: We expect H2 to end at around 20% higher revenue, as I mentioned in the previous call, than H1 on a consol basis as guided in the last quarter.

items.statement: FY27 domestic revenue growth target ~25%; international (incl. acquisitions) 12-15%
items.quote: Domestic business overall should grow around 25% for next year. That's the plan for next that's the plan we have been making and we are working on that. And export business should grow around 12% to 15%.

items.statement: Consolidated FY27 revenue growth expected >20% including full-year acquisition impact
items.quote: That's correct, Bharat. More than that I think, of course, what we are projecting right now, definitely, the numbers look to be around 20% or even more.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin guided 25-27% for FY26; currently at higher end at 26.6% for 9M
items.quote: On a 9-month basis, our stand-alone EBITDA margin is 26.6%, which is at the higher end of the guidance as per what we have provided at the beginning of the year, and we expect to remain maintain it for the rest of the year.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 consolidated gross margin 68.4% (+300 bps YoY); operating EBITDA margin 24.2% (excl. acquisition costs)
items.quote: The gross profit in quarter 2 was INR338 crores and quarter 3 was INR338 crores, reflecting a margin of gross margin of 68.4%, an increase of almost 300 bps as compared to quarter 3 last year.

items.statement: Standalone Q3 EBITDA margin 26.8%; 9M standalone EBITDA margin 26.6%
items.quote: On a stand-alone basis, operating EBITDA is INR112 crores, reflecting an EBITDA margin of 26.8%.

items.statement: Dialysis machine sales target revised to ~450 for FY26 (from 500-600); >600 machines in pipeline
items.quote: We have sold more than 300-plus machines till now. And hopefully, we end the year close to around 450 machines, though it is slightly lower than what is projected around 500 to 600 machines earlier.

items.statement: PendraCare and Citieffe acquisitions added INR48-49 crores revenue in Q3; expected ~15% of consolidated FY27 revenue
items.quote: These 2 acquisitions for quarter 3 have added about INR48 crores, INR49 crores to the top line.

items.statement: INR234 crores capex in 9M FY26 for new plants at Mitrol, Haridwar, Faridabad; YEIDA land acquired, plant operational in 18-24 months
items.quote: We continue to invest in future growth with a capex of INR234 crores we have done in the first 9 months of the current financial year. These funds will be deployed to set up new factories in Mitrol and Haridwar. Faridabad, Haryana, with Haridwar also in Utarakhand as well as expand capacity at our existing plants.

items.statement: PendraCare and Citieffe operating at 50-60% capacity, offering immediate growth pathway
items.quote: Currently, both the businesses are operating at 50% to 60% of the current capacity, offering a clear and immediate pathway for growth as we integrate and scale.

items.statement: Transitioning from low-tech to high-complexity segments: cardiology, critical care, orthopedics via acquisitions and indigenous R&D
items.quote: We are currently transitioning from low technology products to high complexity, high-growth segment. This isn't just a change in our product list, it's a fundamental upgrade of our business model.

items.statement: DCGI approval received for IVL and DEB (ASP >INR1.15 lakh); 90%+ currently imported, Polymed among first indigenous developers
items.quote: We have recently received full regulatory approval from DCGI for 2 groundbreaking next-generation products, Intravenous Lithotripsy System, IVL and Drug Eluting Balloon, DEB.

items.statement: Domestic cardiology: 7,000+ drug-eluting stents implanted; RisoR stent clinical study >200 patients enrolled
items.quote: As of date, we have already implanted more than 7,000 drug-eluting stents, a strong signal that our product is getting traction and earning favorable feedback from our patients and interventional cardiologists.

items.statement: Domestic private market (88% of domestic) grew 22.5% YoY in Q3; government business deliberately reduced (target 6-7%)
items.quote: Further in the domestic business, our private market, which is almost 90% of our current domestic business grew by 22.5%, while the government business, which is around 10% to 12% of our current business has witnessed a degrowth of 18%.

items.statement: International organic business stabilizing; Europe revenue +25.7% YoY in Q3 (INR162 crores); RoW +9.5% (INR181 crores)
items.quote: Revenue from Europe stood at INR162 crores in quarter 3 FY '26, showing a year-on-year growth of 25.7%. Revenue from rest of the world region has grown at 9.5% from quarter 3 '25 to reach INR181 crores in quarter 3 of FY '26.

items.statement: Chinese dumping across global markets (ex-US) at 25-30% growth; pressing government for anti-dumping duties and FTA route closure
items.quote: And globally, you have seen that data that Chinese exports have considerably increased, though they were minus 20% in U.S., but still they've grown 25% to 30% in all other global markets, because they have been dumping and reducing pricing.

items.statement: Engaging government on Chinese imports via FTA at 0% duty; PLI insufficient without systemic protection
items.quote: And I think probably that's a bigger concern today. And even today, I had a meeting with the Secretary in the medical device department and pharmacy department, and we have clearly told them that what is happening today and what is actually hampering India's exports and India's manufacturing growth, what are these factors.

items.statement: US-India trade deal cuts tariffs 15-18%; 15 FDA-approved products, 5-7 in pipeline; re-engaging customers post-tariff reduction
items.quote: The recent trades announcement with EU, U.K., U.S. creates good long-term opportunity for Indian companies in medical devices, and we are hopeful that we should be able to capitalize on them and when they get formalized on both sides.

items.statement: Net working capital ~140 days for 9M FY26
items.quote: Our net working capital number for 9 months will be close to 140 days.

items.statement: Liquidity INR840 crores at quarter end; supports organic and inorganic growth
items.quote: Turning to our balance sheet, we ended the quarter with a liquidity of INR840 crores. This strong cash position allows us to continue backing ambitious growth strategy, both organic and inorganic.

items.statement: Completed PendraCare (EUR10M) and Citieffe (EUR17.5M) acquisitions; integration progressing well; targeting tech acquisitions in critical care, cardiology, orthopedics
items.quote: We have successfully completed the acquisitions of PendraCare and Citieffe Group. These are not just transactions. These are strategic additions to significantly enhance our portfolio and market reach.

items.statement: Hired ~100 people in 9M FY26 (80-90 sales reps + clinical/R&D); cardiology hires cost ~INR2 lakh/month vs INR60-70k for infusion
items.quote: Actually, number Rahul was saying is 100, close to 100. So we have almost hired 100 people. Now all these people will become productive in the coming, so we are building the whole operational structure.

items.statement: Dialysis market share 10%, targeting 15-17% in 2-3 years
items.quote: Poly Medicure holds 10% share of the dialysis market today with a target of 15% to 17% over the next 2, 3 years.

items.statement: China dumping, trade disruptions, regulatory delays, government payment delays remain key uncertainties
items.quote: Having said that, there are still considerable uncertainties, specifically around aggressive China dumping as well as trade-related disruption.

items.statement: Operating profit pool growth expected roughly equal to revenue growth in FY27
items.quote: I think it will be more or less equal, Bharat bhai.

items.statement: FY27 capex guided at INR2,000 crores plus/minus INR200 crores
items.quote: Our FY '27 capex will be close to about INR2,000 crores plus/minus INR200 crores.

items.statement: FY26 capex spend estimated at INR600-700 crores so far
items.quote: This year, I don't have the exact number right now, but we would have spent close to about INR600 crores to INR700 crores in the current financial year.

items.statement: Ari Dongri iron ore mine capacity to double from 2.35 to 6 million tons with EC received, CTO expected soon
items.quote: GPIL has received much awaited environment clearance from Ministry of Environment for risk and climate change for more than doubling the iron ore mining capacity of Ari Dongri mine from 2.35 million to 6 million tons.

items.statement: Beneficiation plant of 5.4 million tons EC received, completion targeted by end of Q2 FY27
items.quote: Environment clearance and consent to establish for 5.4 million ton crushing and beneficiation plant has also been received and we expect to complete the work for beneficiation plant by end of Q2 FY '27.

items.statement: Additional 2 million ton pellet plant commissioned in Dec 2025, total capacity now 4.7 million tons
items.quote: I'm pleased to highlight that additional 2 million ton iron ore pellet plant has commissioned and operations commenced in December '25, with commissioning of GPIL total pellet manufacturing capacity to more than 1.7x from 2.7 million to 4.7 million tons.

items.statement: CRM complex 0.7 million tons on track, construction starts April 2026, commissioning targeted March 2027
items.quote: Progress on 0.7 million tons CRM complex remain on track with land acquisition completed, major equipment order finalized and bank funding secured. Construction will begin in April 2026. Commissioning targeted for March '27.

items.statement: Captive solar capacity expanding 3x from 165 MW to 540 MW, phased completion March 2026 to March 2027
items.quote: GPIL is also expanding its solar -- captive solar capacity by over 3x from 165 megawatt current to 540 megawatt to support captive consumption across iron ore mine, integrated steel plants and CRM operations.

items.statement: Battery energy storage system (BESS) manufacturing 20 GW capacity with INR1,025 crores capex, commissioning targeted Q4 FY27
items.quote: Additionally, as you are aware, company has decided to venture into manufacturing of battery energy storage system with an initial capacity of 20 gigawatt with a capex of INR1,025 crores during 2026, '27 and commissioning of BESS project is targeted for Q4 FY '27.

items.statement: Disinvestment of 37.85% stake in Ardent Steel for ~INR91 crores, completion expected by March 2026
items.quote: As a part of the company's ongoing efforts to simplify and streamline group structure, the Board has approved disinvestment of its entire 37.85% stake in Ardent Steel, which operates a merchant iron ore pallet plant. This stake is being divested for an approximate value of INR91 crores. This transaction is expected to be completed by March '26.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin expanded to 20% from 17% YoY despite lower pellet volumes and softer realization
items.quote: In Q3, on year on base year basis, EBITDA margin expanded to 20% from 17% in Q3 FY '25, despite a marginal decline in realization and pellet volumes.

items.statement: 9M FY26 EBITDA and PAT margins strong at 22% and 14% respectively despite softer realization
items.quote: Still EBITDA and PAT margins remained strong at 22% and 14%, respectively.

items.statement: Domestic steel demand expected to grow steadily in CY26 supported by INR12.2 lakh crore infrastructure capex in Budget 2026
items.quote: India's steel demand is expected to grow steady through the calendar '26 supported by infrastructure-led growth with budget '26 allocating INR12.2 lakh crores towards infrastructure capex, providing strong demand visibility.

items.statement: Safeguard duty led to 5-10% price rise in finished and intermediate products, expected to support profitability in 2026 onwards
items.quote: With imposition of safeguard duty, the prices of finished and intermediate products across value chain have risen by 5% to 10%, which is expected to support profitability in 2026 and onwards.

items.statement: No export plans currently as domestic demand strong and export delta over $15-17 per ton; booked till end of Q4
items.quote: Today -- see, today, we are selling everything domestically. We have no intentions of entering the export market at the moment because the difference is almost -- the delta is very huge. The delta is more than $15, $17 at the moment.

items.statement: DRI uses 100% imported RB1 coal (0.5-0.6 MT annually); pellet and power plants use 0.4 MT domestic coal; 60% imported, 40% domestic mix
items.quote: See, for our DRI, 100% we completely import RB1 coal. So that's about 0.5 million, 0.6 million tons annually. And for our coal gas operation for pellet plant and for our power plant, we do about 0.4 million tons of domestic coal. So the ratio is about 55% or 60-40, 60% is imported and 40% is domestic.

items.statement: Q4 imported coal cost ~INR11,000/ton; DRI coal cost INR8,000/ton in Q1 due to forward buying; max 5-7% variation in Q1, substantial impact from Q2 onwards
items.quote: Our current cost in the Q4 quarter, absolute value is about INR11,000 of import. Our DRI per ton contribution is INR8,000 in Q1 because we have -- we do forward buying. So Q1, the cost will vary maximum is about 5%, 7%.

items.statement: Pellet plant utilization expected >90% in FY27, targeting 4-4.2 million tons production
items.quote: for next year -- next financial year, we will operate at more than 90% capacity. Siddharth: The entire capacity? Abhishek Agrawal: Yes. So we should be able to produce more than 4 million, 4.2 million tons from next year onwards

items.statement: BESS first year utilization assumed 40-50% (8-10 GW of 20 GW line), operating margin modeled at 7%
items.quote: So just to be on a very -- because it's a new vertical, totally a new field, even we have considered a 40% to 50% plant load for the first year. So April '27 to December -- March '28, we consider a production capacity of say 8 to 10 gigawatts only against 20 gigawatt line.

items.statement: CRM complex EBITDA margin expected 8-10% once established, conservative initially due to branding/marketing costs
items.quote: On a year-on basis, I see EBITDA -- operating margin level at about 8% to 10% on the maximum side, 8% to 10%.

items.statement: FY28 revenue guidance INR12,000-15,000 crores from steel complex (INR6,500-7,000 cr), BESS (INR5,000 cr at 8 GW), CRM (INR2,000 cr at 50% capacity)
items.quote: So put together, anything between INR12,000 crores to INR15,000 crores will be the turnover from FY '28.

items.statement: Peak gross debt ~INR1,500 crores in FY27 for announced capex; debt tied up with prepayment option and drawdown flexibility
items.quote: Debt will be close to about say -- peak debt at FY '27 as of the capex which have been announced till date will be in the range of net debt will be lower but on the gross side, it will be in the range of about INR1,500 crores.

items.statement: New labour codes impact minimal at ~INR7-8 crores annually (INR70-80 lakhs/month) from FY27
items.quote: So there will be a very marginal impact, probably, I think, hardly about INR7 crore, INR8 crores on an annual basis. So not a huge impact.

items.statement: Free cash flow ~INR2,000-2,500 crores annually from FY28 if no steel plant; all FCF deployed to steel plant if approved
items.quote: Very difficult because see, if you don't go ahead with the steel plant, then probably from FY '28 once all our capex are done and the new production capacity comes up, there will be close to about INR2,500 crores or INR2,000 crores of free cash every year.

items.statement: 1 million ton blast furnace steel plant decision by April-May 2026 Board meeting; capex ~INR5,000 crores if approved
items.quote: Capacity will be 1 million, and the capex we envisage should be somewhere about INR5,000 crores.

items.statement: Boria Tibbu mine expansion to 4 million ton beneficiation (1.5 MT concentrate at 40% recovery) planned, EC filing Q1 FY27, operational ~FY30
items.quote: So 4 million, 100%, 4 million beneficiation. So the output concentrate will be close to about 1.5 million tons at 40% recovery.

items.statement: Pellet split shifting to 80% high-grade / 20% low-grade from current 65/35; two new plants high-grade, one commercial grade
items.quote: So 80% will be high grade, 20% will be low grade. My apologies.

items.statement: Ferro alloy prices range-bound at INR70,000 ±5% (INR68,000-74,000); currently at INR74,000-75,000 expected to hold for few months
items.quote: Yes, so ferro alloy prices has been hovering INR70,000 plus minus 5% benchmark. On the lower side, it went to INR68,000 when the market was lull in Q3. And today, when the market is good, the prices have moved up to about INR74,000.

items.statement: Mining cost expected to remain ~INR3,000/ton long-term despite deeper mining (100m to 140-150m) offset by solar, BESS, beneficiation
items.quote: So we still expect the mining cost to be at 3,000 level in the longer term, which is currently right now.

items.statement: Solar + BESS to reduce average power generation cost from INR3.75 to below INR3/unit; mining grid tariff INR11 to INR3, plant INR7 to INR3
items.quote: On total put together, our annual cost -- average cost of generation, which is currently about INR3.75, should be well below INR3.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA and PBT to grow faster than revenue in coming quarters
items.quote: With integration behind us, we expect EBITDA and PBT to grow faster than revenue in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Express EBITDA grew 19% YoY and 6% QoQ in Q3 FY26
items.quote: The EBITDA from the business for the quarter stood at INR 18 crores, representing a 19% growth year-on-year basis and 6% sequentially.

items.statement: Consultative Logistics EBITDA grew 2% YoY in Q3 FY26
items.quote: The EBITDA from the business for Q3 FY '26 stood at INR 46 crores, which is a 2% growth on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: E-waybill generation grew 23.6% YoY in December 2025 to 138.4 million
items.quote: E-waybill generation under GST reached 138.4 million in December 2025, representing a robust 23.6% growth.

items.statement: GST collection grew 6.2% YoY in January 2026 to INR 1.93 lakh crores
items.quote: GST collection for Jan 2026 stood at INR 1.93 lakh crores, up 6.2% year-on-year.

items.statement: Consultative Logistics warehouse space under management at 8.1 million sq ft as of December 2025
items.quote: The business has a warehouse space under management of 8.1 million square feet as on the close of December 2025.

items.statement: Realization per tonne increased 2% YoY and 0.4% QoQ to INR 11,610 in Q3 FY26
items.quote: The realization per tonne for Q3 FY '26 came in at INR 11,610 per metric tonne, which is 2% up year-on-year and 0.4% up from last quarter.

items.statement: Price hike of 10.2% effective January 2026 expected to flow through to EBITDA
items.quote: If you see in our presentation on the Express side, we have given the price realization number, which has gone up by 2%. The growth would be slow, but definitely, the focus is there on that number to grow. And whatever delta will straight away have an impact flow through in our EBITDA.

items.statement: Technology budget of INR 12 crores for next financial year, INR 2-3 crores per quarter
items.quote: On a year, we are looking at INR 12 crore number. On a quarter-on-quarter, it will be around INR 2 crores to INR 3 crores, which would be spread across 5 to 6 key initiatives.

items.statement: OU modernization deferred to next year, estimated INR 10-15 crores
items.quote: OU modernization is some piece which we were looking, but we had deferred it for next year. That could be in the region of INR 10 crores to INR 15 crores for next financial year, not in this year.

items.statement: Asset-light model maintained, no owned trucks, all on rental basis
items.quote: We are on an asset-light model, Thomas. We don't own any of our trucks. These are that model actually, available on rent.

items.statement: Signed major multinational 3PL player for automotive MNC in January consuming both Express and CL services
items.quote: As recently in the month of Jan itself, we signed a major multinational third-party logistics player that operates for large automotive MNC and now is consuming both services and was previously consuming only 1 aspect of our business.

items.statement: E-commerce clients deferred expansion plans muting CL growth in Q3
items.quote: The growth in the CL, Contract Logistics for our consultative logistics was muted as certain e-commerce customers deferred their expansion plans.

items.statement: Gained market share in organized sector in December and July-September quarters while 3 other large players lost share
items.quote: In the month of December, we were only ones along with another to grow the market share. We are 1 of the 2, 3 other large players lost market share.

items.statement: Targeting 20% EBITDA CAGR from FY25 base over 3 years to FY30
items.quote: We are looking at '27, '28, and eventually going to FY '30. So, this year, if you see the numbers which we have shared, we have a 7% growth as of December.

items.statement: 9-month FY26 revenue grew 7% YoY to INR 1,544 crores, EBITDA grew 9% YoY to INR 174 crores
items.value: Revenue INR 1,544 crores, EBITDA INR 174 crores
items.quote: On a 9-month basis, the revenue reached INR 1,544 crores, a 7% growth from same period last year. The EBITDA came in at INR 174 crores, representing 9% growth as compared to last year.

items.statement: Plan to reduce debt in phased manner over next 2 quarters, debt profile lower by Q1 next year
items.quote: On the deleveraging front, yes, we would look at pairing out some of the debt. That is not much of a concern because that's within the tolerance level. So, we would do it in a phased manner. Over the next 2 quarters, actually, if you see Q1 of next year, the debt profile will be slightly lower as compared to what we are now.

items.statement: New leadership team from Allcargo Gati now managing merged entity, priorities unchanged focusing on service quality and shareholder value
items.quote: Allcargo Gati, which is merged with Allcargo Logistics. So, the management team of Allcargo Gati have now been given the responsibility in the name to manage this business under the name of Allcargo Logistics. So, nothing changes on a broader horizon. Just that the team, which was managing earlier, Allcargo Gati is now managing Allcargo Logistics. I hope that answers your question. And the priorit

items.statement: Confident of better Q4 for both Express and Consultative Logistics businesses
items.quote: As I said earlier, some of your other colleagues on the call also asked us about both the Express and CL business, how Q4 is going to look? How it's both going to be? Is it going to be better? And the answer was definitive definitely. So, I will stay with that answer.

items.statement: Refer to Slide 17 for indicative guidance on revenue, margins, EBITDA for FY27
items.quote: Slide 17, if you look at, you will get indicative guidance on revenue, margins, EBITDA, if you refer to Slide 17.

items.statement: Balancing volume growth and yield growth critical for profitable growth strategy
items.quote: We are very cognizant that the business operates on 2 important pillars. One is the yield pillar and the second is the volume pillar. So, going ahead, we will balance both of these.

items.statement: Government FY27 capex outlay increased to INR 12.2 lakh crores supporting logistics sector
items.quote: Even in the recent budget announcement, the Government's FY '27 capital expenditure outlay has been increased to INR 12.2 lakh crores.

items.statement: Arena expected to reach breakeven next year; steady-state revenue around $400-500 million
items.quote: I think next year, we might move towards a breakeven. That's the thought process. But all the efforts are on to make sure this turnaround is in place.

items.statement: ROCE internal threshold 16%, expected range 18-20%
items.quote: Our internal target, I mean, that's the threshold which we would not want to breach is 16% for sure. Our expectation, we should range between 18% to 20%.

items.statement: PC demand strong at 21% YoY growth driven by component shortage and price increases; AI PC penetration at 28% of commercial revenue
items.quote: On the End Point Solutions Group, the PCs, we saw some really nice growth this quarter at 21% year-on-year, contributing to 32% of the top line. The PC demand was strong, partially driven by the component shortage and the price increases.

items.statement: Refresh cycle delayed; volumes may be under pressure for 12-18 months due to component shortage
items.quote: Yes. I think it is very possible. We're still not seeing that refresh cycle on the 10 to 11 that active anymore. People are delaying those refresh cycles.

items.statement: Gross margin down 47 bps YoY; 38 bps from Arena exit, balance from TSG margin drop and inventory provisions
items.quote: Overall gross margin is down just by about 47 bps on a year-on-year basis. Out of this, about 38 bps is on account of Arena alone. And the balance, it is on account of drop in TSG.

items.statement: TSG margin compression due to excess competition and brand margin pressure; limited legroom to increase gross margin unilaterally
items.quote: There is an excess competition in this space. Even the brands are compressed in terms of margins. So we see not much legroom in terms of increasing the gross margin unilaterally.

items.statement: SSG delivers higher-than-average PAT; gross margins stable in MSG, ESG, SSG; mix shift driving overall gross margin decline
items.quote: Again, I don't think there's a structural issue. We did talk about TSG, there is a margin compression. But in terms of MSG, ESG and SSG, we see stable margins there.

items.statement: TSG large deals pipeline building; some closed in Q3, more to fructify in Q4 and Q1
items.quote: We have a lot of orders in the pipeline. So you will see this moving up as we move forward.

items.statement: Capex INR112 crores in Q3; net fixed assets up INR60 crores YoY to INR653 crores; investments in ProConnect warehouses, AI COEs
items.quote: It is a INR60 crores increase in net assets from INR 591 crores to INR653 crores on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Building AI capability center in Chennai; creating AI go-to-market teams in India and Middle East; developing AI Agentic catalog
items.quote: We are creating a capability center Information Classification: RL\General Business\Redington in Chennai. It started with an AI competent team to work on its internal and external use cases and proof of concepts

items.statement: PC price increases passed to consumers; no gross margin benefit to Redington; new price hikes coming in upcoming quarters
items.quote: The price rises clearly will be passed on to the consumer. And I think there was a window of opportunity and time where there's still the OEMs are sitting on older stock.

items.statement: Working capital days reduced to 28 days; net debt down INR1,000 crores YoY despite 22% revenue growth; interest cost 22 bps of revenue (ex-Arena)
items.quote: Very efficient management of working capital has led to the overall lowering our working capital days to 28 days.

items.statement: Normal working capital range 35-40 days; upside risk from data center deals, SSG and TSG growth requiring higher working capital
items.quote: I think -- I mean, on a steady-state basis, that's the range that we all need to look for. Second, with the data center type of a business, which requires sometimes high working capital deployment.

items.statement: Arena factoring cost down 50% YoY to INR18 crores; overall factoring cost INR33 crores vs INR71 crores; Arena debt down to INR94 million from INR126 million
items.quote: Overall factoring cost for the current quarter is INR 33 crores vis-a-vis INR71 crores for last year.

items.statement: Arena interest cost INR43 crores vs INR38 crores YoY; net finance cost down 17% to INR60 crores from INR73 crores
items.quote: But if you take the interest cost, Arena's interest cost for the current quarter is INR43 crores vis-a-vis INR38 crores last year. So net-net, overall, INR60 crores in the current year vis-a-vis INR73 crores last year, a 17% drop.

items.statement: Turkey concordat cases: INR20 million exposure, INR8 million provided, INR12 million outstanding; no reversal expected, slow collection
items.quote: Out of INR 20 million, as we discussed, about INR 8 million we had provided and the balance INR12 million. It's going to take time.

items.statement: Mobility 15% YoY growth, 35% of revenue; premium segment and direct-to-retail strong; Arena Connect exit offset some growth
items.quote: Mobility continues to be a good shining star for us at 15% year-on-year, contributing to 35% of the top line, driven by strong demand in the premium segment.

items.statement: TSG declined 7% YoY due to deal timing; YTD growth 5%; data center deals emerging with Neo cloud and sovereign cloud players
items.quote: While we saw a decline at 7%, it is largely driven by timing of large deals executions across quarters. There's clearly a lot more data center business and deals with the emergence of Neo cloud and sovereign cloud players in the market.

items.statement: AI PC penetration 28% of India commercial PC revenue; gaming strong in consumer; desktop surge as brands gain share from white label
items.quote: The AI PC penetration in India Commercial PC segment was on the rise with 28% of the revenues coming from AI-focused PCs.

items.statement: Data center opportunity emerging from budget tax holiday for foreign investments; building strategy for power, cooling, services, colocation for mid-market
items.quote: With the recent announcements in the budget on tax holiday for data center investments from foreign companies, this area definitely holds great promise for us.

items.statement: Government mandating reseller appointment for global data center players in India; early days but exploring direct business with hyperscalers
items.quote: It's early days, but we think it is definitely an opportunity. We are reaching out to the hyperscalers to explore the direct business that goes into corporates.

items.statement: Labour Code impact not significant; actuarial assumption changes caused INR13-14 crores one-off employee cost
items.quote: Because of the Labour Code, there is no significant impact. But there are certain assumption changes in the actuarial valuation that has resulted in some incremental one-off cost, and this is to the extent of about INR13 crores, INR14 crores.

items.statement: Employee cost quarterly run rate INR380-390 crores plus increment cycle; expected to remain in that range
items.quote: We think so. I mean, in terms of working capital, we are quite at it. Interest rate, we only see that coming down across the board. So we don't expect any major movement.

items.statement: Arena divested Vodafone contract to reduce interest cost and local currency exposure; executed well but impacts current quarter
items.quote: In order to reduce interest costs in the Arena operation, as we spoke in the past and to minimize local currency exposure, Arena has divested from their Vodafone contract as informed last quarter. This has been executed well.

items.statement: ProConnect goodwill impairment INR9.2 crores from 7-year-old acquisition; one-off due to contract renewal probability assessment
items.quote: This is in ProConnect, this is out of an acquisition we did about 7 years back. And we thought it may be important to have a clear review and take -- because this depends on a few of the contracts.

items.statement: Arena loss INR22 crores in Q3; trajectory improving with working capital down to INR129 million from INR179 million; hopeful for healthy levels by 2027
items.quote: The overall loss in Arena for the quarter was INR22 crores for us. Over the last few quarters, Arena has been taking a series of actions as we have discussed.

items.statement: ROCE 22.1% in Q3; India distribution opex 1.3% of revenue; PAT margin 1.43% similar to global level
items.quote: I'm sure you can very clearly see for the quarter, the ROCE stands at 22.1%. So that's something which is very critical for us.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR 8,849 crores as of Dec 31, 2025, split 29% Roads, 19% Irrigation, 12% Pipeline, 40% Mining
items.quote: As of December 31, 2025, the company's total order book includ ing the recently won EPC project stand at INR 8,849 crores. This is divided into 29% for the Roads pro ject, 19% for Irrigation project, 12% for Pipeline project and 40% for Mining project

items.statement: Q3 FY26 standalone EBITDA margin 5.2% due to subcontractor costs, project completion stage, and viaduct cost overrun
items.quote: And as you know, subcontractor project has compared to less margin. So, that is also one of the reason that our total EBITDA has reduced. And other reason, as I already told you, due to c ompletion of our projects in the final stage and one issue in viaduct construction in Ramanat tukara. So, these things actually has factored and reduced the

items.statement: Consolidated debt to reduce to ~INR 500 crores by March 2026 after SPV monetization
items.quote: Overall, actually, our debt consolidated as of December is around INR 2,400 crores. Out of INR 2,400, out of the 4 SPV that we are doing the monetization, their debt is around INR 2,100. So, debt consolidated as of December will be around INR 300 crores. And in future, also the debt is basically, we have this three HAM project is going on, and that only debt will come. So, you can say by March, af

items.statement: Executed SPA with Indus Infra Trust to sell 3 HAM SPVs for INR 1,543 crores total proceeds
items.quote: On December 24, 2025, the company executed Share Purchase Agreement with Indus Infra Trust for the proposed sale of its 100% shareholding, along with the subordinate debt in the following special purpose vehicles, KNR Palani Infrastructure KNR Guruvayur and KNR Ramanattukara. As part of this transaction, the company will invest around INR 566.8 crores in 4 SPVs in the form of equity and subordinat

items.statement: Standalone working capital days improved to 82 days from 93 days as of March 2025
items.quote: The working capital days stood at 82 days compared to 93 days as of March 25.

items.statement: Received LOA for iconic bridge project worth INR 319 crores from Musi Riverfront Development Corporation
items.quote: The company also received a letter of acceptance from the Musi Riverfront Development Corporation Limited for the construction of an iconic bridge across the Mir Alam Tank connecting Bengaluru National Highway at Shastripuram to Chintalmet under the EPC Mode. The project has a contract value of INR 319 crores and a construction period of 24 months.

items.statement: CRISIL reaffirmed long-term rating at AA/Stable and short-term at A1+, removed from Rating Watch
items.quote: Lastly, the CRISIL reviewed the company's long-term bank rating and reaffirmed them as a CRISIL AA with Stable outlook while removing the rating from the Rating Watch with Developing Implications. The short-term rating was also reaffirmed as CRISIL A1+ and also removed from Rating Watch with Developing Implications.

items.statement: NHAI awarded 712 km and MoRTH 1,448 km in 9M FY26; NHAI bid pipeline of INR 1.5 trillion
items.quote: Reflecting this trend, road project award during 9 months of FY '26 remained muted, with the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways and NH AI awarding 1448 km and 712 km of the project respectively. Looking ahead, the outlook for project award is improving. NHAI has already invited bid for projects aggregating to 1.5 trillion

items.statement: HAM project equity infusion: INR 727 crores invested of INR 962 crores revised; balance INR 235 crores (INR 87 crores FY26, INR 148 crores FY27)
items.quote: As of December 31, 2025, the company has already invested INR 727 crores out of INR 962 crores revised equity infusion required for all the HAM projects. The additional equity requirement of INR 235 crores to be infused as INR 87 in FY '26 and around INR 148 in FY '27.

items.statement: Mining project delayed 8-10 months due to forest clearance and Gram Sabha issues
items.quote: So, mining to start with, I think we are able to start that in coming second quarter next financial year or third quarter. Practically, it is possible to make it in third quarter as the forest clearance and the Banha rdih Village Gram Sabha could not be conclud ed. So, this is going to further take another 8-10 months’ time to start with

items.statement: NHAI bidding highly aggressive; may dilute margins 2-3% on some projects to win orders
items.quote: But I think one aspect I can say, but because the aggression in the market is very heavy here. So, we are also not looking at the margins as we used to look at earlier. Maybe we will have to dilute 2%-3% of the margins and then go ahead.

items.statement: Standalone debt zero with INR 80 crores cash surplus as of Dec 2025
items.quote: The standalone debt is 0 actually. And there is a cash surplus as of December of INR 80 crores on standalone basis.

items.statement: Completed acquisition of Allianz's 23% stake in Bajaj General and Bajaj Life Insurance on 8 Jan 2026; Bajaj Group now holds 97% in each.
items.quote: I am happy to confirm that on 8th January '26, Bajaj Finserv Limited, along with its promoter group companies, namely Bajaj Holdings and Investment Limited, and Jamnalal Sons Private Limited, successfully completed the acquisition of 23% equity stake held by Allianz SE in the two insurance subsidiaries namely Bajaj General Insurance Limited and Bajaj Life Insurance Limited

items.statement: Boards approved buyback of remaining 3% Allianz stake in each insurance company, subject to approvals; post-buyback Bajaj Group holding expected at 77.33% BFS, 18.1% BHI, 4.57% Jamnalal Sons.
items.quote: As regards the remaining 3% equity stake held by Allianz SE in each of the insurance companies, the Boards of the respective companies have approved to offer a buyback to its shareholders, subject to applicable law and necessary approvals.

items.statement: Buyback of Allianz stake expected to strengthen ROE and ROEV of both insurance subsidiaries going forward.
items.quote: The buyback, on one hand, will conclude the buyout of Allianz stake, and on the other hand, will also strengthen the ROE and ROEV of both the insurance subsidiaries going forward.

items.statement: Consolidated total income grew 24% YoY to INR 39,708 crore; PAT before exceptional items grew 32% to INR 2,936 crore.
items.quote: The consolidated total income grew 24% to about INR 39,708 crores versus INR 32,042 crores for the same quarter last year. The consolidated profit after tax before accelerated ECL provision of BFL and the one -time charge of new Labor Code grew by 32% to about INR 2,936 crores versus INR 2,231 crores for the same quarter last year.

items.statement: One-time Labor Code impact of INR 380 crore gross (INR 167 crore net PAT impact); accelerated ECL provision by BFL of INR 1,406 crore gross (INR 540 crore net PAT impact).
items.quote: The first one being the one-time impact of the new Labor Code, which impacts the bottom line by close to about INR 380 crore s at a gross level across all our companies. However, this has a net consolidated PAT impact for BFS of about INR 167 crores

items.statement: Bajaj General GWP grew 11.5% to INR 7,389 crore; excluding crop and government health, GWP grew 17.2%; GDPI growth 17.7%.
items.quote: The GWP for the Quarter 3 increased by 11.5% to about INR 7,389 crore versus INR 6,626 crores for the same quarter last year. Excluding the bulky tender-driven crop and government health business, the GWP increased by 17.2%.

items.statement: Bajaj General combined ratio improved to 97.9% from 101.1% YoY; ROE reasonably above 22% excluding surplus capital at 200% solvency.
items.quote: The combined ratio stood at a very healthy 97.9% for the quarter as against 101.1% for the same quarter last year. We believe that this combined ratio for Bajaj General will be among the lowest in the multi-line market, with the ROE reasonably above 22%, excluding the surplus capital at 200% solvency.

items.statement: Bajaj General adjusted PAT before Labor Code impact grew 8% to INR 430 crore; AUM grew 12% to INR 36,417 crore.
items.quote: The adjusted PAT before the impact of new Labor Code for the quarter stood at INR 430 crores versus INR 400 crores for the same period last year, a growth of about 8%.

items.statement: Bajaj Life VNB grew 59% to INR 405 crore; NBM improved to 19% from 15.1% YoY; retail weighted received premium grew 19.9% to INR 1,856 crore.
items.quote: The VNB for the quarter grew at a healthy 59%, up from INR 254 crores for the same quarter last year to about INR 405 crores during the quarter. The new business margin, NBM, is up at 19% for the quarter as against 15.1% for the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Bajaj Life retail product mix: Par 23%, non-par savings 14%, term 9%, annuities 11%, ULIPs 44%; retail protection grew 47%, group protection grew 29%.
items.quote: On overall retail weighted received premium basis, the product mix for the quarter was well balanced and stood as follows: Par was at 23%, non-par savings at 14%, term at 9%, annuities at 11%, and ULIPs at 44%.

items.statement: Bajaj Life setting up Pension Fund Management business and GIFT City branch; regulatory approvals process initiated.
items.quote: The company is also in the process of setting up a Pension Fund Management business and a branch in GIFT City for which process of regulatory approvals has been initiated.

items.statement: Bajaj Finance new loans booked grew 15% to 1.39 crore; AUM grew 22.1% to INR 4,85,883 crore; net total income grew 19% to INR 13,875 crore.
items.quote: Number of new loans booked during the quarter was at about INR 1.39 crores as against INR 1.21 crores in the same period last year, a growth of 15%. The company's diversified business model has enabled its AUM to grow at a strong 22.1% at about INR 4,85,883 crores.

items.statement: Bajaj Finance PAT before Labor Code and accelerated ECL grew 23.3% to INR 5,227 crore; Opex to Net Total Income improved to 32.8% from 33.1%.
items.quote: The profit after tax before the impact of the new labor codes and the accelerated ECL provision grew at a very healthy 23.3% during the quarter, from about INR 4,246 crores to INR 5,227 crores. The Opex-to-Net total income improved to 32.8% as against 33.1% for the same period last year.

items.statement: Bajaj Finance net Stage 2 and 3 assets decreased by INR 93 crore; GNPA 1.2%, NNPA 0.5%; capital adequacy 21.4%, Tier 1 20.6%.
items.quote: In Quarter 3, net decrease in Stage 2 and 3 assets were at about INR 93 crore s, reflecting a significant improvement in portfolio quality and a positive outlook on credit cost. The GNPA and NNPA stood at 1.2% and 0.5% respectively as of 31 December 2025, as against 1.1% and about 0.48% for the same period last year

items.statement: Bajaj Housing Finance AUM grew 23.2%; home loans 18%, LAP 32%, LRD 39%, developer finance 18%; NII grew 19% to INR 1,153 crore.
items.quote: It was a stable quarter with AUM growth of 23.2%, driven by good momentum and disbursement amidst higher portfolio attrition. Growth was very well -distributed across all the business segments. The home loans AUM grew 18%, loan against property grew 32%, lease rental discounting grew 39% and developer finance by 18%.

items.statement: Bajaj Housing Finance Opex to Net Total Income 19.0% vs 19.8% YoY; GNPA 0.27%, NNPA 0.11%; PAT before Labor Code grew 23.2% to INR 675 crore; CAR 23.15%.
items.quote: Operating efficiencies continued with Opex-to-Net total income at healthy 19 .0% as against 19.8% for the same quarter last year. Healthy asset quality was maintained with the GNPA and NNPA at about 0.27 % and 0.11% as of 31 December 2025.

items.statement: Bajaj Finserv Health transactions grew to 6.2 million from 2.1 million YoY; provider network: 1,34,000 doctors, 16,000 hospitals, 6,300+ lab touchpoints; revenue grew 22%.
items.quote: Bajaj Finserv Health in Quarter 3 carried out about 6.2 million healthcare transactions as against 2.1 million transactions for the same quarter last year. Bajaj Finserv Health continued to expand its provider network, which includes about 1,34,000 doctors, about 16,000 hospitals, and upwards of 6,300 lab touchpoints.

items.statement: Bajaj Markets lending disbursements INR 1,800 crore vs INR 1,549 crore QoQ; unique partners 101; revenue declined to INR 94 crore from INR 156 crore YoY due to SFDC migration.
items.quote: During the quarter, the lending in the BFSI space in the form of disbursements stood at about INR 1,800 crore s for the quarter as against INR 1,549 crore s for the preceding quarter, which was Quarter 2 of FY ‘26

items.statement: Bajaj Markets revenue growth expected to resume from Q4 FY26 after SFDC migration completion; no capital infusion since March 2022.
items.quote: Now, with the migration likely behind us during the Quarter 3, we are likely to see the growth resume here on. And from Quarter 4 onwards, we are hopeful that the revenue growth should get reinstated.

items.statement: Bajaj Finserv AMC AUM crossed INR 30,000 crore (26th rank); equity mix 56%, non-group share 87%; fastest to reach INR 30,000 crore in ~2.5 years.
items.quote: The AMC company continued its good run, recording an AUM of upwards of INR 30,000 crores as of 31st December 2025 and moving to the 26th spot amongst all the mutual fund companies in India in terms of AUM.

items.statement: Bajaj Life VNB margin expansion of 4-6.5% and ~50% VNB growth over last 4 quarters; base effects will cause tapering; GST impact delayed strategy by 2-3 quarters.
items.quote: Over the last 4 quarters, we have consistently seen margin expansion of 4% to 6%-6.5% and VNB growth close to an average of about 50%. However, the base effect does start kicking in. So, the margin expansion and VNB growth will definitely taper down from here on.

items.statement: Bajaj Life mitigated ~325 bps of 450 bps GST impact by Q4 FY26 exit; remaining 125 bps reset impact from 1 April 2026 to be absorbed in base.
items.quote: What we know today and based on what we have executed, I think as we exit next quarter, we would have mitigated close to about 325 bps against 450 bps that we had communicated earlier. We believe that delta of 125 is a reset impact from 1st April.

items.statement: Bajaj Life agency channel: ULIPs now profitable, term pickup wholesome, Par healthy; proprietary sales ULIP-heavy transitioning to term/riders; enhanced risk cover 44-47% of customer base vs 19% YoY.
items.quote: Our agency is unique. I have said this earlier as well, when we moved from a mass to a mass -affluent base of customers in the last 6-7 years, we used ULIP products significantly. The ULIPs we used to sell earlier weren 't necessarily very profitable. Now our ULIPs themselves are looking quite healthy.

items.statement: Bajaj General motor OD loss ratio elevated industry-wide due to GST-driven IDV drop reducing premium collection and inflation increasing repair costs; industry combined ratio ~128% vs Bajaj General 97.9%.
items.quote: If you look at IDV, due to the GST change, IDV dropped. And motor OD is calculated as a percentage to IDV. Due to this drop, it eventually leads to lower premium collection for the same vehicle, compared to what would have been earlier. Also, with inflation, the cost of repairs goes up.

items.statement: Bajaj General targets combined ratio close to 100% while maintaining/growing market share; industry correction expected cyclically.
items.quote: And for the combined ratio, we always maintain that we would be close to 100% and that is our ambition. And that is what we have been doing for so many years while maintaining or growing our market share.

items.statement: Bajaj General fire/commercial lines pricing softened due to good loss ratios and no major NATCAT events; pricing cyclical with loss ratios.
items.quote: So, right now, to answer your question specifically, on the Fire portfolio, the price has softened. This is because, if you look at the results for the past few quarters , the commercial line of businesses had a better loss ratio.

items.statement: Bajaj Alts (alternatives platform) being set up as separate company; staffed and targeting AIF/PMS launch by end of FY27 subject to regulatory approvals.
items.quote: we have also now set up Bajaj Alts as a separate company. And that company now has been staffed. Subject to regulatory approvals, we will be looking, to start off a set of one or two alternative funds and possibly a PMS operation targeting that segment of the market, where the minimum investment required for an AIF is INR 1 crore and above.

items.statement: Bajaj Finserv AMC to continue building mutual fund suite; also pursuing SIF, PMS, GIFT City opportunities in coming financial year.
items.quote: we will be certainly continuing that path. But there are also additional opportunities that have come up, particularly with regard to SIF, PMS, as well as GIFT City. So, these are on our plan for this coming financial year. And you will see us active on these fronts as well.

items.statement: Full-year FY26 R&D spend guided at INR 600-650 crores
items.quote: R&D expenses increased by 33% year-over-year to INR 165 crores for the quarter, and this is in line with the full year guidance of INR 600 crores to INR 650 crores that we had provided earlier.

items.statement: India Branded business expected to match market growth rate in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Q1 of the coming financial year is where we feel we should be back in line with the market growth rate.

items.statement: U.S. business expected to grow 10-12% for full year FY26
items.quote: But I expect the U.S. business to grow between 10% to 12% for the full -- on full year basis. And we are well on track for that.

items.statement: U.S. business could grow at mid-teens (10-15%) in FY27 and FY28
items.quote: Yes, it could. Ideally, I would like to go into the mid-teens like between 10% to 15%, at least I would expect the U.S. business to continue growing every year.

items.statement: R&D spend expected to remain in 8-9% of revenue range for FY27
items.quote: But by and large, we will be along the same numbers between that 8%, 9% kind of range generally.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 revenue grew 11% YoY to INR 1,876 crores driven by volume expansion, new launches and ex-U.S. traction
items.quote: Revenue for the quarter grew by 11% year-over-year to INR 1,876 crores. The quarter saw broad-based growth driven by volume expansion, new product launches and increased traction in ex-U.S. markets, offset in part by pricing pressure in U.S. generics and API.

items.statement: ROW markets grew 36% in Q3 FY26 reflecting geographic expansion
items.quote: The performance was driven by a 36% growth in ROW markets, reflecting our strategic geographic expansion and focused execution.

items.statement: U.S. business grew 6% in Q3 FY26 supported by higher volumes and new launches despite pricing challenges
items.quote: The U.S. business grew 6%, supported by higher volumes and new launches in the last few quarters despite continuing pricing challenges.

items.statement: India Branded business delivered 6% YoY growth to INR 652 crores in Q3 FY26
items.quote: The India Branded delivered a 6% year-on-year growth, reaching a revenue of INR652 crores for the quarter.

items.statement: Gross margin at 72% in Q3 FY26 vs 74% YoY due to product mix and pricing pressure, within 70-75% operating range
items.quote: Gross margin was at 72% for the quarter compared to 74% in the previous year. The moderation was primarily driven by change in product mix and pricing challenges, partially offset by cost improvement programs that we have in our International Business.

items.statement: EBITDA before R&D and exceptional items at 25% of revenue in Q3 FY26 vs 23% YoY, up 20% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA before R&D expenses and exceptional items stood at INR464 crores for the quarter, representing 25% of revenue compared to 23% in the previous year, again, reflecting an improved operating leverage and prudent management of discretionary spending during the quarter, and hence the year-on-year EBITDA growth was at about 20%.

items.statement: 9M FY26 EBITDA before R&D at 25% of revenue, up 25% YoY due to strong revenue growth and better capacity utilization
items.quote: EBITDA before R&D spend and exceptional items for the previous -- for the period was about INR 1,391 crores, which is 25% of the revenue and resulting in a 25% year-over-year growth. This reflects strong revenue growth and better utilization of facilities -- capacity utilization across facilities.

items.statement: Pricing pressure persists in U.S. generics and API business, mitigated by cost efficiency programs
items.quote: Pricing pressure in international generics, particularly in the U.S. and API business has persisted during the quarter. These headwinds were mitigated by sustained cost efficiency programs, helping us remain competitive in the market.

items.statement: Out-licensing and manufacturing agreements executed to scale utilization in injectable and onco facilities over next 12-18 months
items.quote: We have executed a few out-licensing and manufacturing agreements as well that support our injectable and onco capabilities. These strategic contracts, along with the in-house products, will help us scale utilization in these new facilities over the next 12 to 18 months.

items.statement: Gynaecology, Ophthalmology and animal healthcare segments showing accelerating performance in India Branded business
items.quote: Gynaecology, Ophthalmology, animal healthcare segments have demonstrated accelerating performance.

items.statement: Focus on complex differentiated areas: injectables, peptides, oral solids, drug discovery with emphasis on First-to-File, Day-1 and NCE-1 launches
items.quote: The focus remains on complex and differentiated areas such as injectable, peptides, oral solids and drug discovery with an emphasis on early-entry opportunities, including First to File, Day-1 and NCE-1 launches.

items.statement: Plan to launch 4-5 products in U.S. in Q4 FY26
items.quote: We hope to launch another 4 to 5 products in the fourth quarter of the year.

items.statement: First U.S. branded product Pivya (oral antibiotic for UTI) on track for launch in February 2026
items.quote: We're also on track to launch our first branded product in the U.S. in February 2026. Sometime in Q4, we'll do it. Pivya is a first-line oral antibiotic targeting uncomplicated urinary tract infections in women with a track record of low treatment and emergent adverse events.

items.statement: Net working capital at INR 2,944 crores, broadly near September levels
items.quote: Net working capital stood at INR 2,944 crores, broadly near the September levels.

items.statement: Net debt marginally declined to INR 1,213 crores vs previous quarter
items.quote: Net debt marginally declined to about INR 1,213 crores compared to the previous quarter.

items.statement: One-time provision of INR 42 crores recognized for employee benefits under New Labour Code, no cash flow impact
items.quote: Pursuant to the changes under the New Labour Code, the company has recognized a onetime provision of INR42 crores towards employee benefits. However, this does not impact operating performance or any immediate cash flow.

items.statement: Pivya launch will impact near-term profitability; margin drag uncertain until product scales over 12-18 months
items.quote: While the launch will have an impact on near-term profitability, we expect the product prescription share to scale up during the course of the next 12 to 18 months.

items.statement: U.S. growth opportunities becoming less due to increased competition and competitive intensity
items.quote: What's happening is due to increased competition and competitive intensity, we are finding that the opportunities are becoming little less.

items.statement: Other income of INR 15.5 crores in Q3 FY26, mostly forex gain
items.quote: Yes. And forex gain should not be big. So yes, so the other income is about INR15.5 crores, and most of that will be forex gain.

items.statement: Chennai park launched with total investment of roughly Rs 600-611 crore in about 21 months
items.quote: we have been able to execute this project in about 21 months and with a total investment of roughly 600 crores, 611 crores.

items.statement: Chennai park opened December 2, 2025; reported positive EBITDA of Rs 1.3 crore in Q3
items.quote: Chennai Park also reported a positive EBITDA contribution of Rs. 1.3 crores, underscoring the strength of our execution.

items.statement: Q3 revenue grew 12% YoY to Rs 141.5 crore, highest-ever Q3 revenue
items.quote: During the quarter, the income grew by 12% year -on-year to Rs. 141.5 crores, delivering our highest-ever Q3 revenue.

items.statement: ARPU increased over 8% for the year to Rs 1,377
items.quote: ARPU has increased by over 8% for the year to Rs. 1,377.

items.statement: Resort revenues grew 71% YoY with occupancy reaching 68%
items.quote: Our Resort Property also did very well, with our Resort revenues growing by 71% year-on-year and an occupancy reaching 68%.

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA before exceptional items Rs 40 crore, up 8% YoY; reported EBITDA Rs 32.17 crore, down 13% YoY with 23% margin
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at Rs. 32.17 crore, down by 13% year -on-year, with EBITDA margins at 23%.

items.statement: 9M EBITDA Rs 116.3 crore, down 9% YoY with 28% margin
items.quote: EBITDA for the period stood at Rs. 116.3 crore, down by 9% on a year-on-year basis, with EBITDA margins at 28%.

items.statement: PAT declined 29% YoY in Q3 and 34% in 9M due to new labour code impact and higher depreciation from new projects
items.quote: The decline impact was primarily driven by adoption of new labour co de related regulatory changes and increased depreciation of new locations and projects during the quarter.

items.statement: One-time Rs 8 crore impact from adoption of new wage code recognised as exceptional item
items.quote: During the quarter, company adopted the provisions of the new wage code. The resultant one-time financial impact of Rs. 8 crore has been recognised and disclosed under exceptional item in line with the accounting standards.

items.statement: Chennai park has 600-700 employees; monthly labour cost Rs 2.5-3 crore; total monthly expenses expected to stabilize at Rs 3-5 crore
items.quote: In the Chennai Park, we have about 600 to 700 employees, both on-roll and off-roll, which will get optimized over a period of time. At present, we are incurring a cost of about 2.5 to 3 crores per month which can again optimize over a period, as I said.

items.statement: Chennai park targets Bangalore-level EBITDA margins of 40-45% over 3-4 years; peak revenue potential similar to Bangalore
items.quote: I think within 3 to 4 years, we slowly plan to pace this park to be in line with the Bangalore numbers. Because this is the first year, we would also want to wait and see how the overall response is. But our long -term goal is that by the fourth year, it should be able to reach the potential of one of our larger parks like Bangalore.

items.statement: Footfall flat YoY at 9.17 lakh in Q3; 9M footfall down 1% to 23.4 lakh; management expects 2-3% footfall growth possible in Q2-Q3
items.quote: Footfall for the quarter stood at Rs. 9.17 lakh, remaining largely in line with the previous period. For 9 months ended December 2025, total footfall reached Rs. 23.4 lakh compared to Rs. 23.7 lakh in the previous period, reflecting a marginal 1% decline.

items.statement: January demand strong for Chennai park; good buzz and on track
items.quote: Demand is strong. It's a new park, and we have been able to create a lot of buzz. So, I think we are on a good track.

items.statement: No formal revenue/footfall/margin guidance given; significant revenue growth expected from Chennai park
items.quote: We don't give guidance like that. So, that's not how we look at it, especially because we have a new park that's coming in. So, you can expect significant revenue growth. The rest of it, we will have to wait and see.

items.statement: Plans to announce 1-2 more large parks in next 1-3 years; discussions ongoing with multiple state governments including Maharashtra for Mumbai
items.quote: We will definitely sign minimum one, maybe two or three at more locations. Like I said, I can't give you a timeline because this involves the government and government approvals and land acquisitions. So, these are not things that we can say. We are hoping to finish some of them early. For example, working with the Maharashtra government on doing something in Bombay, so these are all, it will take

items.statement: Payback period 4-6 years historically; Chennai park (Rs 600 crore) may take 7-8 years for full payback
items.quote: Historically, we were able to get a payback within some 4-5 years or 5-6, depending on the size of the park. Larger the park, suppose, for example, for Chennai, we are investing roughly about some 600 crore. It can take about some 7-8 years to completely get the entire investment back.

items.statement: Bangalore resort has 123 keys (84 resort + Isle); no mid-term plans to add more keys in Bangalore
items.quote: We have 123 keys, which is a mix of both the resort and the Isle. We have just launched the isle about seven months ago. So, I think we are well-capacitated, and we have already expanded this. We have also refurbished our existing resort, which has 84 keys.
