So that is how we plan to go about and just make sure that we are able to position ourselves through branding and technical services and other things at a good price band compared to our competitors.

items.statement: Target net debt/EBITDA <1.5x; QIP to fund expansion if threshold approached
items.quote: So, ideally we'd want to keep our debt to EBITDA ratio to be less than 1.5X EBITDA and so I think that is what we are targeting and then we will make sure that whenever we are reaching the threshold or before that we will do a QIP to fill in the gap.

items.statement: East region EBITDA/ton Rs 600-700, potential to reach Rs 800 with price improvement
items.quote: I think the EBITDA per ton that we earn in East is about Rs. 600 to 700 and I think with some price betterment I think it can reach to about Rs. 800.

items.statement: 50 MW solar project in Assam under review; may shift to Rajasthan due to regulatory changes
items.quote: The 50 MW that we are looking at Assam, we are still i n discussion. There is some regulatory change and we will consider, now we are thinking of Rajasthan and generation of power in Rajasthan is high so we may decide to put up in Rajasthan so we will have to probably get back to you in the next quarter investor call on that.

items.statement: Astec LifeSciences targets EBITDA breakeven for FY26 and revenue around INR5 billion
items.quote: We had said we are targeting ourselves to be EBITDA breakeven this year. I think that guidance stays for us. I think we're pretty confident that we should be able to pull that off.

items.statement: Astec LifeSciences targets 15% revenue growth for FY27
items.quote: And for next year, we're targeting revenue growth of about 15% and we are very pleased to see that our equity funnel has doubled from 22 to 45.

items.statement: Vegetable Oil business expects FFB tonnage CAGR of 12-15% over long term
items.quote: But on a regular basis, I think the business is slated for FFB tonnage growth of I think a good healthy teens in terms of anywhere between 12% to 15%.

items.statement: Crop Protection domestic business targets 28-30% margin range in midterm
items.quote: But I think in the long -- in the midterm, we are pretty confident of holding on to the range of 28%, 30%.

items.statement: New CPO processing plant in Khammam to go live in 2 months; downstream refinery to be commissioned in Q1 next year
items.quote: One is, before I go downstream, our new CPO processing plant on the upstream in Khammam will go live in a matter of 2 months and our downstream refinery will also go get commissioned by somewhere in the first quarter of the coming year.

items.statement: Pet food plant ready for commissioning in about a month
items.quote: The pet food business is that we have put up the plant for the pet food business of the group and that plant is ready to get commissioned in a matter of a month or so from now.

items.statement: Expanded oil palm acreage by 15,000 hectares in 9M FY26, targeting 17,000-18,000 hectares for full year
items.quote: Today, we have done 15,000 hectare expansion in the 9-month period and we are slated to be roughly around 17,000 to 18,000 hectare by the end of the year.

items.statement: Animal Feed underlying EBIT per metric ton improved to INR2,020 in Q3 FY26 from INR1,937 in Q3 FY25
items.quote: The underlying segment results grew 17 % year-on-year and underlying EBIT per metric ton improved to INR2,020 per metric ton in quarter 3 fiscal year '26 from INR1,937 per metric ton in quarter 3 fiscal year '25.

items.statement: Vegetable Oil segment revenue grew 27% YoY and segment results grew 25% YoY in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Our Vegetable Oil business continued to deliver stellar performance with segment revenue growing 27% year-on-year and 25% growth in segment results driven by improved Fresh Fruit Bunch arrivals and a better oil extraction ratio.

items.statement: Astec LifeSciences EBITDA turned positive at INR5 crores in Q3 FY26 vs loss in Q3 FY25
items.quote: The EBITDA for the quarter turned positive at INR5 crores, a sharp improvement compared to a loss in the same period last year, supported by higher volumes and improved gross margins in the enterprise category.

items.statement: Creamline Dairy EBITDA declined to INR11 crores with margins at 3% due to higher milk procurement cost
items.quote: Profitability, however, remained under pressure with EBITDA declining to INR11 crores and margins softening to 3%, primarily due to higher milk procurement cost and a shortfall in revenue growth.

items.statement: Godrej Foods EBITDA grew 51% YoY to INR17 crores with margins expanding to 8% in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Profitability strengthened significantly with EBITDA growing 51% year-on-year to INR17 crores and margins expanding to 8% supported by improved contribution margins in the branded portfolio and better live bird prices.

items.statement: CPO prices lower YoY in Q3 FY26 while PKO prices higher, offsetting price impact on Vegetable Oil revenue
items.quote: Actually if I were to see in Q3 over Q3 last year , year-on-year, actually pricing overall in fact is a negative one, right? Because while the palm kernel oil prices were higher than last year, the CPO prices were lower than last year.

items.statement: PKO prices holding steady despite 20-25% drop in copra and coconut oil prices from peak
items.quote: The answer is since we have been tracking this number, have we seen any drop happening in PKO prices? As of now, it's holding.

items.statement: Godrej Foods branded salience rose to 81% in Q3 FY26 from 77% in Q3 FY25; Yummiez ~28%, RGC ~52% of branded
items.quote: The business continued to advance its strategic shift towards value-added offerings with branded salience rising to 81% in quarter 3 from 77% last year.

items.statement: Crop Protection domestic business launched Ashitaka (maize herbicide) and Takai (multi-crop insecticide) in Q3 FY26; 2 in-house products planned for FY27
items.quote: We have launched Ashitaka, which is our first foray into maize herbicide. And I'm pretty happy to share that even though I think we could have connected the season a little bit earlier, the response in the market we have launched that has been very, very positive.

items.statement: Animal Feed cattle feed salience at ~54% of volumes in Q3 FY26; launched state-specific products Doodh Vriddhi, Dhanalaxmi, Bypro Plus
items.quote: And the salience of the cattle feed business for us is now in this quarter is around 54% and 9 months is almost similar. It's around 54%-odd on volume.

items.statement: Creamline Dairy direct farm procurement increased to 85-90% of total procurement
items.quote: I think there are some structural changes which the team had done in the last couple of years that we have moved to almost 85% of our procurement being direct farm procurement.

items.statement: Astec facing price pressure from Chinese overcapacity but stabilizing; monitoring potential export tax benefit changes in China
items.quote: Price pressure is there because the competition is there because of the overcapacity in China. But that is also a little bit coming down. It is not -- it is more or less flattened out.

items.statement: Astec secured own registrations for triazole products in Europe (3) and Brazil (2), with 3 more in pipeline for next 1.5 years
items.quote: Secondly, strategically we have shifted our registration from being source registered, now we have got our own registrations. So most of the geographies like Europe and Latin America, we have started getting registrations.

items.statement: Astec CDMO inquiries doubled from March 2025 driven by China Plus One from Western world and Japan
items.quote: One is what is our involvement in R&D because if you see from March onwards, we have almost doubled the number of inquiries we are getting. So one hand is the future looks to be a little bit -- again China Plus One is slowly coming into being.

items.statement: Astec agrochemical pipeline inventories largely cleared, demand back to 2019-20 normal consumption levels
items.quote: So what we are currently seeing is that the production of the demand of agrochemical has come back to 2019 -'20. So that is the normal consu mption norm. So most of the pipeline stock inventories have moved out of the major geographies

items.statement: Crop Protection Q4 FY26 to face base effect from Hitweed co-marketing sales in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Going forward in the quarter 3 -- quarter 4, I think this quarter, there is one last base effect which will come into play for us and I would like to call that out is that the Hitweed normally has a co-marketing sales in our base of quarter 4 last year.

items.statement: Milk procurement inflation driven by global butter exports expected to continue in Q4 FY26 then stabilize
items.quote: We are expecting this to maybe continue maybe for this quarter and then hopefully it should start stabilizing.

items.statement: Portfolio strategy review nearing completion; detailed communication planned for early April 2026
items.quote: We are going to make some very clear sharp choices in the businesses which we clearly see as the top end of our investments and top end of our growth choices. We'll make some choices about businesses. We may say that okay, we want to put them into maybe a little bit of a de-priority. And I guess somewhere towards early April, we should be able to come back to the Street with a proper communication

items.statement: Targets double-digit revenue growth FY26 vs FY25 and calls FY27 a year of disruptive growth
items.quote: we are poised to definitely achieve what we had given a guidance of a double-digit growth on an FY-to-FY basis as we really step on the gas in Q4FY26

items.statement: Red lines of 20% EBITDA margin and 15% PAT margin to be maintained on half-yearly or annual basis
items.quote: our red line is 20% EBITDA margins. And we will try and definitely maintain that on an half yearly or an annual basis

items.statement: Total order book at all-time high of INR 9,262 crore as of Q3 FY26; expects to touch INR 10,000 crore by Q1 FY27
items.quote: We are at an all-time high of INR 9,262 crore and definitely the way Q4 is going, we should be able to try and touch INR 10,000 crore by about Q1FY27

items.statement: Turnkey order book INR 4,500 crore, 65% about a year old; consultancy INR 2,750 crore; leasing and REMCL INR 300 crore
items.quote: consultancy is INR 2 ,750 crores, export is INR 1 ,700 crores, turnkey is INR 4 ,500 crores and 18 RITES Limited Q3 FY26 Earnings Conference Call 05.02.2026 balance leasing and REMCL is about INR 300

items.statement: Maintained strike rate of 1.5 orders per day in Q3 (143 orders); eighth consecutive quarter with at least one order per calendar day
items.quote: quarter three, we have got 143 orders, which is a strike rate of 1.5. So, now successively for about seven, now eighth quarter, we have been able to maintain a strike rate of one order a calendar day

items.statement: Turnkey margin low at 1.3% but blended mix managed to keep consolidated EBITDA above 20% red line
items.quote: turnkey margin is significantly lower at 1.3% . So, as turnkey now constitutes 49% of the total order book, so what structural changes are being made to ensure that the overall consolidated PBT margin doesn't compress

items.statement: REMCL finalized third 1,000 MW RTC tender, total 2,500 MW; earns consultancy fees from each tender
items.quote: it has again finalized another 1,000 megawatt RTC tender, which is a third one. So now we have done 3 tenders totaling to 2,500 MW

items.statement: Mozambique 10 loco order: 4 shipped in H1, targeting 4 more in Q4, last 2 by Q1 FY27; 30 in-service loco conversions: first 2 prototypes by early Q1 FY27
items.quote: four have gone, at least four more definitely in Q4FY26. The last two -- because they go in lots of two. The shipment happens in the lots of two. So maybe we will try and pull it up to end of Q$FY26, but it may slide to Q1FY27

items.statement: Bangladesh 200 coach order: prototype approved, production started, first rake of 20 coaches targeted early FY27, full delivery by FY29 contractual outer limit
items.quote: the first rake of 20 coaches, we are definitely targeting to ship out in next FY. So, the execution of the Bangladesh order should definitely start from this coming FY27

items.statement: Annual revenue mix target: consultancy + export ~70%, leasing ~5%, turnkey balance; Q3 mix favored consultancy/export
items.quote: consultancy and export combined would definitely be in the range of about 70% odd, which has been our broad business strategy. And on an annual basis -- if you look at quarter basis, sometimes they tend to get deviated from that

items.statement: Fresh order inflow 70%+ competitive across domestic and international; nomination orders limited to long-standing PSU/government agreements
items.quote: the fresh order inflow in competitive business is literally more than two-third or roughly 70% plus. That breakup of 61 is basically the existing order book breakup

items.statement: Consultancy faces highest competition across 13 verticals; strike rate maintained at 1.5 orders/day; not exiting any vertical but bidding disciplined to protect 20% EBITDA red line
items.quote: we are constantly trying to get more and more orders at a strike rate as I said of one plus order a day, and the consultancy order book is growing

items.statement: Export working capital minimal and staggered; mostly covered by advances
items.quote: There is hardly any working capital requirement. Most of it, we covered by advance. Also, our orders are structured like that. And it is very, very minimal

items.statement: Dividend payout policy of 95% maintained in Q3 and will continue going forward
items.quote: We maintained that in Q3 , and as I have been reiterating in every quarter, our business strategy is very clear and transparent, and we don't like to bring any surprises. So, our broad policy of giving a high dividend payout would definitely be maintained

items.statement: REMCL operating at 50%+ PAT margins, growing sequentially and YoY; expanding into renewable energy consultancy and international
items.quote: It's been doing very well, sequentially growing, YoY growing, operating at about 50% plus PAT margins

items.statement: Bangladesh order execution risk low: EIB-funded, advance received, prototypes approved, Bangladesh Railways in urgent need
items.quote: We have already received the advance, the six types of coaches which are there. Four types of coaches, the prototypes have already got approved and the production of the prototypes have started

items.statement: Quality Assurance (QA) business recovering to FY23-24 revenue levels after restructuring; expects double-digit growth next year
items.quote: we will definitely, after an entire, reinventing the whole business, taking on new clients, varied clients, including some international order, we will come back to that level after the first time in terms of the revenue where we started in FY23-24

items.statement: FY26 organic revenue growth guidance 12-13% with expanded margins
items.quote: we remain confident of delivering on our guidance of 12% to 13% organic growth rate and expanded margins for FY '26

items.statement: Core Diagnostics expected high single-digit EBITDA margin in Q4 FY26
items.quote: The margin for Core Diagnostics is expected to meet the stated guidelines of high single-digit as an exit run rate for quarter 4 FY '26

items.statement: Organic EBITDA margin expansion target 70-100 bps for FY26
items.quote: at the beginning of the year, we have made an estimate of 70 to 100 bps improvement in the margins, and we stay put with that

items.statement: Patient volume growth aspiration 7-8% in near future
items.quote: 7% to 8% volume growth has always been our aspirations in the near future, and we are working towards it

items.statement: FY26 capex estimated at INR 55-60 crores
items.quote: Estimated capex for the year is INR 55 crores to INR 60 crores

items.statement: 9-month capex at INR 40 crores group level
items.quote: The 9-month period is about close to INR 40 crores at a group level

items.statement: Added 110 new centers in Q3, total 300+ in 9 months, now in 750 towns
items.quote: During this quarter, we added 110 new centers, most of it through the franchisee, taking total addition to more than 300 centers in 9 months and strengthened our presence in 750 towns now

items.statement: Plan to consolidate duplicate labs, 2-3 more closures expected in Q4
items.quote: there are a couple of more labs that we may shut down in the quarter 4 as well

items.statement: Q3 organic revenue growth 15% YoY, patient volume up 9%, test volume up 8%
items.quote: Organic revenue growth remained healthy at 15% for the quarter and 13% for the 9 months, supported by balanced volume expansion, improving test mix and disciplined execution across businesses

items.statement: B2C and B2B both grew 15% YoY organically
items.quote: Our B2C and B2B revenue both grew by 15% on a year-on-year basis

items.statement: TruHealth grew 25% YoY, Specialty grew 16% YoY organically
items.quote: TruHealth and Specialty grew by 25% and 16%, respectively, on a year-on-year basis

items.statement: Group EBITDA margin 23.4%, lower due to Core Diagnostics
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 23.4%. The decrease compared to the organic business was largely attributable to lower margin profile of Core Diagnostics

items.statement: Core Diagnostics Q3 EBITDA lower due to genomics launch delay, expects improvement in Q4
items.quote: The Q3 margins for Core were expected to be slightly higher than Q2 because the plan was to launch the genomics platform in Q3 '25, which would have meant higher gross margins for these genomics tests. However, due to delay of machine arrival into India, these got launched 3 months later in January '26

items.statement: GST rate reduction on reagents from 12% to 5% gives marginal benefit, price revision deferred
items.quote: the GST on materials into the diagnostic was at around 12% and it's moved up to 5%. And some of the reagents were already at 5% and some of them are at 12%, 18% has come down to now 5%

items.statement: Market conducive for price increase but deferred to pass GST benefits to customers
items.quote: We see the market is definitely may be able to absorb some price increase and the environment is conducive. But we are delaying it, deferring it for the reasons I've already mentioned

items.statement: Genomics launch in Delhi via Core Diagnostics integration, national reference hub for advanced molecular testing
items.quote: A key milestone during the quarter was the launch of our Centre of Genomics established in Delhi foll owing the integration of Core Diagnostics, which now functions as our national reference hub for advanced molecular testing and precision diagnostics

items.statement: AI applied in targeted areas: test interpretation, quality monitoring, scientific selling, customer conversion
items.quote: Currently, AI is being applied in a few targeted areas at Metropolis, including enhanced test interpretation, strengthening quality monitoring, supporting scientific selling and enhancing customer conversion

items.statement: First patent granted for TB infection monitoring system
items.quote: we achieved an important milestone this quarter with the grant of our first patent by the Patent Office of the Government of India for a system focused on monitoring and managing TB-related infections

items.statement: Structured cleanup of low-quality institutional accounts, built better quality partnerships
items.quote: Over the last year, I have spoken about our efforts towards the structured cleanup of low er- quality institutional accounts, exiting businesses that were margin dilutive, operationally inefficient or misaligned with our service and quality standards

items.statement: Genomics has 7-15 players vs 3 lakh in routine; Metropolis focuses on diagnostic-grade quality
items.quote: there are at least 7, 8 players in the space, but it's only 7, 8 compared to all the other tests where you have 3 lakh players

items.statement: Reliance genomics acquisition appears data/screening strategy, not diagnostic; different positioning
items.quote: there was already a business, a genomics business, which was in distress, which they th en acquired from, I think, NCLT. And I don't know what their goal with it is because obviously, they are not in the larger space of pathology

items.statement: Union Budget prioritizes healthcare, 100k allied health professionals over 5 years, Tier 2/3 infrastructure
items.quote: A strong focus on workforce development, including upgrading existing allied health institutions and setting up new ones across public and private sectors aims to add nearly 100,000 professionals across 10 disciplines over 5 years

items.statement: Company remains net debt-free with INR 127 crores cash reserves
items.quote: the company remains net debt-free with a current cash reserves of INR 127 crores

items.statement: Board approved 3:1 bonus shares (3 shares of INR 2 face value for every 1 held)
items.quote: the Board of Directors has approved the issue of bonus shares in the ratio of 3:1, that is 3 fully paid-up equity shares of face value of INR 2 each for every 1 existing equity share

items.statement: Quality framework launched: Internal Quality Control Index across lab network
items.quote: At the beginning of this year, we launched the Internal Quality Control Index, a scientific performance framework designed to establish uniform, measurable and real-time quality benchmarks across the entire laboratory network

items.statement: North India revenue contribution rose from 9% to 17% post acquisitions
items.quote: revenue from North now contributes 17% of overall revenue, largely because of recent integration, which has its major presence and revenue coming from North region

items.statement: No material impact from global tariffs/trade policies; healthcare diagnostics is domestic
items.quote: healthcare and diagnostics is predominantly domestic in nature with localized sourcing and service delivery and remains largely neutral to these developments. And at this time, we do not see any material impact on our operations and cost structure

items.statement: Order book stands at INR 450 crore with no new orders in the last quarter; update expected next quarter
items.quote: We are currently quoting for a lot of business. There have been no new orders in the last quarter. We should update this by next quarter.

items.statement: Revenue target revised to INR 3,000-3,500 crore over next four to five years
items.quote: The estimation should be about INR 3,000 crore to INR 3,500 crore in the next four to five years.

items.statement: INR 80.49 crore capex approved for NDR Hayashi JV; timelines to be shared later this year
items.quote: That is the capex that we have approved for the JV. We are currently acquiring a lot of businesses for the JV. We will share the timelines slightly later, towards the end of the year.

items.statement: Q-on-Q margin compression due to seasonal shutdowns in Q3; Y-on-Y is better indicator; normal quarter margins slightly higher
items.quote: Q-on-Q is not the best indicator for our margins. Y -on-Y is the best indicator as Q3 tends to be a quarter which has many shutdowns. So, our expenses tend to be higher there.

items.statement: Gross margin decline of 100 bps Q-on-Q due to business mix, not commodities
items.quote: It is normal business model mix. It is nothing to do -- not with commodities.

items.statement: Volume fluctuations impact margins by only 0.5-1%
items.quote: There should not be a significant impact in our margins. It should not be more than 0.5% or 1% compared to the volume going up or down.

items.statement: Maruti EV production scale-up started in Q3 FY26, larger scale-up expected in Q4 FY26
items.quote: So Q3FY26 had some scale ups, Q4FY26 should have a larger scale up.

items.statement: Supplying seat frame and cover to Bharat Seats; shades and BIW parts directly to Maruti; also working with Toyota and Kia
items.quote: The seat cover and the seat frame goes through Bharat Seats. Apart from that, the shade and some of the BIW parts go directly.

items.statement: Actively expanding OEM base beyond Maruti to include Toyota, Kia and others
items.quote: We are continuously working on expanding customers. We have got Maruti, we have got Toyota, we have got Kia, and we are working on adding a few more.

items.statement: Cost competitiveness is main USP vs global peers like Lear; targeting cheaper products
items.quote: Our scale in the country should be similar, so our cost competitiveness should be more. So we will probably go after a cheaper product.

items.statement: Continuously evaluating JVs and acquisitions; will disclose when deals materialize
items.quote: We are continuously looking at JVs and acquisitions. When it converts then we will share that with you.

items.statement: Asset turnover for NDR Hayashi JV expected at 3-4x at peak capacity
items.quote: The asset turnover should be about 3 to 4.

items.statement: Market share gains achieved historically; expect to continue gaining share
items.quote: So we have gained market share in the past. We have acquired a lot of new business and we should continue gaining market share.

items.statement: Vande Bharat seat program remains minor; not a current focus area
items.quote: That remains a minor part of it, and we are currently not focusing too much on that.

items.statement: NDR Hayashi JV focuses on ambient lighting assembly and mounting with some electronic capability; not LED manufacturing
items.quote: It will not focus on LED lights; it will focus on the assembly of the ambient lighting and the mounting in the car. Anubhav: Will that also involve some electronic capability

items.statement: Bidding for sheet metal and BIW parts for Maruti and Toyota; updates to follow
items.quote: We are currently bid ding for sheet metal and BIW parts for Maruti and Toyota. When there is an update, we will share it with you.

items.statement: Tire and wheel assembly business for Bharat Seats won last year; additional business expected next year
items.quote: That has come last year. We have got a little bit more business for tire and wheel. That should come sometime next year.

items.statement: Revenue growth expected to exceed volume growth due to premiumization and market share gains
items.quote: Yes, definitely. In addition to that we are also expanding our market share.

items.statement: No annual guidance for FY27; focused on long-term 5-year vision
items.quote: We are not sharing any annual guidance at the moment. We are happy to talk about our long -term 5-year vision.

items.statement: Order book pipeline for FY27/FY28 not disclosed; reiterating 5-year target instead
items.quote: We do not share that at the moment. I think our 5-year target is what we are reiterating towards.

items.statement: Management expects volume and value growth every quarter going forward, with EBITDA margins improving gradually and better numbers from H2 FY27
items.quote: The way things are going with the changes in tariff structure in US and signing of trade agreements, we are fairly confident that the worst quarter is behind us and now every quarter we will see volume and value growth happening.

items.statement: Management targets export share to rise from 9% to as high as 50% of revenue
items.quote: Obviously, our target is to go much , I mean, from 9%, we want to go up as high as 50% on exports.

items.statement: Paint sector offtake was lower in Q3 FY26 due to market-share disruptions from new entrants
items.quote: The paint se ctor witnessed lower material off take during the quarter, which appears to be linked to market - share disruptions following the entry of new players

items.statement: US export viability was impacted by trade policy uncertainty; no sample approvals were taken up by US customers for six to eight months
items.quote: Since last six -eight months nothing was happening on that front. In fact, to the extent that no sample approval work was also not being taken up by the US customers.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin was 4.2%; nine-month EBITDA margin was 3.97%
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was Rs. 4 crores with EBITDA margin of 4.2%.

items.statement: Dimer acid margins remain under pressure from aggressive Chinese pricing and unchanged 7.5% import duty
items.quote: margins on our dimer acid segment continued to remain under pressure, impacted by aggressive pricing from Chinese suppliers and the unchanged 7.5% import duty, which constraine d our pricing

items.statement: If China removes export incentives on dimer acid, domestic prices could rise 12-13%, flowing largely to EBITDA
items.quote: If dimer falls under that, then automatically we will see a 12 % or 13% price hike coming from the Chinese players. So, that would help us a lot b ecause automatically then our sales price would go up by that percentage

items.statement: Raw material prices elevated due to 16.5% customs duty on vegetable oil imports versus 7.5% duty on finished dimer acid imports
items.quote: Raw material prices remained elevated due to higher custom duty levels, currently at around 16.5% for our raw materials, and margins on our dimer acid segment continued to remain under pressure, impacted by aggressive pricing from Chinese suppliers and the unchanged 7.5% import duty.

items.statement: Vegetable oil prices have risen ~25% in the last two months
items.quote: In last two months, they have gone as high as 25%.

items.statement: Domestic sales contributed 91% of revenue in nine months FY26
items.quote: The domestic sale contributed 91% of the total revenue.

items.statement: Tocopherol business (100% exported to US) has been zero for two quarters; revival needed after tariff changes
items.quote: I mean, tocopherol business, basically 100% of our material is getting exported to US, so it is, since two quarters our business has been zero.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 volume throughput was 9,850 tonnes; management says capacity can double from current levels
items.quote: Yes, it was 9,850 tonnes.

items.statement: Current capacity utilisation is around 55%; no further capex needed to achieve export target of 50% of turnover
items.quote: Since our capacity utilization is close to around 55%, w e don’t expect any further CAPEX to happen

items.statement: Animal feed plant is ready, awaiting GMP certification; new product equipment expected in production by Q3 FY27
items.quote: Animal feed plant is ready. Yes, the plant is ready and for which we have already applied for the GMP certifications. Once the GMP certificate comes, we will start the plant.

items.statement: Initial capacity for new product will be small; major expansion after buyer approvals (2-3 years)
items.quote: Initially, we are doing a very small capacity. Once we are absolutely satisfied with the quality and once we receive the approvals from our buyers, we will go in for major capacity expansion.

items.statement: Work ongoing on alternative raw materials to mitigate import duty differential; material impact expected in Q2 or Q3 FY27
items.quote: Maybe second or third quarter.

items.statement: Company sources byproducts from 80-100 refineries covering 80-90% of India's vegetable oil processing; no raw material shortage
items.quote: See, these 80 to 100 refineries constitute more than 80 % to 90% of India's vegetable oil processing. So, I mean, the other guys would be marginal players and these 80 to 100 refineries can give us 100% of our raw material requirement.

items.statement: Chinese dimer acid suppliers benefit from export incentives; dumping limits pricing power
items.quote: China is giving export incentives to dimer manufacturers there, and so they are in turn doing dumping.

items.statement: New entrant in paint segment is marginal; no market share lost, but volumes restricted due to low margins
items.quote: They are very marginal players.

items.statement: US level-playing-field tariff structure and progress on UK/EU FTA improve export visibility for isosteric business
items.quote: The recent announcement of the level playing field tariff structure in the US, along with progress towards the proposed free trade agreement with the UK and EU, provides improved visibility for our export recovery.

items.statement: China may remove export incentives on 700 chemical products from 1 April; if dimer acid included, Chinese prices could rise 12-13%
items.quote: See, to be frank, like you, we have also heard that from 1st of April on 700 chemical products, China is going to remove export

items.statement: Isosteric acid major markets are Europe and US; India market very small; FTA with EU/US not a threat
items.quote: In fact, we are selling our isosteric acid to EU. So, it does no t make any difference to us. Yes. And for isosteric acid, India does not, it i s a very, very small market. Major market is Europe and the US

items.statement: No cash flow pressure; buyback done to increase promoter holding as capacity utilisation is only 55% and no major capex needed
items.quote: No, there is no pressure in cash flow. In fact, the complete volume increase, which is going to happen in the next two years, is going to come from the current capacity only.

items.statement: Buyback executed to increase promoter holding; no cash flow pressure
items.quote: This was one way to increase the promoters holding.

items.statement: Revenue declined from ~Rs 650 crore (FY22) to ~Rs 450 crore (past 12 months) due to both lower volumes and realisations
items.quote: Both, combined effect.

items.statement: Prices down 10-15% from FY22 peak levels
items.quote: 10% to 15%, you can say 10%, 15%.

items.statement: Rajasthan project expected to contribute ~INR200 cr annualized revenue in FY27
items.quote: Rajasthan revenue should be able to contribute approximately around INR200 crores of annualized revenue.

items.statement: RPL retail business targeting breakeven in Q4 FY26
items.quote: considering our breakeven, yes, we are in line with the quarter 4, where we'll be looking for breakeven for the RPL business.

items.statement: Base business (ex-Rajasthan, ex-B2C) targeting higher teens revenue growth on annualized basis
items.quote: we try to achieve revenues in the higher teens is what we are aspirational, and that's what we are currently focusing.

items.statement: Full annualized revenue potential of Rajasthan project expected by end of FY27
items.quote: most probably by -- end of FY '27, we should be able to achieve the full annualized revenue that we are targeting from Rajasthan.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin 26% (INR474M), normalized EBITDA margin 27% (INR484M) after absorbing Rajasthan project costs
items.quote: Our EBITDA for quarter 3 has registered at INR474 million, translating into the EBITDA margin percentage of 26%, post absorbing temporary costs related to the project readiness and employee-related adjustment of Rajasthan project.

items.statement: Maharashtra radiology project under implementation; 10 MRI sites nearing readiness, revenue expected from Q4 FY26 or FY27
items.quote: the Maharashtra project, it's under implementation. We've now received a lot of clearances on various sites. So hopefully, by Q4, these sites will be under implementation and the revenue shoul d also start coming through in the subsequent quarters or in the next financial

items.statement: Rajasthan pathology rollout: ~20 labs installed, ~300 collection centers, majority completion targeted by Q4 FY26 with spillover to Q1 FY27
items.quote: we have around 20 labs currently, which have almost been installed and about 300 collection centers and the rest are in progress. So hopefully, by Q4, majority of them should be done. And by Q1, there might be some spillover for the collection centers and some satellite labs.

items.statement: Selective bidding on new PPP tenders; chasing a couple of projects with results expected in coming quarters
items.quote: there are a couple of projects that we are chasing. Two things. One is we have also been selective about the PPP project that we want to undertake given the kind of maturity and experience Krsnaa has.

items.statement: Apulki Healthcare Hospital (150-bed cancer/cardiac PPP) launched in Pune; mature revenue potential ~INR20-25 cr in 2-3 years
items.quote: considering it's a 150-bedded hospital, so we expect the revenues -- mature level revenues to be in the range of around INR20-odd crores, which we believe it will take around between 2 to 3 years to come to a mature level.

items.statement: Additional Apulki hospitals under construction, will add to long-term revenue growth
items.quote: The other hospitals are also under construction. So they will also further add to our growing kitty of revenues.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 revenue INR1,812M (+4% YoY); seasonally softer quarter accentuated by operational pauses for receivable recovery
items.quote: During quarter 3 FY '26, the revenue from the operations stood at INR1,812 million, representing a year-on-year growth of approximately 4%.

items.statement: Retail (B2C) revenue grew ~8x YoY in Q3 FY26; contributed ~8% of 9M FY26 group revenue; network expanded to 3,000+ touch points
items.quote: During quarter 3 FY '26, retail revenue grew by nearly 8x year-on-year and contributed approximately 8% to the overall group's revenue contribution in 9MFY26.

items.statement: Retail expansion planned across Maharashtra, Punjab, Assam, Odisha with growing home collection and preventive health traction
items.quote: we expect this segment to scale steadily supported by expansion across Maharashtra, Punjab, Assam and Odisha, along with the growing traction in home collection services and preventive healthcare offerings.

items.statement: Collected INR130+ cr in Q3 FY26, INR100 cr more than Q3 FY25; Himachal received INR40 cr, Karnataka confirmations received
items.quote: during the quarter, we recovered over INR130 crores, materially strengthening our cash position. Importantly, our focused efforts on strengthening cash flows are clearly bearing fruit. During Q3, we collected over INR100 crores more compared to Q3 of the last year

items.statement: Receivable recovery expected to improve in Q4 due to government budgetary cycles; temporary operational pauses taken in Q3 to accelerate collections
items.quote: Hopefully, in the coming quarters, we don't expect to have such impact because Q4 is considered to be a good quarter in terms of co llecting our receivables because there are budgetary limits that the governments have to exercise

items.statement: Interest expense expected to decline with working capital collections; finance lease component not significant
items.quote: For the current business, the way you see with the collections, we expect the financing cost to go down.

items.statement: Rajasthan project debt via ADB facility in final stages; project-specific, not company-level debt increase
items.quote: we have availed a certain facility from ADB, which is in the final stages of completion. So I think once we get that debt raised, we'll certainly inform, but the debt is towards the project and not on the overall debt for the company.

items.statement: GST rationalization provided positive impact on consumable costs; benefit expected to continue
items.quote: In terms of the GST, yes, there has been some impact for us, positive side on the GST where we were able to also control our consumable cost, and we hopefully see that continuing in the coming quarters as well.

items.statement: CGHS rate revisions not impacting existing PPP contracts (contractually embedded); new tenders may reflect better rates
items.quote: Since we are in PPP and our rates are contractually embedded, we have not seen an impact there. But for the newer tenders, since they will be aligned to the new rates, we might see an uptick there or better rates there.

items.statement: Current radiology-pathology revenue split ~50-50; post Rajasthan & Maharashtra ramp-up, pathology share expected to rise to 65-70%
items.quote: we expect overall pathology to have a higher share in the revenue, which, in my opinion, could be in the range of around 65% of pathology, 70 pathology and the rest of radiology.

items.statement: Pathology has slightly lower gross margins than radiology; management deploying cost levers to minimize consolidated margin impact
items.quote: Ideally, pathology does have slightly lower margins compared to radiology. But as I said, again, we are trying certain cost levers to ensure that on a consolidated basis, we should be able to have a minimal impact on the margins

items.statement: Significant headroom: 6x district expansion potential, horizontal modality expansion, municipal corporation penetration
items.quote: currently, there are about 700 -- 730-plus districts in India and Krsnaa is present in only about 100 plus. So, there's almost a 6x more of capacity that we can expand.

items.statement: CFO Pawan Daga departed; structured transition completed with existing financial leadership team; successor search initiated
items.quote: Mr. Pawan Daga, our Chief Financial Officer, has moved on from the organization. We sincerely thank him for his valuable contribution and services and wish him continued success in his future

items.statement: Union Budget: Health Ministry allocation crossed INR1 lakh cr for first time; validates PPP model as key mechanism for healthcare scale-up
items.quote: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare allocation almost INR1 lakh crore, reflecting a stronger national commitment to healthcare infrastructure, preventive care and capacity building.

items.statement: Budget proposal for 5 healthcare hubs with state governments understood to be PPP-based; Krsnaa expects to benefit
items.quote: As of now, yes. As of now, we understand it will be through a PPP model.

items.statement: No major PPP contracts nearing expiry; demonstrated continuous growth despite tender cycles
items.quote: No, as of now, there are no major contracts which are nearing expiry to just confirm that to you.

items.statement: Technology obsolescence risk in radiology deemed negligible; CT/MRI core tech stable (magnet life ~40 yrs, CT 10-15 yrs); AI seen as efficiency enhancer
items.quote: the core technology doesn't change or has not been obsolete. What is changing over the years is bringing more software for concepts like 3D modeling or more clearer images.

items.statement: Served 4.6M patients in Q3 FY26; 81M+ patients served since inception across integrated network
items.quote: In Q3 alone, approximately 4.6 million patients accessed affordable diagnostics through our network.

items.statement: Plant 6 mechanical completion expected by end of FY26; commercialization targeted in H1 FY27
items.quote: Plant 6 is progressing towards mechanical completion by end of FY '26.

items.statement: Plant 6 capex INR50-60 crore, mostly incurred; INR10-15 crore remaining; maintenance capex INR15 crore annually
items.quote: On which the expected capex is about INR50 crores to INR60 crores. Most of it is already incurred in coming period, about INR10-odd crores should get added. So other than that, the maintenance capex of about INR15 crores continues.

items.statement: Post Plant 6, revenue capacity INR1,000 crore (ex-injectables) plus INR100 crore from injectables
items.quote: So this is -- with this, we would reach INR1,000 crores revenue capacity from all the plants, excluding injectables. And from injectables, we are talking about INR100 crores additional.

items.statement: India healthcare budget crossed INR1 lakh crore; chronic/sub-chronic segments expanding; IPM grew 11.8% YoY in Q3 FY26 with 1.6% volume growth
items.quote: India's health care budget has crossed INR1 lakh crores, signalling stronger support for health infrastructure and affordable treatments. Chronic and sub-chronic therapeutic segments are expanding rapidly due to lifestyle shifts, dietary changes and rising medicine consumption.

items.statement: 9M FY26 EBITDA INR79 crore (reported), INR89 crore (ex-ESOP) at 13.3% margin; PAT INR50 crore (reported), INR60 crore (ex-ESOP) at 9% margin
items.quote: Excluding the impact of ESOP expenses, EBITDA for 9-month FY '26 was INR89 crores, 13.3% of revenue and PAT INR60 crores, 9%.

items.statement: CDMO growth primarily volume-driven as cost-plus model with stable API prices; exports also cost-plus with quarterly orders limiting forex impact
items.quote: One thing that we can share, Gautam, is that most of our growth comes from volume, right? Because we are a cost-plus business and API prices are not increasing. So the growth is primarily volume oriented.

items.statement: CDMO mix includes both complex and volume products; no structural shift in outsourcing pattern observed; mix changes based on Windlas capabilities
items.quote: We think it has always been both low and high end. We don't think that there is a change in the pattern, but at least the top four, five CDMO players have always been getting a combination of very complex and difficult to crack drugs as well as a few just volume products.

items.statement: CDMO growth driven by expanding customer base, increasing wallet share, new product launches; organized BD teams for existing and new customers; 70-80 client audits annually
items.quote: Generic Formulations CDMO vertical grew 20% in 9 months FY '26 and 23% in Q3 FY '26, driven by expanding customer base, increasing wallet share and new product launches.

items.statement: Schedule M enforcement driving industry consolidation; fragmented CMO base of 13,000+ unsustainable; compliance requires capital, talent, know-how, systems
items.quote: In the overall scheme of things, if you see just from the perspective of how many CMOs are needed to really handle this market, it's certainly not 13,000-plus, right? There is no reason for the CMO industry to stay at this kind of a fragmented level.

items.statement: Schedule M fully enforced with no further extensions; government conducting inspections, issuing observations and closures; Windlas undergoes 70-80 audits annually
items.quote: And then the smaller enterprises were asking for increase in time to give them more time to comply, but even this -- I think this last quarter was probably, I think, maybe even October or some December time frame, no more extensions were granted. Now everybody is expected to comply.

items.statement: Exports grew 36% YoY in Q3 FY26; focused on RoW markets (SE Asia, CIS, Africa); zero sales to US/EU; cost-plus model limits forex impact
items.quote: Exports vertical grew 29% in 9 months FY '26 and 36% in Q3 FY '26 with increased penetration to RoW and semi-regulated markets.

items.statement: Cash conversion cycle stable around 14-15 days; no negative change or surprise by December
items.quote: Yes, not mentioning the exact number, but there's no negative change, no negative surprise by December.

items.statement: Debt-free currently; open to using debt for strategic acquisitions or capex; maintain financial discipline and cash-rich position
items.quote: In past, we have taken several debt for working capital and for capex and for -- whenever we see an opportunity, so like if I have to do an acquisition, it's a very good strategic fit, I won't be shy in using my cash and also taking a debt.

items.statement: ESOPs granted to 100 of 1,100 employees; no reduction in salary increments expected; focus on operational efficiencies to offset ESOP cost
items.quote: So basically, the ESOPs have been given to say 100 employees. And we have 1,100 employees. So we are not sure that we would let the ESOP, which is a long-term strategy for keeping the employees, not let them move out and motivate them for better results, that should affect the increment percent, which is a regular annual this thing.

items.statement: IPM grew 11.8% YoY in Q3 FY26 with 1.6% volume growth; Windlas outperformed with 20% revenue growth in Q3
items.quote: The Indian pharma market grew 11.8% Y-o-Y in Q3 FY '26 with volume growth of 1.6%.

items.statement: Export approvals binary and time-consuming; some efforts may not materialize; competitive intensity in Trade Generics increasing
items.quote: And in CDMO, we have been mentioning that we continue to work on the long-term growth strategy where we want to continue to increase our customers. We want to continue to increase the product portfolio. We want to look at the pipeline products and spend money there. And we want to increase our business development teams to be able to execute much better.

items.statement: Added 54 net new KFC outlets and 18 net new Pizza Hut outlets in India during Q3 FY26
items.quote: In India, new store openings accelerated during the quarter with 54 net new KFC outlets and 18 net additions to Pizza Hut.

items.statement: International business added 20 new stores in Thailand and Nepal during Q3 FY26
items.quote: The international business added 20 new stores during the quarter between Thailand and Nepal.

items.statement: Total store count reached 2,279 stores at end of Q3 FY26
items.quote: At the end of Q3' 2026, the total store count for DIL stood at 2,279 stores.

items.statement: Achieved break-even brand EBITDA for Biryani by Kilo ahead of earlier guided target
items.quote: We are happy to state th at we have achieved break -even brand EBITDA results for Biryani by Kilo much ahead of our target as guided earlier

items.statement: Proposed merger with Sapphire Foods to create platform with 3,000+ stores and ~USD 1 billion turnover
items.quote: Earlier this year, we announced the proposed merger with Sapphire Foods, a transformative step that will create one of the largest diversified F&B platforms in India. The combined entity will have more than 3,000 stores globally and a turnover approaching USD 1 billion.

items.statement: Estimated annual merger synergies of INR 210-225 crore
items.quote: The proposed merger will furthe r help us build a strong growth foundation in India and the estimated annual merger synergies of approximately INR 210 crore to INR 225 crore will allow us a greater headroom to invest in India and grow the business

items.statement: Merger applications submitted for exchange approvals, CCI filing shortly, no material deviation in timeline
items.quote: We have already submitted our applications for exchange approvals and will also be shortly filing the application for CCI approval. At this point, we do not anticipate any material deviation in the merger timeline that we have outlined earlier.

items.statement: CEO Virag Joshi to superannuate effective March 31, 2026, will continue as Non-Executive Director
items.quote: Virag has expressed his desire to superannuate from the Company. The board has accepted his request effective March 31, 2026, and has requested him to continue as a Non-Executive Director and provide his valuable insights on strategic matters as and when required.

items.statement: CFO Manish Dawar elevated to President and CEO effective April 1, 2026
items.quote: Manish Dawar shall get elevated as President and CEO for DIL with effect from April 1, 2026.

items.statement: EVP Finance Anupam Kumar to take over as CFO effective April 1, 2026
items.quote: I a m also pleased to inform you that Mr. Anupam Kumar, currently EVP Finance, will take over the role of CFO

items.statement: Early signs of consumption recovery in broader economy due to government support
items.quote: On the macro front, we are beginning to see some early signs of consumption coming back in a few sectors in the broader economy, thanks to the government support and fiscal measures.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin improved 20 bps YoY to 68.9% in Q3 FY26 (70 bps excluding Sky Gate)
items.quote: Consolidated Q3 FY26 gross profit came in at INR 993 crore, up 11.7% Y-on-Y with margins at 68.9%, reflecting an improvement of 20 basis points Y-on-Y (excluding Sky Gate, the improvement is 70 basis points Y-on-Y) and 110 basis points versus Q2 FY26.

items.statement: Consolidated brand contribution margin improved to 13.9% from 11.7% previous quarter
items.quote: The brand contribution margin improved to 13.9% versus 11.7% in the previous

items.statement: Consolidated pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin at 8.6% vs 6.8% previous quarter
items.quote: Consolidated operating EBITDA on a pre-Ind AS basis was INR 124 crore with margins at 8.6% versus 6.8% i n the previous quarter

items.statement: KFC India gross margin improved 1.2% YoY to 69.8% in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Gross margin at 69.8% showed 1.2% improvement compared to the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Pizza Hut India gross margin improved 1.2% QoQ to 76% in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Gross margin was at 76%, an improvement of 1.2% from the preceding quarter.

items.statement: International gross margin improved to 64.9% in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Revenues reached INR 473 crore in Q3 FY26, up 10.1% Y-on-Y with improved gross margins at 64.9%.

items.statement: Sky Gate brands achieved break-even brand EBITDA in December 2025 ahead of expectations
items.quote: I am happy to report that Sky Gate brands posted a breakeven brand EBITDA. This is ahead of our initial expectation and guidance given earlier.

items.statement: Vaango crossed 100 stores, maintains healthy gross margins and brand contribution
items.quote: Happy to report that Vaango has crossed a count of 100 stores in this quarter. The revenues for the quarter came in at INR 20 crore and the brand continues to maintain its healthy gross margins and the brand contribution.

items.statement: Pizza Hut store closures will utilize existing assets/equipment to reduce capex for new openings
items.quote: This will also help us to utilize the existing assets and equipment in our new stores and bring down the capex for the new openings as well.

items.statement: No net new Pizza Hut units planned for calendar year 2026, store count to remain broadly in line with December 2025
items.quote: We will start to shut down the loss-making stores in the Pizza Hut portfolio, and our plan is not to add any net new units in the brand for 2026. However, we will ensure that the overall store count remains broadly in line with December 2025 numbers.

items.statement: KFC India store addition plan of 110-120 stores per year remains unchanged
items.quote: If you remember, we have said in the past that as far as DIL is concerned, we plan to add about 110 to 120 stores every year for KFC. That stays.

items.statement: Corporate G&A guidance at 5% of revenue for FY27
items.quote: For let us say for 2026-27, you can take a 5% G&A.

items.statement: KFC India ADS stable sequentially at INR 90,000 in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Average daily sales for Q3 FY26 was stable sequentially at INR 90,000.

items.statement: Pizza Hut India ADS at INR 31,000 in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Pizza Hut India revenue for the quarter was INR 178 crore with ADS at INR 31,000.

items.statement: KFC brand contribution margins improved over 200 bps despite negative SSSG
items.quote: If you look at the SSSG, it was negative and despite all of that, if you look at the brand contribution, we have managed to improve the brand contribution by more than 200 basis points.

items.statement: Target to deliver KFC brand contribution margins at INR 105,000-110,000 ADS vs previous INR 125,000 ADS
items.quote: We are very confident that we will be able to deliver those kind of brand contribution margins at about INR 105,000 to INR 110,000 kind of ADS numbers.

items.statement: Pizza Hut turnaround will take couple of years, joint strategy with Sapphire post CCI approval
items.quote: It will take a couple of years to finally sort it out, but we have absolutely started this exercise. And now until we have the CCI approval, obviously between us and Sapphire we are not in a position to talk to each other at this stage. But once we have the CCI approval, we will sit jointly and draw out a merged company strategy plan for Pizza Hut.

items.statement: Technology and supply chain transition from Yum! to take about a year post-merger
items.quote: We will take over technology operations from Yum!, we will take over supply chain management from Yum!. Now all of these things will come back and help us. And therefore, once we overlay that with the operations piece, I think it is a great win-win combination for us.

items.statement: Management expects stronger revenue growth in FY27 and beyond driven by capacity expansion and new products
items.quote: With capacity expansion, steady demand for existing products and a gradual scale up in volumes for the new product categories, we are optimistic about delivering stronger revenue growth in FY '27 and beyond.

items.statement: Bioprocess containers capacity at Panchla commissioned; full facility revenue potential over INR 150 crores
items.quote: I believe that at full capacity, most of these bioprocess containers, what we've set up in our new facility, could generate revenues of in excess of INR 150 crores.

items.statement: Panchla facility breakeven expected at INR 70-75 crores revenue
items.quote: I think once the entire Panchla facility has been somewhere close to $8 million to $9 million overall as a facility, not only in bioprocess containers, so about INR 70 crores, INR 75 crores in revenue, we should be in cash positive, EBITDA positive numbers.

items.statement: Cell culture products sampling to take few weeks; vendor qualification in large companies to take 2-3 years to reach optimal capacity
items.quote: The sampling part is very, very quick, which should not take more than a few weeks all over India. But being able to enter into large companies, SOPs, and being able to become one of their preferred vendors or even one of the secondary vendors because they would have long-standing relationships with existing brands for many, many years, that would be the time-consuming process.

items.statement: Domestic demand picking up with increased order inflows; operating at near full capacity in existing plants
items.quote: In the domestic market, demand for our products has begun to pick up, reflected in increased order inflows for plastic labware products. We have been operating at near full capacity over the past few months in the existing plants, and are actively working to expedite the ramp-up of new capacities.

items.statement: Domestic competition moderately increasing with aggressive pricing from existing players post-COVID capacity expansion
items.quote: On competition, intensity in the domestic market is moderately increasing with several competitors adopting aggressive pricing strategies, which has kept pricing under pressure.

items.statement: India-US FTA could be significant benefit with tariff reduction from 50% to 18%; India-EU FTA reduces duties from 6% to 0%
items.quote: But the U.S., if executed perfectly, and if the executive order is signed, it could be a big benefit because 50% coming down to 18% gives us a new lease of life and would definitely help expand our business in America.

items.statement: New bioprocess and cell culture products expected to have similar material margins of 68-70% as existing portfolio
items.quote: Material margin-wise, it would be similar to what we currently work at. We work at about 68% to 70% gross margin across product lines, with the exception of a few which could be lower, and the exception of a few which could be higher.

items.statement: Working capital cycle at 125 days for 9-month FY26 with inventory breakdown provided
items.quote: Currently we have -- on sales, we have a working capital cycle of 125 days, right, of last 9 months. And it includes raw materials of INR 41 crores. It includes WIP of INR 5 crores. It includes finished goods of INR 39 crores. It includes stock and trade of INR 7 crores. It includes packing material of INR 13 crores.

items.statement: Cell culture customers are much stickier; Tarsons leverages 30-40 years of trust in basic products to cross-sell new categories
items.quote: Much higher, much, much higher. But the advantage what we have over other companies, which try and get into cell cultures, we've spent 30 years selling them basic products. Compared to cell culture, you can call the products what we make basic or standardized or commoditized products, and build a level of trust around this user base.

items.statement: New cell culture capacity ramp-up expected: 15-20% in year 1, 30-35% by year 2, reaching optimal levels in 3-4 years
items.quote: We would start selling immediately once we launch the products within the first month. And then the scale-up will happen over 2 to 3 years where we expect to reach close to optimal levels of capacity. So, I would believe from 0 to 100, we would get to the installed capacity maybe in -- within 3 to 4 years at even levels, maybe 15%, 20% capacity going in the first year, 30%, 35% by year 2 and so on

items.statement: Government procurement via GeM platform hindering domestic institutional business growth due to L1 process
items.quote: See, the problem with the domestic business in India is that now it is controlled by GeM, which is called the Government e-Marketplace. And unfortunately, this is not the most organized way of purchase because vendors and suppliers with products which do not fit the needs of the customers. Customers are forced to buy from them because of the systems and because of the L1 process.

items.statement: Automation-compatible pipette tips not pursued due to high capex and OEM-dominated market; focus remains on manual consumables and new cell culture products
items.quote: We do not produce the same today because India, again, is a very nascent market. The capex for such product lines is large. And it's not prudent at this time for a company like us to invest $10 million or $15 million on a product line, which is just about gaining certain momentum in areas where we never sold product in the past.

items.statement: Consolidated Q3 FY26 revenue INR 108 crores, up 12.8% YoY; EBITDA INR 31.5 crores at 29.2% margin
items.quote: Consolidated revenue for the quarter was INR 108 crores, marking a growth of 12.8%, compared to Q3 FY '25. EBITDA for Q3 FY '26 was around INR 31.5 crores with EBITDA margin of 29.2%.

items.statement: Equity infusion in Singapore subsidiary for loan repayment on German entity acquisition, not for expansion
items.quote: This investment of equity in Singapore is not related to any kind of expansion. This investment of equity is basically related to the loan which we have taken in Singapore entity for the acquisition of German entity. We need to serve the EMI obligations and the loan obligation from India.

items.statement: Global geopolitical uncertainty remains key external risk for international growth despite FTA benefits
items.quote: But we'll see how the external political environment all over the world plays up and what sort of stability the world continues to have over the next 3 to 4 years. I think that would be a very important factor, more external than internal, where we'll have to watch out.

items.statement: Currency depreciation of ~12.5% (USD from INR 80 to 90) improves competitiveness versus MNC importers
items.quote: The dollar which was 2 years back hovering around INR 80 now hovers at INR 90. So, it's like a 12%, 12.5% depreciation from INR 80 to INR 90.

items.statement: Nerbe Europe subsidiary grew 22% in Q3 mostly due to rupee depreciation against Euro; underlying business flat in challenging German economy
items.quote: It's mostly due to the rupee depreciation because the Euro has shot up against the rupee. I think Nerbe overall has been just a marginal growth from last year. It's a very challenging economy. 2025 calendar year was a very challenging time for the European economy, especially the German economy.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 growth expected ahead of YTD FY26 growth of 11.1%
items.quote: We believe that with all the plans that we've got in motion, our Q4 growth will be ahead of the YTD FY26 growth that we've delivered, which is of 11.1%.

items.statement: Long-term ambition of 2x revenue and 3x EBITDA by FY30 unchanged
items.quote: we have complete conviction. And we believe that we are well on track to deliver to the ambition that we've outlin ed, which is of 2x the Revenue and 3x of the EBITDA

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY26 in range of INR 60-70 crores
items.quote: Our YTD FY26 capex this year is running close to INR 60 crores. And we've given out a guidance that we intend to keep our capex in the range of INR 60 crores to INR 70 crores.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 57 bps YoY to 11.3%
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA margins expanded by 57 basis points to 11.3% in Q3.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 331 bps YoY to 60.8% in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Gross margins expanded 331 basis points year-on-year to be at 60.8% during Q3.

items.statement: Gross margins expected to remain range-bound, not at 61% level
items.quote: We do not expect to keep our gross margins at a level of 61% that you would have seen in this quarter. But you've seen our trajectory over the last 4 years, and we intend to keep it range bound at those levels.

items.statement: Post-festive slowdown led to elevated trade inventories, most pronounced in e-commerce and Water Purifiers
items.quote: A slowdown post the festive period led to elevated trade inventories, which weighed on growth. This impact was the most pronounced in the e-commerce channel and on the Water Purifier category.

items.statement: Air purifier demand growing 3x on low base, out of stock end of quarter, expected to stay strong and broaden geographically
items.quote: The air purifiers portfo lio did very well and delivered a breakout performance in Q3. We built a stronger product range this year and rolled out strong awareness and point-of-sale activation programs, which helped the business grow 3x, albeit on a low base, and we were out of stock during the end of quarter

items.statement: AMC bookings grew double-digits for third consecutive quarter
items.quote: Our AMC bookings growth trajectory continued strongly, making Q3 as a third consecutive quarter of double-digit growth.

items.statement: Emerging categories (Robotics, Softeners, Air) driving growth; Robotics now nearly 2/3 of Vacuum Cleaner portfolio
items.quote: As far as Robotic is concerned, that has continued to be in a very strong growth trajectory. It is now already nearly 2/3 of our Vacuum Cleaner portfolio.

items.statement: COGS program well institutionalized, driving gross margin headroom for growth investments
items.quote: Our COGS program is now well institutionalized and is helping create the headroom for growth investments.

items.statement: A&SP spends grew 23.3% YoY in Q3 FY26, focus remains on category expansion
items.quote: Our A&SP spends grew by 23.3% year-on-year in Q3, and the focus will remain on investing for category expansion.

items.statement: Market share gained in Water Purifiers both sequentially and YoY across channels
items.quote: We have gained market share in the Water Purifier segment, both sequentially and year-on-year. This market share gain has come across channels, online and offline.

items.statement: New entrants in Water Purifiers not impacting Eureka Forbes; share gains continue

items.quote: During Q3 FY '26, consolidated revenue stood at INR 200 crore, while EBITDA was at INR 71 crore, translating into an EBITDA margin of 35.3%.

items.statement: 9M FY26 consolidated net revenue grew 15.3% to INR 524 crore, EBITDA up 12.8% to INR 165 crore, PAT INR 54 crore

items.statement: Healthy mix of corporate travel, weddings and leisure demand supported Q3; hotels outperforming market with occupancy premiums of ~25% vs competitors in Delhi, Hyderabad, Goa, Vizag, Indore

items.statement: Flurys EBITDA margin 12% pre-Ind AS in Q3 FY26; same-store growth 9%; target INR 500 crore revenue in 3-4 years
items.quote: It was in the range of 12%, Q3 FY '26.

items.quote: Our balance sheet remains comfortable, supported by healthy cash flows, a net worth of about INR 1,329 crore and mutual fund investments of nearly INR 58 crore.

items.statement: AI-first culture with Nor1 AI upselling platform launched across portfolio; digital check-ins, intelligent guest engagement, automation; technology to enable people not replace

items.statement: Hotels outperforming market with ~25% occupancy premium vs competitors in Delhi, Hyderabad, Goa, Vizag, Indore; Kolkata RevPAR growth 11% vs market 6-9%
items.quote: Hotels across Delhi, Hyderabad, Goa, Vizag and Indore outperformed their respective markets, reporting occupancy premiums of close to 25% compared to competitors.

items.statement: Management acknowledges misjudging Q1 slippage velocity and Q2 recovery; Q3 has corrected the trajectory
items.quote: I think that should give you a good sense of what we missed as a management team. The higher slippages in Q1, less recovery than we anticipated in Q2. But happy to report that Q3 has kind of paid for all of that, and we are back to our growth path.

items.statement: LCR normalized to 120%; 90.8% bulk deposits and 90.4% retail deposits with tenor 1 year and above
items.quote: For folks who want to know more details about it, our LC R has normalized to 120%, and we continue to be a bank which focuses on long tenor deposits with 90.8% of our bulk deposit 1 year and above and 90.4% of our retail deposits with 1 year and

items.quote: Compared to last year, the average relationship is up to 4. Gold penetration up from 2% to 2.6%. CASA continues to be at the same levels. Our business loan program is up at 21%, two-wheeler has moved up to 1.2%.

items.statement: Management does not provide quarterly or annual guidance; growth benchmark is outperforming the 12% outsourced market growth rate
items.quote: We don't give guidance. And that's why I keep saying that in general if we're growing faster than 12%, we're gaining market share. If we're growing slower than 12%, we're losing market share.

items.statement: Medicare Advantage rate pressure is a macro tailwind for value-based care portfolio as providers need to optimize premium capture and cost of care
items.quote: So when you really think about it, the more the pressure on these risk-bearing entities or providers, the more attractive our value-based care portfolio becomes to them. And so I fundamentally look at it as a macro tailwind for the value-based care business.

items.statement: Two unnamed deals kicking into revenue in Q4 FY26; Femwell and StrideCare deals expected to start revenue in Q1 FY27, with StrideCare fully live by end of Q1/early Q2 and Femwell rolling out over 6-9 months from Q1 to Q3
items.quote: Two of those deals that are unnamed are actually kicking into Q4 itself. And the other two deals, Femwell and StrideCare are expected to start kicking into revenue in Q1. StrideCare should go live entirely by the end of Q1, perhaps early Q2. The Femwell deal, which is, you know, their base of 800-plus providers, is likely to go live across that 800-provider base over the six-to-nine-month duration

items.statement: 85-90% of growth comes from existing customer expansion; top 5 and top 10 customers grew healthily YoY and QoQ with vintage north of 6 years; 90% of new deals replace in-house incumbent
items.quote: And we still continue to maintain that in most healthy growth years, somewhere between 85% to 90% of our growth is going to come from existing customer expansion versus new customer addition.

items.statement: Headcount grew only 1.5% YoY (13,150 to 13,350) while revenue grew 24% YoY in INR terms (19% CC), demonstrating AI-driven non-linearity between revenue and people growth
items.quote: Our headcount as of December 31st, 2025, is about 13,350. Same time last year, it was about 13,150. So you can see there's only a 1.5% growth in headcount for a 24% growth in revenue in rupee terms or a 19% growth in revenue in dollar terms.

items.statement: Adjusted OCF and FCF conversion from EBITDA and PAT remains close to 100%; INR90 crores ($10M) upfront performance guarantee to large customer booked as asset to be recovered through platform deployment savings
items.quote: The actual OCF numbers you need to adjust a INR90 crores or $10 million number. This is towards an upfront performance guarantee that has been provided to a large customer. This will be booked as assets in our books, which will be recovered through the savings that we will be generating in our customer as we deploy our platform.

items.statement: Revenue grew 24% YoY in INR (19% CC) to INR815 crores; EBITDA grew 40.4% YoY to INR281 crores (35% margin); adjusted PAT grew 48% YoY to INR215 crores; EPS INR11 (40% YoY); RoE 30% (33% adjusted)
items.quote: Happy to note that in this quarter we were able to grow our revenue to INR815 crores, which is about a 24% year-on-year growth in revenue, 19% in constant currency terms and we were able to do this while delivering some very strong EBITDA numbers. EBITDA came in at about INR281 crores.

items.statement: Acknowledges unpredictability in dynamic regulatory/AI environment; potential quarterly hiccups possible; no linear growth guarantee; clients under increasing margin pressure testing pride of owning everything in-house
items.quote: I don't think this is a mature stable market where you can predict a linear growth curve quarter-on-quarter, year-on-year. So if your question is, does this create unpredictability in the market and could there be hiccups? Absolutely.

items.statement: Interested in acquiring point-solution leaders in health system segment and system-of-record leaders in any segment; conservative on valuations; balance sheet kept healthy for opportunities
items.quote: I think if there are some significant leaders in the point solution system of action in the health system market, those will be attractive, and then absolutely a system of record leaders in any of the segments of the market will be attractive.

items.statement: No dividend planned in near term; priorities are organic growth investment, complementary acquisitions, and paying down remaining $50M debt
items.quote: We still have multiple opportunities to continue to grow our business as well as look at acquisition opportunities which will be complementary to our business. And of course what the $50 million of debt that we still have, is of course something that we want to pay that down pretty quickly.

items.statement: R&D, marketing, and sales force expansion planned by market segment; headcount nearly flat at ~13,350 despite 24% revenue growth
items.quote: And then we'll continue to expand our sales force by market segment because each of the market segments are so nuanced and have their own dynamics.

items.statement: Outcome-based pricing model (% of customer revenue); new net economic value add advance model (e.g., $16.5M advance to Palomar Health, $3M value generated in 4 months post go-live)
items.quote: We have two streams of economics. One stream of economics is obviously at the deployment of our platform, the customers pay us the usage fee for basically eliminating those chore tasks. But the second pool of economics is where often we are incentivizing our customers to buy the full platform through what we call a net economic value add advance.

items.statement: Uses Anthropic's Claude for code generation, collapsing engineering cycle; expects compute and logic (LLM) costs to fluctuate, reflected in rising R&D spend; not a pure product company so marginal cost not zero
items.quote: We use Anthropic's leading platform Claude to actually do a lot of our code generation. And what it does is it collapses the development of the engineering cycle for us dramatically.

items.statement: FY27 consolidated revenue target of INR5,700 crores with double-digit EBITDA margin
items.quote: Yes, so FY '27, with everything put together, we will be looking at a top line of close to 5,700 and a double-digit EBITDA on that.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA guidance of INR90-100 crores on revenue of INR1,200 crores
items.quote: Q4, we are looking at anything between INR90 crores to INR100 crores consolidated EBITDA.

items.statement: Silvassa technical textile yarn capacity doubling from 9,000 to 18,000 MTPA in Q1 FY27
items.quote: This expansion will double our installed capacity from 9,000 metric tons per annum to 18,000 metric tons per annum in Q1 FY '27, strengthening our presence in the high -value technical textile and supporting long-term margin improvement.

items.statement: Punjab Phase 1 polymerization capacity of 700 MTPD targeted by end of Q4 FY26
