items.statement: Silvassa technical textile expansion capex of INR80 crores funded through internal accruals
items.quote: Yes, it's about INR80-odd crores for the expansion at Silvassa.

items.statement: Punjab Phase 2 capex of INR125-150 crores to add 200 MTPD by end of FY27
items.quote: And the investment for that expansion is not very large because most of the work for that part of the journey has been done along with this. So it's only a small capex maybe about INR150 crores or INR125 crores to INR150 crores which will add up to adding that additional 200-odd tons per day.

items.statement: Madhya Pradesh cotton yarn project capex of INR400+ crores, commissioning in H2 FY28
items.quote: we will be doing spending about 400 and odd crores at the cotton facility for Madhya Pradesh. Which will be done over gradually over the period of time , and we will be moving and seeing our cash flows accordingly we will be moving on that subject.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin of 5.6% in Q3 FY26 impacted by Punjab ramp-up and QCO removal
items.quote: Consolidated normalized EBITDA was INR59.9 crores with a margin of 5.6%, while reported EBITDA stood at INR57.2 crores with a margin of 5.3%.

items.statement: Standalone normalized EBITDA margin of 7.3% in Q3 FY26, down sequentially due to GST deferral and BIS QCO removal
items.quote: Standalone normalized EBITDA was INR56 crores with a margin of 7.3%. As disclosed, normalized EBITDA excludes the one-time impact of additional gratuity liability under the new labour codes of approximately INR2.6 crores. The sequential moderation in margins was largely driven by temporary industry factors, including GST -related demand deferral and pricing pressure following the removal of BIS an

items.statement: Gross margin target of 30-31% for Q4 FY26 and going forward as raw material costs stabilize
items.quote: So we can expect a gross margin at anything around 31%-odd in the coming quarters? Management: That's right

items.statement: US tariff impact reduced orders from export-oriented customers in home textiles and apparel segments
items.quote: During the quarter, demand for textile products was impacted by the elevated US tariff, which led to reduced orders from certain export -oriented customers, particularly in the end -use segments such as home textiles and apparels.

items.statement: India-US tariff settlement expected to revive export demand; India-EU trade agreement opens new opportunities
items.quote: The settlement of the India-US tariff issue is expected to revive export demand and enhance India's competi tiveness, vis-a-vis other supplier countries. In parallel, the India -EU trade agreement opens new opportunities across fashion -led consumption as well as value-added segments such as technical and automotive sectors.

items.statement: FDY prices dropped 10-12% after QCO removal, recovered ~50% since; DTY prices stable
items.quote: Yes, initially when the QCO was removed, a lot of material, a cheaper material did flow in from China, which impacted our pricing, yes. And the pr ices dropped by almost about 10%, 12%. But having said that, post that almost 50% of that we have recovered back and we are on a way to get there.

items.statement: PET and MEG prices fluctuated ~10% during quarter, now stabilizing and trending downwards
items.quote: Yes, you're absolutely right, the PET and MEG, the fluctuation was as much as about 10% from the bottom to the top.

items.statement: Standalone working capital cycle at 1.6x; inverted duty structure (18% to 5% GST) increases fund blockage but refunds accelerating
items.quote: See, the working capital is c lose to 1.6 for the standalone as the requirements of the Poly cot plant at Punjab are very negligible.

items.statement: Consolidated net debt of INR1,300 crores; foreign debt of 50 million euros fully hedged for 10 years
items.quote: The net debt at consolidated level was close to INR1,300 crores. And the foreign debt was close to 50 million euros. But the entire foreign debt which is in Euros has been hedged for the entire period of the debt, which is 10 years.

items.statement: Interest cost run rate similar to current quarter (~INR130-140 crores) but slightly lower due to scheduled repayments; hedging premium ~INR17 crores
items.quote: It will be slightly on the lower side on account of repayments which are scheduled during the course of the year

items.statement: Punjab facility volumes successfully placed with existing and new North India customers without inventory build-up
items.quote: Importantly, the incremental volumes were successfully placed with existing and new customers in the North India textile market without any inventory build -up.

items.statement: Indirect exports ~25% of sales, of which 5-7% to US; diverted volumes to domestic commodity market during tariff impact
items.quote: Yes, as we have said earlier, our indirect exports is about 25% and we have said about 5% to 7% of that is to the US. So yes, there was some impact. And more so because most of these customers were high-end value purchasers. So we had to divert because the entire volume was not coming from them, we had to move to the local market and domestic market where more of the commodity play was there, whic

items.statement: GST on fabrics reduced from 12% to 5% caused inventory buildup; BIS QCO removal in November created temporary margin pressure
items.quote: In addition, the change in GST rates on fabrics from 12% to 5% resulted in a brief period of inventory buildup across the value chain, as customers deferred purchases to benefit from the revised rate. This was followed by the sudden removal of the BIS QCO requirements in November, which created temporary margin pressure for the industry.

items.statement: Anti-dumping probe on PTY imports from China under investigation; would help if implemented but minimal imports currently
items.quote: No, it will only help us if it comes through. But I think there are still investigations on and we are yet to see the result of that. But having said that, in today's condition, hardly anything is coming there.

items.statement: Silvassa revenue mix: ~INR400 crores cotton, ~INR100 crores technical textiles, balance filament yarn; Punjab 100% filament yarn
items.quote: So, effectively on our Silvassa facility of where the top line is close to INR3,000 crores, we do about 400 and odd crores revenue comes from the cotton side and about 100 and odd crores comes from the technical textiles and the balance comes from the filament yarn. Aradhana Jain: Understood. Management: For the Punjab facility, it's all from the filament yarn

items.statement: Promoter holding at 78%, must reduce to 75% per SEBI regulations; will address over time
items.quote: So as per the SEBI regulation, we have to bring it down to 75%, but we have some time on that, so we will look at it as we go across the journey.

items.statement: Cotton yarn spreads improving with stable raw cotton prices; polyester spreads follow cotton with a lag, expected to improve from Q1 FY27
items.quote: Yes, you're right. The cotton spreads have improved and we personally feel that yes, it's on a good wicket and it's going to move up further. The raw cotton prices are also more or less stable, so that's also helping the cause. And yes, more or less every time the cotton moves up, the polyester responds a little late, but it follows the track. So we expect that's why we expect from first quarter o

items.statement: Revised FY26 revenue growth guidance to 28-30% YoY from earlier ~25%, and PAT margin improvement guidance to 150-200 bps from earlier ~75 bps
items.value: 28-30% revenue growth; 150-200 bps PAT margin improvement
items.quote: While we had earlier guided for approximately 25% year-on-year revenue growth, we are revising it upward to 28% to 30% along with an improvement in profitability of around 150 to 200 basis points compared to the earlier guidance of approximately 75 basis points for the whole year.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin expanded 200 bps YoY to 11.2%; PAT margin rose to 7.9% from 5.5%
items.quote: Operating performance continued to improve as EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR545.7 million, with EBITDA margin expanding to 11.2% from 9.2% in Q3 FY'25, translating into a strong 200 bps increase.

items.statement: IDC estimates 2026 new PC shipments could decline up to 8.9% due to memory shortages and rising prices, driving higher acceptance of refurbished PCs
items.quote: According to IDC, global new PC shipments stood at about 284.7 million units in 2025. Against this backdrop, IDC estimates that shipments in 2026 could decline by up to 8.9% due to memory shortages and rising prices.

items.statement: DDR5 8GB RAM prices rose ~270% from $23.35 to $86.61 (Oct 2025 to Jan 2026); DDR5 16GB rose 3.4x from $54.85 to $189.99; new PC prices up ~20% so far
items.quote: To put this into perspective, as DDR5 8GB RAM prices increased from $23.35 on 1st October 2025 to $86.61 by 1st January 2026, nearly a 270% increase. Similarly, DDR5 16GB RAM prices rose from $54.85 to $189.99 over the same period, a 3.4x increase.

items.statement: Signed strategic partnerships with world's largest technology distributor and India's 2nd largest, plus India's 5th largest distributor; both traditionally focused on new PCs
items.quote: We have partnered with one of the world's largest technology distributors and the second largest distributor in India, and separately partnered with fifth largest technology distributor in India.

items.statement: Expanded to 8 facilities in UAE (from 3), added larger facility adjacent to Navi Mumbai site, increasing US space; headcount grew from 1,194 to ~1,900 including 600+ engineers
items.quote: We have now around eight facilities in the UAE from three what we had earlier. And we have now taken one bigger facility adjacent to our existing facility in Navi Mumbai. And we are increasing our space in the US market as well.

items.statement: Working capital days in 120-130 day range; sequential improvement of a couple of days; comparable quarter identical
items.quote: The working capital days are in the 120 to 130 day odd range on an overall basis. Sequential quarter-wise there's actually been an improvement in of a couple of days in the working capital cycle, and in terms of comparable quarter, it's been identical.

items.statement: Procuring from diverse global suppliers (leasing companies, corporates, ITAD partners, recyclers); proactively securing large supplies leading to elevated stock; still enjoying pricing advantages but broad trend rising
items.quote: The availability because of our relationships we are able to procure material because we buy from plethora of partners which are like leasing companies, corporates, IT asset disposition partners, recyclers. So we continue to get good supplies and we are taking steps proactively to secure large supplies and that is leading to elevated stock positions.

items.statement: No impact from labor code on business
items.quote: No, there is no impact of labor code in our business.

items.statement: Memory prices expected to normalize by end of 2027; new PC prices up 20% in last 45 days; core i3 laptops may not be available below INR 35,000-40,000 (USD 375) in new segment
items.quote: We see memory prices coming back to shape by end of 2027. But this current situation, as we have seen, the brand new prices have already gone up from 8th December till 7th of January. We have done the plotting, the brand new computer prices have gone up by 20% across the board

items.statement: ~100% of sales now under own brand Electronics Bazaar; devices carry premium positioning; 3-year warranty in India, 1-year internationally
items.quote: I would also like to highlight that nearly 100% of our sales are now under our own brand, Electronics Bazaar. This reduces dependence on external brands strengthens customer recall, reinforces trust, and supports long-term value creation.

items.statement: Elevated inventory maintained deliberately to secure supply amid structural memory shortages; higher interest cost offset by expanded margins; working capital intensity high but supports ROE/ROCE
items.quote: Finally, given the ongoing memory shortages and rising prices of new PCs, we believe it is critical to maintain elevated inventory levels. This ensures continuity of supply for our customers and is essential for sustaining both sales growth and margin expansion during this period of structural supply constraints.

items.statement: No dividend policy framed yet; business needs fuel for growth; will remain fluid and share thoughts later
items.quote: We'll come back to you on this Atul. At this point of time business requires fuel and we need to grow. I guess, we remain fluid in this and we will keep sharing our thoughts on this.

items.statement: Large new-PC distributors partnering with GNG validates refurbished segment acceptance; high entry barriers due to product+service+credibility model; not channel/geography dependent
items.quote: Importantly, the fact that these two distributors, who have traditionally been focused primarily on the distribution of brand new computers will now also distribute our refurbished products, demonstrates the increasing acceptance, scalability, and long-term potential of the refurbishment industry in general and Electronics Bazaar, GNG Electronics in particular.

items.statement: Private label contribution target raised to 22% from current 17% over next two years
items.quote: The company plans to increase private label contribution to 22% from current 17% over the next two years.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin improved 137 bps YoY to 8.01%
items.quote: We significantly improved our profitability with EBITDA climbing 63.59% year on year to INR24.91 crores, bringing our EBITDA margin to 8.01 %, an increase of 137 basis points.

items.statement: 9M FY26 EBITDA margin improved 104 bps YoY to 8.38%
items.quote: We grew our EBITDA by 33.79% to INR60.34 crores achieving an EBITDA margin of 8.38% which shows an improvement of 104 basis points.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth at 8% YoY blended across all products
items.quote: The same store growth is 8% for year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Private label volume growth in retail stores at 17-20% YoY
items.quote: We are growing almost in the range of 17% to 20% and it is growing year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Retail capex ~INR1,500/sq ft for 5,000 sq ft stores; no major manufacturing capex needed for 2-3 years
items.quote: So capex for the retail store is almost INR1,500 per square foot and on an average we have a 5,000 square foot store size. And as far as manufacturing and processing capex is concerned, we already have enough capex installed to meet the supply.

items.statement: Capital cycle days increased to ~100 due to longer export transit to US, UK, Europe, Canada (45-60 days)
items.quote: Now we are now – now majority of our export operation is in U .S, U.K, European countries, Australia, Canada where the transit is more than 45 days, 50 days, 60 days depending on the vessel and depending on the geopolitical situation what route is open, what route is not open.

items.statement: Export customers are top private-label FMCG brands (e.g., Heera in UK), not direct retailers
items.quote: So, basically what we -- when I say about top players, I mean about the players who have their own private label well-established in those countries, which caters the local crowd within that country, right. So, for example, I can give you in UK there is a brand called Heera which is the leader in UK when it comes to Indian commodities.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 revenue grew 35.5% YoY to INR311.12 cr; 9M FY26 revenue grew 19.05% YoY to INR719.75 cr
items.quote: Our income grew by 35.51% year on year to INR311.12 crores.

items.statement: Pricing strategy tracks offline/online competitors; negotiates better trade terms with FMCG majors; loyalty via free home delivery and 15+1 scheme
items.quote: We try to break deal with all with all the leading FMCG companies for the terms of trade if not to get a better term of trade terms of trade than our competitors. And when it comes to retention of our consumers, we try to give them services like free home delivery. And offer them 15 plus one which is basically you get one month of free shopping on shopping of 15 months.

items.statement: Plan to open 10-15 stores per year; targeting 60-65 stores by FY27 from current 49
items.quote: 10 to 15 stores in the next year. So right now we are at the count of 49 so by FY '27 you can see at the number of around 60 to 65 stores

items.statement: Differentiation via neighborhood format, distinct product basket, pack sizes, quality focus within 4 km radius; not competing directly with DMart
items.quote: We are value driven, we are neighborhood stores, our design of product basket is way different than what DMart does, our packing size is way different than what DMart does, our quality of food is way different than peanut oh than what DMart does right.

items.statement: Geopolitical shipping route disruptions affect export transit times and working capital
items.quote: depending on the geopolitical situation what route is open, what route is not open because we see consistency in this market rather than the Middle Eastern market where the prices fluctuation and the quality is negotiable for them.

items.statement: Sugar export ban for 2 years caused revenue dip after FY23 (INR300 cr sugar exports lost)
items.quote: Now due to the government circumstances in regards to the trade of sugar, it was banned for the next 2 years right so the dip that you saw was account of that. And in that year we did around something INR300 crores worth of sugar exports.

items.statement: No store closures in history; 49 stores operational; emphasis on long-term sustainable model
items.quote: Even when it comes to our stores, we have opened 49 stores, none of them has been shut till yet right.

items.statement: Stores may serve as dark stores for quick commerce; partnerships with quick commerce players under negotiation
items.quote: are talking with them. S o basically what we said is whenever we introduce our quick commerce feature in our application we would use our stores as dark stores. Apart from that we are also talking with the key players in the quick commerce market to take up as our store as the dark store and that's still in the talks we ar e trying to negotiate with them

items.statement: Indian Chaska brand revenue INR8 cr in first year; targeting 15-20% month-on-month growth, 2-3% full-year contribution
items.quote: We did an exceptional revenue of around INR8 crores this year and we plan to grow on 15% to 20% month on month. The overall percentage at the year -end should give you an overall impact of 2 %-3% by just Indian Chaska.

items.statement: Industry expected to grow high single digits in FY27, with moderation in second half due to high base.
items.quote: So overall, the industry for the next financial year is likely to grow in high single digits.

items.statement: January price increase of INR300 per vehicle taken to mitigate commodity inflation.
items.quote: The price hike we've taken in January was INR300 is what we've taken from 1st of January per vehicle, INR300 per vehicle.

items.statement: Commodity inflation impacted Q3 by 40-50 bps; prices continue rising in Q4.
items.quote: So your first part of the question was how much is the impact coming from the commodity in the previous quarter was approximately 40 to 50 basis points.

items.statement: May take further price increases during the quarter if required, given strong market conditions.
items.quote: I also would like to add that the market conditions are strong, and we'll be taking adequate price increase if required during the quarter.

items.statement: ICE business EBITDA margin expanded 100 bps YoY to 17% on pricing, LEAP savings, operating leverage.
items.quote: ICE business EBITDA margin expanded by 100 bps year-on-year to 17%, driven by pricing, LEAP savings and operating leverage.

items.statement: Overall EBITDA margin improved 20 bps to 14.7% after EV investment of INR208 crores.
items.quote: During the quarter, after taking into account the investments behind EV business, approximately INR208 crores, the overall EBITDA margins improved 20 basis points to 14.7%.

items.statement: Margins to hold; growth to drive overhead dilution and expansion.
items.quote: On the margins, I think with the growth, we will get overhead dilution, and we will see expansion there.

items.statement: Positive demand trend expected to continue; January retail grew 21% YoY.
items.quote: Post festive demand continues to stay strong with January '26 retail growing at 21% year-on-year.

items.statement: Q4 and Q1 expected strong, especially rural, aided by wedding season and early festives.
items.quote: We also expect that as we see the wedding season unfolding from February onwards, some early festives that set in from March, we expect quarter 4 also to be strong

items.statement: Scooters, EV, and premium expected to grow faster than other categories.
items.quote: Some segments are likely to grow faster as Harsh said, scooters, both ICE, EV and premium we are -- we expect a faster growth than the rest of the categories.

items.statement: EV capacity expansion expected to see marked increase in FY27.
items.quote: So we are looking at F '27 as the year in which we would be able to see a marked increase on this front.

items.statement: ABS regulation timelines uncertain; company ready to comply with any guidelines.
items.quote: There are different options being discussed -- and we are awaiting further guidelines, if any, when they come. But we will be ready to fulfil those guidelines, whichever guidelines come.

items.statement: Interim dividend announced on back of strong festive season.
items.quote: You've all seen the interim dividend getting announced. This was on the back of a strong festive season.

items.statement: Expects Q4 FY26 volumes of 9-9.5 million tons, with demand momentum continuing through March.
items.quote: I can easily and with a great deal of confidence, say that within this quarter, we will do 9 million to 9.5 million tons.

items.statement: Expects FY27 industry demand growth of 7.5-8%, with Shree growing in line or better.
items.quote: So next year, I expect the demand to be around 7.5% to 8%.

items.statement: Guides FY27 capex at INR500 crores, excluding any new cement capacity additions.
items.quote: So I am giving a guidance of next year capex at INR500 crores.

items.statement: FY26 capex to be INR2,000 crores, with INR1,500 crores already spent.
items.quote: This year I'll be doing INR2,000 crores.

items.statement: Plans to expand RMC plants from 19 to 45 by September 2026.
items.quote: We intend to take it to 45 within next 6 to 8 months, means you can easily assume that by September'26, the number of plants will increase to 45 from 19.

items.statement: Narrowed price gap with UltraTech from INR30 to INR15 per bag; expects further improvement.
items.quote: If you will notice by restraining our volumes, we have narrowed the gap from about INR30 a bag to about INR15 a bag.

items.statement: Expects to restore EBITDA per ton premium of INR100-150 over competition.
items.quote: Otherwise we had always maintained a INR100 to INR150 delta plus side. And I expect to catch that up.

items.statement: Fuel cost at INR1.56 per kilocalorie, lowest in industry; may rise in Feb-Mar but stay below INR1.80.
items.quote: As on date, we are at 1.56 per kilocalorie. It may remain same for January, but it may go up in February and March. In any case, I don't think it should increase to1.80, which is my peer group fuel cost.

items.statement: No let-up expected in demand through March due to government budget spending.
items.quote: We don't find any let up in February and March because the central government budget has to be spent by 31st March, so I don't think there will be any let up in volumes.

items.statement: Premium cement share at 21-22%; expects to maintain same run rate this financial year.
items.quote: And at the moment with the current demand scenario we are at 21%-22%, and we expect to maintain the same run rate for this financial year.

items.statement: Dividend payout for FY26 expected to be materially better than FY25.
items.quote: But I expect the dividend payout for FY ‘25-‘26 to be better than FY ‘24-‘25. And it is not a differential of INR5 rupees kind of a thing.

items.statement: 80 MT capacity target by FY29 may be deferred depending on demand.
items.quote: I had hinted that 80 million tons by FY '29 may get deferred or may culminate is completely dependent on how the demand pans out in FY '26-'27.

items.statement: Depreciation expected at INR1,600-1,700 crores next year.
items.quote: Depreciation should be about INR1,600 crores.

items.statement: MCA investigation under section 210 is routine; information shared, no report yet.
items.quote: It is a routine inquiry. They have asked for information; the information has been shared. Now, they have not come up with any report.

items.statement: Management expects double-digit earnings growth in FY27, targeting around 10% given GDP growth of 7-7.5% and currency depreciation of 2-3%.
items.quote: if you look at our macroeconomics, GDP growth at about 7-7.5%, currency by about 2-3%, I think 10% is a given. So, a double-digit growth, I think from a business perspective, seems very realistic.

items.statement: Travel segment EBIT margin guidance maintained at 4% plus for the full year.
items.quote: broadly, the guidance that we have given is that we will continue our trajectory on the 4 -plus percent as far as the Travel segment is concerned.

items.statement: Foreign Exchange EBIT margins expected to sustain at 40% plus trajectory.
items.quote: We will continue to be in that trajectory. I think that's what we have been delivering year-on-year. And I don't think there's anything that should be less from that part. The 40-plus percent will see.

items.statement: Sterling plans to add 15-16 hotels/resorts in CY2026, mostly asset-light, taking 6 months to ramp up.
items.quote: this year as well, we are looking at a similar number minimum. So typically, that's how the top line keeps growing with new addition as well as the org anic growth that we have, number one. Number two is most of these expansions that are happening this year are our asset-light model as

items.statement: Sterling occupancy improved to 68% consolidated in Q3, up 4 percentage points; room nights sold grew 22% vs 17% available growth.
items.quote: The room nights sold increased by 22% again on an enterprise network basis for Q3. And the occupancy improved to 68% on a consolidated basis, up by 4 percentage points in Q3.

items.statement: Corporate Travel added 8 new accounts in Q3 across ITES, automobile, telecom, e-com; air revenue grew 12.4%, non-air transactions up 19.8%.
items.quote: During Q3 FY '26, we continue to strengthen our Corporate Travel portfolio with the acquisition of 8 new accounts across key sectors, including ITES, automobile, telecommunications and e-com.

items.statement: Consolidated PBT grew 20% YoY in Q3 to INR897M excluding one-time Labour Code impact; 9M PBT INR2,852M vs INR2,936M last year.
items.quote: Consequently, our PBT for Q3 stood at INR897 million, which improved by 20%, which excludes the onetime impact of the new Labour Code.

items.statement: Foreign Exchange EBIT grew 10% to INR316M with margins expanding to 41.5% from 38.7% YoY.
items.quote: I'm pleased to report a 10% increase in our EBIT in Q3 FY '26 to INR316 million. Correspondingly, our EBIT margins expanded to 41.5% from 38.7% last year.

items.statement: Travel segment EBIT margin 3.1% in Q3 vs 2.9% YoY; 9M margin 3.7% vs 3.9% last year.
items.quote: EBIT margins for the segment stood at 3.1% versus the 2.9% last year. For the 9 -month period, our EBIT improved by 4% to INR1,979 million and margins stood at 3.7% versus 3.9% last year.

items.statement: Sterling EBITDA margin 36% in Q3 (4pp above H1 average); EBIT margin 29% vs H1 23%; underlying EBITDA would be 37.5% excluding GST input credit impact.
items.quote: EBITDA margin was sustained at a healthy 36% , which is a 4% over H1 average. And as mentioned earlier, we've had 24 consecutive profitable quarters and this being the 25th.

items.statement: DEI EBITDA up 38% QoQ and EBIT up 42% YoY in Q3; steady-state margins expected to improve with WeC full implementation by Q1 FY27.
items.quote: EBITDA-wise, we've strongly worked on our cost structures, and we've seen a 38% increase from the last quarter. And at EBIT levels, we are 42% better than Q3 2025.

items.statement: Retail forex sales grew 25% YoY driven by 39% education segment growth and 11% holiday turnover growth; LRS industry data shows travel down 6%, study abroad down 22% Apr-Nov 2025.
items.quote: Against this backdrop, our operating performance remains strong with Retail sales growing at 25% Y-o-Y, driven by a 39% increase in the Education segment, whereas the Holiday segment turnover improved by 11%.

items.statement: B2B Travel grew 5% YoY; international DMS portfolio up 9% with Asian Trails +14%, Private Safaris +41%, East Africa +20%; Middle East and US entities faced headwinds.
items.quote: The B2B business, which contributes approximately 80% of the segment recorded a 5% growth during the quarter. Wi thin this, the international DMS portfolio grew 9% Y -o-Y, driven by a healthy performance across our overseas entities

items.statement: B2C Leisure revenue declined 6% YoY in Q3 due to Durga Puja calendar shift (INR200M moved to Q2) and IndiGo air disruptions; short-haul grew 23% 9M vs long-haul 5%.
items.quote: Travel performance during Q3 FY '26 was influenced by a combination of calendar shifts and evolving customer preferences. The advancement of Durga Puja during the period of September this year compared to October last year resulted in a portion of our festival demand shifting to the previous quarter

items.statement: Budget reduced TCS on overseas tour packages to flat 2% from 5%/20%; TCS on Education/Medical under LRS also cut to 2%, expected to spur consumer spending.
items.quote: The rationalization of TCS on overseas tour packages to a flat 2% from the earlier rates of 5% and 20%, respectively, provides immediate relief and leaves more cash in the hands of travellers.

items.statement: Rupee depreciation against Euro making Europe holidays expensive; recalibrating product portfolio to more affordable options.
items.quote: because of the sharp depreciation of rupee to the euro, our European holidays start becoming very expensive. So, we're kind of recalibrating our product portfolio, starting to make it far more affordable.

items.statement: Short-haul destinations driving growth: Vietnam +30%, Japan +15%, China 10x (small base) on 9M basis; long-haul Europe sluggish due to rupee depreciation.
items.quote: Within our p ortfolio, short-haul destinations such as Vietnam has grown in sales by 30%, Japan by 15% and China has seen over 10x growth, albeit at a smaller base

items.statement: Corporate Travel non-air hotel transactions +11.2%, car +29.2% YoY in Q3; expanded international footprint with Cyprus office for air/hotel ops.
items.quote: On the non -air side, hotel and car transactions recorded healthy growth of 11.2% and 29.2%, respectively, reflecting improved wallet share and deeper engagement across our corporate client base.

items.statement: Total debt INR220 crores including INR85-90 crores ECLGS (repayable over 2 years); overseas working capital funding for suppliers; net cash INR780 crores vs INR405 crores Dec 2024.
items.quote: out of the INR220 crores of debt, about close to about INR85 crores to INR90 crores is the ECLGS debt, which is long term, but we will be paying off in the next 2 years or so over the course of the next 2 calendar years.

items.statement: Company will move to new tax regime in FY27 to utilize MAT credits; expected positive impact on EPS.
items.quote: the government has now mandated that all companies have to move to the new tax regime if they want to utilize the MAT. And therefore, we will also do so. So effective '26-'27 we'll move into that new regime.

items.statement: Sterling RevPAR grew 17% YoY in Q3 (ARR +5% to INR6,976, occupancy +4pp to 68%); F&B +14%, rooms +16%.
items.quote: RevPAR grew 17% year-on-year on a consolidated basis in Q3, backed by a growth of 14% in food and beverage and 16% growth in rooms.

items.statement: Forex digital adoption at ~21%; app transactions grew 2.7x to 835 in Q3 from 300; app bookings grew 3x; Blinkit collaboration expanded to 8 cities.
items.quote: In terms of our digital adoption, we were at the ~21% mark. Our app engagement continued to see an upward trend and grew 2.7x to 835 transactions in the current quarter, up from 300 odd transactions in the corresponding quarter of last year.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions in Middle East and US travel advisories impacting Desert Adventures and AlliedTPro; India inbound flat due to Operation Sindoor and Nepal unrest after-effects.
items.quote: Two of our units and namely that was in U.S.A. and Middle East, which is Desert Adventures that we operate in the Middle East market, we had subdued growth. And obviously, in the case of Middle East, it was more the macro driven by the geopolitical tension.

items.statement: Sterling operating free cash flow INR346M in Q3 (+52% YoY); cash and investments INR3,243M (+54% YoY); zero debt maintained.
items.quote: Our operating free cash flow for Q3 stood at INR346 million that is a 52% growth year -on-year. Cash and investments, as mentioned earlier, is INR3.2 billion and the company continues to remain debt free.

items.statement: India prices expected to improve ~Rs 2,300/t QoQ in Q4 FY26; Netherlands realisations seen down €30-33/t QoQ due to mix; UK up ~£5/t QoQ
items.quote: I think the guidance we are giving is, India prices on QoQ will be about Rs. 2,300 /t higher, and on a spot basis of course , hot rolled will be much higher, but I think when you look at the mix and you look at some of the contracts that we have, we see an improvement of about Rs. 2,300/t. In UK, it's going to be about £5/t higher or so. In Netherlands, on a spot basis it is going to be higher on

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA expected to improve in Q4 FY26 vs Q3 FY26; volumes up ~0.5 Mt QoQ
items.quote: So overall we expect EBITDA to be better in 4Q compared to 3Q, and volumes to be almost half a million tons better in 4Q compared to 3Q.

items.statement: NINL expansion ~35-40 months to commissioning after EC; FID in next couple of months; Meramandali next; Maharashtra longer term
items.quote: We are maybe weeks away from getting the environment clearance and once we get that, our basic engineering ordering is in progress. So, I guess it will take about 35 -40 months when we get into the execution level. I think it is also important to mention that we will get to the FID in the next couple of months.

items.statement: UK 3 MTPA scrap-based EAF: major demolition done; securing high-power electricity access critical; working with Electricity System Operator and National Grid
items.quote: Major demolition work has been completed and securing access to high power electricity is critical for our plan ned transition. We are working with the Electricity System Operator and National Grid for the new electrical infrastructure which remains critical for the project commissioning.

items.statement: Ludhiana plant starting up by mid-March 2026
items.quote: we also have the Ludhiana plant coming up in the next couple of months.

items.statement: India crude steel production ~6.34 Mt in Q3 FY26 (+12% QoQ/YoY); deliveries >6 Mt for first time
items.quote: India is a core market, and our crude steel production rose about 12% QoQ and YoY to about 6.34 million tons . The sales ramped up in line with the production and outpaced the domestic demand, taking quarterly deliveries past 6 million tons for the first time for Tata Steel in India.

items.statement: Netherlands liquid steel production stable at 1.7 Mt; deliveries 1.4 Mt in Q3 FY26
items.quote: In Netherlands, the liquid steel production was broadly stable at 1.7 million tons, while deliveries were 1.4 million tons.

items.statement: UK deliveries 0.5 Mt in Q3 FY26, lower QoQ due to subdued demand

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 15% in Q3 FY26 (9M FY26: 15%, +300 bps YoY); India standalone EBITDA margin 24% in 9M FY26
items.quote: our consolidated EBITDA margin improving by about 300 basis points YoY for the nine months ended 31st December 2025.

items.statement: India Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin 23%; NINL Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin 22% (+35% QoQ)
items.quote: this helped offset the drop in net steel realisations on a QoQ basis and deliver a 23% EBITDA margin during the quarter.

items.statement: India Q3 vs Q2: realisations down ~Rs 2,100/t (guided Rs 1,500/t); coking coal consumption cost up $4/t
items.quote: price drop was about Rs. 2,100 /t, in 3Q compared to 2Q. We had guided Rs. 1,500 /t but the market was softer, particularly in October and November. Prices started going up only towards the middle of December. In terms of coking coal, I think the consumption cost was up by $4/t for India, in 3Q compared to

items.statement: India Q4 coking coal consumption cost expected +$15/t QoQ (purchase +$22/t); hot rolled coil spot ~Rs 3,500/t higher QoQ
items.quote: Coking coal, like I said, on a consumption basis will be about $15 /t higher in 4Q compared to 3Q. On a mixed basis, India prices will be Rs. 2,200/t higher, but if I were to look at the hot rolled coil, I think it will be about Rs. 3,500/t higher.

items.statement: Net debt Rs 81,834 cr (down Rs 5,200 cr QoQ, Rs 3,900 cr YoY); net debt/EBITDA ~2.6x (target <3x)
items.quote: Net debt at Rs. 81,834 crores was lower by about Rs. 5,200 crores vs. the end of the previous quarter in Sep’25, and lower by about Rs. 3,900 crores v s. Dec’24. Our net debt to EBITDA stands at about ~2.6x, well within the stated range of below 3x for the cycle

items.statement: UK safeguards expire June 2026; revision needed to narrow gap with EU quotas; government engaged but not yet announced
items.quote: The UK steel safeguard measures are due to expire in June 2026, and the framework needs to be revised to reflect the market conditions and narrow the policy gap with the EU.

items.statement: US tariffs 50% on Netherlands exports (auto, packaging) weighed on Q3 performance
items.quote: The levy of tariff to the tune of 50%, weighed on the performance.

items.statement: Auto & Special Products: best ever quarterly and 9M volumes; auto downstream mix >50% of 9M sales; Tata Tiscon best ever Q3 volumes; Tata Steelium +20% QoQ; tubes best quarterly volumes (+0.3 Mt capacity)
items.quote: Special Products business delivered the best ever quarterly and nine -month volumes driven by rapid OEM approvals for the advanced steel grades from our Kalinganagar plant. The cold rolling mill and the galvani sing lines are ramping up very well. The auto downstream mix is now more than 50% of the nine month sales level, reinforcing our leadership and preferred supplier

items.statement: Omni-channel GMV Rs 2,380 cr (+68% YoY); new products: mobile bore pile cages, internationally certified grades for Oil & Gas, Shipbuilding
items.quote: Our omni channel model is deepening customer engagement and with Aashiyana and DigECA, we achieved a gross merchandise value of about Rs. 2,380 crores which is up 68% on YoY basis.

items.statement: Consolidated stake in color coated business; acquired 50.01% in Thriveni Pellets Private Limited
items.quote: I'm happy to share that we consolidated our stake in the color coated business and completed the acquisition of the 50.01% stake in Thriveni Pellets Private Limited.

items.statement: Auto contracts renewal due April 2026; quarterly pricing; spot benefit only in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Contracts are due for renewal in April , I think , and the next set of new prices will be effective April. So, we are not seeing the benefit of auto prices this quarter. Whatever we see this quarter is a benefit of the spot orders.

items.statement: UK EBITDA loss £170m in 9M FY26 (narrowed £135m YoY); needs ~£100/t spread expansion to break even; dependent on government quota revision
items.quote: So, I'm saying that, wherever the spread is today, that spread has to expand by about £100/t to make it a profitable entity.

items.statement: Class action lawsuit filed against Netherlands in Dec 2025 by foundation backed by litigation financiers; in initial defence phase
items.quote: So that has been filed, as you know, by a foundation or a trust, which is backed by professional litigation financiers. It is kind of a suo moto class action, and there is a three months or four months phase during which we are required to submit our defence, and that's the process that is currently going on.

items.statement: Mining cost transition planning for 2030 lease expiries started; MDO model an option; BRPL in that space; redeployment from new mines (Kalamang, Koira, Gandhalpada)
items.quote: We are not going to exit captive mining. We have mining reserves which are opening up and therefore mining as an activity will continue for Tata Steel. Mine Developer and Operator ( MDO) as an option will always remain and we will be looking at certain opportunities. We also now have BRPL which will be in that space , if required. So, I think the transition planning for 2030 has already started.

items.statement: Q3 demand weak due to low crop prices, extended rainfall, and lower farm incomes; South and West India saw sharp declines, East and North stable
items.quote: During this quarter, agrochemical demand remained weak due to stressed demand drivers, weather issues, low crop prices, leading to industry-wide volume decline.

items.statement: Q4 started well with good Rabi harvest; Kharif outlook depends on weather forecasts in late March and early April
items.quote: Q4 has really started well. January has done well for us. South Indian paddy, East India paddy is looking really good.

items.statement: Full-year FY26 revenue expected to be flattish despite Q4 growth
items.quote: Yes, in case of Q4, definitely there will be a growth. But on a yearly basis, we are of the opinion it should be flattish year.

items.statement: Bayer product revenue guidance reduced from Rs 40 crore to around Rs 30 crore for FY26 due to grape season underperformance
items.quote: No, because of the grape season not behaving as per our expectation, it would not be Rs. 40 crores. It would be significantly lower than Rs. 40 Cr. Maybe around Rs. 30 crores.

items.statement: Expecting annual EBITDA margin decline of 100-110 bps vs FY25; 9-month EBITDA margin down 115 bps
items.quote: In 9 months, our EBIT negative is by 115 bps. So in overall annual basis, we are expecting a similar decline 100-110 bps.

items.statement: Long-term sustainable gross margin seen at 38% as technical prices stabilize and NEB benefit phases out
items.quote: I am of the opinion that 38% gross margins are sustainable in the long term.

items.statement: Targeting double-digit CAGR over next 3-5 years driven by macro tailwinds, new products, and export expansion
items.quote: I believe we will continue to grow at Dhanuka with a healthy double-digit growth on a short to mid-term horizon of next 3 years to 5 years.

items.statement: MPP-2 plant capex estimated at Rs 60-70 crore; business plan to be finalized within FY26
items.quote: And the MPP-2, we are expecting a CAPEX in the range of Rs. 60 crores to Rs. 70 crores.

items.statement: Dahej plant targeting 80% capacity utilization in FY27 with three products (difenoconazole, bifenthrin, iprovalicarb); second product commercialized in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Next year FY'27, we are looking at a capacity utilization of close to 80% for these two. Plus we will be adding one more product in this plant, that is the Iprovalicarb.

items.statement: Dahej B2B EBITDA negative Rs 4 crore in Q3 FY26, similar to last year; expected to turn EBITDA positive in FY27
items.quote: Dahej, we see EBITDA is still negative. In Q3, it is around 4 Cr. as against the 5 Cr. as against last year's 4 Cr.

items.statement: B2B EBITDA significantly lower than B2C; Bayer product gross margins in line with company average (~40%)
items.quote: See, B2B, of course, the EBITDA is significantly lower than B2C.

items.statement: Launched 3 new products in 9M FY26: Dinkar, Melody, Verdour; 3 more planned for FY27 (2 fungicides 9(3), 1 spray enhancer)
items.quote: In 9-month period, we have launched one is Dinkar, one is Melody and one is Verdour.

items.statement: Biostimulant regulatory impact: Rs 15 crore in Q3, Rs 49 crore in 9M (50% sales loss); 3 of 4 products expected approval by end Q4 FY26 for Q1 FY27 relaunch
items.quote: Product under regulatory changes in this category we were having a contribution of around 19% but this year the impact in our Q3 is around Rs. 15 crore and 9 month is the impact of Rs. 49 crore.

items.statement: Bayer product revenue Rs 25-27 crore in 9M FY26 (domestic only); net economic benefit Rs 19.5 crore in 9M, Rs 6 crore in Q3; NEB to phase out by FY28
items.quote: Revenue from Bayer molecule in the balance sheet of Dhanuka is around 25 crores to 27 crores.

items.statement: China export rebate reduction may raise some commodity prices but no material sourcing impact; Dhanuka passes on cost increases downstream
items.quote: Since it is an industry wide phenomena, it will not significantly impact either our sourcing or ou r competitive edge in the market

items.statement: Direct China procurement 10-15%; indirect difficult to quantify; Glufosate sourced domestically, Glyphosate export benefit already removed
items.quote: Direct procurement would be in the range of 10% to 15%.

items.statement: Cash over Rs 250 crore; debtors improved vs Dec FY25; inventory increased due to imported molecules mismatch with sales plan
items.quote: It is more than Rs.250 crore.

items.statement: Sales returns Q3 FY26 Rs 72 crore vs Rs 74 crore last year; 9M returns ~Rs 220 crore
items.quote: This year is Rs. 72 crores as against Rs. 74 crores last year.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 revenue Rs 409.92 crore vs Rs 445.27 crore; EBITDA Rs 58.66 crore vs Rs 75.56 crore; PAT Rs 40 crore vs Rs 55.04 crore
items.quote: For the last quarter, our revenue from operations stood at Rs. 409.92 crores in Q3 FY '25-'26 versus Rs. 445.27 crores in Q3 FY '24-'25.

items.statement: Zone-wise Q3 revenue: North 25%, East 11%, West 30%, South 34%; Category-wise: Insecticides 28%, Fungicides 21%, Herbicides 37%, Others 14%
items.quote: Zone-wise percentage share of turnover for Q3 FY '25-'26: North India 25%, East India 11%, West India 30% and South India 34%.

items.statement: Draft Pesticide Management Bill seen as positive for organized players; tougher rules on misbranding, spurious products, fly-by-night operators
items.quote: Draft Pesticide Management Bill would be really good for the organized industry and organized players.

items.statement: Key risks: weather/El Nino uncertainty, commodity price volatility, policy changes (e.g., Gram), farm income pressure; execution risk in Bayer supply chain transition
items.quote: Apart from the weather patterns, the commodity prices and sometimes the policies like G Ram G now could also have an impact on how the farmer move towards agri-input.

items.statement: Organized players to benefit from Pesticide Management Bill curbing spurious products; Dhanuka optimizes channel inventory faster than industry
items.quote: We try and turn it around faster than what the industry averages would be.

items.statement: Discussions ongoing with one Japanese and one European MNC for exclusive Dahej manufacturing contracts; two companies visited Dahej last quarter
items.quote: There is one discussion which is going on. In last quarter, two companies have visited us at Dahej. So one Japanese and one European.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance for FY27 expected to be better than 9% achieved in 9M FY26, previously guided 10-12% for full year
items.quote: Somehow we are maintaining our commitment to the market and uh here on we are estimating it should be at least better than whatever we have delivered so far in 9 months.

items.statement: Volume growth guidance of 4-5% for full year, 9M volume down 3%
items.quote: we've given volume group guidance of about 4 to 5% for the year. This 9 months, we are already 3% down.

items.statement: Assembly business (busbar + PCB) expected to reach Rs 250-300 crore over 3 years, FY27 ~Rs 70-75 crore, FY28 ~Rs 150-200 crore, FY29 ~Rs 250-300 crore
items.quote: It could be in the in the range of 250 to 300 cror es. With the first year this FY27 being about 70-75 crores out of that um this is already developed these components are already designed developed ready to move

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin over 24%, up 400+ bps YoY; company EBITDA expected to stay 23-25% despite lower margin assembly business
items.quote: Continuing the company's trend of improving profitability EBITDA margin continues to grow disproportionately to sales with a quarter closing with an EBITDA margin of over 24%. Marking an increase of over 400 basis points year on year.

items.statement: Assembly business EBITDA margin ~8-10% lower than current products but higher topline; overall company EBITDA to remain 23-25%
items.quote: As a percentage maybe it should be about 10% lesser, maybe 8 or 9% lesser EBITDA but of course the topline value is more than more than 15 times or so of the component alone.

items.statement: US tariff disruption caused reduced orders in Q3; expect reversal in current and upcoming quarters with US exports of shunts and bimetals to grow
items.quote: Quarter 3 in general has been challenging for us with unpredictability related to geopolitical factors especially related to US tariffs. We generally experience reduced orders from our US -based customers during that time. We hope to see this trend reverse in the current and upcoming quarters.

items.statement: Indian thermostatic bimetal market flat for 12 quarters due to switchgear market stagnation; growth depends on market growth or new applications
items.quote: See when it comes to the Indian market thermostatic bimetal is simply driven by market growth. So if you see in the last four years as you mentioned uh the general switch gear market has also had this sort of a flat kind of a performance.

items.statement: Margin expansion supported by mix improvement and higher value-added component supplies to marquee global customers
items.quote: This quarter's margin expansion was supported by a mix improvement and higher supplies of value added components to some marquee global customers alongside cost discipline.

items.statement: Shift from strip to component supply for US shunt business (Vishay) due to tariffs; components are higher value-add
items.quote: What has happened is that a lot large portion of our US-based export of EB welded or shunt materials was in in raw material form. That means we were welding strip and shipping large quantities of that to Vishay. Now that because o f these tariffs immediately put you know Vishay and us into action to move those into components.

items.statement: Two largest Indian EV two-wheeler manufacturers (by volume) are key customers for busbar assembly projects
items.quote: The two EV projects that we are working on right now for two wheelers which we are closest to supplying are both number one and number two of when it comes to EV when it comes to two -wheeler manufacturing in India not just EVs but as a whole the two largest are the ones that we are working with.

items.statement: Vishay business returning to peak levels (2-3 years ago) in FY27; already supplying components for top global EV manufacturers
items.quote: Vishay business value coming to coming back to you know similar levels to what it used to be during its peak. So that business has already begun and that business is already we've already got orders.

items.statement: No Indian competition for EB welded busbar assemblies; barrier is EB welding technical know-how (30+ years experience)
items.quote: As of now there is no competition because Nobody does this EB welding. Nobody now unless somebody makes this entire complicated assembly somewhere else in the world and then ships it to India which I highly doubt.

items.statement: Raw material pricing fully passed through; silver contacts had temporary inventory impact during factory move when silver prices spiked
items.quote: Our raw materials- our pricing structure is such that all of the raw material pricing is passed through because you know it can go either ways.

items.statement: Net working capital days increased to 250-260 due to early inventory receipt and 10-day collection increase; targeting previous year levels by Q4 FY26 via domestic suppliers and tripartite agreements
items.quote: So as far as the corrective action is concerned for raw material side We are in the process of developing three or four domestic supplier which will uh eventually reduce a certain days not uh the complete may be under 180 Produced & transcribed by - 14 - days or 200 days

items.statement: Revenue split: Thermostat bimetal - 80% switchgear, rest automotive/energy meters/appliances; Shunts - 60% automotive, 35% energy meters, rest appliances/gas meters/others
items.quote: So in thermostatic bimetal switch gear industry constitutes around uh 80% of our supplies rest is uh between automotive energy meters and some home appliances. Similarly in registered business around 60% goes to automotive and 35% goes to energy meters.

items.statement: Busbar assembly value per vehicle Rs 2,000-3,000 (60-65% material cost); 4-8 components per battery set depending on design
items.quote: To give you a simpler answer to this I would say that this kind of an assembly for a let's say a high value design let's say a design in which there's more number of bu s bars and more number of more welding or more material required would be the value of that product overall would be about 2,000 to 3,000 rupees and roughly about 62 or 60 or between 60 to 65% of that would be material cost.

items.statement: Board declared interim dividend of Rs 2 per equity share
items.quote: I'm pleased to inform you that the board has declar ed an interim dividend of 2 rupees per equity share.

items.statement: Applied for ECMS scheme (replaced PLI); approval pending; grant quantum depends on revenue from assembly business (Rs 250-300 crore potential)
items.quote: PLI has now been converted into ECMS scheme from the central government where we have already applied put our application uh which is under examination and very soon hopefully we will get the approval Produced & transcribed by - 11 - from the government

items.statement: US tariff uncertainty paused new product development for 12-18 months; considering US facility/tie-up for final packaging to improve service
items.quote: What we are also considering is to see if we can have a facility or tie up with a you know partner to have a small final packaging or a final storage area in the US because sometimes we feel that we can providing that additional service to a US-based customer can help us do more business there.

items.statement: Exploring automotive fuses (power window, tailgate) and automotive inductors as new product verticals leveraging EB welding technology
items.quote: We are looking at um you know there are certain types of automotive fuses that we are working on and we are working with the possibility of looking at getting this technology from another company foreign company or maybe even look at the possibility we are open to the idea of you know acquiring that technology or the company.

items.statement: PCB assembly revenue separate from busbar; under development; included in Rs 250-300 crore assembly target
items.quote: Technically they fall in the same category but those opportunities were different from this and those are also under development. So that business is also happening as on the side.

items.statement: Shunt baseline business (ex-assembly) expected to grow 13-19% in FY27 driven by Vishay, Denso, Japanese customers
items.quote: We should be able to add to a shunt baseline business anywhere between a you know like 13-14 to a 18-19% kind of a uh number.

items.statement: Thermostatic bimetal baseline growth expected 8-10% in FY27 for India and other markets (ex-US)
items.quote: We do expect we have an indication from our customers for India and certain other markets that we do expect to see uh you know like a 8 to 10% kind of a growth in that area.

items.statement: US strip exports not viable even at 18% tariff due to Section 232 steel/copper surcharges; component conversion permanent
items.quote: Even after this tariff gets reduced to 18% , if we continued to supply in strip form, it would have that business would have suffered. So what that has done as a result is quickly converted a lot of that strip business into parts.

items.statement: Pune facility capex incremental (Rs 20 cr) as main EB welding capacity already exists; can scale to Rs 250-300 cr revenue; may add new facility in Year 2 for other electronics opportunities
items.quote: So now it now this 20 crores is actually more of assembly work and having an assembly line and that's why we can set it up very quickly. because a lot of our main key processes equipment cannot be set up that quickly.

items.statement: Management aims to cover significant lost ground in Q4 FY26 after a soft October; long-term EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 22-25%
items.quote: In quarter 4, we aim to cover up significant lost ground.

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA margin guidance of 22-25% reiterated; current margin compression due to planned marketing and trade spend
items.quote: See in a margin fund, I always guided with the 22% to 25% of EBITDA in a longer term.

items.statement: Targeting ATL/BTL marketing spend of 7-8% of revenue for the full year, up from 4-4.5% in 9M FY26
items.quote: For the 9 months, we have done almost 4%, 4.5% of ATL, BTL. So, that we also want to take to the 7% to 8% around of revenue.

items.statement: Greenfield capex of INR 40-45 crore planned after FY27 to support INR 500 crore revenue target
items.quote: And I think after '27, we can, we will assume that we will start for the new greenfield and that will be around INR 40 crores to INR 45 crore rupees of greenfield new expansion.

items.statement: October demand was very soft across building materials; strong recovery in November and December with December exit rate matching Q2 growth
items.quote: This quarter witnessed a very soft October while sales recovered strongly in November and December. Our exit rate in December was very strong matching our quarter 3 growth.

items.statement: Q4 demand looks good; market returning to rhythm with strong December and January carpenter meets driving pull
items.quote: In quarter 4, we had a good demand in December and in December, due to a push in the trade, in January, we are focusing more into the pull side.

items.statement: EBITDA margins compressed from 32-34% to 25-26% over 3 years due to geographic expansion, trade marketing, ATL spend, and competitive discounts
items.quote: So, this is the exceptional EBITDA what we have delivered in last three years. So long term we have always guided to this. The reason is that 7% to 8% is the different situations what we need to face and we need to put that for the growth front.

items.statement: Brownfield expansion 70-80% complete; capacity increasing from 2,000 to 3,500 tons/month within 1-2 quarters, enabling INR 600-700 crore revenue potential
items.quote: After that we are moving for the 3,500 ton per month. In that, almost 70%, 80% work has been finished. So, after one or two quarters, end of this quarter, maybe we will have the capacity of 3,500 tons.

items.statement: Current capacity 2,000 tons/month; average utilization 1,200-1,250 tons/month with peaks of 1,500-1,800 tons; brownfield expansion to 3,500 tons/month nearing completion
items.quote: About the capacity, right now, our capacity is 2,000 tons per month. Averagely, we are doing 1,200, 1,250 tons per month that is average.

items.statement: No pricing pressure; competition has become more aggressive but VAM prices currently flat, not significantly affecting profitability
items.quote: It is not about the pricing pressure. Yes, it is about the competition that has become aggressive.

items.statement: VAM prices currently flat, not rising significantly, limiting impact on profitability
items.quote: It is definitely affecting our profitability, but the right now it is flat around. So, not much rise into the VAM prices.

items.statement: Focused solely on white glue (PVA) segment; peers have broader adhesive portfolios including epoxies, cyano-adhesives, construction chemicals
items.quote: So, they are more into the epoxies also, the cyano-adhesives also, construction chemicals, waterproof adhesives, tile adhesives. So, it is a different adhesive and we are into the white glue only.

items.statement: Dealer margins 8-13%, carpenter incentives 8-13%; higher in new markets (12-13%) vs mature markets (8-9%)
items.quote: For the Euro, we are giving 8% to 13%, for the dealers also and 8% to 13% for the carpenters also. So, that is depends upon the older and new market.

items.statement: Competition intense from day one (Pidilite, Astral); Gujarat market share 35%; new states penetration ongoing against established players
items.quote: the competition was there from the first day and it is very strong. You all know that, right? And in the same competition, we have came out and reached this level

items.statement: NSE listing process underway; no specific timeline given, will update once finalized
items.quote: Sure. So exact dates, I don't have available right now, but NSE process is on.

items.statement: Management focusing on shifting from push to pull strategy to reduce trade promotion and commission expenses
items.quote: So, if market pull is there, you can save a lot of money on the trade push.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free; strong cash balance of ~INR 170-180 crore funded by internal accruals
items.quote: Because of that, today the company did not need any funds, it became debt-free, it is doing so much development with internal accrual.

items.statement: Board to discuss share buyback proposal internally; management acknowledges investor suggestion but prioritizes business reinvestment
items.quote: Okay. We will take this into account and discuss it internally in the Board. We will look positive around that, what we can do.

items.statement: Hiring professionals from multinationals for leadership and ground roles across new geographies; transformation phase with hiring spree
items.quote: So, we are on the hiring spree at the leadership level, at the ground level, with the right talented guys on board to drive the business for that.

items.statement: Volume growth flat y-o-y in Q3 FY26; 9M volume growth ~4-4.5%; Q2 FY26 volume growth was 20% y-o-y
items.quote: Volume growth for Q3 is almost y-o-y flattish around and 9 months is 4% around, 4% to 4.5% for the 9 months.

items.statement: Mature market benchmark: 20-25% market share in a state; currently 5 mature states, 9 in build-up phase
items.quote: So, any market where we have got a decent market share in the range of around 20% and above is we have termed as a mature market, though the benchmark is 25%.

items.statement: Revenue growth below 20% target for last 4 quarters; management admits consolidation phase and plans to reset guidance based on execution
items.quote: But you are very right, we had a growth plan of 20%. But anyhow, because of so many circumstances, we were not able to deliver.

items.statement: Auditor currently R Kabra (solo partner of Ecovis Germany); management open to Big 4/5 auditor appointment in future
items.quote: But right now, if we talk about the current auditor, so it is R Kabra and that is a solo partner of the Ecovis firm that is from the Germany.

items.statement: IR communication acknowledged as poor; management commits to improve proactive shareholder engagement
items.quote: Sure. So, we will correct that way and we will pass this message to the team for that.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance of INR 925-1,000 crores
items.quote: So we feel -- see, for the INR 1,000 crores guidance, we feel fairly confident of being able to achieve anywhere between INR925 crores to INR1,000 crores.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margins expected to remain in high teens
items.quote: So, we expect to continue the high teens as we are doing. So, we feel fairly confident that we will continue to maintain margins in the high teens.

items.statement: Surat greenfield plant Phase 1 on track for Q4 FY26 operationalization
items.quote: The Surat greenfield plant has completed pilot runs and Phase 1 is on track to be operational by Q4 FY '26.

items.statement: Q3 capacity utilization at 70-75% weighted average after debottlenecking
items.quote: So in Q3, we were -- again, we have many products. But as an overall weighted average, I would say, with the increase now on the debottlenecking, we were probably at about 70%, 75% on a weighted average.

items.statement: Surat plant Phase 1 to start production mid-March with 30-40% utilization in FY27
items.quote: In the next fiscal year, we would probably see around 30% to 40% capacity utilization because there is another product line, as I mentioned, which will only start in the second quarter of next Fiscal Year.

items.statement: Two new frozen product lines at Surat plant: one in Phase 1 (March), second in Q2 FY27
items.quote: So the Surat plant is going to have 2 new product lines. One is getting completed in Phase 1. So from -- in fact, from March onwards, one new product line is going to come out of

items.statement: US demand robust despite tariffs; January started well; tariff clarity enables new product pitches
items.quote: This fourth quarter has also started off well. I mean we had a good month in January as well. And we feel fairly optimistic that this will now continue to -- now with the tariff situation also getting cleared off, we feel fairly confident that we will have a good robust demand on our products.

items.statement: Consolidated Q3 EBITDA margin 19.4% (down 260bps QoQ, up 150bps YoY); standalone 25.1% (up 400bps YoY)
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA for the quarter was a record INR37.1 crores, which is a 40.6% increase from the previous years. EBITDA margin was 19.4%, which has increased by 150 bps year-on-year and a decrease of 260 bps quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Distribution business steady-state margins 12-14%; recent quarters higher due to promotional support
items.quote: Our distribution margins, as we have been previously mentioning, remains at 12% to 14% in terms of our margin on an ongoing basis. We were better off in the last few quarters due to extra promotional supports.

items.statement: Truly Indian brand in 2,000+ US stores across major chains including Whole Foods, Costco, Albertsons-Safeway
items.quote: The brand is available in more than 2,000 stores across the United States.

items.statement: Tariff reduction to lower consumer prices by $0.20-0.25; price increases were at distributor level, not company level
items.quote: So if at all, any reduction is there, it will be $0.20, $0.25 at the consumer end. So I don't know how much that will help in further uptake, but it's still a positive thing.

items.statement: No active hedging; Q3 forex gains negligible; rupee strengthening expected to reduce future gains
items.quote: What we anticipate is the dollar with the rupee now strengthening for the coming quarters, we would not be having too much of a gain in terms of our forex. So that's our guidance for the coming quarters. And Q3 has very negligible amount of forex in our revenues.

items.statement: PLI incentive: ~INR 7 crores received (70% of Year 1); Years 2-3 and balance Year 1 expected by September
items.quote: Anyway, it's about INR7 crores, I think, approximately that we've received so far.

items.statement: New CFO Srinivas Ayyagari joined; new sales head for Soul brand joined December
items.quote: Firstly, I would like to introduce our new CFO, Mr. Srini Ayyagari on the call. I welcome him to the ADF family.

items.statement: Volume growth drove ~70% of Q3 revenue growth; price growth ~30%
