items.quote: Despite elevated zinc and dollar prices during the quarter, we managed our operating margins well with prudent commercial discipline across receivables, inventory and payable front, we contained net working capital to less than 15% of revenue.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR317 crore after INR167 crore investment in Jammu facility
items.quote: Strengthening the balance sheet remains a key priority for us. During the quarter net debt reduced to INR317 crores post investment of INR167 crores in the Jammu alkaline facility.

items.statement: Board approved divestment of non-core Noida land parcel with minimum price guidance of INR250 crore; monetization targeted within 6 months; further asset rationalization to be reviewed annually
items.quote: Yesterday only this declaration has been given. So we got one cut of first guidance from the Board that minimum price required for this is to be INR250 crores. So that indication has been given. And I think this is the first kind of things after the immediate embargo has been happened.

items.statement: Company initiated employee stock option scheme (ESOPs) to align long-term employee interests with shareholder value creation
items.quote: During the quarter the company also initiated stock scheme under employee stock options plan. We view ESOPs as an important mechanism to align long-term employee interests with shareholder value creation to support leadership continuity.

items.statement: Zinc prices remain at elevated levels; further price corrections may be needed in popular/economy segments if zinc stays high; commodity volatility a near-term headwind
items.quote: That being said, the zinc prices continue to remain right at the top, right? And thus, will there be more corrections needed if zinc continues the way it is over the quarter? Maybe. And it might impact some of the popular and the economy segment of zinc as well.

items.statement: Launched lithium AA/AAA Ultima batteries (up to 15x longer life); entered mosquito rackets and mobile accessories; white-label manufacturing capability planned for Jammu plant for domestic and export markets
items.quote: During the quarter, the company launched its mightiest battery ever. Lithium AA and AAA home batteries under the Ultima brand offered up to 15 times longer life within high intense devices.

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY26 guidance of 60% YoY growth across key KPIs
items.quote: With strong performance in the first 9 months, we are firmly on track to achieve our FY '26 guidance of 60% Y-o-Y growth across key KPIs.

items.statement: Committed to 60% growth guidance with no downward revision
items.quote: We stand by our guidance. 100%. If there was any c hange we would have come forward ourselves to say that. pretty confident to meet what we said on an annual basis

items.statement: Order book at 6.4 GW with 1.9x book-to-bill ratio
items.quote: Yet again, highest ever order book of 6.4 gigawatt reaffirming our market leadership, powered by over 3 gigawatt new order wins in this financial year itself, resulting in book -to-bill ratio of 1.9x.

items.statement: Order pipeline of 3-4 GW under discussion via non-bidding route
items.quote: as we speak today, we are now clearly talking about three to four gigawatts non bidding route of discussions are happening.

items.statement: India wind installations hit record 6.34 GW in 2025, trajectory to surpass 10 GW annually in 2 years
items.quote: The year 2025 has been a landmark with wind installations touching a record 6.34 giga watt, surpassing the previous peak and clearly reaffirming the vast demand potential of wind energy in the country.

items.statement: C&I segment drives 51% of order book, data centers to push renewable demand by 2030
items.quote: First one is that the current order book even if you look at 51% is from C&I and captive segment. No involvement in the bidding.

items.statement: WTG EBITDA margin dipped to 13.7% in Q3 due to customer mix and higher project revenue share
items.quote: What happens is that it depends upon a couple of things. One is the average sales price during the quarter depending upon who is the customer we supplied. So the impact of one large customer not being there this quarter impact is almost about 1.9%.

items.statement: 9-month consolidated EBITDA grew 77% YoY to INR2,058 crores
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA increased to INR2,058 crores, reflecting a strong turnaround with 77% Y-o-Y growth.

items.statement: Establishing three new AI-enabled smart blade factories to expand manufacturing footprint
items.quote: We are also establishing three new AI-enabled smart blade factories, further expanding our footprint.

items.statement: 4.5 GW manufacturing capacity fully operational, scaled for current order book
items.quote: On the manufacturing front, our 4.5 gigawatt manufacturing capacity is fully operational and scaled to support the current order book.

items.statement: SE Forge capacity utilization improved from 21% to 31% in last three quarters
items.quote: As we said that the overall between foundry and forging, the capacity utilization has gone up from 21 to 31.

items.statement: EPC share grew from 20% to 27% in Q3, S144 order book exceeds 5.4 GW
items.quote: The focus now is on expanding our EPC offering, which ha s grown from 20% to 27% in Q3, which enhances our competitive edge and further help to accelerate order book growth.

items.statement: Two largest recent orders (BrightNight, ArcelorMittal) are EPC contracts
items.quote: Two largest orders what we announced in the last 1, 1.5 months are of EPC, both BrightNight and ArcelorMittal.

items.statement: Appointed Paulo Soares as President Europe; export revenue expected from FY28
items.quote: We are exploring Europe, Australia, South Africa, Middle East and few other countries. As I said earlier, you will see some traction some terms of orders getting announced in the next financial year, but the supply starting and the revenue flowing in will be in FY28.

items.statement: US market not favored by current administration; waiting for policy change
items.quote: On the US, Deepesh, everyday morning I check whether we have a potential or not. Because it depends upon what comes on the truth threshold. So wind will happen or wind will not happen, you know and I know. So it is nothing to do with the trade deal because right now from the current government point of view, wind is not favored and they don't want to do wind.

items.statement: Working capital elevated due to delayed payments in public sector projects; expected to remain at current levels
items.quote: working capital requirements today Sudhanshu as long as we keep doing this public sector projects these projects would continue to be at a high level. It may not significantly increase but will remain at this levels.

items.statement: Net cash position of INR1,556 crores as of December 2025; net worth INR8,332 crores
items.quote: Our net cash position is at INR 1,556 crores, further enhancing our financial flexibility and resilience.

items.statement: MNRE formed task force with MoP and state agencies to resolve land, ROW and connectivity issues
items.quote: they formally announced a task force by MNRE by giving the terms of reference which includes MNRE, includes MoP and includes every state nodal agency and other people basically to resolve issues with respect to land and ROW and the connectivity.

items.statement: Record quarterly deliveries of 617 MW in Q3 FY26, highest ever in India
items.quote: Suzlon has set a new benchmark in execution by delivering a record -breaking 617 megawatt in Q3 FY '26, the highest ever quarterly deliveries in India since inception.

items.statement: 9-month deliveries of 1,625 MW surpassed full-year FY25 level of 1,550 MW
items.quote: In 9 months FY '26, deliveries grew 66% to 1,625 megawatt surpassing the full -year FY '25 level of 1,550 megawatt in FY '25.

items.statement: OMS fleet at 15.5+ GW with machine availability consistently above 95%
items.quote: Our OMS business remains strong with 15.5 gigawatt -plus under management in India and machine availability consistently above 95%.

items.statement: SE Forge revenue grew 33% YoY to INR429 crores with EBITDA of INR88 crores in 9M FY26
items.quote: Our forging and foundry business is unlocking its potential, delivering 33% Y -o-Y reven ue growth in nine months to INR429 crores with EBITDA to INR88 crores.

items.statement: Execution delays due to land acquisition, ROW issues, and grid connectivity; 253 MW pre-commissioned awaiting grid
items.quote: For example, this quarter we have a 253 megawatt s of turbines pre-commissioned means they can generate today provided they get connected to the grid.

items.statement: Pre-FY25 execution backlog of 50-60 MW stuck in one Karnataka project due to land issues
items.quote: Pre '25 I think would be somewhere around 50 to 60 megawatts. Talking about pre-FY '25, okay? Sumit Kishore Yes. J.P. Chalasani: So that is what it is that -- be predominantly one project in Karnataka, which is stuck because of land and various things

items.statement: Appointed Paulo Soares as President Europe to drive export growth
items.quote: To accelerate this, we have strengthened our global leadership with the appointment of Paulo Soares as President Europe, ensuring deeper engagement and faster market scaling across key geographies.

items.statement: 5 MW turbine prototype stage; 3.3 MW with revised power curve now selling with lower cost per kWh
items.quote: our 5 megawatt turbine is now getting into the proto stage and that will come at appropriate time. But the thing let me tell you is that the in spite of the fact there is a 5 megawatt turbine launched, our 3.15 megawatt is going significantly. And now we have also introduced started selling 3.3 megawatt with the revised power curve which has a lower cost per kilowatt hour compared to 3.15.

items.statement: AI digitization of OMS targeting 97-98% availability and higher EBITDA margins
items.quote: If today we are at 96.1% of availability, how do we go towards 97, 97.5, 98 is one. Second thing is today I am at 40% EBITDA margin, plus how do I not just sustain can I increase this margin. This is what AI would help me.

items.statement: Calendar 2025 was the strongest year ever for Indian theatrical business with Rs. 13,400 crores gross box office, up 13% YoY and 32% above pre-pandemic levels.
items.quote: Calendar 2025 emerged as the strongest year ever for the Indian theatrical business with highest ever all-India gross box office collections of Rs. 13,400 crores up 13% year-on-year and nearly 32% above pre-pandemic levels.

items.statement: Hindi box office delivered its strongest year ever with collections over Rs. 5,500 crores, representing 18% YoY growth.
items.quote: Original Hindi language films contributed substantially to the growth. Hindi box office delivered its strongest year ever with collections of over Rs. 5,500 crores, representing an 18% year-on-year growth.

items.statement: Hollywood staged a strong recovery in India with Rs. 1,400 crores box office, up 49% YoY.
items.quote: Hollywood also staged a strong recovery in India, delivering its best post-pandemic year with box office collections of Rs. 1,400 crores, up 49% year-on-year, aided by a stronger and more consistent content slate.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 admissions grew 9% YoY to 40.5 million guests.
items.quote: During the quarter, we welcomed 40.5 million guests to our cinemas, representing a growth of 9% year-on-year.

items.statement: Occupancy improved to 28.5% in Q3 FY26 from 25.7% in Q3 FY25.
items.quote: Occupancy improved to about 28.5% compared to 25.7% in Q3 last year, reflecting both the strength of content and the impact of various footfall driving initiatives we have been implementing.

items.statement: Average ticket price and F&B spend per head both increased 4% YoY to Rs. 293 and Rs. 146 respectively.
items.quote: Average ticket price and food and beverage spend per head both increased by 4% year-on-year to Rs. 293 and Rs. 146, reflecting stable consumer spend trends.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 revenue Rs. 1,908 crores, EBITDA Rs. 345 crores, PAT Rs. 115 crores vs Rs. 1,739 crores, Rs. 258 crores, Rs. 68 crores in Q3 FY25.
items.quote: Total revenue for the quarter was Rs. 1,908 crores. EBITDA was Rs. 345 crores and PAT was Rs. 115 crores, as compared to revenue of Rs. 1,739 crores, EBITDA of Rs. 258 crores and PAT of Rs. 68 crores in the same period last year.

items.statement: Added 20 new screens and exited 3 in Q3 FY26; YTD added 62 screens, exited 11; on track for ~100 new screens in FY26.
items.quote: During the quarter, we added 20 new screens while exiting three underperforming screens located in malls that are nearing end of their life cycle. Year-to-date, we have added 62 new screens and exited 11 loss-making screens, and are on track to add nearly 100 new screens in FY 2026.

items.statement: 149 screens signed under capital-light model: 54 FOCO and 95 asset-light.
items.quote: Staying true to our capital-light and scalable growth strategy, we now have 149 screens signed under the capital-light model, of which 54 screens are under the FOCO model and 95 screens are under the asset-light model.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to Rs. 365 crores as of Dec 31, 2025, down over Rs. 1,000 crores since merger.
items.quote: As of December 31, 2025, net debt reduced to Rs. 365 crores, representing more than Rs. 1,000 crores reduction since the merger, driven by strong free cash flows and disciplined capital allocation strategy.

items.statement: Divested entire stake in 4700BC to Marico for Rs. 226.8 crores all-cash consideration.
items.quote: In line with thi s focus, last month, we concluded the divestment of our entire stake in 4700BC premium snacking brand to Marico for an all -cash consideration of Rs. 226.8 crores, further strengthening our balance sheet and moving us closer to negligible net debt levels

items.statement: FY27 screen additions target ~150 screens; CAPEX outlay Rs. 350-400 crores inclusive of new screens, renovations and maintenance.
items.quote: First of all, we will be opening about 96 screens roughly this year. And next year, we are looking at about 150-odd screens to open. And CAPEX intensity, Gaurav, can you just help me out there? Gaurav Sharma: Yes, it will be between Rs. 350 crores to Rs. 400 crores of CAPEX outlay that we are planning for next year, all inclusive, including new screens plus renovations and maintenance

items.statement: ATP and SPH expected to grow ~3.5-4% annually on an even ground.
items.quote: On an even ground, every year w e are looking at about 3.5%, 4% increase in ATP and that would be the trend going forward and so would be the case with SPH as

items.statement: Deferred tax assets expected to be fully utilized over next 3.5-4 years.
items.quote: I think our estimate is that our deferred tax assets will be u tilized fully over the course of next three and a half to four years. So from a tax perspective, we have enough losses to absorb any future tax payouts for the next three to four years

items.statement: Electricity cost down 4% YoY due to solar panel deployment on rooftops; will accelerate further. Rental renegotiations and revenue-share deals to improve rental efficiency.
items.quote: For example, electricity cost is one area where if you notice, we have seen a 4% year-on-year drop because we are deploying solar panels on the rooftops of many of our cinemas, which are on the top floor of the malls. We will accelerate that deployment further. Also, rental renegotiations and seeking discounts and moving to more revenue share kind of deals will further make the overall rental cost

items.statement: Margins at 28% occupancy and 18% EBITDA margin are optimal; slight increase possible but bulk of margin improvement already achieved.
items.quote: I think it's already at a very optimal and healthy level in terms of the margins, if you look at it at 28% occupancy, 18% margins. Having said that, there are still line items in our P&L where we are working towards optimizing.

items.statement: Content cycle well-oiled and synchronized; 2026-27 slate very strong across Hindi, regional, Hollywood; best years ahead post-COVID.
items.quote: The content cycle is pretty much in shape, and one should expect sustenance in terms of occupancies. I would go to the extent of saying that our best years are ahead of us. We have not yet seen our best years post-COVID. 2026, 2027, just on paper looking at the slate is looking like a very, very strong year.

items.statement: Unique visitations grew strongly in CY2025 vs CY2024 and CY2023; Tuesday promotion driving new users.
items.quote: So, we have seen more unique visitations in 2025 calendar versus 2024. There has been a healthy growth. That said, we would not like to get into specifics because this is business-sensitive information. I hope you understand. But yes, there has been a very, very strong noticeable growth in the unique visitations.

items.statement: Over 50% of tickets sold through online channels (aggregators and own apps); full access to customer data at transaction level.
items.quote: I would say this that a substantial portion of more than 50% of our tickets gets sold through the online channels, be it our aggregators or our own digital platforms, the PVR app and the INOX app. So a substantial portion g ets sold through the online channels and data is shared by the aggregators with us

items.statement: 4700BC gourmet popcorn sold in only 50 screens, Rs. 13 crores revenue (<1% of F&B); will continue selling in premium properties, no margin/revenue dent.
items.quote: See, roughly over Rs. 1,800 crores is our revenue on F&B, and 4700BC gourmet popcorn was only being sold in 50 of our screens and 50 of our properties, and represented only Rs. 13 crores of revenue. So it is less than 1%. Having said that, it will continue to sell in our premium properties. S o it will hardly have any dent on our margins or hardly have any dent on our revenues

items.statement: Launched own F&B brands (Dogfather hot dogs, pizzas, French fries); scaling food court JV with Devyani (3 opened, more planned).
items.quote: We have also launched some new brands in food categories where there are limited other third-party brands. For example, on hot dog, we have launched a brand called Dogfather, which is currently being sold in our cinemas, similarly on the pizzas, French fries. And we will continue to nurture them and see if they have potential to scale beyond cinemas as well.

items.statement: CCI VPF matter ongoing, fully cooperating, no material update. Karnataka ticket price cap stayed by High Court, no cap implemented.
items.quote: On VPF CCI matter, the process with CCI is ongoing, and given that it is subjudice, we are fully cooperating with CCI and sharing information. At this point, there is no new material update to share. On Karnataka pricing update, the Karnataka High Court had stayed the state government's order on capping th e ticket prices. The matter is again currently subjudice at the High Court level. And there

items.statement: Monitoring Warner Bros-Netflix development closely; US Senate hearing held, US government reviewing combination seriously.
items.quote: On Warner and Netflix, again, the matter is ongoing. We continue to monitor it closely with our colleagues in North America, Europe and other parts of the country. It's an event which is going to have an impact on the global exhibition industry and, therefore, all exhibitors are looking at the events and the developments in a very close fashion.

items.statement: No guidance on dividend or buyback; Board will decide capital allocation at right time; cash used for debt reduction and growth.
items.quote: I think capital allocation with respect to distribution to shareholders is a decision that the Board will take at the right time. We will not be able to give any guidance on that at this stage. But the cash which is there will be definitely used towards reducing debt as well as funding growth.

items.statement: Scheduled gross debt repayment plus prepayment using surplus cash; gross debt to fall materially by end of FY26.
items.quote: So, one is the scheduled repayment of gross debt, which is largely term within our case. So that will happen. On top of that, we will also prepay some of the gross debt using the surplus cash that we are carrying. So that exercise will take place over the course of the next couple of months. So we are expecting that gross debt levels will also fall materially by the time we finish this financial y

items.statement: Promoter pledge levels stable for some time; no expectation of increase.
items.quote: On the promoter pledge, I think the pledge levels have been pretty sort of at the same level for quite some time. We do not expect that to change, or rather we do not expect that to increase.

items.statement: No plans to impair goodwill on balance sheet.
items.quote: No, there are no such plans as of now.

items.statement: Film distribution business EBITDA margins ~8-9% on revenue; high return on capital, working capital focused.
items.quote: So I think on EBITDA margins, we will be roughly in the range of 8% to 9% overall on the revenue. It's a business where we sort of take distribution rights and it's a working capital focused business, but a very high return on capital kind of business profile.

items.statement: Group targets 12-14% revenue CAGR over next 2-3 years and aims to achieve double-digit EBITDA margin at group level next financial year
items.quote: Overall, at a group level, we are looking at a 12% to 14% revenue growth in the next 2, 3 years. That's what we have stated, and we always strive to really beat that number.

items.statement: India operations expected to grow from FY27 onwards with U.S. trade deal and FTAs with U.K. and EU
items.quote: With the U.S. trade deal and the FTAs with U.K. and EU and the existing trade deals of Japan and Australia, we expect higher volumes, increased sourcing from India and growth in our India operations from 2027 financial year onwards.

items.statement: Guatemala losses to reduce substantially in FY27 and reach breakeven next financial year
items.quote: We are working very aggressively, and we are charting out a plan where Guatemala losses should reduce substantially in FY '27 onwards or it should reach a breakeven in the next financial year itself.

items.statement: Bangladesh apparel unit construction targeted for completion by Q2 FY27; INR66 cr of INR110 cr committed
items.quote: Construction of apparel manufacturing unit is targeted for completion by quarter 2 FY '27. Out of INR110 crores allocated, INR66 crores has already been committed.

items.statement: Sustainable laundry facility in Bangladesh targeted for completion by Q2 FY27; INR51 cr of INR90 cr committed
items.quote: Construction of the laundry facility is targeted for completion by quarter 2 FY '27 out of INR90 crores allocated, INR51 crores has been committed.

items.statement: Bihar capacity expansion completed and commercialization in progress; full allocated capex already incurred
items.quote: Capacity expansion in Bihar is completed and commercialization is in progress. The entire capex, which was allocated has been already committed -- incurred.

items.statement: Solar power installation completed for all 5 plants in India; power generation started
items.quote: Solar power installation is completed for all plants in India and -- all 5 plants in India and power generation has started.

items.statement: India operating at INR1,100 cr annualized run rate with capability to exceed INR1,500-1,600 cr
items.quote: The India business is operating at an annualized revenue run rate of about INR1,100 crores, and we have built up the capability to generate revenues, which can exceed even INR1,500 crores to INR1,600 crores.

items.statement: Bangladesh capacity expansion to add 6 million pieces by Q2 FY27
items.quote: Our capacity expansion plan remains on track for completion by second quarter of financial year '27. This will lift the capacity by about another 6 million pieces in Bangladesh.

items.statement: Bihar facility planned for 900 machines; 500 already installed and bulk production started
items.quote: Bihar, we have planned for 900 machines. As of now, already 500 is already installed. And we are hiring all the people and trained -- most of the people is already getting trained at this point of time, and we have started the bulk production.

items.statement: Vietnam experiencing >15% growth; Indonesia ramping up after factory shift 2 years ago
items.quote: Vietnam, we are experiencing about, I would say, more than the 15% kind of growth at this point of time. And Bangladesh, we had -- sorry, you wanted only Vietnam or Indonesia?

items.statement: Bangladesh operations smooth post regime change; 2 major customers added in Dhaka
items.quote: Since the regime change, our operations have been very smooth in Dhaka. Bangladesh as a country is clocking a year-on-year growth in garment exports, and we expect it to grow on its strength, and we have a mature operation, which is running. 2 major customers just got added in our portfolio in Dhaka.

items.statement: 9M FY26 consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin 9%; 10.1% excluding INR31 cr tariff and INR11 cr ramp-up costs
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA margin stood at 9%, excluding tariff impact of INR31 crores and incremental ramping up cost of new operation of INR11 crores, adjusted EBITDA margin stands at 10.1% for 9 months FY '26.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin 8.3%; 9% excluding tariff and ramp-up costs
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA, excluding ESOP expense at INR97 crores, up by 4.4% year-on-year with a margin at 8.3%. Adjusted EBITDA margin, excluding tariff costs and incremental ramping up cost of new facilities stand at 9%.

items.statement: Standalone 9M FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin 5.5% (up 220 bps YoY); 7.3% excluding INR14 cr tariff cost
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA stand at INR43 crores grew by 64% year-on-year with margin at 5.5%, up by 220 bps year-on-year, mainly due to cost restructuring. Adjusted EBITDA margin, excluding tariff cost of INR14 crores stand at 7.3%.

items.statement: Indonesia EBITDA margin still single digit; expected to reach double digit next year and year after
items.quote: So EBITDA margin will be still in the single digit. We expect it to be double digit in the next year and year after.

items.statement: U.S. tariff reduced from 50% to 18% under bilateral trade deal; penalty tariff waived from Feb 7
items.quote: A major and long-awaited development was the India-U.S. bilateral trade deal, which reduces the tariff from 50% to 18%, significantly enhancing the India's textile export competitiveness.

items.statement: U.S. retailers passing on tariff costs surgically on certain products; slight decrease in buying volumes observed
items.quote: Now this -- what we are seeing is that there is an increase in the U.S. market in terms of price ticket, but it has been done surgically. It is not done across all products across all retailers.

items.statement: India had 12% tariff disadvantage vs Bangladesh for EU/U.K. until FTAs operational; U.K. FTA expected April, EU FTA 2027
items.quote: For an Indian vendor who was competing with the Bangladesh competition, they had a disadvantage of this 10% of additional tariff to European Union and U.K., which from 1st of January has become 12%.

items.statement: Bangladesh order book showing further growth after consolidating 30%+ growth last year
items.quote: Bangladesh operation has well consolidated the last year 30% plus growth and order book is showing now further growth.

items.statement: India seeing positive movement in order books with FTA tailwinds
items.quote: We are seeing a very positive movement in our order books. There are 2 things that was, I would say, if you have to club the problems of India into 2 parts.

items.statement: Long-term credit rating upgraded from ICRA BBB stable (2021) to ICRA A+ stable (2026); short-term rating ICRA A1+
items.quote: We are happy to share that the company has achieved a notable improvement in its credit profile with a long-term credit rating upgraded from ICRA BBB stable in 2021 to ICRA A+ stable in 2026. Concurrently, the short-term rating has advanced to ICRA A1+.

items.statement: India concluded BTAs/FTAs with all major markets (EU, U.S., Japan, U.K., Australia) covering ~$250 bn market
items.quote: India has concluded the BTAs and FTAs negotiations with all major markets that Pear l Global is selling its products to. These are the European Union, U.S., Japan, U.K. and Australia, with a total market for these countries approximately about $250 billion

items.statement: EU-based customers ~17-20% of total revenue; all facilities EU-ready on traceability, ESG, water, solar, waste management
items.quote: as I speak, I think our EU -based customers were already 17% plus or moving towards a 20% kind of thing, if I tal k about total import into the country of So then see this -- most of our production is EU ready

items.statement: Added marquee retailer to portfolio; continuously targeting growing brands gaining market share
items.quote: As I just mentioned in my earlier speech that we have added recently to a very marquee ret ailer in our mix. So we'll continue to add that and look for that opportunity

items.statement: Bangladesh faces competition risk as India ramps up with FTAs; retailers with high Bangladesh exposure may diversify sourcing
items.quote: I don't see an immediate impact on Bangladesh, but yes, there will be this competition as these countries like India and all really ramps up there, then definitely, there should be some competition in Bangladesh, but still some time to -- before that.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 consolidated revenue INR1,170 cr (+14.4% YoY), highest in 5 years; adjusted EBITDA INR97 cr (+4.4% YoY); PAT INR52 cr (+6.8% YoY)
items.quote: For quarter 3 FY '26, total revenue stood at INR 1,170 crores, an increase of 14.4% year-on-year. And this is the highest ever revenue registered in the last 5 years in quarter 3 by Pearl Group.

items.statement: Target to double AUM, income and PAT over next 3 years while preserving asset quality below 1%
items.quote: Over the next 3 years, our objective is clear to double our AUM, income and PAT while preserving best-in-class asset quality.

items.statement: Full-year NIM target of 6% already achieved and will be maintained for FY26
items.quote: In terms of our NIM outlook, we had projected and guided for about a 6% NIM achievement on the full year basis. So we have already achieved the same. So we are going to maintain the same for this year.

items.statement: Full-year cost of borrowing target of 10.5% already achieved; Q3 FY26 at 10.3%
items.quote: Our full year target for this year cost of borrowing, which was given in quarter one of this year was 10.5%. So we have already achieved it and we are at 10.3%.

items.statement: AUM increased to INR 55,082 million, up 16% YoY in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Our Assets Under Management increased to INR 55,082 million, registering 16% year-on-year growth, reflecting steady portfolio expansion across income generation and MSME lending segments.

items.statement: Disbursements for Q3 FY26 stood at INR 10,574 million
items.quote: Disbursements for the quarter stood at INR 10,574 million, reflecting sustained borrower demand and healthy sourcing momentum.

items.statement: 9M FY26 cumulative disbursements at INR 29,180 million, up 21% YoY
items.quote: Cumulative disbursement for nine months FY26 stood at INR 29,180 million, which grew by 21% year-on-year, supported by steady demand across income generation and MSME lending segments and improving productivity across channels.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 total income INR 2,401 million (+18% YoY), NII INR 1,453 million (+19% YoY)
items.quote: Total Income for the quarter increased to INR 2,401 million, registering 18% year-on-year growth, while Net Interest Income rose to INR 1,453 million, up 19% year on year.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 PAT INR 663 million, highest ever quarterly, +29% QoQ and +6% YoY
items.quote: We delivered our highest ever quarterly Profit After Tax of INR 663 million, marking a 29% sequential growth.

items.statement: 9M FY26 total income INR 6,828 million (+18% YoY), NII INR 3,960 million (+18% YoY), PAT INR 1,650 million

items.quote: The standalone EBITDA margin stood at 10.07% in quarter ended December '25 from 12.82% in quarter ended December '24. The decrease is primarily due to onetime claims income recognized amounting to INR37.7 crores in quarter ended December '24.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin target 10-12%; incremental orders above INR14,000-15,000 crores expected to improve margins
items.quote: Margin, what we believe is that to remain in the same range, maybe if we are targeting -- 10% to 12%, that is the target which we are having in our mind.

items.statement: Oil & gas EPC target EBITDA margin at least 10%; currently dragging overall margin due to lease model and low revenue base
items.quote: See that has to be basically tested, but we are targeting at least 10% kind of margin so far.

items.statement: No capex planned for oil & gas EPC; equipment taken on lease; capex only if order visibility improves
items.quote: No, no. It's totally different set of machineries to be utilized. But so far, we have not targeted any capex, unless until we have some sort of visibility out to -- in terms of our order intake and all that.

items.statement: Standalone working capital days 93 at end Dec'25 vs 117 at end FY25; decrease due to lower SPV debtor days; standalone trade receivables INR1,614 crores (incl INR1,038 crores HAM debtors); unbilled revenue INR851 crores
items.quote: The working capital in days at the end of December '25 is 93 days as compared to 117 days at the end of fiscal '25. The decrease is primarily on account of decrease in SPV debtor days.

items.statement: Standalone debt repaid INR262 crores in Q3; standalone debt/equity 0.03x (borrowings INR244 crores); consolidated debt/equity 0.68x (borrowings INR6,281 crores)
items.quote: During the quarter, the company has repaid the debt of INR262 crores, which has resulted in improved debt equity ratio to 0.03, which is one of the best in the sector.

items.statement: Equity infusion Q4 FY26 target INR500 crores for HAM, BOT, T&D, BESS, ropeway; balance equity commitment INR3,044 crores as of Dec'25
items.quote: The balance equity contribution required to be made from our operational HAM or BOT projects is INR3,044 crores, of which we are expecting a contribution of approximately INR500 crores in quarter 4 of current fiscal.

items.statement: InvIT transfer: targeting 3 assets in current quarter, 4-5 assets in FY27 subject to approvals
items.quote: So for current quarter, we are having target -- I mean, 3 at least, assets which we are targeting, subject to the necessary approval we are having in place. And next financial year, again, we'll be having around 4 to 5 assets, which we'll be transferring eventually to that InvIT.

items.statement: NHAI MCA for BOT under modification; finalization expected in 15 days to 2 months; projects may be bid in March; execution from FY27 Q2-Q3 onwards
items.quote: That is under modification and maybe in next 15 days or next, I would say, 1 or 2 months at max probably. And maybe even during the month of March itself, we may see that some projects coming in for participation and for bidding.

items.statement: Government shifting from HAM to BOT toll model; BOT MCA tweaked based on industry feedback; more favorable for EPC-graduated developers
items.quote: It is -- that the government is shifting their strength from HAM to BOT -- right, BOT toll mode. And for that, actually, we need full MCA also, that model concession agreement.

items.statement: Agra BOT project appointed date delayed due to land compensation issues; expected resolution in couple of months; revenue booking from FY27 Q1
items.quote: Some land compensation issue is going on over there. And maybe next couple of months, it would be settled. Once they get the compensation, we'll be having the appointed date, and we are fully ready with our mobilization and shipments over there.

items.statement: MSRDC projects (INR4,300 crores) likely to be cancelled and retendered due to new alignment; status unchanged from last call
items.quote: Because so far, I mean, what we believe is that because of the new alignment, that would be cancelled and they would be retendering and all that.

items.statement: NHAI debt/equity fallen from 50% (FY22) to 20% (FY25); fiscal headroom for INR8 lakh crore project pipeline FY26-28 including tunnels
items.quote: NHAI debt -to-equity ratio has fallen from about 50% in financial year '22 to around 20% in financial year '25, creating fiscal headroom to support more than INR8 lakh crore project pipeline in our financial year '26 to '28, including tunnels of significant amounts.

items.statement: Diversification into oil & gas EPC (subsea pipeline, platform modification/erection), power transmission, railways, metro, hydro tunnelling, logistics warehousing, BESS
items.quote: We are into Oil and Gas EPC where we are laying pipeline to the -- subsea pipeline we are laying, right? And we are platform modification and platform erection in the subsea -- in the sea side, right, offshore side.

items.statement: Oil & gas EPC currently executing INR2,000 crores orders via association with existing company; forming subsidiary to bid directly for ONGC etc.; target INR20,000 crores bidding, INR4,000-5,000 crores wins in FY27
items.quote: So -- and going forward, we will be directly bidding into -- we'll be participating directly with ONGC or the client who are coming up with these orders, right? So -- and when we'll be participating directly, we'll be targeting around INR20,000 crores of orders, right, where we target to participate.

name: Aptus Value Housing Finance India Ltd

items.statement: KFC store opening guidance of 60-80 new stores per year going forward
items.quote: from an expansion perspective, we opened 60 stores in the calendar year, and we had called out that going forward also 60 to 80 is the range that we believe, these number of new stores we should be opening.

items.statement: Merger process expected to take around 12 months to become effective
items.quote: From now, it could be maybe around 12 months for the merger to become effective.

items.statement: KFC SSSG was 1% in Q3 FY26 and trending above that in January
items.quote: So for the quarter, we ended up at an SSSG of 1%. And in January, we are trending above that number for the moment.

items.statement: Sri Lanka SSSG was 11% in Q3 FY26
items.quote: SSSG was up by 11%, backed by a healthy transaction growth as well.

items.statement: KFC restaurant EBITDA margin improved to 18.8% in Q3 FY26, up 60 bps YoY
items.quote: Gross margin was up by 40 basis points over last year, and this improvement was on account of discount reduction and value offer construct rationalization. This, along with the cost efficiencies meant that we actually improved our restaurant EBITDA over last year by 60 basis points. It came at 18.8%.

items.statement: Pizza Hut restaurant EBITDA margin was -3.1% in Q3 FY26 due to negative operating leverage
items.quote: And while restaurant EBITDA came in at minus 3.1% majorly on account of the negative leverage or negative operating leverage on account of negative SSSG.

items.statement: Sri Lanka restaurant EBITDA margin was 16.7% in Q3 FY26, down 110 bps due to minimum wage increase and cyclone costs
items.quote: The growth which we see in terms of absolute EBITDA, restaurant EBITDA is 7% in LKR terms and 8% in INR terms. Ho wever, there was a drop in terms of margin percentage, 110 basis points drop. This was mainly on account of significant increase in minimum wages, which that country has seen. And also Q3, in particular, had cyclone-related cost impact as well

items.statement: Added 31 stores in Q3 FY26: 27 KFC, 1 Pizza Hut India, 3 Pizza Hut Sri Lanka; total store count 1,028
items.quote: We added a total of 31 stores in this quarter, 27 KFCs, 1 Pizza Hut in India, 3 Pizza Hut in Sri Lanka. In Pizza Hut, over the calendar year, we added a total of 0 stores. So whatever stores that we added, we also closed an equal number of stores. And our count as of 31st December stands at 1,028.

items.statement: KFC opened 60 stores in calendar year 2025
items.quote: Calendar year '25 saw us adding 60 restaurants for the year.

items.statement: Sri Lanka opened 7 stores in CY25 and plans similar pace in CY26
items.quote: We also opened 7 stores in CY '25, and this is the pace that we think we should be able to continue in CY '26 also.

items.statement: KFC INR 99 Chicken Krisper Meal pilot in 25% of stores driving dine-in and takeaway traction
items.quote: And in about 1/3 of our estate have piloted a Chicken Krisper Meal for INR 99 in dine-in and takeaway channels in about 25% of the stores. And we are seeing good traction on the dine-in and takeaway channel, which is driving overall SSSG also.

items.statement: INR 99 offer expected to be gross margin dilutive by 50-60 bps from current levels
items.quote: Yes, this particular promotion would be dilutive on gross margins, but I don't see an impact beyond 50 basis points to 60 basis points from current level in terms of gross margin.

items.statement: Pizza Hut delivery credentials improved to above 4 rating on Swiggy/Zomato backed by Dragontail tool
items.quote: whether it is the delivery credentials on Swiggy and Zomato, which used to be around 3.5, now gone above 4, backed by our Dragontail tool, which is helping us drive deliver hot and fresh pizzas.

items.statement: CCI approval for merger expected in 3-6 months, enabling closer coordination on Pizza Hut strategy
items.quote: once the CCI approval comes in, which could be anywhere between now and let's say, maybe around 3 to 6 months, one can expect a bit more closer coordinati on on some of the strategy points

items.statement: Consolidated adjusted PBT before exception was INR 24 crores (2.9%) in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Our consol adjusted PBT before exception was INR 24 crores or 2.9%.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue was INR 811 crores with 7% YoY growth in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Our total revenue for the quarter was INR 811 crores with a 7% growth year-on-year.

items.statement: Consolidated restaurant EBITDA grew 5% YoY but margin declined 40 bps to 15% in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Our consolidated restaurant EBITDA grew 5% year-on-year. Margin was at 15%, which is down 40% year-on-year.

items.statement: KFC revenue grew 11% YoY in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Revenue for KFC grew by 11%.

items.statement: Pizza Hut revenue declined 11% YoY in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Pizza Hut declined by 11%.

items.statement: Sri Lanka revenue grew 15% YoY in INR terms in Q3 FY26
items.quote: overall revenue in terms of LKR grew by 15% in terms of INR grew by 16%.

items.statement: Pizza Hut brand revival dependent on CCI approval and alignment with Devyani for joint marketing strategy
items.quote: I think for Pizza Hut, it would be important that both the franchisee partners come together and decide on a way forward. And hopefully, that can happen sooner once the CCI approval comes into the picture.

items.statement: Achieved DJSI ESG rating score of 73/100 for 2025, ranked top 3 QSR globally and #1 in India
items.quote: We've got a global ESG rating score of 73 on 100. And our key highlights are that we are indisputably the number 1 QSR brand in the country and top 3 in the world.

items.statement: Volume guidance for FY26 is 5.5 lakh tons plus/minus 5-10%
items.quote: So basically, we have given our guidance of 5.5 lakh tons. So I'll be -- plus/minus 5%, 10%, we'll be there in that range.

items.statement: FY27 volume target of 6.5 lakh tons at 65% utilization of 1.05 million ton capacity
items.quote: Yes, because with this new capacity of 1.05, we do a 65% utilization. So 6.5 lakh tons is quite conservatively, we'll be achieving this.

items.statement: Target 25% year-on-year volume growth for next 6-7 years
items.quote: So I -- at Hi-Tech, we feel confident that 20%, 25% volume growth we can achieve for next 6, 7 years at least.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton outlook of INR4,000 from Q4 onwards
items.quote: And Q4 onwards, INR4,000 per ton is a realistic number that we are looking at.

items.statement: Medium-term EBITDA per ton operating range of INR4,000-4,500 excluding price volatility
items.quote: we are definitely between -- if you leave the price volatility, we are operating between INR4,000 to INR4,500 per ton.

items.statement: Export volume target of 10% of total volumes
items.quote: And our ultimate goal is to take our export volume to 10%. This is our target, and we are working on that.

items.statement: Value-added product mix target of 42-43% by end of FY26 and 50% by end of FY27
items.quote: So we are taking this to 42%, 43% by end of this year, and it will gradually move up to 50% in the coming years.

items.statement: Capex of INR500-600 crores for additional 1 million ton capacity, half already in CWIP
items.quote: And the total capex is between INR500 crores to INR600 crores for this incremental capacity. And half of it is already under capital work in progress.

items.statement: Commercial production started at Sanand Unit II Phase 2 adding 1 lakh tons annual capacity
items.quote: I'm glad to share that commercial production has commenced at Sanand Unit II Phase 2, adding 1 lakh tons of annual capacity.

items.statement: Commercial production started at greenfield Jammu facility with 80,000 tons annual capacity focused on value-added products
items.quote: Further, the commercial production has commenced at our greenfield Jammu facility with an annual capacity of 80,000 tons, primarily focused on value-added and higher-margin products.

items.statement: Sikandrabad UP greenfield facility commissioned, awaiting compliance clearance to start operations
items.quote: Additionally, our Greenfield facility at Sikandrabad, UP is expected to commence operations at any time.

items.statement: Total installed capacity reached 1 million tons, targeting 2 million tons by FY28-FY29
items.quote: With these expansions, the company reached -- the company reaches to 1 million tons installed capacity and is actively gearing up for the next phase of expansion towards 2 million tons

items.statement: Hindupur Telangana 2.5 lakh ton capacity expected by end of FY27
items.quote: That is almost 2.5 lakh ton capacity. And we are coming -- we will be coming with this capacity by end of FY '27.

items.statement: Exit capacity for FY26 at 1.05 million tons
items.quote: It will be 1.05 million tons.

items.statement: Current order book stands at INR200-250 crores including EPC, solar, export and institutional orders
items.quote: Yes. So currently, the order book stands between INR200 crores to INR250 crores. This comprises of all our large EPC orders, our solar orders and export orders and some institutional.

items.statement: Strong demand outlook driven by government infrastructure spending, private investment, urbanization, renewable energy and industrial development
items.quote: Government-led infrastructure spending, increased private sector investments, rapid urbanization, renewable energy focus and ongoing industrial development continue to support sustained demand for steel pipes and tubes.

items.statement: Jal Jeevan Mission orders subdued this year but strong pipeline expected in FY27 for ERW galvanized tubes
items.quote: But now what we are lately hearing is the allocation in the current budget remains the same. And we are -- what we are talking with the various departments, we see in FY '27, there will be a strong order pipeline in the Jal Jeevan segment, especially for our ERW tube segment for galvanized product.

items.statement: Steel prices declined INR2,500 per ton in Q3 but reversed after 12% safeguard duty on Dec 30, 2025
items.quote: So the steel prices declined by almost INR2,500 per ton in this quarter -- in Q3. However, after this introduction of safeguard duty on the 30th of December, the steel prices have bounced back.

items.statement: Raw material price changes passed through with 7-10 day lag
items.quote: The transmission of prices, there may be a lag of 7 to 10 days, but then eventually, whatever price decrease or increase is generally a pass-through.

items.statement: Value-added products currently 37% of sales, margin INR4,500-5,000 per ton vs regular INR2,500-3,000 per ton
items.quote: So yes, the current value-added products contribution is 37%. And we hope to -- with this new Jammu facility and our new galvanizing facilities in various plants.

items.statement: New capacities focused on value-added products: color-coated at Jammu, solar top tubes in Gujarat, galvanized products at other locations
items.quote: So whatever new -- the capacities are coming, they are focused towards value-added products like color-coated at Jammu, our solar top tubes in Gujarat and galvanized products in the other locations.

items.statement: Exported to 28 countries in last year, Europe largest market, 6,000-7,000 tons in Q3, volumes to increase significantly in Q4
items.quote: In this quarter, we have done almost 6,000 to 7,000 tons of export volume. And -- in the coming quarters, it is going to go up

items.statement: U.S.-India trade deal and EU-India trade pact expected to open export opportunities and improve competitiveness
items.quote: The U.S.-India trade deal is expected to open new opportunities, enhance market access and support long-term volume growth. Similarly, on the EU India trade pack, it is significantly positive as it is likely to improve export competitiveness, reduce trade barriers and create meaningful opportunities for Indian manufacturers

items.statement: Long-term supply MOUs signed in Q3 with SAIL, ArcelorMittal, Tata Steel and NMDC for raw material security
items.quote: So we got into these supply contracts with these -- with our current suppliers, which are Steel Authority of India Limited, ArcelorMittal, Tata and NMDC.

items.statement: Working capital improvement trend continuing from FY24-FY25 into FY26
items.quote: If you see in FY '24, FY '25, there is a good improvement in the working capital. And hopefully, in FY '26 also, that trend will continue.

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA INR42 crores up 4% YoY, PAT down 9% YoY to INR17 crores due to HRC price correction from imports
items.value: INR42 crores EBITDA, INR17 crores PAT
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR42 crores, registering a 4% year-on-year increase from INR40 crores in Q3 FY '25. However, profitability during the quarter was a little impacted with profit after tax declining by 9% year-on-year to INR17 crores compared to INR19 crores in the same period last year.

items.statement: 9M FY26 EBITDA INR127 crores vs INR125 crores in 9M FY25, stable despite price volatility
items.quote: EBITDA for the 9 months stood at INR127 crores compared to INR125 crores in the corresponding period last year, reflecting stable operational performance despite price volatility and margin pressure during parts of the year.

items.statement: 12% safeguard duty imposed Dec 30, 2025 stabilized domestic steel prices and stopped dumping for 3 years
items.quote: Importantly, this trend has reversed following the government's introduction of a 12% safeguard duty on 30th December 2025, which helped in stabilizing the domestic steel prices, restoring pricing discipline and margin improvement.

items.statement: Order book reached all-time high of INR1,868 crores
items.quote: Our order book has reached an all-time high of INR1,868 crores, largest in the history of Data Patterns, underscoring our strong execution capabilities, deep domain expertise and growing relevance within the defence ecosystem.

items.statement: Orders negotiated but not awarded stand at INR1,100 crores expected to convert in 1-2 months
items.quote: I think these contracts should happen in the next 1 to 2 months' time because these are only document work which has to be done in time.

items.statement: Additional INR500-600 crores of contracts expected to be signed in next 2-3 months
items.quote: We also expect to sign more contracts in the next 2 to 3 months' time, probably another INR500 crores, INR600 crores of contracts, which can get signed.

items.statement: Committed to 20-25% revenue growth over medium term with healthy EBITDA margins and net debt-free balance sheet
items.quote: We remain committed to delivering 20% to 25% revenue growth over the medium term, maintaining healthy EBITDA margins and preserving our net debt-free balance sheet.

items.statement: Confident of achieving full year revenue and EBITDA margin guidance
items.quote: With a record order book, strong execution visibility and disciplined cost management, we remain confident of achieving the full year revenue and EBITDA margin guidance.

items.statement: EBITDA margin sustained at 44% in Q3 FY26, driven by in-house IP and favourable execution mix
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR78 crores, up 44% year -on-year with EBITDA margins sustained at a healthy 44%.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to remain similar to historical levels, varying by contract mix
items.quote: So, largely, the EBITDA margin should be similar to what we've been presenting till date.

items.statement: Strong policy tailwinds from Union Budget with increased capital procurement for radars, EW systems, missiles and advanced electronics
items.quote: The sharp rise in allocations for other equipment, including radars, electronic warfare systems, missiles and advanced electronics clearly signals a focus on new age defence technologies.

items.statement: Export order book healthy at ~INR63 crores; building export-focused team and targeting EU and US markets with IP-driven products
items.quote: Our export order book remains healthy at approximately INR63 crores, and export continue to evolve as an important pillar of our long -term growth strategy.

items.statement: Export strategy includes co-investment, faster delivery timelines, lower development cost vs Europe; formal export team to be built early next year
items.quote: We need to -- these are early days. We need to actually do a lot more work in the export market, put a team together and drive the export market on a consistent basis to see th at 2, 3 years down the line, we have a steady business, which can scale.

items.statement: Revenue mix: 57% production, 37% development in 9M FY26
items.quote: Production contributes highest to the revenues at 57 percentage, followed by development at 37 percentage.

items.statement: BrahMos seeker trials completed; production orders expected from FY26-27; also developing missile-to-missile higher band seeker
items.quote: We've completed the seeker trials. We've got a development contract with marginal differences, which go into production orders. We'll be delivering it in the next 1 or 2 months' time ahead of schedule.

items.statement: Developing flight control radar and modern EW suite with INR15,000-20,000 crores TAM; user trials ongoing
items.quote: We've taken money for QIP money to invest in large development activities , which can give business of around INR15,000 crores to INR20,000 crores of potential revenue. One is the flight control radar. Second is the modern EW suite.

items.statement: Partnered with Bharat Forge for AMCA production bid; shortlisted among three for RFP
items.quote: We have partnered with Bharat Forge to bid for the AMCA production and are one of the three shortlisted to get the RFP.

items.statement: Developing smart cockpit, avionics, IRST and missile approach warning systems for LCA Mark 2 and AMCA
items.quote: We're actively involved in developing the smart cockpit and avionics systems for LCA Mark 2, which we believe will be adopted for AMCA. We're also offering the advanced sensors like infrared search and track and missile approach warning system for LCA Mark 2 in partnership with a European partner Made in India content.

items.statement: Investing in additional factory coming up in 1-2 years with large space for production and design; test equipment designed in-house enables quick scaling
items.quote: We're also putting up additional factory, which is going to come up in the next one to 2 years' time with a large space available for production as well as design.

items.statement: Working capital days improved from 428 (Mar'25) to 340 (Dec'25); target 270-300 days over 3-5 years
items.quote: it was around 428 days in March. It has come down to -- we have not published the b alance sheet numbers for December. But internally, it has come down to 340 days

items.statement: Large development contract receivables expected to be collected in 2-4 months, recharging cash position
items.quote: The debtor situation has been extended, but we are expecting all the cash to come in the next 3 to 4 months' time. And that will again take care of the cash on hand situation you talked about.

items.statement: Net debt-free; zero net borrowing from banks, only non-fund based limits (bank guarantees) used
items.quote: And we also get advance against all these contracts help us. So, the net borrowing from banks is actually zero. We only work on bank guarantees . Non-fund limits is what we're working on.

items.statement: ~1,100 engineers currently; recruiting another 150 this year to build competency for export and domestic opportunities
items.quote: We have done about 1,100 engineers, recruiting another 150 this year. So, we are building a competency skill, which will be useful in these areas.

items.statement: Order pipeline potential of $2-3 billion from current product portfolio over next couple of years
items.quote: Products we develop now, we can expect another $2 billion to $3 billion of order pipeline and capability.

items.statement: Government-driven order delays are inherent; building product bouquet to mitigate impact on scaling ambitions
items.quote: There has been some delays. But anyway, that's part of the problem with government-driven orders. We know they're going to be. So , we need to have a bouquet of products to see that the areas are not a ffecting our scaling ambitions and revenue growth as we plan to be.

items.statement: Differentiation through full-system IP ownership, not subsystem integration; avoid L1-driven commodity contracts
items.quote: We need to differentiate ourselves from competition. That's the only way we will get differential treatment. That's one. Second is though there are a number of companies talking radars and EW and all that. We are not developing all the portions of the radars.

items.statement: UK export business provides predictable monthly delivery model; seeking similar recurring revenue streams
items.quote: Whatever orders we're getting from UK, it's a predictable business. They give you a long -term order, which is monthly deliveries. We want the part portion of our turnover to at least be that so that we can tabularize these, these ups and downs or unpredictability in the market.

items.statement: Make in India mandate and indigenization push align with company's IP-driven approach; government policy supports domestic content
items.quote: The recent Union budget has also reinforced the government's long -term commitment to defence modernization and indigenization with a meaningful increase in capital procurement.

items.statement: Exploring civil aviation electronics with OEMs; early stage, 1-4 years before predictable revenue model
items.quote: It's very early stage, Jayakanth. We can't comment on it now. We're exploring opportunities and trying to work with one or two OEMs to see whether we can do some products for them.

items.statement: Ordered 3 new high-capacity high-speed wagons and swapped 3 old rakes; total rakes to reach 37 by May-June 2025
items.quote: We've also swap ped 3 of the old capacity rakes for 3 high -capacity rakes. So by the end of May, June, we would be at 37 rakes

items.statement: Annual capex guidance of INR100-150 crores; 75-80% debt financed; also pursuing build-to-suit model
items.quote: Majority would be debt, about, say, 75%, 80% would be debt. But we'll also be looking at build- to-suit expansion

items.statement: Indore ICD project operational within 2 years with 120,000 TEUs/year capacity; land possession secured
items.quote: So it should be operational within 2 years, and we're looking at about 120,000 TEUs per year capacity at the terminal.

items.statement: Snowman warehousing margins declined due to mix shift to chilled/dry storage and Park & Pay model; dry storage rates improving from INR600-700 to INR850-1000 per pallet
items.quote: The dry storage is typically to address some of our customers who are into quick commerce or typically into QSR business or coffee chains. And thus, the margins are lesser with ample availability of dry warehousing around.

items.statement: Snowman targeting 7-8 year payback on warehouses; replacement costs for chillers/compressors not in first 7-8 years
items.quote: What we try to aim for is about a 7 to 8 year payback. It is slightly longer than -- but capex costs have gone up in the last few years.

items.statement: Expecting export volume boost from US and EU trade deals; US currently 25% of export volumes, EU 10%
items.quote: So we are expecting a major traction, especially in the exports of handicrafts, textiles, leather and chemicals. And right now, we have 25% of U.S. sales of the total volume kitty we have export.

items.statement: Current rail capacity can handle 4x volumes; CFS utilization can increase 20-30%; adding rakes for volume growth
items.quote: So our capacity at our terminals on the rail side is that we can go 4x of our volume with the current land bank. Even on the CFS side, we can still increase our utilization by, say, 20%, 30%.

items.statement: DFC last connection to JNPT expected by end March 2025; double stacking to increase 2-3%; some Mundra volumes may shift to JNPT
items.quote: Yes. So the last connection to JNPT DFC corridor is expected by end of March. And once this gets completed, so we are expecting some volume to get moving.

items.statement: Consolidated net debt reached zero in January 2025; INR140 crores cash on hand after Indore land purchase; gross debt ~INR200 crores without Snowman
items.quote: So INR140 crores is the cash in hand, but there is a gross debt still in the books, but the number that you're seeing is probably with the Snowman figures as well.

items.statement: Declared one-time special dividend after achieving net debt-free status on standalone basis; not a recurring annual dividend
items.quote: We had touched a surplus like we had crossed the net debt figur e on a consolidated basis without Snowman for the first time in the company. And we have healthy cash flows. We're sitting on about INR140 crores as on date

items.statement: Indore land vetted with direct registry, no aggregator, no encroachment; Benami issues unlikely to recur
items.quote: We've done proper due diligence. We've done direct registry. We've not used any aggregator. We've gone and seen the sites to see that there's no encroachment.

items.statement: Snowman securing price hikes at contract renewals; able to pass on cost increases in last 5-6 months
items.quote: Yes, we are able to get those price hikes in all our last contracts, which have been done in last 5 to 6 months, we have got the price hike.

items.statement: Will report only company-wide EBITDA per TEU going forward; provided 2 years historical comparable data in investor presentation
items.quote: So as of this quarter, and we announced it last quarter as well that we won't be giving a split between the segments anymore. We will just be reporting a company-wide EBITDA per TEU.

items.statement: Scrap paper import volumes in North India stable at lower level vs peak 2 years ago; no operations on Eastern DFC
items.quote: It's been on a similar trend for the last year. 2 years ago, there was a dip, and it recovered slightly. But if you compare it with at its peak, then it's gone down still.

items.statement: Snowman warehousing mix shifted from predominantly frozen to include chilled/dry for QSR/quick commerce customers; dry storage in same facilities
