items.statement: Government allocation of INR 3.1 lakh crores for highways, projected doubling of toll collection from INR 55,000 crores to INR 1.4 lakh crores within two years
items.quote: India's toll collection is projected to surge from INR 55,000 crores to INR 1.4 lakhs crores within two years. And the government is very much focused on expansion, highway construction, wider tollway , coverage and fast-track adoption.

items.statement: INR 1.87 lakh crores allocated to NHAI for FY27 for National Highway construction, especially Greenfield Express Corridors
items.quote: NH AI has been allocated INR 1.87 lakh crores FY27 for the construction of National Highways, especially Greenfield Express Corridor.

items.statement: Kaza Fee Plaza on NH16 secured for INR 328.8 crores, largest tollway collection mandate in company history
items.quote: We secured the largest tollway collection mandate in our history, the INR 328.8 crores Kaza Fee Plaza on NH16 in Andhra Pradesh.

items.statement: Kaza toll plaza expected to generate approximately INR 1 crore per day average collection, translating to INR 30-31 crores per month
items.quote: From Kaza, we are expecting a collection of about approximately an average of INR 1 crores per day. So, you can amount it up to INR 30 crores to INR 31 crores per month.

items.statement: EPC working capital cycle approximately 3 months, tollway collection cycle 1-2 months
items.quote: Working capital cycle for EPC is almost 3 months. And in toll, almost 1 to 2 months.

items.statement: Customer mix remains robust with about 77% government clients ensuring predictable payments and strong cash flow security
items.quote: Our customer mix remains robust, about 77% of government, ensuring predictable payments and strong cash flow security.

items.statement: High value toll orders have less competition due to fewer NHAI registered contractors capable of tendering for such contract values
items.quote: For high value toll orders, there is less competition. That is because NHAI has very less registered contractors which can actually tender for these kinds of contract values.

items.statement: Diversifying into renewable EPC, EV charging infrastructure, ropeway operations, and ancillary commercial services at toll plazas
items.quote: Operationally, we are building adjacencies across renewable EPC, EV charging infrastructure, ropeway operations and collections and ancillary commercial services at tollway plazas, such as warehousing, fuel stations, retail and commuter amenities.

items.statement: Real estate strategy focusing on hospitality and commercial leasing to create recurring annuity-style income from owned land assets
items.quote: I think we are looking at two major fronts. One would be hospitality. Why hospitality? Because I think given the wedding industry in India is one of the biggest in the world and more and more the spending on w eddings has been increased year -on-year, you can see the trend.

items.statement: Tollway collection order book executable within one year; INR 550 crores toll orders to be completed by next year, INR 250 crores EPC orders executable in FY27
items.quote: Sir, the tenders that we get in the toll business, we have to complete them in a n year. So, for example, we have to complete INR 550 crores work orders in tolls by next year. And we have INR 630 crores work orders in EPC, out of which we will complete INR 250 crores in FY27.

items.statement: Approximately INR 750-800 crores of current order book executable in near term with new contracts to be executed as won
items.quote: Overall, we have approximately INR 750-800 orders in hand that are executable. And f urther new contracts that we will get next year, we will execute them as well.

items.statement: Government shifting from BOT model to public-funded EPC mode for highway construction, creating more tollway collection opportunities for operators
items.quote: Now, the government is allocating a lot of projects under E PC mode. So, after the completion of the project, it directly comes under public-funded tolls.

items.statement: Geographic expansion into Gujarat, Rajasthan, Northeast, evaluating entry into Jammu & Kashmir and Kerala to reduce concentration risk
items.quote: Geographically, we are expanding into Gujarat, Rajasthan and the wider Northeast, while evaluating selective entry into Jammu and Kashmir and Kerala. This reduces concentration risk and broadens our addressable market.

items.statement: Targeting minimum 20-30% revenue contribution from new states in near future
items.quote: But we are looking at least a minimum of 20 % to 30% contribution from different states in the near future.

items.statement: Open to partnerships and JVs for new verticals like renewable energy to leverage external expertise
items.quote: Definitely. I mean, the good part about this is that we would love to partner up with people who have great experience. We are always open to connect with people to broaden our horizons and always to learn and impart something that we have learned previously.

items.statement: Toll plaza selection considers growth potential, local issues, weather risks, and geographic diversification to counter seasonal traffic downtrends
items.quote: So, that is how we try to select the tolls and then we also try to create a balance. So, let's say, if a toll collection goes down in the winter due to fog in one particular state, then we also try to take up a toll in other parts of India where there is no downtrend during the winter season.

items.statement: Multi-Lane Free-Flow tolling system expected to benefit business by reducing manpower requirements and increasing efficiency and margins
items.quote: So, government only aims to ease the flow of the tolls. And in fact, for that matter, we will require less manpower at tolls, which will increase our efficiency and margins. So , I think we are on the benefit side of that MLFF strategy.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 expected to be very significant with good turnover and growth in margins due to strong toll collection seasonality
items.quote: So, we expect Q1 FY27 will be very good because in toll business the profitability and collection in Q1 is strong. We expect that in the coming time that Q1 FY27 will be the best

items.statement: IPO funds being deployed according to policy for growth in tollway operations and new infrastructure projects
items.quote: Our target is to enter the top 10 tollways in India because there is less level of competition. So , the fund which we got from IPO , the policy which was there we are moving forward.

items.statement: Full-year revenue growth guidance of 32% to 35% for FY26
items.quote: we will for a full year guidance we will grow in the range of 32% to probably 35% this year, with strong growth coming in both in the online as well as offline and our commitment to continue to grow in both these segments.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 Pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin at 20.2% with PAT margin at 9%
items.quote: Pre-Ind AS EBITDA of INR219 crores translating to 20.2% margin. A PAT of INR102 crores equivalent of 9% and this is in spite of the INR23 crores of one-time expense that we booked in this quarter related to you know the changes in the Labor Code and IPO expenses which we just concluded in on 18th of November.

items.statement: Online segment grew 38% YoY, offline grew 26% YoY in Q3 FY26
items.quote: In terms of our breakup of our online and offline segment, our online segment grew at, now contributes almost like 51% and grew at 38% year-over-year. Offline grew 26% year-over-year and contributes at 46% and others contribute 3%.

items.statement: Nine-month revenue of INR2,980 crores surpassed full-year FY25 revenue of INR2,886 crores
items.quote: Revenue was clocked at INR2,980 crores, a 31% year-over-year increase and surpassed the full year revenue of last year of INR2,886 crores.

items.statement: Planning 70 new offline centers next year with INR200 crores outlay
items.quote: We will continue to invest in opening centers. We are looking at 70 centers next year with an outlay of INR200 crores.

items.statement: Three new categories (CLAT, NEET PG, IIT JAM) contributed INR32 crores in 9M FY26
items.quote: There are three additional categories now this time we have reported. So we used to report 13 categories but now we had three new categories that crossed the annual collections of INR10 crores, that is CLAT, NEET PG and IIT JAM. These three categories put together this year for the first nine months have contributed INR32 crores and we will continue to invest in these new categories to actually, t

items.statement: State boards vertical launched June 2025 scaled to 175,000 paid learners with INR22 crores revenue in 9M FY26
items.quote: The second category that we wanted to talk about today are state boards. There are almost like 6 crores kids studying in state boards exams across India and this vertical was launched in June '25 and we've scaled to 175,000 paid learners with a revenue of INR22 crores for the first nine months.

items.statement: Vernacular batches in five regional languages enrolled 94,000 paid students with INR24 crores revenue in 9M FY26
items.quote: The third key category online expansion that we are seeing is on the vernacular side. We've started batches in five regional languages and enrolled 94,000 paid students in the first nine months with a revenue of INR24 crores.

items.statement: Sarrthi acquisition doubled revenue YoY; Q3 revenue INR22 crores, EBITDA INR15 crores
items.value: INR22 crores revenue, INR15 crores EBITDA
items.quote: On like-to-like basis Sarrthi doubled its revenue for nine months for this year as compared to last year. This quarter Sarrthi reported revenues of INR22 crores and EBITDA of INR15 crores, this is what we consolidated in our books and we can now surely say that our overall UPSC practice is now the market leader in terms of the overall, all our competition as well.

items.statement: Utkarsh Classes turned to 6% pre-Ind AS EBITDA from negative last year
items.quote: Utkarsh Classes had a great year in reimagining the entire state exams business, they reported 6% pre-Ind AS EBITDA against a negative for last year and we will see significant amount of cost leverage continue to come in that business.

items.statement: Xylem acquisition revenue grew from INR90 crores to INR330-340 crores run rate; opened 13 new centers
items.quote: Also in Xylem our test prep business in Kerala that has been growing this year they will close the year at roughly around INR330 to INR340 crores of revenue top line. When we bought the acquisition, I think they were INR90 crores in top line. We opened 13 new centers in Xylem supplementing our vernacular reach in southern states and we see that helping us to build our vision of a formidable player

items.statement: Planning to announce a couple of M&As in next two quarters; evaluating both offline and online domestic assets
items.quote: In terms of within India, yes, we are evaluating both offline and online assets and we will announce a couple of M&As in the next two quarters as well. But the thesis here is the synergies with the group.

items.statement: Treasury stands at INR5,000 crores post IPO fresh issue of INR3,100 crores; generated INR600 crores operating cash flow in 9M
items.quote: In terms of our treasury, our treasury now stands at INR5,000 crores post our IPO of INR3,100 crores which was the fresh issue that we did. We generated almost INR600 crores from cash flow from operations in the first nine months.

items.statement: Greenfield schools use build-to-suit lease model (9-year leases), asset-light approach
items.quote: And what I mentioned about greenfield, four such schools are happening, and in this, the land and property is a build-to-suit model where the owner is constructing the school as per our need and we are leasing out these properties for nine years. And therefore such schools will be coming and it's completely asset-light.

items.statement: 3.4 million daily active users on app with 106 minutes average daily engagement
items.quote: Currently having 3.4 million daily active users on our mobile app and getting engaged for 106 minutes on a daily average basis.

items.statement: Curious Junior (K-12 online) achieved ~100% improvement in EBITDA and enrolment
items.quote: We achieved almost 100% improvement in terms of EBITDA and enrolment, and we will continue to grow at the same rate in the coming time. So that makes us the largest online tuition player as well with the brand name of Curious Junior.

items.statement: PW Talks (English speaking) targeting $1 million ARR run rate by end of year
items.quote: by the end of this year, this initiative will reach a million-dollar ARR run rate. And we have also beautifully integrated its monetization within the student journey in the app.

items.statement: Tech and product team headcount up 40% YoY; investing in AI tech talent
items.quote: Our overall tech spends because of the scale that we have grown last year, we see almost like a percentage leverage on the tech spends in spite of our AI pod cost of the tech and product team going up by 40% from last year.

items.statement: ESOP expenses increased to INR125 crores for 9M FY26 from INR73 crores last year due to valuation impact
items.quote: Our employee cost were higher including the ESOP expenses. So our ESOP expenses now are at INR125 crores for nine months against the 73 for last year. Largely due to the valuation impact on the new ESOPs that we issue.

items.statement: Direct cost leverage of 2.8% YoY from cost reduction initiatives on consultants and professional fees
items.quote: In terms of the overall cost initiatives, the direct cost gave us a leverage of almost like 2.8% year-over-year obviously due to all the cost reduction initiatives that we ran, especially around the consultants and the professional fees.

items.statement: AI models (Aryabhata) claim better accuracy than Gemini/GPT for Indian test prep due to proprietary RAG layer
items.quote: See education is a very niche use case. A teacher cannot go wrong. So if you look at the accuracy of our models, it is better than Gemini and the existing GPT because it operates on a RAG layer which is a fine-tuned layer on top of these large language models.

items.statement: K-12 school competition is local non-tech-led schools; PW has curriculum, pedagogy, data-driven systems advantage
items.quote: For example what is my competition here? Here is my competition is a local non-tech led schools where the curriculum and the standard practices are not there. So even it is much more easier market to win and create brand is what we have seen in our initial interventions.

items.statement: No plans for international M&A or expansion; bandwidth focused on domestic market
items.quote: Outside India, the answer is a simple no. We are not evaluating any assets outside India right now, nor are we going to acquire any. We don't have the bandwidth to go outside India at this point of time.

items.statement: School Integrated Program (asset-light) runs in 50 partner schools with 25,000 students generating INR25 crores revenue
items.quote: So we have both the models here, Prateek here, that we have an asset-light model with the name of School Integrated Program, where we have partnership with 50 such schools will teach almost 25,000 -- will generate almost INR25 crores of top line through that model also.

items.statement: Operating cash flow to adjusted EBITDA ratio typically 105-110% on sustainable basis; Q3 was 142% due to higher collections
items.quote: Capillary as a business generates more cash and typically a 105 to 110 is what we see on a sustainable basis.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 16.4% in Q3 FY26 from 15.3% in Q3 FY25; nine months margin 13% vs 10.5% prior year
items.quote: for the Q3 FY26 we saw adjusted EBITDA of INR 30 crores, which is about 16.4%. And for the same time last year, the adjusted EBITDA was INR 24 crores at about 15.3

items.statement: Gross margins around 69-70% currently; improved ~1.5% over first nine months FY26
items.quote: Our gross margins are around the 69%-70% now. So it is a high gross margin software business in that sense.

items.statement: Net Revenue Retention (NRR) at 111% for trailing twelve months ended Dec 2025; organic NRR 115%, inorganic NRR 96%
items.quote: For the trailing twelve months period for December 2025, the NRR has been 111%. If we break this down into organic and inorganic business, the organic business NRR is at 115%.

items.statement: Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) grew 21% over March 2025 in first nine months FY26
items.quote: So for the nine months FY26, the ARR has grown by 21% over March 2025.

items.statement: Added 12 new customers in first nine months FY26 (3 in Q3); new order book INR 66 crore vs INR 53 crore same period last year
items.quote: Through the first nine months, we've added 12 customers, we've added three in the last quarter. So if you look at new order book in that sense, we've added INR 66 crores of new order book over the 9-month period.

items.statement: D&A increased from INR 13 crore to INR 19 crore per quarter due to Kognitiv acquisition in May 2025
items.quote: The depreciation and amortization has increased from about INR 13 crores a quarter to about INR 19 crores and this is largely on back of the acquisition that we did earlier this year, we acquired company called Kognitiv in May this year.

items.statement: Fourth acquisition Kognitiv completed May 2025; multiple LOIs in pipeline; acquire competitors at 0.5-1.5x revenue and migrate customers to Capillary platform
items.quote: We did our fourth acquisition this year in Kognitiv back in May. We also have a couple of other letters of intent on the M&A side that we have in the market right now.

items.statement: aiRA AI product in early monetization; 10-15 of 115 customers in POC/post-POC; free 3-month pilot then annual license linked to usage
items.quote: we now actually in conversations with a few of our first few POCs to actually start billing them for an annual license linked to numb er of usage and things like that. It's still early days I would say, but we at least have out of our 115 customers today we at least have 10 or 15 who are in a POC or a post-POC type place with aiRA now

items.statement: US healthcare payer (top-5 client) member base grew ~50% after Jan 1 go-lives; no Medicare exposure; NRR motions strong
items.quote: We've had some major go-lives happen on the 1st of January this year, which means that our member base for this specific customer actually gone up by roughly 50%.

items.statement: Forrester Wave leadership translating to wins; new order book up 25% YoY (INR 66 cr vs 53 cr) despite market slowdown
items.quote: I think this year we've had a like I said our new order book has gone up from INR 53 crores to like INR 66 crores in the same period of the 9 months. So unlike a lot of the other folks where you're hearing about like new business slowing down, we are not seeing that as much.

items.statement: Pricing linked to transactions/members not seat-based; insulates from AI-driven seat-based pricing disruption
items.quote: In our case, our pricing as I said is linked to number of transactions or number of customers or number of members, right? So slightly more outcome linked. And that again insulates us from any of these seat-based pricing shocks.

items.statement: Nine months operating cash flow INR 101 crore vs adjusted EBITDA INR 71 crore (142% conversion); sustainable rate 105-110%
items.quote: Nine months operating cash flow as compared to the nine months adjusted EBITDA of about INR 71 crores. So that ratio stands at about 142%.

items.statement: Closing cash balance INR 463 crore at end of Q3 FY26
items.quote: The other factor to look at is our closing cash balance for the quarter has been INR 463 crores.

items.statement: Tech and corporate cost ~18% of revenue (down from 28% few years ago); expect further leverage as non-COGS costs grow near inflation plus modest team growth
items.quote: our technology and Cor p cost used to be about 28% of revenue. It came down to about 18% for last year and it's on a similar trend now

items.statement: One-time INR 1.6 crore gratuity expense in Q3 FY26 due to Direct Labour Code change
items.quote: As you would be aware, there has been a change in the Direct Labour Code, which has resulted in a higher one-time gratuity expense that the impact of that we have taken in Q3, that's about INR 1.6 crores.

items.statement: AI disruption risk low: loyalty is niche with proprietary data; enterprise switching costs high (avg 9 integrations); 97% revenue from large enterprise
items.quote: Loyalty is very niche, right? So I think there's also a lot of very proprietary data that ends up getting generated in a loyalty stack. So I feel we're fairly insulated from, you know, in that sense as well.

items.statement: Q4 traditionally contributes upwards of 30% of full-year revenue and is the heaviest quarter
items.quote: If you look at the quarter wise, traditionally, last several years Q4 is the heaviest, that means it is upwards of 30%. That has been the trend. 30% of the total revenue for the year is what we clock in Q4 and that has been a trend for the last several years and this year could be no exception.

items.statement: Secured multi-year engagement with Civil Services Commission of Philippines for digital examinations starting 2026 using SARAS platform
items.quote: In collaboration with ASEAMETRICS, Excelsoft will provide power the civil services digital examination starting in 2026. Leveraging our SARAS eAssessment platform, this multi-year engagement validates our ability to deliver high integrity, large-scale digital assessments and establishes a clear path for recurring platform-driven revenue repeating our success in other civil services examinations th

items.statement: Signed major multi-year engagement with VTCT Skills to deploy SARAS eTesting platform for 300,000 vocational examinations annually
items.quote: We have also solidified our UK footprint through a major multi-year engagement with VTCT Skills which is Vocational Training Charitable Trust, to deploy our next generation SARAS eTesting platform facilitating 300,000 vocational and technical examinations delivered online every year.

items.statement: AQA partnership contract nearly finalized, revenue expected to start next quarter and build over several years
items.quote: The contract is nearly finalized. So, it will be a contract signed this quarter and we will start seeing revenues starting next quarter and revenues will grow and build up over the next few years as the number of exams that are put through our system increase.

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA margin 27.7% vs 32.8% prior year due to 61% increase in other expenses from vendor costs and legal fees
items.quote: EBITDA margins were 27.7% compared to 32.8% in the prior year. The reduction in the margin is primarily attributed to a 61% increase in other expenses which rose from Rs.98 million to Rs.157 million, driven by higher vendor stock resources cost as well as legal and professional fees.

items.statement: One-time legal and professional fees of Rs.2.9 crores for acquisition due diligence reduced EBITDA margin by ~430 bps
items.quote: This is an exceptional item. This is one-off expense in the quarter which was to the tune of roughly almost Rs.2.9 crores. So, Rs.2.9 crores is what the expense towards this one-off item on legal and professional services. So that if you add that back into the EBITDA, the EBITDA margin would be 32%, which is in line with the previous period.

items.statement: New labor code implementation impact of Rs.40.7 million on gratuity and leave encashment
items.quote: We have implemented the new labor code, the impact of which is to the tune of Rs.40.7 million on increased gratuity and leave encashment policy.

items.statement: AQA deal margin profile expected to be better than company average as it is mostly licensed revenue
items.quote: Definitely better and not below, it is mostly licensed, it will be better than the company average.

items.statement: Infrastructure upgrade to AI-enabled hardware across network edge to laptops to be implemented over two years
items.quote: It would be implemented in the two years. Dhananjaya Sudhanva: We have identified some of the more modern clouded GI devices. So, we are going from outside and we have already identified vendors and placed orders. So, we will actually start from the edge of our network in implementing AI and buying AI devices and tools and work inwards to every single person's laptop

items.statement: Withdrew Rs.300 crores corporate guarantee and released Rs.165 crores fixed deposit lien, reducing contingent liabilities
items.value: Rs.300 crores guarantee, Rs.165 crores FD lien
items.quote: On a different note, we have successfully withdrawn the Rs.300 crores corporate guarantee and also released the Rs.165 crores fixed deposit lien that was marked earlier. These milestones reduce contingent liabilities and provide us with the financial flexibility to aggressively invest in innovation and growth through organic and inorganic means.

items.statement: Net cash balance of Rs.421 crores after IPO proceeds
items.quote: Ravi Subramaniam: Rs.421 crores. Praful Rai: Net cash balance means net of all outstanding debt is that? Ravi Subramaniam: Yes.

items.statement: Completed due diligence on US acquisition target, discussing valuations; UK targets in early due diligence stage
items.quote: We have an American company where we have completed due diligence and we are discussing valuations. As always, sir, as you would know there will be a little bit of a higgle-haggle towards before we converge on the valuation. That is the stage we are in with an American company which we target to acquire. There are a couple of other targets in the UK, where due diligence has started, we have not ye

items.statement: Launching six new AI and Quantum Computing-driven assessment products next month from innovation lab
items.quote: We have developed new products which will be rolled out next month, six new products in broadly the area of assessments driven by technology using AI and Quantum Computing as Prashanth mentioned, and we will launch officially these six products which have in the output of our innovation group.

items.statement: Achieved 98.6% accuracy in AI-based handwritten text extraction using multiple LLMs on proprietary hardware
items.quote: We have delivered a 98.6% accuracy on the AI-based extraction of handwritten text. How was that possible is because of the ability to use multiple LLMs on our own hardware and adding the right kind of weights for different models which are good in one thing or the other, some for the image and processing, some for text and things like that.

items.statement: Top 10 customers average tenure nearly 11 years, contributing 80% revenue; added 10 new clients in nine months
items.quote: We have added 10 new clients during the nine-month period, yet our top-10 customers maintain an average tenure of nearly 11-years. Top 10 customers have been with us on an average of 11 years. In this volatile market, this 80% revenue contribution from long-term partners provides us with a highly predictable cash flow and a robust foundation for cross-selling.

items.statement: North America 72.2% of Q3 revenue, Europe/UK 18.3%, top 5 customers 72.2% concentration
items.quote: North America remains our largest geography contributing 72.2% of Q3 revenue and 65.7% of nine months revenue, Europe and UK contributed 18.3% in Q3 and 21.5% in nine months. Revenue concentration among the top five customers stood at 72.2% in Q3, reflecting our long-term relationship with the major global clients.

items.statement: Global demand accelerating for secure, scalable, tech-enabled assessment and high-stakes testing solutions driven by digital transformation in education, skilling, professional certifications and public sector exams
items.quote: The global demand for secure, scalable and tech-enabled assessment and high-state testing solutions is accelerating. It is driven by the digital transformation happening in broadly the education and skilling sector including professional certifications which are becoming very important particularly in vocational space. And public sector examinations, which are large in number which deliver volumes

items.statement: AI productivity gains partly passed to customers but largely absorbed internally; customer-specific risk appetite determines AI enablement level
items.quote: Partly passing it on to the clients but largely absorbing it ourselves. The approach has been that the tools that we use already for developing and deploying for customers get benefited from the new AI models and new AI tools. So, it is not as though the core tools that we use, we stop using and everything we use is used to deliver to customers with AI.

items.statement: Expanding direct sales presence in US, Middle East, Singapore; hiring senior consultants with client networks in government and publishing sectors
items.quote: We have been successful in adding a few people already in the US, in Middle East, Singapore, and we are many more adding into the sales force, they are all in the various stages of the of hiring. Dhananjaya Sudhanva: And one nuance in this approach, sir, is, we have hired consultants in each of these geographies. Consultants who have worked earlier with our clients but have retired or moved on to

items.statement: Capitalized product development expenses of Rs.2.7 crores in the quarter
items.quote: We have a product development expenses, Rs.2.7 crores, okay, this is the capitalized.

items.statement: No AI headwinds seen in niche assessment business unlike IT services; competition monitored via market intelligence team feeding innovation lab
items.quote: In our case, because the products are AI-native it delivers all the benefits, but we do not face headwinds because there is a significant benefit and value proposition that gets passed on to our customers. So, yes, there is competition. Yes, we have to watch out for competition. We have our team who attend all the relevant conferences, give us an analysis of competition. We have to work hard to st

items.statement: IPO expenses of Rs.70 lakhs charged to P&L this quarter per advisor guidance; remainder goes to share premium account
items.quote: Around Rs.70 lakhs which was spent before this filing DRHP in all those stages, advised by the consultant and PrLM not to show as IPO expenses and not to adjust against the share premium account which only it is taking to the P&L directly, Rs.70 lakhs is already done in this quarter itself.

items.statement: Engaged Big Four consulting firm for business process and controls audit; will appoint one as statutory auditor next financial year
items.quote: We are engaged with one of the big four consulting firms in India. They are currently doing a business process and controls audit on Excelsoft and eventually we will have one of the big four as our statutory auditor for the next financial year.

items.statement: Management expects to sustain recent growth trajectory with stable margins in FY27; battery materials revenue contribution from FY28
items.quote: What I can say is, I think the growth that we've done over the last couple of years , is what we will continue to sustain with a very stable and similar margin profile.

items.statement: Dahej Battery Materials Facility Phase 1 (25,000 tpa) on track for early 2027 commissioning; Nandesari Greenfield (51,200 tpa) commissioning March 2026; specialty ingredients at 35-40% utilization
items.quote: We broke ground on January 23rd and Phase 1 capacity of 25,000 metric tons per annum remains on track for commissioning in early 2027.

items.statement: 34 battery material customers engaged; ~70% have approved/validated samples; commercial scale-up orders received; active off-take discussions with large OEMs and cell manufacturers
items.quote: We are currently engaged with 34 customers across the battery value chain and our iron phosphate qualification process is progressing well. Around 70 % of these customers have approved and validated Sud eep samples.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin 37.3%; 9M FY26 EBITDA margin 37.6%; ex-NSS margins in 35-37% range; battery materials expected to achieve better margins than industry
items.quote: EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at 37.3%.

items.statement: Broad-based geographic momentum: APAC strong growth from FMCG/infant nutrition; Europe emerging with regulatory approvals; India ~20% growth; export markets to drive incremental growth
items.quote: During Q3, we saw steady and broad-based momentum across regions. This reflects both robust underlying demand and the early benefits of strategic investments we have made over the last few years.

items.statement: Specialty ingredients 41% of Q3 revenue (up from <10% in FY23); encapsulated/premix lines strong; new tortilla manufacturer and expanded big goods company sourcing; liposomal revenue from H2 FY27
items.quote: For Q3 FY '26, as Shanil mentioned specialty business did very well and is continuing to do very well. It contributed to 41% while pharma, food and nutrition contributed 59%.

items.statement: Net working capital days ~180 days; supports growth trajectory
items.quote: our networking capital days remain in the range of about 180 days and which supports our growth trajectory in the coming period.

items.statement: Battery materials capex majorly financed through internal accruals; no significant interest impact expected before FY28 revenue commencement
items.quote: Majorly, it is getting financed through our internal accruals. So, we don't see a significant interest impact coming in for the project as of now.

items.statement: CEP certification for calcium carbonate (only Indian company, 1 of 9 globally); Europe regulatory approvals progressing; US tariff reversal favorable; China VAT rebate elimination supports battery material pricing

items.statement: Gold loan demand ample; market shift from unorganized to organized continues; operational excellence matters more than demand

items.statement: Proactively strengthening governance and compliance for potential transition to higher NBFC regulatory layer

items.statement: Conservative underwriting; no aggressive pricing or relaxed standards; growth paced to keep systems and controls ahead

items.statement: Cost rationalization of ~INR220 cr annualized; ~50% achieved; balance flowing through Q4 FY26 and FY27

items.statement: Cost synergies from Profectus acquisition to reflect meaningfully from Q4 FY26

items.quote: On Operational EBITDA, which is inclusive of the provisioning we have done for the New Labour Code is at 13.1% vis-a-vis last year of 10.2%.

items.statement: Blended gross margin on equipment around 30-35%; varies by product
items.quote: overall, we will be around that.

items.statement: 9M FY26 revenue INR 912 cr (32% YoY); Q3 FY26 revenue INR 314 cr (44% YoY)
items.quote: we've had the highest ever turnover for 9 months, achieved INR912 crores against INR693 crores in the corresponding last year 9 months.

items.statement: 9M FY26 power tiller volumes 37,374 (+55% YoY); tractor domestic 3,352 (+18% YoY); power weeder 8,399 (+63% YoY)
items.quote: power tiller we've grown by 55.1%, 37,374 power tillers against 24,100 power tillers the previous year.

items.statement: SFM factory at Malur running near full capacity (70k installed, up to 1 lakh with 3 shifts); evaluating new plant in North or West
items.quote: We are at about 70,000 in terms of installed capacity. But if you do a third shift, we can go up to 1 lakh of power tillers, plus weeders, plus reapers, plus new products that are coming up.

items.statement: FENTM tractor series launched in Gujarat; Maharashtra launch at Gudi Padwa next month; other states in FY27
items.quote: We have just launched in one state, which is Gujarat, so now we'll be launching in Maharashtra which is the next place we will be launching at Gudi Padwa, coming next month.

items.statement: ZETOR revamped series relaunch starting March (Q4 FY26) and continuing into FY27
items.quote: ZETOR is a complete revamped series now we'll be launching, because we've been seeding in the last 1 year or so. And now we have a complete revamped product, so that process of relaunch is happening in Q4 to begin with in March and then going forward into the next financial year.

items.statement: Electric power weeder and power tiller seeding to start in March (Q4 FY26); scale-up in FY27
items.quote: we would be starting to seed them in this quarter. In March, we should be able to start seeding them in the market and scaling up steadily based on the response from the market in the next financial year.

items.statement: Copper price increase steep but impact not material (only on copper radiator models); ferrous metal fluctuation low
items.quote: On ferrous metal the fluctuation has not been very high or the increase has not been very high, so nothing is happening on that front. But on the copper, it has been pretty steep.

items.statement: VST products 15-20% more expensive than quality Chinese imports; compete on warranty, service, parts availability
items.quote: roughly, I can say we would be expensive by 15% to 20% roughly.

items.statement: SFM distribution expanding: 650 dealers + pilot distributor-retailer network (10 distributors, 300 retailers); target 6,000 counters
items.quote: We will have to get to every taluka. That is about 6,000 counters is what we are looking at to begin with. We are roughly at around 1,000 counters at this point.

items.statement: Chinese imports in power weeder segment; VST gaining share via 2-year warranty, service, parts; Chinese influence expected to diminish
items.quote: with more trust on the brands like VST, they are coming forward, because we offer a 2-year warranty on these machines, which the Chinese do not offer.

items.statement: Global brands (German, Japanese) mostly import from China; cannot match VST's warranty and service
items.quote: most of them are still importing from China as well. So I don't see them able to offer the same trust and the warranty and all that we are talking today.

items.statement: FY26 export mix: Europe 90%, Africa 5%, Rest of World 5%, US 0%
items.quote: FY '26, U.S. is zero. Europe is 90%, Africa would be 5% and Rest of the World, 5%.

items.statement: Europe logistics and distributor cash flow challenges; local base to improve rotation and growth
items.quote: we have been trading or rather exporting from India to our distributors in Europe. That had its own challenges with all the conflicts going around and the logistics cost and the time required for logistics varying through the year.

items.statement: Subsidy flow regular but not increased; SPARSH scheme streamlined; state elections may slow Q1 FY27 flow temporarily
items.quote: Subsidy is normal, continuing, regular. With the SPARSH scheme last year where they introduced a new mechanism of paying the state governments the central portion, so all those things have been streamlined.

items.statement: Tractor industry: ~1M units; 30-50 HP segment ~8-9L units; 40-50 HP growing fastest; VST <1% share, targets 2-3% in 4-5 years
items.quote: Typically, 1% market share in this industry is about INR500 crores. We are less than 1% market share today. But we strongly believe that in the next 5 years, we can definitely claim 2% to 3% market share.

items.statement: Small farm mechanization potential: 15 cr farming households, 10 cr without mechanization; retail finance penetration for power tillers at 12-13%
items.quote: I'm very happy to say today, almost 12% to 13% of our business is retail finance for power tillers, which will continue to grow and kind of create capital enough for people to buy small farm machines.

items.statement: Marine engine entry in initial days; no capex commitment (third-party marinization); exploring compact engine adjacency
items.quote: it's an adjacency for us. We have compact engines. There is no need for any separate capex required. We see this as an opportunity, and we are exploring it.

items.statement: US tariff volatility acknowledged; product development continued; entry planned 2027 if stable
items.quote: all of us know it is a very volatile situation, and things change every other day, so we are hoping things now are stable going forward.

items.statement: Improved cash generation INR 108 cr in 9M FY26
items.quote: We've had improved cash generation of INR108 crores this year.

items.statement: FY26 tractor volume target 6,000-6,500 units
items.quote: cumulatively, tractor, domestic plus Export, I have guided anywhere between 6,000 to 6,500.

items.statement: SFM factory at Malur near full capacity at 70,000 installed; evaluating new plant in North or West
items.quote: We are at about 70,000 in terms of installed capacity. But if you do a third shift, we can go up to 1 lakh of power tillers, plus weeders, plus reapers, plus new products that are coming up, electric weeder, electric tiller and all of that.

items.statement: 9M FY26 revenue INR912 crores, up 32% YoY
items.quote: we are at a 32% growth at INR912 crores vis-a-vis INR693 crores last year.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 operational EBITDA margin 12.9% vs 8.9% YoY
items.quote: Operational EBITDA at 12.9% against 8.9% of the previous year

items.statement: Power tiller 9M volume up 55% to 37,374 units; power weeder up 63% to 8,399 units
items.quote: power tiller we've grown by 55.1%, 37,374 power tillers against 24,100 power tillers the previous year. Tractor domestic, 3,352 against 2,846 of the previous year with the 17.8% growth.

items.statement: Domestic tractor 9M volume up 18% to 3,352 units; export tractor down 23% to 886 units
items.quote: Tractor domestic, 3,352 against 2,846 of the previous year with the 17.8% growth. Export has been down at 886 against previous year of 1,151 with a minus 23%.

items.statement: FENTM tractor series launched in Gujarat; Maharashtra launch at Gudi Padwa; ZETOR revamp relaunch in Q4
items.quote: We have just launched in one state, which is Gujarat, so now we'll be launching in Maharashtra which is the next place we will be launching at Gudi Padwa, coming next month. And then, go on for launches in all the other states in the next financial year.

items.statement: US market entry planned for 2027; product development ongoing
items.quote: in 2027, we will enter the U.S. market. But all of us know it is a very volatile situation, and things change every other day, so we are hoping things now are stable going forward.

items.statement: Copper price rise steep but impact not material; ferrous metal fluctuation low
items.quote: On ferrous metal the fluctuation has not been very high or the increase has not been very high, so nothing is happening on that front. But on the copper, it has been pretty steep. And in some of the areas, especially radiator, on a particular model that we use our copper radiator, otherwise it's aluminium, only on that front. So it has not been material at this point in time.

items.statement: Chinese power weeder imports present but VST gaining share via warranty, service, parts; VST 15-20% costlier than quality Chinese products
items.quote: Let me be very frank with you. We won't be able to achieve parity with Chinese costs. That is very clear. But what we can definitely do is more -- create more value for the buyer to buy from us, provide him warranty, provide him service and provide him parts when he needs it.

items.statement: Tractor industry: 1M units; up to 30 HP ~1 lakh; 30-50 HP ~8-9 lakh; 40-50 HP fastest growing
items.quote: tractor segment typically is divided into up to 20 HP, 20 to 30 HP, 30 to 40 HP and 40 to 50 HP. And above 50 HP is very small in terms of the industry size. And up to 30 HP is also only about 50,000 to 60,000 Nos. And compact tractors and total industry size up to 30 HP is about 1 lakh out of the 1 million, right?

items.statement: Subsidy flow regular but unchanged; state elections may slow Q1 FY27 disbursement
items.quote: Subsidy is normal, continuing, regular. With the SPARSH scheme last year where they introduced a new mechanism of paying the state governments the central portion, so all those things have been streamlined. So it's been regular this year, but not increased.

items.statement: Marine engine entry initial; no separate capex; marinization via third party
items.quote: it's an adjacency for us. We have compact engines. There is no need for any separate capex required. We see this as an opportunity, and we are exploring it. Like I said to the previous caller, it's very initial days.

items.statement: CEO Antony Cherukara awarded ET India's Impactful Turnaround CEO
items.quote: Happy to share that I was also awarded as ET India's Impactful Turnaround CEO

items.statement: No specific capex guidance provided; Data Center investments to increase significantly over next 3-4 years
items.quote: I think, at this point in time, I cannot give you a capex guidance, but clearly you will see us investing more and more behind Data Centers; I think, there is no question about that in my mind.

items.statement: Added 11,000 5G sites in Q3; 5G population coverage now 74%
items.quote: adding about 11,000 5G sites in the quarter- we now cover about 74% of population with 5G.

items.statement: Rolled out over 11,000 km fiber and added 2 million fiber home passes in Q3
items.quote: Our step up on fiber deployment continues strongly - we rolled out over 11,000 km of overall fiber and added about 2 million fiber home passes in the quarter.

items.statement: Data Center capacity target of 1 GW in next 3-4 years from current 120-130 MW
items.quote: our sense is that, in the next three to four years, we will have about a gigawatt capacity, which will give us about 25% share

items.statement: International roaming revenues growing over 30% year-over-year
items.quote: Our efforts are yielding strong outcomes in international roaming revenues, and they are growing at over 30% year-over-year.

items.statement: Broadband net adds of 1.2 million in Q3, highest ever quarterly; installed base crossed 13 million
items.quote: On broadband, we delivered another strong quarter with our highest ever quarterly net adds of 1.2 million customers. We have crossed 13 million installed connected homes customer base.

items.statement: FWA customer base now over 3 million
items.quote: FWA continues to expand addressable market for us, and we are deepening our supply footprint with FWA. This is reflected in strong momentum in FWA customer base, which now stands over 3 million.

items.statement: India mobile ARPU at Rs.259 in Q3
items.quote: ARPU came in at Rs.259, led by our continued efforts on premiumizing and improving our portfolio mix.

items.statement: Added 4.4 million revenue earning mobile customers and 5.2 million smartphone data consumers in Q3
items.quote: In mobility, we added 4.4 million revenue earning customers and 5.2 million smartphone data consumers during the quarter.

items.statement: 5G customer base reached 181 million; over 90% of smartphones are 5G
items.quote: We ended the quarter at 181 million 5G customers. Our share in 5G shipments is seeing sustained improvement. 5G handset penetration continues to grow and over 90% of our total smartphones today come in as 5G.

items.statement: Postpaid net adds of 0.6 million in Q3
items.quote: Postpaid net adds came in at 0.6 million.

items.statement: Airtel Business revenue Rs.5,350 crores, up 1.5% sequentially
items.quote: Moving to Airtel business, its revenues came in at Rs.5,350 crores, growing 1.5% sequentially.

items.statement: Digital portfolio revenue grew 39% year-over-year
items.quote: Our digital portfolio delivered robust revenue growth and grew 39% over last year.

items.statement: Airtel Finance monthly loan disbursement run-rate over Rs.500 crores
items.quote: Monthly loan disbursement run-rate now stands at over Rs.500 crores.

items.statement: Payments Bank MTU at 108 million; annualized revenue run-rate crossed Rs.3,250 crores, up 16% YoY
items.quote: Payment Bank, its MTU stand at about 108 million, annualized revenue run rate has now crossed Rs.3250 crores and it is growing sequentially year-on-year at 16%.

items.statement: Payments Bank deposits at Rs.4,300 crores, up 28% YoY
items.quote: Deposits remain strong at about Rs.4,300 crores, growing 28% over a year.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDAaL Rs.27,700 crores, up 4.2%; margin 51.3%, up 30 bps sequentially
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDAaL came in at over Rs.27,700 crores, a growth of 4.2%. Our EBITDAaL margin stood at 51.3%, which is about 30 basis points improvement sequentially.

items.statement: India EBITDAaL (ex-passive infra) Rs.18,450 crores, up 2.8%; margin 51.8%, up 30 bps
items.quote: India EBITDAaL, excluding passive infra, came in at over Rs.18,450 crores, growing at 2.8% sequentially. EBITDAaL margin stood at 51.8%, again a 30 basis points improvement.

items.statement: Consolidated net debt to EBITDAaL improved to 1.02x; India net debt to EBITDAaL at 1.38x
items.quote: Our consolidated net debt to EBITDAaL improved to 1.02 with India now at 1.38.

items.statement: Rights issue called as 3-year timeframe ended; no option to foreclose
items.quote: We have already, sort of, given that there was a timeframe of 3 years which is now over, we have no provision to foreclose the call on the rights issue, so we have called it.

items.statement: Written to DoT requesting parity on AGR dues treatment; awaiting response
items.quote: We have written a few letters to the DoT, asking for a clarification and basically requesting parity on the treatment of the AGR dues. We are yet to hear from the DoT.

items.statement: 5G SA rolled out pan-India on FWA and Mobile; most FWA customers on SA experiencing superior uplink speeds
items.quote: We have now rolled out 5G standalone pan-India on both FWA and Mobile services. Most of our FWA customers across circles are now on 5G standalone network, experiencing superior uplink speeds.

items.statement: Site running costs declined over 6% in last 4 years despite accelerated rollouts and new tech layers
items.quote: A prime example of this is our site running cost, which have declined by over 6% in last four years despite accelerated rollouts and addition of new technology layers.

items.statement: AGR payments of ~$1 billion start March; letters sent to DoT for parity, awaiting response
items.quote: We have written a few letters to the DoT, asking for a clarification and basically requesting parity on the treatment of the AGR dues. We are yet to hear from the DoT. Once we hear from the DoT, we will then decide what our next steps are.

items.statement: Won two deals in B2B cloud/software; one deepening with repeat business, another in final stages, plus conversations with many more.
items.quote: we have won two deals, one of which is now getting much deeper, where we are actually winning repeat businesses across a bunch of things that we have already done. The second is that we are in the final stages with another couple, and we are having conversations with many more, so that is a very different business.

items.statement: Increased shareholding in Airtel Africa because it was undervalued; stock price doubled over last 5-6 quarters; will continue to look for value-creation opportunities.
items.quote: the reason that we stepped up our investment in Airtel Africa is simply because we thought it was an undervalued asset. You can see that, clearly, having played out, the stock and the price of the African asset has, more or less, kind of, doubled in the recent, let us say, five to six quarters, so this has been a really, really good asset

items.statement: Africa constant currency growth consistently 20%+; reported growth now higher than constant currency after Naira stabilization.
items.quote: We have been consistently growing now for several quarters at about 20% plus, and in fact now, with the currency having stabilized, particularly the Naira, and in fact hardened a little bit, that is also showing through now in reported numbers because, actually, it is the other way around, the reported growth is now higher than the constant currency growth.

items.statement: Currency volatility is the only risk in Africa; long-term view factors 5-7% annual devaluation as cost of doing business.
items.quote: currency volatility is the only risk in Africa, but if you take a long-term view over a 10-12 year period, you typically factor in, let us say, a 5 to 7% devaluation per year and that is the cost of doing business in that continent

items.statement: Industry 4G/5G net adds slowing due to tariff hardening causing SIM consolidation and reduced feature-phone funnel; Airtel's share of net adds holding.
items.quote: the industry is seeing a slowdown in terms of the total number of net adds the industry was doing a couple of years back, I think, two, three years back, very difficult to handle why it is happening, except the one thing, which is saying with some of the tariffs hardening over last two cycles, I think there have been a little bit of sim consolidation that has happened in the industry

items.statement: Wi-Fi net adds approach is fiber-first; FWA augments supply gaps; UBR used judiciously where needed.
items.quote: Our approach is fiber first; we believe that is the best experience for the customer and we want to have as many customers as possible on fiber. FWA augments this, and wherever we have had supply gaps, we have augmented with 5G and FWA rollout. As required, we will judiciously bring in UBR into the mix as well

items.statement: Committed to disciplined, prudent capex; every dollar spent must create value.
items.quote: one thing that you can trust us on is that we will be prudent, we will be disciplined, and we will make sure that every dollar that is spent goes to create value for us.

items.statement: Evaluating inorganic opportunities in Data Centers at right value and with right partner; also doubling down on Cloud and sovereign cloud certification with MeitY; scouting B2B portfolio additions.
items.quote: Data Center is clearly a play that we want to be large on. Obviously, we will be keen to look at where there are opportunities to consolidate a fragmented industry, it has got to be at the right value, it has got to be done with the right kind of partner, so that is something that we will certainly look at. On the Cloud, we have already made a reasonable investment, and we are committed to dramati

items.statement: External net debt (ex finance leases and DoT debt) almost down to nothing; one of lowest leveraged telcos globally.
items.quote: the external net debt, if you take the external net debt without the finance lease obligations and without the DoT debt, which is almost like a, think of the DoT debt almost like an annual payout based on of a right to use, so it is not even a debt, and in a way it is just a right to use kind of a debt, so if you remove the finance lease obligations and the DoT debt, the external net debt is almos

items.statement: Not at a point to return capital or re-lever to 2x; focused on growth investments in Data Center, Cloud, Financial Services.
items.quote: I think that we are not at that point at this stage to do this. We think that there is still a lot of growth in this market and that is the place that we are really going to be focused on right now.

items.statement: Rolling out 2 million fiber home passes per quarter; target 100 million broadband homes in 4-5 years from current 45-46 million.
items.quote: do not forget we are rolling out 2 million fiber home passes for the quarter, so we are really stepped up on our fiber home passes every quarter, and we are trying to see, can we do more of this. Today, the total number of broadband homes are about 45-46 million, one day, not in the very distant future, could be about maybe 4 years or 5 years, this will be 100 million

items.statement: FWA churn initially modestly higher due to wrong placements; now improving; theoretical churn lower than fiber; migration to fiber planned but still in land-grab phase.
items.quote: I think in the past, as we started with FWA, we did see modestly higher levels of churn because it was being put in the wrong places where we did not have the right experience. I think those problems are now getting behind us. Theoretically, you should actually see a much lower churn on fixed wireless access because there is no fiber, there is no cut, there is nothing

items.statement: No supply constraints for FWA; headroom very high; fiber rollout accelerating to cover 100 million homes.
items.quote: No, we are not at that stage at all. The amount of headroom for supply is very high, and do not forget we are rolling out 2 million fiber home passes for the quarter

items.statement: Three growth investment ports of call: Data Center, Cloud, Financial Services; succession plan enables focus on deployment.
items.quote: there are three ports of call right now: one is Data Center, the second is Cloud and the third is opportunities in Financial services, and one of the reasons that we have put in place a succession where Shashwat runs the India business and I have a little more time to actually look at some of these areas is really the deployment of this for growth

items.statement: No formal capex guidance; strong balance sheet allows faster growth investment in homes/FWA/5G as opportunities arise.
items.quote: as a rule, we do not give guidance, but let me put it in this way. This is a Company which has a very strong balance sheet and will not shy away from putting investment where growth is required. So if I were to answer you, if we find, let us say, a new urban periphery coming up in one of the cities in any of these, we will immediately put up sites over there

items.statement: Hexacom mobile revenue underperformance vs Airtel due to unresolved partner issue causing customer drag; inroamer revenue volatile; underlying growth trending near national average.
items.quote: You would recollect that in the last quarter, we had called out that there were some issues because of which we had some customer drop; whilst we are working very closely with the other partner to see that it gets resolved, it has not yet got resolved completely, and hence there is a bit of drag which we still have on that

items.statement: Hexacom FWA opportunity estimated at 30-35% household penetration in Rajasthan/Northeast vs 40% national; affordability lower.
items.quote: I would hazard a guess anywhere between 30% to 35% penetration of households should be something which we can easily aspire to.

items.statement: Hexacom new businesses: SMB via Hexacom, Data Center via Nxtra, Digital TV/IPTV launched with strong adoption; no large enterprise B2B in circles.
items.quote: We, of course, have small and medium business which happens through Hexacom, but as you know, in these two states we do not have large enterprises, and as was mentioned in the previous call, bulk of the market is restricted to the top 500 companies, and none of them have their head office in either of these two states, so B2B clearly is not an option there. The other option is Data Center, which i

items.statement: Hexacom homes capex spike due to low base; FWA expansion driving disproportionate percentage increase vs Airtel.
items.quote: You see, any spike is a function of the base, and the very thing that you said, and I explained, that fiber density in these two circles is lower, which is why our homes business was also lower. If you look at pre-FWA and you look at share of homes business on total topline or homes as a percentage of mobile in Airtel versus Hexacom, Hexacom was minuscule

items.statement: Technology preference: fiber > FWA > UBR; UBR deployed only where 5G handset penetration low but demand exists; no strategic shift, demand-driven.
items.quote: According to us, the gold standard is if you give fiber, because that gives you the most consistent delivery and lowest latency. There are two others. The next best is FWA, and the least best is UBR because of interference as you mentioned. We will try everything to deliver and increase our addressable market, so this will be no different.

items.statement: Management expects annual EBITDA margins around 30% plus/minus 200 bps, not on a quarterly run-rate basis
items.quote: On the margin, I think, we have always said 25%. I think it is now safe to think of Navin as a 30% annual number. But let us not kind of hold that on a quarterly sort of treadmill run rate, yes? So it will be an annualized number that we are looking at 30% give or take plus/minus 200 basis points.

items.statement: cGMP-4 Phase-1 facility commissioned and commercial supplies started in Q3 FY26; full optimal utilization expected in FY27
items.quote: I am pleased to highlight that our cGMP-4 Phase-1 facility has been commissioned based on our timelines. Post successful validation of batches, we started commercial supplies during the quarter.

items.statement: MPP-1 utilization expected to hit near full capacity for full year; MPP-2 at 70-80% with pickup expected next year; Nectar at ~50% of par this year; dedicated plant at ~70%
items.quote: Utilization for the MPP-1 is solid. For the full year, we expect to almost hit the par. Utilization for MPP-2 is about 80%, 70% around in that range, but we expect that to pick up in the coming year. And utilization for Nectar is again, as we had always said, this year, we would hit roughly 50% of the par. So, we are on track for that. Sanjesh Jain: And dedicated plant? Anish Ganatra: Our dedicate

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin 34.5% vs 24.3% YoY and 32.5% QoQ; nine-month margin 32% vs 21.5% YoY; improvement driven by better realizations and operating efficiencies
items.quote: Operating EBITDA stood at Rs.308 crores, up 109% year-on-year and 25% quarter-on-quarter. EBITDA margins improved to 34.5% compared to 24.3% in Q3 FY25 and 32.5% in Q2 FY26, driven by improved realization and operating efficiencies.

items.statement: Input costs for sulfur and fluorspar are increasing; management monitors closely and ensures pricing decisions reflect this
items.quote: So you are right. So the only issue, and I am sure you guys know it, the price of sulfur keeps increasing, the price of fluorspar is increasing. So, there are input costs that are going higher. And therefore, obviously, that is something that we monitor very closely. And we work in to make sure that our pricing decisions reflect this accurately well.

items.statement: Net working capital below 80 days of sales as of Dec 31, FY25; net debt-to-equity at 0.03x
items.quote: As of December 31, FY25, our net debt-to-equity ratio stood at 0.03x and net working capital was below 80 days of sales. This reflects a disciplined approach to access growth.

items.statement: Employee costs contained at 7-8% of revenue vs historical double-digit; capability enhancement planned as projects progress
items.quote: But, I think a safe bet is to look at what we are saying, 7%, 8% percent of revenue as our employee costs. See, we were historically at a two-digit number. But I think we have now contained it to where we should be in terms of comparison to peers or where we think it is appropriate.

items.statement: EU FTA and US trade deals seen as positive for bilateral trade; India Semiconductor Mission 2.0 supports Advanced Materials business
items.quote: Both the EU Free Trade Agreement and the US trade deals are good news for our industry. We expect these to support our bilateral trade. The government's focus on strengthening domestic manufacturing is also very encouraging for the chemical sector. Further, we are encouraged by the launch of India's Semiconductor Mission 2.0, which focuses on Semiconductor Manufacturing in India, along with the As

items.statement: Expect major growth in spring maize in Bihar, UP, Punjab and summer millet in Gujarat, Rajasthan, Western UP next quarter
items.quote: During the next quarter, we are expecting major growth in spring maize in Bihar, UP and Punjab. Similarly expecting growth in summer millet in Gujarat, Rajasthan and Western UP.

items.statement: Gross margins fell 4% YoY in Q3 due to higher production costs in cotton, maize and rice and inability to pass on costs to farmers
items.quote: When you're talking about this quarter, the gross margins fell by 4% compared to previous year, which is in line with the consolidated one.

items.statement: Cost of production stable or lower for coming season; expects margins to normalize to 45-48% range
items.quote: But if the costs are stable, then anyway we will increase the prices to some extent that can be absorbed. So it will normalize to what it used to be earlier between that 45% to 48%.

items.statement: Maize volumes up 21% and revenues up 42.6% in nine months; hybrid rice revenue up 17.9%, selection rice volume up 7% revenue up 14.2%
items.quote: Maize volumes increased by 21% and revenues increased by 42.6%. Vegetable seeds volumes increased by 1.5%, whereas revenue increased by 11.4%.

items.statement: Research paddy volumes grew 51%, sunflower 94%, mustard 64% in nine months
items.quote: Research paddy has grown by 51% in volumes, whereas vegetable seeds have grown by 5% in volume. Sunflower has grown by 94% in volume and mustard has grown by 64% in volume.

items.statement: Exports revenue grew 86% in Q3; expects continued growth each year barring major disruptions
items.quote: Exports have witnessed steep growth of 86% in the revenue during the current quarter and continue to grow and every year would be better than the previous year unless there is going to be any major unforeseen disruption in these markets.

items.statement: R&D and capex spend currently 5-10% of revenue; expected to stabilize at lower level as most capex already done
items.quote: As of now, our spend is in between 5% to 10% of our total revenue, both including revenue and capex. Going forward, they should stabilize at decently lower than what we have spent in the last year because most of the capex is already done there.

items.statement: Cash down to Rs 309 cr from Rs 409 cr; Rs 200+ cr deployed in inventory build-up; trade payables lower; expects normalization as season progresses
items.quote: If you see the overall inventory levels, if you take the overall cash flow, like majority of that, close to RS. 200 crores plus has been into the inventory.

items.statement: Receivables at Rs 250 cr vs Rs 175 cr YoY; Rs 75 cr increase due to higher sales; expects normalization to Rs 80-90 cr by year-end
items.quote: If you see actual receivables as of now at the end of 31st December, last year it was close to RS. 175-odd crores. This year is close to RS. 250-odd crores. Just RS. 75 crores have gone up because the sale is also higher in these quarters.

items.statement: Export receivables minimal as sales mostly on LC basis; domestic receivables expected to normalize at year-end
items.quote: No, usually we work on LCs. We don't give any credit there. Very few cases.

items.statement: Draft Seeds Bill 2025 aims for one nation one license, proper hybrid registration; overall positive for organized market; draft circulated, comments submitted, may pass soon
items.quote: In the new Seed Bill, lot of the things are trying to be addressed, one nation, one license. Most of the license are decentralized now. Proper registration of the hybrids, proper research, proper documentation, everything is coming in the new seed act.

items.statement: Three tax appeals pending for Rs 56 cr and Rs 70 cr demands; no provisions made as appeals payments done and shown as contingent liability; outcome expected in next six months
items.quote: There are three cases pending at the appeal stage. It's been almost like two and a half, three years there. Most probably it should come back in the next six months or so because the hearings are going on.

items.statement: Government corporation receivables still pending; received Rs 3-4 cr; fully provided for in provisions
items.quote: Still we have pending payments there. We received some RS. 3 crores or RS. 4 crores. We are trying to get it. We are doing that. But it is all provided in the provisions.

items.statement: Illegal cotton seed sales at same level as last year and increasing; impacted cotton sales
items.quote: See, that it will be in the same level as what it was in last year and increasing now.

items.statement: Cotton inventory 8-9 million packets, in line with anticipation; new hybrids with 3-5 year life; new production starting May-June 2026
items.quote: As of now, we are having enough stock till the end of the season, I mean to say by next year's season will be in between 8 million to 9 million packets for us, which is in line with our anticipation.

items.statement: Non-cotton hybrid volumes up 6.1%, revenues up 13%; cotton seed volumes and revenues also grew
items.quote: During the quarter, volumes of non-cotton hybrids increased by 6.1% and revenues increased by 13% and volumes as well as revenues of cotton seed has registered a growth.

items.statement: Dividend continued; buyback decision deferred to Q1 or follow-up quarter; open to inorganic growth as cash frees up in 3-6 months
items.quote: We used to do all the buybacks in the last years. This year, because we were building up the inventory, we have seen some sort of liquidity. I mean the cash got stuck in these activi ties. So we have not taken any decision on it

items.statement: Farmer engagement and demand forecasting already digitalized; large database of early farmers with follow-ups; digital marketing and social media networks in place
items.quote: That's already we have done it. Most of that is digitalized now. We have a huge database of the early farmers, follow-ups are already there. We have digital marketing network. We have huge social media networks for that.

items.statement: Maize prices dropped to Rs 1,200-1,300/q but recovered to Rs 1,800-1,900; Rs 2,000/q considered good for farmer returns
items.quote: In fact, it went down to as low as RS. 1,200 crores to RS. 1,250 crores, RS. 1,300 crores. But right now it's close RS. 1,800 to RS. 1,900. Anything about RS. 2,000, RS. 2,000, near to RS. 2,000 is a good price for maize.

items.statement: Maize volumes expected to remain healthy despite price dip as acreages and usage increasing
items.quote: We think maize volumes should remain good and healthy and because the acreages are going up and the usage is also going up.

items.statement: Industry-wide maize inventory overproduction in FY26 led to price pressure; expects normalization as supply known
items.quote: If you see, that's what happened this quarter itself because last year, by seeing the demand for the maize, everyone has produced more inventory, including us. All the industry players have produced more inventory.

items.statement: New cotton hybrids performing well; expects good revenue growth from June 2026 (FY27) onwards
items.quote: Our products have really done well, performed well, and we will see that good set of growth numbers coming in the next couple of years starting from '26, '27. I mean to say like June '26.

items.statement: Mustard and wheat driving 59% growth in other crops segment; segment small vs maize, cotton, rice (80%+ of revenue)
items.quote: It's a combination of all other crops. Other crops include like wheat, mustard, bajra, sunflower, everything comes in the other crops. So the mustard and wheat moves in this segment, that's the reason we have seen a good growth in the other crop segment.

items.statement: Cost of production higher in cotton, maize, rice vs previous years; unable to fully pass on to farmers in rabi season
items.quote: Even in maize and rice, the cost of production is a bit high when compared to the previous years. And usually, we used to sell higher, in terms of higher rates in rabi, but we were not able to pass it on to the farmer this time.

items.statement: Government sales insignificant portion of maize seed receivables; not worried about collections
items.quote: We don't see any government portion in it, where is an insignificant portion of government in it. We are not worried about that.

items.statement: FMCG sector showing revival signs with easing inflation, steady consumption, and supportive policy environment; rural markets strong, urban demand improving but value-driven
items.quote: We entered Q3 with a favorable macro backdrop. The FMCG sector has begun showing signs of revival, aided by easing inflation, steady consumption and the supportive policy environment.

items.statement: Rural markets remained strong supported by good monsoons, stable farm income and sustained government spending; urban demand improved as quarter progressed
items.quote: Rural markets remained strong, supported by good monsoons, stable farm income and sustained government spending. Urban demand too improved as the quarter progressed, although it remains value-driven and highly competitive, particularly in online channels.

items.statement: Fabric Care delivered 9.2% value growth driven primarily by volume; Liquid detergents posted high double-digit volume growth profitably despite price cuts
items.quote: Fabric Care delivered a 9.2% value growth, driven primarily by volume. Our entire Liquid Detergent portfolio across Ujala, Henko, Mr. White and Morelight continued to perform strongly.

items.statement: Dishwash category saw 7% volume growth despite 1.3% value decline due to price reductions, grammage increases and promotional offers
items.quote: Dishwash category saw 7% volume growth despite a 1.3% value decline, an outcome of price reductions, grammage increases and promotional offers.

items.statement: Personal Care segment returned to profitable growth with nearly 11% value growth primarily volume-led; Margo franchise performed well across channels
items.quote: Personal Care segment returned to profitable growth in Q3. It grew by nearly 11% in value, primarily volume-led. The post-GST disruption in September and October was resolved by November.

items.statement: HI segment posted 12.6% value growth driven by volume; coil sales declined but offset by liquid vaporizer growth; Maxo Aerosol scaling up well
items.quote: The segment posted 12.6% value growth driven by volume. Coil sales continued to decline, but the drop was more than offset by a decent volume growth in liquid vaporizers.

items.statement: Gross margin for Q3 was 46.5%, lower by 330 bps YoY due to MRP cuts, lower sales realization in Dishwash and Liquid Detergent, and elevated input prices of LABSA, SLES
items.quote: Gross margin for the quarter was 46.5%, lower by 330 basis points year-on-year. Gross margins remained under pressure due to MRP cuts and lower sales realization, especially in the Dishwash and Liquid Detergent categories and elevated input prices of select commodities such as LABSA, SLES, etcetera.

items.statement: EBITDA margin stood at 15%, nearly 150 bps lower vs Q3 last year; Operating EBITDA INR111 crores, PAT INR81 crores
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 15%, nearly 150 basis points lower compared to Q3 of last financial year. Operating EBITDA for Q3 stood at INR111 crores and PAT was at INR81 crores.

items.statement: Gross margin likely to remain subdued over next couple of quarters at minimum due to geopolitical situation, forex/crude unpredictability, and competitive intensity
items.quote: Given the current geopolitical situation and resultant unpredictability in the forex and crude prices, coupled with increased competitive intensity, the gross margin is likely to remain subdued over the next couple of quarters at the minimum.

items.statement: Dishwash competitive intensity escalated with multiple players dropping MRPs and pushing larger packs impacting average realizations; pricing action downward revision 8-9% at portfolio level
items.quote: See, our pricing action, downward pricing revision at a portfolio level would be between 8% and 9% in Dishwash category.

items.statement: Liquid detergents posted high double-digit volume growth in profitable manner despite price cuts with several players reducing MRPs and offering higher grammage
items.quote: Liquid detergents posted high double-digit volume growth in a profitable manner despite price cuts with several players reducing MRPs and offering higher grammage.

items.statement: Elevated input prices of select commodities such as LABSA, SLES, noodles; no respite seen in key raw materials on YoY or sequential basis
items.quote: In our context, if you look at the key raw materials such as LABSA, SLES or noodles for that matter, we have not seen a respite in these key commodities, which is bulk of our raw material procurement.

items.statement: HI segment expected to turn around completely by end of FY27; coil share reduced from 50% to one-third of HI revenue over last 3-4 quarters
items.quote: And as indicated earlier, maybe by the end of FY '27, we are quite positive that we should be able to turn around this completely and we'll be out of woods.

items.statement: A&P spend on broader time horizon will remain in 8% to 9% range; current quarter at 7.7% of revenue
items.quote: Advertisement and promotion spends were at 7.7% of revenue. However, our A&P spend on a broader time horizon will remain in 8% to 9% range.

items.statement: Volume value gap likely to persist in near term at 2% to 3% range; trend expected to continue
items.quote: In the near term, the volume value gap is likely to persist to the range of 2% to 3%. And if you see it, in every quarter, you are seeing volume value gap of 2% to 3%.

items.statement: Direct reach expansion: reached 13 lakh retail outlets directly last year, targeting 14 lakh this year (adding 1 lakh outlets pan-India)
items.quote: Last year, we reached about 13 lakh retail outlets directly. This year, we will we are close to closing it at 14 lakh retail outlets, which is direct reach.

items.statement: Modern trade, e-commerce, quick commerce delivered strong growth; GT faced recovery across all regions; e-commerce and quick commerce still very small portion of total revenue
items.quote: Modern trade e-commerce and quick commerce delivered strong growth for us. Encouragingly, GT faced a recovery across all regions in the country, marking a welcome shift after a few subdued quarters.

items.statement: Dishwash competitive intensity high; largest player in market resorting to price cuts and downgrading brand; local players not taking such actions
items.quote: No, no. It is the large player, very well-known player, the largest player in the market who is resorting to these kind of cheap tricks. They have literally downgraded their brand and brought it to this level.

items.statement: HI segment coil share reduced to one-third of total HI revenue from 50% previously; focus on growing LV and NPDs profitably; Maxo Aerosol scaling up
items.quote: Now coiI stands at one-third of total HI revenue as we speak. So in the last 3, 4 quarters, there has been a lot of work which has been done on the LV side.

items.statement: Revenue from operations Q3 INR740 crores, value growth 5.1%, volume growth 7.2% YoY; 9M revenue INR2,227 crores, value growth 2.2%, volume growth 4.5%
