items.quote: Revenue from operations for Q3 stood at INR740 crores, reflecting value growth of 5.1% and volume growth of 7.2% year-on-year.

items.statement: 9M gross margin 47.5% vs 50.4% last year; operating EBITDA margin 15.9% vs 17.8%; PAT INR266 crores vs INR294 crores
items.quote: For the 9 months period ended 31st December 2025, revenue from operations stood at INR2,227 crores. Gross margin was 47.5% compared to 50.4% in the same period last year, while operating margin EBITDA margin was 15.9% against 17.8% in the previous period.

items.statement: Divested JV JKBL in Bangladesh after 10+ years due to cheaper products availability and operational issues; sold stake to minority shareholder in March last year; focused on domestic growth and select export markets (Middle East, Southeast
items.quote: We have put in a number of years in making inroads in Bangladesh market and through our subsidiary, JKBL. More than 10 years, we tried that market. It's a difficult market, and we tried a number of things in order to expand our presence over there.

items.statement: New labour codes impact assessed; pay structure already aligns with revised wage definitions; financial impact negligible; will continue tracking developments
items.quote: With the introduction of India's new labour codes, we have assessed the likely impact and made necessary disclosures based on ICAI guidance. Given that our pay structure already aligns with the revised wage definitions, the financial impact remains negligible.

items.statement: Geopolitical volatility and forex fluctuations remain watch points; near-term margin pressures persist in Dishwash and Liquid Detergent due to reduced MRPs and input cost inflation
items.quote: Geopolitical volatility and forex fluctuations continue to remain watch points. We remain cautiously optimistic about the sustained recovery in consumption.

items.statement: Laundry business (Fabric Spa) has 200+ outlets across few states; growing reasonably well, not incurring cash losses; first goal to arrest losses achieved; profitability may take time
items.quote: And under Fabric Spa brand, we have 200-plus outlets spread across a few states. We are growing reasonably well in this segment. We are not incurring cash losses over there.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 top line expected around INR1,100 crores; EBITDA margins similar to Q3 range; FY27 expected better than FY26 but no exact numbers given
items.quote: Q4 is going to be slightly better than Q3. And so overall, we should touch a top line of about INR1,100 crores. And EBITDA margins, as you're already seeing, will be around that range.

items.statement: PM2 upgrade INR45 crores (30-day shutdown in Feb 2026); PM3 upgrade INR140 crores (45-day shutdown in May 2026); part of INR735 crores overall plan financed by banks and internal accruals
items.value: INR45 crores PM2, INR140 crores PM3
items.quote: PM 2 upgrade is about INR45 crores and PM 3 upgrade will be about INR140 crores. And this is part of the overall plan of INR735 crores, which we've already shared on several occasions in the past. And the entire upgradation sort of stands financed by banks and internal accruals.

items.statement: Launched Kuantum Kopio copier brand (65, 70, 75 GSM) well received; developed Kuantum Pura on PM3 with 65% agro pulp furnish for sustainable solutions; specialty papers (coloured copier, straw/cup/soap wrapping base) small volume high margi
items.quote: we have launched Kuantum Kopio, our new dedicated Copier brand available in 65, 70 and 75 GSM, which has been received very well by our dealer network and the consumers. Addit ionally, we have successfully developed a new product on our PM 3 with the name of Kuantum Pura, utilizing a 65% Argo Pulp

items.statement: 100+ functional dealers (business partners) keen to absorb entire additional capacity; no marketing issues
items.quote: We are very, very sort of blessed to have the network that we have. We've created it over a period of time, and we have with us about 100-plus functional dealers. We call them our business partners now, and they are very keen to take up the entire additional capacity within their own network.

items.statement: Long-term debt currently INR600-650 crores; peak long-term debt INR750 crores; repayment ~INR30 crores/quarter; working capital facility INR100 crores (70-80% utilized); confident of prepayment capability from FY27 cash flows (INR1,800 cr r
items.value: INR600-650 crores current, INR750 crores peak
items.quote: As of now, the peak debt, as you asked, it will be not more than INR750 crores for long-term loan. And as the repayment of, say, around INR30 crores per quarter will be repaid. So as of now, it is somewhere around INR600 crores to INR650 crores, but peak debt will be INR750 crores.

items.statement: INR735 crores overall capex plan financed by banks and internal accruals; no new fund raise mentioned
items.quote: And the entire upgradation sort of stands financed by banks and internal accruals.

items.statement: No share buyback planned; focus on increasing shareholder/investor value through growth; promoter taxation changes not prompting buyback
items.quote: No, I think I would want more our inve stors to be happy. If they grow, I'm happy. So, I would not want to take away that opportunity from them. I'm happy where I am. And in fact, my focus is to increase shareholder value, investor value

items.statement: Project Nirmaan (Industry 4.0): advanced process control baseline study completed for PM4, Phase 1 rollout and tests planned Jan-Feb 2026; MACS system stable in wood/agro bleaching; Agro Cook trials progressing to optimize pulping yields
items.quote: Under Project Nirmaan, our Ind ustry 4.0 led transformative initiative, we have successfully completed the advanced process control baseline study for PM 4 with Phase 1 rollout and the necessary tests planned for Jan and Feb of 2026 now. Simultaneously, our MACS system is delivering stable operations in the wood and agro bleaching, and we are currently progressing with the Agro Cook trials to furt

items.statement: Agro fiber scarcity from Punjab floods impacting pricing this quarter and next; import pressure from ASEAN/China on pricing sentiment; GST on notebooks at 0% forces ITC reversal costing ~INR7,500/ton (passed on to customers); rupee volatili
items.quote: So, this is quite a double-edged sword because if we, as a company or any company is, wanting to sell notebooks at 0%, they are also forced to reverse the input tax credit that they have availed on their inputs as well as capital items that they have spent on. So, for us, as an industry, the impact is close to about INR7,500 per ton.

items.statement: Expects Q4 FY26 EBITDA margins similar to Q3 (~23%) if prices hold
items.quote: Provided prices hold, which is what we expect it to be, we expect it to be sort of similar.

items.statement: Targets FY27 ferrochrome production of ~400,000 tonnes and FY28 475,000-500,000 tonnes
items.quote: we have indicated that w e expect production volume in FY '27 to be approximately 400,000 tonnes, and we expect the volume in FY '28 to be between 475,000 to 500,000

items.statement: Ethanol project (120 KLD) commissioning March 2026; top-line contribution from April 2026 (FY27)
items.quote: Finally, in as much as the ethanol project is concerned, that's again at a very advanced stage, and we expect to commission it in March 2026, that is next month. So, there is a slight delay because we were initially targeting the second half of February, but there's been a slight spillover on that, and we are expecting to commission it in March. And this is something after the initial sort of stab

items.statement: Primarily long-term contracts with binding offtake; spot sales are repeat sales to same customers; no new customer spot sales
items.quote: We have primarily long-term contracts, Akshita. The difference between the 2 categories of long-term contracts is where we have binding offtake contracts for 1 year or 5 years as in the case of POSCO. But what we technically categorize as spot sales is repeat sales to the same customers without any monthly or annual commitment. So, we don't really do spot sales where we find new customers and all

items.statement: Domestic ferrochrome prices INR118,000-120,000/t; Chinese prices USD0.96-0.97/lb; expects similar levels in Q4
items.quote: Now as far as Q4 is concerned, there was a slight dip in prices, but now they have again moved back up. So domestic prices are roughly in the INR118,000 to INR120,000 a tonne mark, and Chinese prices are around USD0.96 to USD0.97. Now, we expect these prices to continue during the ongoing quarter, barring any exceptional situations, which I don't foresee at this point in time to be very clear.

items.statement: Metallurgical coke consumption ~USD250/t (INR28,000/t); expects slight increase (USD5/t or more) in coming quarter
items.quote: Broadly, we are currently consuming coke, which is around USD250 a tonne mark, and we are expecting that to move up a little bit in future procurements. Sureshbabu Chigurupalli: It is around INR28,000 and USD5 are expected to rise in the coming

items.statement: Long-term debt drawn ~INR80 cr of INR470 cr sanctioned; peak debt expected INR450-470 cr; debt/equity max 0.5, likely ≤0.3
items.value: INR80 cr drawn, INR470 cr sanctioned, peak INR450-470 cr
items.quote: Broadly, at the moment, our, the long -term debt drawdown against the sanctioned limit is just short of INR80 crores. The sanctioned amount is INR470 crores but depending upon how the ongoing and the next quarters go, we may not even draw down the full debt amount. We'll see how that, but theoretically, the maximum it will go up to is INR450 crores, INR470 crores. And from a debt equity point of v

items.statement: Tata acquisition (INR610 cr base + GST + NWC ~INR700 cr outflow) funded from internal accruals; KNR1 has INR470 cr loan sanction
items.quote: Just to remind everyone that as far as our acquisition is concerned, which is at a base price of INR610 crores plus GST plus net working capital, that's going to be funded entirely out of internal accruals, and in as much as our KNR 1 project is concerned, we do have a loan sanction of about, lffl fa Indian Metals & INR470 odd crores

items.statement: Export share >90% currently; targets 60-40 export-domestic in 2 years
items.quote: Very heavily skewed towards exports in excess of 90%. Going ahead, in 2 years' time, we are expecting 60-40 still slightly in favor of exports, but certainly more sort of more focus on the domestic market to ensure that demand is properly met.

items.statement: South Africa special tariff (USD0.087/kWh) for Glencore/Samancor seen as uncertain/sustainable; may be zero-sum if Chinese ore imports fall
items.quote: But that's predicated on a couple of things. One, that as we understand that the tariff of USD0.87 covers broadly Eskom's variable cost and some degree of legacy costs, but not their full overheads. So that in itself, to my mind, cast some sort of uncertainty about how practicable this is. And secondly, that NERSA has also said that the difference betwe en the tariff to be paid by these 2 customer

items.statement: Started producing niche ferrochrome (0.15% P max, 1.5% Si max) with ~25% premium; selling to specific customers in Japan
items.quote: Now with added tonnage, we will certainly look at certain niche geographies and all of that, plus we have also started producing niche ferrochrome with 015 phosphorus maximum and 1.5% silicon maximum, which has a significant premium of about 25% or so. For that, we are selling now, starting to sell to some specific customers in Japan.

items.statement: Key customers: POSCO (JV + 5-yr contract), Taiwan, Japan, China, small Europe volumes; long-term oriented strategy
items.quote: We have a joint venture with POSCO alongside a long -term contract. We sell to customers in Taiwan, in Japan, we do have sales in China. We sell small quantities in Europe, which will probably we will look to perhaps increase a little bit when we expand our capacity.

items.statement: Evaluating critical minerals opportunities (mining & processing) aligned with govt PLI & corridor; will invest only if value-accretive
items.quote: It's an area which we have identified as a potential area of interest for us because there is a degree of similarity because it involves mining and processing of minerals. That's something that we are closely evaluating. And when we find the right opportunity, which is value accretive, we will move forward on it.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 ferrochrome production 67,196 t; sales 64,802 t; power generation 256.17 MU; chrome ore raising 265,468 t
items.value: 67,196 t production, 64,802 t sales, 256.17 MU power, 265,468 t ore
items.quote: Ferrochrome production during the quarter has been 67,196 tonnes. Power generation stands at 256.17 million units and chrome ore raising during the quarter is 265,468 tonnes . And if you look at sales of ferrochrome during the quarter, that stood at 64,802 tonnes.

items.statement: FY26 production target ~265,000 t; sales similar; FY27 jump from KNR1 & KNR2
items.quote: We expect in terms of production for the ongoing FY '26 we expect to close at about 265,000 tonnes and sales broadly similar numbers. lffl fa Indian Metals & The real jump, of course, will come from Q1 FY '27 onwards when additional volumes come into play

items.statement: Tata Steel Kalinganagar ferrochrome plant acquisition: 99 MVA (4x16.5 MVA operational + 1x33 MVA partial), base INR610 cr + GST + NWC; 5th furnace completion ~1 yr, INR50 cr
items.quote: You're right. The unit has 4 16.5 MVA furnaces, which are capable of producing 100,000 tonnes, which are good to go. And there is a 33 M VA furnace, which is partially complete, which can produce another 50,000 tonnes. Our estimate is approximately a year's time and roughly INR50 crores of capex to make that operational. So, when we take control of the unit, our first focus will be on maximizing o

items.statement: Will consider shareholder suggestion on stock split (face value INR1/2) for liquidity; no decision yet
items.quote: Thank you, Amitji, for your suggestion. We will certainly take that under consideration. I know this topic has come up about having adequate floating stock to provide liquidity, but there are pros and cons to everything, but this is certainly, we will certainly take your suggestion on board and always have the interest of shareholders paramount when we look at taking any actions.

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance Rs 1,300-1,400 crore; EBITDA margin target ~12%
items.quote: For FY 2026 already for nine months our sales are around Rs. 1,100 crores, so we expect to close the year between Rs. 1,300 crores to Rs. 1,400 crores.

items.statement: Q3 demand hit by 49% above-average October rainfall, low pest pressure, high trade inventory
items.quote: October 2025 witnessed exceptionally high rainfall across the country. India recorded rainfall that was nearly 49% higher than the long-period average, making it the second highest October rainfall since 2001.

items.statement: Q3 gross margin held at 32% despite revenue drop; EBITDA margin improved to 1.9% from -2.1% YoY
items.quote: Despite the unfavorable seasonal conditions, we were able to maintain gross margins of 32%.

items.statement: Nine-month EBITDA margin 11.5%; PAT Rs 46.1 crore vs Rs 91.8 crore YoY
items.quote: EBITDA for nine months FY 2026 was Rs. 127 crores, with an EBITDA margin of 11.5%, while PAT for the period was Rs. 46.1 crore, compared to Rs. 91.8 crore in nine months FY 2025.

items.statement: Patented portfolio sales down only 5% YoY in 9M; non-patent down 48%; two new patented products each crossed 4 lakh treated acres
items.quote: Each product has crossed more than 4 lakh treated acres, which is a strong validation of our innovation efforts.

items.statement: Capex on hold; existing capacity sufficient for Rs 2,000+ crore revenue; will revisit in 4-5 months
items.quote: Yes, it is still on hold. We will think about it four, five months down the line, not now.

items.statement: Current capacity can support Rs 2,000+ crore revenue without additions
items.quote: Based on our existing capacity, we can do Rs. 2,000-plus crore. So, capacity is not a constraint.

items.statement: OPEX (ex-depreciation) cut 36% in Q3 and 20% in 9M; sales & marketing spend high for new product launches
items.quote: Operationally, we focused on cost optimization with OPEX, excluding the financial depreciation, reduced by 36% in Q3 and 20% over nine months.

items.statement: Shift from generic to patented portfolio; patented products stable, generics down sharply
items.quote: Despite the overall decline, the patented portfolio remained relatively stable, with only a 5% reduction, whereas the non-patent portfolio declined by 48%.

items.statement: Stricter sales return policies reduced returns 40-45% YoY in 9M; Q3 provision Rs 70 cr vs actual Rs 90 cr returns
items.quote: Overall nine months to nine months, we have improved a lot, 40% to 45% sales return we have reduced.

items.statement: Receivables delayed ~1 month due to late government payments to farmers; collections Dec-Apr
items.quote: This year mostly it has been delayed by a month or so, but we do not see any major surprises as I said. So, most of our collections will happen now between December to April.

items.statement: Interest cost Rs 50-55 crore annually; charging dealers interest on delayed payments to offset
items.quote: Sir, because we are already paying Rs. 50 crore to Rs. 55 crore interest to the bank and our profitability is below since last few years.

items.statement: Preferential issue 25% received used for working capital; balance 75% (Rs 64 pre-split, Rs 42 post-split) awaited; no Plan B yet
items.quote: Yes, yes, so the 25% amount what we got, those as part of our utilization, this thing we already utilized it for the working capital purpose.

items.statement: Export registrations progressing in Sri Lanka, Vietnam, Morocco; China subsidiary trading; revenue visibility from FY27
items.quote: From the year that is 2027 onward, you should be able to see a good amount of revenue.

items.statement: Three new formulation patents granted; one process patent for intermediate; four international patent applications filed
items.quote: We secured three patents for novel combination formulation. In addition, we were awarded a process patent for an intermediate with export potential.

items.statement: El Nino risk for FY27; managing via cautious inventory placement and supply chain preparation
items.quote: El Nino effect might be there, but it will show only in July-August, but before that we have to prepare ourselves with the inventory, which we will do, but we will go with a caution.

items.statement: Total addressable market for patented portfolio ~$3.5 billion
items.quote: But yes, as others are playing, we are playing in the overall market which is around $3.5 billion or so.

items.statement: Sales team restructuring and territory realignment completed; team now stable
items.quote: Even our sales team is more stable now. Because last year, because of restructuring of territories, there might be situation where people are moving from one place to another. But now everything is pretty stable.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 15%+ maintained, split into ~10% volume and ~5% ARPP growth
items.quote: We continue to maintain our guidance of 15%+. But as I said, our aspiration would be to do better than that. But as of now, the guidance stays the same.

items.statement: EBITDA margin aspiration of 23-24%+ in three to four years
items.quote: Our aspiration, of course, is to be 23% - 24% plus in the three-to-four-year period, and we are very confident of delivering that.

items.statement: ROCE target of ~20% in next four to five years
items.quote: We feel we are confident of delivering the ROCE margins that we have committed in our Investor Day deck of about 20% in the next four to five years.

items.statement: FY26 capex expected at INR 275-280 crore; FY27 capex 10-12% higher
items.quote: For capex this year, our expected closure is about INR 275 crore - INR 280 crore of capex and next year, probably about 10% - 12% higher than that.

items.statement: North Bangalore greenfield (120+ beds) to commence by end of Q4 FY26 with MR-LINAC; Whitefield greenfield and 20 beds added to Bangalore CoE
items.quote: The North Bangalore facility with a planned capacity of over 120 beds is expected to commence operations by the end of Q4 FY '26, with clinician hiring largely completed. It will be the first in Bangalore to offer MR -LINAC technology, creating a strong clinical and technology-led differentiation.

items.statement: Brownfield expansions: ~60 beds at Cuttack by end FY27; 20 beds at Bangalore CoE; expansions across Vizag, Kolkata, Ranchi, KR Road, Ahmedabad, Bhavnagar, Borivali (20-60 beds each)
items.quote: We will be adding about 60 beds to our Cuttack Hospital, which is expected to be operationalized by the end of FY '27.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 adjusted EBITDA INR 111 crore, margin 17.5% (up from 16.5% YoY); 9M FY26 margin 18.3% (+60 bps YoY)
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA for Q3FY26 was INR 111 crore, reflecting a 20% year -on-year growth with EBITDA margins expanding to 17.5% from 16.5% during Q3 FY '25.

items.statement: Margin expansion driven by operating leverage from improved utilization; medical oncology mix dilutive to gross margin but positive for EBITDA
items.quote: Margin expansion during the quarter was driven by operating leverage as the utilization of the hospitals improved. This was achieved through continued investments in clinical talent, technology and infrastructure, which remain essential to suppo rting long-term growth.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 revenue INR 633 crore (+13.4% YoY); ex-fertility INR 618 crore with 8% patient volume growth; 9M FY26 revenue INR 1,893 crore (+16% YoY)
items.quote: Q3 is typically seasonally softer for the health care services industry. Despite this, HCG delivered revenues of INR 633 crore, representing a year -on-year growth of 13.4%.

items.statement: Outpatient volumes +26% YoY, inpatient volumes +37% YoY in Q3 despite traffic decline from Google Ads disruption
items.quote: While traffic declined due to external disruptions in Google Ads, outpatient volumes grew 26% and inpatient volumes grew 37%, clearly indicating higher conversion, better case mix and superior demand quality.

items.statement: ARPP ~INR 84,000 (+5% YoY); medical oncology ramp-up (immunotherapy, CAR-T) improving case mix; East ARPP -3% YoY due to Odisha scheme transition
items.quote: Average revenue per patient, including our fertility business during Q3FY26 stood at approximately INR 84,000, marking a year-on-year increase of 5%.

items.statement: Digital revenue +26% YoY with paid media spend reduction; website 67% of digital, app 13% (4.5x scale); aggregator share down 12% to 9%
items.quote: In Q3 FY26, digital revenue grew 26% year-on-year despite a meaningful reduction in paid media spend. Our own channels strengthened materially. The website remained the primary contributor at 67% of the overall digital contribution, while the mobile app scaled 4.5x to contribute 13% to our digital revenues.

items.statement: ~45% patients come after opinion at multi-specialty hospitals; medical tourism 3.5% of revenue, target 7% in 4 years
items.quote: Currently, it is about 3.5%, Rajat, and our endeavour is to take it to about 7% in the next four years.

items.statement: CGHS norms and GST cut on drugs had marginal impact, offset by pricing/consumption changes; CGHS neutral at company level
items.quote: As far as GST is concerned, there was a marginal impact on the top line as well as margin and we were able to offset that by some initiatives that we took within the organization around pricing and consumption. So that's been offset because of that. As far as CGHS is concerned, yes, there was some immediate impact, but we have been able to offset that too by changing consumption patterns in our ho

items.statement: Andhra Pradesh strike (20-25 days) impacted volumes but receivables improved: Q3 billing INR 25 crore, net receivable addition INR 5 crore
items.quote: The fact that Q3 had a billing of about INR 25 crore, but we had a net receivable addition benefit of INR 5 crore. So, net-net, there is a positive flow from the government side as far as the receivables are concerned.

items.statement: Rights issue announced to strengthen balance sheet and capital structure; specifics after Board meeting
items.quote: So, Ali, we believe that an equity infusion at this stage will strengthen the company's balance sheet and the capital structure. And that is directionally why the rights issue is there. But at this point in time, that is all I can divulge. But very shortly, we will share the specifics after our Board meets.

items.statement: New regional business head appointed for East cluster (30+ years experience) to support execution
items.quote: During Q3 FY26, cluster leadership in the East was further strengthened with the appointment of a new regional business head, bringing over three decades of experience in East India markets, which is expected to support execution and performance consistency going forward.

items.statement: Pre-tax ROCE 13.3% for 9M FY26; mature centres at 28-30% ROCE; target 20% company-level ROCE in 4-5 years
items.quote: In terms of returns, pre -tax ROCE stood at 13.3% for the 9 M FY '26. We expect ROCE to continue to trend higher over time as incremental growth can be achieved with relatively limited capital deployment, enabling returns to improve as fixed costs are absorbed more efficiently.

items.statement: Andhra Pradesh strike (20-25 days) caused volume disruption in Vizag; impact normalized within quarter
items.quote: The strike did impact our volumes because the Vizag market is a big market for us whe re we are the dominant players. The strike continued for twenty- twenty-five days, and it did impact the subsequent month volumes as well because for cancer, that is the kind of nuance we have

items.statement: Founder contract amendment one-time cost of INR 2 crore to hit in Q4, not Q3
items.quote: So, to your first question, the impact of that amendment will come in Q4. We have not taken that in Q3.

items.statement: Q4 expected to be best quarter of FY26; North Bangalore greenfield impact visible from Q1 FY27
items.quote: Obviously, Q4 is trending better than Q3. And our hope is that it will be the best quarter for us this financial year. But the impact of North Bangalore, we will only be able to see in Q1 coming in because from the time of operationalizing to the business impact will probably take us a quarter.

items.statement: Mumbai cluster grew high teens in revenue and exponential EBITDA growth; Kolkata consolidated, needs clinical talent infusion
items.quote: Mumbai market has done exceptionally well for us. We have grown quite strongly in the whole of last year at high teens. And not just in revenue terms, but in EBITDA terms as well, it is been an exponential growth for us.

items.statement: Gross margin declined to ~72% from ~75% due to medical oncology mix (pharmacy costs); offset by EBITDA operating leverage
items.quote: So, Devang, it is largely driven by our case mix change, which is favouring medical oncology. The ramp-up in medical oncology and pharmacy costs has been slightly margin dilutive, but we are working towards increasing our case mix and improving our payor mix, which should offset that in the ensuing quarters.

items.statement: Corporate initiatives on revenue leakage reduction, procurement optimization, clinical density enhancement, and data/AI analytics driving margin expansion
items.quote: In the last four-five months, we have started work on several value creation initiatives around revenue leakage, reducing revenue leakage, improving conversions. There is work that is being done on procurement optimization, and we have seen that flow into our margin and EBITDA as well.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 revenue expected to be close to 1,900 crores full-year run-rate; Q4 FY26 revenue growth expected over Q4 FY25 (~500 crores)
items.quote: Right now the way we look at it and the schedules what we have from the various AMISPs, I think we should do a fairly good turnover in for the smart metering and the consumer and industrial also is set for another good quarter and a good growth.

items.statement: C&I segment revenue targeting 1,000 crores in FY27
items.quote: Although I don't give too much of a guidance many times, but I think the C&I next year we should be looking at probably crossing let's say thousand crores in a way or coming close to that.

items.statement: Management sees 20-25% topline growth achievable in FY27 over FY26
items.quote: I think it is achievable and internally when probably by next month when we are finalizing our budget for the next year internally with our teams I think that is something that should be minimum required.

items.statement: Smart metering order book over 3,000 crores providing multi-year visibility
items.quote: We currently have an order book of over 3,000 crores, which gives us clear multi-year visibility.

items.statement: Smart metering deliveries up 25% sequentially and 11% year-on-year in Q3
items.quote: Deliveries increased by around 25% sequentially and were up about 11% year-on-year.

items.statement: Switchgear grew over 33% yoy in Q3 to 68 crores; wires & cables up nearly 60% yoy; lighting & electronics up ~20% yoy
items.value: Switchgear 68 crores, +33% yoy; Wires & cables +60% yoy; Lighting & electronics +20% yoy
items.quote: Switchgear grew by over 33% year-on-year in Q3 to roughly 68 crores and by 25% in the first 9 months to 233 crores. Wire and cables recorded strong growth of nearly 60% year-on-year in Q3, while lighting and electronics returned to growth at around 20%.

items.statement: Expect industry smart meter installations of 5 crore per annum over next 2-3 years; HPL confident of supplying its share
items.quote: I think that seems to be a possibility of having at least 5 cr meters being implemented. Of course I cannot talk for the AMISPs or the government but just my sense of the way we read the market, I think that should not be a big problem for the industry to achieve those figures.

items.statement: Copper price increases passed on to consumers with 2-3 week lag in wires & cables, 3-6 month lag in switchgear; margins under pressure but cost eventually passed on
items.quote: So any increase in the cost is getting passed on to the consumer but with a lag. So the maximum impact would happen in the wire and cable where typically it takes two to three weeks to pass on the cost to the consumer.

items.statement: Launched NRAM plus smart water meters, expanding metering platform into water infrastructure
items.quote: We have recently launched NRAM plus smart water meters, expanding our metering platform into water infrastructure.

items.statement: Actively evaluating entry into HT and EHV cables; expect update within calendar year
items.quote: We have been studying the market to go into the higher kind of cables going up to HT and then EHV. It's a progression which typically for any good company would take 3 to 5 years to actually come out with those ranges. But yes we are actively looking at it and to come into the higher set of cables.

items.statement: Distribution network expanded to over 900 authorized dealers and 85,000+ retailers
items.quote: We now work with over 900 authorized dealers and more than 85,000 retailers, which is helping us improve reach, improve conversions, and build repeat demand across markets.

items.statement: Significant room for deeper penetration in Tier 2/3 cities; new channel partner appointments planned in Feb-May
items.quote: Yes, I think if you see, like we are present in all the states, but still the penetration into tier 2 and tier three I think there's a huge gap which probably we need to do that.

items.statement: Exploring export opportunities for smart meters; targeting global fairs in Dubai and Hanover; expect certifications in ~12 months
items.quote: We have upcoming fairs coming up in Dubai and in Hanover in Germany. So I think we will be pitching in now to the global market with our smart meters in a bigger way.

items.statement: UK and EU FTAs expected to boost export competitiveness for engineering products; HPL well-positioned on IEC standards
items.quote: So I think we stand as HPL electric we stand to gain from both these FTAs in a big way. Now as we read from the news that the import duties of engineering Transcribed by ElevEase 12 products into Europe would get reduced

items.statement: Smart metering policy clarity achieved; tenders awarded to AMISPs; execution challenges being addressed
items.quote: So right now the policy is clear. I think if you look at the government data, the tenders, a lot has been already given out to the AMISP, even the last bit of tenders are all on the table waiting to be given out to the AMISP.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 revenue ~475 crores (+21% yoy), EBITDA ~72 crores (+29% yoy)
items.quote: In Q3, our revenue grew by about 21% year-on-year to roughly 475 crores. EBITDA increased by about 29% to nearly 72 crores.

items.statement: 9M FY26 switchgear revenue 233 crores (+25% yoy)
items.quote: Switchgear grew by over 33% year-on-year in Q3 to roughly 68 crores and by 25% in the first 9 months to 233 crores.

items.statement: Water meter revenue contribution expected only from H2 FY27 due to approval processes
items.quote: So in terms of revenue we should start seeing something probably in the second half of next year because there are approval processes and others, but we have already initiated those.

items.statement: Order book disclosure limited due to new regulations requiring customer/price details; competitive sensitivity cited
items.quote: Under the new regulation, if any company listed company if they are to give out their order book details, it is no more one has to give out the quantity, the pricing, the customer details and other things.

items.statement: Digital transformation underway: launching 2-3 new apps to connect dealers, retailers, electricians with loyalty programs via QR codes
items.quote: We are on the way of a lot of digital transformation where we are looking to launch two three new apps in the coming months which would connect all our dealers, all our retailers and a lot of our electricians including the loyalty programs of electricians through the app and everything going digitally through the QR codes.

items.statement: R&D team of over 180 engineers across metering, switchgear, wire & cable, lighting, electronics, communication
items.quote: In HPL with over 180 engineers in R&D, which covers all Transcribed by ElevEase 7 things, not only meters but also switchgear, wire and cable, lighting, and then into lot of common technologies like electronics or communication and other things

items.statement: Indian meter quality/specifications considered superior to Chinese due to diverse utility requirements driving R&D; Indian products command premium internationally
items.quote: So if you compare one-on-one on the technology, I think India is far above and now with the smart meter in place and probably I would say one of the biggest rollouts of smart meters in the world, I think India is very well placed here.

items.statement: Supply chain consolidated from 30 peak warehouses to 6 master warehouses; improving distribution efficiency
items.quote: Because at peak time we had almost 30 warehouses in the country. Today we operate only with six master warehouses and I think our supply chain through the 900 channel partners and the retailers today is much better off.

items.statement: Digital marketing spend increased 2-3x; BTL activities strong; ATL brand building planned after C&I reaches ~1,000 crores revenue
items.quote: Our advertising has seen a stronger push mainly in the digital segment where we have really probably made it 2x or 3x the spend what we were doing on the digital marketing on all the social media and other things.

items.statement: Spencer's targeting mid-single-digit top-line growth in Q4 FY26; expects operational EBITDA breakeven for Spencer's in two quarters (Q1 FY27)
items.quote: Q4, I can give some guidance that on the Spencer's part of the business, we are looking at good growth. We will get to, I would say, mid -single-digit growth as far as Spencer's is concerned on top line.

items.statement: Targeting 100,000 paid members by end of Q4 FY26 and doubling membership base in FY27
items.quote: We are hoping to exit this year, which is at the end of Q4 with about 100,000 members for the membership program which is, I think, in 9 months is good progress. And the intention is to see how we can double that in the year going forward.

items.statement: E-commerce sales targeting close to INR200 crores for FY26; out-of-store mix target 20% by early Q1 FY27
items.quote: We will exit this financial year with close to INR200 crores coming from our e -commerce business alone, phone deliveries extra. And I think that's a good jump from where we were last year.

items.statement: Jiffy orders target 300,000 per month from current ~240,000 without disturbing unit economics; no dark store additions
items.quote: We need to get to a level of close to 300,000 orders a month. We are currently at around 240,000. So, I think that will be the level. I would measure myself more in terms of can I go from 240,000 orders a month to 300,000 orders a month without disturbing the unit economics.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin 21.2% in Q3 FY26; Spencer's at 20% (up 40bps QoQ, 30bps YoY); Nature's Basket dropped 300bps YoY to ~27%
items.quote: Our gross margins, despite a little bit of a blip in Nature's Basket have been commendable 21.2% gross margin consolidated level, Spencer's at 20%.

items.statement: Nature's Basket margin expected to recover to 29-30% range; Spencer's sustainable at 19.7-20%
items.quote: We are quite confident that this is something which we will fix because the true margins of this business have to be what we have delivered in the past, in the region of 29 -30%.

items.statement: No further one-off Labour Code provisions expected; Q4 operating expenses to reflect true run-rate
items.quote: On operating expenses, we don't see any more one -off provisions on account of the new Labour code. They've been largely baked in, in Q3. So, we will come back to the true operating costs in Q4.

items.statement: Spencer's offline sales flat YoY in Sep-Dec period; online grew 27% YoY to INR54 crores; membership driving 3x spend and 2x frequency
items.quote: Online in Q3 for us has grown compared to Q3 of last year, by 27%. So, we delivered close to INR54 crores in sales on Jiffy, which is the online platform.

items.statement: Staples, fresh, processed food and beverages driving growth; home care and personal care outperforming beauty
items.quote: If I look at it from a category point of view, what is really firing growth for us is staples and fresh, which are important ones because they are the m onthly planned shopping basket and we are getting a higher share of that, which is

items.statement: Membership program at 70,000+ paid members (10-11% of active base); members spend INR7,500/month (3x non-members), shop 4+ times/month (2x), 80%+ N+1 retention
items.quote: We exited Q3 with more than 70,000 members who have registered and paid for this membership, which is roughly about 10 -11% of our active monthly customer base.

items.statement: Members contribute ~25% of sales and 15-16% of bills; recruitment focused offline but benefits apply omnichannel
items.quote: Just to give you a colour, I mean, these members account for close to 25% of overall sales and 15 -16% of total number of bills in a month.

items.statement: Jiffy unit economics positive in Q3: RGM per order ~INR100, fulfilment cost INR94, net INR6/order; AOV INR775, in-full 93.5%, cancellations <3%, on-time 92%, delivery <30 min
items.quote: We make roughly about INR100 plus as far as our RGM per order is concerned, and our fulfilment cost is INR94. So, we make about INR6. Now obviously, this is at a contribution margin.

items.statement: Jiffy monthly orders ~235,000 in Q3 (avg); target 300,000/month; online losses reduced from INR12 cr (Q2) to INR9 cr (Q3)
items.quote: Our number of orders in Q3 of this year was close to 235,000 orders per month at an average.

items.statement: Consolidated SPSF ~INR1,800/sq ft/month; Spencer's offline EBITDA losses halved in 9M FY26 vs 9M FY25
items.quote: At a consol level, we are at about INR1,800 a square foot per month. But I think there is opportunity for us to grow that.

items.statement: No aggressive store additions in Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27; only relocations (Lucknow, East) from underperforming stores
items.quote: We are not going to add on too many new stores at least in Q4 and Q1. We believe we have the playbook. We have the levers to drive growth from our base of stores which are currently there.

items.statement: Inventory optimization improved availability despite constrained working capital; focus on quick-selling items; Nature's Basket stockholding high, sell-through improvement planned in Q4
items.quote: Despite, I would say, constrained working capital, we've done a good job in terms of inventory optimization, not just from days on hand optimization, which has resulted in better availability, but we focus on what we call our quick selling items and got a higher level of availability.

items.statement: Price index managed pragmatically vs offline and online competition; consistent fair pricing on staples; membership gives 6% cashback
items.quote: We are being again very pragmatic as well as I won't call it aggressive, but very mindful of our price index versus both offl ine competition and online competition.

items.statement: Not competing with large quick-commerce players on scale or burn; differentiated model using store footprint for fulfilment; fresh assortment, value, membership as hooks
items.quote: We are not in the same league as the other quick comm players which you're talking about. They have a much higher scale. They have a slightly different business model, both i n terms of acquisition of customers in fulfilment and in terms of their ability to sustain losses of far higher magnitude

items.statement: Private label ~35% of staples; strong in staples, cleaning, some packaged foods; not expanding into other categories
items.quote: Close to 35% of our staples category is accounted for by private label. So yes, private label is an integral part. But again, we have to be pragmatic enough to see which of the categories which lend themselves to private label better than certain other categories.

items.statement: Store footprint covers 99% pin codes in Calcutta; 4-5 km delivery radius; no dark store additions; using existing stores as fulfilment centres
items.quote: In cities like Calcutta, we have stores which have a coverage of at least 99% of the pin codes, and we are able to deliver within the radius of 4 -5 kilometres, which is what it is.

items.statement: Online grocery growth expected to moderate as players face P&L pressures post-IPO; no profitable online grocer globally; sustainability focus increasing
items.quote: So far, across the world, we haven't seen a profitable online grocer, right. But we have seen profitab le offline grocery retail chains across the world. So , I think, look, I mean, that says it all.

items.statement: Nature's Basket app migrated to Jiffy tech stack at end of Q2; e-commerce revamp completed; online growth expected
items.quote: We've done that migration or upgradation of the Nature's Basket app to the Jiffy's backbone. And that has been completed at the end of Q2, and we will see growth.

items.statement: Targets ROCE of 24% pretax for hydra flask plant long-term
items.quote: our target would be that we should generate a ROCE of 24%. That's our target for -- across our business.

items.statement: Expects consolidated EBITDA margin to reach low-20s in very short foreseeable future
items.quote: we should be in the low-20s in the very short foreseeable future.

items.statement: Glassware demand strong with 21% growth in 9MFY26 driven by plastic-to-glass shift
items.quote: Borosil glassware range has grown by an impressive 21% in 9 months FY '26 compared to the same period last year with a revenue of INR231 crores compared to INR 191 crores in 9-month FY '25.

items.statement: Appliances and stainless steel demand fantastic with strong growth
items.quote: As far as demand for appliances has been fantastic. Our stainless-steel, again, the same trend on health and better products, upgrading kitchens, all of those trends are leading to very strong demand in appliances and steel.

items.statement: Opalware demand growth not great at 7%, needs category refresh
items.quote: Opalware growth has not been great. And that's something I think we need to -- as an industry, we have to look into this and get some excitement back into opalware.

items.statement: Glassware margins attractive, expects to achieve or surpass opalware margins in next 2 years
items.quote: I still stand by my statement that in the next 2 years, we probably will achieve or surpass the opalware margins. I'm quite confident about that.

items.statement: Approved INR 65 crore capex for 3 double-wall vacuum insulated flask lines in Rajasthan via Stylenest
items.quote: the Board has approved the project for our upcoming manufacturing facility in Rajasthan for these bottles through our wholly owned subsidiary, Stylenest India Limited. This project includes 3 double -wall production lines for vacuum ins ulated steel flasks, bottles and containers with an estimated capacity of close to 4 million units per year with an estimated capex of approximately INR65 crores.

items.statement: Investing INR 75 crore for 20 MWp solar plant with battery storage, commissioning in Q4 FY26
items.quote: The company is further investing INR 75 crores towards setting up a 20 MWp ground-mounted solar plant with a battery energy storage system that will further reduce the overall power cost. And this project is expected to be commissioned in this month itself, that is Q4 of FY '26.

items.statement: Opalware furnace rebuild maintenance capex ~INR 15-16 crore per furnace every 2.5 years
items.quote: It's roughly per furnace about INR15 crores to INR16 crores roughly. So, we have 2 furnaces -- so it's about -- so this is the part of maintenance capex.

items.statement: Glassware brownfield expansion planning underway, announcement expected next quarter
items.quote: this is already in the planning phase, probably in the next quarter or so, we'll be a ble to make some announcements. In terms of expansion

items.statement: FY27 capex not yet approved by Board but reasonable capex expected given growth opportunities
items.quote: FY '27 capex has not been approved yet by the Board. So I would not like to take a stab at it. But it's -- we see many growth opportunities. So there will be reasonable capex in FY '27, I think.

items.statement: Hydra flask plant: 2 lines commercial production by end Q4 FY26 (March), 3rd line by end Q1 FY27
items.quote: Estimated commercial production from 2 of these lines is expected by the end of quarter 4 of this year, that is in March in the next month and from the third line by the end of quarter 1 of financial year '27, subject to receipt of necessary approvals.

items.statement: Hydra plant ramp-up to 100% utilization expected in 3-6 months
items.quote: it may take between 3 and 6 months to ramp up the facility to 100% capacity utilization.

items.statement: Opalware furnace at 95% utilization, glassware furnace at 90% utilization
items.quote: Opal is close to 100%, I would say, 95% and glass would be about 90%.

items.statement: Glassware brownfield expansion possible with 50% capacity increase at existing facility
items.quote: No, brownfield. We have space in the existing facility to expand by 50%.

items.statement: Opalware capacity expansion from 84 to 90 tons/day at next furnace reconstruction in FY27
items.quote: we operate one of the country's largest opalware facilities at 84 tons per day, which will soon b e expanded to 90 tons per day alongside a 25 ton per day borosilicate glassware plant that was commissioned in early 2024.

items.statement: Advertising spend reduced from INR 62 cr to INR 60 cr in 9MFY26 due to hydra unavailability
items.quote: Expenditure on advertising and sales promotion remained well controlled, declining from INR62 crores to INR 60 crores in this 9 months FY '26. Again, the main reason for this was a lack of availability of the bottles.

items.statement: Power and fuel costs reduced from INR 64 cr to INR 56 cr in 9MFY26
items.quote: Power and fuel costs also saw a very good reduction falling from INR64 crores to INR56 crores over the same period, underscoring the effectiveness of our ongoing cost optimization initiatives and margin-focused approach.

items.statement: Solar plant Phase 3 to cover 65% of total power requirement, reducing energy costs
items.quote: This Phase 3 of solar shall take care about 65 % of the overall power requirement of the company, which means that from -- as a large power consumer, approximately 65% of our total power will come from renewable energy sources.

items.statement: QCO for electrical appliances effective 19 March 2026; company advanced inventory and localized sourcing to mitigate impact
items.quote: Effective 19 March 2026, that is in the next month, the order mandates certification for a broad range of electrical appliances, including coffee makers and cooking ranges, hobs, ovens and similar appliances. Accordingly, the company is building up not only a domestic s upply chain, but also advancing inventory to mitigate potential sales disruptions.

items.statement: Inventory INR 324 cr (99 days) as of Dec 25, includes QCO buildup; receivables INR 120 cr (35-36 days); payables INR 83 cr
items.quote: inventory as of 31st December '25 is roughly INR 324 crores, so which is about 99 days of inventory. This includes the inventory that we are trying to build up for the appliances in terms of the quality control order, which is going to be implemented. And receivables is about 35, 36 days

items.statement: Net cash position ~INR 13 cr with INR 104 cr cash/investments and INR 91 cr total debt including working capital
items.quote: Borosil Limited maintains a strong balance sheet with investments, cash and bank balance of approximately INR104 crores and a total debt, including working capital of INR91 crores, resulting in a net cash position of roughly INR13 crores.

items.statement: Finance costs declined by INR 6 cr in 9MFY26 due to debt repayment
items.quote: finance costs declined by INR6 crores, primarily due to debt repayment in 9-month FY '26 as compared to last year.

items.statement: Hydra plant INR 65 cr capex to be financed through mix of equity, debt and internal accruals
items.quote: This investment of INR 65 crores will be financed through a mix of equity, debt and internal accruals.

items.statement: Domestic sourcing for appliances increased to ~60%, targeting 85% by end of next year
items.quote: I think we are now inching towards 60%. And I think by the end of the coming year, we'll be at 85%.

items.statement: Non-glassware appliances and cookware growing 3x industry rate, still scratching surface
items.quote: our stainless steel range and our appliances have done phenomenally well before, and they have been growing at really good rates. And we are still scratching the surface of this industry, both for appliances as well as for serving -- the serveware, cookware, stainless steel products.

items.statement: Hydra shelf space lost to competitors with local manufacturing; brand strong but supply miss acknowledged
items.quote: we have actually taken a big hit because we are not available in many of the shops and many of the large format stores and so on. So we've taken a hit that shelf space has been taken by others in this period, those who had local manufacturing. So it's been unfortunate. And I guess it's a miss on our side.

items.statement: Revenue growth commitment of 10-plus percent in constant currency for FY26 and EBITDA margin range of 20-22%
items.quote: Looking ahead, our priorities remain unchanged: delivering 10-plus percentage on revenue growth in constant currency and maintaining EBITDA margins in the 20 to 22% range. This is for the current financial year.

items.statement: Expects to show significant increase in guidance above 10% growth when Q4 results announced
items.quote: And we expect to show significant increase in the guidance we have been giving over and above the 10% growth we have committed for 4 years.

items.statement: Plans to grow AI/GenAI team to 1,000 employees by end of FY27
items.quote: Aligned to our First strategy, we plan to grow our AI/GenAI team to a 1,000 Happiest Minds by the end of FY'27 while maintaining financial discipline in the process.

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA margin 20.4% within guided 20-22% range; operating margin improved 40 bps to 17.4%
items.quote: EBITDA was INR123 crores, translating to a margin percentage of 20.4%, compared to the 20.2% in Q2. And this range of 20.4% to 20.2% is well within our guided range of 20% to 22%.

items.statement: Adjusted PAT margin improved to 11.6% from 11% in previous quarter
items.quote: adjusted PAT, which is PAT adjusted for the noncash acquisition costs and exceptional items, which includes the charge for the new wage code was at 11.6% compared to the 11% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Customer conversations becoming more decisive with focus on embedding AI into core workflows and platforms
items.quote: In Q3, we saw customer conversations becoming more decisive. Enterprises are moving beyond experimentation and are increasingly focused on embedding AI into core workflows and platforms where the business impact is clear and scalable.

items.statement: Pipeline showed significant increase during quarter with more large deals of 3-4 year tenure
items.quote: There was a significant increase in the pipeline. And the increase has been more in some of the larger deals. So, contrary to the point you made, we are actually seeing quite a few deals that are 3 to 4 years tenure.

items.statement: GBS and AI services revenues grew close to 50% quarter-over-quarter as customers move from pilots to production
items.quote: GBS and AI services saw strong momentum, with revenues growing close to 50% quarter -over- quarter as customers move decisively from pilots to product ion deployments

items.statement: 32 GenAI and Agentic AI use cases moved from prototype with several scaling into production
items.quote: We now have 32 GenAI and Agentic AI use cases that have moved from prototype, with several scaling into production.

items.statement: BFSI and Healthcare led growth; Industrial showed modest uptick; rest of portfolio stable
items.quote: From a vertical perspective, BFSI and Healthcare led growth this quarter, with Industrial showing a modest uptick while the rest of the port folio remained broadly stable

items.statement: DSO increased to 92 days from 87; focus on bringing back to 85 days
items.quote: DSO increased to 92 days from 87 in the previous quarter, and we remain focused on collections and billing discipline. The idea is to bring that back down to the 85-day number, and that's where we'll be focusing our efforts on.

items.statement: Almost all debt is working capital debt at 4.6-4.7% rate; healthy current ratio and significant cash on balance sheet
items.quote: Almost all our debt is working capital debt, Mr. Rakesh. And if you look at our current ratio, that's quite healthy. And we get -- we have a significant amount of cash on our balance sheet.

items.statement: Utilization improved to 82% in Q3, highest in recent times
items.quote: Our utilization for the quarter was 82%, and the highest in recent times.

items.statement: Constant currency revenue growth 1.2% QoQ and 7.1% YoY for Q3; 9-month growth 10.2% YoY
items.quote: For the quarter, revenue stood at $65.7 million, showing a growth sequentially and year-over-year in constant currency of 1.2% and 7.1% respectively.

items.statement: IP-led sales at 10.4% of revenue with higher gross margins than services
items.quote: It's all of this is covered in the IP-led sales which is at about 10.4% as of end of quarter.

items.statement: Proactively evangelizing productivity tools to customers; sharing productivity gains in managed services/fixed price engagements
items.quote: And what we are seeing customers come back with is new additional features, tech debt that they have, that can be managed by the same team so that the throughput increases. And we've not seen any customers come back and ramping down because of productivity increases.

items.statement: AI First positioning making tangible difference as customers prioritize AI-embedded workflows and platforms
items.quote: This is where our AI First positioning is making a tangible difference.

items.statement: Happiest Health IPO estimated at least 6 years away; revenues currently 'rather sad'
items.quote: As I said that, I would imagine IPO could be easily 6 years away.

items.statement: Participating in India AI Summit; leading state government expressed interest in MoU for long-term AI relationship
items.quote: We will be participating and I'm also happy to share with you that one of the leading state governments, I can't name this at the moment, has really been written to us saying that we'd like to meet you there.

items.quote: But I think between Thane and Mahadevapuram in Bangalore and towards the end of Q1 next financial year, we should become EBITDA positive or EBITDA neutral. Electronic City might take a little longer by because we commissioned it only in the month of December. So I think by end of Q3, Electronic City also should turn EBITDA neutral or positive.

items.statement: Kondapur new facility (850 beds) to be commissioned in 3-4 months; old 250-bed facility to shut down within 6 months; expect 20-25% YoY growth at new facility
items.quote: In 6 months, once the new building is ready, we will shut down the old hospital. And I think 20% -- 20%, 25% year-on-year growth at the new Kondapur facility is something that we are extremely confident about.

items.statement: Capex for FY27 estimated at INR500-600 crores; no plan yet for FY28 as no new hospitals commissioning
items.quote: '27, the full closure and capex will be another incremental INR500 crores to INR600 crores. And for '28, we have not yet put a plan together because there's no new hospitals that we're commissioning that.

items.statement: Debt has peaked for current expansion; should moderate quarter-on-quarter unless large new opportunities announced
items.quote: Yes, I think for the current expansion the debt numbers have peaked out. If we add more new facilities, then it could potentially go up. But for now we're almost done with most of the capex that we planned for 3 years ago.

items.statement: Chennai hospital construction on 26-year land lease expected to complete within 2 years
items.quote: KIMS entered into an agreement with Andrea Saba for its land to construct and operate a hospital at Chennai for 26 years. The construction is expected to be completed within 2 years.

items.statement: 7 new hospitals launched in 2025 across 5 states; total network now 25 hospitals
items.quote: In 2025, we launched 7 hospitals –, Bangalore – Mahadevapura and Electronic city, 2 in Guntur, Kollam in Kerala, Thane & Sangili in Maharashtra.

items.statement: Ongole 50 beds commissioned; Anantapur cancer center +75 beds by end March; Rajahmundry end Q4; Kundapur 2 end Q1; Kompali from March
items.quote: Onngol 50 beds got commissioned. That's what I just mentioned 3, 4 a week ago. Anantpur towards the end of March, we should commission the cancer center and add an incremental 75 beds of the 250 beds that we are supposed to add. Rajahmundry, were again stated towards the end of Q4. Kundapur 2 end of Q1, we are stated to start. And Kompali also from March, we will start commission the hospital.

items.statement: Secunderabad renovation of 200-250 beds to complete by H2 FY27; Kondapur new 850-bed facility in 3-4 months
items.quote: Towards the end of next year, second half of next financial year.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin 20.4% vs 25.9% YoY and 21.6% QoQ; decline due to new unit EBITDA erosion
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 20.4% versus 25.9% in Q3 FY 25 and 21.6% in Q2 FY 26.

items.statement: Nashik turned EBITDA positive in January with INR8.5 crores revenue after 13 months
items.quote: Nashik yes, there is, it took us 13 months to achieve break even and in January we are EBITDA positive in Nashik, Rahul. We've achieved almost INR8.5 crores revenue and we turned EBITDA positive.

items.statement: Kerala: Kannur ramping well; Kollam (6-7 months old) to breakeven in next 1-2 quarters; one hospital had one-time write-off in Q3
items.quote: Kollam is just 6, 7 months old. It should breakeven in the next 1, 2 quarter.

items.statement: Consolidated ARPOB grew 20.5% YoY and 10.3% QoQ; ARPP grew 13.9% YoY and 9% QoQ
items.quote: Average revenue per operating debt (ARPOB)grew by 20.5% and 10.3% on year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter basis, respectively. Average revenue per patient (ARPP) grew by 13.9% and 9% on year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter basis, respectively.

items.statement: IP volume 61,139 (+13.2% YoY, -4.9% QoQ); OP volume 585,499 (+24.5% YoY, -1.2% QoQ)
items.quote: IP volume (61,139) grew by 13.2% year-on-year and declined 4.9% quarter-on-quarter basis. OP volumes (5,85,499) an increase of 24.5% year-on-year and a decline of 1.2% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Telangana cluster ARPOB improved from INR65,000 to INR70,000 QoQ; Bangalore cluster ARPOB ~INR76,000 but may normalize to INR70,000-75,000
items.quote: Telangana was at 65,000 last quarter has now moved to 70,000 this quarter.

items.statement: Bangalore hospitals priced ~15% below competition initially; may rationalize in coming months
items.quote: Vis-a-vis in respect to competition, we are slightly priced at least at least I would say that around 15% lower in the initial days. We may rationalize it in the coming few months.

items.statement: Top 5 insurer empanelment: Nashik & Thane - 2 done, 3 more by end Q4; Kannur - all 5 done; Kollam - 2 quarters; Bangalore - 6-9 months
items.quote: There has been some progress in both units on insurance empanelments. But the top 5 companies that we wanted to do, out of which 2 are done, 3 more are to be done. We are almost in the last leg of closure on all 3 for both Nashik and Thane. It should be done by -- before the end of this quarter, quarter 4.

items.statement: State scheme empanelment only in Andhra; institutional bed/revenue share from govt schemes to decline as expand to other states
items.quote: No, we only are empanelling state schemes in Andhra, not in other states.

items.statement: Net debt INR2,850 crores as of Dec 31, 2025; includes all expansion debt; minority buyout funded from internal sources
items.quote: Chirag, it is about INR2,850-odd crores at a consolidated level as on 31st of December '25.

items.statement: Expect INR600 crores receivable from govt creditors; cash INR206 crores; debt to decline QoQ unless new large expansions
items.quote: The debt portion is even though we have INR2,800 crores, we are supposed to get nearly INR600 crores from our creditors, from mostly the state and central government, which are sent for the payment.

items.statement: No debt raised for minority stake purchase (to 9%); funded from internal sources/working capital
items.quote: For minority, we do not get any -- we have not raised any debt. But of course, it is out of the internal sources.

items.statement: No sizable M&A opportunities; only a couple of small potential acquisitions
items.quote: Nothing sizable. There are a couple of small acquisitions, potential acquisitions that have come our way, but nothing significant and sizable at this point in time.

items.statement: ~200 doctors onboarded across two Bangalore hospitals (120 Mahadevapura, 90 Electronic City); onboarding continuous for Phase 1 growth
items.quote: Yes, that's right. Close to 120 in Mahadevapura and other 90 doctors in the Electronic City unit.

items.quote: NABH in Nashik, entry level is completed. NABH and Thane is in pipeline, it will take some more time. But both of them -- for both units or any other unit, NABH is not a prerequisite for empanelment with insurance company.

items.quote: In quarter 3, we had a strike with the state government. So we had not taken Aarogyasri scheme for almost a month, and that's why you see a significant dip in volume. But otherwise, January, things have bounced back.

items.quote: But definitely the order book and the program tenure, what we have received we expect somewhere about, you know in between 12 to 14% CAGR growth on for the next three to five years.

items.quote: Operating cash flow we had for the first half it is almost 87 odd crore free cash flow what we have generated again within CAPEX of hardly 12 crore in terms of couple of furnaces and a small 4G client.

items.quote: As you are very much aware that company is having negative debt for last couple of years. Company is having surpluses which has been parked for to raise another income so overall there is a negative or rather debt equity ratio.

items.quote: Here in this quarter also PAT is being reduced by almost two and a half crore rupees. That is by way of exceptional item which is for the impact of the new labour code which has been implemented from 21st November 25.

items.quote: we are targeting to directly with the 30 customers to our DC part of container and we are targeting 4-5 government projects where we will supply DC plus AC battery energy storage system direct to the Government of India.

items.quote: We expect that the payback will be in the range of 2-3 years of time for the CAPEX, whilst ROCE we are expecting in high double digits in the range of 25%-30%.

items.statement: BESS margin pressure not visible for 3-5 years due to tailor-made solutions and technical complexity

items.statement: Maharashtra demand recovered with consistent single-digit growth in recent months
items.quote: Encouragingly, in Maharashtra, our largest market, we have seen demand recovery and a return to consistent growth in the past few months.

items.quote: Very pleased to say that in the first 9 months of FY '26, we gained significant market share in the domestic elite and premium wine segment across corporation markets for which we get industry data, including Karnataka and

items.statement: Wine Tourism revenue grew 34% YoY in Q3; 9M revenue INR49 crore, up 22% YoY
items.quote: Very pleased to say that we delivered robust year -on-year growth of 34% over last year Q3, marking yet another record quarter.

items.statement: Wine Tourism footfall increased 17% YoY in Q3; occupancy stable at ~80% despite 50% room capacity increase
items.quote: The strong growth in Q3 was powered by the healthy double -digit growth in footfalls, which increased more than 15% year-on-year and the opening of our third resort, The Haven by Sula.

items.statement: Added 50 keys (30 in Oct, 20 in Dec) at The Haven resort; total capacity up ~50% to 154 keys
items.quote: We added 30 keys in October under Phase 1, followed by 20 additional keys in December in Phase 2. And this Phase 2, in particular, was delivered 3 months ahead of schedule.

items.statement: Expect lion's share of capex over next 2 years allocated to Wine Tourism; plan to add ~50% more rooms
items.quote: Given this strong momentum and favorable outlook, we are decisively doubling down on investing in this segment. In fact, we expect that over the next 2 years, a lion's share of our total capex will be allocated to Wine Tourism.

items.statement: FY26 and FY27 capex expected to moderate to INR20-25 crore annually vs ~INR60 crore last year
items.quote: Capex in FY '26 and FY '27 is expected to moderate to INR20 crores to INR25 crores levels annually, which is less than half of around INR60 crores incurred in last financial year.

items.statement: Gross margin contracted 270 bps YoY due to adverse state mix (Karnataka share down 900 bps to 11%)
items.quote: Gross margins contracted by 270 basis points year -on-year. This contraction was driven primarily by an adverse state mix led by lower contribution from Karnataka, which is one of our high -margin markets.

items.statement: EBITDA declined 40% YoY to INR32 crore; margin contracted 800 bps
items.quote: As a result of the revenue decline and adverse geographic mix, EBITDA for the quarter declined to INR32 crores from INR53 crores in the corresponding period last year, representing a 40% year-on-year decline and an 800-basis-point contraction in margins.

items.statement: Expect margins to improve and gradually revert to normalized levels going forward
items.quote: Overall, we expect margins to improve and gradually revert towards normalized levels going forward.

items.statement: Destocking in Karnataka strengthened working capital position; no further material destocking anticipated
items.quote: Following this action, we believe we are now at a comfortable level in terms of stocks across markets across the country. So, we do not anticipate any further material destocking going ahead.

items.statement: Net debt declined sequentially by INR36 crore to INR319 crore in Dec 2025; debt/EBITDA ~3x TTM
items.quote: Encouragingly, our net debt declined sequentially by INR36 crores to INR319 crores to close December as compared to INR355 crores as of September 2025.

items.statement: Expect further debt reduction by end of March supported by improved inventory and lower capex
items.quote: We expect to further reduce the debt by end of March, supported by improved inventory levels and continued moderation in capex.

items.statement: India-EU FTA: duty reduction only for wines above EUR2.50 CIF; first cut to 75% expected ~1 year from now; full phase-in over 7-10 years
items.quote: The reduction in import duties is applicable only to wines priced above a minimum import price of EUR2.5 per 750 ml bottle CIF. The same level of duty applies also to bulk wine. Imports below this EUR2.50 threshold will continue to attract the existing 150% duty.

items.statement: At EUR2.50 CIF and 75% duty, EU wines would retail ~INR1,700 MRP in Maharashtra; 95% of Sula portfolio priced below INR1,600 MRP
items.quote: At these levels, an imported European wine with a CIF price of EUR2.50 and 75% duty would typically retail at about INR1,700 MRP in Maharashtra, which is the largest market for imported wines.

items.statement: Domestic unsustainable discounting (BOGO, buy 1 get 2) remains key pain point, especially in sub-INR700 segment
items.quote: That continues very unfortunately to be today, really the pain point. So , the pain point today is not from imports. The Australia FTA really in fact, Australian wine imports have declined precipitously over the past year or so. So today, the pain point is, I would say, a lmost unscrupulous, and I always use the term unsustainable discounting by other domestic wine players

items.statement: Grape harvest lower this year due to extended monsoon; no supply impact for wines above INR800; cash flow benefit from lower grape intake
items.quote: This year, the grape harvest is looking quite a bit less than in years past. For us, for Sula, that's not such a bad thing this year, I must say. Having said that, our hearts go out to our grape growers. It's a very difficult year for them.

items.statement: Plan to hold price increases for wines above INR1,300; focus on quality improvement and distribution breadth
items.quote: We will probably have to hold on price increases for our wines that cost, say, more than INR1,300. And in any case, in the last 1 year, we've been going very slow in terms of price increases.

items.statement: Open to spirits opportunities but cautious on valuations; evaluating import portfolio rebuild for when EU wines enter
items.quote: We have taken a good look at some opportunities that have come our way. I must be very frank that we have not looked very strongly at starting our own greenfield brand, but there have been certain opportunities that have come our way.

items.statement: Euro appreciated 20% vs rupee in past year, mitigating FTA impact; state governments could impose additional excise on imports later
items.quote: But I note that in that 1 year, euro has appreciated by 20% against the rupee. And that puts us today, I would say, in a much less scary position, a much more comfortable position.

items.statement: Expect Own Brands to return to growth over next couple of quarters; Wine Tourism to sustain strong momentum; overall optimistic on healthy recovery
items.quote: Looking ahead, we expect Own Brands to return to growth over the next couple of quarters. As Rajeev mentioned earlier, demand conditions have improved across all key markets. We also expect Wine Tourism to sustain its strong momentum, providing additional support to our performance in quarter 4 and the coming fiscal.

items.statement: Company is world's only US FDA approved camphor manufacturer with WHO and GMP certification
items.quote: world's, to the best of my knowledge, we are the world's, and I stand corrected, we are the world's only US FDA approved camphor manufacturer, point number one. We also have WHO and GMP certified

items.statement: Nine-month production grew 11% and sales volume grew 10% year-on-year

items.statement: Fragrance division benefits from softer raw material costs and new customer wins
items.quote: The performance of the fragrance division continues to be very strong and sustainable benefits from a softer pricing of raw materials and new wins with existing customers and new customers being added.

items.statement: American customers were buying hand-to-mouth due to tariff uncertainty; now returning to place orders as clarity improves

items.statement: Specialty aroma ingredients industry continues to grow but is crowded; companies with unique process or chemistry will stay ahead
items.quote: The specialty aroma ingredients business continues to grow, looks strong, but is also crowded.

items.statement: FMCG strategy remains work in progress; camphor branding under profitability pressure but sales maximization mode continues
items.quote: We had an internal discussion of the subject. It is still work in progress. Point number one. Point number two, I think the FMCG segment of the business continues to stay stronger.

items.statement: Cash profit for nine-month FY26 was Rs. 22.65 crores despite net loss of Rs. 0.67 crore

The overall demand outside of India.

items.quote: The other part of the quarter was the continued increase in copper prices and commodity prices. We had to take multiple price corrections. Overall, during the quarter, we took a correction of about 12% in the selling prices and most of the input price increases have been covered.

items.statement: Two price hikes taken between January and call date; will continue pass-through with lag
items.quote: Last quarter, we took 5, with an overall correction of about 12% in the selling prices. This quarter, between January and today, we have already done two changes. So as and when it is necessary, depending on how the fluctuation is or how big the fluctuation is, we will take that call.

items.statement: Solar, auto and power cable plant utilizations in late 70s; others catching up
items.quote: Utilization, like I mentioned earlier, solar, auto and power cable plant utilizations are in the late 70s, Others are catching up.

items.quote: Capex. In the quarter, we spent about INR 36 crores and for nine months, it is INR 146 crores in line with the projections that we had made in the beginning of the year so most of those projects should be coming to a solution by now.

items.statement: Preform factory under production trials, expected commissioning within FY26; fiber draw expansion Phase 1 equipment at site, Phase 2 by March end; 8 million km capacity by end Q1 FY27
items.quote: Currently, the preform factory is under production trials, and we expect to commission it within this fiscal. The Fiber draw expansion, the building is more or less ready. items.quote: I think, two months cycle across the chain is reasonable given the fact that when you get into industrials and automobile cables, the number of SKUs are substantially large.

items.quote: A lot of it is tied up on the preform project so as I mentioned in my opening remarks, at the preform factory right now, production trials are ongoing, and we expect to commission the plant by next month, so when that is done, out of the INR 300 crores, about INR 230 crores or INR 220 crores, somewhere around that will get capitalized.

items.statement: Birla cable plant likely production Q2-Q3 CY2026; Adani plans unclear; competition to intensify on wire segment but sufficient space to coexist
items.quote: Our information is that it is likely to get into production more sometime next calendar year. items.statement: Sustainable EBIT margin for Cables division 11-12%; currently slightly behind due to mix shift toward auto/industrial

items.statement: Provision of INR 6 crores taken for gratuity obligations reassessment after new labor code effective 21 Nov
items.quote: Additionally, one single point I would like to make is that after the announcement of the new labor code going live effective 21st of November, we have reassessed the obligations towards gratuity and have taken a provision of INR 6 crores, which has been booked in this current quarter.

items.statement: Future capex planned for auto, solar, construction wires as utilization touches 70-80%; E-Beam plant commissioned two quarters ago opening new applications
items.quote: So because planning to execution will take about a year and a half. items.quote: from an average of about slightly under $3, which was prevailing during quarter 3, the prices currently as on date, are closer to $5 a month so that's the extent of the demand pull that has happened over the last few months.

items.quote: More of automobile, cable-related sales are more of industrial products tend to depress the margin a little bit because of the nature of that business. As the volumes grow faster and higher on the construction side, then the balancing would happen.

items.quote: Currently, we have a market share of about 11% - 12% in India. The biggest player is Sterlite followed by the Birla Cables and then HFCL.

items.quote: We, from fiscal year 2023 to the nine months in fiscal year 2026, we had a standalone gross margin improvement of 320 basis points.

items.quote: And the front-load washers business for us continues to accelerate. It is not shocking because it is on a smaller base, but we have grown the business about 50%, greater than last year.

items.statement: Targets high single-digit CAGR over five years; could become early double-digit if market grows slightly ahead of GDP

If the market were to grow slightly ahead of GDP, then I do not see why the high single-digit cannot become an early double-digit kind of growth number over a five-year period.
