items.statement: Meller grew >42% YoY in first 9 months FY26; launched in India and Middle East, went out of stock within weeks; potential global brand for House of Brands strategy
items.quote: Meller grew more than 42% year-on-year in first 9 months this year, unlocking fashion sunglasses as a new category for Lenskart. Within weeks of India's launch, we went out of stock, saw tremendous success in Middle East too.

items.statement: India same-store sales growth (SSSG) 28% in Q3 FY26; 9M SSSG 20% and same pin code sales growth (SPSG) 26% across metro, Tier-1, Tier-2+
items.quote: We have added 169 stores in India in Q3. This is more than what we added in 9 months last year. And we did it with 28% SSSG and 36% same pin code sales growth - showing we are expanding the market , not splitting it

items.statement: Gold membership over 8 million active members; 37% of Q3 sales from members acquired in prior quarters; 2-year repeat rate ~98%
items.quote: Gold membership has now over 8 million active members, wi th 37% of Q3 sales coming from members acquired in prior quarters. This is recurring compounding revenue, requiring zero incremental CAC

items.statement: Frame manufacturing shifting to India (Hyderabad facility) and Thailand to derisk China supply chain; Thailand offers component ecosystem and tax treaty benefits
items.quote: So, there is no change in plan, and we are strengthening our frame manufacturing in India. But Thailand just adds to it because it actually derisks our supply chain from China as we are building in India.

items.statement: International revenue grew 32.7% YoY in current currency, 24% in constant currency; 8% currency tailwind; natural hedge from JPY/SGD earnings vs frame imports
items.quote: International business, again, seeing a volume-driven growth with both units up 21% year-on-year and eye tests also up 20% to 0.8 million eye tests. We have added 26 net new stores in Q3, resulting in 48 net additions year-to-date.

items.statement: ₹485 crores operating cash flow in 9M FY26 funded store expansion (₹288 cr) and manufacturing capex (₹267 cr); ex-IPO/M&A, generated ₹7 crores free cash
items.quote: From a cash flow standpoint, in the first 9 months of this year, we generated ₹485 crores of cash flow from operating activities. This was used to fund the store expansion. And we used ₹288 crores to open 420 new stores and also invested ₹267 crores in manufacturing, including the new Hyderabad facility.

items.statement: Closing cash balance including IPO proceeds ₹3,978 crores; operations funded expansion without external borrowing in 9M FY26
items.quote: And closing cash balance, including the IPO proceeds, stands at ₹ 3,978 crores.

items.statement: AI used for hiring at all levels including CXO; improved quality of hire; talent identified as largest expense that cannot compound at same rate as revenue
items.quote: In fact, every person we are hiring in the corporate today, the interviews are taken by AI, even at a CXO level. That has really improved the quality of hire. So that's your only large talent is going to be your biggest, largest expense.

items.statement: Key risk: execution at scale stretching customer experience; currency exposure on frame imports (RMB); detractor handling and churn management via AI CRM
items.quote: I think ensuring that customer experience remains intact and grows when we are opening so many stores, growing internationally, the risk is always stretching too thin.

items.statement: B by Lenskart smart glasses soft launch in Q4 FY26; features: photos, videos, meal logging, AI chat; focus on data ecosystem not hardware revenue near-term
items.quote: B by Lenskart, our smart glasses, will have its soft launch in Q4 this year. We believe the future of consumer technology is in wearable intelligence. This shift from looking down at a screen to looking up into the world is bound to happen.

items.statement: NPS reached record 80.9 in Q3 FY26; Lenskart Foundation served 150,000+ with free eye screening; government budget support for optometry aligns with vision
items.quote: This quarter, we did our record NPS of 80.9. Beyond commercial impact, through the Lenskart Foundation, we served over 150,000 people with free eye screening and provided eyewear to many, often their first pair.

items.statement: Order book stands at Rs 142.45 crore as of Q3 FY26; fresh orders of over Rs 54 crore secured in Q3
items.quote: During the quarter, we secured fresh orders worth over Rs. 54 crore. As on date, our total order book stands at Rs. 142.45 crore, giving us strong revenue visibility for the coming quarters.

items.statement: Exit order book for FY26 expected around Rs 250 crore by end of March; Rs 55 crore new orders added in January
items.quote: Right now, we have confirmed order book till March. Because even after this plan-out, today, we have secured almost one order. So, our order book was almost Rs. 48 crores. So, by the end of March, our order book should be around Rs. 250 crores.

items.statement: Capex underway for 2,000-ton press unit; 2 pultrusion machines delivered, 3 more coming; lab equipment ready by end-February for Nashik unit
items.quote: Basically, we have almost planned out the press unit of 2,000 tons. Technical clearance is going on. Plus, there is a requirement for dyes so for that drawings and everything are up for approval. We have already bought out the machines for pultrusion. We have already delivered 2 machines. We will get 3 more machines.

items.statement: Capacity utilization expected to reach 60-80% by end of FY26, targeting 90% thereafter
items.quote: So, mainly, my production ratio will be around 60%-80% by the end of the year. After that, we will do a better performance and want to go up to 90%.

items.statement: PAT margin target 10-12% for FY26 and FY27; current PAT margin at 11%; EBITDA margin not explicitly guided but linked to PAT focus
items.quote: Right now, our minimum target is around 10%. But we are already doing better performance up to 11%. So, the target is not the same if we go up to 12% and go with the same growth speed.

items.statement: Receivable days reduced from 83 days in H1 FY26 to ~40 days in Q3 FY26; target max 60 days
items.quote: Right now, H1 was for 83 days. In that also, we have enhanced it to 40-45 days. If it is government, then 45 days. If it is public, we have increased it to 30 days. That is why, our average is at 40 days right now.

items.statement: Copper price fluctuations passed through back-to-back in government tenders; long-term purchase deals of 3-6 months for other materials
items.quote: Basically, the copper has more fluctuation other materials don't have that much fluctuation, so we have to hedge but mostly whatever we deal with the purchaser we have a long-term deal almost 3 months or 6 months according to which our order book is clear so we do a standardization.

items.statement: Government/utility business ~60% of total; payment cycles fixed with ~10% advance; private customers 30-45 days
items.quote: Right now we have almost 60% government-based business. Because for the last 30 years my grandfather and others were in this business. So, that is a good catch with which the payment is safe.

items.statement: Export focus increasing; trial container of FRP products (cable trays, grating, pultrusion) sent to Oman; targeting Africa and Europe next; UK plan for next year
items.quote: products are we going to enter what stage are we at already? Neel Shah: Already we had one trial order in which we have already sold the other one, we are doing LTCT now which we are focusing in this month, that will also go in this month, and the rest are going regularly. We were targeting Oman and Africa; next we will target Europe. Right now, the plan out is for that, some supply. Actually, fro

items.statement: Order execution timeline 7-12 months; order book regenerates December-March
items.quote: Normally, it is year-to-year. So, we have to clear it within 7-12 months. Then, again, there is an update till December. So, from December to March, your total order book will be regenerated.

items.statement: Strong demand visibility for next 10 years driven by utility revamp, smart metering, renewable energy, and government infrastructure push
items.quote: So, the main focus is that the visibility is clear for the next 10 years that the market is booming. So, we are focusing on that. There was smart metering earlier. Now, there is work going on as well. There is a lot of better performance on the government plus Utilities.

items.statement: No major hurdles seen; risks mitigated by approvals, diversified product range (utility, railway, defense, export), and purchasing power
items.quote: Right now, I can't see the hurdles because I have already passed them. Normally, the hurdles are that we want to continue like this So, there will be a lot of planning and systematic. After IPO, we get a free hand that whatever we are planning should perform well.

items.statement: Sales head Ranjit Mishra (ex-Sintex, 30 years experience) leads team; team built from Sintex alumni with 30-40 years industry experience
items.quote: Yessir, last our Sales Head President of our Company Ranjit Mishra he used to be Head Northern Belt in Syntax for last 30 years, he gives better experience in performance and his team works in this standard. So, almost last 30-40 years' experience in this industry, so that's why we focused on team build up in starting phase.

items.statement: IPO completed (Rs 92 crore); proceeds used for capex and working capital; no further fund raise mentioned
items.quote: No. Right now, we have that working capital because the IPO is over. We have that and this year's profit will also be added. It will be easy to serve for us. We can easily achieve next year's numbers.

items.statement: No dividend or buyback mentioned; focus on growth and ROE/ROCE improvement
items.quote: We are committing our investors on a good ROE and ROCE. And our efforts are on a positive side only because what I can say is we are building a good team as Mr. Neel said we are building a good team with a good vision.

items.statement: Railway approvals for SMC washrooms expected by March-end; first supply targeted September FY27; dyes and production setup to follow approval
items.quote: given design approvals, our main approval and registration should come in this month and remaining if designing approval comes by March end we will be able to start production because after that dyes and all will be made because we have already submitted designs then we will see when approvals will come after that dyes and all will be planned which will take almost 3 months after that supply will

items.statement: FY26 full-year lead acid capex may reach INR750-800 cr including tubular plant reinstatement partly funded by insurance
items.quote: On a full year basis, it can go up to INR750 to INR 800 crores in the financial year.

items.statement: BESS plant targets ~15% share of 30-40 GWh market by FY31; current supplies <1 GWh, multiple tenders floated
items.quote: And going forward, the storage requirements both because of the round-the-clock power requirement from the solar generation side as well as the intermittency in the solar power generation is also required to be mitigated with appropriate storage.

items.statement: Standalone operating margin 11.2% in Q3; adjusted for lithium trading and lead recycling efficiency, margin ~12.3%; lead acid sustained ~12% despite raw material cost pressures
items.quote: At a LAB level (lead acid battery business), we are able to sustain the operating margins of about 12% despite this cost pressures at raw material levels.

items.statement: 2% price increase taken in January 2026 to offset alloy cost increases; acid and lead prices remain volatile, further hikes possible if costs sustain
items.quote: We took a price increase of around 2% in January '26 to mitigate this cost pressures.

items.statement: Domestic 4W OEM volumes +25% YoY, aftermarket +3%; 2W flat (+1%) due to high base; industrial ex-telecom +2%, UPS +5%, home inverter +10%; telecom lead acid volumes -45% YoY
items.quote: During the quarter, a steady growth of 7% in domestic automotive 4-wheeler volumes along with other applications, supported the top line expansion in the lead acid business. 4-wheeler OEM volumes have demonstrated robust growth of around 25% and aftermarket volumes grew around 3% on a Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: New Energy revenue >INR200 cr (2x YoY), 250 MWh telecom packs supplied, stationary capacity utilization 80%+; lead acid 93% of consolidated revenue
items.quote: On the New Energy business, during Q3, we have delivered a strong performance with a revenue of more than INR200 crores, which is a growth of almost 2x compared to the previous year.

items.statement: Export volumes -15% YoY due to US tariff issues and geopolitical uncertainties; competitive intensity rising in Middle East/APAC; telecom lead acid structural decline >45% YoY
items.quote: Despite these growth numbers highlighted earlier, the lead acid business reported a muted top line of a round INR3,174 crores during the quarter. This was primarily driven by the decline in industrial telecom lead acid volumes and decline in automotive export volumes by around 15% on account of tariff issues and other

items.statement: INR200 cr infused into lithium subsidiary AR Advanced Cell Technologies in Q3; cumulative investment now INR1,400 cr
items.quote: During Q3, we infused around INR200 crores into Amara Raja Advanced Cell Technologies, which is a lithium subsidiary. And with this, the total investment is now INR1,400 crores.

items.statement: Lead recycling plant battery breaking to start Q4 FY26; refining ops already adding 0.6% EBITDA margin accretion
items.quote: Yes. Yes. The battery breaking is going to start from Q4. And as Swajitha has articulated earlier, the refining operations are providing that additional margin comfort at this point of time.

items.statement: NMC cell line (up to 2 GWh) can be migrated to LFP if needed; sodium-ion under evaluation; LFP remains mainstay for mobility
items.quote: In the worst case, if at all, there is a problem with it, as we have explained earlier also, migrating this whole line to LFP chemistry is not going to be from a capital point of view, very taxing.

items.statement: OEM contracts have automatic lead price pass-through via PVC formula; other commodities not covered
items.quote: Yes, it is automatic pass-through based on the PVC contract that we have. But that's only for the lead, not for all commodities.

items.statement: BESS asset turnover expected 9-10x; INR280 cr capex could yield ~INR2,700-2,800 cr revenue at current cell prices
items.quote: INR280 crores should give or take give about INR2,800-INR2,700 crores kind of revenue, assuming the current cell prices.

items.statement: Balance 10,000 tonnes CPVC expansion expected to complete next month, raising annual capacity to 50,000 tonnes
items.quote: As previously communicated, the balance 10,000 tonnes CPVC expansion is progressing on schedule, and is expected to be completed next month. commissioning, our annual CPVC capacity will increase to 50,000 tonnes.

items.statement: Long-term legacy loans expected to close FY26 at INR 225 crores and reduce to INR 80 crores by end of FY27
items.quote: So by end of FY '27, we would be around INR 80 crores on the legacy loan, which basically is not a legacy loan. It's a loan which has been taken in the last couple of 1 or 2 years, which is basically to fund our CPVC project. So legacy loan gets all over by FY '27.

items.statement: Steady-state interest cost expected around INR 45 crores for FY27
items.quote: So I think on a steady-state basis, not an exact number we can say, but on a steady-state basis, we should be a number of around INR 45 crores interest.

items.statement: Underlying Indian demand stable supported by housing, infrastructure and water management; domestic producers face significant import competition
items.quote: In India, underlying demand has remained stable, supported by housing, infrastructure and water management-related consumption. However, domestic producers continue to face significant import competition.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA INR 50 crores, down 19% YoY; Basic Chemicals breakeven, Specialty grew 4.2%
items.quote: The EBITDA, including other income for the quarter stood at INR 50 crores, which is 19% lower on a Y-o-Y basis, down from INR 61.8 crores. While Specialty Chemicals showed a growth of 4.2%, this was pretty thin growth compared to the Y-o-Y volume increase, both in SIOP and CPVC.

items.statement: 9M FY26 EBITDA INR 170 crores, up 10% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA, including other income for 9 months basis stood at INR 170 crores as against INR 155 crores a year back, an increase by 10%.

items.statement: SIOP dispatches in Q4 expected to exceed production, reducing inventory; advanced stage of concluding contracts with traditional customers for next year
items.quote: Quarter 4, we will have dispatches more than our production, and we will definitely see a reduction in our inventory. And as we talk now, we are also in a very advanced stage of concluding our contracts with our traditional customers for next year.

items.statement: PVC prices up over INR 10,000/tonne since January 1; CPVC price hikes expected mid-February and March
items.quote: So now that there is a clarity on the price direction, directionally, there is an improvement in the prices and prices are moving up as we are talking now right from 1st January till date, we have seen over INR 10,000 increase in the price.

items.statement: CPVC realizations declined 26% YoY in Q3; PVC down 17% YoY; soda ash down 9% YoY
items.quote: The price erosion has also witnessed across all product segments with CPVC and PVC demonstrating severe cuts of 26% and 17%, respectively, on a Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Specialty Chemicals revenue grew 27% YoY to INR 156 crores in Q3; CPVC volumes up 80%, SIOP up 19%
items.quote: The increase in top line has been driven by sales volume growth across all the product segments with CPVC and SIOP sales growing at a pace of 80% and 19%, respectively.

items.statement: Specialty segment generated strong operating profitability, offsetting Basic Chemicals weakness; 9M EBITDA up 14% YoY per opening remarks
items.quote: On a 9-month basis, our EBITDA has improved approximately 14% year-on-year, reflecting improved operational efficiencies, disciplined execution and benefits of our portfolio rebalancing.

items.statement: SIOP in advanced stage of concluding contracts with traditional customers for next year
items.quote: And as we talk now, we are also in a very advanced stage of concluding our contracts with our traditional customers for next year.

items.statement: China withdrew 13% VAT rebate on PVC exports effective April, expected to improve export pricing discipline and benefit domestic producers
items.quote: Finally, China has removed the export incentive on the PVC. So it's in line with their overall direction of having a cap on the dumping or overselling by the Chinese producers. So there has been a 13% V AT on the Chinese exports, which was given to them as a subsidy that has been withdrawn.

items.statement: ADD petitions for PVC and soda ash not approved by Finance Ministry; no petitions currently in pipeline
items.quote: As you may be aware, the ADD petition for both PVC and soda ash has not been approved by the Finance Ministry. So as of now, we have no petitions in the pipeline.

items.statement: Exports contribute 22%; US SIOP demand unaffected by tariffs (under exclusion); Europe zero tariff may benefit more than impact
items.quote: Our U.S. supplies of SIOP was never impacted by the tariff, because it was under exclusion. Now when the tariff has come down or has been proposed to come down, it is not going to impact the prices of the product in the end market, which is U.S.

items.statement: Healthy cash and equivalents of INR 220 crores against working capital borrowing facility to tide over commodity down cycle
items.quote: The company maintains a healthy cash and cash equivalent of INR 220 crores, against which it is running a working capital borrowing facility to tide over the undergoing commodity down cycle.

items.statement: Scheduled repayment of long-term borrowings ongoing; long-term legacy loans expected at INR 225 crores by end FY26
items.quote: On the balance sheet side, the company is steadily deleveraging itself by making its scheduled repayment of long-term borrowings and is expected to close the year at INR 225 crores of long-term legacy loans.

items.statement: Finance cost flat at INR 16 crores for Q3; 9M finance cost INR 46.8 crores, down 9% YoY
items.quote: The finance cost stood flat at around INR 16 crores for the quarter, totaling to INR 46.8 crores for 9 months, which is a reduction of 9% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: CPVC sales volume grew 80% YoY in Q3 backed by capacity expansion from 20kt to 40kt with negligible commercialization lag
items.quote: The CPVC sales volume is backed by capacity expansion from our 20 kt to 40 kt with negligible lag in commercialization of the incremental volumes.

items.statement: Synthetic Rutile Q4 dispatches expected to exceed production, reducing inventory
items.quote: Quarter 4, we will have dispatches more than our production, and we will definitely see a reduction in our inventory.

items.statement: Renewable power cost savings roughly INR 25-26 crores annually; uneven quarterly due to monsoon Oct-Dec
items.quote: See the cost savings for a yearly basis would be roughly around INR 25 crores to INR 26 crores. Having said that, it will not be even in all the quarters, because unlike the West, in the South, we have monsoon between October and December.

items.statement: Renewable expansion on hold awaiting Tamil Nadu policy clarity; current policy not economically viable without battery storage
items.quote: We are exploring because there has been a change in the renewable policy of Tamil Nadu government, which is not very conducive to add any renewable capacity at this juncture. And there are a lot of court cases which have been filed challenging the policies. So we are waiting for clarity on the policy of the government.

items.statement: PVC price bottomed out per management; personally expects range-bound $750-800; crude at $60 limits upside
items.quote: I personally feel prices will be range bound maybe between $750, $800. I don't think we can speculate more than that, because you should also see from the overall perspective, the crude prices are also not high. They are lowering at $60.

items.statement: Focused on capability building, digital integration, governance processes and technology adoption; SAP S4 HANA implementation underway
items.quote: Over the past year, we have focused on capability building, digital integration, governance processes and technology adoption. The SAP S4 HANA implementation, process standardization and internal systems development are not short-term initiatives. They are foundational steps intended to support scalable growth.

items.statement: Expects strong growth in Performance Chemicals business for next few years in multiples on small base, but declines to give specific numbers
items.quote: We are going to see a very strong growth this year, both in terms of revenue as well as profit, on a small base. And I'm quite confident that we are going to see good growth in the years to come. So, we are not talking about percentage growth here. Not allowing optimism to overflow, we are hopefully going to see growth for the next few years in multiples.

items.statement: Prepaid INR582 crores debt in Q3 FY26 via preferential allotment (INR467 crores) and internal accruals (INR116 crores); plans INR75-100 crores more in Q4 and INR100-150 crores in April 2026
items.quote: We have utilized the entire INR467 crores for the prepayment of the existing debt, which includes the term loan as well as the working capital. Apart from this, we have paid INR116 crores more debt in the third quarter itself, this was through our internal accrual. We are also planning to prepay some of the debt, say about INR75 crores to INR100 crores, in Q4 that will also be through our internal

items.statement: Target term loan of ~INR1,100 crores by March 31, 2026; normal repayment of INR285 crores next year plus prepayments depending on cash flow
items.quote: So hopefully, we will close on 31st March 2026 around INR1,100 crores term loan. Apart from this, we are not having any big size capex. And any capex will be undertaken only after the demerger. And our efforts are continuing relating to the prepayment, and we are planning to pay, say, about INR100 crores, INR150 crores in April '26 also.

items.statement: Swapped INR130 crores high-cost debt to low-cost debt saving 125-150 bps; further swaps planned to reduce interest cost visible from Q4 FY26
items.quote: We are also in the process of swapping the high-cost debt to the low-cost debt in which we have recently swapped, about INR130 crores debt, which will save us about 125 basis points to 150 basis points. So, we are on the track to reducing the interest cost and the impact of all the efforts will be visible in Q4.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 15.0% for 9M FY26 and 16.0% for Q3 FY26, up from 11% in FY22
items.quote: The EBITDA is up 28.9%, and our EBITDA margin for 9MFY26 is 15.0%. The 3 months' revenue is up 13.0% and EBITDA has an excellent growth of 36.1% with EBITDA margins of 16.0% overall.

items.statement: Chemicals EBIT margin rose to 12.8% in Q3 FY26 from 8.5% YoY and 11.6% for 9M FY26 from 8.8% YoY, driven by exit from low-margin businesses and operational changes
items.quote: For the quarter, we've seen some decline in sales, which is a 3.8% decline and a 46.1% increase in EBIT. And year-on-year, it is a decline of about 17.1% with a growth in EBIT of 8.3%. And our EBIT margins are up from 8.5% for the quarter to 12.8% and 8.8% for 9M to 11.6%.

items.statement: Biofuels EBIT margin improved to 8.4% in Q3 FY26 from 3.3% YoY; expects range-bound profitability going forward due to policy-linked pricing and DDGS byproduct dynamics
items.quote: So, I have a lot of data on various sources of protein for veterinary and poultry use. DDGS prices, for example, of late have been going up. Now DDGS availability has also been going up. But the reason it has been going up is that, the biggest, for example, sources of protein for animals and veterinary and poultry has been soya and some others. items.quote: In general, in the Chemical space, there has been some recovery, particularly in Performance Chemicals, Agrochemicals. But it has been gradual, I think, and the sentiment globally is cautious optimism, with pricing still being soft. And to some extent, some of these things impact on how we think about our company. And there have been some weaknesses in base and petrochemical materials. And in some

items.quote: We've continued to maintain our strong foothold in the Eastern and Southeastern market despite introduction of rPET. items.quote: We've rolled out Amazing Dark Spice Rum, and Amazing Premium Brandy in Kerala, with a focus on diversifying the offering, strengthening our presence in the high consumption market. We've rolled out some major products in Kerala, strengthening overall presence in high consumption markets. items.statement: No major capex planned until after demerger; any capex will be undertaken only post-demerger
items.quote: Apart from this, we are not having any big size capex. And any capex will be undertaken only after the demerger.

items.statement: Ethanol blending at 20%; NITI Aayog committee examining >20% blending but vehicle modifications and infrastructure (hydrophilic ethanol moisture/corrosion issues) needed; feedstock shifting from molasses to grain (corn) for scalability
items.quote: Now as I had mentioned in some of my earlier discussions that there is clearly a committee appointed under NITI Aayog to look at blending over and above 20%. So just to let you know that blending of ethanol is a bit tricky and it is not a linear blending, which can happen from 20% to 30% to 40% to 50% to 60% to 80%. So, the way this goes is that when you increase from 0% to 5%, there are hardly an

items.statement: Biofuels revenue up 45.2% YoY in Q3 and 51.2% for 9M; EBIT up 273.2% in Q3 and 108.5% for 9M; driven by 20% ethanol blending mandate
items.quote: As far as the Bio-Fuel segment is concerned, you are aware that this was driven by India's plan to increase blending of ethanol to about 20%. And our revenue for quarter 3 increased by 45.2%, EBIT up 273.2% and for 9M, revenue increased 51.2% and EBIT increased about 108.5%.

items.statement: Ethanol/ENA manufacturing flexibility from multiple feedstocks (rice, corn, molasses); captive ENA consumption for Potable Spirits; evaluating in-house ethanol for Chemicals vs imports given surplus capacity
items.quote: We have the ability to use several feed stocks, which is different kinds of rice, corn, molasses and so on. And this is crucial for our Potable Spirits business; this is the backbone of our Bio-Fuels business and is often significantly important for our Chemicals business as well. It has been the backbone. And the reason I use the word often is that we look at the make or buy versus opportunity on

items.quote: Thiocolchicoside the raw material feedstock, which is Gloriosa seed is now being stabilized, and the new crop is coming. So we don't foresee any problem in getting the material, and we are expecting a better price in the international market also. And the nicotine sales, which was earlier under stress, now it has been started again. So, we are expecting a good margin and a good turnover in the fou

items.quote: It has been going through a bit of a challenging time essentially because of cost pressures on feedstocks and a significant amount of volatility in the Western market; that is where we sell this in Europe, U.S., etcetera. But our focus is very clear. It is to graduate into the branded portfolio where we can add more value, implement stringent standards on quality and innovative products and formul

items.statement: JV margins squeezed due to feedstock price gap vs Reliance; greener products more expensive; working on exports and value-added products; expects ethanol price decline to help regain margin
items.quote: So Saket, yes, so there has been not as much as a pressure on the top line, but there has been a squeeze of margins for the joint venture, essentially because as you know, we talk about price of the alternate material, which comes from Reliance as a feedstock versus ours. items.quote: Our current long-term contract with our global innovator customer continues to gain traction. We are supplying commercial quantities for the portfolio that we had validated.

items.quote: From FY '29 onwards, we should start seeing a reduction in overall debt, which is already reducing compared to where we were. We are not doing any major new c apex or

items.statement: Pharma CDMO: sharp uptake in early-stage RFPs for high-value small molecules and advanced intermediates
items.quote: We are capturing this momentum, witnessing a sharp uptake in early-stage RFPs, particularly for high-value small molecules and advanced intermediates.

items.statement: Targets ~25% EBITDA margin and 25-35% top-line growth next year
items.quote: I won't be surprised that we'll be going back to that level with this increased revenue flow and efficiencies what we created in existing businesses by downsizing MES and adding Beryl. So probably we can still look at a 25% EBITDA margin is possible.

items.statement: Aims for INR230-240 crore consolidated revenue next year
items.quote: INR60 crores plus INR180 crores, somewhere around INR240 crores, INR230 crores to INR240 crores, we can aim next year from the current level of about INR175 crores, INR180 crores.

items.statement: Targets 20-25% CAGR on top line over 3-5 years
items.quote: And your question about 3 to 5 years, we'll continue to grow at the rate of at least 20%, 25% CAGR on the top line.

items.statement: Beryl acquisition contributed $137k (INR1.25 cr) in Nov-Dec; one-time costs reduced net contribution to INR20 lakh
items.quote: In fact, the bottom line from Beryl's 2 months operation, that is November and December stand at $137,000, which is equal to about INR1.25 crores. But we have to write-off the acquisition cost of legal, due diligence and travel and all those costs as per the new standards.

items.statement: Beryl adds 40 US employees, $5.5M revenue last year; targets $6M+ this year for ~30% top-line boost
items.quote: They have a top line of around 5.5 million last year. And hopefully, at least if they cross 6 million this year, it will be a 30% addition to our top line.

items.quote: We are also into contact with a couple of steel structural designing companies. That means high-rise buildings, plants and companies of that cadre. We are in touch with them to see for a probable matching.

items.statement: Building own campus in Nashik to save INR2-2.5 cr annual rent; land acquired 3-4 years ago
items.quote: We are keeping this cash and funds for further acquisitions or even constructing our own campus in Nashik, which has started just recently, land has been acquired 3, 4 years ago. That will considerably save our rental costs, which are running almost INR2 crores to INR2.5 crores per annum.

items.statement: Downsizing MES automotive team from 160 to ~60; retraining staff for poles/towers; completes by April 2026
items.quote: So the team size from 160, we are dropping it down almost to 60 in due course of time. And some of the people have been retrained in poles and towers and transmission lines, where we are seeing improved traction.

items.quote: What used to be a 20, 25 members team, we have currently 60 members and added several new clients recently. And that team might grow at a good pace in the next couple of years, mainly due to the increased transmission lines, poles and towers and substations near to the data centers being constructed.

items.statement: Civil design team expanding from 20 to 30 designers by next year; has 2 US PEs in-house; Beryl adds 1-2 PEs
items.quote: Earlier, it used to be 7, 8 people. Now this year, we are 20 and planning to have 30 designers by next year. And we have in-house 2 professional engineers US certified professional engineers. working in our company as of today.

items.statement: Civil engineering seeing major jump in project wins last 4-5 months; expects 20% growth next fiscal year
items.quote: And last 4, 5 months, we are seeing a major jump in civil project wins. And we being established retailer and connection designer, we have been getting preferred by major fabricators as a reliable outsourcing company. And there, we are seeing traction coming in our way. So I'm very confident that Civil will see at least a 20% growth in the next financial year.

items.statement: Data center civil work yields ~$0.5M per project; targeting 4-5 projects/year for $2-2.5M incremental revenue
items.quote: In the civil side, already many data centers, each data center contributes about close to $0.5 million work for us in civil side. And even if we capture 4 or 5 data centers a year, it will be about $2 million to $2.5 million top line growth, which is more than 15% of our top line.

items.statement: MES mandate to place 30 people on-site in next 3 months; could turn division positive
items.quote: We have a mandate to place 30 people in the next 3 months. And if that happens, MES also can turn around into a positive zone from what has been bleeding in the last few quarters.

items.quote: Beryl has last year, 8% to 10% EBITDA. That EBITDA margin can shoot up to 30%, 35% within a year's time once half of their work is outsourced to our Indian office.

items.statement: Expects overall EBITDA to cross 20% with revenue growth and MES loss elimination
items.quote: So going forward, we are very confident that the EBITDA margins and the top line revenue growth will be definitely somewhere in -- I mean, the top line growth should be in the region of 25% to 35% and EBITDA should at least cross 20% overall.

items.statement: Employee costs jumped to INR37-38 cr/quarter due to Beryl; Indian cost base to grow 10-12% annually
items.quote: Yes, Indian expenditure, you can take a factor of 10% to 12%, considering the annual increment and increase in headcount, maybe around 12% you can take.

items.quote: Now with clarity coming at 18%, I'm sure we will start exporting some buildings of Interarch and helping them erect in United States and providing them engineering services and stamping, which is the agreement.

items.quote: Currently, Beryl is only in Florida and that too working for 2 counties. There are at least 8 to 10 counties, I think, in Florida, where they can immediately expand if the work can be handled from India.

items.statement: CEO Richard Leon to buy $0.5M shares; demat process completing; 3-year lock-in; no buyback planned as cash reserved for acquisitions and Nashik campus
items.quote: Mr. Leo Cannyn will be buying about $0.5 million worth of shares and the demat process is just getting completed. And then the shares may be issued in the next couple of months. So he is going to hold on them for a period of minimum 3 years.

items.quote: AI has no entry into engineering services. This engineering services require a lot of internal knowledge of detailing of fabrication, specifications and steel and many other inputs. items.quote: 9 months, we have achieved INR130 crores. So probably we'll be ending this year at around INR175 crores, INR180 crores, let's say, INR180 crores plus.

items.quote: Pre-engineered building is a small portion of our civil engineering services. items.quote: And who may get trained by the Beryl team who will start visiting us from March, April onwards for training the team out here.

items.quote: we do have some surplus cash. As most of you have noticed, we are sitting with 150 crores or something of cash, and so we do have some surplus.

items.quote: FraudZap is built pretty much like, I would say, a platform on which we are able to do different use cases. So currently, the use case that is active is device fraud. And if I look at, let's say, device fraud as a market, it's 4.5 billion or 4.2 billion, actually, to be precise.

items.statement: All five regions covered (EMEA, APAC, North America, Africa, Australia); exploring Korea, Japan despite language/competition barriers
items.quote: I actually don't think there is any region, Mahesh, that we don't have customers. So, I tell you, our basic, we are EMEA, right. We have Europe and Middl e East. We are covered in APAC. We have coverage in the North America, and we have coverage in Middle East

items.quote: It’s actually from Q2, RAFM. So, we do the entire i ncremental post the incremental cycle or process around in Q1, which it gets effective from Q2

items.quote: For FY26, we remain on track to deliver a top line of about Rs. 2,300 crores, driven entirely by optimization and high utilization of existing capacities with no incremental capex planned. items.statement: No fresh capex planned for FY27; planning stage for next capex phase in FY28

items.quote: We currently have orders of approximately Rs. 1,200 crores translating into 17 crores litres for ESY 25 and 26. Our total ethanol production capacity stands at 26 crores litres per annum.

items.statement: No segment-wise leadership division; promoters supervise plants vertically across all segments
items.quote: There is no division of leadership across segments. But yes, we do supervise independent plants from top to bottom between the promoters. So, it is more like a vertical supervision which we are looking at within plants, but there is no division of segments between the promoters.

items.statement: Interest subvention scheme (ISS) accounting changed to cash receipt basis; reversed Rs. 5.36 crores provision due to 1.5 year delay in government payments; expect partial receipt in Q4
items.quote: We have decided to keep on a received basis, cash received basis. Because ISS has been getting delayed from the government side. We have not received ISS of more than one and a half years. So factoring into the P&L was not looking fair to us. So, then in this quarter, we decided to reverse the ISS provision which we had already taken for this year and we have decided to go ahead with a policy of r

items.statement: Grain processing revenue mix: 60% sorbitol & by-products, 30% starch, 20% fructose (note: sums to 110% per transcript)
items.quote: And regarding the product mix, about 60% of our revenue is coming from sorbitol and its by-products, about 30% comes from starch and 20% comes from fructose.

items.statement: Ethanol by-products (DDGS) contribute ~25% additional revenue on top of ethanol revenue; Rs. 1,200 crore ethanol orders yield ~Rs. 300 crore by-product revenue
items.quote: Whatever revenue you see which comes from ethanol, there is additional revenue of about 25% from the by-products. If we have ethanol orders of Rs. 1,200 crores, then we'll get an additional revenue of about Rs. 300 crores from its by-products.

items.statement: US DDGS import not seen as threat; landed cost minimum Rs. 26/kg vs domestic Rs. 22-24/kg; Indian DDGS has better protein and oil content
items.quote: Regarding allowing import of maize DDGS from US, as we see it, we only see it as good news for the ethanol industry. Number one, because the import of maize DDGS in the country will not be less than Rs. 26 a kg, and the current DDGS domestic prices is about Rs. 22 to Rs. 24 a kg. Secondly, the protein content and the oil content in Indian DDGS are better than what is in the US DDGS.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance of Rs. 2,600-2,800 crores at 80%-85% utilization; Rs. 3,000 crores possible with current infrastructure depending on market dynamics and OMC tender allocations
items.quote: That will be at about 80%-85% capacity utilization. With the current infrastructure, we have the scope to go up to Rs. 3,000 crores, but that again depends on market dynamics and the tender allocation from OMCs. But looking at the current scenario, we think Rs. 2,600 crores to Rs. 2,800 crores should be a reasonable guidance for FY27.

items.statement: Last ethanol capex of Rs. 500 crores for MP and Assam plants generated ~Rs. 1,500 crores revenue; next capex in FY28 at least similar scale
items.quote: Our last capex in the ethanol segment between Madhya Pradesh and Assam was about Rs. 500 crores between both the plants which generated revenue of close to Rs. 1,500 crores. So, any new investment will be at least in this capacity or maybe more.

items.statement: MP PLI for FY24 and FY25 received; FY26 PLI due in Q2/Q3 FY27; Assam PLI paperwork underway, expect 6+ months; NEIIPP central incentive of ~Rs. 5 crores expected for Assam
items.quote: For MP, we have received PLI for FY24 and FY25. The PLI for FY26, which is the current year, is due, which will only be received in second or third quarter of FY27. As far as PLI for Assam is concerned, there is a lot of paperwork which is required for that and the pre-preparation to get the PLI is very high in Assam. So, we are working on that, getting all the clearances, and that should also sta

items.statement: Full-year FY26 biosimilars EBITDA margin guided at mid-20s percent
items.quote: on a full year basis, we'll of course be in the mid-20s on our margins as well

items.statement: Group capex moderated to under $225 million from ~$275 million; further moderation expected as Malaysia build-out completes
items.quote: At a group level, we were tracking roughly $275 million plus, Neha, if you recollect, of capex every year. That has moderated to less than $225 million

items.statement: Insulin drug product capacity to double in FY27; drug substance expansion 1-1.5 years later
items.quote: The drug product capacity comes online in the coming fiscal year, so we expect to double our capacity

items.statement: Biosimilars Q3 EBITDA margin 28% driven by favorable mix and operating leverage; full-year average expected lower
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 700 crores, representing growth of 44% on a year-on-year basis. This translates into an EBITDA margin of 28%

items.statement: Biosimilars 9M FY26 revenue grew 17% like-for-like; growth largely from existing franchise
items.quote: For the 9 months FY '26, biosimilars revenue and EBITDA grew at 17% and 42%, respectively, on a like-for-like basis

items.statement: North America share of biosimilars revenue rose to 46-47% from ~40% typical, boosting margins
items.quote: usually, the North American geography mix out of total biosimilars is roughly 40%. This quarter, it's beyond 46%, 47%

items.statement: Extended BMS partnership through 2035 broadening integrated services scope
items.quote: Syngene extended its longstanding partnership with Bristol-Myers Squibb, or BMS, which runs through 2035, broadening the scope of its integrated services

items.statement: Cranbury OSD and Vizag API facilities received US FDA EIR with VAI status; Bangalore API got ANVISA GMP certification
items.quote: We received an EIR with VAI status from the U.S. FDA for our OSD facility in Cranbury, U.S.A., following an audit conducted in October 2025

items.statement: All structured debt retired (~$550-600M); net debt to bondholders/banks $1.1-1.2B; debt/EBITDA below 2.5x
items.quote: the net debt that we owe to the bondholders and the banks, it shifts in a narrow range of $1.1 billion to $1.2 billion

items.statement: Annualized interest cost savings ~INR 300 crores from FY27 after structured debt retirement
items.quote: Interest cost has already started coming down and as indicated earlier, we should see annualized savings of approximately INR 300 crores from FY '27

items.statement: Insulin demand robust; Biocon and innovators only players; doubling capacity to meet growing demand
items.quote: demand is absolutely not a challenge here at all. And it is as much as we can make, which is why when I was responding to Tushar, we've been very responsible in taking on more patients

items.statement: Four biosimilar molecules crossed $200M annualized revenue in FY25: trastuzumab, pegfilgrastim, insulin franchise, adalimumab
items.quote: the four molecules we have named last year, so I think trastuzumab, pegfilgrastim, insulin franchise, including glargine and adalimumab

items.statement: Acquired full global rights to Hulio (adalimumab) from FKB Japan for end-to-end manufacturing and commercialization
items.quote: we have secured full and exclusive global rights for Hulio®, which is our very successful biosimilar adalimumab, from Fujifilm Kyowa Kirin Biologics Company Limited, or FKB, Japan

items.statement: First interchangeable insulin aspart approved in US; near 100% conversion in closed-door hospital networks
items.quote: We're very proud of the fact that we are the first interchangeable rapid acting analog that the FDA has approved. We've got prior approvals in other jurisdictions as well

items.statement: Other operating expenses largely fixed; growth rate lower than revenue growth going forward
items.quote: that is largely fixed in nature. There is some element which is linked to the sales across all the three companies. And the growth of that particular line will be lower than the revenue growth

items.statement: CRDMO impacted by one customer challenge; pressure transient but will take time to ease
items.quote: the business has been impacted by challenges faced due to one customer. While this pressure will take some time to fully ease, it is transient

items.statement: No specific quantitative guidance given for FY27 biosimilars growth or margins; future described as more exciting than past
items.quote: we've refrained from giving specific guidance for the future. We did say that we will have the mid-20s for the current financial year

items.statement: Launched generic liraglutide in Netherlands as first direct-to-market GLP-1 in EU; out-licensed semaglutide to Ajanta for 26 countries
items.quote: We launched generic Liraglutide for diabetes and obesity in the Netherlands as our first 'direct-to-market' GLP-1 in the EU

items.statement: Semaglutide filings underway in Canada, Brazil, Saudi, Turkey; Health Canada yet to approve any generic GLP-1
items.quote: We have filed in Canada, Brazil, Saudi, Turkey. And we continue to file in other markets. Of course, the review cycle is long drawn, especially in markets such as Canada

items.statement: Generics capex largely complete; mainly maintenance capex going forward
items.quote: large part of capex in generics is over, and now it will be mainly the maintenance capex, which will be there, which is going to be very small compared to the previous investments

items.statement: Generics 9M FY26 revenue grew 18% YoY; EBITDA declined 32% due to new facility costs
items.quote: For 9 months FY '26, generics revenue grew at 18% year-on-year, while EBITDA declined by 32%, attributable to higher costs related to the new facilities we have commissioned in the recent past

items.statement: Out-licensing agreement with Ajanta Pharma for semaglutide in 26 countries across Africa, Middle East, Central Asia
items.quote: We also signed an out-licensing agreement with Ajanta Pharma to market our vertically integrated drug product, Semaglutide, in 26 countries across Africa, Middle East and Central Asia

items.statement: Oral insulin program dropped due to financial non-viability despite physiological success
items.quote: physiologically, it worked, but financially, it didn't make sense because insulin is a very low-cost product from that point of view. And to make it work, it was going to cost a lot more. So financially, it was not viable. And hence, we dropped the program

items.statement: Two QIPs raised nearly $1 billion to retire Viatris acquisition structured debt
items.quote: Over the past year, we proactively addressed acquisition-related leverage through 2 successive QIPs cumulatively raising nearly $1 billion

items.statement: Biocon Biologics merger with Biocon valued at $5.5B; creating integrated biopharma platform
items.quote: This milestone transaction valued Biocon Biologics at USD 5.5 billion and will establish an integrated biopharma enterprise with global reach and scale

items.statement: Domestic revenue grew 4% YoY and 18% sequentially to INR160 crores, led by non-FCT and digital momentum.
items.quote: During the quarter, we recorded a domestic revenue of INR160 crores, reflecting a year-on-year growth of 4% and a sequential growth of 18% for the year.

items.statement: EBITDA excluding digital was INR23 crores with an 18% margin.
items.quote: Our EBITDA excluding digital stood at INR23 crores, translating into an EBITDA margin of 18%.

items.statement: Cash balance stood at INR372.5 crores as of 31st December 2025.
items.quote: The company continues to maintain a robust balance sheet with a cash balance of INR372.5 crores as on 31st December 2025.

items.statement: Event and IP business grew 10.5% despite festive season shift between Q2 and Q3.
items.quote: Even with that, our event and IP business continued its strong trajectory growth of 10.5%, building on the level of recent quarters.

items.statement: Digital revenue reached INR30.8 crores, contributing nearly 50% of radio revenues, up from 27% a year ago.
items.quote: Revenues from digital business reached INR30.8 crores, contributing close to 50% of our radio revenues, up sharply from 27% in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: YTD investment in digital business was INR29 crores, a 22% decline versus same period last year.
items.quote: Total investment in digital business during the current year at YTD level stood at INR29 crores, reflecting a significant 22% decline compared to the same period last year.

items.statement: Radio advertising demand remains weak but shows early signs of stabilizing; advertisers remain cautious.
items.quote: While the demand has now started to show early signs of stabilizing, advertisers remain cautious, which has kept pressure on all traditional mediums, including radio.

items.statement: Company retains market leadership with 25% volume share in radio.
items.quote: We continue to outperform our peers, retaining our position as a market leader in the ind ustry with a strong 25% volume share

items.statement: Radio capacity utilization is around 75%.
items.quote: Gaana revenue for this quarter, almost about INR20.8 crores and our capacity utilization is around 75% for radio.

items.statement: Radio volume growth remained flattish this year.
items.quote: It's remained almost flattish this year.

items.statement: Radio rates remained flattish; festive shift caused some inventory drop and pricing pressure.
items.quote: More or less remained in the same bag. But as I said, there is a festive shift. So, there was some bit of drop in the inventory levels, and that could have put pressure on the pricing, but more or less in the flattish range ma'am.

items.statement: Radio rates still down 25-30% versus pre-COVID levels.
items.quote: It's still a drop. As I said, in the last previous meetings also, it's almost about down 25% to 30%.

items.statement: Radio contributes 51% of overall business; non-radio (digital and solutions) contributes 49%.
items.quote: So, our overall business, radio now contributes to about 51%. The non-radio business is 49%.

items.statement: Non-FCT gross margin was 27.2% and EBITDA margin 18.5% this quarter.
items.quote: So, the gross margins this quarter has been around 27.2%.

items.statement: Committed to achieving Gaana breakeven in the next few quarters.
items.quote: We remain committed to get Gaana breakeven in the few quarters going forward.

items.statement: Share of Gaana users on new pricing increased from 54% to 66% quarter-on-quarter.
items.quote: Last quarter, I had said about 54%. This now it's about 66%.

items.statement: No current plan to spin off digital business; focus is on building profitability first.
items.quote: Good question, Prashant, but it's too early to say about this. We want to build the business first, make it profitable. So, one milestone at a time.

items.statement: Ishq FM station sold to another radio player; no major station closures.
items.quote: On closures, yes, there has been one radio station, which has not closed on, but sold to another player. So, in that regard, it still remains robust, because somebody is still buying the radio company.

items.statement: Marketing spend on Gaana increased this quarter to drive subscriber growth and counter competition.
items.quote: One is on the marketing front on Gaana, we spent a little more on this quarter compared to the last year quarter because we were in a building phase and there were market requirements and competitive performances also which were happening.

items.statement: Company not reducing subscription prices despite competitive tactical offers; believes model unsustainable at lower prices.
items.quote: We are very clear that we don't reduce the price. We came under a little pressure. Our marketing spends went up, but we remain focused of getting at the right price.

items.statement: Expect path to Gaana profitability in next 2-3 quarters; not in a price drop game.
items.quote: So, but having said that, we remain committed. We believe next 2, 3 quarters, we have a path to profitability on that, 1 or month here and there, but we should be there. We are not in a price drop game.

items.statement: Future digital spend will shift to marketing (CM3 level) rather than product development (CM1) as platform is ready.
items.quote: Yes. So, it will be more on marketing to drive subscriber growth. As we breakeven in 2.5, 3 quarters, the nature of spend will be largely towards marketing, which will be on the CM3 level and not on the CM1 levels.

items.statement: Ad revenue recovery seen but not major; base effect and sentiment improvement noted; remains cautious.
items.quote: Yes. So, there is some bit of recovery. We're seeing that not major. I would not say we are very bullish on that. There is some bit of recovery, some base effect coming in, some sentiments improving. So, it's a little bit there.

items.statement: Production cost spike due to growth in Events and Solutions business; in line with EBITDA margins.
items.quote: So, it's largely our Events and Solutions business, which has shown growth. For that, the production cost has gone up. So, it's the production on those lines. So, it's in line with our EBITDA margins and all that.

items.statement: Product and content now at par with Spotify; international expansion to begin with US focus.
items.quote: Yes, the product is ready, the content is at par with Spotify. So, then you can start looking , you are looking at the Indian market, get the Indian diaspora first, get a basic number up there. So now, as I said, the international market is a given.

items.statement: Management guides 15-20% revenue growth for next 12-24 months, with 4-wheeler contribution on top of this organic rate
items.quote: Over the next 12 to 24 months, we continue to guide with our initial guidance, just 15% to 20% growth. We have kind of always outperformed the industry. So we will strive to do the same.

items.statement: Management targets 14%+ EBITDA margin going forward, believes efficiency gains will sustain margins despite planned capex
items.quote: From a going forward perspective, we feel confident that the efficiency parameters that we have done will keep helping the margin. So we believe that we should ideally be at 14% plus EBITDA margin in future as well.

items.statement: Current plant capacity utilization around 77-78%; capex being deployed to add capacity for next 2 years growth
items.quote: It's between 77%, 78%-odd. But again, these numbers also depend on how many shifts you are running and so on and so forth. But I think overall, we are well positioned with our capex plan for the next year.

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA margin 14.25% (all-time high) driven by operating leverage, efficiency drives, product mix, and escalations
items.quote: The EBITDA for this quarter is INR97.7 crores, which works out to 14.25% as compared to an EBITDA of INR77.88 crores, that is 13.2% in the corresponding quarter of previous year.

items.statement: Force Motors RFQ converted and under development; at least 2 major Mahindra RFQs at final stages; Mercedes plant approved as potential global supplier for small lamps
items.quote: Force Motors has converted. We're -- this is under development. We will be reporting that in the next meet. And also, Mahindra, we are working on certain RFQs, which are at final stages. At least 2 major RFQs are at final stages.

items.statement: Mercedes top-level team visited in January; plant approved as potential supplier globally for small lamps; RFQs expected next financial year with 18-24 month development timeline
items.quote: Mercedes top-level team visited us in the month of January, members -- senior members from Germany and India, the top people. And our -- I'm happy to inform that our plant and other things stand approved as a potential supplier to Mercedes globally for small lamps.

items.statement: Electronic content in lighting systems varies 30-80% per product; electronics R&D and EMI/EMC lab investments to drive higher content per vehicle
items.quote: It is totally dependent on product-wise. It is very difficult to say percentage, but it always varies from 30% to 80%.

items.statement: Hero MotoCorp share growing with 10+ products in front/rear lighting; Destini, Xtreme, X440 in mass production; more models upcoming
items.quote: Hero, there's -- see, we are working already on 10-odd products of Hero that is for front and rear lighting, both, wherein a few projects are already in mass production. Destini is already in mass production. Xtreme is also in mass production. X440 is in production.

items.statement: TVS Norton mass production starting in couple of months; vehicle homologation ongoing; supplies to Norton UK and TVS India expected in 3 months
items.quote: Norton, as of now, it is being launched, and mass production will start in a couple of months. We are ready, and it is -- vehicle homologation is as of now on. And might be in next 3 months' time, we'll be in a position to start our supplies.

items.statement: Yamaha Tracer 700 in production and supplying to Europe for last 4 months; domestic Yamaha models accelerating; export volumes fluctuate quarter-to-quarter
items.quote: This Tracer 700 is already in production right now, and we have started supplying to Europe. In last 4 months, it is in continuous supply. The decline in Yamaha is only because of there are a few models, which are being exported, are always based on the period base.

items.statement: Market share with HMSI stable; lower growth vs competitor due to model mix (some models exclusive to competitor); 4-wheeler business difference also affects comparison
items.quote: This is totally dependent on the model mix, which are as of now. And there are a few models which are exclusively with the competitor. Those are giving the right volume on the volume, which is giving this kind of -- yes.

items.statement: Input costs passed on rolling basis with occasional lag; no specific supply constraints currently
items.quote: Nothing specific. And if it does, as we mentioned, it is kind of passed on. It sometimes comes with a lag. But otherwise, all the input costs are passed on, on a rolling basis.

items.statement: Renewable energy rollout across plants: solar rooftop, open access solar, exploring wind in South; rooftop 4-6 months, open access ~2 months to start; impact visible in 2-3 quarters
items.quote: For these green energy initiatives and whatever the renewable energy we are implementing across our plants, one major part is the solar, solar in both forms, that is rooftop, as well as the open access. And in the South, we are also exploring the wind energy.

items.statement: Open to acquisitions for 4-wheeler growth but conservative; no advanced-stage deals currently
items.quote: Yes. To answer your question, yes, we are open for acquisition and high-growth route. However, we are also conservative in acquiring any organization because it has to be a right fit with our philosophy.

items.statement: Cash balance INR222 crores as of 31st December; surplus cash to be deployed for organic/inorganic growth opportunities in 2W/4W space
items.quote: So this is INR222 crores as of 31st December.

items.statement: Management will evaluate surplus cash utilization at appropriate time; currently focused on growth opportunities including INR200 crores capex over 18-24 months
items.quote: But yes, you're right, even then, we will have some surplus. And I think we will, at an appropriate time, take a call. But at this time, we think business presents opportunities, which we could utilize this cash at some point of time.

items.statement: Fire incidents at Rai (short circuit) and Tapukara plants; insurance claims under process (INR50 crores received for Rai, INR82.30 crores filed for Tapukara); third-party safety audits ongoing
items.quote: Rai plant, whatever fire incident has happened, happened because of short circuit. And it is being claimed. It is being already highlighted and being presented. And similarly, all the plants, we have a full commitment and safety measures.

items.statement: 2-wheeler industry production grew 15% YoY to 6.8M units in Q3; 9M production at 19.6M units; expected to cross FY19 peak of 24.5M units
items.quote: Total 2-wheeler production grew by 15% year-on-year to 6.8 million units in the quarter. For the first 9 months, industry production is already at 19.6 million units.

items.statement: Ambient interior lighting proof-of-concept approved by customer; RFQ received; long development cycle (hardware, software, validation) but good growth potential
items.quote: We have got some official go-aheads from the customer on developing proof of concept for the technology that you mentioned and a couple of other technologies. We are in the process of doing that.

items.statement: Bank angle sensor supplied to all Honda models under technical assistance from Toyodenso; canister phasing out (only few customers like Yamaha/TVS)
items.quote: Yes, bank angle sensor, we are already supplying as of now for all models of Honda. And yes, this is -- these are all under technical assistance, and it is being supplying to Honda only. And canister, of course, is no more right now.

items.statement: Direct exports to Piaggio and Aprilia in Europe; most exports indirect via Indian OEM entities (Honda, Yamaha, TVS); FTA with EU/UK not expected to materially change export model
items.quote: We are already supplying -- like in Europe, we supply directly to Piaggio, Aprilia. We supply directly both the customers from here to -- for their different models.

items.statement: EMI/EMC laboratory in Gurgaon started trials and product validation; enhances electronic capabilities and in-house testing infrastructure
items.quote: In line, with our state-of-the-art EMC and EMI laboratory in Gurgaon has started trials and product validation. This enhances our electronic capabilities and significantly strengthening our in-house testing and validation infrastructure.

items.statement: Aftermarket flat due to OEM agreements restricting aftermarket sales of developed products; new LED products have minimal aftermarket (accident replacement only)
items.quote: We are working with the OEM, and the product belongs to -- our product, whatever is being developed, it belongs to the customer. And we are bound to -- as per with the agreement, we cannot sell those supplies to market. So market is flat.

items.statement: No demand-side challenges seen for next 12-24 months; supply-side issues from 12-18 months ago resolved; industry outlook positive
items.quote: From a demand side, we don't see any challenges. From a supply side, also, there are a little bit of supply shocks were there, say, 12, 18 months on some -- few components, that have been taken care of.

items.statement: GST rationalization improved affordability in 2-wheeler segment; supportive macro and policy environment for automotive ecosystem
items.quote: In addition, GST rationalization has improved affordability in the 2-wheeler segment. This has supported retail traction and overall industry sentiment. Overall, the macro and policy environment remains constructive for the automotive ecosystem.

items.statement: US scaffolding demand slowed July-November due to capex delays and tariff uncertainty; strong pickup from November, December very strong, January-February back to 2024 levels
items.quote: The slowdown has been very prominent in the months from July till November. This has obviously adversely affected the Scaffolding segment results of December quarter, which we had expected. Having said that, from November onwards, we have actually seen a pickup in demand in the US, and that's before the trade deal got announced. December was a very strong month in sales and we have also started th

items.statement: Target 15% net margin for scaffolding segment in FY27 assuming trade deal holds and US demand continues
items.quote: In the scaffolding segment, which has been really volatile, I think, as I said earlier, our outlook is to be at 15% margin next year, barring any more majo r geopolitical disturbances, if the implementation of the trade deal remains intact, if the US demand continues to be like it is right now, I think with our product mix, with our strategy, we should be able to have growth in revenue as well as

items.statement: Scaffolding margins dropped to ~8% in Q3 due to volume decline from INR400cr to INR300cr; aluminium formwork margins pressured by competition and rising aluminium prices
items.quote: The margins have dropped only because of decrease in volume. There is from INR400 crores to INR300 crores. So that's the big effect. There has also been some reduction in operating margins in the domestic Aluminium Formwork business. That's getting a little more competitive. Aluminium prices have been rising. So that's been putting pressure.

items.statement: Engineering services margins seasonally lower in Q3 (9.5%) due to holiday employee costs; expect return to 15% in Q4
items.quote: This is seasonal. December quarter traditionally is always due to holidays, November and December, December in particular. So there are a lot of the employee costs rise because a lot of our employees around the world take their paid leaves and things like that. So as a result of that, we always have reduction in gross margin. Even last year in the December quarter, it was the same. We'll be back t

items.statement: Scaffolding capacity doubling on track; Phase 2 extrusion plant and Mach One expansion planned late FY26/FY27; Sambhaji Nagar plant at 100% utilization
items.quote: We are almost at 100% capacity utilization in the new Sambhaji Nagar plant where we completed our capex 1.5 years back. We do plan to add Phase 2 probably sometime towards the later part of '26, '27, where we will put up another extrusion plant and further increase in Mach One capacity. That will probably be towards the end of '27 or maybe early '27, '28. So yes, I mean, we are on track.

items.statement: Scaffolding pricing fully variable linked to NALCO aluminium prices; no absorption of aluminium cost fluctuations; 6 weeks scrap inventory maintained
items.quote: are fully backward integrated, as you know. So we have our own alumin ium extrusion plant. We keep about 6 weeks or so of inventory of alu minium scrap, which is our main raw material. We don't absorb any in this business, because aluminium is so volatile, all our contracts are variable. We don't have fixed price wi th any customer, and it's all the pricing is entirely linked to NALCO

items.statement: US scaffolding tariffs: 50% on steel content (Section 232) unchanged; reciprocal tariff on non-steel content reduced from 50% to 25% (Russian oil tariff removed), expected to fall to 18% after notification
items.quote: Currently, we are paying 50% on only the steel content, and we are subject to the reciprocal tariff on the non-steel content. That reciprocal tariff until now was also 50% because there were 25% reciprocal and 25% Russian oil tariff. Now the Russian oil tariff has gone away with immediate effect. So to that effect, it has come down to 25%, which will further come down to 18% once the US administra

items.statement: Drum closure US tariff reduced from 50% to 25%; previously absorbed 25% and passed 25% to customer; absorption no longer needed
items.quote: The tariff used to be 50%. We were absorbing 25%, and we were passing on 25% to the customer. Now the tariffs are reduced to 25%. So we don't need to absorb anything.

items.statement: Mach One (aluminium formwork) revenue INR200cr in Q3, INR550cr in 9M FY26; full year target ~INR900cr
items.quote: I think for the entire year, we should be on track to do INR900 crores or maybe close to INR900 crores.

items.statement: Combined Scaffolding + Mach One segment revenue target ~INR1,400cr for FY26
items.quote: We should be looking at close to INR1,400 crores.

items.statement: China drum closure volumes ~2 million sets/month in 9M FY26; targeting 10-15% volume growth in FY27 with available capacity
items.quote: Currently, we are selling close to 2 million sets a month in China. And we are continuously growing that. So I think going into FY '27, we should be able to average maybe a 10% to 15% increase in this volume and the capacity is available.

items.statement: Textiles: yarn at full utilization, fabric near breakeven (positive in 2-3 quarters), garments at 60% utilization (loss-making) targeting 80-90% in 2-3 months with US orders
items.quote: We are now moving towards higher-value garments and the US market will again reopen up. And there, in garments, we could not fulfill our entire capacity utilization. We, I think, operated at about 60%, which was also one of the reasons why we are in the red. So we expect the capacity utilization in garments to go up to 80%, 90% in the next 2 to 3 months when orders from US start coming in.

items.statement: Scaffolding inventory days increased to ~100 days due to US sales slowdown; aluminium formwork inventory days decreased
items.quote: No, it is primarily for the Scaffolding division because of the reduction in sales. Hence -- and we have not reduced our inventory in the US. So hence, the increase in inventory in days. Aluminium Formwork on the contrary, the number of days of inventory has come down this quarter.

items.statement: Engineering services: 7 verticals, dominant in industrial products, machinery, transportation (~50% of customers); offshore 60%, onsite 40%, offshore share increasing
items.quote: Currently, offshore is about 60% and on-site is 40%. Going forward, we'll probably see offshore further increasing.

items.statement: Aluminium formwork seeing influx of new/unorganized competitors in India; pricing pressure but demand growing; expect consolidation over 1-2 years
