But yes, once we have identified how well it is performing, our ability to scale is what drives future growth and profitability. So, this is the core of our model and how we are doing things. And that remains to be there. Other than this, obviously, even the styles that

items.statement: Bhiwandi warehouse fire caused INR21.85 crore inventory loss; insurance claim filed, net P&L impact INR31.22 lakhs
items.quote: On 25th November 2025, an accidental fire resulted in the loss of inventory and certain fixed assets stored at that location. I am relieved to share that there was no loss or injury to life. The affected inventory was adequately insured under a valid insurance policy. The estimated losses are fully covered and the insurance claim process is currently underway.

items.statement: Fire incident may have cost 15-20% additional revenue in Q3; management estimates revenue could have been INR75-80 crores without fire
items.quote: purely based on my judgment, we believe that 15% to 20% additional revenue could have been expected in this particular quarter.

items.statement: Thomas Scott average selling prices: denims ~INR1,200, trousers ~INR1,200, shirts INR800-1,000; high MRP-high discount strategy for marketplace visibility
items.quote: our Denims typically have an average selling price of close to actually Rs.1,200, our trousers are close to again Rs.1,200, shirts are between Rs.800 to 1,000. That is where the average selling price tends to trend.

items.statement: Primary demographic 25-40 years, secondary 20-25 years; young men entering corporate jobs
items.quote: our major demographic actually is the 25-to-40 years segment. And there is also the secondary demographic that we target, which is between 20-to-25 years segment. Essentially, a lot of purchases that happen are, for young individuals who are young men who are moving into their first job or into corporate jobs or have just in the first two, three years of their corporate jobs.

items.statement: Customer returns ~20% (vs industry 28-30%), Return to Origin 6-9% (vs industry 10-20%)
items.quote: In our case, our customer returns are quite low. So, we have customer returns of somewhere approximately close to 20%, which is lower than 28% to 30% than most other apparel brands experience in terms of customer returns. Our return to origin, which is basically in the case of cash on delivery (COD) orders, where the customer does not accept the order, so generally at the industry level, it is any

items.statement: Menswear trends have long cycles; only 2-3% of 2-3 year old bestsellers de-trended; growth driven by color extensions on winning styles
items.quote: even today, amongst the bestseller products that we created, say, two or three years back out, maybe just 2% or 3% of those products have actually gone into a de-trend bucket. Otherwise, these trends are long term. In fact, in the case of menswear, we find that launching more colors. If a base color, say a black color short is doing well and if we launch a few more colors in that, we end up findin

items.statement: Manufacturing units in Solapur, Bangalore, Gurgaon; fulfillment centers across India; factories worked extra shifts post-fire to recover output
items.quote: With manufacturing units in Solapur, Bangalore, and Gurgaon, and fulfillment centers across India, we ensure a high degree of control over quality, efficiency, and delivery speed.

items.statement: Online apparel market growing 25-35%; mass premium to premium segment expected to outpace baseline growth
items.quote: Generally, online apparel in major marketplaces is experiencing a 25% to 35% kind of growth even right now. We believe that there will be outside growth that there would be in the more premium or mass premium segments. And our focus will continue to remain out there.

items.statement: Global e-commerce partnerships being explored as small seeds for future growth
items.quote: And at the same time, we are also looking at how we can work with the right partners who can distribute inventory globally as well. There is an entire global e-commerce angle that has come into play right now. But, these are small seeds that we are putting in right now, which may give a bigger resolve over the next few quarters.

items.statement: Teams worked around the clock post-fire to minimize revenue impact; supply chain reacted quickly
items.quote: Our supply chain was quick to react. So there is a lot of things right from the grass-root factory worker to the operational logistics teams, that have worked around the clock to make sure that the journey that the company is on in terms of growth is collectively kind of achieved.

items.statement: Targets 25% CAGR for micro-irrigation over next 3 years and 50-50 revenue mix between micro-irrigation and solar EPC
items.quote: For the micro-irrigation business, we are targeting growth of 25% for the next 3 years, 25% CAGR growth. And we are targeting to change the business mix towards solar pumps -- solar EPC segment. So, we are expecting that our business mix will be 50% from micro-irrigation and 50% from solar EPC after 3 years.

items.statement: Solar pump order wins of 1,500 units with 60% executed; rooftop has no sizable order book due to fast churn
items.quote: As on date, we have total order wins of 1,500 out of which, as I said already, 60% is already executed. Also, there is further new orders expected in the coming months in that segment.

items.statement: Ahmedabad plant capex of INR10 crores, 50% incurred, balance in current quarter; no other sizable capex planned
items.quote: The expected capex amount for this plant is INR10 crores. So, almost 50% of it is already incurred and the 50% is of, the balance 50% would be incurred in the current quarter. Apart from that, going forward, there is no sizable capex planned at the moment.

items.statement: Two existing MIS plants support INR400 crore revenue; Ahmedabad plant coming online next month, full utilization by FY28
items.quote: With these existing two plants, we can comfortably achieve a revenue of INR400 crores for the micro-irrigation business alone. Also, right now, we are in process of setting up a new plant at Ahmedabad, which should come online during this quarter.

items.statement: Government budget continuity for PM KUSUM (INR5,000 crores) and PM Surya Ghar supports demand growth in solar pumps and rooftop
items.quote: The budget for PM KUSUM has been kept at the similar level. And also for the rooftop business, there is continued support under PM Surya Ghar project as well. So, for these two segments where we are operating, we see that the demand will continue to increase in the next year as well.

items.statement: GST reduced from 12% to 5% on micro-irrigation and solar products, improving affordability and demand
items.quote: Also, the government has recently announced the reduction in GST from 12% to 5% on both micro-irrigation and the solar products. So, this further improves the affordability of our products and hence, we also see that there will be a demand improvement in both the segments going forward.

items.statement: Solar pump margins vary by tender pricing, generally higher; rooftop margins in high single digits under competitive pressure
items.quote: Generally, for the rooftop segment, the operating margins are in high single digits. So, if you compare both the segments, solar water pumps, the margins are higher. Whereas in the solar rooftop, the market is competitive. And obviously, because of that, the margins remain under pressure.

items.statement: Solar pump execution: 1,500+ order wins, 60% executed as of date, balance in current quarter
items.quote: So far, if you see, we have almost 1,500 plus order wins, out of which almost as on date, 60% of the work is executed. And the balance would be executed in this quarter.

items.statement: Management expects to arrest revenue decline and move toward profitability augmentation in coming quarters.
items.quote: We have experienced close to 40% decline in the first half. We are bringing it down to about 14%, 15% in quarter 3. And we believe we are now heading towards a quarter wherein we should arrest any decline and thereafter, look at profitability augmentation.

items.statement: U.S. business targeting first profit in Q4 FY26 at $1 million+ for the quarter.
items.quote: Yes. So yes, we are looking at, hopefully, fingers crossed, making money first time in our U.S. business in quarter 4. The business internally is targeting $1 million plus of profit.

items.statement: Knit Gallery factory targeting 40-50% growth next year with margin improvement.
items.quote: And at present, given the developments that are unfolding on the tariff front, this factory is actually aiming at almost about 40% to 50% growth in terms of its internal planning for next year.

items.statement: Knit Gallery expected to achieve 50% growth next year with commensurate margin improvement.
items.quote: We are looking at a 50% growth next year in this factory. We believe that is pretty much doable. And one really does not need to do any significant capex.

items.statement: Global apparel demand remains restrained and value-led with shorter order visibility and tight inventory control.
items.quote: The global apparel environment is continuing to be very, very restrained and measured. Consumer demand across U.S. and Europe is still value -led. In fact, in value led as well, customers are restraining spending for now.

items.statement: U.S. tariff-driven price increases of 5-10% causing reduction in quantity and demand.
items.quote: I think with the U.S. tariffs, what we've been speaking to the customers, there has been a 5% to 10% price increase in the market, which has led to some reduction in quantity and demand, what they are buying.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 236 bps YoY in Q3 and 45 bps in 9M FY26 driven by procurement efficiencies, mix and cost discipline.
items.quote: Gross margin expanded 236 basis points year-over-year in Q3 and 45 basis points in the 9 -month period. This is driven by procurement efficiencies, mix and cost discipline.

items.statement: EBITDA increased 11% YoY in Q3 with margin expansion of 28 bps.
items.quote: This translated into EBITDA for Q3 increasing 11% year-over-year with margin expansion of 28 basis points.

items.statement: Manufacturing business now profitable at 3.5-4% PBT margin with potential to scale up.
items.quote: But now after all these efforts, the business is profitable, making closer to 3.5% to 4% margin, and we believe there is potential to scale up to next level.

items.statement: Knit Gallery currently at 4-5% PBT margin with potential for improvement.
items.quote: We are looking at current year somewhere around ₹250 crores plus of sales from Knit Gallery this year and a profit at this juncture about 4% to 5% of PBT margin from this factory.

items.statement: Order book growth currently at 6-7% but individual customer dialogues indicate 10-15% growth visibility for next year.
items.quote: But having said that, on the order book, what was in the mid of the year, a 14%, 15% growth in the order book, it actually right now a 6%, 7% growth in the order book.

items.statement: Primark, the largest customer, showing 10-15% growth visibility for next year.
items.quote: Primark, which is our single largest customer, basis a recent discussion that we were internally having our vertical simple approach, which is largely focused on serving them, continues to be conservative, continues to keep -- be cautious when it comes to managing working capital and opex, but clearly seeing a visibility of growth within 10% to 15% with this customer next year.

items.statement: No significant capex needed for Knit Gallery 50% growth; leveraging existing capacity and PDS processes.
items.quote: We believe that is pretty much doable. And one really does not need to do any significant capex. There is inherent potential built in by bringing in PDS -established process systems from Bangladesh factories into Knit Gallery, we should be able to scale up.

items.statement: Knit Gallery factory has 40 million pieces capacity, comparable to Bangladesh units.
items.quote: Because it's got 40 million pieces of capacity, and in terms of space also, if compared to Bangladesh, if you look at both the units in Bangladesh it is almost as big as that.

items.statement: Procurement efficiencies and factory underutilization globally enabling better negotiation and gross margin expansion.
items.quote: About 3 to 4 of our top verticals had better gross margins largely because the factories across the world are facing the challenge of the headwinds in the industry, which meant that they are not operating at anywhere close to the desired capacity, which is an opportunity for a player like PDS, which has marquee customers and a robust order book.

items.statement: Sourcing as a service now 25% of business (up from near zero 3-4 years ago) with $1B potential pipeline.
items.quote: 75% of our business is apparel, 25% other categories, 3-4 years ago, other's category was almost zero. So we are very fortunately have added based on certain kind of customers like Asda giving home business and a few others, we've now benchmarked, and we've basically positioned PDS as a sourcing company not only for apparel for other categories as well.

items.statement: New major U.S. accounts opened: Walmart, Target, PVH, T.J. Maxx onboarded as vendors in last 6 months.
items.quote: like Walmart, Target, PVH, T.J. Maxx, some of the largest retailers in the U.S. have now onboarded PDS as a vendor

items.statement: New verticals contributed ₹700 crores (45% YoY growth) and Manufacturing grew 35% YoY in 9M FY26.
items.quote: Out of the ₹9,000 crores circa turnover in the first 9 months, the business from new vertical is close to ₹700 crores, and it is almost a 45% growth over the same period last year. The Manufacturing business is 35% growth over the same period last year.

items.statement: Gerry Weber bankruptcy and Matalan restructuring impacted revenue; Design Arc merged with Poeticgem to mitigate Matalan exposure.
items.quote: Gerry Weber if you look at, unfortunately, the retailer went bankrupt. We didn't have any direct hit on our margin because end of the day, we were secured on our payments. But obviously, the gross margin that was there linked to that business doesn't continue into the future.

items.statement: PDS and Li & Fung are the two remaining global players for sourcing-as-a-service deals; PDS winning 7 of 10 pitches.
items.quote: the final 2 players left in the industry is PDS and Li & Fung. And Li & Fung is a 125-year-old company, PDS is a 25-year-old company. So there's a huge gap between where they are positioned, where we are positioned. But today, our scale and size is almost similar, right? They've had a huge contraction based on their b usiness model last few years. So PDS and Li & Fung scale and size is almost simi

items.statement: U.S. reciprocal tariff framework reduced India's effective tariff exposure from 50% to 18%; Bangladesh now at zero reciprocal tariff.
items.quote: The U.S. reciprocal tariff framework has resulted in India's effective tariff exposure reducing from a peak level of 50% to 18%, materially improving India's competitiveness in the U.S. market. At the same time, Bangladesh has subsequentl y benefited now from a recently announced zero reciprocal tariff position, further strengthening its relative advantage in global apparel sourcing

items.statement: India-EU Trade deal and U.K. FTA strengthening medium-term growth visibility for India-led exports.
items.quote: The India-EU Trade deal and the U.K. FTA are strengthening our steps in the right direction and from any India-led exports are steps in the right direction and therefore, should strengthen the medium-term growth visibility.

items.statement: Revenue split 9M FY26: U.K. 43% (up from 37%), Europe 31% (down from 38%), Americas 20% (up from 18%), Asia/Middle East 7% (flat).
items.quote: We had 43% of our revenue came in from U.K. in terms of the 9 months this year as compared to 37% last year. There's a 24% growth in absolute terms and the share going up from 37% to 43%. Europe, it came down from 38% to 31% in terms of share, a 12% decline. Gerry Weber is one case that is there. But in general, we believe EU has been far more hit by the subdued customer sentiment. Germany has bee

items.statement: Net working capital tightly managed at ~7 days (down from 17 days); operating cash flow ₹644 crores in 9M FY26.
items.quote: Net working capital remains tightly managed at around 7 days, supporting strong operating cash flow generation of ₹644 crores for the 9-month period.

items.statement: Net debt reduced sharply to ₹70 crores (from ₹374 crores March '25) despite ₹98 crores Knit Gallery acquisition debt; net debt/EBITDA ~0.2x.
items.quote: Net debt reduced sharply to around ₹70 crores as of December from ₹374 crores in March '25, despite the addition of debt of ₹98 crores from Knit Gallery acquisition. Net working capital remains tightly managed at around 7 days, supporting strong operating cash flow generation of ₹644 crores for the 9-month period. Leverage ratios of the company remain comfortable with net debt-to-EBITDA at around

Rahul has immensely added value to PDS profitability and process and systems. And therefore, we want to continue to benefit from his strategic inputs. And at the same time, as part of an internal transition management and successfully executing that, Mr. Sadik Sunasara, who has bee

items.quote: And it is wi th this context that we strengthened the leadership with Abhishek Nawani as CEO of Manufacturing business, who will be supported by our CFO, Mansi Agrawal, for the Manufacturing business. Both of them are internal elevations and Abhishek Nawani had earlier work w ith leading retailer Gap and also worked with one of the leading manufacturing companies in Indonesia called Busana. So he

items.statement: Customer creditworthiness remains key risk; 90%+ customers financially secured with insurance coverage and 6-12 month pre-warnings.
items.quote: Only thing we don't have control if customers are going bankrupt. But in our kitty of customers, I would say 90% plus customers are financially secured and having insurance from all the top insurance providers and are able to factor those invoices. So the insurance companies pre-warn us 12 -- 6 months in advance at least. So we don't have any of those warnings in existing customer base.

items.statement: GMV reached ₹14,760 crores (7% YoY) and revenue ₹9,591 crores (6% YoY) in 9M FY26; excluding Matalan and Gerry Weber, growth was 11.2%.
items.quote: For the 9 -month period, GMV reached ₹14,760 crores, reflecting a 7% year -on-year growth and revenue grew 6% to ₹9,591 crores. Top line growth was largely impacted by Matalan and Gerry Weber business, excluding which the growth, as Sanjay mentioned, is around 11.2%, demonstrating steady throughput across our platform.

items.statement: Normalized ROCE at approximately 28% reflecting improving capital efficiency.
items.quote: Leverage ratios of the company remain comfortable with net debt-to-EBITDA at around 0.2 and normalized return on capital employed at approximately 28%, reflecting improving capital efficiency.

items.statement: Management expects to close FY26 order book at INR800-900 crores and maintain revenue growth momentum into FY27, but does not provide specific forward projections.
items.quote: we are envisaging to close. We still have a good pipeline, may slip to Q1, but we are trying to close it in Q4. So -- but what number we have promised, we will be reaching up to 90% to 100% of those. That's for sure

items.statement: Q3 FY26 new orders of INR170 crores (excl. mobility and product services) brought closing order book to INR999 crores as of 31 Dec 2025.
items.value: INR170 crores new orders; INR999 crores closing order book
items.quote: During the quarter, we booked new orders totaling to INR170 crores, excluding mobility and product services, taking our closing order book as on 31st December to a healthy INR999 crores.

items.statement: Order book segmental split: ~INR460 crores Technology Solutions, ~INR520-530 crores Geospatial (incl. river linking project).
items.value: INR460 crores Technology; INR520-530 crores Geospatial
items.quote: So on the technology absorption side, it is around INR460 crores and around INR520 crores -- INR530 crores is towards the geospatial side, majorly of which is an order in relation to the river linking project.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin expanded 452 bps YoY to 23.48%; 9M FY26 margin up 302 bps to 21.59%. Management expects margins to sustain and improve further.
items.quote: EBITDA increased by 88% to INR40 crores, with margins expanding to 23.48%, reflecting a strong improvement of 452 basis points compared to the last year.

items.statement: EBITDA margins have grown steadily for 8 quarters from ~17% to 23.4%; management believes operating leverage and higher-margin technology mix will sustain improvement.
items.quote: If you see the presentation also, we have seen the EBITDA margins growing steadily quarter-on-quarter for the last 8 quarters. So from a base level of 17% every quarter we have seen increase, and we have reached at 23.4%.

items.statement: Demand remains strong across segments; Geospatial & Engineering Services grew 122% YoY in Q3 (INR109 crores) and 77% in 9M (INR257 crores); Technology Solutions declined 3% in Q3 but grew 79% in 9M (INR233 crores).
items.value: Geospatial Q3: INR109 cr (+122% YoY); Tech Solutions Q3: INR61 cr (-3% YoY)
items.quote: For the quarter under review, our Geospatial and Engineering Services revenue increased by 122% year-on-year to INR109 crores, while on the Technology Solutions side, revenue declined moderately by 3% to around INR61 crores.

items.statement: INR24 crores invested in Q3 for technology innovation and business development (US expansion, AI/ML); INR16 crores expensed to P&L.
items.value: INR24 crores invested; INR16 crores expensed
items.quote: During the quarter, we invested INR24 crores in technology innovations and business development, specifically aimed at expanding our presence in the U.S. and other territories. Out of this investment, INR16 crores was charged to our profit/loss account.

items.statement: Net working capital cycle at 160-162 days in Q3; collections of INR170 crores matched revenue. Target to reduce to ~125 days by Q4 FY26 as government disbursements accelerate.
items.quote: We have maintained discipline of working capital with our net working capital cycle in the range of 160 to 162 days. During the quarter, our collections were INR170 crores, which is equivalent to operational revenue.

items.statement: Receivables: INR150 crores total (INR125 crores <1 yr, INR25-27 crores >1 yr); Unbilled revenue ~INR250 crores; INR140 crores billed in Q3.
items.value: INR150 crores debtors; INR250 crores unbilled
items.quote: Sir, our debtors as on 31st December is around INR150 crores, out of which INR150 crores, INR125 crores is approximately within 1 year only. So only INR25 crores to INR27 crores is pertaining to year -- more than 365 days. And as far as unbilled is concerned, it is approximately around INR250 crores of unbilled revenue.

items.statement: Only cash credit borrowing of INR29-30 crores (limit INR80 crores); no long-term debt; net debt-to-equity negative.
items.quote: Right now, we are just using our INR29 crores, INR30 crores of CC. So that's the only loan we have in our book.

items.statement: INR40 crores capital infused into US subsidiary in Q3 (part of ~INR28M mobilised for inorganic growth); used for business development, team building, product development.
items.quote: INR 40 crores was infusion of capital. Kaushik Khona: That's infusion of capital. Not everything is P&L. What we have mentioned in the P&L is only INR16 crores, which is towards the business development for the geospatial business and the acquisition -- the new business which we took of VTS

items.statement: Inorganic acquisition targets under due diligence; compliance delays; conclusion expected in next 2-3 months (by Q4 FY26 end).
items.quote: The due diligence process is also almost over. There has been a slight delay from the compliance side because we are evaluating all the aspects. So I think we are not able to give you the answer right now. Hopefully, by quarter end -- quarter 4 end, you will have a little more clarity about the acquisition targets.

items.statement: Key Q3 wins: UP Jal Jeevan Mission extension INR107 crores (to Mar 26-27), Maharashtra NSMP ~INR7 crores cumulative, MSRDC digital platform INR12 crores, MMRDA urban change detection & BIM INR20 crores, Vasai Virar STP PMC INR12 crores.

items.statement: Strategic MOUs signed with Tech Mahindra (global BD & execution, telecom, Europe, Middle East, Australia) and Aetosky (AI/image interpretation, Middle East, South Asia, Far East).
items.quote: In our efforts to build long-term strategic partnerships with few technology domain experts and those who can provide us a platform for expanding our services and geographies where we serve, we have entered into MOU with Tech Mahindra and Aetosky, which adds to the long list of strategic and OEM partnerships.

items.statement: US subsidiary revenue: INR19 crores top line (INR21 crores incl. other) in 9M FY26; EBITDA ~20%; FY26E ~INR23-25 crores (<5% of consolidated). Targeting Middle East (KSA, Dubai) as second geography.
items.quote: If you analyze that, the U.S. subsidiary would be contributing this year at around INR23 crores, INR25 crores at the end of this year. And we are -- so if you look at the U.S. subsidiary this year, it will be in the range of around less than 4% to 5%.

items.statement: Bid pipeline delayed by 4 months due to back-to-back Maharashtra election code of conduct; INR600-700 crores of bids expected to close in Q4 FY26 or Q1 FY27; 3-5 year pipeline being built for sustainable growth.
items.quote: We stated that we are pursuing some INR600 crores to INR700 crores of order. We bagged 2, 3 orders, one is INR117 crores and then INR20 crores or so. There has been a code of conduct, which we didn't anticipate back-to-back, 2 code of conduct has come and it's almost lost over 4 months of operation.

items.statement: Land mapping/modernization opportunity ~INR1,000+ crores per state; Maharashtra Unified Land Management at EOI stage; company bidding aggressively.
items.quote: This is kind of INR1,000 crores-plus kind of project for each of the states. we are definitely going to bid those projects. We will be aggressively putting up our bids for those.

items.statement: Management changes described as planned: Dr. Abhay Kimmatkar (28 yrs), CFO Amita Saxena returned after short break; Prashant Kamat moved to Independent Director; Chairman Sagar Meghe joined as Whole-Time Director.
items.quote: Dr. Abhay Kimmatkar is there since last 28 years. Ms. Amitaji was already the CFO prior to 2024. She had a short break by which we had Samir for a short time, but she is back to the company. We had the planned exit of Prashant Kamatji, who has completed his tenure, but he is already onboarded with -- as an Independent Director.

items.statement: Order inflow timing risk: code of conduct delays pushed INR600-700 crores of expected bids from Q3/Q4 to Q4/Q1; river linking and JJM projects subject to government pace.
items.quote: There has been a code of conduct, which we didn't anticipate back-to-back, 2 code of conduct has come and it's almost lost over 4 months of operation. So government was standstill on taking decisions and coming out with tenders.

items.statement: New AI/ML & embedded electronics vertical launched; product development for infrastructure domain; AI solutions being integrated into MMRDA change detection project with Aetosky.
items.quote: Additionally, the company has initiated and invested into development of product solutions focused on the infrastructure vertical and emerging technologies through a new vertical focused on the artificial intelligence and machine learning and embedded electronics.

items.statement: FY26 revenue target around Rs 1,000 crore with PAT margin ~8%
items.quote: Sir if I talk to you about this year, what my opinion is, my thinking is that somewhere around Rs. 1,000 crores topline revenue should come. And we should be at a PAT margin of around 8% or so approximately.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target Rs 1,500 crore with profitability improvement
items.quote: Now next year sir I still maintain my earlier statement of Rs. 1,500 crores. Which I believe should not be any problem.

items.statement: Medium-term revenue target Rs 2,500-3,000 crore by 2029 with 9-10% PAT margin
items.quote: Sir look, if you want a very straight answer to this question from me then somewhere in 2029 there should be minimum Rs. 2500 thousand revenue. And you know if these things running at the level they are running continue at this level also, and there is no expectation of any very big improvement also then sir somewhere 9% to 10% PAT lines we should get.

items.statement: Unit 6 capex Rs 25-30 crore remaining, to be completed before March
items.quote: Sir in Unit 6 still Rs. 25- Rs. 30 crores of capex is left which is ongoing. We haven't you know that is under process. Which I believe should be completed before March.

items.statement: Unit 8 greenfield project estimated completion by March 2028
items.quote: Sir it is a practical estimate because you know there are three plants in Unit 8 also. It is not only one plant. These are three plants. And the capacity is also quite decent capacity is almost the double the capacity of our existing unit 6. So we believe this is at least going to take 2 years or so.

items.statement: Unit 5 and 6 trial production expected by March if electricity connection received by February
items.quote: We are expected to start the trials somewhere by the March if we get electricity connection by February.

items.statement: New units assumed at 60-65% utilization for FY27 guidance
items.quote: Sir I am not doing too much in them. I am assuming utilization somewhere around 60 -65% in this.

items.statement: Current utilization 65% in chemicals, 55-60% in fertilizers for 9M FY26
items.quote: Our utilization in chemical sector is 65% and in fertilizers it is 55% to 60% in nine months.

items.quote: Look sir at this moment what I am understanding based upon your question and the data you provided, is that this margin dip that is visible, this is mainly due to the increase into the raw material prices. That too also specifically due to the sulphur.

items.value: Force NXT value growth 26.5%, volume growth 48.1%
items.quote: Force NXT continued its strong momentum, registering a year-on-year value growth of 26.5% and volume growth of 48.1% in quarter 3 FY '26. For the 9 months ended FY '26, Force NXT achieved a value growth of 16.7% and volume growth of 27.1%.

items.statement: Modern trade, e-commerce and quick-commerce channels contributed 12.8% of Q3 revenue, growing 36% value and 38.9% volume in 9M
items.quote: Collectively, these channels contributed 12.8% of overall revenue during the quarter. For the 9 months ended FY '26, these channels recorded strong value growth of 36% and volume growth of 38.9%, contributing 11.6% to overall revenue.

items.statement: Exports grew 10.9% value in Q3 FY26, accounting for 5.6% of revenue
items.quote: On the export front, we delivered a value growth of 10.9% in quarter 3 FY '26 with exports accounting for 5.6% of overall revenue for the quarter.

items.statement: No major capex commitment in near term, focus on free cash flow and debt reduction
items.quote: With no major capex commitment in the near term, the focus remains on enhancing free cash flow and further reducing debt.

items.statement: Operating cash flow of INR 60 crores generated in 9M FY26
items.quote: The company generated operating cash flow of INR60 crores as of December '25.

items.statement: Trade discounts and incentives at 6-6.5% of revenue, advertisement spends rationalized to 6.5% of operating income in 9M
items.quote: Advertisement spends were rationalized to 6.5% of operating income in 9 months FY '26, and we expect this ratio to moderate further in the coming quarter as operating leverage improve.

items.statement: No price hikes in industry for last 18 months; yarn prices (50% of production cost) drive pricing
items.quote: The last 18 months, in our industry, no one took a price hike as such. And we are very hopeful that with this tariff thing going down and now Tiruppur as an export hub, the yarn demand will increase, and it will give some push to the industry with respect to some raw material prices going up and maybe we'll be able to take a price hike then.

items.statement: Backward integration in spinning (45,000-46,000 spindles) provides cost advantage; cotton procurement at competitive rates
items.quote: We have a spinning mill of about 45,000, 46,000 spindles. So, we are very well covered with that also for this quarter of the yarn whereas as backward integration, we are much in a better space.

items.statement: Medium-term EBITDA margin target of 14-15% sustainable level; FY27 expected to be better than FY26's 11.5-12%
items.quote: Over time, I think in our industry, the segment where we operate, it would be very -- it would be nice to say or the sustainable level of EBITDA that we look forward to is somewhere between 14% to 15%, keeping in mind the operating leverage that we get at a certain level of volumes. And -- so this year, we'll be doing somewhere between 11.5% to 12%. And next year will definitely be better. And in

items.statement: Merger of 9 proprietary companies filed with SEBI; expected to rationalize INR 5-7 crores annualized expenses and improve net worth
items.quote: So overall, we analyze around INR5 crores to INR7 crores of expenses is to be rationalized due to this merger. And more than this, the net worth of the company -- in our net worth of the company, basically because due to the brand coming at very low -price, at book value price. So, net worth of the company -- in the net worth of Dollar Industries is increased.

items.statement: Competitive intensity easing but still present; company maintains pricing discipline with 1-1.5% discounts vs competitors' 4-5%
items.quote: So, if someone is involved in the deep discounting of, let's say, 4% to 5%, we are in -- like we are giving around 1%, 1.5%. We are not going down to 5% kind of a thing. And we are very sure about it internally also that we won't be doing that.

items.statement: Raw material volatility due to US tariff changes and cotton/yarn price fluctuations; Bangladesh zero-duty access may divert export demand
items.quote: Current situation of exports also, if you see with the Trump slapping so many tariffs and again going down, and all of a sudden now he has removed the tariffs. So, the market has gotten more tighter with the yarn rates coming up and again. So, the market right now is extremely volatile in terms of raw materials.

items.statement: Shareholder suggested buybacks instead of dividends for tax efficiency; management acknowledged suggestion
items.quote: So, with the new tax regime, buybacks have started falling under long-term capital gains or short-term capital gains. So, they are being treating as capital gains. So, I would request you to consider doing buybacks instead of paying out dividends as they are tax efficient and they also extinguish outstanding shares and serve as a reward for long-term investors.

items.statement: Expects to close NGC contract next month and end FY26 with order book around ₹50,000 crores
items.quote: we are confident of this contract getting concluded during the current financial year, which means next month we intend closing this contract , signing the contract with the Indian Navy. They have also indicated that the approval process is well on track which means we are hopeful and confident of ending the current financial year with an order book around ₹50,000 crores.

items.statement: Targets FY27 order book of around ₹70,000 crores assuming P-17 Bravo win as L2 shipyard
items.quote: if things go on well , we would like to look at ending FY '2 7 with an order book plus around ₹70,000 crores.

items.statement: Expects revenue CAGR of 25-30% in FY26 and FY27 to be peak revenue year
items.quote: we will be able to provide a CAGR between 25% to 30% in this financial year. Next financial year, that is FY '27, is going to be a peak year

items.statement: Order book at ₹18,482 crores as of 31 Dec 2025, first time below ₹20,000 crores
items.quote: Our order book position as of 31st December is ₹18,482 crores. And interestingly, this is the first time we are dipping below ₹20,000, which is good news for you, which means our execution rate has picked up.

items.statement: Won NGC order as L1, 5-ship project worth ~₹33,000 crores, contract negotiations in final stages
items.quote: We have won it. We have become the L1 and it is a big project. It is a five-ship project amounting to approximately ₹33,000 crores and the price negotiations have been completed and the contract negotiations are in final stages.

items.statement: Non-defense pipeline of ~₹1 lakh crores from 207 platforms, conservative estimate
items.quote: a conservative, very conservative value of these projects could be plus ₹1 lakh crores . Naturally, they will come out in a staggered fashion.

items.statement: Concurrent construction capacity increased from 24 to 28 platforms in 2025, targeting 32 by end of CY2025 and 35 by end of 2026
items.quote: Two years back we had a capacity to construct 24 platforms concurrently. Today, that is in 2025, we increased it to 28 platforms. That is big and small and medium sized put together. And with the ongoing modernization that we are executing , by the end of this calendar year , we intend on enhancing this to 32 ships

items.statement: Brownfield expansion at 3 Kolkata port sites, two to start production by end of CY2025, third in 2 years
items.quote: With two of these facilities, we will be able to commence production by end of the calendar year. And the third facility, which is a bigger facility, we expect the production to commence there after the modernization efforts are completed in a span of two years.

items.statement: Greenfield expansion in Gujarat at Kandla and Bhavnagar, conservative estimate 3-5 years for production readiness, targeting 12 large vessels
items.quote: Our conservative estimate is 3 years from now. And this should meet the demand for large-size platforms, both in India and for abroad because we are getting a lot of queries from abroad.

items.statement: Margins will be healthy, order book enhancement not at cost of margins; NGC margins similar to P-17 Alpha
items.quote: margins will be, let us say, healthy. Order book enhancement will not be at the cost of margins . I think that answers your question.

items.statement: Commodity price inflation has minimal impact on margins as 65% equipment cost is customer-nominated and steel tied up with SAIL
items.quote: Commodity price increase has got minimal impact on our margins, because in our case, in a project, if you take 100% as a pr oject cost, around 65% come out of equipment. Most of this equipment being customer -nominated, or in a pool of customer -nominated band. So , fluctuations really don't affect

items.statement: Indigenous content of completed projects over 85%, gap mainly in propulsion and weapon systems
items.quote: the indigenous content of the 3 projects that we have completed in the last 5 years completed, completed means done and dusted, it is plus 85%.

items.statement: Delivered 5 major platforms in 9M FY26 (1 Frigate P-17A, 3 ASW SWC, 1 Survey Vessel), plans 3 more in next 3 months
items.quote: we have delivered five major platforms, that is, ships, during the last nine months. That is the first nin e months of the financial year. items.statement: German client increased order from 4 to 12 multipurpose vessels, keel laying of 2 done, 3rd planned this month
items.quote: I think last time when we met , we had a contract of four of these vessels. Then after seeing our performance and inspecting our site and the progress, they increased to eight and as of now it has been increased to 12.

items.statement: Government announced ₹69,725 crores shipbuilding schemes including 15-30% subsidy, credit notes, maritime development fund, interest subvention, cluster development
items.quote: The various schemes for incentivizing or revitalizing the shipbuilding segment. So, the total financial outlay what they have provided is about ₹69,725 crores divided into two, three pillars. The first is about the shipbuilding financial assistance. It is a very attractive scheme where certain kind of platforms which are constructed in India based on the type of platforms get incentivized subsidy,

items.statement: Export opportunities huge from Europe (Netherlands, Germany, Sweden, Norway, Belgium) as they shift from China/Korea; Middle East also approaching
items.quote: Most of the European countries, be it Netherlands, be it Germany, be it Sweden, be it Norway, they are actually looking at India. Most of the customers who approached us and Belgium, most of whom we are engaging are all European customers. They were going to China, Korea. They are no longer taking orders for the kind of platforms which they approached us.

items.statement: Inducting 137 executives from top institutions, maintaining lean blue-collar workforce, strong vendor base for skilled work
items.quote: we are induc ting another 150 executives, 137 executives. And all of them, I can assure you, come from top institutions of the country, the best. That is what we pick up.

items.statement: 30mm naval surface gun project: 17 guns ordered by Navy, 4 installed, completion by mid-2027; Coast Guard discussing 49 more, contract expected Q1 FY27
items.quote: Currently we got order for 17 guns and all from the Indian Navy. And of these 17 guns, 4 guns have already been installed on board the various platforms and the sea trials and so on and so have been completed. As far as the execution of these 17 guns are concerned, we intend completing this project by mid of 2027

items.statement: Non-defense order conversion uncertain, only 2 RFPs and 1 EOI in last year; suggests wait and watch for 6 months
items.quote: The stocks on RFPs com ing out has been going on for the last one year. So far, only 2 RFPs have come out in the last one year, plus one EOI. So, let us just wait a bit and watch for the non-defense.

items.statement: Investing in automation including robotic welding, plasma cutting; capex need-based to maintain execution excellence
items.quote: As far as automation is concerned, yes, this is an imperative, and we already started investing, and should you visit our facilities, we have some of the best in terms of the welding machines, the plasma cutting machines, the robotic welding machines, and so on. And we will continue investing in that.

items.statement: NGC contract will have stage payments per DAP, no advance payment; first stage payment on signing for pre-production activities
items.quote: I don't want any advance. Don't give me any advance. I want a stage payment. It is as per the DAP. There is a stage payment. I don't get any advance. I get a stage payment. So, to answer your question, yes, we will get a stage payment as soon as we sign the contract.

items.statement: Government interest subvention scheme provides 3% interest subsidy for shipowners, active and being leveraged
items.quote: around ₹5,000 crores has been earmarked for an interest incentivization policy. So, here the interest is unfortunately very, very high and none of the shipowners are able to afford that kind of interest . So, 3% interest subsidy has been provided. This scheme is also active.

items.statement: Target 15-20% volume growth for FY26, focused on Q4 recovery
items.quote: Our target is to bring 15% to 20% growth. We are still focused on how to convert that in this quarter.

items.statement: No volume or revenue guidance for FY27 until Q4 and Q1 FY27 performance reviewed
items.quote: After Q4 finishes and we study how things are in Q1, only then can we make a goal for FY'27.

items.statement: Q3 volume declined 29% QoQ due to 40-50% gold price surge; demand recovering as prices stabilize
items.quote: In this quarter, our volume degrowth is 29% in terms of quantity, quarter-on-quarter comparison.

items.statement: Gold price volatility caused retailers to hold purchases; demand returning as prices stabilize over last 10-15 days
items.quote: Now that the gold price has stabilized, the demand that has emerged again in the market gives us a prediction that this recovery will be a benefit for us.

items.statement: IIJS Premier orders 80-90% dispatched; IIJS Signature orders 80% dispatched; new orders from two national chains for 18-carat jewelry
items.quote: The orders we booked for IIJS Premier, the dispatching is almost clear, about 80% has been dispatched. Ongoing daily dispatching is happening. So, maybe 80% to 90% of IIJS Premier is dispatched. Regarding IIJS Signature, the order booking there -- our target is to dispatch it in the next 60 days. Almost 80% of that is also dispatched.

items.statement: Order book summary to be filed on exchange in 1-2 days; previous orders on hold now being dispatched
items.quote: We will put the overall summarized working on the Exchange in one or two days.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 233 bps to 8.78% in Q3 FY26; PAT margin improved 103 bps to 6.11%
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin expanded by 233 basis points to 8.78% and PAT margin improved by 103 basis points to 6.11%.

items.statement: Aggressive push into high-margin Diamond Polki segment as gold price drives customer shift
items.quote: We will go aggressively for Diamond Polki, which is a high-margin centric product.

items.statement: Successfully developed 18-carat handmade jewelry achieving 22-carat quality; received orders from two national chains
items.quote: Achieving 22-carat quality standards in 18-carat handmade jewelry is quite difficult for the industry. Somehow, as an organized manufacturer, we did R&D in our SOPs and got success in 18 carat.

items.statement: Introduced 14-carat in diamond polki segment; increased casting component in fusion category for lightweight machine-made jewelry
items.quote: We are introducing 14-carat jewelry in the diamond polki segment. Before the gold price hike, we were doing jewelry in 18 carat in diamond and polki. But now we are moving to 14 carat.

items.statement: Corporate national chains contribution increasing; hired dedicated sales team for corporate accounts; two new national chains onboarded with agreements complete
items.quote: Majorly, the contribution we have currently, the weightage of corporate national chains is increasing in overall sales contribution. Our focus is also on national chains.

items.statement: Retailers holding purchases not reducing stock; waiting for consumer budget clarity at new gold prices
items.quote: They are not reducing stocking; they are holding their purchase. They have no plan to reduce stock because they don't know what the c onsumer mindset is

items.statement: Capacity setup ready for 750 kg (added second floor for 250 kg); utilization at 52% due to gold price impact; 93% achieved last year on 500 kg floor
items.quote: Regarding capacity utilization, last year, we had achieved 93% on one floor of 500 kgs. This year, we added another floor. On that floor, we have a plan for an additional 50%, 250 kgs. So, for the target of 500 kgs to 750 kgs utilization, our setup is all ready.

items.statement: Hedging policy maintained; stock quantity hedged regardless of price volatility
items.quote: We are managing, as I said in the last concall, our policy is a hedging policy. Whatever we book, we maintain our stock quantity. No matter what happens, we don't focus on price volatility; we maintain our stock and keep it hedged.

items.statement: Credit cycle roughly 15-20 days varying by customer
items.quote: Roughly, it is a cycle of 15 to 20 days generally.

items.statement: NSE main board listing application submitted 1-1.5 months ago; NSE scrutiny ongoing
items.quote: we mentioned our plan to list on NSE. We applied about before one or one and a half months ago. Currently, NSE’s scrutiny of documentation is ongoing

items.statement: Artisan workforce stable; no procurement or skilled labor bottlenecks; artisans with company for many years
items.quote: It is absolutely stable. Our artisans are not new; they have been with us for many years. They have experienced many ups and downs in the market. They have confidence in the company.

items.statement: Design-to-product cycle 45-60 days typically, up to 90 days for high jewelry
items.quote: Generally, design to final product takes around 45 to 60 days. But again, depending on the intricacy and the use of components we are taking, it depends on that. So, roughly you can say 45 to 60 days. If we have to do fine and very high jewelry designs, it goes up to 90 days as well.

items.statement: Gold price volatility caused temporary demand destruction in wedding season Q3; recovery expected in 1-2 quarters
items.quote: This can be counted as short-term pain which came in this quarter. Now, the gold price has become somewhat sustainable in the last 10 to 15 days. So, the market demand has started being ongoing again. This gap will be recovered in the next 1 or 2 quarters.

items.statement: Plan to file design patents for unique components, shapes, and manufacturing techniques starting August 2026
items.quote: Suppose from August this year, our pl an is to start filing for patents for the unique components we have developed, unique shapes we have designed in -house, and the manufacturing technique or component design

items.statement: No significant competition in organized antique jewelry design manufacturing; each player has distinct design focus
items.quote: No, as such, we are not at a stage where there is any competition. We can't call it competition because this is a designing field. Among organized designed manufacturers in antique jewelry, there is no such difficulty or challenge or competition.

items.statement: Expect double-digit e-commerce growth in FY27 driven by CPCB EPR exchange
items.quote: We are very optimistic about this exchange, and definitely, we are hoping that there will be good double-digit growth.

items.statement: CPCB EPR exchange revenue to start from Q1 FY27, stabilize by Q2 FY27
items.quote: Revenue start flowing right from the Q1 of next financial year, if everything goes as per our plan. But the actual growth will happen after it stabilizes over a period of two quarters.

items.statement: Dividend payout minimum 30% of PAT or 4% of net worth per DIPAM guidelines
items.quote: Dividend payout is clearly spelt out in our policy that is 30% of the PAT or 4% of the net worth whichever is higher, which is as per DIPAM guideline.

items.statement: Capex mainly for end-of-life hardware/software replacement and new Delhi corporate office
items.quote: Most of the CAPEX that is needed, apart from exceptional items like this new building, which happened in the last fiscal is on end-of-life replacement cost, basically hardware and software of our electronics, of our backbone.

items.statement: Awarded CPCB EPR certificate exchange development, platform live, trading to start FY27
items.quote: has been awarded the work of developing and operating the country's first exchange for trading EPR certificates. This project, on behalf of CPCB, is now in a fairly advanced stage with the lifestyles already operational and trading expected to begin in the coming fiscal year

items.statement: Completed first tranche of DGFT gold bullion TRQ allocation, further events scheduled
items.quote: I am happy to inform you that the first tranche of gold bullion allocation has successfully been completed on our platform and further events have now been scheduled by DGFT.

items.statement: Sold 3.5 million tons iron ore for NMDC, allocated 22 coal blocks in 13th/14th round
items.quote: we have sold about 3.5 million tons of iron ore for NMDC. And we have also allocated about 22 coal blocks in the 13th and 14th round of Commercial Coal Block Auctions

items.quote: Out of the 21 mines put up for critical minerals so far, the technical bids have been received for 17 mines. items.quote: We have signed the key agreement with the Mata Vaishno Devi Shrine Board for sale of precious metals.

items.quote: In this quarter, it is share of loss is Rs. 1.05 crores. And the corresponding period of last year, it was Rs. 1.57 crores share of loss. So, it is a positive step and we hope that it will be converted into a positive one in the coming days.

items.quote: As a part of this augmentation, unit at Noida, which was incurring a very high running cost has been closed. A new one is being started at Kalyan, Maharashtra. items.quote: As of now, five categories of materials have been identified and for which the EPR framework is already operating. But in the coming years, in another one or two years, we expect that the other three to four categories will be added. So that will be a very robust framework.

items.quote: We expect that this will be encouraging and it will be paving the way for future commodities like silver and others.

items.quote: See, I do not think we should be analyzing it quarter-to-quarter as far as e-commerce revenue is concerned. What happens is a lot of factors come into play when we offer our services for auctions. So, the state government and policy matters and all those things.

items.quote: Consolidated operational revenues for the quarter stood at INR 586 crores, virtually flat on a quarter-on-quarter and in year-on-year basis.

items.quote: Retail Broking income was INR 288 crores this quarter versus INR 271 crores in Q2 FY '26, which is up 6%, mostly on line of increased volumes.

items.quote: Operational profit before tax was INR 119 crores, down 27% on a quarter -on-quarter basis, primarily on account of increase of expenses.

items.quote: Depreciation increased by 13% on account of investment in branches. Fees and commissioning expenses increased by 10% due to higher payouts, which is now standing at INR 130 crores. Admin expense was up 5% to INR 91 crores.

items.quote: I think we will be adding maybe another 10-15 RMs. Beyond that I don't think that will happen in the next two months.

items.statement: TBR/ARR mix broadly 60/40; last quarter saw increase in TBR due to NCDs and fixed income allocation; expect 60/40 or 65/35 going forward
items.quote: No, actually, if you see that mix between TBR and ARR has been broadly in the 60 /40 range, and I think last quarter we have seen some increase in the fixed income space because of increased allocation of fixed income like NCDs. items.quote: We constantly explore strategic and other opportunities to enhance shareholder value. If and when there is a development that requires any disclosure in the SEBI's LODR regulations, we will make it.

items.statement: Aspiring for double-digit volume growth in FY27
items.quote: next year should be a double-digit kind of volume growth that we are aspiring for.

items.statement: Targeting 10-12% EBITDA margin excluding Bathware losses for FY27
