items.statement: Unbilled revenue Rs.283 crores; total receivables Rs.500 crores (less than 6 months Rs.116 crores, 6-12 months Rs.23 crores, 1-2 years Rs.87 lakhs)
items.value: Unbilled Rs.283 cr, Total Rs.500 cr
items.quote: The Rs.500 crores is the total sum of all the receivables. That includes unbilled and billed also. So, the unbilled portion is Rs.283 crores. Less than six months is about Rs. 116 crores. Six months to one year is about Rs. 23 crores. One year to two years is about Rs.87 lakhs. That is all

items.statement: Revenue cycle 60-120 days after expenditure, average 90 days working capital requirement
items.quote: Once we execute the work, we get the receivables and the 90-days we take as the receivable amount. So, this is 60-days-to-120-days and sometimes as an average, we take it 90-days period after expenditure.

items.statement: Total bank exposure ~Rs.700 crores (Rs.650 cr non-fund-based BGs, Rs.50 cr cash credit and HAM project loan)
items.quote: So, that would be around Rs.700 crores is our exposure to the banks which includes Rs.650 crores of non-fund-based bank guarantees, and about Rs.50 crores in shape of cash credit limit and this loan that I told you about.

items.statement: No plans to expand borrowings; current facilities sufficient for project execution
items.quote: No plans on expanding in our borrowings. The facilities that we have are sufficient for execution of our projects.

items.statement: Promoter pledged shares for personal loan of Rs.210 crores (Rs.70 cr repaid, Rs.140 cr outstanding); plan to reduce to <Rs.100 cr by end FY26, full repayment by FY27
items.quote: So, we took loan of about Rs.210 crores, out of which we have already paid about Rs.70 crores and the current outstanding stands at Rs.140 crores. Within this financial year, we will reduce it to about Rs.100 crores, and by next financial year, this would be settled.

items.statement: Pledged shares can only be released after full loan repayment
items.quote: The shares that are pledged with can only be released after we repay the whole amount.

items.statement: Acquired Fatehpur factory (120 bighas near Kanpur) for Rs.60 crores via NCLT; current market value ~100% higher
items.quote: So, we purchased that land for about Rs.60 crores and currently its market value would be almost 100% higher than that.

items.statement: Fatehpur factory self-sufficient, 50-100 employees, producing 800-900 tons, targeting 1,100+ tons next FY
items.quote: Sir, it might be possible in future. But till now, I think that plant is producing about 800-900 tons of output. And it can reach an output of about 1,100-plus tons in the coming financial year.

items.statement: Q3 revenue impacted by Uttarakhand heavy rainfall, landslides and disaster management delays; 15-20 days lost in Q3
items.quote: And as you know, Uttarakhand saw unexpectedly huge rainfall and natural disasters in the Q2. So, in Q3, our work was mainly focused on repair and revamping of the work-in progress and due to extension of the monsoon to Q3, about 15-to-20 days were lost in the Q3.

items.statement: FY27 revenue expected to be better than FY25
items.quote: Yes, FY27 would be better than FY25.

items.statement: Civil engineering projects face land clearance issues, weather disruptions, administrative priorities causing quarterly fluctuations
items.quote: Sometimes the land is not clear, sometimes as we have seen in these two quarters that rainy season has affected so much. In Q2, it affected so much. In Q3, we tried to revamp it and to reorganize it. But, once there is a heavy rain, there are some disasters also. So, the administration which look after the development work, they also give the priority to the disaster restoration.

items.statement: 70-80% revenue from water sector, rest from buildings, electricity transmission and distribution
items.quote: We primarily execute the projects in infrastructure sector with our focus being in water sector. About 70% to 80% of the revenue comes from water sector and rest is from other infrastructure sectors such as buildings, electricity transmission and distribution, etc.

items.statement: Fatehpur factory employs 50-100 semi-skilled and technician staff
items.quote: Employees, I think are somewhere between 50-100 employees. Mostly semi-skilled and technicians.

items.statement: Vizag greenfield project groundbreaking scheduled this month with Rs.1,000 crores investment over 3-4 years for API and intermediates capacity
items.quote: This project was approved by a board with a total investment plan of Rs.1 ,000 crores over the next three to four years.

items.statement: Unit 3 expansion nearing completion for contrast media intermediates, Rs.146 crores incurred to date, validation expected Q1 FY27
items.quote: We have incurred a cumulative CAPEX of approximately Rs.146 crores to -date. This plant exemplifies our approach to securing supply chains and defining leadership in complex high barrier segments like iodinated contrast media.

items.statement: Rs.40 crores investment for new Hyderabad R&D center focused on GLP-1 intermediates, peptide chemistry, bio-catalysis and CDMO late-phase RFPs
items.quote: As a part of our next phase, we are investing about Rs.40 crores to build a new R&D center at Hyderabad, focused on emerging technologies including intermediates for GLP -1s and some other chronic therapies, peptide chemistry, bio -catalysis, and a faster turnaround of CDMO -tailored late phase RFPs.

items.statement: Vizag Phase-1 capacity for API and intermediates aligned with customer demand and long-term business visibility
items.quote: The initial capacities under development are aligned with customer demand and long-term business visibility

items.statement: Unit 3 block for contrast media intermediates ready for qualification in Q1 FY27, will de-bottleneck supply chain
items.quote: The facility incorporates robust safety, environmental and automation systems , and is expected to be ready for qualification in Q1 '27. It will play a key role in de-bottlenecking our supply chain and supporting future growth.

items.statement: Hyderabad R&D expansion development work to commence Q3 FY27, strengthening innovation pipeline
items.quote: Development work is expected to commence from Q3 FY27, further strengthening our innovation pipeline and technical capabilities.

items.statement: End molecule showing mid-teens growth month-on-month, new markets opening including Japan and Canada launch gaining traction
items.quote: Month-on-month I would say, it is still showing good mid-level two-digit growth. And new markets are also opening up, like a very big market, that is Japan is opening up.

items.statement: Six high conviction Phase-3 programs in CDMO pipeline including GLP-1 candidates and contrast media NCE, two commercial products may evolve into strategic lateral entries
items.quote: Currently, we are tracking around 20 active RFPs. Of these, six are high conviction phase -3 programs, including a couple of GLP-1 candidates and one contrast media NCE.

items.statement: Q3 gross margin 52% slightly lower than normal trend due to product mix change and one-time inventory write-off
items.quote: Gross margin for Q3 was at 52%, slightly lower than our normal trend , mainly due to change in product mix and one-time write-off of inventory.

items.statement: Nine months gross margin 53% vs 55% last year, 1% impact from inventory write-offs, 1% from product mix swing
items.quote: If you see gross margin on a YTD basis is around 53% compared to 55% last financial year. So, it is only a difference of 2%, out of which roughly 1% impact is on certain inventory write -offs, which are old stock, which was sitting in our inventory.

items.statement: Normalized gross margin range 50-55% depending on product mix
items.quote: It should be between 50% to 55% depending on the product mix.

items.statement: Binding forecasts and confirmed purchase orders exist for FY27 for key molecules, specifics not disclosed
items.quote: No. So there are binding forecast. And there are confirmed purchase orders. But at this point in time, it is very difficult to give specifics around that.

items.statement: Two lateral entry opportunities in advanced conversations, Vizag capacities will cater to these opportunities
items.quote: Last time we spoke about two lateral entries. Very advanced conversations are on both of them. And to some extent, the capacities that are envisaged at Vizag, will be also catering to these opportunities.

items.statement: Contrast media and pharma intermediates verticals highly profitable with gross margins over 50%, some cases 55%
items.quote: But at the end of the day, both contrast media and the pharma intermediates vertical is highly profitable with gross margins over 50%. And in some cases, about 55%.

items.statement: Saccharin experiencing slight price erosion contributing marginally to gross margin reduction
items.quote: And if you look at products like Saccharin, there is a little bit of price erosion. So, that would have actually contributed marginally to reduction in the gross margin.

items.statement: Multi-year supply agreements in place for contrast media, relationships described as very sticky
items.quote: These are very sticky relations. And in most of these cases, these are backed by multi-year supply agreements.

items.statement: Onboarding senior resource in Europe to ramp up customer engagement for CDMO pipeline
items.quote: We are also ramping up customer engagement including onboarding a senior resource in Europe.

items.statement: Top four players hold 75% market share in contrast media, strategy to increase wallet share with these large innovators
items.quote: Yes, those three, four needle movers that we spoke about in terms of the portfolio , will definitely contribute to the increase in the wallet share.

items.statement: New supplier entry for Bempedoic acid requires regulatory pathway, Blue Jet was primary supplier and expects to continue
items.quote: You must also understand that these are advanced intermediates. So, any change will have a regulatory pathway. And we were the primary suppliers in the past. And we believe that we will continue to be the primary suppliers.

items.statement: Goods in transit cut-off similar in Q3 opening and closing, steady-state dispatches expected to be recognized in Q4
items.quote: The closing cut -off for this quarter is also similar to the opening cut -off. So you did not see the impact. But actually our dispatches, if you actually see from a production front, we have a pretty strong production of contrast media this quarter.

items.statement: Company debt-free with Rs.410 crores cash as of December, will use internal accruals for initial CAPEX phase, debt and equity options open
items.quote: Right now, we have Rs.410 crores cash as of December. We will continue to use internal accrual for the initial phase of CAPEX. We have both opportunities open. We could actually tap the debt market or we could also like use the capital market.

items.statement: Evaluating co-investment options with customers for long-term contracts, promoter stake headroom available for capital market raise
items.quote: And as we get into long -term contracts with the customer, we are also evaluating co -investment options. So, for us, being a debt -free company, we have all options available.

items.statement: Iodinated contrast media commercial launch expected FY27 with ramp-up from Q1, value per kg higher than main molecule
items.quote: So in FY27, you will see the commercial launch. And the ramp-up will happen from Q1 itself, is our understanding. The value per Kg, it would be higher than our main molecule because it is a forward integration thing.

items.statement: Artificial sweetener exhibit batches initiating FY27, target capacity 10% of $1 billion market
items.quote: I think in terms of the target capacity that we are targeting is about 10% or $1 billion.

items.statement: Destocking and supply chain realignment may take couple of quarters to fully realign, but end molecule growth remains strong
items.quote: Now, our assessment is that it might take a couple of quarters for this to get completely realigne d. But, if you would see that over the past nine months also, we have done significant volumes as far as our API , PI vertical is concerned.

items.statement: Foreign consultant engagement is recurring strategic expense, not one-off
items.quote: This would be a recurring expense. And it is more strategic in nature.

items.statement: R&D infrastructure and talent pool doubled over last 18 months
items.quote: Over the last 18 months we have doubled our R&D infrastructure and talent pool.

items.statement: Management expects Tritium EBITDA breakeven in Q4 FY27 and consolidated breakeven in later part of FY27
items.quote: I expect, we have publicly stated the management expectation of break-even quarter as Quarter 4 FY27.

items.statement: Critical Power revenue target of close to Rs 1,000 crores for FY27
items.quote: we think there are opportunities to make this Critical Power business into close to a Rs. 1,000 crores business going forward for FY27.

items.statement: Export revenue target of 20% of sales for Critical Power in FY27
items.quote: In FY27, our objective will be to grow exports to about 20% of the sales.

items.statement: Tritium revenue scale-up of 3x from FY26 levels
items.quote: we are looking at 3x revenue scale up from compared to FY26.

items.statement: Critical Power open order position over Rs 1,400 crores executable over 24-30 months
items.quote: The open order position for Critical Power is strong. It's more than Rs. 1,400 crores, which will be delivered over the next 24 to 30 months maximum.

items.statement: Tritium secured $30 million firm PO and forecast from Fortune 50 US customer for CY26 deliveries
items.quote: At Tritium, we bagged almost a $30 million combination of firm purchase order and forecast for high-speed DCEV charges from a large US customer, from one of the Fortune 50 US customers, with deliveries spread over full calendar year '26.

items.statement: Tritium backlog of about $15 million as of January 31st including TRI-FLEX
items.quote: In addition to this last year, we also have about $15 million of backlog as of January 31st.

items.statement: Hyderabad plant to be fully functional by March 2026 with all production lines
items.quote: by the coming quarter end, which is March '26, we will have the plant in Hyderabad fully functioning with all cylinders and doing all production.

items.statement: IPO funds of Rs 400 crores almost fully deployed
items.quote: We had raised about Rs. 400 crores. All of that is almost spent.

items.statement: Rights issue funds exhausted as per plan
items.quote: In terms of the rights issue that came out last year in August, that again has been exhausted almost completely based on the plan

items.statement: Telco CAPEX plan of 120,000+ towers/sites for FY27 driving Critical Power growth
items.quote: For Fiscal '27, the estimated CAPEX plan, which includes both new build and upgrade of old sites, is more than 1,20,000 towers or sites by various Telcos and TowerCos as per our management estimates and discussions with our customers.

items.statement: Standalone gross margin percentage flat at 22.5% YoY but dipped QoQ due to battery mix
items.quote: Our gross margins have increased from last year Q3 '25 of Rs. 33 crores in absolute terms to Rs. 51.61 crores. And the margin percentage in that last year, Quarter 3 '25 was 22.5%, remains pretty much the same. However, if we compare it over the previous quarter, it's dipped a little. And that's primarily because of the product mix that we have had.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin improved to 32.4% for 9M FY26
items.quote: our margins are also higher as compared to the previous year, which stand at 32.4%.

items.statement: Tritium EBITDA losses expected to halve in Q4 FY26 vs current levels
items.quote: what this means on a high level, this will help us cut EBITDA losses in Tritium to almost half compared to the current levels.

items.statement: Battery energy storage breakthrough with Rs 10 crores initial orders in C&I segment
items.quote: this quarter we have been able to make a breakthrough in this category with initial orders of about Rs. 10 crores secured, and we hope to build on this in FY27.

items.statement: Exicom One end-to-end service offering gaining traction with 3 big customers
items.quote: We are working on this model with at least three big customers at this point and hope to expand this offering further in Quarter 4 of FY26, the current quarter.

items.statement: BharatNet project represents >50% market share with RVNL, HFCL, NCC, ITI as SIs
items.quote: We continued execution for key system integrators who have won this contract, which includes RVNL, HFCL, NCC, and now we have secured formal from ITI as well. This represents more than 50% market share of our products in this program.

items.statement: EV charger customer base diversified across portable, 2W, truck OEMs and CPOs
items.quote: We have added new customers across our portable charger, 3.3-kilowatt portable charger, across multiple new CPOs. We also started DC charger for a two-wheeler OEM and bagged business from some electric truck OEMs.

items.statement: Critical Power export revenue 10% of sales in Q3, targeting 20% in FY27
items.quote: Our Q3 export revenue was at 10% of sales. In FY27, our objective will be to grow exports to about 20% of the sales.

items.statement: EV charger revenue geography: 59-60% India, 11% US, 20% UK/Europe, 10% ANZ
items.quote: The centre of revenue still being India at about almost 59%-60% of our revenue comes from India, but because of Tritium, 11% comes from US, 20% comes from UK and Europe, and about 10% comes from Australia and New Zealand.

items.statement: $10 million equity capital secured from UK PE for Tritium at holding company level
items.quote: We secured $10 million in equity capital from a UK-based PE, which we are drawing on as we speak, as well as there are progressive discussions ongoing with multiple other players for minority stake.

items.statement: Finance costs increased due to loans for Tritium acquisition impacting PAT
items.quote: The PAT, marginally down because of the finance cost that is coming that we are taking loans for acquiring Tritium.

items.statement: Critical Power sector average growth 8-10% YoY but cyclical 20-30% in tower addition years
items.quote: On average, this is a sector which is mature, which grows by 8% to 10% year-on-year, but there are some years where this business will grow 3% to 5% and there are some years where it will grow 20% to 30% and we hope FY27 is one of the latter type of years.

items.statement: Tritium turnaround dependent on execution of $30M PO, TRI-FLEX ramp, and customer sentiment recovery
items.quote: Because of the hard work we have put in service, spare parts, maintenance of chargers globally, that has restored some of the lost confidence of Tritium customers. Now we are back in the playing ground.

items.statement: Management expects organic business to demonstrate significant operating leverage in Q4 FY26 with meaningful top-line growth while SG&A growth tapers.
items.quote: we expect to see a meaningful growth in top line in Q4 while the SG&A will not grow at the same pace and hence we should see a significant flow through to the bottom line. So, we remain convinced on that and that is on organic business not counting CV.

items.statement: Air business momentum to continue in Q4 FY26 with at least double-digit GTV growth.
items.quote: we anticipate the same momentum as we go into Q4. And hopefully it should be in the same lines, at least double digits.

items.statement: North America business (including Classic) expected to grow at high double-digits over next 3-4 years.
items.quote: we would definitely endeavor to find high double-digit growth in North America as a whole over the next three or four years.

items.statement: Enterprise GP to Adjusted EBITDA conversion was 23.7% in Q3 FY26 vs 25.3% in Q3 FY25; organic 25.3%, Classic 19.6%.
items.quote: Gross profit to adjusted EBITDA conversion at enterprise levels stood at 23.7% for the quarter, compared to 25.3% in Q3 of FY25. Within this, the organic business delivered a conversion of 25.3%, while Classic Vacation delivered a conversion of 19.6%.

items.statement: Enterprise GTV to Adjusted EBITDA conversion improved to 1.18% in Q3 FY26 from 1.05% in Q3 FY25.
items.quote: On a holistic basis, Enterprise GTV to Adjusted EBITDA conversion improved to 1.18% in Q3 FY26 from 1.05% in Q3 FY25, supported by contribution from Classic Vacation, which delivered a 2.46% GTV to adjusted EBITDA conversion for the quarter.

items.statement: Classic GP to EBITDA conversion at ~20% vs TBO organic ~25%; convergence expected over time but no timeline given.
items.quote: Classic business is converting from GP to EBITDA at about 20%, TBO business is converting at about 25%. And this convergence, we do expect that to happen, I cannot give you a timeline right now, it is very early days.

items.statement: Variable costs below GP are hosting bandwidth and payment gateway charges; employee and business support costs are largely fixed, driving operating leverage.
items.quote: primarily the variable nature of the expense is hosting bandwidth cost and the payment gateway charges. So, that expense would primarily grow in line with the growth in the revenue of the GP or the GTV numbers. But the other cost, which is the employee benefit cost and the business support service and the others, those would primarily be looked at fixed nature of cost.

items.statement: Air business recovered strongly with 16% YoY organic GTV growth in Q3 despite carrier disruption in December.
items.quote: we also had this disruption in December with one of the carriers, which all of us know about, yet we kind of pulled through with a good growth.

items.statement: Booking-to-check-in window has shrunk but appears stable now.
items.quote: I do not think there is a major deviation. It has shrunk but I do not think it is shrinking further. It seems to be stable at this point in time.

items.statement: No incremental capex for Classic platform migration; only minor in-house IT capex.
items.quote: is no incremental Capex for it. Ankush Nijhawan: There will be some in-house Capex for the IT work, but that is not a substantial amount

items.statement: No pricing action anticipated; blended take rates expected to remain range-bound.
items.quote: We would expect the numbers to remain range bound, Karan, because we are not actually anticipating any pricing action on our end. And we are also not expecting the saliency of the business to change dramatically over the next few quarters.

items.statement: Air GP per booking maintained at 1.1-1.2%; management prefers consistent GP over chasing volume via lower take rates.
items.quote: our intent is to continue our 1.1, 1.2 as a GP on the airline business. And if the growth has to come, Prateek, that is a matter of discounting. So, if we drop it to a 0.8, we will start winning GTV. So, that is our intent. So, I think this is a true growth we have demonstrated in Q3 maintaining our GP as well.

items.statement: Classic Vacations sourcing is ~85% direct vs TBO core ~40% direct.
items.quote: CV has a significantly higher contribution on direct sourcing. I do not remember the exact number but maybe it is in the range of about 80%, 85%. CV's sourcing is 85% direct. TBO core is about 40% direct.

items.statement: Enterprise to retail GTV mix for TBO organic hotels is ~50:50; Classic is 100% retail.
items.quote: Enterprise to retail GTV for the TBO organic hotel business is around 50:50. Classic is all actually retail.

items.statement: Monthly transacting buyers: TBO organic ~14,880; Classic ~2,500-3,000 quarterly (annual ~10,000).
items.quote: 10,000 is an annual number for classic. So, the quarterly number for Classic would be in range of around 2,500, 3,000 only.

items.statement: No major customer concentration in Classic; it is a pure retail business with no large enterprise clients.
items.quote: I do not think on the whole, there is any major concentration of business with specific customers, especially Classic is a pure retail business, right? There is no large enterprise business over there.

items.statement: Competitive landscape unchanged; status quo across geographies.
items.quote: I do not think there is any material change in the competitive landscape in the last few quarters, Prateek. You know, things remain competitive as they were before. I would not say that anything has become more competitive or anything has become less competitive at this point in time. Pretty much status quo.

items.statement: Hedging policy: hedge 70-75% of net payable/receivable difference per currency; started hedging international business after Q4 FY25.
items.quote: We try to hedge the difference amount in the range of around let us say 70% to 75% we try to hedge that amount in any particular market.

items.statement: Forex line includes hedging costs, MTM on hedges, unhedged gains/losses, and revaluation of USD loan to Dubai entity for CV acquisition.
items.quote: that line would have all the hedging cost as well as MTM impact of the hedges as well as if there are any unhedged positions, if there is any gain or loss that is also included and plus, since we had given a foreign currency loan from TBO Tek- the holding company to Tek Travels DMCC Dubai entity for the CV acquisition any benefit or cost pertaining to the devaluation of those loans also get captur

items.statement: Classic Vacations is a highly negative working capital business due to long booking-to-check-in window; supports consolidated negative working capital.
items.quote: Classic Vacations business because the window between the booking and checking travel is too large. So, it is a highly negative working capital business and it would obviously support in generating more negative working capital business at an enterprise level.

items.statement: Hotel business negative working capital (collect at booking, pay near check-in); Air business working capital neutral.
items.quote: For hotels basically, even in organic business, it is a negative working capital cycle business because generally we would be paying near to time check-in or after check-in to hotels or suppliers but we generally would be collecting starting from at the time of booking till at the time of check-in. So, it is a negative working capital business. Air is I would say, almost a working capital neutral

items.statement: Depreciation and finance costs include full quarter impact of CV acquisition loan and PPA amortization; steady state expected.
items.quote: this quarter includes the debt and amortization cost for the PPA provisional that we have done. While the PPA study is currently provisional, but we do not anticipate major changes in the same. So, the debt cost is already taken into account, the amortization cost is taken into account.

items.statement: Organic hotel take rate 10.5%; blended enterprise take rate 8.08% (organic 6.04%, Classic 24.94% including 12.4% pass-through commission).
items.quote: Revenue from operations of Rs. 784 Cr for the quarter translates into an enterprise take rate of 8.08%. The organic business delivered a take rate of 6.04%, while Classic Vacations reported a headline take rate of 24.94%. It is important to note that Classic Vacation's take rate includes a 12.4% commission component that is passed to the travel advisors.

items.statement: GP as % of GTV preferred over revenue take rate due to pass-through commissions; Enterprise GP to Adjusted EBITDA conversion 23.7%.
items.quote: we believe gross profit as a percentage of GTV is a more analytically robust measure of value capture. Gross profit strips out pass-through commissions and better reflects the net economic value retained by the platform.

items.statement: Ramadan straddles Feb-Mar in Q4 FY26 vs fully in Mar last year; monthly deviation but no material quarterly impact expected.
items.quote: Ramadan fell pretty much in the same quarter last year as well. So, while there will be a monthly deviation in numbers because Ramadan is straddling February and March this time. Last year, it was completely in March. But from a full quarter perspective, there will not be a very material change.

items.statement: Classic revenue recognition on check-in basis (vs TBO booking basis) creates blended metric noise; accounting alignment not possible due to multi-product itineraries and long booking windows.
items.quote: We tried that but it is simply not possible. The main reason being that CVs business books much in advance and then because of the nature of that business. So, it is luxury and complex. So, unlike the TBO business where each booking is essentially one hotel or one flight, bulk of what CV books is multi-hotel, multi-product itineraries.

items.statement: Total headcount (including Classic, consultants, retainers) north of 2,600 as of Dec-end.
items.quote: we do share our overall headcount including Classic, including all our consultants and retainers that we have is north of 2600+ as of December end.

items.statement: Management declined to provide FY27 revenue guidance, stating budgeting is in progress and guidance will be given by Q1.
items.quote: At this point in time, we will not be able to give you a number as to what we are projecting because we are in the process of budgeting and we will probably give it to you by Q1.

items.statement: Management reaffirmed the Rs 1,000 crore revenue target within 1,000 working days, noting no change in intention despite recent headwinds.
items.quote: we had always mentioned th at it would be 1,000 working days, so that’s technically what it was anyway. Nevertheless, I think we are definitely keyed into getting towards that number. There is no change

items.statement: Capex for 9MFY26 was Rs 62-63 crores; cash reserves remained flat YoY. Next year's capex plan will be shared by end of Q1.
items.quote: We have invested o ver Rs. 62 crores in expansion in the first three quarters, yet our cash reserves remain at the same level as last year, reflecting prudent financial management

items.statement: Nine new stores opened in 9MFY26 (7 COCO, 2 FOFO); six more stores (5 COCO, 1 FOFO) expected by early Q1 FY27, taking total to 12 COCO and 3 FOFO.
items.quote: we have already opene d nine and six are pending. We are confident of doing between now and Q1, within early Q1 we will do it

items.statement: Kitchen & cabinetry (KCD) share of order book rose from 12% in Dec 2024 to 37% in Dec 2025, indicating a shift to full-home solutions.
items.quote: Last year, December, we had an order book of roughly about 12% of our total order book coming from kitchen and cabinetry. This year on December 31, it has gone up by 20%, so almost 30%.

items.statement: Order book remains robust; management confident integration will strengthen execution capability towards FY2027.
items.quote: Order book remains robust and we are confident this integration will stren gthen execution capability as we move towards FY 2027

items.statement: 9MFY26 EBITDA margin stable at 18.8% vs 18.9% YoY; Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin fell to 11.9% from 18.7% due to new labor laws, operational deleverage and expansion costs.
items.quote: After considering the impact of new labor laws, EBITDA margins moderated at 11.9% in Q3 FY 2026 compared to 18.7% in Q3 FY 2025, representing a contraction of 680 basis points.

items.statement: Gross profit grew 6.2% YoY in 9MFY26 on improved product mix and operational efficiencies.
items.quote: Encouragingly, gross profits grew by 6.2% compared to t he corresponding period last year, supported by an improved product mix and continued operational efficiencies

items.statement: Demand traction improved meaningfully from January 2026; premium housing deliveries expected to accelerate from 2026, unlocking significant furniture demand.
items.quote: traction has improved meaningfully from January onwards. Data across the six metros where we are present now shows that the prem ium housing sales over the past three, four years have been at historic

items.statement: RERA data indicates ~109,000 premium homes (>Rs 1.5 cr) for delivery in 2026, ~150,000 in 2027, ~163,000 in 2028 across six metros.
items.quote: From our collection of data, we will have close to 109,000 homes coming into play above the value of Rs. 1.5 crores in 2026. That's going to almost 150,000 in 2027 and 163,000 in 2028.

items.statement: Pivot from leather sofas to full-home luxury provider; KCD order book share jumped from 12% to 37% YoY, driving 6-7x higher average ticket size.
items.quote: our KCD in full home order book is at 37% versus 12% and we ha ve grown by 20%. So thereby, we are very clear that once we get into the house with kit chen and cabinetry, the loose furniture also will start

items.statement: Obtained BIS certification for products under QCO this month; expect ~90% of SKUs certified by end of Q4 FY26. QCO will restrict non-certified importers, benefiting organized players.
items.quote: We obtained our BIS certification this month on products covered under QCO, among the early movers in the furniture segment. items.statement: Product funnel reimagination underway; longest gestation but largest impact; design, material, comfort authority focus

items.statement: Marketing spend elevated double-digit for second consecutive quarter; focused on product campaigns (festive, Victoria Ballerina, Power Easy Slide)

items.statement: Product funnel reimagination has longest gestation; younger consumer relevance needs improvement; inventory reduction sustainable but demand softness risk acknowledged

items.statement: TAN plant completion scheduled for April 30, 2026

items.statement: IMACID P2O5 capacity increase from 5 to 7 lakh metric tons by December 2026
items.quote: The increase in P2O5 production capacity from 5 lakh metric tons to 7 lakh metric tons is expected to be implemented by December 2026.

items.statement: 12 new CPC products and 1 specialty nutrient product lined up for launch in FY27
items.quote: Looking ahead, our pipeline remains healthy, with 12 new CPC products and one new speciality nutrient product lined up for launch in FY '27, supporting our growth ambitions.

items.statement: Biologicals volumes up 31% and revenue up 58% YoY in 9M FY26; Uttam Pranaam up 250% YoY

items.statement: Rabi sowing increased 2.8% YoY to 652.3 lakh hectares as of January 2026

items.statement: 9M FY26 standalone EBITDA INR 2,424 crores, up 4% YoY, margin 13.46%

items.statement: Urea segment EBIT margin stable at 17.28% in Q3 FY26

items.quote: EBIT margins improved modestly to around 1.4%, supported by better operating leverage.

items.quote: EBIT margins remained healthy at around 22.8%.

items.statement: Adequate P&K fertilizer volumes sourced for Kharif season
items.quote: Further, we have sourced adequate volumes of P&K fertilizer, ensuring preparedness for the Kharif season.

items.statement: Subsidy receipts INR 3,880 crores in Q3 FY26 vs INR 3,349 crores YoY; 9M FY26 INR 10,228 crores

items.quote: As of 31st December' 25, total receivables stood at around INR 2,346 crores, comprising market debtors of INR 367 crores and subsidy receivables of INR 1,979 crores.

items.quote: About INR 800 crores. About INR 800 crore as of today.

items.quote: No, as far as we understand, we have raked up this issue with the government. We have met the requisite personnel, but they said that we have to start the exercise. They are busy with other things, on other matters so far.

items.statement: Gas cost for quarter $14.6 per MMBtu on NCV basis

items.statement: Gadepan-II maintenance shutdown of 30-35 days from February 20, 2026

items.statement: Urea sales volumes flat at 9.83 lakh metric tons in Q3 FY26 vs 9.88 lakh metric tons YoY
items.quote: Urea sales volumes were largely flat at 9.83 lakh metric tons in the quarter, compared to 9.88 lakh metric tons in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Complex fertilizer sales volume rose to 2.94 lakh metric tons in Q3 FY26 from 2.13 lakh metric tons YoY
items.quote: Sales volume also rose to 2.94 lakh metric tons, compared to 2.13 lakh metric tons last year, reflecting strong seasonal demand.

items.statement: CPC, Specialty Nutrients and Seed segment revenue up 33% YoY to INR 340 crores in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Revenues increased 33% year -on-year to about INR 340 crores in the quarter, representing strong growth driven by portfolio expansion and improved penetration.

But I think there has been a re -engagement and a positive re -engagement.

items.statement: Refinery white premiums under pressure due to global surplus; lower spread environment expected to continue for next 2 quarters

So, we expect this tightness or the lower white premium environment to continue at least for the next 2 quarters going forward.

items.statement: Refinery energy efficiency projects implemented end of last year sustaining lower cost of $41/MT going forward
items.quote: The costs have come down during the current year mainly on account of energy efficiency projects that are implemented over end of last year giving results. So, we expect we should be able to sustain these cost levels going forward.

items.quote: On the grain route, we have only 1 facility in Andhra, roughly about 120 KLPD, the balance 400-KLPDs in the molasses route.

items.quote: We will really need to look towards the policymakers for some respite on upward revision of MSP and perhaps ethanol price as well. We haven't really seen any positive changes from that front.

items.quote: Recoveries, as of 31st December, it is about 11.19%. So going forward, it may slightly increase.

items.quote: I only say that at least for a short period, we should enjoy that, because I have a coverage of coking coal for 3, 4 months.

items.statement: Embedded value grew 16% YoY to INR 28,110 crore; annualized operating RoEV 16.9% in 9M FY26.

items.statement: Solvency ratio healthy at 201% as of Dec 31, 2025.

items.quote: This industry segment saw a growth of 8.6 % while Trident Hotels grew at 12.5%. So, we saw healthy growth in this segment versus the industry, both for Q3 and YTD. A very healthy growth of RGI of 173 versus 167.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue Rs 910 crore, up 9% YoY; EBITDA up 6%; PAT down due to Rs 30 crore wage code impact
items.quote: We ended the quarter with revenue of 910 crores with a growth of 9% over same quarter last year. EBITDA grew at 6%, it was lower than the revenue growth due to change in the business mix mainly on account of OFS growth which grew much more faster.

items.statement: Standalone revenue up 12% YoY; EBITDA up 8%; PAT impacted by Rs 29 crore wage code
items.quote: On standalone basis revenue growth was higher. The growth was in the range of 12% while the EBITDA grew at 8% over last year. EBITDA growth was lower than the revenue on account of change in the busin ess mix . A nd again , on the standalone basis we got impacted by 29 Crore due to change in the quarter

items.statement: YTD consolidated revenue up 7%, EBITDA up 4%, PAT down 20% due to Rs 109 crore Mashobra loss and Rs 30 crore wage code
items.quote: On a 9 months YTD consolidated performance, growth is at 7% while the EBITDA grew at 4%. Bigger impact on PAT because of two exceptional items. One exceptional item was the loss of case in Mashobra with an impact of 109 crores in Q1 and additional impact of 30 crores in Q3 because of the wage code.

items.statement: Development pipeline of 30 hotels with ~2,450 keys to be added over next 3-4 years
items.quote: As of the current quarter, we have a healthy pipeline of 30 hotels with approx. 2450 keys which we are going to add in next three to four years' time.

items.statement: Added 4 new management contracts in Q3: Oberoi Kabini, Oberoi Hampi, Oberoi Coorg, and 1 hotel in Cairo
items.quote: In the current quarter we have signed new management contracts. We have added Oberoi Kabini, Oberoi Hampi as well as Oberoi Coorg and 1 hotel in Cairo. Overall, 4 hotels being added in this quarter, all of them are managed.

items.statement: Oberoi Rajgarh Palace opened and in ramp-up stage with positive initial response
items.quote: The hotel currently is in the ramp-up stage and the initial response is very positive.

items.statement: Trident Hebbal keys increased from 250 to 300 due to potential demand
items.quote: We believe that there is potential demand for the increase in the number of keys, and that's why we've done that.

items.statement: Renovation plans: 4 floors at Trident Nariman Point and 4 floors at Oberoi Mumbai in coming financial year
items.quote: And the intent is to do another four floors in the coming financial year. And we'll obviously do that in the slower months. But again, I want to point out that you have to take out additional rooms so that guests don't get disturbed. What we've seen at Trident, Nariman Point, is on the renovated rooms, we get a high rate and we get RevPAR based on each category of room. So, signs are encouraging.

items.statement: Trident Jaipur and Oberoi Grand closed for renovation; Trident Cochin leased not renovated
items.quote: So, Jaipur is closed for renovation. That also has an impact. Grand is closed for renovation. Cochin is not closed for renovation, that has been leased. The two hotels which are closed for renovation is Grand and Jaipur.

items.statement: OFS revenue Rs 135 crore in Q3, up 25-30% YoY; margins lower than lounge business (50%+ margins)
items.quote: So, for the OFS business, for Q3 the revenue was 135 crores, which saw an increase of 25 to 30% versus last year.

items.statement: Like-for-like Q3 revenue growth 14% excluding Grand, OAS Mumbai, Wildflower Hall impacts
items.quote: In terms of your other point, which is on a Y-o-Y basis, taking all the impacts which we had on account of The Oberoi Grand, of course for The Oberoi Grand there is hardly any impact, OAS, Mumbai and the other things, including the Wildflower Hall, we have grown 14% in Q3, as against the 9% growth, what you saw earlier.

items.statement: Employee expenses up 11% YoY due to new hotel additions (Rajgarh, Wildflower Hall) increasing headcount
items.quote: Yes, the employee expenses growth will be on account of the new hotel additions we have done. This includes The Oberoi Rajgarh, as well as W ildflower Hall, which we are operating . So, due to headcount increase and employment costs on account of new hotels added in our portfolio the costs have been increased

items.statement: February traditionally very strong month for hospitality; current February looking strong
items.quote: February is a time, and all indications are that February will be a very strong month for us, as I would imagine it would be for the industry.

items.statement: Spillover demand from Delhi AI Summit to Gurgaon hotels (Oberoi and Trident)
items.quote: There has been a spillover to Gurgaon and I know that has happened both at Oberoi and at Trident for us, perhaps for others as well.

items.statement: Bhubaneswar expansion plans pending board approval and stock exchange disclosure
items.quote: Once it is presented to the board and approved by the board and information is shared with the stock exchange, of course, we'll make that available on an investor call as well.

items.statement: Naila Fort launched as first luxury residence (4 bedrooms, Rs 12 lakh whole property); owned by OHPL; exploring second opportunity
items.quote: This is, actually, it's not a hotel. It's a luxury residence. It's four bedrooms and you can, and although it's four bedrooms, it's a very large space. There are multiple areas, large gardens, a pool, four bedrooms, multiple living rooms, multiple dining rooms, a gym, etc. You have to take the whole of Naila Fort. It's not rented out individually. And the price for that is 12 lakhs. And this is, t

items.statement: Foreign vs domestic guest mix not disclosed; varies significantly by location (Delhi/Gurgaon higher international)
items.quote: Yeah, we, we don't disclose the mix between our Indian guests and our international guests, both in terms of contribution to occupancy and revenue.

items.statement: Surplus funds increased from operational profits and Rs 115 crore Mashobra settlement; supports organic and inorganic expansion
items.quote: Also, we got one time cash increase, from Mashobra settlement which was in the range of INR 115 crores adding to our cash position. We continue to have good cash reserves to support our future expansions, both organic as well as inorganic.

items.statement: Expects Q4 FY26 to be better than Q3 FY26 and Q1 FY27 to be better still for Advanced Intermediates segment
items.quote: I definitely expect Q4 FY26 to be better than Q3 FY26. I also want to be cautiously optimistic on this front because whatever happens with regards to India and the Western countries that are our traditional markets, it doesn't change the fact that there is a significant Chinese overcapacity.

items.statement: Polycarbonate project targeted for commissioning by December 2027
items.quote: December 2027 is the timeline we had discussed for being onstream. So we are roughly on track.

items.statement: MIBK/MIBC project targeted for commissioning within Q4 FY26
items.quote: The MIBK/ MIBC project is progressing well and is targeted for commissioning within this quarter.

items.statement: FY27 capex estimated at INR 2,500 crore; FY26 capex approximately INR 1,200-1,300 crore including INR 100 crore remaining spend
items.quote: INR 2,500 crore is for FY27, not FY26. FY26 is already underway, that would involve spending of around INR 100 crore, bringing the total to approximately INR 1,200–1,300 crore.

items.statement: Nitric acid, nitration and hydrogenation plants expected to run at 95-105% utilization from Q4 FY26; fluorination, chlorination, photochemical assets to pick up in Q1 FY27; high-pressure alkylation asset commissioning June-July 2026 with 2-
items.quote: on the nitric acid invest ment, on the nitration and on the hydrogenation, we are expecting to run at 100% or close enough to 100% utilization from this quarter onwards. They may be between 95% to 100%, 105

items.statement: Pipeline of ~15 new products at various stages from R&D to customer validation; key applications in mining chemicals, flame retardants, personal care, flavors & fragrances, polymer applications
items.quote: At the moment, we have a pipeline of about 15 products at various stages between R&D, piloting and awaiting customer feedback with regards to samples.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 11% from 10% in Q3 FY25; Phenolics EBIT up 20% YoY; Advanced Intermediates EBIT at INR 15 crore impacted by pricing pressure
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 219 crore, registering a 16% improvement compared with Q3 FY25. This growth highlights the benefits of operating leverage, process optimization initiatives and sustained cost discipline. The EBITDA margin improved to 11% compared to 10% in the corresponding period quarter last year.

items.statement: Advanced Intermediates margin pressure largely due to pricing (Chinese oversupply) not volume; self-inflicted compression from aggressive market placement before upstream integration
items.quote: I would say that at the very moment, a substantial amount of this is because of pricing, not so much because of volume. There is some volume impact because of key agrochemical intermediates. But there is more than that, I would say, a pricing impact because of the oversupply situation from China.

items.statement: U.S. removed anti-dumping duty on Deepak's sodium nitrite exports; total tariff overhang reduced from ~105% to significantly lower (countervailing duty ~3-5% + 18% reciprocal duty vs previous 50%)
items.quote: And over the last 8 months, there has been a tariff overhang between antidumping duty, tariffs and other things in excess of about 105%. So now, of course, the total tariff overhang would b e substantially less than

items.statement: Sourcing 60-70% of energy mix from hybrid renewable sources to improve energy efficiency and embed green chemistry principles
items.quote: We are accelerating our transition towards green energy by sourcing 60% to 70% of our energy mix from hybrid renewable sources, improving energy efficiency and embedding green chemistry principles across operations.

items.statement: Domestic phenol demand robust; agrochemicals outlook marginally improving but rocky; dyes & pigments, mining chemicals, explosives, polymer, food, pharma, personal care expected to improve from trade agreements
items.quote: So, agrochemicals continues to be a space where there is a marginal improvement in the outlook, but it is not a consistent improvement. It is still a little bit rocky. And places where we expect to see an uptick because of these trade agreements are places su ch as dyes and pigments, mining chemicals, explosives, polymer applications, food applications, pharmaceuticals, personal care, those are pl

items.statement: India's polycarbonate resin imports surged from ~200,000 to >300,000 tonnes/year; domestic consumption growth supports integrated project viability
items.quote: Right now, India has already been importing in excess of 300,000 tonnes. So just within a year, our estimates of what India's domestic requirement of polycarbonate resins has changed by a factor of 50%.

items.statement: India-EU FTA ratification expected in 6-8 months; U.S.-India bilateral trade agreement and EU FTA seen as positive tailwinds for chemical industry; Deepak may procure cyanuric chloride from Europe under FTA
items.quote: So what is there is a proposed FTA and it will take whatever period of time it takes six to eight months, is what we believe, in terms of full ratification by all the 20-something member countries of the EU.

items.statement: U.S. removed anti-dumping duty specifically for Deepak Nitrite on sodium nitrite exports (not for all Indian manufacturers)
items.quote: It's also heartening to just share that the removal of the duty, by the way, is specific for Deepak Nitrite. It is not a removal of duty for Indian manufacturers. It's only for Deepak.

items.statement: Working capital efficiency improved through tighter inventory planning, supply chain optimization and improved receivables discipline; better cash flow management and enhanced balance sheet quality
items.quote: Working capital efficiency remained a strategic priority and through tighter inventory planning, supply chain optimization and improved receivables discipline, we achieved better cash flow management and enhanced balance sheet quality.

items.statement: Strategic focus on fluorination, nitration, diazotization, amination segments for product innovation and geographical expansion; integrated ammonia-nitration-to-amines value chain completed
items.quote: To navigate current near-term headwinds, the Group is strategically prioritizing product innovation and geographical expansion with a specific focus on our fluorination, nitration, diazotization and amination segments.

items.statement: Chinese oversupply affects ~30-40% of products; 60-70% not directly affected; Chinese government implementing deflation control measures; Far East Asian phenol capacities shutting down (Singapore)
items.quote: I don't anticipate that it affects every single one of our products, maybe many of our products, 60%, 70% of our products are not as directly affected by Chinese oversupply. But when this oversupply is there, it does affect our customers.

items.statement: Consolidated ROCE at 15% for Q3 FY26, reinforcing consistent value creation across business cycles
items.quote: Strong capital efficiency continues to underpin our performance with consolidated ROCE at 15%, reinforcing our ability to consistently create value across business cycles.

items.statement: Nitric acid plant commissioned mid-December 2025; Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 first periods with ~100% self-consumption; earlier spot purchases at higher rates compressed Q3 margins
items.quote: We commissioned the nitric acid plant in the middle of December 2025. This quarter and next quarter will be the first period where we would have pretty much 100% consumption of nitric acid.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 beer volumes declined 24% YoY due to colder-than-expected weather in key markets and slow recovery in Karnataka.
items.quote: Our company posted subdued numbers in Q3 FY26 on account of more -than-expected cold weather conditions in our key markets like Madhya Pradesh, Delhi, which led a volume decline in the beer volumes.

items.statement: Management targets total income of INR 1,500 crores for FY26, implying ~INR 450 crores in Q4.
items.quote: Looking at the scenario right now, I think we would reach close to about INR 1,500 crores by the end of this financial year.

items.statement: Q4 net sales aspiration is INR 450 crores (excluding excise duty).
items.quote: Yes, sir, that's our aspiration.

items.statement: UP greenfield Phase 1 (INR 370 crores) on track for June 2026 completion; financial closure achieved for both phases.
items.quote: Phase 1 investment is about INR 370 crores. Phase 2 is INR 200 crores. Phase 2 will happen approximately one year after Phase 1.

items.statement: UP Phase 1 adds 1 crore cases brewery capacity; expected 80-85% utilisation yielding INR 650-700 crores top line.
items.quote: Phase 1 entails establishment of a brewery with a capacity of one crore cases. And we expect that on an 80% to 85% capacity utilization, that capacity can give us close to about INR 650 crores to INR 700 crores of top line.

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA margin 9.1% vs 12.9% 9M; gross margin hit by lower Hunter share (28% to 19%) and barley (+5-6%), glass (+3-4%) cost increases.
items.quote: I think, sir, the gross margin was impacted mainly by the share of Hunter going down in the overall sales mix. So if you look at Q2, it was about close to 28% of our total beer sales, and it has gone down to about 19%.

items.statement: No price hike planned for Q4; focus on volume growth; excise policy allows only annual price revisions.
items.quote: No, there is no plan to take any price increase. If there is an opportunity that is presenting to us, then we'll look at it. At this point in time, we are not looking at it in Q4.

items.statement: Beer realisation rose to INR 543/case (mix shift); IMFL realisation fell to INR 988/case; IMFL volumes up 46% YoY to 5 lakh cases.
items.quote: Beer realization for Q3 FY26 was INR 543 per case compared to INR 516 in Q3 FY25, driven by a shift in product mix. For IMFL, realization stood at INR 988 per case, down from INR 1,068 in Q3 FY25, reflecting pricing pressures across the category.

items.statement: Bhopal plant licence suspended; petition heard in MP High Court, order reserved, decision expected within days.
items.quote: We have made the required submissions in the MP High Court, and we expect a judgment on the issue in the next 2 to 3 days.

items.statement: Higher finance costs and depreciation from increased working capital utilisation and capex for capacity expansion.
items.quote: Reduction in profit before tax and profit after tax is primarily attributable to higher finance costs and increased depreciation during the period, consequent to higher working capital utilization and capital expenditure undertaken for capacity expansion and strategic investments.

items.statement: UP project fully funded; debt tied up with banks; no equity raise needed for Phase 1.
items.quote: Sir, that already has been funded.

items.statement: Promoters aim to raise stake to 51% in short-to-medium term (2-3 years) via preferential issues or open market purchases.
items.quote: I think the time frame for increasing it to 51% is short to medium term, maybe in the next 2 to 3 years. And the increase is going to come through preferential issues as and when the capital is required in the company or from open market purchases.

items.statement: Andhra Pradesh tender expected to open soon; brands already quoted; supply possible in Q4 if tender finalised quickly.
items.quote: We received a communication from the Andhra government through APBCL , on 23rd of January that they are opening the tender and deciding on it by 10th of February. So 10th of February, they have not opened it. We got the latest update that they are likely to open it this weekend.

items.statement: Management sees EU/US trade deals as opportunity, especially for IMFL (10-15% of revenue); beer less affected due to price/logistics barriers.
items.quote: Maybe overall, if you look at the European markets and American markets, and the FTA thing will probably help the IMFL a little more than beer because beer, it all depends on price and depends on logistics.

items.statement: Q3 plant utilisation: Bhopal 56%, Woodpecker 42%, Odisha 36%; no further expansion planned at existing plants.
items.quote: Sir, Q3, we operated the Bhopal plant at 56%, Woodpecker at 42% and Odisha plant at about 36%.

items.statement: Barley prices up 5-6%, glass bottles up 3-4% QoQ; ~3 months glass inventory held ahead of peak season.
items.quote: Plus, there were some cost pressures on quarter-to-quarter where the prices of barley have risen in the range of 5% to 6%. Glass bottles have risen by about 3% to 4%.

items.statement: 9M FY26: Beer volume 154.6 lakh cases (-13% YoY), IMFL volume 13.1 lakh cases (+55% YoY), total income INR 1,054 crores, EBITDA INR 135 crores (12.9% margin).
items.quote: For the nine months of FY26, our IMFL portfolio grew by 55%, reaching a total of 13.1 lakh cases. Our beer volume reached 154.6 lakh cases, down 13% from the same period last year. For the first nine months of FY26, our total income reached INR 1,054 crores with an EBITDA of INR 135 crores and a margin of 12.9%.

items.statement: Bhopal plant closure could impact Q4 if prolonged; peak season starts March; resolution expected within days.
items.quote: I mean, if it goes on for a long time, then obviously, but we are trying to ensure that it should have minimal impact as of now.

items.statement: Management guides for double-digit revenue and PAT growth for full year FY26 and double-digit PAT growth north of 20% for FY27
items.quote: Overall, again, we expect healthy double-digit growth in revenue and PBT for the full year.

items.statement: Long-term sustainable PAT margin target of 7% within next 2 to 3 years
items.quote: Our long-term sustainable PAT margin is at 7% levels and we're quite confident we'll achieve that in the next, within the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Finance cost guidance maintained at 4% of net revenue (1% long-term loans, 3% working capital)
items.quote: Finance cost stands at 3.56% of our net revenue, which is better than our guidance of 4%. Our guidance break-even breakup still remains the same: 1% on long -term loans and 3% o n our working capital

items.statement: Consolidated tax rate guided at approximately 25.5%
items.quote: We continue to guide to a consolidated tax rate of approximately 25.5%.

items.statement: All five core verticals (PEB India, PEB US, Boilers, Hydraulics, Engineering Services) firing and expected to grow in revenue and profitability
items.quote: five core growth drivers that we had mentioned, which includes our boilers and process equipment, hydraulics, pre-engineered buildings India, pre-engineered buildings US, and engineering services are all firing and we expect growth in each and every one of those of those business units in revenue and profitability

items.statement: PEB India order backlog at INR810 crores; US combined Ascent Buildings and Ascent Structural order book at $60.6 million ($52M buildings + $10M Telco)
items.quote: The order book stands at INR810 crores for the PEB India. PEB US, the combined Ascent buildings and Ascent structural order book is now at 60.6 million.

items.statement: Boilers division order backlog increased to INR123 crores with strong export orders from Australia, Sri Lanka, Saipem, Browns Industry
items.quote: The boilers division saw a very strong increase in our order backlog to INR123 crores this quarter. We received a lot of strong export orders from Australia and Sri Lanka, Saipem, and Browns industry.

items.statement: Hydraulics order backlog more than doubled; US tariff reduction from 50% to 18% to accelerate growth
items.quote: Hydraulics, our order backlog is more than double. The reduction in tariffs for the US will now help this business grow even quicker.

items.statement: Q3 PAT margin at 3.56%; excluding one-time costs would have been 4%; revenue and profit trajectory shifting to higher-margin businesses
items.quote: Our Q3 PAT margins were at 3.56%. After including the one-time events, we would have been at 4%. So our revenue and profit trajectory continues to shift towards higher-margin businesses, and this positive trajectory will continue to grow our PAT at double-digit rates.

items.statement: ROCE at 21.3% and ROE at 12.1%; confident of sustaining returns as performance scales
items.quote: Capital efficiency, our ROCE stands at 21.3%, and return on equity is at 12.1%. We're quite confident of achieving these returns as performance continues to scale through the year.

items.statement: Depreciation increased by INR4.25 crores (INR1.33 cr standalone from capex and repair/maintenance capitalization; INR2.92 cr subsidiary from Telco acquisition and robotic machines at US operations)
items.quote: Depreciation, amortization has increased by INR4.25 crores. At a consolidated level, INR1.33 crores comes from standalone, which is on account of primarily capex and other repair and maintenance capitalization that we had, and INR2.92 crores comes from subsidiary on account of Telco acquisition and robotic machines that we have installed at our US operations.

items.statement: PEB India capacity utilization improved, manpower challenges eased, inventory reduced by ~4,000 tons; Engineering services capacity locked but quickly expanding
items.quote: Our PEB division's capacity utilization has improved, manpower challenges have eased, and inventory also has reduced by about 4,000 tons.

items.statement: Steel price increases do not impact PEB margins due to quarterly pricing with JSW (protected for next quarter rate) and long-term contracts with price escalation clauses
items.quote: The price increase directly do not impact us in any way. There are short-term contracts and there are long-term contracts. We have the quarterly pricing with JSW wherein we are protected for the next quarter rate and what we have the indication from them. And in the long-term contracts, we are -- the increase margin is, is there as part of the contract.

items.statement: Working capital at 76 days due to timing-related revenue impacts; expect improvement in Q4 and next quarters with stronger PEB projections
items.quote: Working capital at 76 days reflecting timing-related impacts from revenue perhaps not coming in in some of the segments. With stronger Q4 projections, especially in PEB and other key segments, we expect good improvement on this number in this quarter and the next quarter, Q4 and the next quarters.

items.statement: Telco acquisition (asset purchase) completed late September/early October; order backlog transfer delayed but now contributing strongly in Q4; monthly order booking run rate of ~$2M (INR18-20 crores)
items.quote: We are doing about $2 million, about INR18 crores - INR20 crores per month. typically over the medium term, short term to medium term, your revenue and your order booking tend to converge.

items.statement: Ascent Structural acquisition started booking orders; will contribute meaningfully to revenue in Q4 and following quarters
items.quote: Ascent Structural, our acquisition, also has started booking orders and will be contributing very meaningfully to our revenue in Q4 and following quarters.

items.statement: One-time costs of ~INR4 crores from labour code implementation, Chennai High Court union settlement order, and wage agreement revisions; all non-recurring
items.quote: The one-time cost from an account of three things, which comes in salaries and wages. One is on account of labour code compliance implementation. Second, we have received a Chennai High Court order for the union employees settlement, which, for which we need to have made a provision. Third, there are wage agreements that have been finalized with the workers. So all inclusive, close to around INR4

items.statement: PEB India labour issues resolved through building labour quarters, increasing contract and skilled manpower; no longer labour bottlenecked
items.quote: We have now resolved it. We've undertaken many initiatives including building our own labour quarters, including increasing our contract manpower, including increasing our skilled manpower which is sourced from other verticals as well. So now the issue is resolved. I don't, we're not labour bottlenecked anymore

items.statement: Diversified Engineering revenue grew 25.19% YoY to INR520.31 crores driven by Steel BU, Boiler and BIW
items.quote: Within these segments, the diversified engineering revenue has increased from INR415.6 crores to INR520.31 crores, a growth of 25.19%, primarily driven by our strong performance in the steel BU sector.

items.statement: Custom Designed Building Solutions revenue stable at INR440 crores consolidated; US growth of INR42 crores from Telco acquisition offset by lower PEB India sales
items.quote: Custom designed building solutions revenue remains stable at INR441 crores to INR440 crores at a consolidated level. The growth of INR42 crores is in the US business driven by the Telco acquisition. This was offset by lower PEB sales in India due to the challenges that we have.

items.statement: Other income increased by INR9.23 crores including INR2.71 crores forex transaction/translation gains, INR3.72 crores interest income, INR8.4 crores collection of old receivables and creditor write-backs
items.quote: To give you a detailed explanation, INR2.71 crores comes from Forex transaction and translation gains. INR3.72 crores comes from interest income from mutual funds and deposits. INR8.4 crores is from collection of old receivables and write-back of creditors.

items.statement: Revenue recognition timing gaps cause order backlog reconciliation differences; shipped goods not recognized as revenue until customer confirmation received
items.quote: From a revenue recognition point of view, there's a lot of what we follow effectively is when the risk has passed. So we have shipped, it debits our, our order backlog, but it won't show up in revenue because our auditors will not allow us to, to take that revenue in until we have received some measure of confirmation from our customers about goods that are shipped.

items.statement: PEB India monthly revenue run rate improved significantly in January with >INR200 crores order booking in PEB India alone; exact monthly run rate to be provided later
items.quote: In the month of January, for example, we had well over INR200 crores in order booking in PEB itself, in PEB India itself.

items.statement: PEB India order book at INR810 crores; US Ascent buildings order backlog at USD52 million, structural at USD10 million, combined USD62 million
items.quote: The PEB order book stands at INR810 crores. The Ascent company's order backlog stands at -- Ascent buildings specifically 52 and Ascent structural 10 million. So if you're asking what's the order book, that's the answer.

items.statement: Hydraulics order backlog projected to more than double in next few weeks due to US duty change from 15% to 18%
items.quote: I can tell you, however, that the order backlog is projected to more than double in the next few weeks. So that I can tell you...

items.statement: Boiler business order book at INR123 crores, expected to be executed within next six months (blended average of 3-4 months for process boilers, 9 months for power boilers)
items.quote: So the what you see is a blend of both of those sectors, but as a blended average, this INR123 crores is something we expect to be able to revenue out within the next six months.

items.statement: Peak combined India and US PEB/structural capacity at 80% utilization could generate INR200-220 crores per month
items.quote: If you were to combine India and the US both for PEB and structural, at peak capacity let's say 80% I think is fair. I don't think we should go much higher than that. We will absolutely be able to hit a revenue number closer to INR200 crores to

items.statement: PEB India monthly run rate up north of 20% vs 2-3 months ago, growing quickly; order backlogs remain strong
items.quote: But what we can tell you is that the monthly run rate right now compared to what it was 2 months ago, 3 months ago is higher by double-digit numbers. You can say north of 20% higher. So it's, it's growing and growing quickly. PEB India.

items.statement: PEB order inflows primarily from process engineering, automotive, and high-rise building sectors
items.quote: We are primarily seeing it in the process engineering space, the automotive space and the high-rise building space. Those are the three growth vectors where we've received significant order inflows.

items.statement: US PEB order book geared toward warehouse and data centers; data centers doing quite well
items.quote: So the 52 is a blend. It's geared more towards warehouse and data centers. Data centers is doing quite well in the US. A major driver of our US order book and why we are very confident that can scale also is the discussions we're having on this.

items.statement: Near-perfect steel price pass-through via quarterly rate contracts (1.5-3 month lag) and price escalation clauses; target operating margin retention on percentage basis during increases, value basis during decreases
items.quote: we are not a perfect, but a near-perfect pass- through. And as Shrikant had mentioned, the way this happens is we have quar terly rate contracts for steel. So any steel price increase typically we have one and a half to three months to pass on what we need to, depending on when that price increase comes in. So that's an advantage. More importantly, a lot of our contracts have price escalation clau

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance inclusive of other income; sustainable EBITDA margins growing year-on-year; one-time costs in Q3 (acquisition-related INR1-2 crores, other items) not expected to recur
items.quote: Inclusive of other income, sir. Inclusive other income and again, I don't want to belabour the one-time expenses point too much, but what we're committing to is one-time means one-time. I shouldn't come back to your next quarter and say there's more one-time costs, right? I mean, that doesn't make sense. So I think what we're guiding you to is sustainable EBITDA, EBITDA margins all growing year-on

items.statement: No customer contributes >6% of revenue (down from 7-8%); customer base diversified, entirely private sector, high repeat order proportion (often >50%)

items.quote: So, our current total debt is Rs. 507 crores at blended interest cost of about 9.15%.

items.statement: Will draw ~Rs 120 cr debt next quarter for new wind capacity; negotiating lower rates post rating upgrade to BBB
items.quote: Actually, next quarter loans will increase somewhat because we will be drawing down loans for the new capacity. So, we will be drawing down about Rs. 120 crores of debt for the new wind capacity.

items.statement: Subsidiary Delta to raise preference capital from parent and group captive customers only, not public
items.quote: There will be a Pref issue from Delta, which is the subsidiary which holds the solar, which will be holding the solar assets from the parent. So, that is only from the parent and from group captive customers. So, we are not raising money from the public.

items.statement: Greenfield solar capex ~Rs 5.5 cr/MW; wind ~Rs 7.5-8 cr/MW with higher PLF
items.quote: today your solar per MW is costing you to Greenfield about Rs. 5.5 crores per MW. Wind is today actually much more expensive. It is going up to almost Rs. 7.5 crores to Rs. 8 crores per MW.

items.statement: Wind generation seasonal: Q1-Q2 heavy, Q3-Q4 muted; 9M PLF 22% newer assets, 17% older assets
items.quote: For the nine-month period, the PLF was about an average of 22% for the newer assets and about 17% for the older assets.

items.statement: Tamil Nadu repowering policy allows life extension of >20yr turbines with annual fee; relaxes spacing norms; permits hybrid conversion
items.quote: The regulatory environment has also been quite benign. We have had a good outcome in the Tamil Nadu repowering policy, which stabilizes the outlook for our older wind turbines and allows us to continue operating our old turbines until they are ready for repowering.

items.statement: One-time refund of excess interest charged by erstwhile lenders in prior periods supported profitability
items.quote: The profitability was also supported by a one-time refund of excess interest charged by our erstwhile lenders in previous prior periods.

items.statement: Promoter pledge target to be unpledged before middle of next month
items.quote: I think the target is to get them unpledged sometime before middle of next month.

items.statement: No control over wind behaviour; next year monsoon indications okay but uncertain
items.quote: We have no control over how the wind will behave in the next season. This year was a slightly above average wind season. Next year we will see how it goes.

items.statement: Croatia 10.5 MW asset profitable (~800k EUR EBITDA LTM); no expansion plans; 51% owned with local partner
items.quote: last nine months I think we had about 1 million units generated in about 800,000 Euros of EBITDA in the last year which is about ….

items.statement: New capacity EBITDA impact: ~Rs 10 cr PBT; PAT neutral due to depreciation cover
items.quote: So, the immediate impact on PBT will be about Rs. 10 crores, after providing for interest and depreciation. PAT will be more or less rim because we will have enough depreciation cover for not paying tax.

items.statement: Strategy: deploy higher capacity turbines, expand solar, develop hybrid wind-solar projects for balanced portfolio
items.quote: we remain aligned with our strategy of deploying higher capacity turbines, expanding solar capacity, and developing hybrid wind-solar projects. This will allow us to build a more balanced, sustainable and future-ready portfolio.

items.statement: Group captive customers to participate in Delta subsidiary preference issue for solar assets
items.quote: It is only from the parent company and from the investors who will be buying power from us.

items.statement: Management indicates loan growth guidance will be provided tomorrow in a TV interview, noting 36% growth in 9 months and expecting to grow a little more
items.quote: I think we have grown by 36%. We should grow a little more. I will be able to give some number tomorrow, sir.

items.statement: Gold loan demand driven by difficulty in obtaining unsecured loans and microfinance sector challenges, not just gold price
items.quote: We feel that the demand is coming because unsecured loans are not easy to get. And even the microfinance sector has degrown. People need money, and they are increasingly starting to use gold collateral to get money.

items.statement: Yields increased due to INR667 crores interest recovery from old NPAs, INR110 crores fresh NPA, INR100 crores auction income, INR25 crores ARC recovery; regular yield 18.5-19%
items.quote: We just explained it, but there has been a recovery of the old NPA accounts, which has translated to an additional interest of around INR667 crores. And there's a fresh NPA of around INR110 crores. Then there is an auction income of around INR100 crores, then there is a recovery from the ARC sale of around INR25 crores.

items.statement: Pricing strategy aims to maintain net interest margins; borrowing costs passed to customers when bank MCLR rises; bank MCLR not yet reduced despite RBI rate cuts
items.quote: We try to maintain our net interest margins. So if the cost of funding is low, our yield also would be lower. But we try to maintain our net interest margins and spread.

items.statement: RBI draft regulations withdraw requirement for prior permission for branch opening, seen as positive for gold loan business growth
items.quote: Reserve Bank of India has sent out a circular or rather draft regulations for Comments, where our long-standing request or request for permitting branch opening without getting prior permission from the Reserve Bank stands withdrawn.

items.statement: Branch expansion will be calibrated, not accelerated despite regulatory easing; no plans to open 1,000-2,000 branches immediately
items.quote: Not that, as I said, not going to open 1,000, 2,000 branches tomorrow. It's not that easy to open.

items.statement: Standalone gold loan AUM grew 50% YoY to INR1,39,658 crores; 9-month increase of INR36,700 crores; total standalone AUM growth INR50,000 crores
items.quote: Our standalone AUM has achieved a historic growth of INR50,000 crores, which is fuelled by the robust 50% year-on-year growth in the gold loan portfolio. Our core gold loan portfolio has grown by 50%. But over the 9-month period, the stand-alone gold loan increased by INR36,700 crores, setting a new record for gold loan of INR1,39,658 crores.

items.statement: Standalone NPA reduced from INR3,700 crores to INR2,300 crores; legacy NPA of INR950 crores closed; fresh NPA INR342 crores; net NPA reduction INR556 crores
items.quote: See, March '25, our NPA was INR3,700 crores. Right now, it is INR2,300 crores. So that much of NPA was there at the beginning of the year. So definitely, 9 months has accrued this year. And probably the earlier accruals also now we have received.

items.statement: Belstar Microfinance Stage 3 assets at 4.93% with 96.59% provision coverage; higher Stage 3 consistent with industry after RBI allowed 40% non-microfinance portfolio
items.quote: The Stage 3 loan assets stood at 4.93%, which has a provision coverage of 96.59%. The higher Stage 3 is also consistent with the industry peers consequent to RBI allowing microfinance companies to have 40% non-microfinance portfolio.

items.statement: Average LTV on outstanding portfolio at current gold price is 57% against regulatory cap of 75%; normal disbursement LTV 71-72% in stable gold price scenario
items.quote: Today, if you look at today's price, the loans outstanding is only 57% of the total book is what is outstanding. So whatever is the permitted LTV, we do not do anything more than the 75%, but average LTV today on the outstanding portfolio at today's price is only 57%.

items.statement: Accrued interest on balance sheet around INR800 crores plus
items.quote: It will be around INR800 crores plus.

items.statement: Banks hold INR13 lakh crores gold loan portfolio vs NBFCs INR3 lakh crores; both growing; agricultural gold loans from PSU banks at 8-10% exist for 10-15 years but Muthoot grows on convenience
items.quote: Banks have about INR13 lakh crores of portfolio. NBFC has about INR3 lakh crores of portfolio. So everybody's portfolio is increasing. Competition is increasing, we are also growing. We grew by 50%, I think that is decent enough.
