items.statement: Muthoot Money gold loan portfolio INR8,003 crores, up 168% YoY; Belstar opened 39 gold loan branches in 9 months to diversify; Muthoot Home Finance AUM INR3,380 crores, up 24% YoY
items.quote: The loan portfolio for 9 months stood at INR8,003 crores as against INR2,982 crores in the previous year, showing an increase of 168%. During the 9 months, the loan AUM increased by INR4,001 crores, showing an increase of 105%.

items.statement: New customer additions around 400,000 per quarter; seasonal variation; new branches may bring more customers but steady flow continues
items.quote: So no, we have 400,000 customers, new customers coming. George Muthoot: Probably it is not that it is stabilized there. It is seasonal also. Sometimes more people come. If as you said, new branches mean some more new customers, but there is a steady flow of new customers

items.statement: Gold price volatility safeguard: 57% average LTV provides margin; ornaments have 15-20% making charge increasing replacement cost; sentimental value prevents abandonment
items.quote: Today, our average loan-to-value is only 57% or lesser than 57%. So we have such a big margin that, that is one side of the price. But again, most importantly, we finance only gold ornaments on which there is a making charge, which is again a 15%, 20%. So the replacement cost for a customer is not 100%, it is 115 to 120.

items.statement: Opex growth driven by employee benefits, rent increases, advertising budget increase for volume business, and consultant fees
items.quote: Primarily, it is because of the employee benefits and the advertisements. And of course, the business promotion expenses.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin 6.19% vs 9M FY26 6.48%; varies by project mix, BOQ billing timing, and client budget constraints
items.quote: EBITDA was INR5.84 crores with an EBITDA margin of 6.19%.

items.statement: Margins vary project-to-project and within projects due to BOQ-based procurement cost changes and billing timing
items.quote: Even within the segments, even project-wise, margin varies and even within the project, the billing-wise also margin varies, because see, as you would be aware, being an EPC company, we work on BOQ basis.

items.statement: Asset-light model with minimal fixed capex; site setups only after order receipt
items.quote: We are not like doing any manufacturing ourselves. So we don't have huge capex also.

items.statement: Negative operating cash flow and high receivables due to milestone-based EPC payments retained until final handover
items.quote: EPC, the business model itself is like that there are payments which are coming on the milestone basis. So till the final handing over happens, the last payment also gets retained in the receivables.

items.statement: Debt already reduced significantly; focus on continued debt reduction
items.quote: We have actually already reduced our existing debt quite a bit. And we -- our effort is to continue to keep reducing the debt in the future.

items.statement: Healthy order backlog with repeat business from established customers; company policy not to disclose order book value
items.quote: We have a healthy order backlog. We have a lot of repeat business from established customers.

items.statement: Revenue from FGD systems and bulk material handling not broken out; both high-margin and often packaged together for same clients
items.quote: What we do in material handling is high profit margin, and so is FGD. So, that's why we don't -- there's not like a substantial difference.

items.statement: Structural growth drivers: tightening emission norms, industrial capex in steel/cement/refining, grid reliability, AI data center power demand, and government INR20,000 crore CCUS allocation
items.quote: Government of India's recent budgetary allocation of INR20,000 crores towards carbon capture, utilization, and storage marks a structural shift in decarbonization framework.

items.statement: Carbon capture R&D: lab validation completed, pilot testing underway, planning small industrial demonstration plant with a client
items.quote: We have done lab validation, and we are right now currently doing pilot testing.

items.statement: iQ Energy AI platform launched October 2025; still in data training and testing with 1-2 existing clients; full commercial launch in a couple of months targeting global customers
items.quote: We announced it in October. And we are still training what we do with the data training, our AI model. We are working on that. And we will be actually going out full maybe in another couple of months where we will be actually soliciting customers.

items.statement: FGD demand persists despite temporary regulatory relaxations; carbon capture requirements reinforce FGD need
items.quote: FGD, like, it is not going away, even though there is a notification on certain relaxations for certain categories. As of now, like, there is no impact at all.

items.statement: 9M FY26 total income INR321.18 crore, EBITDA INR20.82 crore (6.48% margin), net profit INR9.1 crore (2.84% margin)
items.quote: For the nine months ended fiscal 2026, total income stood at INR321.18 crores, EBITDA was INR20.82 crores, translating into an EBITDA margin of 6.48%.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 total income INR94.31 crore, EBITDA INR5.84 crore (6.19% margin), net profit INR2.31 crore (2.45% margin)
items.quote: Total income for Q3 fiscal 2026 stood at INR94.31 crores. EBITDA was INR5.84 crores with an EBITDA margin of 6.19%.

items.statement: No royalty paid to US parent; CCUS solvent technology developed in-house with research lab collaboration; IP ownership not explicitly clarified
items.quote: No, we are not paying any royalty to anyone. There is no royalty being paid. Okay? We have technology, and as we said.

items.statement: BHEL arbitration ongoing (international arbitration); management confident in position but cannot disclose details
items.quote: Currently the arbitration is going on. It is an international arbitration and, it's being represented by both the parties. So it's going on, Yes.

items.statement: Promoter holding ~38% (down from 70%); management open to increasing stake; quarterly earnings calls to continue going forward
items.quote: We are not -- because we are getting into a lot of new areas, which we are very excited about and confident. So we are expanding our capabilities also. So these are --that's why we are now trying to reconnect with the investors and the investing community and let them know what we're doing.

items.statement: No specific revenue or margin guidance given; confident in long-term growth trajectory from policy tailwinds, industrial demand, and capability building
items.quote: We believe Ducon is entering a structurally favorable phase, where policy tailwinds, industrial demand and our internal capability building efforts are beginning to converge. We remain confident about our long-term growth trajectory and our ability to create sustainable value for stakeholders.

items.statement: CCUS interest from power, cement, refineries, chemical industries, and oil companies; existing global customer base for iQ Energy AI platform
items.quote: Well, see, everybody is showing interest, and we are working with even chemical industries, oil companies, and cement plants. Yes.

items.statement: Variable cost dominant (project direct costs); fixed costs minimal (employee costs, site setups post-order); profitability scales with revenue growth
items.quote: Substantial portion of our expense are variable cost. Fixed-wise, like, in fact, very bare minimum thing, like, the employee cost or maybe the -- even we have our own fees and everything, and site setups. We do the site setups after the receipt of the order.

items.statement: Execution cycles: INR20 cr project ~1 year; INR100-150 cr power plant ~2-2.5 years; small modifications ~5-6 months; quarterly billing affected by client readiness and third-party dependencies
items.quote: Suppose it's an INR20 crores project. It could be one year. But if we get an INR100 crores or INR150 crores for a power plant, it could be two years, two and a half years.

items.statement: Q3 lubricant volumes hit all-time high of 41,500 KL, up 8% YoY, outperforming industry 2x; 9M volumes 123,000 KL, up 9.3%
items.quote: I'm very delighted to inform you that this quarter has been an all -time high in terms of quarterly volumes at 41,500 KL, which is a record volume for Gulf Oil. It's been a very strong one for us. We've also notched up the highest quarterly revenue and EBITDA which is a good sign in terms of the momentum that we had gathered earlier in the year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded sequentially by 67 bps to 13%+ despite rupee depreciation, driven by cost management and selective price actions
items.quote: And what is also very good sign in spite of cost pressures coming mainly from rupee depreciation during the quarter, we have been able to expand our EBITDA margins sequentially by nearly 67 basis points because of the cost management and timely selective price actions we have taken. So overall, we are back to 13% plus EBITDA margin this quarter.

items.statement: INR 55 crore capex for Silvassa and Chennai capacity expansion; Chennai ready Q1 FY27, Silvassa by end of Q3 FY27
items.quote: So Mr. Dhaval, basically, we have announced a INR55 crores of CapEx for expansion of our Silvassa and Chennai capacities. The work is in progress. It's going to take maybe in Chennai, it will be coming sooner, but in quarter 1 of next financial year. And Silvassa will will be ready by the end of third quarter.

items.statement: Current plants running third shift to meet demand; new capacity for future growth as volumes grow 2-3x industry; no volume constraint for next 6-12 months
items.quote: Now having said that, we always have maintained that we can produce based on the market demand by running third shift, extra shift in the current plant and current setup with some incremental balancing equipment. So there is no challenge for fulfilling the current demand. And there's no direct correlation between the capacity and market demand and volume growth.

items.statement: Tirex EV subsidiary revenue grew 83% YoY in Q3 and 78% for 9M; acquired new OEM customers including Mahindra, MG, VinFast, bus OEMs
items.quote: Tirex actually closed quarter 3 with a top line growth of 83%. And if you take the 9 -month period, it's close to 78% to be exact in terms of revenue growth in the 9-month period.

items.statement: Revenue grew 11.8% vs 9.3% volume growth in 9M, indicating improved product and segment mix; premium/synthetic share increasing
items.quote: W've recorded a revenue of INR2,951 crores, which is a good double -digit growth of 11.8% for revenue, which shows that it is above our volume growth, so definitely improved segment and market and product mix has happened.

items.statement: Selective price actions taken; OEM pricing via quarterly PVC; base oil prices not fully tracking crude decline due to grade-specific demand-supply and refinery shutdowns
items.quote: We have also taken a few, and that's a good sign. So I think that we are hoping that we get that. Obviously, some of our OEM customers and all there is a quarterly PVC, so that takes a bit of time. But it's on the positive that pricing actions are coming.

items.statement: Base oil prices not fully correlated with crude in short term; PSU refinery expansions may increase domestic supply to 50-70% of requirement over time
items.quote: The capacity increase that the 3 PSUs have planned is going to take up this current capacity by at least, I would say, whatever numbers we are seeing in the market that this would go up to at least 50% to 60%, 70% more than what it is currently. But that is all plated capacity. We don't know what will come.

items.statement: OEM franchisee workshops grew high double-digit; partnerships with Mahindra, Swaraj in agri; new construction equipment tie-ups with Ammann, ACE, XCMG
items.quote: We've also announced strategic tie-ups with the leading construction equipment manufacturers, again, strengthening our presence in construction infrastructure, basically Ammann India, which is a global leader in road building machinery and we are the official lubricants partner for the entire equipment portfolio.

items.statement: Market has 16-17 players; Gulf is top 2-3 brand across segments; competitive intensity rising but company focused on Unlock 2.0 strategy for premiumization and market share gains
items.quote: As you know, there are 16, 17 players, which are the PSUs and multinationals and local brands. So I think that is something which continues to be there. We are also increasing capacity, as you said, others also increasing capacity. So I think each brand has its own position.

items.statement: GST rationalization for ICE vehicles improved consumer sentiment and created growth opportunities; new labor code provisioning had one-time impact of INR 12 crore in base quarter
items.quote: As mentioned, the GST rationalization for ICE vehicles has improved, and this is really providing a renewed sense of optimism amongst the consumers, also creating additional growth opportunities, while EV also grows, which is an area of our entry and growth.

items.statement: Export and marine segments slower this quarter; rupee depreciation created cost headwind; crude stable at $65-70 supportive for input costs
items.quote: Basically, some of our other segments, exports have been slightly slower and marine segment has been slightly slower. But when it comes to other domestic segments, all have done very well.

items.statement: Company remains net debt free; strong cash generation supports dividend increase and acquisition capacity
items.quote: And overall, we continue to remain net debt free.

items.statement: Interim dividend increased to INR 21 per share (1,050% of face value INR 2)
items.quote: And also, as we have announced, the Board has been happy to increase the interim dividend to INR21 per share. That's 1,050% on the face value of INR 2. So overall, yes, the Board has shown confidence in the way business is tracking.

items.statement: Actively evaluating acquisitions in EV space and niche lubricant products; increased Tirex stake from 51% to 65% in December quarter
items.quote: We have been vocal about it that we want to do more acquisitions in the EV space. Also in the lubricant space itself, some of the niche products, including in industrials, other categories. So as we speak, we keep evaluating many proposals.

items.statement: AdBlue volume grew ~8% to 111,000 KL in 9M FY26
items.quote: AdBlue also has grown for us by close to 8% at 111,000 KL volume 9 months.

items.statement: Rupee volatility remains key risk for margins; competitive intensity increasing; EV penetration may impact long-term lubricant demand
items.quote: Overall, we see that market is also looking at more pricing actions, which is going to be helpful because rupee continues to behave very erratic. And the good sign is that crude has been stable. So that's a positive because it is in that band of $65, $70

items.statement: Labor code provisioning driven by long-tenured workforce (15-20+ years); recurring impact marginal
items.quote: The recurring impact will not be very significant as we understand from the current provisioning because it's a company which was many of the employees are more than 15, 20 years with the company, and we started our plant in Silvassa way back in 1993.

items.statement: Launched next-gen products: fire-resistant hydraulic oils, zinc-free energy-efficient hydraulic oils, Syntrac motorcycle oils, synthetic gear oils
items.quote: We've launched a few next -gen product ranges, which basically we have launched fire -resistant hydraulic oils recently, energy-efficient zinc -free hydraulic oils, mainly for the CE segment. We also launched our new range of Syntrac motorcycle oils and a number of other gear oils, which are synthetic.

items.statement: Residential real estate sector remains on strong and balanced footing with end-user driven demand supported by urbanization and rising disposable income
items.quote: the residen tial real estate sector remains on a strong and well-balanced footing as we look ahead into 2026. Demand continues to be predominantly end-user driven, supported by favourable structural factors such as urbanization, rising disposable income and lifestyle- led upgrades

items.statement: FY26 pre-sales guidance maintained at Rs. 1600-1700 crore despite lower launch volumes
items.quote: we are maintaining our guidance, which like you said was about Rs. 1600-1700 crores

items.statement: Business development guidance for FY26 at Rs. 3500-4000 crore GDV, currently at Rs. 2510 crore with healthy pipeline
items.quote: we are aiming for about close to about Rs. 3500 crores to Rs. 4000 crores in terms of our BD guidance. We remain on track.

items.statement: Medium-term pre-sales growth target of 25-30% annually over next 3-4 years
items.quote: we have guided for the next 3-4 years that this is the kind of run rate we want to mainta in over the next 4 years, about at 25%- 30

items.statement: 9M FY26 bookings at Rs. 938 crore (5% YoY growth), Q3 bookings at Rs. 331 crore (48% YoY growth)
items.quote: 9M bookings improved by 5% YoY to Rs. 938 crore. Sales momentum during the quarter remained healthy, with bookings of Rs. 331 crore, a growth of 48% on a YoY basis.

items.statement: 9M FY26 collections at Rs. 744 crore (2% YoY growth), Q3 collections at Rs. 317 crore (38% YoY growth) - highest ever quarterly collections
items.quote: our highest ever 9M Collections in FY26 amounting to Rs. 744 Cr, up 2% on a YoY basis, reflecting strong cash conversion and disciplined follow through on receivables. Quarterly Collections were also the highest ever during Q3, increased by 38% YoY to Rs. 317 crore

items.statement: Sustenance sales run rate guidance at ~Rs. 200 crore per quarter going forward
items.quote: I think going forward, we have a reasonable chance that we ca n maintain this Rs. 200 crores kind of guidance on the sustenance number

items.statement: Medium-term business development investment of Rs. 700-1000 crore over next few quarters
items.quote: over the medium term; we are looking at investing about Rs. 700-1000 crores. So, that number is something that we are con tinuously monitoring

items.statement: Q4 FY26 launch pipeline of ~Rs. 1500-1600 crore GDV across 4 projects including Baroda Phase 1, Industrial Phase 1, Orchards Phase 2, and one Bangalore project
items.quote: So, close to about Rs. 1500-1600 crores of GDV, because like I said, we are launching part of the industrial and part of the Baroda project. So, about Rs. 1500-1600 crores from these four projects that we are bringing in.

items.statement: Cumulative new business development topline potential for the year at ~Rs. 2510 crore including projects in Bengaluru, Ahmedabad and Vadodara
items.quote: Our cumulative new business development topline potential for the ye ar stands at ~Rs. 2,510 Cr, which includes two new projects in Bengaluru, and one each in Ahmedabad and

items.statement: Unrealized operating cash flow from current project pipeline estimated at >Rs. 4581 crore expected to realize over 4-5 years
items.quote: We estimate an unrealized operating cash flow exceeding Rs. 4,581 crore coming from the current pipeline of projects. This is expected to realise within 4-5 years.

items.statement: Marketing cost ~1-1.5% of topline; including brokerage ~3.5-4%; channel partners remain most significant booking channel
items.quote: pure marketing costs will be close to about 1% to 1.5% Including brokerage, typically, what we might be incurring on our portfolio might be closer to about 3.5% to 4%.

items.statement: Management emphasizes velocity and cash flow over land banking; will prioritize sales velocity even in downturns rather than holding inventory for price appreciation
items.quote: We have always, as you know, been a very cash flow focused company. We believe in velocity, our mantra is velocity. We are not the variety to bank land and wait for market and prices to inch up. That has never been the DNA of this company.

items.statement: Significant team strengthening across functions (sales, marketing, execution, legal) in Mumbai and other markets; new COO onboarded recently
items.quote: we continue to strengthen our team on all fronts, whether it is sales marketing, execution, legal, all fronts. So, we are in process of actually scaling up and adding more and more members.

items.statement: Mumbai redevelopment pipeline at advanced stages; expecting decent closures over next 2-3 months
items.quote: Mumbai, our pipeline of projects has really moved quite well over the last few months, gives us confidence that we should be looking at some decent amount of closures over the next 2-3 months.

items.statement: Karjat (Mumbai-Khopoli) project approvals progressing; launch expected in FY27; Surat project status quo with clarity expected next quarter
items.quote: that's a project where we are working on our approvals right now. So, we are actually looking at getting the ap provals in the next few months. Most likely, it's a launch that will come in the next financial year

items.statement: FY26 revenue target revised to INR 6,000 crore from earlier INR 6,500 crore
items.quote: we revised this guidance to INR 6,100 to 6,200. And now, based on the till nine months of growth trajectory, 17% growth, we may touch around INR 6,000 crore now

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth projected at 20-25% on FY26 base
items.quote: based on the order book, so far, we are on the course to achieve at least 20% to 25% growth

items.statement: FY26 order inflow target of INR 10,000 crore
items.quote: We are progressing towards achieving INR 10,000 crore order intake in FY '26

items.statement: FY27 order inflow guidance of INR 10,000+ crore
items.quote: maybe around 10,000+ only we will look at for the next year as a guidance on the order inflow is concerned

items.statement: Total order backlog INR 56,800 crore including MDO, INR 17,300 crore excluding MDO
items.quote: The total order backlog, including MDO projects, is about INR 56,800 crore, INR 17,300 crore, excluding MDO orders

items.statement: Order inflow year-to-date INR 6,761 crore
items.quote: order wins during the year-to-date have reached about INR 6,761 crore

items.statement: Executable order book INR 17,000 crore with no long-pending orders
items.quote: all the order book, of existing INR 17,000 crore is executable order book. There is no long-pending order book in this

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin 12.08%, stable QoQ with slight dip due to Labor Code provisions
items.quote: EBITDA margins at 12.08%. The margin remains stable compared to the previous quarter, with a slight dip due to provisions created for compliance with the new Labor Code

items.statement: 9M FY26 EBITDA margin improved to 12.88% from 12.2% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA margins improving to 12.88% from 12.2%

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expected 12.5% in FY26, rising 0.25% YoY to 13.5-14% by FY29
items.quote: Maybe this year we will maintain at 12.5%. Hoping that this will increase of 0.25% year-on-year, and once we are ready with our washery by FY28 onwards, maybe 0.5% jump will be there in the EBITDA margin

items.statement: FY26 capex INR 380 crore (INR 280 crore washery + INR 100-120 crore regular), FY27 capex INR 520 crore
items.quote: this year and next year together, around INR 690 crore to INR 700 crore as a washery cost in our books, and, INR 100 crore to INR 120 crore, on an average on the regular CAPEX

items.statement: BESS project capex INR 800 crore with 51% stake via consortium
items.quote: It involves a CAPEX of about INR 800 crore, and we have got a consortium of partners led by Power Mech, having 51% share

items.statement: Gross debt INR 833 crore, net debt INR 233 crore, debt-equity 0.35x as of Dec 2025
items.quote: As on 31st December 2025, the gross debt was around INR 833 crore, and the net debt was INR 233 crore. The average debt-equity ratio, as on the same date, was 0.35x

items.statement: Gross debt expected to rise by INR 400 crore by next year for MDO term loans
items.quote: This will go up another INR 400 crore by next year

items.statement: Operating cash flow improved from INR -253 crore to INR 113 crore in 9M FY26 due to receivables realization
items.quote: operating cash flow has improved, reducing from INR (253) crore in nine months FY '25 to INR 113 crore in nine months FY '26, primarily due to realization of receivables during the period

items.statement: Singareni BOP has 10% advance and 5% retention aiding cash flows
items.quote: there is a provision of advance which helps a working capital management, and the retention is only 5%, which can translate into better cash flows

items.statement: Revenue mix: 95% domestic, 5% international; 70% power, 30% non-power in Q3
items.quote: The geographical mix for the quarter was 95% domestic and 5% international, while power sector contribution remained at 70%, with non-power sector accounting for the remaining 30%

items.statement: BHEL subcontracting pipeline 24,000 MW (INR 60,000+ crore), Adani balance 18,400 MW
items.quote: balance tendering is of 24,000 Megawatt. And then tendering subcontracting packages balance by Adani is about 18,400 Megawatt, and that transfers to opportunities of plus 60,000 crore in various sectors

items.statement: Labor Code implementation expected from April 2026; provisions created in Q3 for existing liabilities
items.quote: the labour code is already announced by Central Government in the month of November. We are creating provisions in the Q3 itself for the existing liabilities in the books, and actual implementation will be from 1st April

items.statement: Revenue guidance of INR 2,000 crores by FY27 on consolidated basis maintained
items.quote: We are maintaining our revenue guidance of INR 2,000 crores by FY27 on a consolidated basis.

items.statement: Garment division EBITDA margin guidance of 15% maintained including Young Brand and Sri Lanka
items.quote: No, we, currently, we would like to stick to the guidance of 15 %at the EBITDA level on the Garment division.

items.statement: Young Brand EBITDA margin expected at 15-18% yearly
items.quote: So we expect the margins with respect to YBAPL at an EBITDA margin of 15 to 18 % Quarter-to-quarter, it may vary. But yearly, we expect it to be around 15 to 18%

items.statement: SPUK targeting USD 20 million revenue (approx INR 200 crores) over next two financial years
items.quote: We are targeting a significant growth in the business over the next two financial years with a revenue goal of about USD 20 million, that is approximately INR 200 crores

items.statement: SPUK EBITDA margin target of 4% at trading model level
items.quote: So we are working towards achieving 4% at the EBITDA level.

items.statement: Capex for next financial year estimated at INR 30 crores including maintenance, solar and Young Brand expansion
items.quote: So roughly around INR 30 crores for capex next financial year.

items.statement: India utilization at 4,200 machines, added 700 machines this quarter, closed couple factories due to US tariffs
items.quote: So, 4,200 machines is the utilization. And every factory has got some unutilized machines. And moreover, when we spoke in the beginning, we have closed down a couple of factories due to the U.S. tariff issue.

items.statement: Sri Lanka operational capacity at 1,650 machines, expect normalized operations from Q1 FY27 and optimum utilization in Q2 FY27
items.quote: We expect operations in Sri Lanka to reach normalized levels from Q1 FY 27 with meaningful shipments and optimum utilization in Q2 FY27.

items.statement: Young Brand scaling towards 1,700 installed machines with sales utilization ramp to 1,500 machines
items.quote: We have resumed the sale of expansion that was temporarily paused, and the Young Brand is scaling towards 1,700 installed machines with the sales utilization ramp to around 1,500 machines.

items.statement: Young Brand Salem expansion restarting with 150 machines effective running in FY27, scaling to 350 by end of FY27
items.quote: For this, the coming financial year, it would be around 150 machines effective running, but that can scale up to 350 machines by the end of the next financial year.

items.statement: Order book: SPAL INR 353 crores, Young Brand INR 87 crores, SPUK INR 30 crores
items.quote: The order book status division -wise of SPAL is INR 353 crores, Young Brand apparel is INR 87 crores SPUK is INR 30 crores.

items.statement: Healthy reengagement from US buyers, new customer additions, order visibility strong for upcoming season
items.quote: On the demand side, we are seeing healthy reengagement from American buyers who had earlier preferred for Sri Lanka ships. Many of them now prefer continuity in India under the revised tariff clarity.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 softer due to US tariff discounts, Q1 FY27 transition, Q2 FY27 normalization expected
items.quote: Q4 is going to be under pressure for financial numbers. Q1 is going to slowly improve and Q2 will be the restoration of the original situation.

items.statement: Standalone Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin 15.6%, consolidated 14.8%; 9M FY26 standalone 16.3%, consolidated 14.3%
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA stood at INR 40.4 crores with an EBITDA margin of 15.6%.

items.statement: Garment division ex-YBAPL margins impacted by wage increases and factory closures due to tariffs, expected to normalize from Q1 FY27
items.quote: So, if you look at last year versus this year, our wages have gone up from March 2025 minimum wages have changed. And because of the tariffs, there has been a couple of factories that has been closed down because of, so purely because of tariff and the wag es increase, there is an impact on the margin front

items.statement: Realization degrowth due to product mix shift to children's wear; planning more adult orders to improve average price
items.quote: So, we expect to maintain or move up a little bit because we are planning to bring in more of adult orders also, which will bring up the average price hoping because we need to fill up the capacities by bringing in adult orders.

items.statement: Onboarded 4-5 new buyers during year, adding 2-3 more from US, Europe and UK
items.quote: We also onboarded four to five new buyers during the year which has strengthened our presence in these key markets.

items.statement: Young Brand adding 1-2 new UK/European customers to diversify from US overreliance
items.quote: We are also onboarding one or two new U.K., European customers, whi ch will help diversify the customer mix and reduce overreliance on the U.S. market

items.statement: SPUK existing customers consolidating suppliers, two customers guiding INR 80 crores each, top 4 vendor status achieved
items.quote: So, they have given a guidance of this is the kind of volume, one customer is giving about INR 80 crores, and another one is about INR 80 crores, and we are adding another one or two more new customers.

items.statement: India-US trade deal brings tariffs to 18%, India-EU FTA eliminates up to 12% duties, UK-India FTA <1 year away
items.quote: The India -U.S. pact, which brings tariffs down to 18% strengthens our competitiveness and opens access to USD118 billion U.S. textile import market.

items.statement: New Labour Code aligned since 2020, no material financial impact expected
items.quote: On the new Labour Code, we are already aligned with the most requirements, and we do not expect any material operational impact on the financials.

items.statement: US exposure ~23-25% of consolidated business, Young Brand 85% US-focused, standalone US share 15-17% moving to 20%+ in FY27
items.quote: Young Brand and SP Apparels put together, our U.S. exposure is less than 25%. So it should be roughly around 23% to 25%.

items.statement: Sri Lanka provides duty-free access to UK/EU, can import fabric from any country duty-free for re-export
items.quote: Previously, if it is from China, they used to import 12% duty. Now they have removed everything. They can source import from any country and they re -export it duty free.

items.statement: SPUK working capital requirement ~1 month turnover, high ROCE trading model with 45-60 days supplier credit
items.quote: The working capital should not be a big requirement. As such, we take some suppliers 45 days credit to 60 days with certain suppliers. And it will be a requirement of one month turnover only for working capital.

items.statement: Standalone gross debt INR 275.4 crores, net debt INR 227.9 crores
items.quote: Our current debt position on a standalone basis, gross debt stood at INR 275.4 crores and our net debt is INR 227.9 crores.

items.statement: Sri Lanka revenue INR 37 crores in 9M FY26, targeting INR 50 crores for full FY26
items.quote: For the first nine months, we have done INR 37 crores on the Sri Lanka business, and we expect to go up to INR 50 crores this financial year.

items.statement: Retail division EBITDA positive, Crocodile INR 14.5 crores revenue, Angel & Rocket INR 3 crores in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Retail division Q3FY26 revenue stood at INR 17.2 crores with a positive EBITDA of INR 0.8 crores against a loss of INR 0.6 crores Q3 FY25.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 revenue and margin pressure from US customer discounts agreed to maintain continuity during tariff uncertainty
items.quote: American customers have slowed down their order placing. And in fact, in Q4 shipments, we have agreed to continue all of a sudden, neither we can stop the production of shipments, nor the customer can completely exit from India and move to other countries. So we both mutually agreed to give some kind of a discount to them to maintain the continuity.

items.statement: ESG: Adding ~3MW rooftop solar across 3 units in FY26-27, total in-house solar capacity to reach 4MW
items.quote: On ESG front, we are progressing well on our sustainability commitments by planning for addition of approximately 3 megawatts of rooftop solar capacity across three additional units for the next financial year FY26-27, taking total installed capacity on in -house solar facility to 4 megawatts.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 13.4% in Q3 FY26 vs 14% YoY; standalone EBITDA margin 16% vs 21.5% YoY
items.quote: Our consolidated EBITDA has been INR37.5 crores in quarter 3 versus INR39.3 crores in the quarter 3 last year with a margin of 13.4% in quarter 3 versus 14% in the quarter 3 last year.

items.statement: MedTech consolidated EBITDA turned positive at INR0.7M in Q3 FY26 vs loss of INR69M YoY
items.quote: On the profitability front, consolidated EBITDA turned positive at INR0.7 million compared to a loss of INR69 million in quarter 3 financial year '25.

items.statement: Standalone ARPOB INR43,171 in Q3 FY26, up 1.1% YoY; ALOS 3.9 days vs 3.62 YoY
items.quote: Our ARPOB has been INR43,171, which is up by 1.1% as compared to similar quarter last year, which had an ARPOB of INR42,704. Similarly, our ALOS has been 3.62 in the quarter 3 of the FY '25 as against 3.9 ALOS in the quarter 3 of FY '26.

items.statement: Group occupancy 44% in Q3 FY26 vs 46% YoY; excluding Shalby International, 47% vs 48% YoY
items.quote: Our occupancy rate has been 44% in quarter 3 FY '26 versus 46% in the similar quarter last year. If we talk excluding the Shalby International, which is PK Healthcare in Gurgaon, our group level occupancy rate stands at 47% in quarter 3 of FY '26 and 48% in the quarter 3 of FY '25.

items.statement: Insurance work stopped for 2-2.5 months due to rate negotiations with 2-3 major insurers; contracts re-signed in November, flow positive in Jan
items.quote: So we had to stop doing some of the work with some of these insurance companies, the two or three major insurance companies. And so for 2 to 2.5 months, we had to stop workin g. Then eventually, the positive is that in the month of November, we have signed -- in the month of November end, we have signed the contracts again

items.statement: Expect double-digit volume growth and 5-6% ARPOB growth in FY27
items.quote: We definitely see a double-digit volume growth in the next year. Then, of course, there is an ARPOB growth of 5% to 6% additionally on top of that.

items.statement: Over INR80 crores invested in last 8-9 months on robotics, diagnostics, bunkers; 5 orthopedic robots, 2 other specialty robots installed; 2 more bunkers planned in Mohali and Delhi NCR over 12-18 months
items.quote: Over INR80 crores has been invested in some of these areas over the last 8 to 9 months, which have not started adding to the top line significantly because they have just been commissioned.

items.statement: 50-odd beds can be added in Delhi NCR at appropriate time; no significant capex planned for hospital business in next 12 months
items.quote: With regards to bed addition, we have another 50-odd beds, which can be added in the Delhi NCR region, which at the appropriate time, we w ill take up that project. Besides that, we don't see any significant capex. Even some of the capex that I did mention is likely to come in the 12- to 24-month range. Not much capex is planned over the next 12 months on the hospital business

items.statement: Shalby International (Sanar) targeting average 40 occupied beds for FY27, up from ~20 currently
items.quote: In the next year, for the average, we are looking at, at least, 40 as an average for the full-year.

items.statement: Arthroplasty ~33% of work in Q3, down from 70% 10 years ago; oncology, cardiology, intensive care, neurology, transplant each 10-15% and growing high double digits
items.quote: If you look at the data for this quarter, about 33% of the work is arthroplasty, okay? Exactly, if you ask me 10 years ago, we were at about 70% arthroplasty. 15 years ago, we were at 95% arthroplasty.

items.statement: MedTech India consumption of own implants jumped from 15-20% to 70-80% in January after supply issues resolved
items.quote: I can tell you that more than 70% to 80% of the implants used in the month of Jan -- from the month of Jan this year have been our implants. So that is a big positive for us, which until now, so far until Q3 used to be around 15% to 20%.

items.statement: MedTech revenue split ~60% OUS (India, Indonesia, Japan) and 40% US by year-end
items.quote: So we're currently doing about -- if I have to take on a consol level, we'll be about 60%-40% by the end of the year. 60% of the business would be OUS. When I mean OUS, it includes India, Indonesia, Japan as of now, and it could be multiple countries in time to come. The rest 40% is U.S.

items.statement: NABH accreditation expected very soon for Shalby International (Sanar); will enable CGHS, ECHS, Haryana government tie-ups
items.quote: For the insurance companies, majority of insurance companies are getting closed, and we are waiting for NABH to come on board, which we are expecting by this week. Once NABH coming in, we will be also doing a lot of tie-ups for, say, Haryana government, CGHS, ECHS and all.

items.statement: MedTech received approvals in Malaysia for Unicondylar product and Argentina; dossiers submitted in South Korea, Vietnam, Iran; active discussions in Ethiopia, Paraguay, Sri Lanka, Russia
items.quote: We have received approvals in Malaysia for our Unicondylar product and Argentina. We have submitted regulatory dossiers in South Korea, Vietnam and Iran, and we have ongoing active discussions in Ethiopia, Paraguay, Sri Lanka and Russia.

items.statement: Net debt expected to be lower in 12 months; implant business funding requirement ~30-40% of EBITDA generated; hospital business to generate significant EBITDA
items.quote: The way we see it is that the net debt 12 months from now should be a little lower than where we are at the moment. The way we see it is that the funding requirement of the implant business will be, say, 30% to 40% of the EBITDA that we'll generate.

items.statement: Group ETR ~35%; evaluating move to lower 25% tax rate under new MAT changes, annual impact in next quarter
items.quote: One significant change as also in the budget, the MAT changes have come. We are evaluating it out. Probably, our evaluation is indicating that we would move to a lower tax rate of 25% into the Shalby Limited. That would reduce our tax expense significantly into the coming quarter.

items.statement: Added 40 doctors in Q3, lost 18; net addition; marketing efforts and robotics support for new doctors; takes 1-2 months to rebuild base
items.quote: Apart from that, I think the quarter has been quite positive in terms of doctor recruitment, etcetera, because we've added 40 doctors in this quarter, whereas we've lost about 18 doctors. Overall, we've added doctors for the quarter, and that will -- we are seeing and we will see that play out for us.

items.statement: Closed Rajkot and Lucknow franchisee facilities; converted to OPDs; no plans to add franchisees; patient flow from these cities unchanged
items.quote: In fact, we have closed down the Rajkot as well as the Lucknow facilities. We have started doing OPDs from there. We did realize that a lot of patients did end up traveling and prefer to travel to some of our larger units for treatment. It was a strategic decision taken, and we are not planning to add significant franchisees.

items.statement: Mumbai hospital partner trust reviewing agreement terms; close discussions ongoing; will update on developments
items.quote: Our partner, the trust is reviewing certain terms in the agreement, and there is a close discussion happening with them. Once the terms are reviewed by them, then only we'll be able to update you out that -- any development on that front.

items.statement: Target group EBITDA margin 23-25% at 50% higher occupancy; normalized unit margin 20%; expect visibility in coming quarters
items.quote: can definitely not only stabilize at a 20% margin, 20%, I said, for a typical unit. But at a group level, we definitely -- as we see the ramp-up, we definitely can go up to 23% to 25% also at a 50% higher occupancy than what it is right now

items.statement: MedTech EBITDA breakeven achieved; PAT breakeven not yet but improved from -50% to -25%; no timeline given for PAT breakeven
items.quote: We have not PAT breakeven right now, but our PAT has significantly gone up from negative almost 50% to about negative 25% at a PAT level.

items.statement: ALOS elevated at 3.9 days due to higher medical/critical care cases; expected to remain in this range fluctuating with specialty mix
items.quote: The ALOS is a little bit on higher side due to more medical cases. We have developed critical care unit at 2-3 units and had done some expansion in current beds also. That is how due to medical cases and critical cases, ALOS is on higher side.

items.statement: Shalby International EBITDA breakeven delayed by 2 quarters due to management issues; NABH accreditation and new clinical talent expected to drive drastic change in 1-2 quarters
items.quote: We were likely to be EBITDA positive over there about 2 quarters ago. There has been a delay on that front. As we mentioned, because of some management issues. There are 2 things happening, which give us a lot of confidence. One is the new clinical talent that we are onboarding. Second and more importantly, the NABH is expected to come in very, very soon.

items.statement: MedTech 9M FY26 revenue INR949M, up 47% YoY; India +127%, US +5%, Southeast Asia +35%
items.quote: For the first 9 months, consolidated revenue reached INR949 million, up 47% year-on-year. Shalby Advanced Technologies revenue grew 5% to INR842 million. Shalby MedTech more than doubled revenue, growing 127% year-on-year to INR532 million. Shalby Global Technologies grew 35% year-on-year to INR50 million.

items.statement: MedTech COGS reduced to ~50% of level 4.5 years ago; gross margins improving daily through material optimization, vendor consolidation, manufacturing efficiencies
items.quote: The cost of goods manufactured at our implant business at the factory is now down to almost 50% of what we used to manufacture it at about 4 and half years ago.

items.statement: Lost 2 high-end doctors to new infrastructure offering higher pay; chose profitability over matching offers
items.quote: We also lost two doctors in two of our units, two different units. And, often what happens is, there is a lot of new infrastructure that keeps coming up in some of these cities. And often, they are prepared to pay any price to get that business. We may not be able to match that because we believe that profitability also is equally important.

items.statement: Closing order book of around 130 crore as of 31st December after opening order of 57 crore, new bookings of 132 crore, and deliveries of 59 crore.
items.quote: On order booking, as of December we had an opening order of 57 crores. In this year we booked an additional 132 crores of new orders, from which we delivered 59 crores. As on 31st December we have closing order book of around 130 crores.

items.statement: Total order book is 190 crore including delivered portion; balance order in hand is around 130 crore.
items.quote: Total order book is 190 crores from which we have already delivered around 59 crores, so balance order in hand is around 130 crores.

items.statement: Humro has a confirmed order book of six mobile robots valued at 4.13 crore structured under a two-year lease agreement.
items.quote: The subsidiary has also received a confirmed order book of six mobile robots valued at 4.13 crore, stru ctured under a two -year lease agreement

items.statement: Standalone nine-month EBITDA around 6 crore, PAT around 94 lakh, PAT margin expanded to 9.8% from 0.8% earlier, PAT grew almost 127%.
items.quote: In nine months, we did turnover of around 60 crores and EBITDA is around 6 crores. PAT is around 94 lakhs. PAT margin expanded to 9.8% from 0.8% of earlier years and PAT has grown by almost 127%.

items.statement: Consolidated Q3 top line 68 crore, EBITDA around 7.33 crore, PAT around 2.18 crore, margin expanded to 10.7% from minus 12.6% earlier, PAT grew 116%.
items.quote: On consolidated basis, in Q3 we did a top line of 68 crores and EBITDA around 7.33 crores and PAT around 2.18 crores. The margin expanded to 10.7% from minus 12.6% in the earlier same nine-month period. PAT grew by 116% for the same nine months.

items.statement: Achieved around 30% reduction in material cost and employee cost; employee cost converted from fixed to semi-variable, achieving 31% reduction; total expenses reduced by 28%.
items.quote: By opera tional efficiency we mean we achieved around 30% reduction in material cost and employee cost; employee cost which was earlier fixed, we converted into semi-variable. Hence we were able to achieve 31% reduction there in nine months. So total expenses reduc ed by 28

items.statement: Q4 revenue expected at par with last year level, but bottom line improvement expected.
items.quote: On revenue we will be at par or on the level of last year, but you can see improvement on the bottom line. Definitely there will be improvement on the bottom line.

items.statement: Indian business top line expected to grow around 20 to 30% next year.
items.quote: Quantifying number – top line we expect to grow by around 20 to 30% in the Indian business.

items.statement: Plan to deploy 200-225 Humro machines cumulatively by March 2027, targeting monthly revenue of around 1 crore-plus.
items.quote: We plan to deploy by March 2027 around 200-225 machines approximately. Robinson: 200-225 machines cumulatively deployed by March 2027; that could give us a monthly revenue of around a crore -plus

items.statement: US forklift market ~750,000 units annually; targeting 1-2% market share in next five years.
items.quote: In the US market, forklifts sold annually are about 750,000 units. That is the North America market. We want to take 1-2% share in the next five years to start with.

items.statement: Planning further fund raise at Humro level for inventory build-up; quantum under wraps, talking to interested parties.
items.quote: we will raise the money and like I said we may not be able to get 100% of all the answers but the idea is to raise money definitely we have talk spoken to some intere sted parties and we will raise those money soon

items.statement: Outright sale IP recurring revenue ~10-15% initially, benchmark 20-25% over time; AMC and IP charges for seven years.
items.quote: So it will be approximately 10 to 15% yeah and it will keep increasing as and how we kind of progress there and as and how the credibility our credibility is established in the market as of now we have kept it very very minimal yeah but the benchmark is around 20 to 25%.

items.statement: Developed new vendors for material cost reduction; renegotiated contracts; shifted labour from 300 on-roll/100 contract to 200 on-roll/200 contract.
items.quote: We developed new vendors for material-cost reduction, and for labour cost we now have a lot of labour on contract. Earlier we had, suppose, 300 people on roll and 100 on contract; now we probably have 200 on roll and 200 on contract.

items.statement: Humro delivered first order of Atlas AC-2000 autonomous forklifts to large US logistics firm; revenue started.
items.quote: Humro has delivered its first order of Atlas AC-2000 autonomous forklifts to a large US-based logistics firm and revenue has already started from there.

items.statement: Humro doing POCs with marquee Fortune 500 customers; expect monthly revenue of $25-30k by March.
items.quote: We are doing some marquee Fortune 500 customers' POCs now as we speak. These are huge customers; I can't name them because of various reasons, but we expect to start good amount of revenue by the year-end – monthly revenue of, say, 25 to 30 thousand dollars per month we will be touching by March.

items.statement: Humro has 3 dealers in US (California, Pennsylvania, Dallas); in talks with more; may participate in Promat Atlanta.
items.quote: As of now three but we are in talks with a couple of them more and where we have demonstrated our products and once we are ready for the scale we should be able to hire at least two three of them in the coming year to deliver this 200 equipments.

items.statement: Reduced tariff in Europe is a heartening development; will look at Europe after 50-60 equipments deployed in US.
items.quote: The reduced tariff in Europe is a very heartening development yeah we will not be wasting too much time once we have 50 60 equipments up and ready there in US I think we should start looking at Europe too.

items.statement: Lost a ~21 crore order due to inability to fund inventory and dispatch on time; fundraising delays caused order loss.
items.quote: we lost that order because we did not get the appropriate fundraising at that point in time which needed to ship these robots like I said so our first priority is to build some inventory there so that the depende ncy on you know inventory is lesser

items.statement: Consciously not taking low-margin orders in standalone business to protect profitability; order pipeline not increased.
items.quote: We are consciously not taking orders which are having less profit or which is going to spoil our profitability this year so this is a conscious call we are selecting and we are taking very few orders which you know will give us good profitability from the start.

items.statement: Robinson is co-founder and CEO of RaaS (Humro); based in US, currently in India for fund-raise.
items.quote: Robinson is a co-founder for RaaS and also the CEO of RaaS. He sits in the US but now he's in India for this fund-raise. Otherwise he is working out of the US.

items.statement: Heavy welding joint venture not finalized; still working on own for heavy welding, taking projects from L&T and others.
items.quote: No, so heavy welding joint venture has not gone through and we are still working on our own for heavy welding. We are taking some projects from L&T and others for heavy welding.

items.statement: Autonomy stack monetization across seven layers (navigation, fleet management, dashboard, simulation); targeting India and global applications.
items.quote: There are seven layers in autonomy – navigation, fleet management, dashboard, simula tion, etc. – and we will monetize each layer separately. Now since we are in active discussion with a lot of people, we have started putting that in this

items.statement: FY27 battery chemicals revenue guidance maintained at INR 400-500 crore
items.quote: Our guidance remains the same because, the guidance the expectation was that our Dahej site will be fully ready by June 2026 and our expectation that, we will start having sales of this from basically Q1 and majorly from Q2 onwards. So that remains the same. Therefore, our guidance does not change.

items.statement: Dahej replacement plant commissioning on track for Q1 FY27
items.quote: Concurrently, construction of replacement plant of Dahej is progressing rapidly, with commissioning on track for Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Pakhajan greenfield project commercial production targeted for electrolyte in H1 FY27 and electrolyte salts in H2 FY27
items.quote: Our Pakhajan greenfield project is progressing as per schedule, with commercial production for electrolyte targeted for H1 FY27 and electrolyte salts for H2 FY27.

items.statement: Dahej salt capacity expansion of 1,100 tons now expected by March 2026 after design improvements
items.quote: Its just that we were implementing some changes in the design for further improvement, so it went to March 2026.

items.statement: Dahej electrolyte plant ready for full 30,000 MT annual capacity by end of H1 FY27
items.quote: By end of H1, the way the plant is, we are doing a joint trial with Mitsubishi. So our idea is that the entire 30,000 MT, there are three lines and all the three lines would be tested and we would be ready for the 30,000 tons kind of annual capacity.

items.statement: Salt plant utilization target 80%, electrolyte plant can go up to 100%
items.quote: Normally salt would be at 80%. It is like a chemical plant. In case of electrolyte, it is a formulation plant so you can go up to 100%.

items.statement: Long-term commercial supply approval secured from prominent giga-scale Indian manufacturer after PPAP completion
items.quote: We have already achieved a major milestone by securing long-term commercial supply approval from a prominent giga-scale Indian manufacturer following successful PPAP completion.

items.statement: Provisional approval received from multiple global clients for lithium electrolyte salts; final site audits expected in Q1 FY27
items.quote: On the international front, we have received provisional approval of our lithium electrolyte salts from multiple global clients now, while final site audits are expected to be concluded in Q1 FY 27.

items.statement: Dahej site expected to be fully qualified by several customers by June 2026 with sales starting Q2 FY27
items.quote: So, I would say Dahej site should be fully qualified through several customers by June 2026, that is Q1, by the end of Q1, and sales should start in Q2.

items.statement: Pakhajan site targeting approval by December 2026 to contribute sales from Q4 FY27
items.quote: And Pakhajan we are targeting in the second half, but our target would be to complete it by Q3 so that it starts contributing to the sales from Q4 in the next financial year.

items.statement: Gross profit up 13% with ~150 bps margin expansion in Q3 FY26
items.quote: We delivered 9% revenue growth in Q3, with gross profit up 13% with around 150 basis points margin expansion.

items.statement: EBITDA and PAT pressured by transient costs from Neogen Ionics ramp-up, fire incident toll manufacturing, and higher finance costs
items.quote: While top-line growth was strong, EBITDA and PAT were pressured by transient costs related to Neogen Ionics ramp-up, elevated operational expenses due to fire incident and interim toll manufacturing setup, and higher finance cost from Dahej plant reconstruction and other investments.

items.statement: Toll manufacturing costs to reduce as Dahej plant comes online, improving cost structure
items.quote: Yes, currently some of the higher costs that you are seeing will reduce, as we move from other expenses, which will change a bit. Whatever is the tolling related expenses, that will go away.

items.statement: Bromine price strength has limited impact due to long-term contracts with suppliers and customers
items.quote: So, from one contract to another it kind of gets material. So unless you have a two-times, three-times increase in Bromine (prices), we really do not see a big impact related to that.

items.statement: Inorganic segment revenue decline solely attributed to lower lithium prices; spike impact visible from Q4 FY26
items.quote: It is solely attributed to the downward lithium price and the spike impact we'll see maybe little bit in Q4 but more in the next year if the spike is maintained.

items.statement: Inventory target 140-160 days by end of FY27; debtor-creditor target 60-90 days
items.quote: by the end of next financial year, our inventories would be at around 140 to 160 days, is what we are targeting on the inventory side. And as we said, debtor-creditor usually depending on whether more international or more domestic sales, the debtors are usually between 60 to 90 days kind of a range by the end of the year and that is what we would like to target.

items.statement: Net debt INR 680 crore standalone and INR 1,175 crore consolidated as of December 2025
items.value: INR 680 crore standalone, INR 1,175 crore consolidated
items.quote: The net debt that we have today is around INR 680 crore on standalone basis and around INR 1,175 crore on a consolidated basis.

items.statement: First principal repayment for Dahej loans in Q1 FY28; for Pakhajan in H1 FY28
items.quote: for whatever loans we have in Dahej, let us say if we are completing in Q1, then the first principal repayment will be Q1 of FY28. And in case of Pakhajan, it will be right now say H1. So, if we are saying H1 FY27 is when it starts, then H1 FY28 would be the equivalent first repayment after that.

items.statement: Board approved preferential issue of up to INR 150 crore to Promoter Group, subject to regulatory approval
items.quote: the Board has granted in-principle approval to raise up to INR 150 crore via preferential issue of equity shares to the Promoter Group.

items.statement: Expect ~INR 550 crore from insurance (INR 210 crore), Morita JV (~INR 200 crore), and promoter infusion (INR 150 crore) by Q1 FY27
items.quote: in the worst case, by Q1 next year, we would have INR 150 crore from the Promoter, we would have around INR 200 crore from the partner, and we would have at least INR 200 odd crore from insurance. So we expect around INR 550 crore to come either in this year or in Q1 next year.

items.statement: Formed JV with Morita Investment Limited (80:20) for LiPF6 salt production with $20 million investment from Morita
items.quote: We have successfully concluded a joint venture with Japan's Morita Investment Limited to produce and sell LiPF6 salt globally. Neogen will hold an 80% majority stake in the new entity - Neogen Morita New Materials Limited - supported by a $ 20 million investment from our partner for the rest of the stake.

items.statement: Dahej plant is India's only non-FEOC compliant electrolyte salt plant with proven technology
items.quote: Notably, this establishment is India's only non-FEOC compliant electrolyte salt plant with proven established technology, offering a strategic alternative to the Chinese supply chain while advancing Atmanirbhar Bharat through significant import substitution.

items.statement: US 45X tax credits and non-FEOC requirements creating tailwinds for Neogen as strategic global partner
items.quote: We are currently seeing significant tailwinds from the US 45X tax credits non-FEOC requirements and recent price volatility in China, both of which enhance our appeal as a strategic global partner.

items.statement: Core business demand resilient in Pharma, Flavors & Fragrances, and specialty applications
items.quote: Despite global market volatility, our core business remained robust, underpinned by demand resilience in Pharma, Flavors and Fragrances, and other specialty applications.

items.statement: Indian battery cell capacity expected ~12 GWh by end of 2026, 40-50 GWh+ by end of 2027
items.quote: I think by end of 2027 we should be if everything goes well by end of 2027, we should be 40-50 giga plus entering into 2028 based on what customers have shared till now.

items.statement: Neogen Ionics contributed INR 12 crore revenue in Q3 FY26 as battery chemicals vertical scales
items.quote: Additionally, Neogen Ionics contributed INR 12 crore to the quarter's revenue as we continue to scale our battery chemicals vertical.

items.statement: Customer approval timelines uncertain; some may wait for Pakhajan plant instead of Dahej
items.quote: Maybe we will just wait six months and take it from Pakhajan. So that can happen. But many of them right now are showing urgency to buy now. So we hope that they will start buying from Dahej and then move over to Pakhajan afterwards.

items.statement: R-32 production ramp-up expected to start from Q4 FY2026, pushed from Q3
items.quote: Also, the value creator for us this year going forward in this segment will be R-32 sales ramp-up, which we are expecting to start from Quarter 3, which has now been pushed to Quarter 4.

items.statement: Oman battery materials project estimated investment $216 million, part of Rs 6,000 crore capex
items.quote: We are setting up a state-of-the-art greenfield advanced battery materials project in Oman to produce battery materials for lithium ion batteries with an estimated investment of $216 million.

items.statement: Oman project timeline around 18 months, commissioning mid to end of 2027
items.quote: The Oman, the time line is around 18 months for us to have the plant gets commissioned. Okay. So, it will probably be mid to end of 2027, yes.

items.statement: R-32 first phase target 20,000 tonnes, delayed by a quarter or quarter and a half from March end
items.quote: Our plan is to still commission going to 20,000 tonnes, as I had indicated earlier. Of course, at that time, I had indicated it was going to be March end. Now I expect that to be slightly delayed by a quarter or maybe a quarter and a half, okay?

items.statement: R-32 long-term plan up to 30,000 tonnes by December 2027 quota deadline
items.quote: The capacity can be added up to December 2027, okay? Of course, in the previous call also I had indicated that the long-term plan is to go to 30,000 tonnes, or go up to our quota that we have today.

items.statement: Fluoropolymer demand encouraging from semicon sector with global investments and capacity additions
items.quote: At the same time, demand in fluoropolymers remain encouraging, particularly from the semicon sectors, where global investments and capacity additions continue to be strong.

items.statement: Increasing momentum in EV ESS segments globally with improving order inflows and better visibility
items.quote: We are also witnessing increasing momentum in the EV ESS segments globally. With improving order inflows and better visibility, we are confident that FY 2027 should see healthy revenue growth from this vertical.

items.statement: Refrigerant segment bore brunt of headwinds; R-22 quota reduction and weak R-125 prices impacted profitability
items.quote: The most adverse pressure came from R-22, where we faced a dual impact. First, the production quota reduction constrained volumes; second, seasonally subdued demand affected offtake. Also, the delay in R-32 production start-up resulted in lower-than-expected profitability for us. In addition, R-125 prices remained weak during the quarter, further contributing to the softness in performance.

items.statement: Battery materials order book for current capacity looks very healthy, expect full utilization by end of FY2027
items.quote: So, for the plant that are already there, we expect to get fully utilized probably by the end of this year.

items.statement: Fluoropolymer growth 14% YoY but 3% sequential decline due to US tariff uncertainty and antidumping duty not approved
items.quote: The Fluoropolymer segment delivered healthy growth of 14% year-on-year, though revenue declined 3% sequentially. The quarter-on-quarter moderation was primarily due to uncertainty around U.S. tariff policies, which led to cautious ordering patterns and temporary deferment of demand in key export markets.

items.statement: Inventory days at 201 vs target 120; building inventory for expected orders but delayed by holiday season and tariffs
items.quote: However, last year we saw that in the last quarter also, as it was a holiday period in U.S.A., Europe, and also some of the slowdowns happened due to tariffs also that we had to hold some inventories with us, either over here or in our stock warehouses in other countries. So, that's how the inventory went up.

items.statement: Target working capital days 170-180 realistic due to stock-and-sell model and early shipping
items.quote: So, what we are targeting, Sanjesh, is somewhere around maybe 170 to 180 is what we think is a realistic number going forward because of our business model is based on stock and sell and also shipping material early from here.

items.statement: IFC approved Rs 430 crore investment in GFCL EV Products; sovereign fund approved $82 million investment
items.quote: On 5th of December, 2025, the International Finance Corporation, IFC, has approved investment of Rs. 430 crores in our subsidiary, GFCL EV Products Limited. This investment supports the development of India's first integrated battery materials manufacturing facility and strengthens the domestic EV supply chain ecosystem.

items.statement: IFC and sovereign fund investments in convertible form linked to IPO milestones, pure equity with no put/buyback
items.quote: Both these investments are coming in convertible form where they are linked to the certain milestones on the IPO that way. So, there's no fixed valuation neither for the IFC investment in India nor for the sovereign fund that is going to invest in the subsidiary in Oman. So, they are more like a convertible instrument, which will have a fixed return is linked to the certain milestones.

items.statement: US tariffs reduced from 50% to 18%, restoring competitiveness in key export market
items.quote: The recent reduction in U.S. tariffs from 50% to 18% provides significant relief and restores competitiveness in one of the key export markets.

items.statement: Antidumping duty recommended by DGTR but not approved by Finance Ministry, eroding growth
items.quote: Of course, one of them was antidumping duty, where of course as you know, DGTR had recommended antidumping duty, which was eventually not approved by the Finance Ministry. That, of course, has eroded a few percentage points from the growth that we were looking at.

items.statement: R-32 and R-125 combination targeting global market access including 410 blend
items.quote: R-32, of course, we are looking at it as global market access because we are into a very sweet sp ot with R -125 also with us , so we are looking at R -32 and R -125, combination 410 plus R-32 alone. So, it's going to be both global as well as

items.statement: Battery materials except electrolyte focused on US and European markets for non-China supply chain
items.quote: The products that you mentioned, except electrolytes, the remaining three product verticals are all for global market because Indian market is still not ready. So, the entire business plan is around that.

items.statement: LiPF6 pricing formula-based with lithium carbonate reference, margins intact despite LCE price fluctuations
items.quote: Most of our LiPF6 pricing with our customers is based on a formula with lithium carbonate as a reference. So, as the lithium carbonate fluctuates, so will our LiPF6 pricing, and our margins will be intact. That's the way we have structured our contracts.

items.statement: Fluoropolymer segment revenue Rs 1,136 crore consolidated, EBITDA Rs 275 crore, down 6% YoY
items.quote: Consolidated Revenue for the quarter stood at Rs. 1,136 crores, a marginal decline of 1% year-on-year. In Q3 FY 2026, EBITDA stood at Rs. 275 crores, reflecting a 6% decline from Rs.294 crores in Quarter 3 FY 2025.

items.statement: Fluorochemicals revenue declined 33% YoY and 24% sequentially due to refrigerant weakness
items.quote: In the Fluorochemicals business, revenue declined by 33% year-on-year and 24% sequentially. The decline was largely due to refrigerant business, as explained earlier.

items.statement: Qualification times long for EV/ESS products; more critical products have longer qualification
items.quote: The issue is that, unfortunately, in products in EV and ESS space, the qualification times are long, a nd the more critical the product is, the longer the qualification time

items.statement: Oman capex higher than China due to equipment import but strategic advantage from FTA and opex
items.quote: Of course, the Chinese capex is, of course, right now, the lowest. But however, it's not very far from that. So, it's obviously, Oman being a country where we will have to bring all the equipment and machinery from outside. The capex is expected to be higher. But nevertheless, when we look at the entire Opex and Capex combination, I think it has a strategic advantage for us.

items.statement: Fluorospecialty pharma/agro segment not a focus; continuing existing products but no new investment
items.quote: As of now, Rohit, we do not have much focus on that particular segment. So, we have certain products, which are continuing, which we intend to continue, of course. And those have been picked up based on certain margin expectations. So, we are not really investing in that segment as of now because there are so many other opportunities that we have.

name: Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation Ltd

items.statement: Targeting 15% sustainable growth for FY26
items.quote: You see all of our segments have shown a very good increase and we are targeting to achieve 15% sustainable growth this year.

items.statement: Average daily ticket bookings rose to 14.64 lakh in Q3 FY26 from 13.59 lakh in Dec 2024
items.quote: And the ticket booking, average daily ticket booking in lakhs is around INR14.64 lakh per day as against INR 13.59 lakhs last year December '24.

items.statement: UPI share of transactions increased to 50.18% from 46.86% a year ago
items.quote: And the UPI share has increased from 46.86% last year to 50.18%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin moderated to 32.1% due to revenue mix changes, especially higher catering contribution
items.quote: EBITDA rose to INR465 crores with a healthy EBITDA margin of 32.1%, although margins moderated slightly due to changes in revenue mix, particularly higher contribution from catering and provisions, our overall profitability remained strong and sustainable.

items.statement: Internet ticketing EBITDA margin at 85%
items.quote: The segment delivered an impressive EBITDA margin of 85%, reflecting strong operating leverage and cost efficiency.

items.statement: Tourism EBITDA margin improved to 19% from better product mix and cost rationalization
items.quote: Tourism delivered an excellent performance with revenue of INR 289 crores, marking a 29% year-on-year growth despite temporary geopolitical disruptions. EBITDA margins improved to 19%, reflecting a better product mix and focused cost rationalization initiatives.

items.statement: Rail Neer margins improved due to economy in material costs and operational efficiencies
items.quote: Margins improved during the quarter, driven by economy in material costs and sustained operational efficiencies, along with strong brand acceptance in the market.

items.statement: 40 additional trains introduced in Q3, including 19 Vande Bharat trains, driving catering revenue up 19.1%
items.quote: We have seen that our revenue from Vande Bharat train this time, the billing has increased by INR70 crores and so be the license fee. So the main reason for factoring business revenue enhancement is introduction of additional 40 trains during the period.

items.statement: Railway ministry plans to introduce 260 Vande Bharat train sets over coming years
items.quote: So you must have seen the budget announcement and the discussion thereafter in the parliament and various media coverage, wherein it is very categorically told by rail ministry that they are going to introduce 260 Vande Bharat train sets.

items.statement: Doubling capacity at existing Danapur and Ambernath Rail Neer plants; adding 4 new plants at Mysore, Prayagraj, Bhagalpur, Ranchi for 25-30% capacity increase in 1.5 years
items.quote: We are enhancing the capacity of our existing plant at Danapur and Ambernath. We are doubling its capacity. In addition, our Board has already sanctioned for installation of 4 new plants at Mysore , Prayagraj, Bhagalpur and Ranchi. So we'll be adding around 25% to 30% capacity in say -- in 1.5 years.

items.statement: Rail Neer average daily sales at 12.68 lakh bottles; serving 50-60% of railway demand depending on season
items.quote: The average is 12.68 lakhs bottle.

items.statement: Tourism revenue breakup: Maharaja Express INR 53.14 cr (+39%), State Tirth & Bharat Gaurav INR 118.91 cr (+51%), Tejas INR 50 cr, air ticketing INR 6.7 cr (+41%), budget hotels INR 5.3 cr (+38%), other packages INR 55.26 cr (+19%)
items.quote: Maharaja revenue grew by 39%. And in absolute term, it is INR53.14 crores. Our State Tirth and Bharat Gaurav train revenue grew by 51%, and it's INR 118.91 crores. Our air ticketing business also grew by 41%. And -- but the figure is INR6.7 crores -- our budget hotel and Rail Yatri Niwas business grew by 38% in absolute terms, INR 5.3 crores. And other packages announced by 19%, which is INR55.26

items.statement: Non-convenience fee revenue grew 26% YoY to INR 150 cr; marketing & ad revenue INR 24.78 cr vs INR 13.29 cr; other business INR 62.47 cr vs INR 52.53 cr; loyalty program INR 21.88 cr vs INR 15.35 cr
items.quote: Our convenience revenue is INR 251 crores and non-convenience revenue is INR150 crores during this quarter.

items.statement: Payment aggregator license document submission extended by RBI to August 2025; technology provider engaged
items.quote: So our document submission date has been extended by RBI till August this year. And we have already engaged our technology service provider. So most likely we'll be submitting the documents at the earliest.

items.statement: Assessing labor code impact; gratuity eligibility reduced from 5 years to 1 year plus health checkup; any cost impact to be offset by volume and revenue growth
items.quote: I don't see there is any major impact because we are still examining the impact as such in detail because there are 2 things which may come for us, like earlier gratuity that used to be given in 5 years. So it has been reduced to 1 year and health checkup. So like for our regular employees, we have no problem because we will see to that. And whatever the impact of that will be adding to our cost.

items.statement: Static catering units increased from 543 to 563 stations under Amrit Bharat station scheme
items.quote: Earlier, we were having our projects at 543 stations. It has now increased to 563.

items.statement: E-catering (Swiggy/Zomato) grew 25% and complements traditional catering; no cannibalization seen
items.quote: You see there is no dearth of market for both kinds of things. Like -- as I showed you the figure of this quarter, both our normal catering also increased and our e-catering also increased by, say, 25%. So the difference is like in basic catering, we serve the daal chawal khaana type of thing. But in catering, you can add to what you eat. So both the things are complementing each other, and I don'

items.statement: Tejas Express occupancy: Lucknow route 69%, Ahmedabad route 109%
items.quote: It is -- Lucknow percentage is 69% and Ahmedabad is 109%.

items.statement: 89% of reserved railway tickets in India booked through IRCTC online platform
items.quote: Nearly 89% of the reserved railway tickets in India are now booked through our online platform, underscoring our leadership in digital ticketing.

items.statement: Data monetization plans subject to DPDP compliance; unified portal planned for cross-selling
items.quote: You see we have to see the DPDP compliances. And we have a very -- like we have planned to introduce our unified portal and taking use of data available with us to cross -sell our products, but this will be in compliance to DPDP guidelines.

items.statement: Q4 services run-rate revenue target INR 650 crores to enter FY27 strongly
items.quote: We are hoping to end Q4 strong. There are some key deals under discussion and negotiation, which we hope to finish strongly by March, which will allow us to end Q4 strong, enter FY 2027 with a services run rate revenue closer to INR 650 crores.

items.statement: ICICI Bank and India Post Payment Bank order book INR 750+ crores, ~75% live
items.quote: We have over INR 750 crores of order book just with 2 customers, ICICI Bank and India Post Payment Bank. Both of these are about 75% live.

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA margin expanded 160 bps QoQ to 25.5%; Cash Logistics margin up 170 bps; Managed Services & Tech EBITDA up 12% to INR 78.5 crores
items.quote: EBITDA margins expanded by 160 basis points, moving from 23.9% in Q2 to 25.5% in Q3. This margin expansion was driven by the 2 segments, Cash Logistics, EBITDA up by 6% and margins expanded by 170 basis points; Managed Services & Tech EBITDA up by 12% to INR78.5 crores.

items.statement: ATMs under cash management dipped to 68,000, now back to 70,000; targeting 74,000-75,000 by March/April
items.quote: We were roughly about 70,000 ATMs under cash management about a few quarters ago, which dipped to 68,000. We are back to 70,000 now. We are targeting an aggressive ramp-up to 74,000, 75,000 ATMs by the end of March or April.

items.statement: Tech & Payments revenue grew from INR 235 crores to INR 330 crores in 1 year; on track for INR 400 crores in FY27 (30% CAGR)
items.quote: Our tech and payments business is growing from INR 235 crores revenue to INR330 crores revenue in 1 year and is on track to hit INR 400 crores in FY 2027. This is a 30% CAGR.

items.statement: Hawkai ARR doubled from INR 100 crores to INR 200 crores range over FY24-26; targeting large RFPs in new sectors
items.quote: Our Hawkai business specifically is growing rapidly. We have taken this business from 0 to INR 100 crores revenue run rate ARR in FY 2021 to 2024 in 3 years. And from FY 2024 to 2026, we are seeing this double from INR 100 crores to INR 200 crores level range.

items.statement: Revenue concentration reduced: largest customer 22% to 18%; private banks + direct retail 24% to 30%; PSU banks 19% to 22%; MSP partners 35% to 29%
items.quote: Over 2 years from FY 2024 to year-to-date FY 2026, the contribution from our largest customer has reduced from 22% of revenue to 18%. The whole category of private sector banks and the direct-to-retail revenue, that contribution is increasing from 24% to 30%.
