The PSU bank revenue contribution is up from 19% to 22% and the revenue we earn from our MSP partners is down from 35% to 29% of revenue.

items.statement: Acquired Securens for INR 70 crores; signed term sheet for ATM management solutions business acquisition valued INR 100-125 crores, targeting March close
items.quote: Earlier this year, on the back of having scaled our Vision AI platform into a market leader, we are able to make an accretive acquisition of a leading player, Securens. This was our first deal in the last 4 years. The investment here finally is INR 70 crores. On February 11, a couple of days ago, we signed a term sheet for a business transfer agreement with a leading MSP to acquire their ATM manag

items.statement: DSOs elevated due to midsized MSP stress post-AGS; provisions made in Q2; Q3 actions to limit services improved cash flow; DSOs normalizing by March-end
items.quote: We had made provisions in Q2. And in Q3, we took strong tactical actions, which included limiting services to ensure payment discipline. This has had a negative revenue impact, but was necessary to drive cash flow improvements. DSOs are getting streamlined and should be back to normal levels by end of March.

items.statement: ECL provisioning FY23 5% of revenue, FY24 4%, FY25 3.7%; FY26 expected 4.25-4.5% due to lag effect from DSO increase
items.quote: The risk provision for FY 2023 was around 5% of the revenue, which we have reduced to 4% in FY 2024 and 3.7% in FY 2025. However, this year, we are expecting the same to be range of around 4.25% to 4.5% of the revenue because the ECL specifically have a lag effect.

items.statement: Buyback evaluation deferred to year-end pending clarity on balance sheet, capital needs for organic/inorganic growth; board discussed post tax changes
items.quote: On buybacks, given the feedback we had both at the analyst call and after from shareholders, given the recent change in taxation, which makes it more equitable to all shareholders and also keeping in mind the growth opportunity ahead of us, this has been discussed at the Board. We will be evaluating this in line with better clarity on our balance sheet and the needs of capital by the end of the ye

items.statement: Banks shifting from transaction-based to fixed-based pricing for ATM/recycler contracts; CMS stayed out of transaction market for 12-18 months
items.quote: The second pivot is moving away from transaction-based pricing to fixed-based pricing. That is something that at CMS, we've been advocating for a long time. We've stayed out of the transaction market for almost last 12 to 18 months now.

items.statement: RFP pipeline reviving in FY27: 6,000-8,000 ATM units in pipeline, ~INR 2,000 crores contracted value opportunity; banks pivoting to recyclers and fixed pricing
items.quote: When I think about the RFP pipeline in FY '27, we see meaningful activity coming back into the market. As we speak, we are aware of almost about 6,000 to 8,000 ATM units, which are in various stages of the pipeline. This means that there's a total contracted value opportunity of about INR 2,000 crores.

items.statement: Retail cash management market share ~38%; focus on yield management and cross-selling tech solutions rather than pure pricing power
items.quote: In the retail, I think we're in a zone where we are focusing more on yield management and yield improvement, which means that we are sort of evaluating things on a contract-by-contract basis. Our focus there is really to continue to increase market share, to continue to expand the addressable market opportunity and to invest in both building the sales capability as well as using that to cross-sell

items.statement: Employee cost + service/security cost up 6-7% YoY in Q3 due to long-term wage settlements (LTS) and capacity investment for anticipated SBI contract
items.quote: If you see that if you add both the service and security and employee cost, it has increased around 6% to 7% over Q3 of FY 2025 to Q3 of FY 2026. And this is because of the - as we explained to you, there is an LTS impact and the new business, whatever we got is impact related to that.

items.statement: Invested ahead of SBI RFP (expected 10,000 ATMs) but won only 5,000; tightened deployment norms to align with contracted milestones
items.quote: In hindsight, we invested ahead of this contract and our anticipation on things becoming normal was very aggressive given the subsequent delays to that RFP. This has been a big learning for us. And since then, we have tightened our deployment norms to align strictly with contracted milestone with key customers.

items.statement: SBI RFP: CMS was sole eligible bidder initially for 10,000 ATMs; after RFP scrapped and reissued, won 5,000 as L1, rest went to other participants
items.quote: In the first version of the outsourcing process, we were the only eligible participant. And that would have meant we get the entire 10,000. But unfortunately, with that getting scrapped and then coming out with a new RFP, of that, we were the L1 participant. So we got about 5,000 of those volumes with rest going to other industry participants.

items.statement: New segment reporting: ATM Solutions (15-18% growth), Retail & Currency Logistics (~12%), Tech & Payments (~20%) targeted for FY27
items.quote: We think that business overall should grow 15% to 18% next year. The retail and currency logistics business should grow about 12-ish percent. And our technology and payments business, which includes Hawkai and cards would, I think, grow about 20% for the next year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin dip drivers: ~1.5% from wage inflation + infrastructure investment for delayed contract; ~1-1.5% from fleet cost + ECL/risk provisions; improving in Q4
items.quote: Our overall dip in EBITDA margins, I would just put them into 3 factors, about roughly about 1.5% impact in both wage inflation and the investments we made in building infrastructure for a contract, which took time to pan out. And then about 1% - 1.5% dip in margins, which is linked to both increase in fleet cost as well as higher overall ECL provisions and risk provisions.

items.statement: Securens acquisition: INR 18 crores revenue (INR 12 crores incremental) in Q3; negative PBT this year due to front-loaded depreciation
items.quote: Securens around INR 18 crores, Total revenue of INR 18 crores, so incremental revenue of around INR 12 crores in Q3. Rajiv Kaul: And Securens will have actually this year a negative PBT because we will be front -loading the depreciation on the assets

items.statement: Retail cash management: 165 direct-to-retail logos (up from ~0 2.5 years ago); cross-selling vaults and Hawkai solutions; pruned unprofitable long-tail points
items.quote: Today, we have almost Anush, what 150-plus direct-to-retail logos. Anush Raghavan: 165. Rajiv Kaul: 165 customers, right? This number was maybe 0, 2.5 years ago. With these customers, we are cross-selling, right? We are not only in the business of retail cash management. We are upselling them in retail cash vaults. We are upselling them with Hawkai-based solutions.

items.statement: Management sees demand supported by positive sentiment, ongoing product launches, and disciplined inventory management, with medium- to long-term opportunity in premium luxury and EV space remaining compelling.
items.quote: Looking ahead, we expect demand to stay supported by positive sen timent, ongoing product launches and disciplined inventory management. While there may be near-term challenges, the medium- to long-term opportunity, especially in the premium luxury and electric vehicle space remains

items.statement: Mahindra XEV 9S and XUV 7XO together recorded over 93,000 bookings in just a few hours, reflecting strong acceptance.
items.quote: The brand saw strong booking momentum for the XEV 9S and the XUV 7XO, which together recorded over 93,000 bookings just in a few hours.

items.statement: Gross margin was 16.4% on reported revenue in Q3 FY26, a 20 bps improvement year-on-year; EBITDA margin was 5.9% on reported revenue, up 13.3% year-on-year.
items.quote: Gross profit for the quarter stood at INR220 crores, reflecting a sequential improvement of 13.6%. The gross margin came at 16.4%.

items.statement: Employee cost and other operating expenses kept below target 4.4% of proforma revenue; company remains committed to cost optimization.
items.quote: During the quarter, em ployee cost and other operating expenses were kept below the target 4.4% of proforma revenue. The company remains committed to its stated plan of cost optimization

items.statement: Capex for the first nine months of FY26 was INR 50 crores.
items.quote: So, our capex number on a nine-month basis is INR50 crores Vaidik.

items.statement: Added new outlets for Mercedes-Benz in Bhopal and Mahindra & Mahindra in Hyderabad during the quarter; newer workshops progressively ramping up.
items.quote: During the quarter, we also expanded our network with the addition of ne w outlets for Mercedes- Benz in Bhopal and Mahindra & Mahindra in Hyderabad

items.statement: New outlets have stabilized; company demonstrated capacity to rapidly and profitably grow when opportunity arises.
items.quote: In the last 18 months, Landmark has set up large capacities. The new ou tlets have now stabilized. We have demonstrated our capacity to rapidly and profitably grow when the opportunity arises

items.statement: Net operating cash flow of approximately INR 265 crores generated in first nine months of FY26, reflecting improved working capital discipline; inventory levels well below industry averages at 31 days.
items.quote: As of 31st December 2025, the company generated net operating cash flow of approximately INR265 crores, reflecting improved working capital discipline.

items.statement: Inventory days currently at 31; desire to bring it even lower, with 30 days considered acceptable and anything below very good.
items.quote: Inventory days at our end, we have been publishing this for a very long time. And we have tried to always maintain it much lower than the industry standard with a discipli ned approach. Now we are at, say, 31 days currently. Our desire would be to bring it even down

items.statement: Aftersales revenue grew 13.1% year-on-year to INR 279 crores in Q3 FY26, delivering record quarter with highest revenue and year-on-year growth outperforming recent trends.
items.quote: Our aftersales business also delivered a record quarter with highest revenue and year-on-year growth outperforming recent trends.

items.statement: New car sales proforma revenue grew 10.6% year-on-year to INR 1,572 crores in Q3 FY26; aftersales revenue grew 13.1% to INR 279 crores.
items.quote: With this, proforma revenue for new car sales grew by 10.6% year-on-year to INR1,572 crores, while aftersales revenue stood at INR279 crores, reflecting a growth of 13.1% year-on-year.

items.statement: Over 50% of Landmark volume comes from OEMs likely to benefit from EU FTA (Mercedes-Benz, Renault, Volkswagen, Stellantis brands).

items.statement: Government paused ethanol blending at 20%, industry expects increase to drive incremental capacity
items.quote: The other concern is that the government has put a stop at 20% or paused the blending at 20% currently. And we are all hoping that this blending percentage should be increased.

items.statement: Target to run distillery for 330 days per year (300+ operating days) by supplementing captive molasses with external purchases
items.quote: If we take let's say 30 days for maintenance, annual maintenance of the distillery, it is our aspira tion that we should raise it at run the distillery for 330 days in a year

items.statement: Expect Q4 cane crush of ~90 lakh quintals at 100% capacity utilization over 90 days
items.quote: Given that 67 lakh crushing is already there in Q3 and 90 days even if we operate 91 days if we operate our sugar mill properly and use 100% capacity. So another 90 million tons of -- 90 lakh quintals of crushing should be available with us.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA INR36.3 crores in Q3 FY26 vs INR37.7 crores YoY; nine-month EBITDA INR125.7 crores vs INR114.8 crores YoY
items.quote: On the EBITDA, we continue to maintain the EBITDA and EBITDA for Q3 FY26 is INR36.3 crores versus INR37.7 crores in the previous year.

items.statement: Consolidated PBT before exceptional items loss of INR18.6 crores in Q3 FY26 vs profit of INR23.7 crores YoY; nine-month PBT INR154.9 crores vs INR53.2 crores YoY
items.quote: Similarly, the PBT before exceptional item for the Q3 is a loss of INR18.6 crores as compared to INR23.7 crores for Q3 of previous year.

items.statement: Improved cane payment cycle over last 3-4 years boosting farmer confidence and cane supply
items.quote: We have been able to improve our cane payment cycle a lot over last three to four years. As a result of which our availability and confidence of farmers in supplying the cane to the company is going up every year.

items.statement: Significant overcapacity in ethanol industry noted as concern requiring resolution
items.quote: As some of you may have noted, there seems to be significant overcapacity in the ethanol industry and I think a resolution must be found out to deal with it.

items.statement: Facing regulatory challenges in Goa due to new law restricting land use change, not factoring land monetization into deleveraging plans
items.quote: we are facing some regulatory challenges in Goa and there has been a new law that has been passed which is restricting the land change in land use, etc etera. So we are examining various options, you know, various legal options, etcetera. And therefore, we are not factoring it into our deleveraging plans as of now

items.statement: Actively looking at acquisition opportunities in the sugar sector
items.quote: We are also looking at, as I mentioned earlier, acquisition opportunities in the sugar sector.

items.statement: Sugar industry estimated production 34.4 million tons, diversion 3.4 million tons, exports 1.5 million tons, closing stock 5-6 million tons
items.quote: I think it is my estimates say that sugar production is estimated at some 34.4 lakh million tons and diversion is around 3.4 million tons. That leaves 31 million tons plus there is an expected export of 1.5 million tons. So that will leave around somewhere around 29 million tons of, you can say, sugar availability in India and consumption being around 28 million tons, 29 million tons.

items.statement: Embedding artificial intelligence across all operations and empaneling domain experts, collaborating with global technology licensors
items.quote: As I mentioned in my previous calls, the company is seeking to build deep technical capability and as part of that it is empaneling domain experts, it is collaborating with global technology licensors as well as research institutions who have proprietary p rocess technology. It is also embedding artificial intelligence in all aspects of its

items.statement: No IPO proposal for Zuari Infraworld on the table, not contemplating any IPO
items.quote: The first question about the IPO of Zuari Infra World. I just want to place on record that there is no such proposal on the table. We are not contemplating any IPO of Zuari Infraworld.

items.statement: Value of listed strategic investments INR4,600 crores as of 31 Dec 2025, slightly lower than previous quarter due to market movement
items.quote: The value of our listed strategic investments as on the 31st of December 2025 was INR4,600 crores, and which was a shade lower than the previous quarter because of the market movement.

items.statement: Oil Tanking JV income increased to INR7.4 crores from INR5.5 crores driven by renegotiated tolling rates with OMCs
items.quote: And it's primarily driven by the renegotiated rates for the tolling facility with the OMCs.

items.statement: Simon India building deep capabilities in fertilizer segment (ammonia, urea, DAP, NPK, phosphoric acid, sulfuric acid) and using AI extensively
items.quote: The idea is to develop very deep expertise in those areas where the Group is already present, which is the fertilizer segment where we make ammonia, we make urea, we make DAP, we make all kinds of NPK. And as part of the DAP plant, we make phosphoric acid, we make sulfuric acid.

items.statement: Double-digit revenue growth guided for FY26 and FY27 with improving earnings quality and sustained margin strength
items.quote: Collectively these levers give us confidence in delivering double digit revenue growth in FY'26 and FY'27 with improving quality of earnings and sustained margin strength.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 topline growth expected at 12% to 14%
items.quote: I would say 12% to 14% in Q4 as a topline growth is realistic.

items.statement: Management fee income expected to grow in high teens in FY27 driven by 60+ openings
items.quote: Management fee income is set to grow in the high teens driven by 60 plus openings. Yes, ladies and gentlemen, 60 plus openings in FY '27 and sustained asset light expansion on what we call a capital light model.

items.statement: Ginger and new business verticals expected to deliver 25%+ revenue growth in FY27
items.quote: Ginger and our new business verticals are expected to deliver 25 % plus revenue growth supported by integration benefits and scale efficiencies.

items.statement: Atmantan projected to generate approximately INR 100 crores revenue in FY27 with strong margins
items.quote: This property and this brand is projected to generate revenue of approximately INR 100 crores in FY '27 with strong margin characteristics aligned to the premium wellness positioning.

items.statement: Brij acquisition expected to contribute approximately INR 100 crores in FY27
items.quote: This will also contribute approximately INR 100 crores in FY’27 and provide IHCL with a differentia ted offering in heritage and immersive leisure destinations

items.statement: Recent acquisitions expected to contribute INR 250-300 crores to consolidated topline in FY26-27
items.quote: These transactions strengthen our presence in high growth segments including mid-scale, experiential leisure and holistic wellness while further expanding our portfolio, scale and geographic footprint. Importantly, these acquisitions are expected to contribute meaningfully in the range of INR 250 crores to INR 300 crores to IHCL's consolidated topline in FY '26-'27.

items.statement: Approximately INR 1,000 crores capex guided for FY26 including routine, new, renovation and expansion
items.quote: We are planning to spend approximately, we have guided on that before als o, approximately INR 1,000 crores in CAPEX, which includes routine and new, and also renovation or expansion

items.statement: FY27 capex expected in similar zone as FY26 with +/-5% to +/-10% variation
items.quote: I think for, we can only talk about next year, because we have more visibility on that. But broadly speaking, I think it will be in a similar zone as what we are going to do this year. So, maybe plus percent, (+/-5%) to (+/-10%).

items.statement: 30,200 keys under development, 80% managed and 94% capital light model
items.quote: when we look at the pipeline which is 30,200 keys under development, 30,200 keys is almost equal to the total number of operational keys that we have. 80% of our pi peline is managed, only 6% is owned or leased. Basically, 94% of the total pipeline is on a capital light model

items.statement: Ginger portfolio to reach 250+ hotels post ANK and Pride integration with 20 hotels signed for brand migration and 30 planned in H1 FY27
items.quote: Post the migration and integration of ANK plus Pride hotels, the combined portfolio will comprise of 250 plus hotels in this segment, significantly enhancing our scale, distribution reach a nd owner network in this structurally under -penetrated segment. We have already signed an addendum for 20 hotels for brand migration with another 30 planned in the first half of FY ’27 demonstrating our moment

items.statement: Atmantan margins comfortably above 40% for six months, expected in high 40s for full year
items.quote: Just to add with the margins, we kind of disclosed the six-monthly margins when we did the announcement. So, they are comfortably above 40% and for the full year, we expected to be in high 40s only.

items.statement: One-off expenses of INR 20-25 crores impacted Q3 margins, adjusted EBITDA growth would be couple of percentage points higher
items.quote: Should be around INR 20 crores to INR 25 crores, Prateek. Of course, we are on a, we have been on a journey of acquisitions. It obviously increases legal expenses. It increases technical expenses. It includes deal expenses, due diligence expenses. These are some of the one-offs and some others are related to GST.

items.statement: Favorable demand-supply dynamics expected to continue driving RevPAR growth structurally
items.quote: Favorable demand supply wil l continue to drive RevPAR growth. That is the core engine of value creation is the continuous growth in RevPAR and over the last few years the sector has benefited from strong demand tailwinds and favorable supply dynamics. Importantly, we believe this is not cyclical alone but structural change that is here to stay

items.statement: Q4 RevPAR growth expected at 9-10%, quarter-to-date comfortably in double digits
items.quote: it would be fair to assume approximately a double digit growth number. If not, then it could be 9, it could be 8.8 but I think with a bit of tailwind that we are currently having, we could get anything between 9% to 10% RevPAR growth

items.statement: ARR growth driving majority of RevPAR growth at 7% in Q3
items.quote: So, the majority of the growth is coming driven by average room rate which if we take everything together comes to 7% which accounts for the 9% RevPAR growth. So, 7% is ARR growth.

items.statement: RevPAR growth of 8.5-10% over portfolio considered realistic for coming years
items.quote: anything between 8.5 % to 10% over our portfolio is realistic.

items.statement: Q3 RevPAR growth 9% with Taj at 8%, Vivanta/SeleQtions/Gateway at 10%, Ginger at 9%
items.quote: Firstly, let me go by brand. At Taj is at 8% at a base of 22,000. In Vivanta, SeleQtions and Gateway is 10% and in Ginger is also around 9%. So, the majority of the growth is coming driven by average room rate which if we take everything together comes to 7% which accounts for the 9% RevPAR growth.

items.statement: Completed 51% stake acquisition in ANK, Pride and Atmantan; signed definitive agreement for 51% stake in Brij
items.quote: We have completed the acquisition of a 51% stake in ANK and Pride. We have signed a definitive agreement to acquire a 51% stake in Brij. We have also completed the acquisition of 51% stake in Atmantan.

items.quote: we have divested our stake in TAJGVK generating INR 592 crores in cash while retaining management contracts for all GVK hotels

items.statement: Gross cash reserves over INR 3,800 crores despite investments in owned assets
items.quote: Our balance sheet remains healthy with gross cash reserves of over 3,800 crores despite having built a few of our owned assets like Cochin International Airport Taj or Vivanta and Ginger in Ektanagar investments into our core assets and our trophy assets like London or Taj Mahal Palace in Colaba or Taj Lan ds End

items.quote: It all depends if you are able to complete by 30 or 29 or 31. It is very difficult to say that today because we are building a 164-meter tall building and a part of the construction is in water. You know, there are things that happen in terms of climate and other things which are beyond anybody's reasonable control.

items.statement: Taj Bandstand expected to contribute INR 1,000+ crores to topline with EBITDA margins close to 50% upon stabilization
items.quote: From a financial standpoint upon stabilization Taj Bandstand is expected to contribute INR 1,000 plus crores to IHCL's topline with EBITDA margins close to 50%.

items.quote: I want to clarify here that we expect a EUR 9 million to EUR 10 million of a business EBITDA.

items.quote: Our target in the next three quarters is to reduce our inventory in the range of EUR 30 million to EUR 40 million.

items.quote: rationalization of production volume in the coming quarters is likely to have an impact on the reported EBITDA due to the release of capitalized overhead or inventorized overhead in the range of EUR 9 million to EUR 12 million.

items.quote: the entire thesis of what we are looking at the long-term 3- to 4-year target, where we are going to deliver EUR 90 million to EUR 100 million comes a lot from assuming that there is normal sales going on comes from cost reduction.

items.statement: Target employee cost at 12-13% of revenue long-term
items.quote: our aim is to get to 12% to 13% of employee cost in the long run.

items.quote: Q3 quarter was a very tough quarter, not just for us, for the specialty chemical industry, very tough quarter and especially we saw big demand issues in Europe and North America.

items.statement: Customer destocking of Heubach-era inventories caused larger dip in acquired group
items.quote: The acquired groups saw a larger dip mainly on account of destocking by our customers as they had high stocks of Heubach-related products.

items.quote: customers promised that they would start buying after January, and we are seeing that already in January and early February, as I mentioned.

items.statement: Demand subdued but not down 20%; performance drop mainly from destocking not consumption
items.quote: customers' demand is not down by 20%, That's the big difference.

items.quote: The EBITDA on the acquired group, we saw a loss of INR38 crores.

items.quote: due to Labour Code, we had INR46 crores approximately of -- due to the Labour Code we had to make for One Sudarshan provision.

items.quote: We already have captured INR40 crores of this which we have realized in our Q3, if you compare it to Q1 and we also have a very healthy pipeline going forward.

items.quote: there has been a lot of improvement in the EBITDA compared to the last year, negative INR20 crores to the current year 9 months performance of INR4.2 crores.

items.quote: Whatever manufacturing footprint changes we wanted to bring in, we have already brought those changes. Frankfurt was to be rightsized, which has been done. items.statement: 19 manufacturing facilities in 11 countries across 5 continents; 55% footprint in Asia
items.quote: Altogether, we have 19 manufacturing facilities in 11 countries and 5 continents. This is a major differentiator for us in the marketplace and 55% of our manufacturing footprint is in Asia, which makes us quite competitive.

items.statement: Net working capital at 25.6%; focusing on optimization in coming quarters
items.quote: the net working capital is at 25.6% and we are focusing on the optimization of net working capitals going forward in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Inventory reduction of EUR 30-40M to generate operating cash and reduce net debt
items.quote: This is business positive as it will generate higher operating cash while reducing finished goods inventory. items.quote: In the short term, there will not be any immediate impact given that it would take at least 10 to 12 months until the agreement gets ratified by EU and India before the actual enforcement. We will continue to closely track developments to assess the implications and accordingly reevaluate our approach as required.

items.statement: Benzene price rise well covered; no Q4 impact; miniscule impact due to larger portfolio
items.quote: on certain raw materials, we do see increases. But I think we are well covered on the raw materials, and we should not see any impact on Q4. Secondly, with our larger portfolio, our dependency, the impact which could have, especially if you refer to benzene would be quite miniscule.

items.statement: Newly invested products performing well; demand better than regular products despite volume slowness
items.quote: I think the products on the newly invested are performing very well. However, albeit given the slowness in demand, we have not seen the volume, but we are still -- so that part has worked. In fact, we see a demand much better for that compared to some of our regular products.

items.statement: Customer trust rebuilt; local service teams created; technical marketing rebuilt; high stocks carried to ensure supply
items.quote: We've done a lot in this region. We've gained back the trust of customers. We've improved our customer service. Example, we've created customer service teams locally in each country. We've rebuilt our technical marketing organization. We carried high stocks for a long time to ensure that we are able to serve the customers well.

items.statement: Structurally advantaged with global footprint; 55% manufacturing in Asia vs global competitors
items.quote: We are structurally advantaged with our global footprint. As I mentioned, 55% of our manufacturing footprint is based out of Asia, which is a big advantage for us compared to any of our global competitor.

items.statement: Org structure streamlined from BU to functional; European management layers reduced
items.quote: As I stated, our org structure design is very lean, and it's a functional organization. Earlier, they were BU organization. There was a lot more management out of Europe, which has been streamlined.

items.statement: Worst is behind us; integration progressing; value capture on track; green shoots visible
items.quote: I'm glad that the worst is behind us. And we look forward and it was an industry issue and one must understand that we acquired this business, the transformation was going forward. And at the same, this subdued demand and of the industry didn't help us. So that's -- but I'm glad to tell you that, that worst is behind us, and we are looking forward to a very positive results

items.statement: Expect high-single digit volume growth for Imperial Blue in Q4 FY26 despite low to mid-single digit degrowth for full FY26 vs FY25
items.quote: Even amidst integration exercise, we expect to register a high-single digit volume growth for IB in Q4 FY26. items.statement: Expect high-single digit to low-double digit volume growth for combined business in FY27 followed by low-double digit growth over next couple of years
items.quote: For FY27, we expect a high-single digit to low-double digit volume growth for the combined business, which will be followed by low-double digit volume growth over the next couple of years.

items.statement: Expect consolidated EBITDA margins to expand by 150-250 bps for combined business over next 24-36 months
items.quote: In terms of margins, we expect the consolidated EBITDA margins to expand by 150 - 250 bps for the combined business over the next 24 - 36 months.

items.statement: Expect net debt-to-EBITDA ratio to go below 1.0x by FY29
items.quote: As highlighted earlier as well, we expect the net debt-to-EBITDA ratio going down below 1.0x by FY29.

items.quote: the steady-state margin of Imperial Blue before acquisition, which is around 11.7%. Now as per the guidance that I have just provided, we are looking at a 225 - 350 bps increase over and above that level, over the next 24 months or so.

items.statement: Overall volumes increased 76.1% YoY to 5.3 million cases in Q3 FY26; excluding IB, volumes grew 16.8% to 3.5 million cases
items.quote: During Q3, our overall volumes increased by 76.1% on a YoY basis, reaching 5.3 million cases. Excluding IB, our volumes increased by 16.8% to reach 3.5 million cases.

items.quote: For the 9 months ended 31st December 2025, the volumes increased by 40.5% to reach 11.9 million cases, and excluding IB, the volumes increased by 19.5% to reach 10.1 million cases.

items.quote: We have witnessed a strong growth of 90.5% on a YoY basis to reach a net revenue of Rs. 664 crore. Adjusted for subsidy, we recorded a growth of 89.2%. Adjusted for subsidy, the EBITDA grew by 49.6% to reach Rs. 90 crore, a 14% margin on the combined business.

items.statement: 9-month revenue grew 43.1% to Rs. 1,471 crore; EBITDA grew 50% to Rs. 265 crore; adjusted for subsidy EBITDA was Rs. 206 crore, up 28.5% vs preceding 9 months
items.quote: For the 9 months ended December 2025, our revenue grew at 43.1% to reach Rs. 1,471 crore. Adjusted for subsidy, we still clocked a growth of 39.5% to reach Rs. 1,413 crore. In the same period, EBITDA grew by 50% to reach Rs. 265 crore. Adjusted for subsidy, the EBITDA was Rs. 206 crore, a 28.5% increase vis-a-vis the preceding 9 months.

items.statement: Received Rs. 2,093 crore from preferential issue including warrant conversion by public investors; promoter warrants to convert in upcoming fiscal year
items.quote: During the year, we have received Rs. 2,093 crore as a part of the preferential issue. items.statement: Completed Imperial Blue acquisition on 30th November 2025 for Rs. 3,442 crore including Rs. 182 crore closing adjustments; EUR 28 million deferred payment due in FY30
items.quote: As disclosed to the exchanges, the consideration paid to Pernod Ricard was Rs. 3,442 crore, of which Rs. 182 crore was towards closing adjustments, primarily relating to inventory taken over by us and prepaid expenses. items.quote: With Imperial Blue under our belt, the distribution network now gives us access to 200 million+ cases opportunity in the Indian Alcobev market. Our strategy to lead the premiumization trend is anchored by dual engine, the strength of our existing portfolio and a robust NPD pipeline.

items.statement: Telangana dues a concern with increased receivables from government; actively engaging with authorities through industry associations for expeditious clearance
items.quote: We are on par with the industry. Of course, it has been a matter of concern in terms of the increased receivables, which we are having from the government. items.quote: There is clear roadmap to reduce net debt over next 2 -3 years as no major capex is planned.

items.statement: USA tariff reduction to improve profitability from US operations starting Q1 FY27 once higher duty paid inventory exhausted
items.quote: Recently announced reduction in the USA tariff will lead to improved profitability from the USA operations starting from Q1, FY27 once the higher duty paid inventory is exhausted.

items.statement: Specialty Chemical subsidiary posted Rs 52 Cr sales with 25% EBITDA in Q3 FY26
items.quote: The Specialty Chemical subsidiary has continued to achieve traction and posted sales of Rs 52 crores with 25% EBITDA in Q3, FY26.

items.statement: Rigid packaging business (Cosmo Plastech) reached EBITDA breakeven and close to 70% capacity utilization in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Cosmo Plastech (which is our Rigid packaging business vertical) has reached EBITDA breakeven in Dec 2025. The business has reached close to 70% capacity utilization in Q3.

items.statement: Zigly (Petcare) posted over 50% topline growth YoY in Q3 FY26; business model shifting to services and house brands
items.quote: Zigly has posted over 50% topline growth in Q3, FY26 on YoY basis. The business model is moving more towards services and house brands which is high margin business.

items.statement: Net debt at Rs 1,215 Cr as of Dec 2025, down Rs 20 Cr from Sept 2025; net debt/EBITDA 2.8x, net debt/equity 0.8x
items.quote: The Company's net debt at Dec 2025 is Rs 1,215 crores (Sept 2025 Rs 1,234). Accordingly, net debt has reduced by Rs 20 crores during the quarter. Company's net debt is 2.8 times to EBITDA and 0.8 times to equity.

items.statement: Expects Rs 200-250 Cr net debt reduction annually (15-18% per year) over next 2-3 years with no major capex planned
items.quote: Depending on the EBITDA level, how much EBITDA gets generated over the years, but we expect between Rs. 200 crores, Rs. 250 crores each year reduction, which translates to 15% to 18% of the reduction in the net debt position each year.

items.statement: Weighted average cost of debt between 6.5% to 6.8%; full impact of RBI repo rate reduction yet to kick in
items.quote: So, weighted average stands between 6.5% to 6.8%, depending on the mix between the foreign currency loans and the India denominated loans. But yes, we witnessed the reduction in the interest rates and full impact is yet to kick in.

items.statement: New 81,000 ton BOPP line ran at 70% avg capacity in Q3; reached ~80% in Jan; expects 100% from March
items.quote: So, see, as far as the new line is concerned, in Q3 on an average, we could run it at 70% of potential capacity, not as much because of orders, but there is a phase -wise improvement or speed increase that the supplier does. Post-February, we should be able to run this line at full output. In January, already there has been some more output increase from this line. We have reached now close to 80%

items.statement: From Q3 run-rate, can get 25-30% more output from assets; BOPP and BOPET to reach full utilization, CPP may take 12 more months
items.quote: First is from a revenue perspective, from what we did in Quarter 3, we can easily get around 25% to 30% more output from our assets. So, if we are able to fully sweat out the ass ets, there is a potential of 25% to 30%. The biggest potential is available in the BOPP line and the CPP line. BOPP line we feel that it will be fairly easy for us to reach full capacity utilization. CPP is growing at a g

items.statement: Specialty as % of total sales volume estimated to drop from 70% in FY25 to ~50% in FY27 at full capacity; target to return to ~70% in a couple of years
items.quote: Because of our new line, our Specialty as a percentage to our total sales volume is estimated to come down temporarily from 70% in FY25 to about 50% in FY27 once new capacities are at full utilization. Our target will be to take this number to about 70% in a couple of years.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty application filed for BOPET (PET) against China; decision may take 12-18 months; BOPP has no anti-dumping duty
items.quote: On the PET, the association has filed an application for anti-dumping duty because China has a lot of surplus capacity and from time to time they do dump goods into the country. Therefore, the association has put this anti-dumping duty application, and it may take some time because what we have seen is normally that it takes 12 to 18 months for the courts to decide on these matters.

items.statement: BOPP imports at 3,000-4,000 tons/month (mostly B/C grade); BOPET imports not significant
items.quote: Yes, so BOPP, there are monthly 3,000 tons to 4,000 tons of imports happening. That is also largely to do with the B-grade, C-grade material and some of the material which India does not make, but most of it is B-grade, C-grade. And BOPET also does not have any significant imports into the country.

items.statement: BOPP margins improving from December; January margins better than December; Q4 expected strong seasonally
items.quote: The BOPP margins have also improved. We started improving from December and right now, January margins are even better than December margins. So, yes, they are also on an improvement side.

items.statement: Window films business projected to break even at Rs 80-85 Cr sales with Rs 15 Cr marketing spend next year
items.quote: What we have projected right now is close to Rs. 15 crores of marketing cost next year and we expect that this business based on the current margins should be roughly Rs. 80 crores, Rs. 85 crores at which it should start to break even.

items.statement: Zigly demerger timeline maintained at FY27
items.quote: We have always stated FY'27 and we maintain that.

items.statement: India FTA with US and Europe positive for exports; JV with Filmax in Korea to grow over next couple of years; Japan phased approach, slower results
items.quote: Yes, if you really see America and Europe are the biggest export regions for us. And now India entering FTA with both, this should be quite positive in the quarters to come. Coming back to the third question, we have also entered a joint venture with Filmax in Korea. So, that is another region that we intend to grow in over the next couple of years. And similarly for Japan, Japan will be the slowe

items.statement: No significant capex or BOPP asset investment for next 3 years; focus entirely on specialty business
items.quote: Our focus now remains on speciality because we have added very significant capacities in recent years. So, for next three years for sure, we are not going to invest in any significant capex or any significant BOPP asset. Our focus will be entirely on shifting to specialty business.

items.statement: Specialty business growing at 10% CAGR over last 6 years; expects double-digit growth to continue with strong new product pipeline
items.quote: Specialty, I mean, the fair point will be to see at the CAGR growth, which in any case, especially we are growing by 10% CAGR growth over the last six years or so. And this is a very strong pipeline of the new products for the S pecialty. So, we definitely see there is scope for further improvement in the growth rate for the S pecialty at an overall basis

items.statement: Expects specialty mix to reach 65% by FY27-28 from 57% in Q3 FY26; target 70% in a couple of years
items.quote: Yes, that is what we intend to target. Right now , In Q3 FY26 we are at 57% . And our Specialty as a percentage to our total sales volume is estimated to come down temporarily from 70% in FY25 to about 50% in FY27 once new capacities are at full utilization. Our target will be to take this number to about 70% in a couple of years.

items.statement: Solar power project gains already coming; more gains expected in FY28
items.quote: We are already getting some gains from renewables, and some more gains are largely expected to come in FY28.

items.statement: BOPP demand-supply in India balanced in FY27; supply may exceed demand in FY28 due to new peer capacity
items.quote: See, as far as world is concerned, we feel BOPP will be fairly balanced. When it comes to India, FY'27 should be largely balanced. But FY'28, supply could be more than demand.

items.statement: BOPP margins expected to remain range-bound in Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27; difficult to comment beyond
items.quote: We can talk about Quarter 4 and Quarter 1, where it is expected to remain in a range -bound manner. Beyond that, it is difficult to comment about it.

items.statement: NSE listing targeted by March 31st
items.quote: NSE is equal priority and that's our next action to finish it by March 31st or as soon as we possibly can.

items.statement: Phase 2 capex INR395-400 crores, government co-financed
items.quote: So Phase 2 capex is INR395 crores to INR400 crores and that lineup will be -- we are currently in process, but we'll tie up that once we have this particular bank financing done for Phase 1 then Phase 2

items.statement: Epitaxy reactor qualification 60 days, commercial production 30 days after
items.quote: So the qualification period is about 60 days and then the commercial production about 30 days after that.

items.statement: First international shipment $20k to Richardson Electronics; expect volume orders after evaluation
items.quote: Last quarter, we did our first international shipment to a very reputed global dealer and there was a sample order of $20,000. Once that is evaluated, we expect volume orders from Richardson Electronics which is the one of the largest and the most reputed distributor.

items.statement: Q3 moderation from order realignment, higher material consumption cost, new labour law provisions
items.quote: Our Q3 numbers reflecte d a temporary moderation arising from realignment of certain orders due to customer -driven scheduling changes, increase in material consumption cost, and provision for cost due to introduction of New Labour Laws

items.statement: Q3 FY26 revenue INR20.27 cr, EBITDA INR0.86 cr, PAT INR0.44 cr, EPS INR0.06
items.quote: the revenue stood at INR20.27 crores, while the EBITDA for the quarter came at INR0.86 crores. Consequently, the PAT stood at INR0.44 crores, while the earning per share stood at INR0.06 per share.

items.statement: 9M FY26 revenue INR66.92 cr vs INR59.74 cr; EBITDA INR8.11 cr vs INR7.95 cr; PAT INR5.33 cr vs INR5.73 cr
items.quote: The revenue for the nine-month stood at INR66.92 crores versus INR59.74 crores for the same corresponding period. EBITDA came in at INR8.11 crores as compared to INR7.95 crores. Consequently, PAT stood at INR5.33 crores as compared to INR5.73 crores.

items.statement: Contract manufacturing in Taiwan/Korea under RIR IP for Silicon Carbide; first shipment to Indian Navy, second to international distributor
items.quote: we are making it with a contract manufacturer in Taiwan and Korea under RIR's name with RIR IP and selling it through RIR as our customers. So first shipment was for Indian Navy and second shipment went to this international distributor.

items.statement: New Labour Laws introduced; provision taken for cost impact
items.quote: provision for cost due to introduction of New Labour Laws.

items.statement: Expects industry-leading volume growth and margin recovery over next 12-18 months driven by US Class 8 truck recovery, domestic CV pickup, richer product mix, cost cuts, and lower interest outflow
items.quote: Looking ahead, recent government announcements on the tariff front, along with recovery in Class 8 truck orders in the U.S., augurs very well for us. Coupled with a pick up in the domestic auto sector, led by the CV market, this should provide a reasonable boost to volumes in the next 12 to 18 months.

items.statement: Targets INR 300 crore revenue growth in FY27 from FY26 exit level, largely from non-16,500 ton machinery
items.quote: As we have said earlier, we expect company to grow by at least INR300 crores in FY '27 from where we close out FY '26. So that growth will be largely out of the non-16,500 ton machinery.

items.statement: Expects interest cost to fall to INR 55 crore in FY27 from INR 80 crore run rate in FY26 via interest rate swaps, lower rupee rates, and bank negotiations
items.quote: We expect our interest rate to come down to the region of INR55 crores for the next year. Or slightly lower, but our target is, we are very sure that we will bring it down to INR 55 crores in the next year. From around a run rate of INR 80 crores this year.

items.statement: Targets INR 40-45 crore combined savings on interest and power costs in FY27, plus INR 4-5 crore from fuel switching
items.quote: So on the interest and the power fronts, we expect to save almost INR50 crores. We are looking at something in the region of INR40 crores to INR45 crores between these 2. And another INR4 crores to INR5 crores will come definitely out of other initiatives like moving over to PNG as against furnace oil, using LPG instead of furnace oil.

items.statement: FY26 capex planned at INR 175 crore, INR 137 crore already spent; FY27 capex expected at INR 150-170 crore (actual spend INR 125-175 crore)
items.quote: We continue to invest in the current year and expect to close the year with a planned capex of around INR175 crores, of which INR137 crores has already been invested. We continue to M M Forgings ... maintain a cap on net debt levels now, in spite of the heavy capex . Next year too, we expect capex to be in the region of around INR150 crores to INR170

items.statement: 16,500-ton press commissioning in FY27; full INR 300 crore revenue potential expected in 2-3 years (by FY28-29); minimal revenue contribution in FY27
items.quote: We expect the 16,000 ton press to deliver about INR300 crores of turnover, but that will take a few years to fill up. Right now, we would start with a few parts that are a struggle to produce on our 8,000. That will get moved to the 16,500.

items.statement: US export demand recovering: partial impact in Q4 FY26, full impact from Q1 FY27 as customers restock after inventory drawdown
items.quote: A little bit partially in Q4, and fully from Q1 FY '27 onwards. One set of parts have gone into production. Another set of parts go into production from February. So the full impact will come from March onwards. So effectively, I would say Q1 FY '27.

items.statement: Expects INR 50-75 crore incremental sales from US Class 8 truck recovery in FY27
items.quote: We would expect a INR75 crores increase in sales because of the return of exports, particularly the U.S. market. INR50 crores to INR75 crores.

items.statement: Domestic CV market expected to grow ~10% in FY27; company expects to grow considerably and has clawed back market share lost earlier
items.quote: Customers are talking of about 10% growth. If that happens, that will be great. But being a Tier 1/Tier 2, we are not the market maker, we are a market follower. So I would expect that we would grow considerably in the coming year and that 10% at least is very good news for us.

items.statement: Gross margin improved 3% YoY to 56.34% in 9M FY26 vs 53.57% in 9M FY25; expects to return to original 58-59% levels
items.quote: In fact, the gross margin went up by 3%. In fact, in FY '26, that is I'm talking about Q3 -- up to Q3 FY '26, it is at 56%, 56.34% as against 53.57% in the corresponding quarter, Q3 FY '25. Corresponding 9 months, it went up by 3%.

items.statement: Machining mix declined to 53% in 9M FY26 from 58% in FY25 due to lower export machining; expects rebound as almost all new orders are for machining
items.quote: Our forged and machines continues to be -one second -our forging is 47% and machining is 53% up to Q3 FY '26. And with the corresponding FY '25, we did 42% in forging and machining at 58%. So machining has come down by 5% and turnaround to forging has become 47%.

items.statement: CV share expected to converge to ~75%, PV ~10%, off-highway/others ~15% in FY27
items.quote: Over the next few months, I would expect the CV to come to around 75% and PV to be about 10%. And the balance 15-odd percent to come from off-highway and others. This would be what we would converge somewhere in FY '27.

items.statement: Clawback of domestic market share lost in FY25 after supply chain revamp; new PV crankshaft program started production in December
items.quote: A few customers were not very happy in the last year on our performance. So we did lose some sales up to Q1 of this year. Then we went back to them and found out why they were not happy with us and found that largely the reason was much better deliveries were expected. Since then, we have revamped our supply chain management and we have gone ahead very positively M M Forgings ... with customers an

items.statement: Power costs rising 5% annually per TNEB policy; shifting to green power to save INR 15 crore in FY27; also switching from furnace oil to PNG/LPG
items.quote: We have identified a few parties, we signed up with them, and we expect to save about INR15 crores this year, this year means FY '27, on power costs by shifting over from grid power to EB power. Sorry, grid power to green power, my apologies.

items.statement: Net debt ~INR 1,065 crore as of Dec 2025 (INR 550 crore long-term + INR 500 crore short-term); repaid INR 177 crore in FY26; plans to keep gross debt flat by borrowing only for capex equal to repayments
items.quote: We've repaid about INR175 crores, INR176 crores. Exact number I'm not so sure. But between INR165 crores and INR175 crores. So Balaji, can you fill in? What is the repayment for... Balaji Gopal: Yes. It is INR177 crores for FY '26

items.statement: Converting rupee term loans to euro via interest rate swaps (principal in euro) to match export exposure; repayment within annual export earnings
items.quote: We have also shifted our term loans with synthetic swaps from rupee to euro. We've done only -- it's IRS, the principal portion being left open. Sorry, yes, it's an interest rate swap with the principal portion being left open in euro itself.

items.statement: Sales volume 58,057 tons in 9M FY26 (56,756 tons production); export ~30%, domestic ~70% split
items.quote: Overall sales tonnage was about 54,000 tons. Am I right, Balaji? Balaji Gopal: Yes sir, yes sir. Sir, up to Q3 FY '26 we did 56,756 sir, 58,057, sir. Sales tonnage is 58,057. And production is 56,756

items.statement: US Section 232 tariff expected between 18-25%; India-EU FTA and US trade deal seen as positive for stability and export competitiveness
items.quote: To the best of our knowledge. We're working, talking to customers. They are also expecting it to be between 18% to 25%. If it is 18%, then we stand at an advantage to competition. If it is 25%, we are ready for it.

items.statement: New PV crankshaft program for Indian OEM started production in December after 1-year delay; volumes reasonable
items.quote: We have looked at, we are getting crankshafts for a PV customer in India. Akash: Understood. So that's a top 3 OEM? Vidyashankar Krishnan: Project was delayed by about 3, by about 1 year to have come last year, but now is coming / has come into production effectively from December onwards

items.statement: Domestic demand improved gradually across key segments, delivering healthy double-digit growth; export volumes remained subdued due to soft international markets.
items.quote: After a measured start to the quarter, demand improved gradually across key segments, enabling us to deliver healthy double-digit growth in the domestic market.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA increased ~15% YoY to INR 81 crore; margins expanded to 17.2%, up ~240 bps, driven by better gross margins from favourable product mix and tighter cost control.
items.quote: On the profitability front, we reported a strong improvement, with EBITDA increasing by about 15% year-on-year to INR 81 crore and margins expanding to 17.2%, reflecting an improvement of over 240 basis points.

items.statement: Capex for FY27 estimated at about INR 100 crore, similar to FY26; FY25 capex was ~INR 150 crore.
items.quote: It should be along the similar lines of this year, about INR100 odd crore.

items.statement: Chennai plant utilisation below 50%, expected to improve in next few months; overall utilisation ~70-75%, flexible packaging slightly higher.
items.quote: Chennai utilization is less than 50% right now but we are expecting some good improvement in coming quarters. Most of our audits and all are done, so it should start improving now.

items.statement: Margin expansion driven by favourable product mix and tighter cost control.
items.quote: This expansion was primarily driven by better gross margins, supported by favourable product mix and tighter cost control.

items.statement: Commissioned gravure cylinder manufacturing facility at Silvassa under Accura Technik, enabling backward integration, better process control, print precision, and reduced outsourcing dependence.
items.quote: I would also like to highlight the commissioning of our gravure cylinder manufacturing facility at Silvassa, established under our wholly owned subsidiary, Accura Technik Private Limited.

items.statement: Minimum Import Price (MIP) on virgin paperboard applies only to domestic use; exporters can import under advance licence and re-export without MIP impact.
items.quote: Yes, MIP is only applicable if the material is meant for domestic use. If you are exporting, then you can import in advance license and then re-export, there is no problem.

items.statement: US tariff reduction from 50% to 18% opens previously closed door; EU flexible packaging tariff (high single digit) to go to zero next year; UK flexible packaging tariff also reduced; benefits will take time to materialise.
items.quote: Because at 50%, you just cannot do any business or you can do just for the sake of like the customer waiting for the tariff to come down so he has been keeping you alive. But with 18% you can do business.

items.statement: Domestic business is quite diversified; not heavily dependent on tobacco segment.
items.quote: Yes, it is quite diversified.

items.statement: Constantly evaluating M&A opportunities but very selective; nothing to disclose currently.
items.quote: Yes, we are constantly working on something or the other but then we are very unforgiving in our assessments. So every time, it is not possible always but we keep trying, something or the other is in motion at any point of time.

items.statement: Board appointed Mr. Saket Kanoria as Chairman and Managing Director; Mr. K.K. Kanoria conferred honorary title of Chairman Emeritus.
items.quote: The Board has also approved the appointment of my father, Mr. Saket Kanoria, as Chairman and Managing Director.

items.statement: Cigarette tax hike creates negative sentiment for domestic cigarette business; volume impact uncertain due to inelastic demand.
items.quote: So definitely it is a negative sentiment for the domestic cigarette business. However, being a very inelastic consumption kind of item, so I am not sure, what at the end of the day the volume impact is going to be.

items.statement: Domestic volume growth low double-digit for both Q3 and 9M FY26; ASP flattish.
items.quote: So there is a low double-digit growth in the domestic volume.

items.statement: Domestic demand expected to remain healthy and be key growth driver, supported by policy measures; export sentiment improving due to trade developments with EU and US.
items.quote: To close, domestic demand continues to remain healthy and is expected to be a key driver of growth, supported by policy measures aimed at boosting consumption and strengthening manufacturing competitiveness.

items.statement: FY26 presales target of INR2,000 crores surpassed
items.quote: We have surpassed our FY '26 presales target of INR2,000 crores, driven by strong booking conversions in Ashiana Aaroham project in Gurugram, which contributed around INR767 crores in sales on launch.

items.statement: Q3 presales INR397.03 crores vs INR303.43 crores in Q2
items.quote: We achieved a sale value of area booked of INR397.03 crores for the current quarter vis-a-vis INR303.43 crores in Q2 FY '26, primarily driven by new launches, Ashiana Amaya in Jamshedpur and Ashiana Vatsalya Phase 2 in Chennai.

items.statement: 9M FY26 presales INR1,131.44 crores
items.quote: For the 9 months ended December '25, total presales at INR1,131.44 crores.

items.statement: Q3 PAT INR56.65 crores vs INR27.54 crores in Q2
items.quote: Profit after tax at INR56.65 crores versus INR27.54 crores in Q2 FY '26.

items.statement: Q3 pre-tax operating cash flow INR179.05 crores
items.quote: The company posted pre-tax operating cash flow at INR179.05 crores during the quarter.

items.statement: 9M FY26 pre-tax operating cash flow INR409.77 crores
items.quote: Pre-tax operating cash flows for the 9-month period was at INR409.77 crores, supported by steady sales momentum and strong collections.

items.statement: Karjat land acquisition 8.83 acres for senior living
items.quote: This parcel, we intend to do a senior living development here. Although 8.83 acres is generally not small for us. It is quite a common parcel size for us.

items.statement: Bangalore and Panvel acquisitions expected to close in 3-6 months
items.quote: I'm hoping that Bangalore and Panvel should conclude in the next 3 to 6 months and move forward in that regard.

items.statement: Active discussions for 2-3 more land acquisitions
items.quote: We are also in active discussions for 2-3 more projects, and we are hoping to execute a few more lands and get that going.

items.statement: Launch pipeline sufficient for next 12-15 months
items.quote: I think that's critical. So that said, for the next year, I think we are fine. We have enough phase launches that are coming up that will keep the momentum going for the next 12-15 months right now.

items.statement: Aaroham realization INR15,200/sqft; senior living floor price near INR7,000/sqft
items.quote: Q4 will be very heavy on average realization due to Aaroham's disproportionate contribution that has already been reported. Aaroham is at INR15,200. So I would not consider Q4 to be a trend. But in general, I would say realization should be going well, particularly in senior living.

items.statement: Senior living pricing improving; higher end INR10,000+ per sqft
items.quote: And the higher end going INR10,000 and plus as well, we're looking at higher end. So I think overall realization in senior living will go up, and that will also pull the realization in the company up.

items.statement: Strategic pivot toward senior living across geographies
items.quote: I think right now, our BD zone is more towards senior living. So if you see the last 2 projects that we have signed up in the company has been in Chennai and in Karjat, both for senior living and the pivot will become towards senior living.

items.statement: Senior living growing at 25%+ CAGR over last 5-6 years
items.quote: What we are seeing now, I would say, over the last 5, 6 years, I think more than 25% CAGR in senior living. We were earlier struggling to get volumes, to get pricing. And that has started changing for the company over the last 5, 6 years.

items.statement: Senior living targets different consumer base across cities
items.quote: Second, since it's differentiated, they are targeting a different consumer base as compared to a regular housing project in the same sort of location. So our Talegaon project, for example, targets consumers from Bombay and not just from Talegaon.

items.statement: Command premium pricing in Jaipur, Bhiwadi, Jamshedpur, Pune and Chennai senior living
items.quote: We command premium pricing across Jaipur, Bhiwadi and Jamshedpur. We command premium pricing in senior living in Pune and Chennai as well. We are the leading developers in senior living in those markets.

items.statement: Gurugram at mid-level pricing; targeting 10-15% premium
items.quote: In Gurugram, we are in the mid-level of price points. So we do not command market leader pricing. So in all these markets, we command market leader pricing in what we do. We are top tier in the micro markets we operate in, in those locations. In Gurugram, we are not in the market leader pricing. We are far off that. But we are also not in the commoditized pricing and generic pricing of every devel

items.statement: GRAP restrictions impacted Q3 construction in Delhi NCR
items.quote: Equivalent area constructed for Q3 FY '26 stood at 6.14 lakh square foot vis -a-vis 7.25 lakh square foot in Q2 FY '26. Q3 got impacted by GRAP related restrictions in Delhi NCR.

items.statement: GRAP considered in projections; slippages lower this year
items.quote: We do consider it, Rahul. That said, this year, the slippages have been much lower than last year. Only one project has slipped over, which is Anmol Phase 3. I think the rest, everything is on track to 1 quarter.

items.statement: No specific debt discussion; focus on cash flow generation
items.quote: Cash flow continues to be healthy, driven by better sales and collections.

items.statement: Cumulative delivery value FY25-30 estimated ~INR11,000 crores
items.quote: If I look at the total sale value of the projects under development and which has been delivered between FY '25 and '26, it's close to about INR7,200 crores already. INR6,840 crores for the ones getting delivered between FY '26 and '29, mentioned on Slide 16 and 17 of the deck. And we had over INR400 crores of deliveries last year, so about INR7,250 crores kind of there.

items.statement: Next year presales expected similar to INR2,000 crores
items.quote: Next year's presales numbers have not been calibrated fully yet. We tend to get it locked in, in March, generally when we do our planning. But I don't think it will be very much anything really higher from this financial year. We'll be in the similar ballpark in terms of presales.

items.statement: Target 20% ROE next financial year
items.quote: We expect to hit 20% ROEs next year itself. Rahul, you've done your math correctly. Are lower-margin projects there? Yes, there is, like Malhar Phase 2 would be a lower-margin project. items.quote: I think the long -term piece is building our people front deeper and deeper. I thin k developing our management capabilities in terms of our people would be the most important piece for us to do

items.quote: All the underwriting that we do is on 30% gross profit margin. But in all first projects in every location, there have been some negative surprises that were not captured into except for Amodh in Pune, where we had positive surprises actually in terms of the pricing we got.
