items.statement: Domestic automotive market saw strong double-digit growth in Q3 FY26 after GST rate rationalization in September; OEMs indicate robust demand constrained by semiconductor and rare earth magnet supply issues.
items.quote: The domestic automotive market witnessed encouraging developments during the quarter. The GST rate rationalization announced in September provided a meaningful uplift to customer sentiment, resulting in improved activity across the automotive ecosystem in quarter 3.

items.statement: Global markets muted in Q3 FY26 due to tariff-related volatility, seasonal softness, and degrowth in North America (-2%) and UK (-19%), Alicon's two largest export markets.
items.quote: In Q3 FY '26, the global automotive industry witnessed moderate de -growth of around 1% on a year -on-year basis. Within this, the market in North America was lower by 2% year-on-year and U.K. was lower by 19% year-on-year.

items.statement: Expects domestic revenue to improve 10-12% sequentially in Q4 FY26 without global exposure.
items.quote: Without global, that we are expecting in this quarter , you are talking about the quarter 4. So approximately, we can say 10% to 12% further improvement in the quarter 4.

items.statement: Targets EBITDA margin of 12.5-13% in Q4 FY26 and 12-12.5% for full year FY26; aims to reach 13% and then 14% EBITDA margin over time.
items.quote: In quarter 4 we are also expecting between 12.5% to 13% margins, so then overall at least around 12% to 12.5% margins we will close for this full year.

items.statement: Order book of approximately Rs. 9,100 crore to be executed by FY29; Rs. 850-900 crore utilized so far; exit revenue target of ~Rs. 3,500 crore by FY29.
items.quote: supported by the healthy order book of approximately Rs. 9,100 crore, strong customer relationships and disciplined execution.

items.statement: Secured 4 new part orders in Q3 FY26: 3 ICE, 1 carbon-neutral; 3 domestic, 1 global (German OEM eAxle housing); 3 CV, 1 PV segment.
items.quote: During the period, Alicon Castalloy secured orders for new parts from 4 different customers. Of these, 3 parts pertain to the Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) business, while 1 part has been secured under the Carbon-Neutral vertical.

items.statement: Won new business from 2 prominent Indian OEMs for critical CV components with series production starting FY27; 100% share of cylinder heads for a Japanese OEM's hybrid vehicles.
items.quote: During the quarter, Alicon Castalloy secured new business from 2 of India's most prominent homegrown OEMs for critical components on their commercial vehicle platform. Development activities of these programs are already underway with series production scheduled to commence in FY '27.

items.statement: Supply cylinder heads to 2 largest Japanese OEMs in India; one ramped up 1.5L engine cylinder head production for SUVs driving strong volume growth.
items.quote: We currently supply cylinder heads to 2 of the largest Japanese OEMs in India. One of these customers has recently ramped up production of a cylinder head of its 1.5-liter engine platform.

items.statement: Gross margin improved 138 bps YoY to 47.2% in Q3 FY26 on favorable mix and operating leverage; declined 170 bps QoQ from 48.9% due to mix changes and input cost volatility.
items.quote: On the margin front, gross margin improved by 138 basis points year-on-year to 47.2%, driven by favourable product mix and operating leverage. On a quarter-on-quarter basis, gross margin moderated by 170 basis points from 48.9% in quarter 2 FY '26.

items.statement: EBITDA grew 34% YoY to Rs. 47.2 crore in Q3 FY26; EBITDA margin 10.9% vs 12.9% in Q2 FY26 due to higher employee costs, translation costs, and asset write-offs.
items.quote: In Q3 FY '26, EBITDA increased by 34% year-on-year to Rs. 47.2 crore driven by operating leverage and improved product mix and a lower base in the corresponding quarter last year, which had been impacted by certain one -off items.

items.statement: Capex of Rs. 28 crore in Q3 FY26; cumulative 9M FY26 capex Rs. 92 crore; on track for full year FY26 capex of Rs. 125-130 crore focused on automation, capacity enhancement, and new program readiness.
items.quote: Capital expenditure during quarter 3 FY '26 amounted to Rs. 28 crore, taking cumulative capex for the 9 months period to Rs. 92 crore. We remain on track to achieve full year capex in the range of Rs. 125 crore to Rs. 130 crore.

items.statement: Plants operating at ~75% utilization; cannot directly correlate utilization increase to revenue growth due to need for new machines for complex/bigger parts; existing facilities can generate Rs. 200 crore with old systems.
items.quote: capex utilization, you cannot directly correlate with the revenues with the capacity utilization here because some machinery, some capacities are the Alicon Castalloy Limited’s Q3 & 9M FY26 Earnings Call Transcript common use, even we are having the orders, but the existing capacities we cannot utilize

items.statement: Metal price increases added Rs. 6-7 crore cost in Q3 FY26 (~0.6-0.7% gross margin impact); pass-through to customers sits in revenue and cost at 100%.
items.quote: if you see the metal prices have started going up. So, around Rs. 6 crore to Rs. 7 crore additional cost has happened. Maybe it is being paid by the customer, but it is sitting in the revenues as well as 100% as a cost.

items.statement: PV business grew 12% YoY and CV business 13% YoY in Q3 FY26; 2-wheeler business grew 13% YoY; mix shift toward lower-value 2-wheeler volumes and away from higher-value global CV parts impacted margins.
items.quote: As a result of these developments, the PV business recorded healthy growth of 12% year -on-year and CV business has delivered a g rowth of 13% year -on-year in quarter 3, contributing meaningfully to overall growth.

items.statement: India-EU trade agreement signed in January 2025 and India-U.S. trade framework announced in February 2025 expected to drive incremental sourcing realignment and new inquiries over coming quarters.
items.quote: On the external front, the signing of the India -EU trade agreement in January followed by the announcement of framework for an India-U.S. trade agreement in early February brings light at the end of the tunnel, and we can anticipate increased momentum now that the overhang is lifted.

items.statement: Europe offers incremental opportunities under evolving FTA framework; U.S. inquiries restarting after trade deal progress; China showing early improvement with potential easing of rare earth/semiconductor restrictions.
items.quote: In Europe, we see a more constructive medium -term outlook emerging. The evolving Free Trade Agreement framework together with Alicon Castalloy established footprint and long-standing customer relationship in the EU region positions us well to benefit from any incremental sourcing realignment over time.

items.statement: Finance costs declined sequentially due to improved working capital discipline and balance sheet management.
items.quote: Finance costs declined sequentially, benefiting from improved working capital discipline and balance sheet management.

items.statement: Depreciation increased 17% YoY and 3% QoQ due to investments in machinery, tooling, and automation per technology and capacity expansion roadmap.
items.quote: Our continued investments in new machineries, tooling and automation in line with our technology and capacity expansion road map have led to increase in depreciation by 17% year -on-year and 3% quarter -on-quarter.

items.statement: Hired CHRO, COO, technical and machining heads in Q2-Q3 FY26 to support new order book execution; added ~Rs. 2 crore employee cost in Q3 vs Q2; full year impact ~Rs. 10 crore.
items.quote: So mainly like we have hired the CHRO, COO and some technical heads, machining heads, like many people, senior level hiring has happened. So that will help us to execution of the new order book.

items.statement: UK OEM cybersecurity incident disrupted production for ~5 weeks in Q3 FY26; US commercial vehicle customer volumes down 25-26% in specific categories; European operations hit by Tier 1 supplier disruption linked to same UK OEM.
items.quote: During the quarter, a U.K. -based OEM customer experienced a cybersecurity incident that disrupted production for nearly 5 weeks, during which we were requested to temporarily pause supplies.

items.statement: 9M FY26 revenue Rs. 1,278 crore, EBITDA Rs. 153 crore, EBITDA margin 11.9%, PAT Rs. 11 crore; revenue exceeded Rs. 400 crore in 9 of last 10 quarters.
items.quote: For the 9 months ended FY '26, total income stood at Rs. 1,278 crore with EBITDA of Rs. 153 crore, translating into an EBITDA margin of 11.9%. Profit after tax for the period stood at Rs. 11 crore.

items.statement: DAR (Defence and Railway) vertical in nascent stage with RFQs in initial to middle discussion stages; dedicated technical/leadership teams and quality framework upgrades underway; revenue conversion will take time.
items.quote: Basically, this DAR vertical is right now in a very nascent stage. But yes, it carries a lot of potential in future. And it requires very tighter process control, traceability, higher certification standards compared to traditional automotive programs.

items.statement: Solar power meets 50-55% of total electricity requirements across India and Europe facilities, reinforcing cost efficiency and environmental responsibility.
items.quote: With the successful induction of solar power generation across our facilities in India and Europe, nearly 50% to 55% of our total electricity requirements are now being met throug h solar energy.

items.statement: Global OEMs increasingly evaluating India as competitive manufacturing/export hub; Alicon's engineering capabilities, quality execution, and scale position it well for structural sourcing shifts.
items.quote: global OEMs are increasingly evaluating India as a competitive and reliable manufacturing and export hub. This structural shift is supportive for Indian component suppliers with strong engineeri ng capabilities, quality execution and scale.

items.statement: Awarded EcoVadis Committed certification, placing Alicon in top 35% globally for ESG across environment, labor/human rights, ethics, and sustainable procurement.
items.quote: Alicon Castalloy has been awarded a committed certification by EcoVadis. This rating places Alicon among the top 35% of companies globally assessed by EcoVadis.

items.statement: Management aims to reach as close to full-year FY26 revenue guidance as possible, with Q4 expected to be the highest revenue quarter ever.
items.quote: We aim to reach as close to our revenue guidance given for the full year FY '26.

items.statement: Order book stands at approximately INR 2,100 crores, diversified across multiple states including Maharashtra, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh, and Haryana.
items.quote: We continue to maintain a strong diversified order book of approximately INR 2,100 crores with healthy representation across multiple states, including Maharashtra, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh, and Haryana.

items.statement: Ajmer KUSUM C order removed from order book due to slow traction; UP order reduced from INR 300 crores to INR 52 crores.
items.quote: Actually, the order from Ajmer KUSUM C was a slow -moving project and we are not seeing more traction in that, so we have removed it from the order book. Second ly, in the UP order, the final order they have given us is of INR52 crores. The remaining orders of INR300 crores were cancelled in a way and in its place, they gave us a new order of INR52 crores

items.statement: Q3 margins pressured by 4% lower realizations in Magel Tyala orders, ~2% raw material cost increase, higher employee costs, INR 4.4 crore one-time labor code cost, and consumption of high-cost Q2 inventory.
items.quote: Margins during the quarter were also impacted by several factors. These included lower realizations of around 4% in Magel Tyala orders, a continued increase of around 2% in raw material prices such as copper, steel, and solar panels, and higher employee costs.

items.statement: Export margins are 10% higher than domestic margins; management expects margin improvement as sales mix shifts to higher HP pumps and execution scales up.
items.quote: In export, there is always a 10% higher margin as compared to the domestic market.

items.statement: Solar plant backward integration expected to increase margins by approximately 3% and release ~50% of working capital currently locked in LCs and deposits for panels.
items.quote: Absolutely. That's why the investment has been done so that our margin increases by approximately 3%. And more than that, the thing is that we will be able to supply on time.

items.statement: Pump expansion capacity trial runs by August 2026; 500 MW module plant commissioning in Q1 FY27; 2.2 GW cell+module capacity operational by April 2027.
items.quote: Most probably, in August ‘26 we will be able to start trial runs and then full-fledged production. In our module capacity, there are two updates. One, we are building a 0.5 gigawatt Module capacity which will get commissioned in Q1 FY27, from which we will be able to start production. Second, the cell plus m odule capacity of 2.2 gigawatts we are talking about, the remaining capacity is expected t

items.statement: Planned debt of INR 400-500 crores for INR 1,200 crore solar plant investment.
items.quote: Because the INR1200 crores investment to be made to install the solar plant, in that we are planning a minimum debt of around INR400 crores to INR500 crores.

items.statement: Current pump capacity utilization at 60%, with 40% headroom available for execution ramp-up.
items.quote: Because currently we are only at 60% capacity, so 40% capacity is already available and we also see our execution on that line that we will be able to do a good execution.

items.statement: Maharashtra government sanctioned INR 1,000 crores and AIIB funds released; next tender of 100,000 pumps expected; execution resumed and ramped up.
items.quote: The Maharashtra government has already sanctioned INR1,000 crores and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank's sanction has also come. So, in this quarter, we think we will increase our execution further and we have already started and are trying to execute at an increased pace.

items.statement: Cash sales (non-KUSUM) grew 68% YoY to INR 66.6 crores in 9M FY26; dealer network expansion ongoing.
items.quote: Cash sales grew strongly during the 9MFY26 period to INR66.6 crores, a Y-o-Y growth of 68%.

items.statement: Export revenue INR 307 crores in 9M FY26 and INR 105 crores in Q3 FY26; retail exports grew 25% YoY; US tariff reduction from 50% to 18% seen as positive.
items.quote: Revenue from export business stood at INR307 crores in 9M FY '26 and INR105 crores in Q3 FY 26. We expect this segment to grow at a healthy pace for the full year, supported by the strong retail exports and expanding international opportunities.

items.statement: Trade receivables stable QoQ despite incremental revenue; collections improving with Maharashtra fund releases; working capital expected to improve by March as INR 1,100 crore state and INR 900 crore AIIB funds released.
items.quote: Even with incremental revenue recognition during the quarter, trade receivables remained broadly stable compared to Q2 FY '26, reflecting improved collections and tighter execution discipline.

items.statement: Interest cost elevated at INR 18 crores due to working capital utilization; expected to normalize by March but rise again with term loans for new solar plant.
items.quote: Regarding the interest cost you talked about, that INR18 crores will come back on that line, but later it will a little higher again. Reason behind this is that for the new projects that we have to br ing, some funds we have to borrow from the bank

items.statement: Q3 margin pressure due to higher mix of low-margin 3HP/5HP Magel Tyala pumps; higher HP pumps (7.5HP, 10HP) in other states and exports carry better margins.
items.quote: Actually, the margin history you are seeing in the last quarter s, in this, we installed more of 3 and 5 HP pumps , which were a part of the Magel Tyala orders from Maharashtra. Whereas in the other states where we supply higher HP pumps, there are higher margins

items.statement: Karnataka order ~37-38% of order book; MNRE advance funding expected to yield 25-30% immediate payment; execution tied to payment milestones.
items.quote: As per the information we have, is that MNRE has alread y given some money in advance to Karnataka. So, we should get 25-30% of the payment for the order we have got immediately from this money and some from farmer's

items.statement: KUSUM 2.0 budget allocation doubled to INR 5,000 crores (from INR 2,600 crores); PM Surya Ghar allocation doubled to INR 22,000 crores (from INR 10,000 crores); management certain scheme will launch.
items.quote: One is the allocation of INR 5,000 crores in the budget for KUSUM and INR22,000 crores for PM Surya Ghar. So visibility is there from both. Because in the last year, this allocation was INR 2,600 crores for KUSUM a nd INR10,000 crores for PM Sury a Ghar. So, you will see that the allocation of the starting budget has just

items.statement: Revenue target of INR 5,000 crores by FY28 driven by pump leadership, rooftop solar, EV motors, backward integration, and export expansion.
items.quote: In FY 28, we will see ourselves doing a revenue of INR5,000 crores. For this, we have planned all the capex, moved towards backward integration, new diversification, and will move forward in the export market.

items.statement: EV motor and controller development progressing; approved by JBM and other OEMs; sales expected to ramp in next year; benefiting from increased domestic content requirements.
items.quote: We have developed some motors, testing has also been done, and we have also started increasing varieties for our existing customer, JBM. We have also made some controllers for them, which have also been proven and tested. We have also got our motor and controller approved in a few other companies.

items.statement: Management pauses execution when payment visibility weak (e.g., paused INR 200 crore Maharashtra orders, previously left INR 500 crore Haryana order); prioritizes balance sheet over top-line.
items.quote: We have been saying this in every call and to everyone, that we move forward only when we have the possibility of payment. See, our whole quarter we paused because we wanted to strengthen our balance sheet. We want to keep ourselves in discipline.

items.statement: Raw material prices (copper, steel, aluminum, solar panels) remain volatile and elevated; dollar-linked costs pressure margins; DCR panel prices slightly decreased recently.
items.quote: Rightly said. As sir already explained earlier, that the price is becoming so volatile, th e Dollar is becoming so volatile, so in this, giving a guideline for the whole year is difficult right now

items.statement: No competitor matches Shakti's quality in solar pumps; management confident in quality-led competition if tender volumes shift to cash/non-subsidized sales.
items.quote: In today's date, no competitor can match our quality. So we see ourselves as leaders in quality competition. So we have no worries about it.

items.statement: Revenue book at INR2,389 crores and order pipeline at INR3,083 crores as of Dec 31, 2025
items.quote: As on December 31, 2025, our revenue book stood at approximately INR2,389 crores, providing strong revenue visibility. In addition, we maintain a robust order pipeline of approximately INR3,083 crores

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin improved to 11.9% from 10.7% in 9M FY26
items.quote: EBITDA grew 49% year-on-year to INR41 crores and EBITDA margins improved to 11.9%.

items.statement: No revenue guidance given per company policy; focus on improving product mix and annuity revenue to enhance margins
items.quote: So, we are not giving any revenue guidance. As per policy, we are not giving revenue guidance there. However, we believe that our continued focus is to ensure that we improve the product mix and have more revenue and annuity-based engagements and service engagements, which will improve the margin profile.

items.statement: Capex for As-a-Service deals funded via internal accruals and long-term leases; ROU asset of INR39.4 crores on balance sheet
items.quote: So as we mentioned, we are creating for all these As-a-Service projects. We are obtaining assets on lease. So when we obtain assets on lease, we need to create a RTU, Right to Use asset, which is what it has been created.

items.statement: Data center and cloud contribution grew from 14% to 37% of revenue; managed services and annuity revenue at 21%
items.quote: The contribution from data center and cloud has been steadily growing. Over the years, it has moved from 14% to 37% as we are today. With that and with the other annuity-based projects and the As-a-Service business that we are getting, we are looking to improve the profitability as we move along.

items.statement: Strong demand across data center modernization, cloud adoption, cybersecurity, and digital workplace driven by AI workloads and data localization
items.quote: Demand remains strong across our core offerings, led by data center modernization, cloud adoption, cybersecurity initiatives and digital workplace transformations. Data center and cloud solutions continue to be our primary growth engine, supported by AI workloads, automation and data localization requirements, which are accelerating enterprise investment in modern IT infrastructure.

items.statement: 35% revenue from global clients (Facebook, Uber, Amazon, Google, S&P, Gartner); BFSI largest segment; ICICI Bank a top customer
items.quote: If you see nearly 35% of our revenues, come from global customers. So, we have a suite of all the large global accounts like Facebook, Uber, then Amazon, S&P, Google, all of these are our customers, S&P Gartner. So, all of these are our customers and they are contributing nearly 35% of revenues to us. Number one. Number two, our biggest segment is BFSI. So BFSI 1s also one of our bigger segments a

items.statement: Debtor days increasing due to project execution cycles but net working capital improved via extended supplier credit terms
items.quote: So because of that, obviously these require a longer implementation cycle, hence the debtor days are increasing there. However, we've got very strong support from all the OEMs and the distributors there, which is why if you see the net working capital cycle has actually been we've been able to improve that over the period of time because we've got good support in terms of the credit periods there

items.statement: Input cost pressures mitigated via back-to-back OEM pricing agreements and productivity initiatives; no material margin impact seen
items.quote: We actively manage input costs and currently do not see material pressures that would impact margins. And this is due to our strong OEM partnerships where we have tied up with them for all these projects there. So, we have a vendor buy-in to all these projects there and we work very closely with them, which helps us mitigate the price volatility there.

items.statement: Order book execution timeline ranges from immediate to 5 years; average ~2 years; O&M component varies 30-40% of project value
items.quote: In terms of timeline, the order execution timeline ranges from some immediate orders to be executed and some to be executed over a period of five years, but an average timeline if you would put, 1t would be around two years

items.statement: Recurring managed services and DaaS revenue at 21% of total; multi-year contracts provide revenue visibility
items.quote: So, if you have seen, our overall managed services revenue is around 21% of our current revenue. Recurring revenues are forming a large and growing part of our business. We have a substantial base of multi-year contracts and ongoing services.

items.statement: Competitive edge from pre-qualifications, proven track record in SD-WAN, private cloud, core banking; able to bid against larger firms
items.quote: So, we Dynacons has a very good track record and good pre-qualifications to bid at significantly large projects there. Now these pre-qualifications enable us to bid against companies which are significantly larger than us.

items.statement: Data localization requirements accelerating enterprise IT infrastructure investment
items.quote: Data center and cloud solutions continue to be our primary growth engine, supported by AI workloads, automation and data localization requirements, which are accelerating enterprise investment in modern IT infrastructure.

items.statement: Continuously evaluating inorganic opportunities; will act when right opportunity arises
items.quote: So we continue to evaluate these opportunities as and when they come across there. Currently, the order book and the projects under pipeline are also pretty robust and heavy there, but we are constantly on the lookout there, and will act as and when we see the right opportunity.

items.statement: Nationwide delivery footprint and execution capability for mission-critical deployments; expanding AI-ready infrastructure and cybersecurity capabilities
items.quote: With strong execution capabilities, a nationwide delivery footprint and continued investments in Al-ready infrastructure and cybersecurity capabilities, we believe Dynacons 1s well positioned to benefit from India's accelerating digital transformation and IT spending growth

items.statement: 35% revenue from global customers; phased geographic expansion targeting APAC (Southeast Asia), then Middle East and Europe via partnerships
items.quote: As far as geographic expansion goes, we have a phased geographic expansion strategy. In the near term, we are focusing on India, because the India growth story is not only intact but is very, very strong there. So definitely that's our primary goal. Having said that, we also are looking, we will look at APAC, particularly Southeast Asia as our next growth there, where because we see a strong deman

items.statement: Lease liabilities increasing for As-a-Service assets; strong banking support for funding; ROCE expected to remain steady
items.quote: We are also utilizing certain lease options, so we are procuring devices on a long-term lease which collaborates with the revenue which is being generated from these devices. So, we are spreading this mix across both these areas there and raising funds accordingly. Keeping that in mind as business grows from this, we have a very good support from all the financial institutions, banks, and other av

items.statement: Quarter-on-quarter revenue volatility due to project-based execution; year-on-year growth more meaningful metric
items.quote: So, we would like to highlight that we are in a project nature of business there. So, our execution, the overall revenue numbers will depend on the execution of the projects. So, it could be completed in one quarter or it could be spilled over to the next quarter. We are not into the run rate sales where we are looking at quarter-on-quarter numbers there and quarter-on-year.

items.statement: Partnership with Cygeniq to enhance AI-ready cybersecurity services portfolio; addresses AI-driven security threats
items.quote: So this partnership that we have done is going to help us enhance our cybersecurity solution portfolio and build specific Al-ready cybersecurity services there, and offer the same to our customers there. So we definitely see a very strong, because you know today AI is not only playing a role in helping customers But it is also helping growing concerns there, because there are a lot of security att

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY26 revenue target of INR 1,150 crores with ~10% growth and healthy PBT; order inflow guidance INR 1,300-1,400 crores
items.quote: From a near-term perspective, we reaffirm our growth targets for FY '26, comprising approximately 10% growth in top line with a healthy PBT level and order inflows in the range of INR1,300 crores to INR1,400 crores.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance ~15% and order book target ~INR 1,500+ crores with healthy bottom line
items.quote: Further, as previously guided, we are on track to deliver revenue growth around 15% for FY '27 and an order book of around INR1,500 plus crores with a healthy bottom line.

items.statement: 4-year outlook FY28-30: INR 8,000-10,000 crores new order booking and ~INR 7,500+ crores concurrent sales
items.quote: MV Reddy and SG Reddy are very confident of giving us a number of around INR8,000 crores to INR10,000 crores worth of new order booking and concurrent sales happening to the tune of about INR7,500 crores plus over the next 4 years themselves.

items.statement: Standalone order book INR 2,226 crores as of Dec 2025; includes INR 1,477 crores defence PSUs/DRDO, INR 249 crores space, INR 369 crores metrology/hydrology, INR 130 crores exports
items.quote: Our stand-alone order book has crossed the INR 2,000 crores mark and stands at INR 2,226 crores, as of December 2025, providing strong visibility for the upcoming quarters.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 order inflow INR 476 crores; FY26 order guidance INR 1,400-1,450 crores; price negotiations concluded for INR 550-600 crores contracts likely to convert by Q4
items.quote: We have also concluded price negotiations for the contracts worth of approximately INR550 crores to INR600 crores, which are likely to convert into firm orders by end of this quarter. With the visibility, we remain firmly on track to achieve our FY '26 order book guidance of INR1,400 crores to INR1,450 crores.

items.statement: FY27 order inflow visibility INR 1,500-1,600 crores; split: defence ~INR 450 crores, metrology ~INR 120 crores, exports INR 100-125 crores, met segment ~INR 50 crores
items.quote: For the next year, for FY '27, we have a clear visibility to book order close to INR1,500 crores to INR1,600 crores around that. And in that majority programs, which, as I mentioned, like orders will come from public sector customers like BEL.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 standalone EBITDA margin 30.9% (INR 80 crores on INR 258 crores revenue); 9M FY26 EBITDA margin 25% (INR 165 crores on INR 668 crores)
items.quote: In Q3 FY '26, the company delivered its best ever performance, supported by margin improvement, primarily due to favourable revenue mix and strong order execution. Our standalone numbers for Q3 is at INR 258 crores with EBITDA at INR80 crores. Corresponding with the margin expansion, the EBITDA margin stood at 30.9%.

items.statement: Margins sustainable and expected to improve with volume growth; R&D projects also profit centers
items.quote: I must tell you that R&D is also a profit center to us even today. Therefore, either low R&D or larger R&D contribution is not going to affect the profitability? But as we grow the top line, I'm sure that there will be an improvement in the margins.

items.statement: No equity capital raise needed for working capital; bank financing sufficient; working capital borrowings will grow with top line
items.quote: I don't think we have to raise any equity capital as such to meet these working capital requirements. I'm sure that the bankers and other stakeholders will be more than happy to support the company. So we won't be raising any equity capital for the support of the working capital.

items.statement: Gross receivables high but 25% covered by customer advances (Dec 25); net receivables manageable; incremental funding cost ~2% of margins; inventory driven by long cycles, foreign content, MOQ
items.quote: advances for customers accounted for nearly 25% of the gross receivables. So our net receivables are accordingly reduced. And that brings the number down to a fairly significant level. And remember that these are sovereign receivables.

items.statement: Advances: 20-25% for development orders, 30% for exports, 0% for production orders; 20-25% for space/metrology orders
items.quote: Generally, for the development orders, we get an advance anywhere ranging from about 20% to 25%. Export orders, we get about 30% advance. Whereas for the production orders, we don't get any advance.

items.statement: Credit rating improved; prime bank reduced interest rate; comfortable with working capital funding via sovereign receivables discounting
items.quote: I must tell you that even with increasing numbers, of receivables and inventory, we have had a credit rating improvement. You would have read about it. And one of our banks has already -- prime banks has already reduced the interest rate, which has been charged to us.

items.statement: Shifted away from low-margin BTP export business to high-margin design-led products; domestic focus driving margin expansion
items.quote: As been mentioned in last few earnings calls, we are slowly moving -- moved away from the BTP business. Now more or less, except serving our joint venture, where, in fact, we have a fairly reasonable good margin. And as we do have a value addition in those products, so we are getting better margin.

items.statement: MOU signed with BEL for design, development, manufacturing of advanced systems; strengthening indigenous capabilities in defence tech
items.quote: To strengthen our relationship and be a partner in Make in India programs, we signed an MOU with Bharat Electronics to work together on design development and manufacturing of advanced systems with a shared objective of strengthening indigenous design and production capabilities in key defence technologies.

items.statement: Key Q3 wins: Doppler weather radar, software defined radios (~INR 300 crores); DcPP for EW suites for Su-30; qualified for Nayan, Medhas, Samudrika, Dharashakti production orders
items.quote: The third quarter has been particularly encouraging with high-value wins in critical defence and weather segments totalling around INR300 crores. This includes Doppler weather radar and software defined radios, reinforcing our leadership in advanced RF and microwave systems.

items.statement: Uttam radar AAAU and ASPJ pod AATRU qualification completed; LCA Mk-1A batch 2 RFP responded, negotiations ongoing; staggered delivery expected
items.quote: We have completed qualification for both AAAU of Uttam radar and also the AATRU of the Pod Jammer, both QT as well.

items.statement: Mission Mausam: 4-5 tenders expected over 2 years for weather radars, wind profilers, weather stations; execution 3-4 years

items.quote: We are in the concluding phase of developing a new 120 -kilowatt 220 newton -meter torque capacity transmission that will go on 4 models of one of our key customers in this

items.statement: Exclusive distribution agreement with Toyota Tsusho India for marketing to Japanese OEMs globally, also working with BorgWarner, Magna, Ford, GM
items.quote: Additionally, to further strengthen this relationship, we have an exclusive distribution agreement with Toyota Tsusho India Private Limited, a member of the Toyota Tsusho Group, which in turn is a member of the 17 companies that make up the Toyota Group globally.

items.statement: Transfer case volumes averaging 13,500-15,000 per quarter, approaching FY23 levels
items.quote: I think we are averaging now about 13,500 to 15,000 per quarter.

items.statement: Exports contributed 17% of total income in 9M FY26, progressing toward 20-25% medium-term target
items.quote: In 9 months of FY '26, exports contributed around 17% of total income, and we are progressing well towards our medium-term target of 20% to 25%.

items.statement: Japanese OEM transfer case program with SOP H1 FY28, prototypes ready and proof of concept demonstrated in vehicle
items.quote: We are developing a transfer case for one of their iconic pickup truck platforms with SOP expected to begin in the first half of FY '28.

items.statement: Recognized incremental financial impact of INR76.5 lakhs due to newly notified labour codes
items.quote: Additionally, during the quarter, the company recognized an incremental financial impact of INR76.5 lakhs pursuant to regulatory changes under the newly notified labour codes.

items.statement: Targets 25-30% YoY revenue growth across all verticals
items.quote: overall revenue that's what at a constrained level, we are defining that we are surely going to grow in all verticals by somewhere around 25% to 30%.

items.statement: Aims to increase retail contribution from 10% to 25% in 2-3 years
items.quote: Over the next 2, 3 years, we aim to increase our retail contribution from 10% to 25%.

items.statement: Expects retail share target of 25% achievable in 1-1.5 years based on current store performance
items.quote: As per our performance here in the current store, we are confident that it can be reached easily in 1 to 1.5 years.

items.statement: Targets PAT margin improvement of 25-30% from current levels once retail mix stabilizes
items.quote: in that case, obviously, we are going to achieve our PAT margin somewhere around 25% to 30% better than here.

items.statement: Incurred INR12 crores capex for 10,000 sq ft flagship showroom in Chennai
items.quote: The capex for the coming showroom was around INR12 crores.

items.statement: Expects showroom capex payback in 1.5 years
items.quote: capex part, it can be covered in 1.5 years.

items.statement: Inaugurated 10,000 sq ft flagship showroom in Chennai on 7th Feb, recorded INR20 crores sales in first 10 days
items.quote: I am pleased to share that our new 10,000 square feet large format showroom in Chennai was successfully inaugurated on 7th Feb. In the first 10 days since its opening, we recorded a sale of approximately INR20 crores.

items.statement: Targets INR500-550 crores annual revenue from new showroom
items.quote: in the upcoming years, we are planning to have a revenue of around INR500 crores to INR550 crores from the showroom.

items.statement: Plans to add a few more company-owned stores in upcoming year
items.quote: the management is planning to open a few more stores in upcoming year.

items.statement: Industry expected to grow at 30-35% pace, order visibility good for Q4 and early FY27
items.quote: The whole industry is going to grow at the pace of 30%, 35%, I believe.

items.statement: B2B EBITDA margins ~6%, retail EBITDA margins 10-11%
items.quote: our B2B margins are -- EBITDA margins, if you define, would be somewhere around 6%. And for the retail segment, these margins are around 10% to 11%.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margins to improve significantly as retail share increases from 10% to 25%
items.quote: since the EBITDA margin is at 6% now currently, so it is expected to improve somewhere higher 20% to 30% from here.

items.statement: Retail margins 10-12% vs wholesale 5-6%
items.quote: margins with regards to wholesale are somewhere around 5% to 6% and retail margins are 10% to 12%.

items.statement: Sees shift to lighter-weight jewellery (20-25% weight reduction) and lower caratage (14K) due to high gold prices
items.quote: There is a shift in the, what you say, lighter-weight jewellery for the marriage purposes. There is a reduction of, say, 20%, 25% in the weight range of the same product.

items.statement: Expects volume demand to surge if gold prices correct significantly
items.quote: Whenever we say a steep correction in the prices, the demand goes up. Sometimes it has even reached dual. So the demand will surely improve if the prices come down.

items.statement: Q3 volume growth 7-10%, revenue growth driven by value; shifted mix to higher-margin verticals
items.quote: we have grown on the volume base. If you take up, we have grown around 7% to 10% in between. But overall, the margins have been improved so much because we are working on the various verticals.

items.statement: Expanding natural diamond category under Vajraa brand gaining momentum with positive trade exhibition response
items.quote: Our expansion into the natural diamond category under our premium brand, Vajraa by Khazanchi, continues to gain momentum. The positive response at trade exhibitions and subsequent orders inflows validate our strategic move into higher-value categories.

items.statement: Top 5 B2B clients contribute 15-20% of total revenue
items.quote: the maximum top 5 clients would be contributing somewhere around 15% to 20% of the total revenue.

items.statement: Revenue primarily from South India (Tamil Nadu, parts of Andhra, Karnataka); plans to expand in South first then pan-India
items.quote: Since we have been in primary phase in South India, most of the revenues are from Tamil Nadu and some upper parts of Andhra and a few parts of Karnataka. Primarily, our presence is in South India.

items.statement: Stock rolling cycle ~50 days; expects similar cycle with possible 10% variation despite gold price fluctuations
items.quote: current working capital is -- that's what our stock rolling cycle is somewhere around 50 days.

items.statement: Plans INR150 crores inventory for new showroom
items.quote: for the new showroom, we have planned that we are going to take up an inventory of somewhere around INR150 crores in that, and we have started operating that.

items.statement: Uses natural hedging mechanism (refilling strategy) and exchange hedging; margins intact despite gold price volatility
items.quote: Yes, we have been using that regular natural mechanism as we have been operating with the refilling strategy. Whatever we sell, we buy it back. And if there is any extra orders, we buy it and we hedge it into the exchanges also when we follow that regular natural mechanism.

items.statement: Current working capital funded through internal accruals; future large expansions may require incremental borrowings
items.quote: Now as per the current requirements, all the fulfillment of working capital requirement has been filled by the internal segment. For the future date, if any expansion is planned on a bigger level, then if any funds is required, that may be planned accordingly then and then the management decides about it.

items.statement: Paid two dividends since listing 2.5 years ago; strong dividend policy to be defined in upcoming years
items.quote: Being a start-up company, we have just now been listed and it is 2.5 years, and we have defined two dividends. In the upcoming years, yes, the policy of strong dividend policy would be defined.

items.statement: Marketing expense planned at 0.75-1% of revenue for current year
items.quote: Sir, out of the total revenue for this current year, we are planning somewhere around 0.75% to 1%.

items.statement: No significant inventory risk seen in premium/diamond categories due to design variety and procurement as per requirement
items.quote: There are not much risk here because always, as we are catering lots of designs and patterns. And diamonds also, we are procuring as per the requirement. Higher quality diamonds are only sold in South India. So we have quality only. So in that case, we don't find any risk for that.

items.statement: Wholesale credit cycle only 2 weeks; cash-and-carry model with minimal credit risk
items.quote: Our portfolio type of business is primarily focused on designs and cash and carry business. Our average credit cycle is only 2 weeks. So we do not find any threat on receiving that.

items.statement: Demand environment mixed; healthy October but meaningful softening in December, weaker than recent years
items.quote: During quarter 3 financial year '26, the demand environment remained mixed. While we saw a healthy momentum in October, demand softened meaningfully in December, making it a relatively weaker December in recent years.

items.statement: Expect 8-10% overall growth in next couple of quarters supported by steelware ramp-up and glassware scaling
items.quote: We remain confident of delivering about 8% to 10% overall growth, supported by the steelware ramp-up and glassware scaling in the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: Margins to revert to normalized 22% EBITDA over next two quarters as steel volumes normalize
items.quote: As steel volumes normalize, we expect margins to revert to our normalized 22% EBIT over the next two quarters.

items.statement: Maintenance capex of INR75-100 crores annually; additional INR50-60 crores for writing instruments in next full year
items.quote: So maintenance capex is going to be at about INR75-odd crores -- INR75 crores to INR100 crores. Apart from that, there will be slight capex in the writing instruments.

items.statement: Opalware expansion capex of INR100-110 crores if pursued this year; maintenance capex INR10-15 crores annually
items.quote: if we do, there is going to be a capex of about INR100 crores, INR110 crores is what we look at if we are going to be ever doing it this year.

items.statement: New insulated steel bottle plant in Rajasthan commissioned; 2 lines operational, remaining lines phased through H1 FY27
items.quote: We have commissioned a state-of-the-art fully integrated insulated steel bottle manufacturing plant in Rajasthan. Two production lines are currently operational with the remaining lines to be commissioned in phases through H1 of financial year '27.

items.statement: Glassware operating at ~60% utilization; expected to remain at this level for next couple of quarters as sales catch up
items.quote: Our glassware business is currently operating at approximately 60% utilization. It continues at this utilization levels because sales is catching up.

items.statement: Opalware at ~85% utilization; no immediate expansion plans due to new competition, will evaluate after exhausting capacity
items.quote: So opalware is almost -- we are at about 85% of utilization at this point of time.

items.statement: Writing Instruments segment revenue INR86 crores, 11% YoY growth; expect north of INR500 crores in FY27 with Unomax and Cello combined
items.quote: In financial year '27, we expect combined revenues north of INR500 crores with the Unomax and Cello brand combined.

items.statement: Writing Instruments scalability target ~INR1,000 crores over next 2 years with both brands
items.quote: And the scalability of this -- both brands put together in the next few years is immense, and we are looking at a top line of about INR1,000 crores over the next 2 years.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin 22.1% impacted by lower steel volumes and INR7.4 crore one-time gratuity provision
items.quote: During quarter 3 financial year '26, the demand environment remained mixed. While we saw a healthy momentum in October, demand softened meaningfully in December, making it a relatively weaker December in recent years. Against this backdrop, we reported revenues of INR553.7 crores with an EBITDA margin of 22.1%.

items.statement: Consumerware margin temporarily impacted by lower steel volumes and glassware at breakeven; steel production expenses without revenue generation
items.quote: So two things. Steelware did not give the revenue. So there was a decline in revenue, which was a big revenue decline. So that is why the profitability was not reflected. Secondly, though we grew, a lot of the revenue growth came from glassware, which is not profitable at this point of time, right? It is only breaking even.

items.statement: No pricing actions taken; unable to pass on cost increases earlier; focusing on manufacturing cost reduction and optimization instead
items.quote: So I think nothing -- so no pricing strategy as such. In an environment like this, we are not -- as I had guided even in the first quarter that some of the expenses had increased, but we were unable to pass on.

items.statement: Premiumization mix increased to 7-8%, target 20% over time
items.quote: We have kind of increased the mix to about 7% to 8%. Over time, this, we want to take it to about 20%.

items.statement: Online channel now 15.7% of total revenues, gaining meaningful traction
items.quote: Our revenues now are about 15.7% of the total revenues, which is meaningfully gaining a lot of traction.

items.statement: Chinese dumping in glassware category; imports impacted by Cello's entry; opalware imports limited and inferior quality
items.quote: While the category continues to face some pressure due to increased dumping from China, the business has reached breakeven and is contributing meaningfully to revenue.

items.statement: BIS standards implemented January 2025 caused steelware supply constraints; 6-8 months stock built pre-BIS, now unable to import full product range
items.quote: Yes. So BIS had come in about last January. We had built a lot of stocks. So we had about 6, 8 months of stocks. And post that, we had also procured some products locally through some OEMs.

items.statement: Will tread cautiously with sharper emphasis on working capital optimization and inventory discipline over next two quarters, may temporarily moderate revenues
items.quote: On the working capital side, we will tread cautiously over the next two quarters with sharper emphasis on working capital optimization and inventory discipline. This may temporarily moderate revenues, but will strengthen our long-term stability and return ratios.

items.statement: Wim Plast merger final hearing last week of February; appointed date April 1, 2025; expect completion in 2-3 months, by Q1 FY27
items.quote: See, in the month of Feb only final hearing is there -- is around last week of Feb. And thereafter, once we get the approval, then everything is set, then we will be in the process of merging the thing. I mean already, as you know, appointed date is 1st April 2025. So definitely, it will be from that date itself. But maybe around 2, 3 months' time, we will see all that get through.

items.statement: No major risks foreseen in coming quarters; regulatory changes like BIS unpredictable; input cost risk limited and passable to consumers
items.quote: I don't see any major risks in the coming quarters. Of course, this is something I can't foresee. If there is something that happens like a BIS kind of a situation where there is a regulatory problem, then no one can foresee that.

items.statement: Opalware peak revenue potential INR400-410 crores at full capacity utilization
items.quote: So opalware at its peak can do about INR400 crores to INR410 crores of revenue at its peak.

items.statement: Steelware current capacity revenue potential ~INR300 crores; brownfield expansion possible with minimal capex
items.quote: This has revenue potential of up to -- upwards of about INR300-odd crores for the moment. And we can just keep adding lines. We have the facilities. So it will just be a Brownfield expansion, post that.

items.statement: Molded furniture growth guided at low single-digit due to direct polymer price linkage (62% of cost)
items.quote: And that is why we have always guided for a low single-digit number growth in the Wim Plast side.

items.statement: Cello brand acquired 2 months ago; revenues from Cello brand to start this quarter; rationalizing loss-making products from acquired portfolio
items.quote: We have been evaluating -- of course, we've just bought the brand about 2 months back. And that is why you'll start seeing revenues from this quarter.

items.statement: Management guides 25%+ revenue growth over coming years with EBITDA margin of 33-35% sustainable long-term
items.quote: Based on plant readiness, secured order book and customer demand visibility, we remain confident of achieving 25% plus revenue growth over the coming years.

items.statement: FY26 is transition year for stabilization; stable operating levels expected by FY27, maximum utilization by FY28
items.quote: We expect stable operating levels by FY '27 and maximum utilization starts by FY '28.

items.statement: Order book strong at over INR6,500 crores providing multiyear revenue visibility, growing quarter after quarter since listing
items.quote: Our order book remains strong at over INR6,500 crores plus, providing multiyear revenue visibility.

items.quote: Despite the initial ramp-up cost associated with the new facility and higher depreciation from recent capitalization of assets, margins have remained stable.

items.quote: For nine month we have capitalized plant and the machinery as we have mentioned that we have capitalized MHI, GE and Siemens plant during the last nine month which amount to around INR250 crores on the plant and machineries side.

items.statement: New plants for GE, Mitsubishi, Siemens capitalized and under stabilization; FY26 stabilization year, stable ops FY27, max utilization FY28
items.quote: The new plants dedicated to GE, Mitsubishi, Siemens programs have been capitalized. Each plant is currently at a different stage and under -stabilization, qualification of both facility and products while scheduling the customer demand.

items.statement: Strong demand from gas turbine OEMs (GE, Mitsubishi, Siemens) driven by data center power needs; wallet share still single-digit with room to grow
items.quote: So this demand is being experienced by all of our OEMs aggressively, right? items.statement: New contract progression with Safran and Pratt & Whitney for critical aerospace components; Rolls-Royce engagement started 2024, supply expected FY27
items.quote: A key highlight this quarter is our engagement and contract progression with Safran and Pratt & Whitney for highly engineered critical rotating aerospace components.

items.statement: Energy and oil & gas majority of revenue; aerospace & defence share steadily increasing for diversified mix over medium term
items.quote: Energy and oil and gas continue to contribute the majority of revenues. At the same time, aerospace and defence is steadily increasing its share and will play an increasingly important role over the medium term in creating a well-diversified business mix.

items.statement: Targeting 190-200 days working capital in H1 FY26, 140-150 days in H2 FY26 after supply chain optimization and discounting
items.quote: H1 as I mentioned that we are targeting around 190 to 200 days. We have working -- started working on that directions and the results are coming, but it will take some time to stabilize and it will take time to have. And for H2, we are targeting around 140 to 150 days.

items.statement: Indigenous jet engine development with GTRE at 75% completion; first delivery expected in couple of months (Q4 FY26)
items.quote: We are around 70%, 75%. We are -- as you ask me the progress scale, we are around 75% on that.

items.statement: US-India trade deal removes tariff concerns; products have long qualification cycles making them tariff-resilient regardless of rate
items.quote: These tariffs won't affect the products what Azad is holding because they are essential. items.statement: Long-term contracts maintain 33-35% margins; not pursuing short-term pricing gains from gas turbine demand surge
items.quote: In terms of the price, we are not seeing any -- so pricing decisions are not being done . And for us, our contracts are longer term where we maintain our 33 % to 35% margins and continue to grow on that front.

items.statement: IPO raised INR240 crores (INR180 crores for debt reduction); QIP raised ~INR700 crores funding capex program
items.quote: We raised INR240 crores in IPO but out of that INR180 crores were towards debt reduction. And hardly any capital from IPO proceeds was used towards building capex. Right? items.statement: QIP proceeds used for capex and debt reduction; balance sheet prudence priority while supporting long-term growth
items.quote: Balance sheet prudence remain a priority even as we support long -term growth.

items.statement: Stabilization of new aerospace/energy plants involves complex certifications, audits, workforce training; non-linear growth with execution risk
items.quote: Managing simultaneous construction, equipment commissioning, workforce training, certifications and deliveries is complex . However, our team has executed this phase with discipline and focus.

items.statement: FY26 operating cash flow guidance of INR100 crores
items.quote: I'm confident that we are on track to deliver operating cash flow for the year in the range of INR100 crores through improvement in EBITDA margin profile and initiatives being undertaken to further optimize working capital.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin guidance north of 4%
items.quote: Yes. items.statement: FY26 like-to-like revenue growth guidance of 30%
items.quote: So coming first to answer your question on this year, which I answered also previously in this call, that Q4, we can work out the math. And you are right in your math that to deliver 30% like-to-like, we'll have to grow 35% in quarter 4.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 gross margin 10.1%, up 30 bps YoY

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin 4%, up 30 bps YoY

items.statement: MedTech acquisitions to add 70-90 bps gross margin and 50-75 bps EBITDA margin pro forma
items.quote: Particularly in MedTech segment, we have added scale in IVD, Cardiology, POCT devices, lab consumables, etc. As I have already guided, post-completion and integration of all these businesses, annualized revenue will cross over INR1,000 crores in MedTech segment. items.statement: MedTech annualized revenue to cross INR1,000 crores post integration
items.quote: As I have already guided, post-completion and integration of all these businesses, annualized revenue will cross over INR1,000 crores in MedTech segment.

items.statement: Maintenance capex minimal at INR30-40 lakhs per warehouse
items.quote: Probably to do one warehouse, you would not need more than INR30-40 lakhs of capex.

items.statement: Net working capital days improved to 61 days like-to-like in Q3 FY26 from 66 in Q1
items.quote: On working capital front, I had shared during the last quarter that optimization remains a key priority for us. The same is now reflected in our net working capital days on a like-to-like basis that improved to 61 days in Q3 FY26 from about 66 days in quarter 1 and 63 days in quarter 2.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 operating cash flow INR49 crores vs negative INR21 crores YoY
items.quote: One of the most important key positive improvements t hat was reflected in operating cash flows with OCF at INR49 crores in the quarter. This is driven by our ongoing focus on EBITDA margin expansion and improvement in working capital management

items.statement: Net debt INR200 crores with cash INR250 crores as of Q3 FY26
items.quote: So net debt is at about INR200 crores. And we had cash of about INR250 crores.

items.statement: No equity raise planned; IPO funds nearly used; some debt movement possible
items.quote: So broadly, we have completed all the big acquisitions now. As of now, we are not looking forward to raise any equity capital. There could be some movement in debt, but overall, we are not looking to do more meaningful acquisitions from here on.

items.statement: Acquisition slowdown for next 2-3 quarters to focus on integration
items.quote: 2, 3 quarters, we have done some big acquisitions in this year. So we'll focus on integrating those with us. And there are a lot of other businesses that can grow significantly. items.statement: Pipeline of INR100 crore+ distributors available for future acquisitions
items.quote: Coming to your second question, how many distributors of above INR100 crores are available? There are many available. So even today, we have so many in our pipeline.

items.statement: MedTech to contribute ~15% of revenue post acquisitions; generics and private label low single digits
items.quote: So MedTech, I think we have given that post INR1,000 crores coming into our books, it will reflect almost 15% of our business. Generic and private label are still very small part of our business in low single-digits.

items.quote: So, in MedTech, we are doing demand generation also, which means higher manpower and more qualified manpower as compared to warehouse and delivery manpower in demand fulfilment business. items.statement: PharmEasy recovery not a major acquisition threat; many targets, few buyers
items.quote: In my view, that's not any much of a concern for us right now because when we started off, PharmEasy was acquiring businesses. And we were also acquiring at the same time. But even if they choose to do so, I don't see m

items.statement: New labor code one-time PAT impact INR6.1 crores; no recurring margin impact expected
items.quote: In this quarter, there is an exceptional impact of new labor code of INR6.1 crores on PAT. Adjusted for the one-off impact of new labor code, PAT margin was 2.3% with PAT at INR40 crores, that is a growth of 36% over last year.

items.statement: New labor code past service cost one-time; no material recurring margin impact
items.quote: So, what we have recognized under exceptional is the past service cost, which is a one-time cost. Going forward, we don't expect the numbers to materially affect our overall margins. We don't expect that.

items.statement: Business insulated from US/EU trade deals; domestic focused, minimal imports
items.quote: In our company, we are insulated from these global trade deals and all that because we are focused on domestic India market. We are not exporting anything out of India and our import component is also very low.

items.statement: IPM grew 12% in Q3 vs 7-8% prior quarters; Entero organic growth 17.1%

items.statement: Value proposition: 89,200 SKUs, 2-3 deliveries/day, 24/7 warehouses, app ordering drives wallet share

items.quote: So, in MedTech, we are doing demand generation also, which means higher manpower and more qualified manpower as compared to warehouse and delivery manpower in demand fulfilment business.

items.statement: Effective tax rate ~18% due to carried forward losses; will rise to 25% once losses utilized
items.quote: So currently, we have certain losses available to us carry forward losses on account of which currently you are seeing the effective tax rate at about 18%. As and when those losses get completely consumed, the tax rate obviously will slowly go up a bit. But for this financial year, we are holding on to our 18% of effective tax rate.

items.statement: FY27 expected to be far better than FY26 due to full-year impact of H2 FY26 acquisitions
items.quote: FY27 is going to be far better than FY26, given the fact that a lot of work we have done in the second half of FY26 is going to have a full year impact for next year.

items.statement: Revenue target to double every 3-4 years; FY26 expected over INR900-950 crores; FY27 similar growth
items.quote: our internal targets are that every three to four years max we want to double our revenues. So last year we closed with about INR857 crores of top line. items.quote: currently utilization would be in the late 70s of the achievable capacity and we've always mentioned that our target is to be in the 80% to 85% range, 85% to 90% max is what we like to do
