Almost all our projects which we have won is within Rs.100 crores, that single project cost. So, we wi ll be having 12-months of execution timeline.

items.statement: Existing order book sufficient for 2-2.5 years of revenue visibility
items.quote: Yes, our existing order book should be sufficient for next two to two and a half years. But we will not remain stayed in that sphere. We will try to capture new orders also…incremental orders will come into our order book.

items.statement: Q3 revenue moderated due to monsoon delays and government billing cycles; 9M FY26 revenue grew 30.8% YoY to Rs.1,950.67M
items.quote: In the year '25-26, for the nine-months ended period, our year-on-year growth when compared to '24-25 has increased by 30.8% and we have clocked revenue of around Rs.1,950.67 million in this nine-months period.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 revenue Rs.535.2M vs Rs.513.53M in Q3 FY25 (~4% YoY growth)
items.quote: In the last year's third quarter, we had clocked Rs.513.53 million. And in this third quarter, we have clocked Rs.535.20 million. When compared to our order book and our execution of the projects, we hope to achieve very good, healthy revenue in next quarter and in the coming quarters.

items.statement: 9M FY26 EBITDA rose 34.02% YoY to Rs.708.47M on better project mix and cost control
items.quote: Our EBITDA is healthy and it is increasing and it has incr eased by 34.02% on absolute terms when compared year-on-year to Rs.708.47 million when compared to Rs.528.60 million in nine-months period ending financial year '24-25.

items.statement: Q3 margins improved due to better project mix, execution efficiency, cost control and focus on higher-margin water infra projects
items.quote: However, our margins have got improved due to better project mix, improved execution, efficiency, greater cost control and focus on higher margin water infrastructure project.

items.statement: Working capital cycle currently 95-120 days; expected to improve in Q4 FY26
items.quote: It will be 9 5-to-120-days with our working cycle period. And our working cycle situation will improve in Q4 of FY25-26 further.

items.statement: Monitoring agency reports Rs.169.51 crore outstanding; ~Rs.65 crore expected to convert to Q4 revenue
items.quote: I think approximately around Rs.65 crores, we are expecting it to be converted into revenue fo r the fourth quarter.

items.statement: Company nearly debt-free; only non-fund-based facilities (bank guarantees) used; credit limits sanctioned from Kotak and SBI for future projects
items.quote: We are almost debt-free company except for some non-fund-based bank facilities, which we have obtained in our execution of the work.

items.statement: Future debt raise limited to non-fund-based instruments (bank guarantees) for project performance security
items.quote: We will utilize mainly first non-fund based financial instrument like bank guarantee.

items.statement: No major capex disclosed; focus on project execution and bidding for Rs.100-300 crore projects
items.quote: Right now, we are searching for the projects between Rs.100 crores to Rs.300 crores, that is Rs.1,000 million to Rs.3,000 million.

items.statement: Key Karnataka competitors: SNC, Amrutha, Brindavan, Srinivasa Constructions; limited competition in groundwater recharge niche
items.quote: Right now, in the State of Karnataka, there are not many in the listed space. There are quite a few players , who do similar type of work, like SNC Construction Company, Amrutha Construction Company, and Brindavan Construction s and Srinivasa Construction s who do execute project similar to the projects which we are handling.

items.statement: Geographic concentration in Karnataka; actively bidding outside state but no orders yet
items.quote: As on today, we are trying to bid for projects outside Karnataka. In our order book only , right now, Karnataka-based projects are in pipeline.

items.statement: Union Budget infrastructure allocation positive; expected to drive tender flow across states
items.quote: Yes, I think they have ann ounced very good investment for infrastructure space. And that translates into healthy invitation of the tenders across the various states where we are interested and we want to capture those orders also.

items.statement: Rs.400 crore Karnataka Mining Environment Restoration Fund projects delayed; tender notification pending committee clearance
items.quote: It is before some committees which has to clear the projects and we are continuously following it up. Tender notification is yet to be issued. We hope to get the tender notification issued early.

items.statement: Revenue recognition dependent on government project milestones and billing cycles causing quarterly volatility
items.quote: Ours is a water -based infra solution project implementation company and it depends on project milestone and it depends on project milestone timing and billing in certain government projects.

items.statement: Water sector structural growth driven by 135-150 LPCD supply norms, 24/7 water supply upgrades, and 1 in 3 Indians lacking quality water access
items.quote: For your kind information, some survey shows that for every three people who are residing in India, one people are not getting good quality, proper water supply. There is a lot of gap to be covered, which presents a very rosy picture for a company like Denta, which is mainly into water-based infra solution.

items.statement: End-to-end water solutions: source procurement, treatment, supply, sewage collection, treatment, groundwater recharge
items.quote: In this way, our company has got unique d istinction of having serving from procurement of water, treatment of the same, collecting the wastewater , which is generated, treating it , and giving it back to the nature.

items.statement: Expects FY26 PAT margin of 9-10% on consolidated revenue of Rs.790-810 crore
items.quote: We still expect to end the year with a PAT of 9-10% on the revenues of between Rs.790 crore to Rs.810, crores.

items.statement: Revised FY26 consolidated revenue guidance to Rs.775-800 crore from earlier Rs.860 crore
items.quote: I expect anywhere between Rs.775-800 crore as our consolidated revenue for the year, with revenue drop being maximum for export on Jash Engineering Limited account of Rodney Hunt

items.statement: Targets Rs.950 crore+ revenue by FY27 with US revenue of $45-50 million
items.quote: So, we are quite confident of Rs.950 crores plus. Let's see how this 18% ratification is done when it is done. But I feel with all these initiatives which we have taken, we should be in striking distance of the same.

items.statement: Consolidated order book at Rs.923 crore as of Feb 1 (Rs.653 crore overseas, Rs.270 crore domestic)
items.quote: As of first February, our order book is close to Rs.923 crores, which is reasonable growth over last year. And I think that we are on the right track.

items.statement: US order book stands at $42 million
items.quote: So this year was bad because of the US tariff, but now the order book in US is $42 million so it is only about our starting production.

items.statement: New SEZ Pithampur plant ready for commercial production from April 2026
items.quote: I am pleased to announce that our new plan t at SEZ Pithampur is ready. It will go on commercial production from the beginning of April

items.statement: Houston plant construction to start June-July 2026, commissioning before September 2027
items.quote: We would be able to get his pricing in this month and we will negotiate a new order with him next month and we expect to start in June, July, the construction and commission the plan next year, before September.

items.statement: Saudi Arabia plant setup underway; land application in progress, expects Rs.20-30 crore revenue in first year
items.quote: See, in the first year beginning, we don't expect more than Rs.20-25-30 crores. But slowly we are expecting Rs.100 crore revenue from that company.

items.statement: Westech acquisition completed; Penstock UK acquisition nearing closure by February-March 2026
items.quote: The Westech acquisition is already done, and the Penstock UK acquisition is also on the verge of closure. If everything goes well, you should be able to do it within February, if not, then in March 26.

items.statement: Westech acquisition cost Rs.30 crore; Penstock UK expected at Rs.5-6 crore
items.quote: So, we have almost spent Rs.30 crore in the West ech deal , how much expected in the Penstock UK. Pratik Patel: Rs.5-6

items.statement: Gross margin decline due to tariff costs paid from pocket, not revenue drop
items.quote: Not because of the drop in US sale. It is also because I paid the tariff from my pocket. It is a cost

items.statement: Expects operating margin of 20-24% and PAT margin of 12-14% in FY27 if conditions normalize
items.quote: Yes, if everything works out, it should happen like that. I will tell you one thing, I cannot forecast the future so accurately today, but there is a good possibility because those projects which were taken considering 50% tariff will now go at 25-18%.

items.statement: US revenue dropped to Rs.35 crore in 9M FY26 from $36M last year; expects $29M in FY26
items.quote: year we did $36 million revenue in America, this $36 million will come down this year to something like $29 million. A $7 Jash Engineering Limited million drop because of this problem

items.statement: Domestic revenue grew to offset US export decline; India target 40-45% of revenue mix
items.quote: We would like something like this to be in the future that India is around 40-45%, America is around 35% and balance is coming from other territories.

items.statement: Forex gain of Rs.4-5 crore in 9M FY26 partially offset tariff impact
items.quote: In our balance sheet, you can see the foreign exchange gain. It is around Rs.4-5 crores for this 9 months.

items.statement: Two consignments cleared at 25% tariff; expects 18% after deal ratification
items.quote: Last week we have already cleared two consignments at 25% tariff rate and we were informed by the submitters that once the ratification of the deal is done, then we should be able to clear at 18%.

items.statement: Pithampur three plants capacity Rs.300-400 crore; new SEZ plant adds spare capacity
items.quote: This is the third plant in Pithampur and with these three plants done, the Pithampur plants have reached a capability of anywhere between Rs.300-400 crore, depending upon what is the pickup of the material which is ready.

items.statement: New products: Surge Vessel (Bladder type), Twin Screw Conveyors for Sludge Handling; strong in desalination gates
items.quote: We have also developed a Surge Vessel – Bladder type as well as Twin Screw Conveyors for Sludge Handling. All these new product developments will go a long way in increasing our revenue in future.

items.statement: Disc filter opportunity estimated at Rs.20-25 crore domestic and export combined
items.quote: We make small disc filters, and we expect domestic and export to together Rs.20-25 crores worth of business.

items.statement: NPCIL qualification strengthens domestic nuclear prospects; no export benefit
items.quote: NPCIL experience will not go outside India. Means, when you work for NPCIL, that will not get my business outside India, but it will definitely get Jash Engineering Limited me lot of business within India

items.statement: Stage-wise payments (10-15-20% advance, 30-35% at inspection) mitigate raw material price risk
items.quote: However, please understand that we have stage wise payment. So, we get 10-15-20% advance and then balance 30-35% by the time the material is ready for inspection.

items.statement: Shivpad quality issues resolved by sending 10 trained personnel from Indore from Feb 1
items.quote: First 10 people have already started working in Shivpad from first of February and slowly we will set up the complete team in Shiv pad through trained people sent from Indore.

items.statement: Tariff uncertainty caused order delays globally; Vietnam shipment delayed but now moving
items.quote: Every market has gone through trouble once tariff hit. Because tariff boils the market confidence and sentiments and so everywhere things had slowed down, whether it is Vietnam or whether it is Hong Kong or Singapore.

items.statement: ONM business remains 5-10% of revenue; gate replacement cycle 25-30 years
items.quote: So, ONM business is not big for us. It is 5-10% however, what is the life is 25-30 years, or sometimes faster.

items.statement: Order book provides 100% revenue coverage through FY2028 and supports double-digit CAGR over next three years
items.quote: order book provides full 100% revenue coverage through FY 2028 and supports a clear double-digit CAGR visibility over the next three years, therefore vastly outperforming the market

items.statement: Exports now contribute over 20% of total order book, well diversified across Clean Air, Powertrain and Advanced Ride Technologies
items.quote: Our order book remains very strong and well diversified with exports now contributing to over 20% of the total order book.

items.statement: DaVinci DCx suspension program with leading Indian OEM has estimated annual revenue potential of INR2,200 million
items.quote: With an estimated annual revenue potential of around INR2,200 million for this one program alone, this win demonstrates our ability to translate mechanical innovation into scalable customer relevant solutions.

items.statement: Clean Air program win with global commercial vehicle OEM has estimated annual revenue potential of INR1,150 million
items.quote: Alongside this win, we also secured a strategic Clean Air program win with a leading global commercial vehicle OEM based on a modular in -line BS6 aftertreatment system with an estimated annual revenue potential of around INR1,150 million.

items.statement: Board approved greenfield plant in Kharkhoda, Haryana with INR710 million capex, production start estimated Q3 FY27
items.quote: Our Board has approved to develop a greenfield plant in North India, namely in Kharkhoda , Haryana, to strengthen proximity to the northern customer base and to support awarded programs across light vehicles, off-highway, and tractor segments. This project envisages INR710 million capex with an estimated start of production in Q3 FY27.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization over 90%, up from 80%, driving need for capacity expansion
items.quote: We were operating at about 80% of the capacity and today with the volumes that we have, we are at about more than 90% of the capacity utilization.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin at 18.6% of value added revenue, up 24.8% YoY, driven by operating leverage and cost management
items.quote: EBITDA for the Q3FY26 was INR2,225 million, a healthy 24.8% year-on-year increase with EBITDA margins at 18.6% of value added revenue.

items.statement: 9M FY26 EBITDA margin at 19% of value added revenue, up 12% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA for the 9MFY26 stood at INR6,682 million, up by 12% year -on-year, while EBITDA margins at 19% of value added revenue supported by operating leverage, commercial actions and disciplined cost management.

items.statement: Strong demand for DaVinci DCx suspension from multiple Indian, Japanese and Korean OEMs
items.quote: The demand is fast and furious. Everybody recognizes that this is a game changer. So it's just not it's Mahindra, it's obviously many other, Indian and also Japanese, Korean OEMs, every everybody is interested in this technology.

items.statement: DaVinci DCx suspension offers near semi-active performance at minimal cost delta versus conventional shocks
items.quote: That delta cost is literally the cost of a dinner for two at a five star hotel. I mean that that's what we're talking about here. So it is very affordable I think from an OEM standpoint, but in return for just that cost, you have now a much, much better performing suspension system.

items.statement: US tariff reduction from 50% to 18% and EU tariff reduction from 3-8% to zero will strongly improve export competitiveness
items.quote: New tariff and duty reduction announcements by the US and EU will strongly improve the tailwinds to allow us to grow our exports further. We're talking about 50% tariffs down to 18% for the US and 3% to 8% range to zero for the EU.

items.statement: Export order book currently led by Asia, followed by US and Europe, but recent bookings balancing mix
items.quote: Right now, what we've booked so far you could say it's a good mix with Asia being the leading destination followed by US and Europe. But I think looking just at what we have order booked just in the last let's say few weeks, it it's going to probably balance out much better.

items.statement: ROCE exceeds 80% for 9M FY26, reflecting disciplined execution and efficient capital deployment
items.quote: From a capital efficiency perspective, returns remain strong with return on capital employed exceeding 80% for the 9MFY26, reflecting disciplined execution, efficient capital deployment and robust operating cash generation.

items.statement: Negative cash conversion cycle and effective working capital management support healthy balance sheet
items.quote: Our balance sheet metrics continue to remain healthy, supported by negative cash conversion cycle and effective working capital management.

items.statement: No pushback seen on CAFE 3 or TREM 5 norms; OEMs pulling for faster compliance to support export competitiveness
items.quote: We're not seeing that . We're seeing that OEMs really want to get ahead of the curve. And there's one main reason for that. And the reason for that is exports, right? OEMs are also very, very interested in exporting to South Africa, to back to Asia, to Japan, to Europe and so on.

items.statement: Advanced Ride Technologies grew 24.5% YoY in Q3 FY26 vs Clean Air & Powertrain at 5.4% YoY
items.quote: Clean Air and Powertrain solutions recorded revenue of INR5,644 million, growing at the rate of 5.4%, while Advanced Ride Technologies delivered INR6,297 million, growing at the rate of 24.5%, supported by strong suspension demand and the program ramp -ups.

items.statement: Continuous improvement culture with 200,000+ ideas implemented over 3 years driving 400bps EBITDA margin improvement
items.quote: Just in India alone there were 200,000 ideas that went and of course some got rejected, some went in. So that kind of new continuous improvement culture has become part of our DNA.

items.statement: FY26 capex includes INR710 million Kharkhoda plant; FY27 capex guidance to be shared later
items.quote: For FY27 we are working on the kind of budgets and on the assumptions and we would soon be sharing that guidance about the next year capex plans.

items.statement: US policy shift revoking EV subsidies and emission standards seen as positive for ICE/hybrid exports
items.quote: This is great news for us because the whole point of Apollo's takeover of Tenneco three , four years ago was the contrarian strategy that EV is not going to completely rule the world and destroy everybody.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 15-20% for FY26, aiming for 20%
items.quote: my guidance is we should look at anything between 15% to 20%. 20% is what we are aiming for.

items.statement: Current order book stands at INR16,300 crores with 68% Rail & Metro, 25% Defense, 7% Mining & Construction
items.quote: the current order book that we have is more than INR16,000 crores -- in fact, it is INR16,300 crores, out of which 68% is from Rail and Metro, 25% is from Defense, 7% is from Mining and Construction.

items.statement: Expect order book to cross INR20,000 crores by end of FY26
items.quote: In the balance period of the current financial year, we expect that we will cross INR20,000 crores in order book.

items.statement: Approved INR1,500 crores investment for Bhopal rolling stock plant in two phases (INR900 crores + INR600 crores including GST)
items.quote: we have recently, in the last board meeting, approved an investment of INR1,500 crores for the Bhopal plant for rolling stock. This investment will be in two phases. The first phase will be around INR900 crores, second phase will be around INR600 crores, and these numbers are including GST.

items.statement: Pipeline visibility of over 15,000 cars in next 5 years including MRVC (2,856 cars), metro (2,500 cars), high-speed (4,800 cars), RRTS (720 cars), LHB coaches
items.quote: the overall requirement if we can look at in the coming five years will be at least around – it will be more than 15,000 cars.

items.statement: Diversifying into Tunnel Boring Machines (6.5m diameter for metro) and maritime cranes (ship-to-shore, gantry, Goliath) with INR5,000 crore revenue potential
items.quote: There is a huge visibility of this particular product, at least INR5,000 crore per annum can be the revenue once it reaches its complete potential.

items.statement: Q3 profitability dipped due to INR80 crore provision for a metro project restart; expects provision to reverse in 16-18 months due to exchange rate trends
items.quote: we had to provide for INR80 crores, around INR80 crores. Barring that, if you see, our performance would have been much better, the profitability would have been much better in this quarter.

items.statement: Target to reduce inventory by at least 20% in FY26; debtor days may not improve significantly
items.quote: Our endeavor is to reduce the inventory by at least 20%. And we are doing it on a war footing. The next component of working capital is the debtor. There, things may not be in our control totally.

items.statement: Bhopal plant capex to be funded through long-term debt financing; financial closure expected in couple of months
items.quote: we'll do it through debt financing. And as I mentioned, we'll do it in phases. And the first phase debt financing, it should happen maybe the financial closure another couple of months from now.

items.statement: Defense pipeline includes high-mobility vehicles (INR1,000 cr), strategic systems (INR1,000-1,500 cr), bridging systems (45-47 units, >INR1,000 cr), ARV RFP (194 units), ARV overhaul (352 fleet), missile programs
items.quote: in Defense we have an order pipeline of high-mobility vehicles for at least, you know, 1,000 crores. Then as far as the strategic systems are concerned, the engineered equipment, there is -- the requirement that is coming out, it will be around 1,000 to 1,500 crores.

items.statement: Mining orders patchy due to delayed rains and shift to MDO model; expect orders from Coal India, Singareni, SAIL, NTPC, MDOs and GCC exports in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Because of the rains getting postponed, mining ordering also has been patchy. That is number one. Number two, the shift from departmental purchase to MDO.

items.statement: Construction equipment to grow at least 30% YoY in FY26 with orders already in hand
items.quote: Construction, we already have the orders and we'll be delivering this year itself and construction will see a growth of at least 30% this year as compared to last year.

items.statement: Casting supply eased 60-70%; critical aggregates (cabins for HMV) eased 80-90%; developing domestic suppliers for HVAC, brakes, interior panels, TCMS
items.quote: casting, the steel cast at least 60% to 70%, it has eased out. As far as other components are concerned, for example, the critical aggregates like the cabins, which are needed for HMV, I would say 80% to 90%, it has been eased out.

items.statement: Developing multiple domestic suppliers for critical rolling stock aggregates; working on indigenous TCMS and propulsion control
items.quote: we are now working on developing our own train control management system by way of which we'll be in a position to decide on the propulsion supplier.

items.statement: Current rolling stock capacity 200-250 cars/year; order book of 1,400 cars; Aditya facility (Sept 2024) and KGF RC2 facility addressing near-term execution
items.quote: The - current capacity, if we take a look at the average in terms of the number of coaches per year, it is between 200 to 250. Our current order book itself is 1,400 cars.

items.statement: Employee count reduced from 4,798 (Dec'24) to 4,622 (Dec'25); value added per employee improved
items.quote: There has been a reduction in the total number of employees from 4,798 up to December '24 to 4,622 up to December '25. And there is a positive in value added per employee.

items.statement: TBM development needs 2-2.5 years for clean sheet design; no revenue expected in near term; maritime crane project needs 100-150 acre waterfront site, 3-3.5 years to revenue
items.quote: it will take some time at least, at least for—two and a half years for us to develop our clean sheet design Tunnel Boring Machine. So I don't expect any revenue as such from the Tunnel Boring Machine.

items.statement: Export order for metro rolling stock expected in 2-3 months; Bhopal plant to cater to cape gauge (Africa), standard gauge (global), broad gauge
items.quote: One of the orders for the metro rolling stock we expect in the coming two to three months. We also have a metro rolling stock projection of at least 2,500 cars in the coming four to five years.

items.statement: Expecting government development contract support for TBM (like Coal India model for rope shovel/motor grader); not seeking PLI/subsidies
items.quote: here also we expect the same kind of model to be followed. But as I mentioned earlier that we will also try to tie up with some organizations or companies who are into such kind of products

items.statement: Construction started on 1 lakh KL expansion at JNPT; Phase 1 (40-50%) expected by Q1 FY27, full commissioning by Q1 FY28
items.quote: that the first phase will be ready in the first quarter of FY '27... Amar Kabra: '26-'27. Rishi Pilani: '26-'27. And the entire construction will be completed with commissioning in -- by the end -- by the beginning of FY '27-'28

items.statement: Full 1 lakh KL expansion expected to add INR45-50 crores incremental revenue at 65-75% EBITDA margins
items.quote: So our estimate is that we should be -- once the full capacity is commissioned, we should have a range of approximately INR45 crores to INR50 crores of additional top line due to this.

items.statement: Lease rental provision increased from INR2 crores to INR24 crores annually (INR17-18 crores for 9 months), compressing margins temporarily
items.quote: Previously, we were taking a lease rental provision of INR2 crores for the full year for one of the plot -- old plot. And now that has been reset to some INR24 crores.

items.statement: Received INR51.33 crores EPC order from Reliance Industries for carbon fiber project; EPC margins typically 5-10%
items.quote: We have received INR51.33 crores order from Reliance Industries for that carbon fiber project that we have.

items.statement: EPC work for Reliance aimed at strengthening relationship for storage business; no committed future orders but Reliance is expanding storage with GBL
items.quote: Reliance is storing a lot of products with us. They are looking to expand their storage business with us. And as a support to them to understand -- build better customer relationships, you take these calls.

items.statement: JNPT land parcels: ~19 acres existing, ~11 acres newly reclaimed from terminated LPG JV with BW LPG
items.quote: So the approximate area of the parcels that we have before is 19 acres. And the new one is approximately 11 acres.

items.statement: Goa terminal utilization improvement pending approvals for handling different petroleum products
items.quote: Yes, we are taking certain approvals to handle a different type of petroleum product there, the approvals are in process right now.

items.statement: Dividend payouts to start from FY27 (quarter April-June 2026), subject to AGM approval in September 2026; intended as regular annual dividend
items.quote: We are looking at starting dividend payouts from the first quarter of next year, so that means in the quarter of April to June from that -- we are going to start dividend.

items.statement: Currently almost debt-free; capex planned from internal accruals but open to debt for strategic acquisitions with good ROI
items.quote: As of now, we have this new expansion coming. And as of now, we are -- as of now, the target is to try and compete it with our internal resources.

items.statement: Land reserved at JNPT for ammonia/cryogenic/LPG storage but no contracts yet; require 10-15 year back-to-back tank utilization guarantees
items.quote: We have kept the land aside for that. But as of now, we don't have a contract in place to start building those.

items.statement: Unauthorized transactions from FY24 shown as contingent liability; management sees no liability risk as company never authorized transactions
items.quote: We have always maintained that there is absolutely no liability that can come on the company based on this since the company has not authorized any transactions in their official capacity ever.

items.statement: Chemical business 9M FY26: revenue INR1,399M (+11% YoY), PBT INR187M (+36% YoY)
items.quote: During 9 months of this current year, the turnover of chemical business of the company increased to INR1,399 million as against INR1,254 million in the corresponding period in the previous year with an increase of 11% Y -on-Y and the profit before tax increased to INR187 million as compared to INR137 million in the corresponding period in the previous year with an increase of 36% Y-on-Y.

items.statement: LST division rental income growing; standalone 9M FY26 revenue INR1,874M (+19% YoY), PAT INR490M (+5% YoY) despite lease rental increase
items.quote: For current year's 9 months, the company achieved a turnover of INR1,874 million as compared to INR1,578 million in the corresponding period in the previous year with an increase of 19% Y-on-Y, and the profit after tax increased to INR490 million as compared to INR466 million in the corresponding period in the previous year with an increase of 5% Y-on-Y.

items.statement: No Board-level discussion on strategic partner or acquisitions to match peers' 'pearls of terminals' coastal expansion strategy
items.quote: No. As of now, there's not been any such discussion at Board level.

items.statement: EPC business focused only on customer-related projects supporting LST division; not pursuing general market EPC work
items.quote: We look at EPC is a very, very strong component to support our LST division. So if you see that the projects that we do are with our customers and related to our -- or they are related to our liquid space.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth guidance 25-30% and PAT growth 40-50%
items.quote: Performance remains aligned with the guidance outlined earlier has translated into tangible results in 9-month FY '26 and we remain well positioned to meet our full year growth for FY '26 and around 25% to 30% on the revenue and approximately 40% to 50% on the PAT.

items.statement: FY27 guidance to be provided in yearly con-call with annual results
items.quote: With the conversion of the awards from the various tenders currently floated by different states in water, power and BESS segment, we shall provide the guidance for FY '27 in our yearly con-call along with the yearly results.

items.statement: Order book INR4,358 cr including taxes and JV share as of Dec 2025
items.quote: Our current order book stands at INR4,358 crores including the taxes which reflects SPML's proportionate share in JV projects.

items.statement: 9M FY26 order inflows INR4,324 cr across water projects in multiple states
items.quote: During the 9 month of FY '26, SPML Infra witnessed strong order momentum securing fresh order inflows of INR4,324 crores across water projects in Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan besides Tamil Nadu.

items.statement: Order book comprises INR1,540 cr legacy and INR2,800 cr new higher-margin orders
items.value: INR1,540 crores legacy, INR2,800 crores new
items.quote: The order book comprises approximately INR1,540 crores of legacy orders and around INR2,800 crores of newly secured projects providing healthy execution visibility for the coming quarters.

items.statement: Active bids worth INR8,000 cr in Q3-Q4 across water, BESS, power
items.quote: We have also bid for tenders worth approximately INR8,000 crores in Q3, Q4 of the current year across the water, BESS and power segments which are active in nature.

items.statement: Visible BESS pipeline ~INR9,000 cr over next 6-12 months
items.quote: Over the next 6 to 12 months, we see a visible pipeline of approximately INR9,000 crores in BESS orders and we remain optimistic about securing a healthy share of these opportunities.

items.statement: Total estimated opportunity size ~INR5.7 lakh cr across water and power EPC tenders
items.quote: We continue to explore opportunities across water and power EPC tenders currently under various stages of bidding across Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, Bihar, Kerala and other states. The total estimated opportunity size across these markets is approximately INR5.7 lakh crores.

items.statement: BESS Phase 1 manufacturing facility 2.5 GWh at Supa MIDC Pune expected operational Q1 FY27
items.quote: SPML Infra has strategically entered into BESS with end-to-end EPC capabilities and a 2.5 gigawatt phase one manufacturing facility at Supa MIDC Pune which is expected to come up in Q1 FY '27, scalable beyond 10 gigawatts, supported by a technology partner with Energy Vault USA.

items.quote: That's the future of AI in Unbound Medicine: agentic workflows that will help us build purpose-built AI assistance for individuals, groups, and institutions to help them with their knowledge problems and educational needs, all for the betterment of education and patient care.

items.statement: Focused on receivables and timely collections; financial hygiene in place

items.quote: We have raised fund raise of INR285 crores for which the allocation was as follows capex INR183 crores, working capital INR30 crores and under GCP i.e., General Corporate Purpose, INR71 crores.

items.statement: INR100 crores investment planned for shipyard expansion over 3 years
items.quote: So, we are going to invest close to INR100 crores in the shipyard, which is going to be a mix of debt and equity.

items.statement: Capex from fund raise to be spread over 3 years
items.quote: That will be spread out over period of 3 Years.

items.statement: Fleet of 45 crafts fully utilized with dredgers at 270-300 days/year and port ancillary crafts at 365 days/year
items.quote: It's 100% utilized. None of our equipment is idle as on date.

items.statement: Dredgers utilized 270-300 days per year, port ancillary crafts 365 days per year
items.quote: So, dredgers are deployed, out of 365 days, the utilization ranges between 270 to 300 days. With regards to port ancillary craft, they are utilized over a full year i.e., 365 days.

items.statement: Inland waterway dredging demand expected to increase multifold over next 5 years with 20 national waterways to be made navigable
items.quote: Because you must have seen in the budget right now, almost 20 more national waterways have been required to be made navigable, and this demand is huge. So, over the next 5 years, in the inland waterway, dredging demand is going to increase in multifold.

items.statement: DCI not direct competition as they focus on larger vessels while company operates in shallow draft and smaller vessels segment
items.quote: We have been investing in smaller dredgers. We plan to invest in larger dredgers going forward. But there is no overlap between the assets. So, the subcontracting from DCI is going to continue as far as shallow draft and smaller vessels is required because DCI is not planning to invest in those dredgers.

items.statement: Market size for maintenance dredging in major ports INR1,500-2,000 crores annually, capital dredging ~INR1,500 crores, river dredging to grow from INR1,500 to INR5,000 crores
items.quote: About INR1,500 crores to INR2,000 crores worth of maintenance dredging is done in major ports of India. The capital dredging is close to INR1,500 crores per annum in major ports in India. If you include minor ports, that crosses close to INR3,000 crores. In terms of river dredging, the market size is going to increase from about INR1,500 crores to close to INR5,000 crores when all the 20 national

items.statement: Company revenue share less than 2% in dredging market, operates <25 of 550-600 required vessels at major ports
items.quote: So, in dredging, out of the overall market of ports, rivers and dams, we are less than 2% right now, our revenue. In terms of small craft business, between the 12 major ports, there are between 550 to 600 vessels that are required. We presently have less than 25 vessels deployed out of the 550 to 600.

items.statement: Receivable days expected to reduce from 45-60 days to 30-45 days going forward
items.quote: Our receivables ranges between 45 to max 60 days. So going forward, receivable days will tend to decrease because the number of days of receivables in the Bahrain books were a little higher as compared to the Indian books. And going forward, it will reduce between 30 to 45 days.

items.statement: Debt outstanding at INR166 crores as on date
items.quote: Debt outstanding as on date is INR166 crores, fixed assets as on date is INR207 crores, and a capital work in progress of around INR36 crores.

items.statement: Raised INR285 crores through preferential issue of equity shares and warrants
items.quote: To support our growth journey, we successfully raised INR285 crores through a preferential issue of equity shares and warrants.

items.statement: Tonnage tax scheme application accepted, effective from Q3 FY26
items.quote: We have chosen to fall under the tonnage tax scheme. We had approached the Income Tax Department, made our application, and our application has been accepted.

items.statement: Shipbuilding mix includes INR240 crores for IWAI supply contracts and green tugs for own operation
items.quote: So, we have got shipbuilding contracts from Inland Waterway Authority of India to the tune of INR240 crores, which is building a vessel and supplying that vessel to Government of India. The green tug, we are building for ourselves.

items.statement: Actively participating in green tug tenders from Paradip, Cochin, Bombay, and Calcutta ports
items.quote: We are actively participating in the green tug tenders that are being floated by major ports of India. There are presently tenders out there from Paradip Port, Cochin Port, Bombay Port and Calcutta Port.

items.statement: Bahrain project on hold until suitable vessel found at right price, no fixed restart date
items.quote: We are currently actively looking for a vessel in the market to place it in Bahrain and start the business. We have not kept on hold the Bahrain Project. As soon as the vessel is identified and purchased and deployed, the business can commence.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA margin at 43%, PAT margin at 34%
items.quote: EBITDA stood at INR38.54 crores with a margin of 43%, reflecting a strong improvement in operating efficiency. Profit after tax stood at INR32.89 crores, with a margin of 34%.

items.statement: Vessel moved from Bahrain to India due to better revenue and tax advantage now available in India
items.quote: The last vessel deployed in Bahrain has been moved to India because there was a high demand for that vessel in India, and we were getting better revenue. Also, we had chosen to move that vessel to Bahrain because of the tax advantage. Since the tax advantag e has come to India as well . We found it more beneficial for the company to operate that vessel in India

items.statement: Share subdivision from INR10 to INR5 effective December 22, 2025 to improve liquidity and retail participation
items.quote: Further, in line with our commitment to enhance shareholder value, with effect from December 22, 2025, we subdivided the company's shares from INR10 to INR5 to improve liquidity, enhance retail participation and improve overall trading efficiency.

items.statement: Shipyard expansion expected to enable INR500-700 crores top line in 3 years
items.quote: We believe that we can reach a top line of between INR500 crores to INR700 crores with the facility 3 years down the line.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 EBITDA fell to Rs 3.02 crore and net loss of Rs 14.96 crore due to supply chain pricing pressure and loss of a large telecom client
items.quote: In Q3 FY'26, revenue from operations stood at Rs. 198.23 crores compared to Rs. 206.85 crores of Q3 FY'25 reflecting a 4.17% year -on-year decline. EBITDA for the quarter was Rs. 3.02 crores. The company reported a loss before exceptional items and tax of Rs. 1.41 crores and a net loss of Rs. 14.96 crores during the quarter.

items.statement: Management expects margin pressure to ease in FY27 as fixed-price contracts expire by March 2026 and customers accept new pricing
items.quote: I a m very hopeful about, you know, this pressure of margin will not be there in the coming year. The reason being, by that time, most of the customers will start accepting the new prices and will get used to it. And my firm contract, which I have signed, whic h is till the year end, will get over as well

items.statement: Q4 order book stands at around Rs 200 crore including infrastructure deployment and cloud managed services contracts
items.quote: The current order book for Q4 is of around Rs. 200 crore which includes our infrastructure deployment projects as well as cloud and managed services contracts.

items.statement: Semiconductor shortage and supply chain challenges expected to persist throughout FY27 driven by AI infrastructure demand
items.quote: So, semiconductor challenge will be throughout 2027. Okay, means the entire FY'27, there will be a challenge.

items.statement: Digital India Corporation managed services contract worth Rs 15 crore per quarter (Rs 60 crore annually) for three years minimum, annuity-based with good margins and no hardware dependency
items.quote: So, Mahesh, of course, it is an annuity-based contract, Rs. 15 crores repeated every quarter this is happening, so yearly this may contribute us Rs. 60 crores of revenue. This is ARR, and this contract is there for minimum three years, extended further. So, this is annuity-based, number one, and the margin currently is fairly good. And it i s basically on the hyperscaler, so there is no component

items.statement: Lost a large hyperscale telecom client in Q3; client moved workloads directly to hyperscaler vendor; recovery unlikely from client but pursuing recovery from hyperscaler vendor
items.quote: From the same customer, probably we will not able to recover anything because he has moved lots of barrels from us to directly on the hyperscaler vendor. So, very honestly, let me tell you, this loss, I am not able to recover it from this customer. But we are trying to recover this loss from the hyperscaler itself.

items.statement: Secured new contracts across government, pharma, utilities, and quick commerce including Rs 15 crore Digital India contract, Rs 2.65 crore pharma data center order, Rs 2.65 crore power utility order, and Rs 8.8 crore quick commerce SD-WAN a
items.quote: During the quarter, Orient Technologies secured multiple new contracts across government, pharma, utilities, and digital commerce, rendering its services net growth. A key win was a three-year managed services contract from Digital India Corporation worth around Rs. 15 crores to manage platforms such as Umang and DigiLocker, reinforcing its presence in mission- critical government projects. The co

items.statement: Foreign bank engagement progressing with digital transformation orders and reporting work
items.quote: Yes, so the work is already progress there. We already got certain orders from that bank. Okay, we are preparing a lot of reporting for them in terms of digital transformation. So, good amount of business we have started doing with this bank.

items.statement: New service delivery center inaugurated in Navi Mumbai Turbhe for 24x7 monitoring, cybersecurity, cloud, and managed services; NOC and SOC operations fully operational with expected 100% utilization in 24-36 months
items.quote: Additionally, the company inaugurated a new service delivery center in Navi Mumbai, Turbhe to enhance 24x7 monitoring, cybersecurity, cloud, and managed services capabilities.

items.statement: NOC and SOC at Turbhe fully operational; revenue ramp-up expected over 24-36 months as enterprise contracts and managed services migrations complete
items.quote: So, let me share the good news today that our NOC and SOC operations at Turbhe is working fully in operation. So, in the last quarter, we started our business from the SOC. But from a revenue, quantum of revenue perspective, we expect utilization and ramp up over next 24 to 36 months as the enterprise contracts and the managed services migrations complete and the new SOC deals come on board.

items.statement: OEM component price increases creating margin pressure; fixed-rate contracts until March 2026 prevent pass-through; mid-market segment also facing pricing pressure
items.quote: One of the components, which is because of the supply chain, the rate contract which we have signed with the customers, we have to execute those contracts at the same price, keeping in mind that our long-term association with the customers, though the OEM has increased the prices, we have to execute the contracts at the same price, which we have signed up earlier and this is there till 31st of Mar

items.statement: Cloud and data center revenue around Rs 250+ crore; managed services including infrastructure managed services around Rs 100+ crore
items.quote: So, you can take cloud is around Rs. 250 plus crores. Managed services, including infrastructure managed services is around Rs. 100 plus crores.

items.statement: Management does not consider Dynacons Systems a direct competitor; business profiles differ
items.quote: They are good friend of us. Naturally, I do not consider them as a competitor as such. They are doing their business. Their business profile is slightly different than our business profile. Okay, so I will not like to say that they are a competitor to us.

items.statement: No plans for US geographic expansion; focus remains on domestic India opportunity
items.quote: Absolutely no at present. Because from an infrastructure space, this is not the right time to go anywhere outside India. There is a huge, huge opportunity in India. Okay, and first we need to capitalize here, then go to the developed countries.

items.statement: AI-driven GPU demand consuming semiconductor supply (RAM, disks) creating 8-10 month manufacturing lead time; shortage expected to last at least one year
items.quote: Now, AI will be oper ated only on the GPU. And that is where Nvidia plays a very important role. There i s so much of infrastructure pull on and around this Nvidia has happened. And those guys are taking lots of RAMs, disks, and other components, where the semiconductor industry is facing the challenge. If they consume so much, as you know AI requires a huge infrastructure. And that is where the s

items.statement: Labor law changes contributed to Q3 margin pressure alongside client loss
items.quote: Yes, correct. One of the factors was labor law. Another factor was because of this customer.

items.statement: Mid-market segment is sweet spot contributing 31.78% of revenue; not solely dependent on government/PSU
items.quote: Our actual sweet spot, if you see in our segment mix, is in the mid -market segment, which is contributing to more th an 31.78%, as I mentioned in my opening remarks.

items.statement: Targeting new hyperscalers, GCCs, and GIFT City entrants for business growth
items.quote: Yes, so from a GTM perspective, we are working on the various front. New hyperscalers or the people who are trying to build hyperscalers in India is one of the focuses, along with GCC, GIFT cities, people coming into the GIFT cities, and the GCC are the next focus for us to increase our business.

items.statement: Government data center investment creates managed services, cybersecurity, NOC and SOC opportunities for Orient
items.quote: And organizations like us will be managing those data centers in terms of managed services, cyber security, NOC and SOC.

items.statement: Management does not predict future operating margins; declined to confirm 8-10% range continuation
items.quote: So, we do no t predict any margin for a futur e business. So, very honestly, I a m not able to comment on that.

items.statement: Freight flows uneven, rates softening, customers cautious on shipment planning and inventory optimization
items.quote: The operating environment during the quarter remained challenging across global logistics and freight market. Freight flows across key corridors stayed uneven, freight rates continued to soften and shipment planning by customers remained cautious.

items.statement: EBITDA margin compressed to 2.8% in Q3 FY26 from 7.4% in 9M FY26 due to lower revenue and price pressure
items.quote: Operating profitability also moderated in line with lower revenue base and price pressure. EBITDA for the quarter was INR 40 million with margin of 2.8%.

items.statement: Sea import 79% of revenue, sea export rose to 14.5% from 12.2% previous quarter; renewable energy 32.7%, engineering products 20.2% in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Sea import continued to be the largest contributor accounting for about 79% of revenue for quarter. At the same time, sea export show gradual improvement in share, increasing about 14.5% of revenue as compared to 12.2% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Top 5 customers contributed 30.5% of revenue in Q3 FY26 and 37.5% in 9M FY26; customer concentration stable with improving relationship depth
items.quote: Contribution from our top 5 customer was about 31% of the revenue for the Q3 FY26 and 38% for the 9M FY26 period. This reflects repeat business and higher wallet share from long-standing clients.

items.statement: Added 25 vehicles in Q3 FY26 taking owned fleet to 42; plan 45 more in Q4 FY26 and 60-70 deferred to Q1 FY27; 1,000 containers to be executed in Q4 FY26
items.quote: We are deploying assets in FY26 and Q1 FY27 combined close to INR 130-odd crores especially on trucking and transport and containers.

items.statement: Owned fleet strength increased to 42 vehicles; targeting 150 trailers from IPO proceeds with 70-75 in Q4 FY26 and balance in Q1 FY27; 1,000 containers live from Q1 FY27
items.quote: Currently our fleet strength is 42. We are again doing some 45 odd fleets in Q4 FY26 which means in terms of transportation like we were trying to add 150 odd trailers from the IPO proceedings.

items.statement: Average revenue per TEU dropped from ~INR 79,000 in Q2 FY26 to ~INR 67,000 in Q3 FY26 (~16% drop); freight rates fell 28-30%
items.quote: For an example in Q2 FY26 the average per TEU cost was around 79,000 and for this quarter Q3 FY26 it is close to 67,000 odd. So, there has been almost like a 16% drop in terms of the pricing.

items.statement: India's ALMM policy and Make in India drive reduced solar module imports; US policy changes under Trump affected renewable sector export visibility
items.quote: Once this ALMM came into place and government of India's Make in India drive is in fact pushing all these module importers to do module assembly or module manufacturing in India.

items.statement: Revenue per TEU approximately INR 77,000; management targets double-digit EBITDA margin in FY27 vs 7.4% in 9M FY26
items.quote: So, this the cost, and revenue we go as per the market practice, and as per the market demand and supply. Q3 FY26 was very soft and the global cues as well as the policies were completely shapeless.

items.statement: Policy fluctuations (India ALMM, US Trump policies) causing demand uncertainty in renewable sector; driver scarcity delaying fleet deployment
items.quote: Due to this policy kind of fluctuations especially from the US, every manufacturer was very cautious about piling up their raw material which brought down the volume especially on the renewable sectors.

items.statement: Engineering products revenue share jumped to 20.2% in Q3 FY26 from 10.8% previous quarter driven by project cargo and equipment manufacturers
items.quote: We also saw a noticeable increase in contribution from engineering products, which increased to 20.2% in revenue in Q3 FY26 compared to 10.8% in previous quarter.

items.statement: Signed contracts with top automobile players; auto segment to show big growth in Q4 FY26 vs FY25; also targeting pharma and engineering verticals
items.quote: We have signed few contracts with top automobile players and we are executing this auto in a big way in Q4 FY26. This auto spread will have a big growth compared with FY25.

items.statement: Opened new branch in Ahmedabad to strengthen West India presence; existing branches in Gandhidham, Delhi, Kolkata, Bangalore, Coimbatore, Tuticorin, Cochin, Mumbai
items.quote: During the quarter, we opened new branch in Ahmedabad to strengthen our presence in West India and to support customer in that region with faster coordination and on-ground service.

items.statement: Cost of services increased to ~91% of revenue from 86-87% previously; management accepted lower margins to retain customer base
items.quote: We also wanted to maintain our existing customer base. So, we don't want to miss out on any of our customer base. We wanted to play it very soft especially in Q3 FY26.

items.statement: Asia contributes 83% of revenue; top TEU origins: China 7,900, Vietnam 3,600, Indonesia 2,000, Malaysia 1,600, US 1,300 TEUs in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Asia continued to remain our core region contributing about 83% of our revenue for both Q3 FY26 and 84% for the 9M FY26 period.

items.statement: Renewable energy sector outlook: energy storage batteries (BESS) and solar module manufacturing capacity expansion (5GW to 15-20GW) to drive volumes in 2026-2027
items.quote: We see a big movement of this energy storage coming into India. And we already started signing contracts with multiple customers and we also started executing in different ports in India.

items.statement: FY26 TEU target near FY25's 112,800; 9M FY26 at 67,742 TEUs, need ~45,000 in Q4 FY26; management bullish on achieving close to FY25 volumes
items.quote: In terms of TEUs in FY25, we did around 1,12,800 odd TEUs. So, as such 9M FY26 we stand around 67,000 TEUs, which is short of like 45,000 TEUs which could be the target to achieve at least that is FY25 numbers in terms of TEUs.

items.statement: Export volumes expected to grow minimum 15% next financial year
items.quote: Exports, we are doing quite fine. And I believe that next financial year, our exports should jump by minimum 15%.

items.statement: Q4 EBITDA margin expected to grow 200-250 bps
items.quote: Definitely, definitely. Even I tell you our fourth-quarter EBITDA will definitely grow by minimum 200 to 250 basis points more.

items.statement: Next financial year EBITDA expected to remain intact
items.quote: And for the next financial year, since we are holding stocks for more than 1 year, 1.5 years, for next financial year also looking at the market, our EBITDA is going to be intact.

items.statement: Domestic Q3 flat due to bulk pack timing shift and competitive intensity
items.quote: In Q3 financial year 2026, our domestic revenue, excluding power, stood at INR1,104 crores, staying broadly flat year -on-year.

items.statement: Bulk pack demand remains very strong on margin and volumes
items.quote: Bulk pack demand remains very strong for us. Bulk pack is actually growing very, very strong, both on margin as well as volumes.

items.statement: E-commerce and quick commerce now 30-35% of consumer pack business
items.quote: Almost 30%, 35% of consumer pack business has started to contribute from the e-commerce and quick commerce channels.

items.statement: Q3 gross margin 30.2% vs 24.0% YoY on lower basmati COGS
items.quote: Gross margin for the quarter stood at 30.2% compared to 24.0% in Q3 FY '25, higher due to lower average basmati COGS and higher other income during the quarter.

items.statement: Q3 EBITDA margin 16.9% vs 12.0% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA margin for the quarter was at 16.9% versus 12.0% in the same period and is higher due to higher gross margin, but was partially offset by higher proportion ate employee costs.

items.statement: 9M gross margin 28.3%, EBITDA 15.8%, PAT 10.6%
items.quote: Gross profit of the company stood at 28.3% in margin terms, while EBITDA and PAT were at 15.8% and 10.6%, respectively.

items.statement: Average basmati cost declined 9% in 9M FY26
items.quote: Average basmati cost declined by 9% in the 9-month period as paddy prices were lower in last procurement season and also the margin is higher because of higher other income.

items.statement: 9M export revenue INR1,276 crores, up 21% YoY
items.quote: For the 9 months ended, export revenue reached INR1,276 crores, reflecting a 21% year -on-year increase.

items.statement: 9M domestic revenue INR3,215 crores, up 6% YoY
items.quote: For 9 months financial year 2026, domestic revenue, excluding power, stood at INR3,215 crores, growing 6% year -over-year.

items.statement: Panipat packaging plant investment ~INR100 crores planned
items.quote: If we go through, I think that investment will be to the tune of around INR100 crores.

items.statement: Potential additional INR500-600 crores for real estate if land at 50-60% market price
items.quote: If opportunity comes where the prices we get the land at 50%, 60% of t he price, we'll definitely invest another INR500 -600 crores

items.statement: Panipat land registry underway; 50-60 acres retained for Barota expansion
items.quote: We are evaluating opportunities to monetize a portion of that land at attractive valuation based on strong market interest, while retaining roughly 50 to 60 acres for future expansion of our Barota operations.

items.statement: Ghaziabad plant shift postponed 2-3 years due to high cost >INR500-600 crores
items.quote: It might be more than INR500 crores to INR600 crores in shifting a plant. So for the time being, we have postponed that planning of shifting Ghaziabad plant.

items.statement: Prices up 7-8% in last 15 days; domestic price hikes expected Q1 next year
items.quote: Present, if you talk of present in the last 15 days, the prices have gone up by practically 7%, 8% in last 15 days. In last 15 days, the prices have gone up quite much. But if you see the domestic market, the effect will come in the first quarter of the next year.

items.statement: Branded non-basmati grew 35% in 9M; Uplife health rice portfolio expanding
items.quote: Branded non -basmati grew strongly at 35%. This value -led growth validates the strategic direction we have taken in widening our portfolio and improving distribution reach.

items.statement: Edible oil sales INR9 crores in 9M; expected to scale further
items.quote: Additionally, edible oil sales stood at INR9 crores in 9 months financial year '26, and we expect this to scale further in this financial year as our distribution deepens.

items.statement: Market share: GT 37.8%, MT 39.3%, e-comm 41.2%
items.quote: Our ma rket share in general trade stands at 37.8%. In modern trade, it is at 39.3% and e-commerce, we enjoy a leading market share of 41.2

items.statement: Retail outlets reduced to 3.2 lakh from 3.6 lakh due to quick commerce shift and co-branding pause
items.quote: Our retail outlets have kind of diminished in the past 4 to 5 months. And broadly, there are 2 reasons. One is there's a lot of shift of branded basmati business happening from general trade to quick commerce.

items.statement: Regional players pressuring prices; KRBL maintained pricing power and margins
items.quote: The basmati category saw increased competitive intensity from loose and regional players, specifically in general trade and modern trad e channels. Lower raw material prices put downward pressure on demand and margins. However, KRBL delivered robust margin expansion while maintaining volume stability.

items.statement: US-India trade understanding sets 18% import duty on Indian rice exports to US
items.quote: The recent concluded U.S. -India trade understanding, which sets an import duty of 18% on Indian rice export to the United States provide greater clarity and stability compared to the earlier reciprocal tariff uncertainty.

items.statement: Total inventory INR3,941 crores (paddy INR1,322 cr, rice INR2,450 cr) as of Dec 31, 2025
items.quote: Our total inventory as of December 31, 2025, stood at INR3,941 crores. This includes INR1,322 crores in paddy inventory versus INR1,239 crores as of December 31, ' 2024, and INR2,450 crores in rice inventory versus INR2,877 crores as of the same date last year.

items.statement: Inventory volumes: paddy 3.58 lakh tons, rice 4.11 lakh tons as of Dec 31, 2025
items.quote: On a volume basis, as of December 31, ' 2025, paddy and rice inventory stood at 3,58,000 tons and 4,11,000 tons, respectively, compared to 3,41,000 tons of paddy and 4,58,000 tons of rice in December 31, ' 2024.

items.statement: Net bank borrowings negative INR388 crores (net cash) as of Dec 31, 2025
items.quote: Net bank borrowings, net of treasury investments were at a negative INR388 crores as of December 31, '2025, as against INR102 crores last year.

items.statement: Considering buyback post budget changes effective April 1
items.quote: Yes. In this budget, it has been quite attractive. So we are thinking about it. We'll think about it.

items.statement: Headcount up 160 YoY to support capacity additions at Ghaziabad and Barota
items.quote: When we look at December '25 versus December '24, total on-roll employee headcount is up by about 160 people. Most of this is coming from increase in capacity that we've done at Ghaziabad and at Barota plants.

items.statement: Iran exports cautious due to geopolitical tensions; no new orders being concluded
items.quote: There is still tension going on, and that is why we are quite restrictive in conclu ding any new business in Iran. So therefore, it will take some time. Till some conclusion takes place, it will be difficult for me to comment

items.statement: Management guides for normalized EBITDA margins around 8% over the medium term starting FY27
items.quote: So, normalized EBITDA margins around 8% over the medium term we can see. Basically, the key driver will be our operating leverage on fixed costs combined with our higher value-added share.

items.statement: Management expects manufacturing revenue of around INR500 crores by next year (FY27)
items.quote: I can tell you 18,000 -- it's round about INR500 crores for the manufacturing side by next year.

items.statement: Management targets more than 18,000 tons volume next year (FY27)
items.quote: I think we will achieve more than 18,000 tons.

items.statement: Cumulative capex of approximately INR190+ crores planned over the next 3 years across Pithampur and Dewas
items.quote: Basically, over the next 3 years, we have planned cumulative capex of approximately INR190 plus crores, which will have a split between our further enhancement at Pithampur, where we have already acquired two acres of land where we are planning our anodizing and powder coating segment.

items.statement: Extrusion capacity expanded from 10,000 to 24,000 MT per annum at Pithampur; Italian press commissioned March 2025 stabilizing
items.quote: Our transformational capex at Pithampur Unit 1 is now live. We have extrusion capacity expanded from 10,000 to 24,000 metric per annum. Latest capability upgraded to handle 300mm profiles and 7 series alloy.

items.statement: Dewas facility acquired March 2025 via slump sale at INR8.75 crores; commercial commissioning expected in 8-10 months, focusing on precision tubing
items.quote: Further, we acquired the Dewas facility in March 2025 via slump sale at INR8.75 crores, where the plant modernization is underway. Our trial projects are started. Commercial commissioning is expected over the next 8 to 10 months.

items.statement: Dewas facility expected to generate INR100+ crores annual revenue at optimal utilization from FY28
items.quote: From FY28 onwards, Dewas can generate around INR100-plus-crores of annual revenue at optimal utilization.

items.statement: Q3 revenue declined 16% YoY to INR152 crores due to lower trading volumes and muted export demand
items.quote: During Q3 our revenue from operations stood at INR152 crores, reflecting a 16% year-on-year decline, primarily due to lower trading volumes, which I have just explained that it is completely opportunity-driven, and muted export demand during the quarter.

items.statement: Manufacturing revenue grew 10% YoY in Q3 and 13% on nine-month basis driven by higher extrusion volumes and value-added sales
items.quote: Our manufacturing revenue grew 10% year-on-year in Q3 and almost 13% on a nine-month basis, driven by higher extrusion volumes and increased value-added sales.

items.statement: US order cancellation of ~450 tons impacted Q3; director in US to recover orders
items.quote: Our round about 500 to 600 tons order will be cancelled from US when they told that we are charging 500% duty on India because of Russian oil. At that time, all orders are cancelled.

items.statement: Anodizing margin INR15,000-20,000 per ton; powder coating margin INR10,000-12,000 per ton
items.quote: We will get round about INR15,000 per ton to INR20,000-ton margin. Our facility is coming for 1000 ton per anodizing. And INR10 to INR12 in powder coating.

items.statement: Aerospace segment expected to yield ~INR80 per kg margin; target 100-150 tons monthly share of 2,500 ton Indian market
items.quote: I can say round about INR80 per kg margins. Madhur Rathi: Okay. Ravinder Nath Jain: And the aerospace consumption in India is round about 2,500 tons per month. And we expect we can get round about 100-150 tons in our share

items.statement: Extrusion-only EBITDA per ton INR10,000-12,000; full value chain (extrusion + anodizing + powder coating) ~INR30,000 per ton
items.quote: The extrusion if I say total mill finish, then anodizing, then powder coating, I can say round about INR30,000 per ton approximately. After extrusion and anodizing. Madhur Rathi: Okay. INR30,000

items.statement: Strategic shift from commodity extrusion to high-value applications in defense, aerospace, automotive, solar, railway
items.quote: We have diversified end markets catering from automotive, defense, aerospace, solar, railway, architecture, electrical, and heavy engineering. The company is investing aggressively to reposition itself towards higher margin application-specific products.

items.statement: Aerospace vendor audits underway; discrepancies to be cleared within 2.5 months; not focused on architectural due to low margins

items.statement: 126% preliminary CVD on India-made cells not applicable as Waaree uses non-India cell sources; FEOC compliance required from April 2026
items.quote: this 126% is for any modules which will be using India-based cells, which again must have all non-Chinese sources. And in our case, we don't use those cells.

items.statement: Provision made in last quarter for potential financial impact from ongoing investigations regarding Chinese cell usage for US exports
items.quote: proactively basis the discussions and advice of our councils, we have already done provision in the last quarter itself on the potential financial impacts.

items.statement: Overseas revenue ~30-35% of total (exports from India + US local manufacturing); similar mix expected in FY27
items.quote: our overseas revenue is as I mentioned earlier in the call also is around one-third of the total volumes that we do. So, you can expect similar range of continued supply.

items.statement: India positioned as primary alternative to China for US supply chain; 100+ GW module, 25-30 GW cell (growing to 50-60 GW), wafer capacity building to 30-40 GW
items.quote: apart from China, the largest capacity resides in India. If you look at the current capacity in India of module 100 gigawatt plus, cell currently 25, 30 gigawatts probably going up to 50, 60 gigawatts over next two, three years of time.

items.statement: Ongoing investigations into Chinese cell usage for US exports; 6-12 month timeline; cooperating with authorities
items.quote: these kind of discussions and investigation generally take 6 to 12 months of time. And we continue to cooperate with the government and continue to supply the information.

items.statement: US installation pipeline 180-200 GW over 2-3 years vs 70-80 GW annual consumption
items.quote: broadly this 70, 80 gigawatt of overall co nsumption every year leads to a demand outlook of 180 to 200 gigawatt over next two, three years of time in
